title: Get the installer URL and an org-scoped install token headless
text: `GET <serverUrl>/api/v2/agent/installerInfo/linux64` (or `/api/v2/agent/installerInfo/<platform>`), header `icSessionId: <v2 session>`, returns `downloadUrl` and a 122-character `installToken`. The token pins the agent to the org whose session minted it, so mint it in the target org and use it fresh: the vendor guide says install tokens expire after 24 hours, and a saved token was found expired weeks later. The v3 agent paths return 404; use the v2 route. Installing still needs a shell on the host.
evidence: 200 on three orgs (2026-07-01, 2026-07-25, 2026-09-28); a saved token found expired (2026-08-15)

title: Install and register a Linux Secure Agent in the right order
text: 1) Create a non-root OS user (the installer refuses root). 2) As that user, download `downloadUrl`, verify the published SHA-256, `chmod +x` and run `./agent64_install_ng_ext.<build>.bin -i silent`. 3) `cd <agent_home>/apps/agentcore` and start the daemon first: `./infaagent startup` (under nohup or its systemd unit). 4) Register: `./consoleAgentManager.sh configureToken <user> '<installToken>'` answers 'Login succeeded' (`configureTokenWithRuntime` also exists). Registering before the start fails with 'Cannot connect to the Agent'. 5) `./consoleAgentManager.sh getstatus` must say READY and `isConfigured` true. 6) Check the cloud side: `GET /api/v2/agent` shows the agent `active: true` in the expected org, and the agent created its own runtime environment. Then read `agentEngines[]`. An idle agent uses about 1 GB RAM.
evidence: Checksum-verified installs registered READY on three orgs (2026-07-01, 2026-07-25/26, 2026-09-28)

title: Prove outbound HTTPS to IDMC from the host before installing
text: From the future agent host, a GET to the login endpoint returning 405 (it is POST-only), a 404 from a package path and a 301 from the `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com` root together prove that egress works. A timeout or TLS failure is a firewall or proxy problem to fix before the install.
evidence: login 405, package 404, domain root 301 (2026-08-18)

title: Installer disk and log traps
text: The Linux installer is about 382 MB and needs about 2 GB to unpack. A full disk produces blank logs and stuck runs that look like application bugs. nohup logs can come back empty because of buffering; do not read that as silence.
evidence: Observed during an install (2026-07-26)

title: Vendor host prerequisites for a Secure Agent (documented)
text: Documented, not re-measured: Windows needs 4 CPU, 16 GB RAM, at least 5 GB free on a 250 GB disk, the MSVC++ 2015 runtime and outbound 443; Linux needs at least 11 GB free, a `libidn.so.11` (symlink it on newer distros) and a non-root install user. Engines are enabled per runtime environment and connectors per add-on connector list; see L-AGENT-039 for the headless route.
evidence: Vendor Getting Started guide citations (2026-08-15)

title: Run consoleAgentManager from the agentcore directory
text: `consoleAgentManager.sh` sources `./version.sh` relative to the current directory, so calling it by absolute path dies with 'cannot open ./version.sh' and looks like a dead agent. Use `su - <agentuser> -c 'cd <agent_home>/apps/agentcore && ./consoleAgentManager.sh getstatus'` and expect READY.
evidence: Observed 2026-07-26

title: Count agent JVMs with pgrep -c -f and the full class name
text: Use `pgrep -c -f 'agentcore.impls.MainApp'` and expect exactly 1 per install directory (per agent). The form `pgrep -af 'agentcore.*MainApp' | wc -l` also counts your own SSH command line, returns 2 on a healthy host and invents a lock conflict.
evidence: Phantom conflict reproduced 2026-07-26; one MainApp per install dir confirmed with two agents on one host 2026-09-28

title: A real readyToRun:false: two agent JVMs fighting the singleton lock
text: When the per-agent `readyToRun` really is false, the agent can be registered and READY on the host while its package manifest holds no DI packages and no error is raised; `ls <agent_home>/apps/` shows what was delivered. A known cause is two agent JVMs fighting the lock (`SingularApplicationLock: Cannot acquire lock, there is probably another instance running`), for example a systemd unit with `Restart=on-failure` respawning against a manual start. Keep one supervisor.
evidence: Observed during an install (2026-07-26)

title: A systemd unit for the Secure Agent that survives reboots
text: `infaagent` forks and resolves paths relative to its own directory, so a naive unit fails silently ('cannot open ./agent_start.sh', `systemctl is-active` inactive while the agent runs). Working unit: `Type=forking`, `RemainAfterExit=yes`, `User=<agentuser>`, `WorkingDirectory=<agent_home>/apps/agentcore`, `ExecStart=<agent_home>/apps/agentcore/infaagent startup`, `ExecStop=<agent_home>/apps/agentcore/infaagent shutdown`, `KillMode=control-group`, `TimeoutStopSec=300`. Leave out `Restart=`: `agent_start.sh` already respawns agentcore, and a second supervisor fights the singleton lock. Stop any manual instance, confirm one JVM, `systemctl restart`, and confirm READY.
evidence: systemctl restart -> active -> READY (2026-07-26); second-agent unit active in its own cgroup (2026-09-28)

title: Without systemd, an @reboot crontab entry keeps the agent alive across reboots
text: An agent with neither a systemd unit nor an @reboot entry stays down after a host reboot and every schedule silently stops, with no alert. A user crontab line `@reboot sleep 30 && <agent_home>/apps/agentcore/infaagent startup` (older installs: `infaagent.sh startup`) is a zero-cost, reversible self-heal; verify with `crontab -l`. Keep a break-glass ladder: restart, reboot, re-register, reinstall, each checked from both sides (per-agent API and on-host `getstatus`). Prefer the systemd unit (L-AGENT-009).
evidence: Crontab entry verified after hardening (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-08)

title: An agent started through a cloud run-command lives in the extension's cgroup and dies on reboot
text: Starting the agent from `az vm run-command` puts agentcore in the run-command extension's transient scope (for example an `...RunCommandLinux.slice` / `enable_<n>.scope` cgroup). Nothing supervises it, it is exposed to the extension's lifecycle, and it does not come back after a reboot. Start agents only through their systemd unit and check the cgroup (`systemctl status <unit>` or `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` showing `/system.slice/<unit>.service`).
evidence: cgroup inspection before and after moving the agent to its unit (2026-09-28)

title: Restart the agent detached from your session
text: `<agent_home>/apps/agentcore/infaagent shutdown`, then `nohup <agent_home>/apps/agentcore/infaagent startup &` (or `setsid ./agent_start.sh`, or tmux). A dropped SSH or IAP session in the middle of a startup can leave the agent down. After the restart, confirm all engines RUNNING (DIS `subState` 0) and re-test one connection.
evidence: 8 engines RUNNING and JDBC test 200 after a nohup restart (2026-06-27); 23 engine processes back after a setsid restart (2026-07-06)

title: Make restarts safe: an orphan reaper in ExecStartPre/ExecStopPost plus a port guard, both scoped to their own install
text: `agent_start.sh` respawns agentcore in place, which can leave engine JVMs and the Process Server's embedded Postgres behind; they hold ports and lock files and the next start stalls. Install a reaper as `ExecStartPre` and `ExecStopPost` in a drop-in (`/etc/systemd/system/<unit>.service.d/10-reap-orphans.conf`) plus a */5 cron check: it kills leftover processes of the agent user (TERM, 30 s, KILL) and refuses to start, loudly, while ports 7005/14479 or `*.mv.db` files are still held. Proven: kill -9 of agentcore and its respawn loop, then `systemctl restart`: 0 orphans and 20/20 engines RUNNING in about 6 min, with CDC and CAI unaffected. Add a Process Server port guard (L-AGENT-073). When a second agent on the host also runs a Process Server (give its embedded Postgres its own port, for example 5434, and its own port guard, L-AGENT-089, L-CAI-072), scope every reaper and guard to its own install: count a port holder only if the PID belongs to that agent's OS user (`stat -c %U /proc/<pid>`), and count `*.mv.db` lock files only under that agent's home. An unscoped guard ('any holder of 7005/14479, any *.mv.db') refused every start of the first agent once the second agent's Process Server held 7005; it surfaced only at the next reboot. After a reboot check the agent process (`pgrep -u <agentuser> -c -f agentcore.impls.MainApp`, L-AGENT-007), not the unit: a `Type=forking` + `RemainAfterExit=yes` unit reads `active (exited)` even when agentcore is dead.
evidence: Forced crash and restart: 0 orphans, 20/20 engines RUNNING in ~6 min (2026-09-26); after a host reboot an unscoped guard blocked every start of the first agent, and with the owner and path filter both agents started (2026-09-30)

title: A locked user account does not stop the Secure Agent
text: The agent authenticates with its own agent token, so already-scheduled tasks keep running while the interactive user is locked out. REST job triggers, exports and UI work stop until the login works again. Keep login-independent work going and do not retry logins in a loop.
evidence: Schedules kept running during a lockout (2026-08-19)

title: Run a second Secure Agent on the same host
text: Give it its own OS user, home and install directory (its own singleton lock and environment) and a separately named systemd unit: `Type=forking`, `RemainAfterExit=yes`, `KillMode=control-group`, `User=<agentuser2>`, no `Restart=`, and an `ExecStartPre` guard that refuses to start while a manual instance runs (match with a `[.]` pattern such as `pgrep -f '<agent_home2>/apps/agentcore[.]...'` so pgrep does not match the guard itself; the first attempt was refused by its own guard). Add `MemoryHigh`/`MemoryMax` and `CPUWeight`/`IOWeight` so it cannot starve the first agent or the apps. Deny the new user read access to the applications' secret files, and share file-lane directories through a group-writable directory instead of the first agent's home. Expect exactly one agentcore MainApp per install directory.
evidence: Second agent READY under systemd, 7 services RUNNING, 0 ERROR lines, peak unit memory 5.2 GB with memory.events high=0, first agent's pid unchanged (2026-09-28)

title: Keep the Process Server off on a second agent that shares a host
text: The on-agent CAI Process Server binds 7080/7443, internal ports such as 7005 and 14479, and an embedded Postgres on 5432. On a host that already runs an agent and a Postgres it clashes, and a first agent's pre-start guard that refuses while 7005/14479 are held would then fail. If CAI can run on the hosted Cloud Server, leave the Process Server deselected on the second agent. Other engines picked free ports (the second agent skipped a port the first one held). Diff `ss -ltnp` before and after each service lands.
evidence: Host watch showed no port clash with the Process Server off (2026-09-28/29)

title: Set agent memory and CPU limits with systemctl set-property, and make sure every agent process and heap fits inside the cap
text: `systemctl set-property <unit> MemoryHigh=12G MemoryMax=14G CPUWeight=100 IOWeight=100` applies live without a restart. Persistent set-property drop-ins land in `/etc/systemd/system.control/<unit>.d/` and take precedence over `/etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/`; with `--runtime` the change is lost at reboot. Check throttling in the unit's `memory.events` (`high=0` means never throttled) and PSI (`/proc/pressure/cpu`, `memory`). Add swap for idle JVM pages if RAM is tight (a second swapfile with `nofail` in fstab). A cap works only if (1) every agent process runs inside it: an agent first started from an interactive SSH session lived in that session's scope, uncapped (8.8 GB RSS, 41 processes), while under its own unit it used 3.6 GB, so helper scripts that start or redeploy agent components must run through `systemd-run --scope --slice=<agent-slice>`; (2) the configured `-Xmx` of every agent JVM (agentcore, the DIS Tomcat, Mass Ingestion runtimes, other engines) plus the DTMs fits under it: about 9.5 GB of configured heap inside a 4 GB cap throttled constantly even when idle (`memory.events` high about 12 million, CPU throttled in 24% of periods at a 0.5-vCPU quota), so deselect unneeded services and lower their heaps, or raise the cap; and (3) there are no duplicate JVMs: three orphaned copies of the agent's Administrator app JVM (none bound to its port) pushed the slice over MemoryHigh (memory.pressure full avg10 62%), and killing them dropped pressure to 4% and freed about 1 GB. Read `memory.events`, `memory.pressure` and `cpu.stat` (`nr_throttled`) under `/sys/fs/cgroup/<slice>/` to see the cap biting.
evidence: Limits raised live 2026-09-29 00:00Z; unit never throttled; second 8 GB swapfile active; an agent moved into its slice went from 8.8 GB to 3.58 GB RSS, and killing 3 orphan JVMs cut memory pressure from 62% to 4% (2026-10-03)

title: Two agents on one 4-vCPU host contend for CPU, not memory
text: With two agents, catalog Metadata services and app containers on 4 vCPU, pipelines slowed from CPU contention while memory was not throttled (`memory.events high=0`). Lower the idle agent's `CPUWeight`/`IOWeight`, give the working agent `MemoryHigh`/`MemoryMax` headroom, add swap for idle JVM pages, and deselect the Metadata services when scans are done (that freed about 3.7 GB RAM and cut CPU PSI from about 16-19% to about 10%). A 16-task lane went from 7.7 min to 3.5 min after the tuning.

title: Cap parallel task fan-out at about the host's vCPU count
text: Mapping tasks on a small agent host are CPU-bound. Staged fan-out at concurrency 4 on a 4-vCPU host shared by two agents roughly halved lane times (a 16-task lane 462 s -> 215 s; sign-up to golden record about 5 min -> 93 s). Going wider risks contention and DTM heap pressure.
evidence: Measured lane times before and after (2026-09-29)

title: Agent health comes from the v2 agent routes, not from v3 objects
text: On `<serverUrl>` with `icSessionId`: `GET /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment` lists runtime environments with nested `agents[]`; `GET /api/v2/agent` lists agents; `GET /api/v2/agent/<agentId>` gives `active`, `readyToRun`, `version` (agent core, for example 76.x), `upgradeStatus`, `lastUpgradeCheck` and `packages[]`; `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` gives `agentEngines[]` with `agentEngineStatus.status`, `desiredStatus`, `appname`, `displayName`, `subState` and the engine version. No v3 object type returns live agent status or version. A health script should be read-only and exit with the number of unhealthy agents.
evidence: 200 on several orgs; 25 engine rows captured per snapshot (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-26)

title: The runtime-environment list reports a stale readyToRun:false; read health per agent
text: `GET /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment` returned `agents[].readyToRun: false` for agents that `GET /api/v2/agent/<agentId>` reported as true, reproducibly (3 reads of 3), while the host said READY and one agent JVM ran. The list value is not refreshed per heartbeat. Trust the per-agent read, cross-check with on-host `getstatus`, and confirm with a connection test before diagnosing anything from the list.
evidence: 3/3 reproductions on one org (2026-07-26); the same false negative on another org's agents (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-09)

title: readyToRun exists twice, and only catalog-source creation checks it
text: The agent object (`GET /api/v2/agent/<agentId>`) can say `readyToRun=true` while the nested `agents[].readyToRun` in `GET /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>` still says false; they sync separately. Mapping-task runs (`POST /api/v2/job`) ignore both flags and complete. The CDGC create-catalog-source call validates the runtime-environment view and returned 500 'Error while validating Runtime Environment detail [<reId>] under global config option [Execution]' while the nested flag was false; existing catalog sources still scanned.
evidence: 22 mapping tasks ran state=1 with both agents reading readyToRun false (2026-07-04); catalog-source create 500 (2026-06-27)

title: Licensed, assigned, deploying and running-and-resolvable are four different states
text: 1 LICENSED: Administrator > Licenses (no licence inventory API). 2 ASSIGNED: the service is selected on the runtime environment (L-AGENT-039). 3 DEPLOYING: `agentEngines[].agentEngineStatus.status` sits at DEPLOYING while packages download. 4 RUNNING and resolvable: only a passing connection test or a job proves it. The API can say RUNNING while the agent log says UNKNOWN and the cloud router still answers 'No running service found of type ...'. Engine versions (for example DIS 77.x, Connector_Service 21.x) move independently of the agent core version (76.x).
evidence: API RUNNING while the router refused (2026-07-26)

title: A confirmation is not a completion: engines deploy for many minutes
text: After services are enabled (UI toast or a selections PUT), engines sit DEPLOYING while installers download and unpack: 45+ minutes for a large set on a small host, about 18 minutes for a trimmed set (PUT at 22:10Z, engines RUNNING 22:28Z). Poll `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` and wait for a passing connection test before using the runtime.
evidence: 45+ min DEPLOYING (2026-07-26); 18 min to RUNNING after a trimmed PUT (2026-09-28)

title: After an enablement the agent pulls packages itself; no reinstall
text: After a licence change or service enablement the agent polls IDMC and downloads the new engine packages on its own, with no restart or reinstall: one agent went from 1 engine to 22-23 engines, all DEPLOYING within minutes.
evidence: 1 -> 23 engines, 9 RUNNING and 14 DEPLOYING (2026-07-26)

title: An error that changes between attempts is deployment progress, not a new wall
text: While engines deploy (20+ minutes), connection tests fail with an error that moves down the stack: 'No running service ... Data_Integration_Server 77.*', then '... Connector_Service 21.*', then a timeout or a driver-level error. Each shift means the previous layer is fixed; wait and re-read instead of reconfiguring. Under host memory pressure the same rotation appears because the engine the handshake needs is being OOM-killed (L-AGENT-052).
evidence: Observed error progression during a bring-up (2026-07-26)

title: An isolated 500 CMN_001 on one package download retries itself
text: An isolated `500 CMN_001` on a single `appspec/dependency/package/.../urls/...` fetch during engine deployment is retried automatically (backoff up to 80 s) and does not stall the other packages. Do not intervene.
evidence: Observed 2026-07-26

title: Alert on real engine failures only, not on transient states
text: Treat RESTARTING and DEPLOYING as transients and RUNNING-while-desired-STOPPED as not an outage; alert only on STOPPED or FAILED when `desiredStatus` is RUNNING, and on a RESTARTING loop that persists across restart cycles. Counting transients as unhealthy made critical alerts flap.
evidence: Flapping stopped (2026-07-05); a persistent RESTARTING loop seen on two agents (2026-07-04)

title: Agent-health alert rules need a scheduled exporter and LF textfiles
text: An exporter script plus loaded alert rules still gives an empty series if nothing runs the exporter. Schedule it (for example every 5 min), write the node_exporter textfile atomically with LF line endings (CRLF breaks the textfile collector), check for one non-empty series per agent, and inject a synthetic agent-down event to prove delivery end to end.
evidence: Empty series fixed; synthetic agent-down alert delivered (2026-07-04)

title: One login sees every runtime environment: loop them all and count them first
text: A single org login enumerates all runtime environments, so one collector can monitor several environments. Iterate every RE, agent and connection (remove any `break` after the first element) and stamp an environment label or `re_id` on every row. Enumerate the REs from the API before asserting 'all N agents healthy'; an assertion written for a third agent that does not exist is wrong by construction.
evidence: Pre-fix collector captured 1 RE; post-fix 2 env rows (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-08)

title: 403 APP_13401 and 500 CMN_001 under /api/v2/agent/* are router artifacts
text: `GET /api/v2/agent/<bogus>` returns 403 `APP_13401` and `GET /api/v2/agent/<bogus>/<id>` returns 500 `CMN_001`, byte-identical to the answers from `POST /api/v2/agent/service`. They prove neither the presence nor the absence of a handler; never cite them either way. Bogus-twin error codes, not only 200s.
evidence: Bogus twins byte-identical (2026-07-26)

title: Preflight in five calls, then read the verdict off the branch
text: Before any agent work: `POST https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas/public/core/v3/login` (org, pod); `GET /api/v2/org` (both id shapes); `GET /api/v2/agent` (any agents?); `GET /api/v2/agent/<agentId>` (per-agent `readyToRun`); `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` (`agentEngines[]`). Verdicts: `agents: []` = entitlement unresolved, install an agent; only `OpsInsightsDataCollector` = telemetry only, agent-bound calls fail 403 APP_105060, select services; `Data_Integration_Server` DEPLOYING = wait, a rotating error is progress; DI RUNNING but the connection test fails = adapter or driver gate; `readyToRun:false` from the list = re-read per agent.
evidence: Used on two orgs (2026-07-26)

title: Bootstrap from zero to a running job
text: 1 log in and pick the plane; 2 confirm org and pod (`GET /api/v2/org`); 3 read the gate (agents, `agentEngines[]`, per-agent `readyToRun`); 4 get the install token; 5 size the host, install and register (needs a shell); 6 read the runtime environment the agent created; 7 select services, then connectors (headless since 2026-09-28, L-AGENT-039), then stage drivers; 8 create and test connections against tables that hold rows; 9 create or clone tasks and schedules; 10 run with `POST /api/v2/job`; 11 monitor with activityLog/activityMonitor. All steps except 5 are REST.
evidence: Run on a new sub-org (2026-07-25/26); step 7 made headless (2026-09-28)

title: Establish the four gates in order: host, engine, adapter, driver
text: A working connection needs four independent things, and each fails with its own error that looks like 'the connection is broken': HOST (RAM, disk, swap, OS libraries, egress, only the engines you need), ENGINE (the service selected and RUNNING, not DEPLOYING), ADAPTER (the connector enabled on that runtime environment and deployed to the agent), DRIVER (third-party JDBC jars staged where the connector reads them). Establish them in that order; only then do connection bodies and credentials matter. Read what the error names (engine, `com.informatica.adapter.<x>`, 'Unable to load driver') and fix that gate.
evidence: Gate order from several bring-ups; the four error signatures observed 2026-07-26 to 2026-09-28

title: Runtime environments: list and create on v2
text: `GET /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment` lists runtime environments and `POST /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment` creates one (an empty body returns 400, so the verb exists). A Secure Agent creates its own runtime environment when it registers. The Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent is the only runtime environment usable without a Secure Agent. `GET /public/core/v3/runtimeEnvironments` returned 200 on one pod and 404 on another, and the singular `/public/core/v3/runtimeEnvironment` answered 415; prefer the v2 forms.
evidence: 200/400/415 live; v3 plural 200 vs 404 A/B across pods (2026-07-25/26)

title: A runtime environment is a network position: choose it by where the data lives
text: Hosted Agent: runs inside Informatica, nothing to install, SaaS-to-SaaS only where the connector supports it; it cannot reach a private network, and a connection bound to it creates with 200 and then cannot see a private host. Secure Agent group: a host you own; the only option that reaches a private database; you own patching, disk, RAM and uptime. Serverless runtime: Informatica-managed compute inside your own AWS or Azure account (your VPC/VNet, subnets and an IAM role); it cannot reach other clouds or data centres, bills IPUs per runtime-hour, and its creation is UI-only (`/public/core/v3/serverlessRuntimeEnvironments` and `/api/v2/serverlessRuntimeEnvironment` both 404 while a control call proves the plane).
evidence: Vendor runtime docs plus live 404s (2026-07-26)

title: An agent reaches only what its own network reaches
text: A connection test from an agent in one cloud to another cloud's private (RFC1918) address never succeeds without a VPN or peering, and a database whose port is open only to tagged hosts or subnets needs the agent on one of those hosts; tests from elsewhere time out whatever the credentials. Point environment mirrors at sources local to the agent's network (containers on the same host network, a local pooler) or provide a VPN or an allowlisted replica.
evidence: Cross-cloud tests timed out; mirrors repointed to local sources tested green (2026-06-27 to 2026-07-08)

title: Sub-org runtime environments inherited from the parent show zero agents
text: A sub-org can inherit all its runtime environments from its parent; they show zero agents until an agent is installed in the sub-org itself. Do not bind a sub-org connection to the parent's shared runtime environment: it creates with 200 and its test error changes from APP_105060 to `error [error [null]]`, which looks like progress but is identical for a bogus host, so nothing was attempted.
evidence: Bogus-host control (2026-07-26); four inherited REs with zero agents (2026-07-25)

title: Select runtime-environment services and connectors headless with GET/PUT selections/ui
text: `GET https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/runtime/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>/selections/ui` with header `IDS-SESSION-ID: <v2 icSessionId>` returns `{services:{selections:[...]}, connectors:{selections:[...]}, additionalServices:{selections:[...]}}`, each selection `{id, name, internalName, mandatory, enabled, visible, productDependencies[], connectorDependencies[]}`. Save that body as the undo, edit only the `enabled` flags, and PUT the same body back to the same URL (200). Read it back, then poll `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` until the engines are RUNNING. With `INFA-SESSION-ID` instead the route answers the login HTML page. The Administrator 'Enable or Disable Services' dialog calls this same PUT, and the managed MCP tool `secureagentmanagement.update_runtime_environment_selections` does the same job. This is the first proven PUT in IDMC.
evidence: PUT 200 plus read-back; engines RUNNING 18 min later; used for several on/off cycles (2026-09-28/29); UI walk showed the dialog calls it (2026-09-24)

title: Selections carry dependencies: enabling one service switches on others
text: Each selection lists `productDependencies` and `connectorDependencies`, and enabling it enables them: Data Quality pulls in the Amazon S3 v2, Google Cloud Storage V2 and Microsoft Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 connectors; Data Governance and Catalog pulls in Data Integration, Data Quality and the Amazon Redshift v2, JDBCV2 and Snowflake Data Cloud connectors; Data Integration - Elastic pulls in the storage connectors plus Hadoop Files V2; B2B Gateway pulls in AS2 and the FTP/SFTP/FTPS/EDI connectors; Data Masking pulls in JDBC_IC. `Platform` is mandatory and not visible. The service list seen: Platform, Data Integration, Data Integration - Elastic, Application Integration, Mass Ingestion-Files, Mass Ingestion-Streaming, Mass Ingestion-Databases, Integration Hub, B2B Gateway, Data Quality, Data Masking, Data Governance and Catalog, Industry Solutions, Data Access Management Proxy, Data Access Management Agent, Python Integration, Metadata Platform Service; additional services: Self-hosted Git Repo, EDC Integration, Secret Manager.
evidence: Selections JSON before/after snapshots on one org (2026-09-28/29); S3 v2 and ADLS Gen2 arrived as DQ dependencies

title: Never select every service on a small or shared agent host
text: Selecting all ~17 services and 26 connectors made a new agent download about 18 GB in about 8 minutes, pushed the load average to about 189 on 4 vCPU, filled swap and made an app container go unhealthy. Enable only what the scope needs (for example Platform, Data Integration, Mass Ingestion-Databases, Data Quality plus the needed connectors), keep the catalog Metadata services and the Process Server off unless needed, and check free disk before any selection change. Deselecting a service does not make its downloaded packages safe to remove: never prune or move `downloads/` to win back space (services run from it, L-AGENT-094); size the disk for the full download instead.
evidence: Load 189, swap 8/8 GB, 18 GB pulled; after the trim load 3.9 and all containers up (2026-09-28); a hold-folder prune of downloads/ broke 14 of 20 services (2026-09-30)

title: Every selections PUT also rolls DIS, Mass Ingestion and Connector_Service to their newest builds
text: Any PUT to `.../selections/ui`, even one that only deselects a service, upgrades Data_Integration_Server, MassIngestionRuntime and Connector_Service to the newest build (seen: DIS 77.0.4 -> 77.0.5 -> 77.0.6, Connector_Service 21.0.3 -> 21.0.5, MassIngestionRuntime 30.3 -> 30.5 across three changes). Jobs submitted meanwhile queue for about 5 minutes while the engines redeploy; a running CDC job was unaffected. Batch selection changes and make them between lanes, never right before a timed run or demo.
evidence: Three rollovers observed; lanes queued ~5 min after each PUT (2026-09-28/29)

title: Catalog scanner services are heavy: switch them on only for the scan window
text: Metadata_Foundation_Agent (selected as 'Data Governance and Catalog') and Metadata_Platform_Service, which run on-agent catalog scans, cost several GB of RAM and a lot of CPU on a small host. Select them just before a scan window, scan sources one at a time, and deselect them afterwards (MemAvailable 10.1 -> 13.8 GB and CPU PSI 16-19% -> ~10% after switching them off). Remember that each selection change also rolls engines (L-AGENT-042).
evidence: Host readings before and after deselecting (2026-09-29)

title: These agent routes do not enable services
text: Still valid as negative facts: `POST /api/v2/agent/service` answers router artifacts (403 APP_13401 or 500 CMN_001); `/api/v2/agent/selectiveservices` gives 500; `POST /api/v2/agent/<agentId>` with `agentEngines[].desiredStatus=RUNNING` returns 500 or an identity-service redirect and reads back `agentEngines: []` (a silent no-op, also as a parent-org admin); `/public/core/v3/runtimeEnvironments` does not select anything. Use the selections route (L-AGENT-039).

title: Re-test connections after an agent is re-provisioned: adapter walls go stale
text: After an agent was re-provisioned on a newer agent core, connections that had failed with 403 APP_105060 ('adapter not enabled') or 'connector not registered' all tested green. A wall that depends on agent state is a state, not a platform limit: re-run the connection test (`GET /api/v2/connection/test/<connId>` or the managed MCP `connectionmanagement.test_connection_by_id`) before escalating. An agent restart alone did not bring back a connector that had been disabled at the control plane; re-enable it in the selections.
evidence: 4 of 4 connection tests successful after re-provisioning (2026-09-23); APP_105060 then 200 after the connector was re-added (2026-09-22)

title: Disable unconfigured services that crash-loop, per runtime environment
text: Data Access Management Agent and its Proxy often restart-loop when no policy proxy is configured (for example 950 restarts logging 'missing privitar.jdbcproxy.userWithConnectionPrivileges'). The loop does not block Data Integration, metadata or connectivity, but the agent reports 'Not All Services Running'. If you do not use them, deselect them on that runtime environment only (selections route or Runtime Environments > Actions > Enable or Disable Services); the agent then reports Up and Running. Undo by selecting them again.
evidence: 20/20 enabled services up after deselecting (2026-09-24); DI unaffected by the loop on two agents (2026-07-07)

title: Small, stable engine sets
text: Catalog plus data integration ran cleanly on 8 services: Data Integration Server, Connector Service, Metadata Foundation, Metadata Platform, Database Ingestion, Mass Ingestion, Common Integration Components, OpsInsights collector. Governance-only work needs Data_Integration_Server, Connector_Service, Metadata_Foundation_Agent and Metadata_Platform_Service (load fell from 65 to 14 after trimming the rest). A CDI-only base is Data_Integration_Server, Connector_Service, Common_Integration_Components and OpsInsightsDataCollector, plus MassIngestionRuntime/Database_Ingestion for CDC.
evidence: All 8 engines RUNNING after a rebuild (2026-06-26); load 65 -> 14 (2026-07-26)

title: The deployed engine list says what is actually running, and what each engine is for
text: `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` lists `agentEngines[].appname`. Seen: `Data_Integration_Server` (CDI and CDQ runtime), `Connector_Service`, `Common_Integration_Components`, `OpsInsightsDataCollector`, `Database_Ingestion` and `MassIngestionRuntime` (Database Ingestion/CDC), `process-engine` (display name 'Process Server', the on-agent CAI runtime), `Metadata_Foundation_Agent` and `Metadata_Platform_Service` (on-agent catalog scans), `Data_Access_Management_Agent` and `_Proxy`, `DataServiceApiMgmt` (API management), `B2BProcessor`, `CIHProcessor` (Cloud Integration Hub), `Streaming_Ingestion_Agent`, `At_Scale_Server`, `FileIntegrationService`, `AIAgentRuntime`. A deployed engine proves the capability is provisioned; the login `products[]` list does not. Application Integration comes bundled with Integration Cloud; a Process Server in the list means the CAI runtime is provisioned.
evidence: 17-20 engines listed per agent on three orgs (2026-07-05 to 2026-09-24)

title: Data Quality runs inside the Data Integration Server
text: Enabling Data Quality adds no separate DQ app directory on the agent: the DQ runtime lives inside Data_Integration_Server (the DIS version bumps when DQ is enabled) with DQ libraries under `<DIS>/.../ICS/main/DQ`. Troubleshoot DQ runs through the DIS logs.
evidence: DQ libraries found under DIS; DIS version bumped on enablement (2026-06-27)

title: MDM SaaS runs in the cloud pod, not on the Secure Agent
text: No MDM engine exists on a Secure Agent: Business 360 and the 360 apps run in the pod behind `<pod>-mdm.<domain>`. Agent sizing and service selection do not affect MDM.
evidence: No MDM service in the engine lists of two agents (2026-07-06)

title: CLAIRE GPT 'Query the data' executes through a Secure Agent in the org
text: CLAIRE GPT's NL-to-SQL execution on a warehouse goes through the Data Gateway service of a runtime environment in that org (L-AGENT-097), so stopping that agent breaks the data prompts even when no data jobs remain on it; glossary, lineage and search prompts keep working. With the agent stopped, a 'Query the data' prompt answers: 'I couldn't execute the data query because the underlying data service connection is currently unavailable ... ensure the data gateway service is running.' Recovery: start the agent (if its systemd unit shows 'failed' because the graceful stop outran its timeout, run `systemctl reset-failed <unit>` and then `systemctl start <unit>`); the agent was READY within minutes and `IDMC_Data_Gateway_Service` RUNNING about 7 minutes after the start, after which the same prompt answered in 96 s. The gateway logs under `<agent_home>/apps/IDMC_Data_Gateway_Service/<ver>/log/system/log/` and holds long-lived :443 tunnels to the vendor cloud, so it opens no new connection per query and a new-connection sampler cannot show that it is in the path (L-METHOD-123). The gateway also parses the warehouse key more strictly than CDI (L-CONN-035). Keep that agent running until another runtime of the org runs the gateway.
evidence: Decision to keep an agent running (2026-09-29); gateway key failures (2026-09-25); agent stopped for about 10 minutes: the prompt failed with that message 4 minutes after the stop, the Data Gateway was RUNNING about 7 minutes after the restart and the re-test passed (chart and SQL returned, 96 s) (2026-09-29)

title: Size the host before enabling services; an over-subscribed agent OOM-kills its neighbours
text: Enabling every service put 23 engines on a 7.8 GiB / 4 vCPU host whose `-Xmx` values summed to about 9.2 GB: 27 OOM-kill events (co-located databases were killed), load 54 on 4 cores, engines flapping RUNNING/STOPPED, `<agent_home>` at 25 GB (19 GB of `downloads/`), root disk 79% -> 95%. Rotating connection-test errors on an undersized host are OOM churn, not configuration. Rules: sum the `-Xmx` of what you enable first; budget at least 16 GB RAM once Data Integration is on (inferred from heaps, not vendor guidance); keep about 20 GB free disk; add swap; cap the agent with a systemd slice (one 4 vCPU / 31 GiB host was given about 12 GiB and 2.5 CPUs); never co-locate a full engine set with production databases on a small host.
evidence: 27 OOM kills, load 54 (2026-07-26); OOM-driven rotating errors on another host (2026-09-12)

title: Memory cost of the agent and of the CAI Process Server
text: An idle, freshly registered agent uses about 1 GB RAM. The CAI process-engine adds about 1.8-2 GB (it ran with `-Xmx1536M`); check free memory before enabling it and watch for a first-start crash loop. For scale: an agent without CAI showed 8 base engines and a fully enabled one 17.
evidence: Measured on two agents (2026-07-01, 2026-07-04)

title: Agent JVMs can dominate a shared VM's load
text: On a VM shared with application and test workloads the agent's engine JVMs alone drove the load average to about 35, leaving no quiet window for deterministic test runs. Keep agent hosts separate from test and app hosts, or schedule heavy agent work away from measurement windows.
evidence: Load ~35 attributed to agent JVMs (2026-07-13)

title: The downloads folder is a re-fetchable installer cache: never clean it by name
text: `<agent_home>/downloads` holds 19-20 GB of installer packages that the agent re-fetches when needed. Its folder names do not map onto `apps/` service names, so a name-matched cleanup reclaimed only about 200 MB and risks deleting files under an in-flight install. Safe options: clear it entirely only when no engine is DEPLOYING, or move the packages the current appspecs do not reference into a hold folder and delete them after the first good run. Size the disk up front instead. Installed services run from those package folders, so a keep-newest prune put 14 of 20 services into ERROR and saved no space (L-AGENT-094). Was believed 2026-07-08 to 2026-09-28; overturned by L-AGENT-094.
evidence: 19 GB cleared on a full disk (2026-07-08); 200 MB from a name match (2026-07-26); 13.2 GB moved aside (2026-09-28)

title: Raise the DTM heap cloud-side (JVMOption1); a host pmrdtm.cfg edit lands in one DIS version directory only
text: For DTM OutOfMemory failures raise the heap, for example to `JVMOption1=-Xmx2048m`, and set it cloud-side as a DTM-type engine value through the agent.do form (L-AGENT-088): the cloud writes it into each new version's `pmrdtm.cfg`. A host edit of `<agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/<disVersion>/ICS/main/bin/rdtm/pmrdtm.cfg` (keep a `.bak`) changes only that version directory: after a few version rolls several `<disVersion>` directories coexist, the first one you find is not necessarily the one serving, and an edit made in a retired directory changed nothing while the mapping kept failing with Java heap OOM. Find the running version from the youngest DIS JVM's command line (`for p in $(pgrep -u <agentuser> java); do tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$p/cmdline | grep -oE 'apps/Data_Integration_Server/[0-9.]+'; done`) and check `JVMOption1` there. Any selections PUT (L-AGENT-042) or cloud configuration save can roll DIS again and leave a host edit behind. The heap is agent-wide, not settable per task. Health checks should read the youngest DIS JVM and alert when its heap or pool value differs from the intended one (L-AGENT-099), not on the version change itself.
evidence: OOM stopped and the affected tasks succeeded (2026-09-23); a host edit landed in the previous version directory while the next one ran and two sessions OOM'd; mirrored into the running version the same mapping ran solo OK (859 rows, parity 0/0); after the cloud-side save DIS rolled once more and the new version's pmrdtm.cfg carried the cloud-pushed JVMOption1 (2026-09-29)

title: More than about five BigQuery readers in one mapping exhaust a small agent's DTM heap
text: When consolidating loads into one mapping, keep BigQuery source readers per mapping at about five or fewer on a small agent (six worked once, seven to eight failed with GC-overhead / Java heap errors), or raise the DTM heap (L-AGENT-056). Select only the needed columns and give STRING fields a small reader precision (256; 4000 made the reader allocate huge row buffers).
evidence: OOM with more than 5 BigQuery readers (2026-09-29)

title: REST-triggered jobs can start on the agent's job-poll cadence
text: On one agent in August 2026, mapping tasks started over REST began on a roughly 3-minute job-poll cadence, so 15 serial tasks took about 45 minutes, and the activity log lagged the DIS statistics by minutes. September measurements on another agent showed about 20 s of fixed cost per task (DTM ~14 s plus ~5 s dispatch), so the cadence is agent- or configuration-dependent. A completion detector should also watch the target, not only the activity log.
evidence: ~45 min for 15 serial tasks (2026-08-20); ~20 s fixed cost per task (2026-09-28)

title: Debian 12: symlink libidn.so.11 to libidn.so.12 for pmdtm
text: Profiling and some DTM work run the native `pmdtm` (`<DIS>/.../ICS/main/bin/rdtm/`), whose `libpmcurl.so` links `libidn.so.11`; Debian 12 ships only `libidn.so.12`, so every profile dies at launch with 'error while loading shared libraries: libidn.so.11' and exit 127 (the same gap also showed as a DTM exit 134). Fix durably, three ways: a system symlink `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libidn.so.11 -> libidn.so.12` (survives reboots and agent re-syncs, which rewrite only the agent directory); a copy in a compat directory registered in `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/` plus `ldconfig`; and the compat directory on the agent's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in `agent_start.sh`. Verify with `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH ldd pmdtm`; `ldconfig -p` will not list the .11 name, which is fine. libidn 1.x is ABI-compatible across that SONAME bump.
evidence: 1,965 exit-127 failures before, 0 after; profiled columns 0 -> 671 in an hour (2026-06-28); DTM exit 134 cleared (2026-07-06)

title: EL8/EL9: install libxcrypt-compat and the EL7 libidn for pmdtm
text: On Rocky/RHEL 8-9 hosts or containers, CDI jobs can die before reading a row because `pmdtm` cannot load `libcrypt.so.1` (fix: `dnf install libxcrypt-compat`) and `libidn.so.11` (libidn v1 is in no EL8/EL9 repo: install `libidn-1.28-4.el7.x86_64.rpm` from vault.centos.org 7.9.2009 with `rpm -i --nodeps`). Verify with `ldd <agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/<ver>/ICS/main/bin/rdtm/pmdtm` showing no 'not found'. `pmdtm` is spawned per job, so no restart is needed. The load failure shows in `<agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/logs/tomcat/tomcat_<ver>.log`.
evidence: ldd clean; the next run succeeded 52/52 rows (2026-08-19)

title: pmdtm exit codes: 127 missing library, 134 SIGABRT, 137 OOM kill
text: Exit 127 means the native loader could not find a shared library; raising `-Xmx` or the DIS heap does nothing for it, run `ldd` on the binary. Exit 134 is SIGABRT (seen from the same missing library and from a preview connector build). Exit 137 is an OOM kill and leaves a heap trace.
evidence: 0 OutOfMemoryError among 1,965 exit-127 failures (2026-06-28)

title: AI Agent Runtime stuck DEPLOYING on Ubuntu 22.04: install unzip, libffi6, libreadline7 and libtinfo5
text: The AI Agent Runtime service sat in DEPLOYING because its `startup.sh` needs `unzip` and its bundled Python 3.13 needs `libffi.so.6` and `libreadline.so.7`, which Ubuntu 22.04 does not ship. Install `unzip`, `libffi6` (3.2.1-8), `libreadline7` (7.0-3) and `libtinfo5` side by side with the distro libraries (nothing is replaced); the runtime then boots. Undo: `apt-get remove libffi6 libreadline7 libtinfo5 unzip`.
evidence: Agent detail 20/20 services Up and Running after the install (2026-09-24)

title: Dangling plugin XML symlinks make every profile run die with 'DTM process terminated unexpectedly'
text: Profiling uses a Java transformation, and DIS parses every XML file in the rdtm plugin folders. When every profile run fails with 'Internal error. The DTM process terminated unexpectedly' while other mappings succeed, and the import log (`<agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/logs/s_profiling_*_import.log`) stops at 'Post validation on imported plug-ins... Error encountered while Parsing file', look for dangling `*.xml` symlinks in the rdtm plugin folders, rename them out of the way and restart the agent. The earlier theory that there were too many tables was wrong.
evidence: Import-log parse error located; the blocker was recorded as resolved (2026-09-04 to 2026-09-16)

title: A containerized agent registers under the container hostname
text: In a container, the agent registers in IDMC under the container's hostname. Set `hostname: <agent-name>` in docker-compose to control the visible agent name; otherwise the container id becomes the name. A hostname left over from another project keeps that identity in the org.
evidence: docker inspect hostname matched the agent name in the org (2026-09-08)

title: Libraries installed into a running agent container are lost on recreate
text: Packages installed with dnf/rpm inside a running agent container live on its writable layer and vanish on `docker compose down -v` or any recreate; the agent volume usually persists only the agent home (for example `/home/infa/infaagent`), not `/usr/lib64`. `docker restart` keeps them, so restart but never recreate such a container, and make the fix durable in the Dockerfile (dnf packages in the install list; offline RPMs such as the EL7 libidn copied into the build context and installed with `rpm -ivh --nodeps`).
evidence: Volume mounted only the agent home (2026-08-19); session rule (2026-09-03)

title: Agent state is large and lives outside application backups
text: A long-lived agent home (for example `/home/infa/infaagent/`) can hold about 27 GB, including Metadata_Platform_Service with several JVMs on ports in the 14xxx range. When the agent runs in a container on a named volume, that volume exists only on the OS disk (and its snapshots), not in application-level archives, so deleting the VM destroys the agent registration and state. Check `docker volume ls` and volume sizes before any teardown.
evidence: 27 GB volume found only in an OS-disk snapshot (2026-09-08)

title: Native agents are invisible to docker ps; find them before deleting a host
text: A natively installed agent does not appear in container lists. When inventorying a host, look for `/home/*/infaagent/` directories and Java processes named Data_Integration_Server or Metadata_Platform_Service, or ports in the 14xxx range. Agents can share a host with other integration runtimes (for example Apache Camel JBang). Deleting the host takes the agent down for good and every task bound to its runtime environment fails; a deletion-impact analysis said the agent would be de-registered from the org (inferred, not observed). Relocate or document the agent first.
evidence: Process lists on two hosts; deletion-impact analysis (2026-09-07)

title: Prove which host runs the agent before deleting one of several VMs
text: Match `InfaAgent.Id` in `<agent_home>/apps/agentcore/conf/infaagent.ini` (which also holds `MasterUrl=https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com` and the org id) with the agent id in IDMC, confirm the agent's Java processes, and check that the hosts in the org's connections match that VM's network. Deleting the wrong VM breaks every connection and task bound to that runtime. Newer evidence: L-METHOD-154.
evidence: Agent id and connection-host match before a VM deletion (2026-07-06)

title: Where the agent keeps its state, configuration and logs
text: Under `<agent_home>` (default `~/infaagent` of the install user): `apps/agentcore/` (`infaagent`, `agent_start.sh`, `consoleAgentManager.sh`, `conf/infaagent.ini`, `agentcore.log` with 'Service Status Distribution ... Deploying: N Running: N Stop: N Restart: N' lines); `apps/<Service>/<version>/` per engine; `downloads/` (installer cache); `ext/connectors/thirdparty/` and `ext/deploy_to_main/` (hand-staged drivers); `apps/Data_Integration_Server/logs/tomcat/tomcat_<ver>.log` (connection-test errors) and `apps/Data_Integration_Server/logs/s_mtt_<taskId>_<n>.log` (one session log per task run); `apps/Database_Ingestion/logs/tasks/*_<jobId>-CDC_COMBINED-*.log`; `apps/process-engine/` (Process Server). In containers without `ss`/`netstat`, poll agentcore.log for RUNNING states.
evidence: Paths used on four agents (2026-06-27 to 2026-09-29)

title: Verify that the Process Server really runs, not just that it is enabled
text: Application Integration showing `enabled:true` in the selections does not mean the Process Server serves. On the agent host, `https://localhost:7443/process-engine/status` (or `:7080`) must return 200 (body `2` = healthy) and `/process-engine/rt` 401 (alive and auth-gated), and `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` must show process-engine RUNNING/RUNNING. A restart loop shows as repeated RESTARTING events in agentcore.log. A 404 from the cloud host root says nothing about the Process Server.
evidence: Status 404 before and 200 after a repair; 355 RESTARTING events seen during the loop (2026-09-23/24)

title: The Process Server's embedded Postgres port 5432 is hardcoded and collides with any local Postgres
text: Every process-engine script uses port 5432 and `server_status.sh` is only `pg_isready -p 5432`. If any other Postgres listens on 5432 on the agent host, each start logs a false 'PostgreSQL database has started'; `prepareDB.sh` then runs `db_init.sh` against the wrong database, fails, and deletes the embedded data directory, so the deploy never completes. Check for a port collision before enabling Application Integration on a shared host.
evidence: Empty embedded data directory, no Postgres process despite the 'started' line (2026-09-24)

title: Process Server deploy.sh deletes the Tomcat context descriptor when conf/Catalina/localhost exists
text: `deploy.sh` runs `[ -d conf/Catalina/localhost ] || mv host.name localhost` and then `rm -rf host.name`. If an empty `localhost/` directory already exists, the context descriptor `process-engine.xml` (allowLinking plus `jdbc/ProcessEngine`) is deleted instead of moved; Tomcat then refuses the symlinked `WEB-INF/web.xml`, the webapp deploys empty in about 37 ms and every request, `/process-engine/status` included, returns 404. Also confirm `conf/ae.keystore` and `ae.cacerts` exist under `apps/process-engine/conf` (copy them from `<peVersion>/conf/certs`), or port 7443 never binds.
evidence: Empty webapp deploy; 7443 bound after the keystore copy (2026-09-23/24)

title: Repair a restart-looping Process Server, then guard its port after every upgrade
text: 1) Back up `apps/process-engine` bin, conf and data. 2) Change `localhost:5432/activevos` to a free port (for example 5433) in `<peVersion>/bin/*.sh` and in the context descriptor. 3) In the embedded Postgres `user.conf` set that port and `listen_addresses='localhost'` (not '*'). 4) Stop the looping Tomcat and re-run Informatica's own `deploy.sh` with the LCM environment captured from the live process (schema created, Liquibase updates, exit 0). 5) Restore `conf/Catalina/localhost/process-engine.xml` from the backup. 6) Verify status 200 and agent details RUNNING. An auto-upgrade ships a new version directory with the 5432 scripts again, so run a root cron port guard (for example every 10 min) that re-applies the port.
evidence: Status 200 and Process Server RUNNING/RUNNING for the first time since install; stayed up afterwards (2026-09-24 to 2026-09-26)

title: A stopped Process Server whose binaries are on the host can be started on the host
text: In July there was no REST call to start an agent service, but when a service's engine binaries were already on the host, the installed-but-stopped Process Server could be started from the agent host itself (or toggled in the Administrator console). Verify by its listening ports (7080 and 7443) and the status URL (L-AGENT-070).
evidence: 7080 and 7443 LISTENING after the start (2026-07-05)

title: DIS in ERROR with subState 303 fails every connection test
text: If Data_Integration_Server shows ERROR with `subState` 303 (its Tomcat listens but the control plane sees it down), every connection test on that agent fails. Restart the agent detached (L-AGENT-012), confirm all engines RUNNING with DIS `subState` 0, then re-test one connection.
evidence: After restart 8 engines RUNNING, DIS subState 0, JDBC test 200 (2026-06-27)

title: 'No running service ... of type Data_Integration_Server' (also PROFILE_SVC_00014) means the DIS engine is missing or down
text: If every connection test on one runtime environment fails with 'No running service found of type Data_Integration_Server <ver>.* service for AgentGroup: <reId>' (often inside 403 APP_105060), DIS is not selected, still deploying, or down on that agent. The connection definitions are fine. Select the service or restart the agent before touching individual connections; a changing engine name in the message is deployment progress. Profiling shows the same condition as `PROFILE_SVC_00014` 'No running service found of type Data_Integration_Server' on profile create or run. Engines left in ERROR after a memory thrash (profiling DTMs filling a capped cgroup, L-DQ-098) did not recover by themselves: Data_Integration_Server, Common_Integration_Components, Connector_Service and MassIngestionRuntime stayed in ERROR for about two hours until one restart of the agent's unit (`systemctl restart <agent-unit>`) brought every engine back to RUNNING in about 8 minutes. Poll `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` until every engine you need reads RUNNING, and remove the cause first (stop or shrink the profiling run, free memory) or the engines fall over again.
evidence: All connections on two runtime environments failed until DIS came back (2026-07-08); three connections before DI was selected (2026-07-26); engines in ERROR about two hours until a unit restart, all RUNNING about 8 min later, profile create failing with PROFILE_SVC_00014 before and a profile COMPLETED after (2026-10-03)

title: An agent in a lifecycle restart loop is fully down in each trough
text: A runtime environment can enter a recurring lifecycle (LCM) crash/restart loop: hundreds of restart events a day, agentcore doing USER_REQUEST shutdowns, and troughs of about 5 minutes in which the agent reads `active=False` and all engines STOPPED before `agent_start.sh` brings it back. Scheduled runs that land in a trough fail. Look at 'Service Status Distribution' lines in agentcore.log and the restart count before trusting a single health read.
evidence: 462 restart events in one day with ~5 min troughs (2026-07-05)

title: Secure Agent registration needs the UI
text: Registration (install token plus register) was believed to need the Administrator UI, and an August note still listed agent registration as UI- or clone-driven. Installer info over v2 plus `consoleAgentManager.sh configureToken` registered agents headless on three orgs. Was believed until 2026-07-01 (restated in an August note); overturned by L-AGENT-002.
evidence: Contradicted by headless installs 2026-07-01, 2026-07-25, 2026-09-28

title: Secure Agent services and connectors can only be enabled in the Administrator UI
text: Because `POST /api/v2/agent/service`, `selectiveservices` and `POST /api/v2/agent` with `agentEngines[]` all failed or were silent no-ops, service and connector enablement was treated as a UI-only toggle ('the API is a silent no-op'). The runtime-environment selections GET/PUT with `IDS-SESSION-ID` does it headless. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-AGENT-039.
evidence: Overturned by a proven PUT with read-back (2026-09-28)

title: Enabling a connector adapter on an agent has no REST verb, and jar copies do not work
text: Mid-September, connector adapters (for example BigQuery V2 and flat file) were believed enable-able only in Administrator. The managed MCP `secureagentmanagement` enabled connectors the same day, a CSVFile connection worked headless the next day, and the selections PUT made connector selection fully headless on 2026-09-28. The part that stays true: copying adapter jars into the agent does not enable a connector (L-CONN-020). Was believed 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-23; overturned by L-AGENT-039.
evidence: MCP enumeration 2026-09-23; CSVFile test green 2026-09-24; selections PUT 2026-09-28

title: No PUT is proven anywhere in IDMC
text: The July corpus held that PUT was effectively absent (update by POST to the id everywhere). `PUT /runtime/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>/selections/ui` is a proven write; documented PUT/PATCH elsewhere remain unproven until probed. Was believed July 2026; overturned by L-AGENT-039.
evidence: Overturned 2026-09-28

title: readyToRun:false on the runtime-environment list means IDMC never marked the agent runnable
text: A `readyToRun: false` from `GET /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment` was read as a layer-2 failure (IDMC sending no packages). The per-agent read said true and the host agreed; the real gap was that no service was assigned. Was believed 2026-07-26 (same day); overturned by L-AGENT-021.
evidence: Per-agent read 3/3 true (2026-07-26)

title: An engine reading RUNNING is usable, so the connection test should pass
text: `agentEngineStatus.status == RUNNING` was treated as proof the engine could serve work. RUNNING is a deployment signal only; the router refused while the API said RUNNING. Was believed until 2026-07-26; overturned by L-AGENT-023.
evidence: RUNNING vs router refusal (2026-07-26)

title: Enabling agent services is free and safe
text: Enabling services was treated as harmless because the agent just pulls whatever it is offered. Every service downloads a package and starts JVMs; nobody had costed the host. Was believed until 2026-07-26; overturned by L-AGENT-052.
evidence: OOM and disk incident (2026-07-26)

title: 403 APP_13401 / 500 CMN_001 on /api/v2/agent/service prove no enablement plane exists
text: The error codes were read as proof that no REST enablement plane existed. Bogus twins return them identically; they prove nothing. Was believed until 2026-07-26; overturned by L-AGENT-031.
evidence: Bogus-twin control (2026-07-26)

title: CAI is not activatable: the agent has no Process Server runtime
text: A CAI capability was declared unavailable because no Process Server runtime seemed present. The agent detail listed Process Server among its engines; Application Integration comes bundled with Integration Cloud. Was believed 2026-09-21 (hours); overturned by L-AGENT-048.
evidence: agentEngines listed Process Server (2026-09-21)

title: The BigQuery V2 403 APP_105060 and the PostgreSQL 'connector not registered' errors are permanent walls
text: Adapter errors on one agent were declared permanent runtime walls. After the agent was re-provisioned on a newer core, all four affected connections tested green. Was believed 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-AGENT-045.
evidence: 4/4 tests green (2026-09-23)

title: Edit an agent's System/Custom Configuration headless through the legacy agent.do form
text: There is no REST verb for agent engine configuration. The Administrator shell iframes the legacy Struts form `GET <pod>.<domain>/runtime/app/agent.do?actionMethod=displayUpdate&iframeWorkspaceId=SecureAgentDetailsWS&id=<agentId>`; driven with UI session cookies, it returns one `AgentForm` (~1,550 fields: parallel `engineConfigKey`/`Value`/`Default`/`Overriden` arrays plus `customConfig*` rows) and a `csrfToken`. Change a value (set `engineConfigOverriden=true`) or add a Custom Configuration row (`customConfigEngine=Data_Integration_Server<major.minor>`, `customConfigTypeEngine=TOMCAT_CFG` or `PMRDTM_CFG`, `customConfigSubType=-1`, `customConfigName`, `customConfigValue`; for example `maxDTMProcesses`, L-AGENT-099). Then POST the whole form as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` with `actionMethod=update` and the `csrfToken`, and read back by re-GETting `displayUpdate`. The cloud pushes the value into `tomcat.cfg`/`pmrdtm.cfg` and restarts DIS about 1.5-2 min later, possibly rolling it to a pending newer build in the same step; unlike host `.cfg` edits it survives version rolls (L-AGENT-056). See [01 Secure Agent - Install, Run & Tune](<../02 - Secure Agent & Connections/01 Secure Agent - Install, Run & Tune.md>) §6.1. Newer evidence: L-AGENT-121.
evidence: A custom DIS Tomcat row plus a DTM JVM option were saved, read back, pushed by the cloud into `tomcat.cfg`/`pmrdtm.cfg`, and followed by an automatic DIS restart about 1.5 min later (2026-09-29)

title: The auth plane is a property of the host and path; never mix planes
text: IDMC serves roughly ten auth planes, each with its own host and header: v2 `icSessionId` on `<serverUrl>/api/v2/*`; v3 `INFA-SESSION-ID` on `/saas/public/core/v3/*`; `IDS-SESSION-ID` on the pod host's FRS, runtime-selection and licence services and on `<pod>-ing` and `<pod>-dqprofile`; the identity three-header set on `idmc-api.<domain>`, `cdgc-api.<domain>` and `<pod>-mdm`; `INFA-SESSION-ID` on `<pod>-cai`; no header on anonymous CAI. A credential on the wrong plane fails convincingly: a 200 carrying the identity-service login page, a misleading 404, or a 401. Choose the header from the host/path map, not from whichever login you happen to hold.
evidence: Plane table from about 360 live host/header/path combinations (2026-07-25); per-service route tests 2026-09-22 to 09-24; login HTML from FRS and selections routes sent INFA-SESSION-ID (2026-09-28)

title: Host map: log in at the domain host, then use the pod, per-pod service and shared domain hosts
text: Login and identity-service: `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com`. Platform: `https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com` with v2 under `/saas/api/v2`, v3 under `/saas/public/core/v3` and, without `/saas`, FRS (`/frs/...`), runtime selections (`/runtime/api/v2/...`) and the licence service (`/license-service/api/v1/...`). Per-pod services: `<pod>-cai` (CAI), `<pod>-mdm` (MDM runtime, no `/saas`), `<pod>-ing` (Database Ingestion), `<pod>-dqprofile` (profiling), `<pod>-dqcloud-api` (CDQ dictionaries). Shared: `idmc-api.<domain>` (CDGC `data360`, Marketplace, MDM control), `cdgc-api.<domain>` (CDGC write plane), `hdm.<domain>` (MCP asset management), `mcp.<domain>` (managed MCP servers). A route sent to the wrong host 404s, which is not a capability signal.
evidence: 200s per host with the matching header on pods under two domain labels, 2026-07-06 to 2026-09-29

title: Derive service hosts from the login's base URL; a pod-literal string replace breaks after an org move
text: Take the base from `products[].baseApiUrl` (v3 login) or `serverUrl` (v2 login) and build service hosts by splitting the host at the first dot: `<pod>` + `-cai`, `-mdm`, `-ing`, `-dqprofile` or `-dqcloud-api` + `.<rest>` (drop `/saas` for `-mdm` and for the pod-host services). Builders that computed the CAI host with `serverUrl.replace("<pod1>.<dom1>", "<pod1>-cai.<dom1>")` silently kept calling the pod host once the org lived on another pod, and hard-coded service hosts needed the same review at the move.
evidence: Code review after an org move (2026-09-28): several builders still targeted the old pod's CAI host; the helper that split the host at the first dot was correct

title: The domain label is one character and not guessable; the wrong label gives 404, IDS_085 or a foreign-org 401
text: Pods sit under domain labels such as `dm-us`, `dmp-us`, `dm-em`, `dm-ap`, `dm-na` and `dm-uk`; some North American orgs are on `dmp-us`, not `dm-us`. Read the label off `products[].baseApiUrl` instead of guessing it from the pod name. A URL borrowed from an org on the other label returns 404 on the platform plane, `400 IDS_085` at login, and a clean 401 on the other domain's `cdgc-api` host (the route is real; the token belongs to another org).
evidence: Every borrowed URL 404'd between two orgs and the other domain's cdgc-api answered 401 to a foreign-org token (2026-07-26); valid credentials gave 400 IDS_085 at the other label (2026-09-22)

title: Log in at the domain host; send authenticated platform calls to the pod host
text: All three logins go to `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com`: `POST /saas/public/core/v3/login`, `POST /ma/api/v2/user/login` and `POST /identity-service/api/v1/Login`. Every authenticated v2 and v3 call then goes to the pod base returned in `baseApiUrl` or `serverUrl`. The entry host answered the login but returned 404 on `/public/core/v3/objects`, and the pod host returned 404 for the login path on one pod.
evidence: v3 objects 200 on the pod host and 404 on the entry host; login 404 on the pod host (2026-09-21/22)

title: A zero-byte 200 is gateway prefix routing, not success
text: A 200 with `Content-Length: 0` and no Content-Type means the gateway routed the path prefix and nothing served it; a bogus sibling such as `/data360/search/api/v99/bogusZZZ` answered identically. It was seen on every `data360` path of one pod while CDGC was licensed there, both with the three identity headers and with Bearer alone. Assert on body shape and Content-Type, never on status alone, and treat the case as a deployment question, not an entitlement ticket.
evidence: Real and bogus data360 paths both 200 with 0 bytes; header variants identical (2026-07-26)

title: A 200 carrying the identity-service login page means wrong plane, wrong header or an expired session
text: Some gateways answer an unauthenticated or wrong-plane request with HTTP 200 and the identity-service login page (the SPA shell). It appeared on FRS and runtime-selection routes sent `INFA-SESSION-ID` instead of `IDS-SESSION-ID`, on `POST /api/v2/miTask`, on `<pod>.<domain>/saas/mftsaas/api/v1/`, on 6 of 26 Database Ingestion deploy probes, and on v2 calls made with a stale `icSessionId`. Treat any 200 whose body starts with `<` or whose Content-Type is HTML as a failure; a session helper should drop its cache and log in exactly once more.
evidence: 6 of 26 probe results were fake 200s (2026-09-22); login HTML from FRS/selections with INFA-SESSION-ID (2026-09-28); the HTML-200 re-login fix in a helper (2026-06-27)

title: Sweep the host family by DNS before believing a service-level 404
text: DNS lookups are free and need no auth. Resolve `<pod>-ing`, `-mdm`, `-cai`, `-dqcloud-api`, `-dqprofile`, `-apigw` and `-apim`, plus `idmc-api.<domain>` and `cdgc-api.<domain>`, and a deliberately bogus `<pod>-bogusZZZ` that must fail. On one `dmp-us` pod `-ing`, `-apigw`, `-apim`, `-mdm`, `-dqcloud-api`, `-dqprofile` and `-cai` resolved while `-dam`, `-prep`, `-dataprep`, `-clairegpt` and `-ai` did not. This check overturned a whole-product UI-only verdict: Database Ingestion paths 404 on the pod host because the service lives on `<pod>-ing`.
evidence: DNS results plus same-path A/B across hosts and bogus-twin controls (2026-07-26)

title: Unprefixed or reversed host forms have no DNS, and -apigw/-apim 503s carry no meaning
text: Service hosts are always `<pod>-<service>.<domain>`: `mdm.<domain>`, `apigw-pod.<domain>`, `<pod>-cdgc`, `<pod>-mdm-model`, `<pod>-b360` and `<pod>-cs` do not resolve. `<pod>-apigw` and `<pod>-apim` answer nginx 503 on every path, bogus ones included: a load balancer with no backend, so a 503 there proves neither presence nor absence of a route.
evidence: DNS failures; identical 503 on real and bogus paths (2026-07-26)

title: Route families mount per pod and per licensed engine, not per org
text: Probed the same week on a `dm-us` org and a `dmp-us` sub-org: `GET /api/v2/license`, `/api/v2/loginAudit`, `/api/v2/{dss,dtemplate,dmask,dreplicate,plan,fileListener}`, `/public/core/v3/runtimeEnvironments` (also with `?limit=1`) and `/public/core/v3/{agent,agentGroups,tags,licenses,orgs,permissions}` answered 200 on the first and 404 on the second, while `/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment` and `/api/v2/agent` answered on both. Prefer the v2 admin forms and never generalise a route inventory from one org.
evidence: Live A/B; runtimeEnvironments retested three ways (2026-07-26)

title: A result proven on one org or pod is not evidence for another
text: Route availability, accepted session types and error behaviour differ by pod, org and licensed engine; for example, one pod's profiling service rejected the v2 session that another pod's accepted. Re-probe every route in the org you are working in, store host, header, path, status and date with each verdict, and work in one org per session unless told otherwise. Newer evidence: L-METHOD-155.
evidence: Live A/B across two orgs (2026-07-25/26); profiling session difference between two pods (2026-09-28)

title: Read the kind of 404 before concluding anything; a 405 proves the route exists
text: A 404 with a text or JSON body means a wrong path, host or domain label: keep hunting. A Spring `No static resource` body means the service is deployed but has no handler at that path; an empty-body 404 after a host sweep means nothing serves the prefix; a typed product error such as `DBMI_TASK_WAS_NOT_FOUND` means a live handler missed a lookup. A 405 means the route exists without that verb, and even known-good collections 404 at their parent path (`.../v1/catalogsources` 200, `.../v1` 404). Confirm with a known-good sibling, the right host and a bogus twin before calling anything a wall.
evidence: 405 vs 404 contrast on data360 routes (2026-07-06); parent-path 404 beside a 200 collection (2026-07-04); typed error on the -ing host vs bare 404 on the pod host (2026-07-26)

title: Jobs, connections and runtime environments live on v2; v3 adds objects, users, licences and logs
text: The v2 plane (`<serverUrl>/api/v2/*`) carries job, activityLog, activityMonitor, mttask, workflow, schedule, connection, agent, runtimeEnvironment and org. The v3 plane (`/saas/public/core/v3/*`) carries objects, lookup, export and import, TagObjects, users, userGroups, roles, privileges, license, securityLog, and read-only activityLog and schedule lists. `GET /public/core/v3/jobs`, `/public/core/v3/connections` and `/public/core/v3/licenses` returned 404 on the org probed (`/public/core/v3/runtimeEnvironments` 404 there and 200 on another pod); `POST /api/v2/alerts` returned 200.

title: v2 and activity-log times are pod-local but labelled Z: use the *Utc fields
text: On the pods seen, v2 `createTime`/`startTime` and activity-log `startTime`/`endTime` were pod-local time (UTC-4) carrying a `Z` suffix. Use `startTimeUtc`/`endTimeUtc` from `GET /api/v2/activity/activityLog` to detect completion, and set schedules with both `startTime` (pod-local) and `startTimeUTC`; a fixed -4 h offset is only a fallback.
evidence: A job list looked 4 h stale after an org move until the *Utc fields were used; re-verified (2026-09-28)

title: Verb conventions differ by plane: POST-to-id on v2, POST-then-poll for jobs, empty-POST verb probes
text: On the v2 plane an update is a POST of the full object to `/api/v2/<resource>/<id>`; elsewhere the idiom is DELETE and re-POST, except where a PUT is proven. PATCH is meaningful mainly in MDM (`entity`, `entity-xref`) and the CDGC content API. Long operations are POST-to-start then GET-to-poll (export, import, metering, scans, CAI publish), and a GET on the starter returns 405 (for example `GET /saas/public/core/v3/export`). There is no HEAD or OPTIONS: probe a write verb with an empty POST (400, 415, 422 or a null-field 500 means the verb exists; 405 means it does not).
evidence: July route corpus and live empty-POST probes (2026-07-25/26)

title: PUT exists: the runtime-environment selections PUT is a proven write
text: The July 2026 route corpus counted PUT 0 and PATCH 0 proven. `PUT https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/runtime/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>/selections/ui` with `IDS-SESSION-ID` (GET the selections, edit the flags, PUT them back) changed an agent's services and connectors, and the same migration updated CDGC catalog sources with a multipart PUT and profiles with PUT. Treat every other documented PUT or PATCH as unproven until probed.
evidence: Selections PUT read back with the new services and connectors (2026-09-28)

title: MCP and CLAIRE hosts and the credentials they take
text: The managed-MCP registry and OAuth clients live on `https://hdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/a2e-mcp-asset-mgmt-svc/api/v1/{mcp-servers,oauth2clients}` with `IDS-SESSION-ID` set to a v3 session. Managed servers answered on `https://mcp.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/mcp-servers/public/<context>` with a Bearer token from `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/authz-service/oauth/token` (client credentials) or with an identity JWT (`client_id=idmc_api`) plus `IDS-SESSION-ID`; the April 2026 vendor guide shows `a2e-prod-<pod>-mcp.<domain>` and three methods (session id, JWT, OAuth). OAuth tokens default to 5 minutes (configurable 5 to 1,440). CLAIRE GPT runs on `claire-gpt.<domain>`, and the CLAIRE agent MCP at `<claire_api_url>/claire-orchestrator-ai-agent/api/v1/mcp` with an identity JWT.
evidence: 19 managed servers listed, an OAuth client created (201) and tool calls answered (2026-09-21/28); vendor MCP guide pp.12-18 (April 2026); CLAIRE GPT chat 201 in the UI (2026-07-09)

title: v3 login returns the session, the 22-character org id and the pod base URL
text: `POST https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas/public/core/v3/login`, `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{"username":"<user>","password":"<pw>"}` returns 200 with `userInfo.sessionId`, `userInfo.id`, `userInfo.name`, `userInfo.orgId` (the 22-character `<orgIdV3>`), `userInfo.orgName` and `products[].baseApiUrl` (`https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas`). Send the session as `INFA-SESSION-ID` on `/public/core/v3/*` and on `<pod>-cai`, and take the API base from `baseApiUrl`, never from a guessed pod. Use this v3 session where a plane rejects the v2 id (the profiling service on some pods, the MCP asset-management service).
evidence: Used for every migration, CDGC, MCP and profiling call of a September org move (2026-09-28)

title: v2 login returns icSessionId and serverUrl; use serverUrl as the v2 base
text: `POST https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ma/api/v2/user/login`, `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{"@type":"login","username":"<user>","password":"<pw>"}` returns `icSessionId`, `serverUrl` (the pod base ending in `/saas`), `orgId` (the 6-character `<orgIdV2>`) and `orgName`. Call `<serverUrl>/api/v2/...` with header `icSessionId`, and use `serverUrl` as the base instead of assuming a pod.
evidence: 200 on two orgs (2026-07-25); every v2 call of the September tooling (2026-09-28)

title: One session value worked on both v2 and v3; the header name is what is plane-specific
text: In September 2026 the v2 `icSessionId` was accepted on `/public/core/v3/*` as `INFA-SESSION-ID`, and the v3 `userInfo.sessionId` was accepted on `/api/v2/*` as `icSessionId`, on pods under both domain labels; wrappers ran every v2 and v3 call on a single v2 login. The July rule "a v3 token on a v2 endpoint gives a 200 HTML page or a 404" was observed on an org where JWT-on-login made the v3 sessionId a JWT, which is probably what v2 rejected (inference; not re-tested). Keep the header name per plane; the opaque session value can be shared.
evidence: v2 calls 200 with the v3 sessionId (2026-09-21); all wrapper calls on one v2 login (2026-09-28)

title: Identity-service Login returns sessionId and orgId; CurrentUserInfo and Orgs read the identity
text: `POST https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/api/v1/Login`, `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{"username":"<user>","password":"<pw>"}` returns `sessionId` and `orgId` (vendor-documented; a SAML variant exists). In July 2026 the same response carried roles, `effectivePrivileges` and `feature.<cap>.*` flags, the entitlement ground truth. `GET .../identity-service/api/v1/CurrentUserInfo` and `GET .../identity-service/api/v1/Orgs` returned 200 with the current identity and the org list.
evidence: 200 live (2026-07-25); vendor Address Verification API guide

title: Mint a JWT at identity-service jwt/Token with IDS-SESSION-ID and the USER_SESSION cookie
text: `POST https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/api/v1/jwt/Token?client_id=<client>&nonce=<random>` (field scripts also append `&access_code=`) with headers `IDS-SESSION-ID: <sid>` and `Cookie: USER_SESSION=<sid>` and an empty body returns `jwt_token`, about 1,700 to 2,200 characters. A `GET` with the same query and `IDS-SESSION-ID` also minted (the CLAIRE and MCP shims). `<sid>` was the identity-service `sessionId` (documented) or the v3 login `sessionId` (proven); use a fresh nonce per request.
evidence: Catalog search returned 5,089 assets with the minted JWT (2026-09-24); JWT lengths 2,138-2,180 (2026-09-28)

title: client_id=idmc_api and client_id=cdlg_app are both in use; each is recorded only where it worked
text: `client_id=idmc_api` is the vendor-documented value and worked for the managed MCP servers and the hosted Data Quality agent MCP; `client_id=cdlg_app` was used for CDGC (catalog-source management on `cdgc-api`, `data360` on `idmc-api`) and for MDM record search on `<pod>-mdm`. The CLAIRE agent MCP shim reads its `client_id` from configuration. Which services refuse the other value was never isolated, so copy the value recorded for the service you are calling.
evidence: MCP, CDGC and MDM calls answered with the respective JWTs (2026-09-21 to 09-29)

title: Send the three identity headers; Bearer alone gets 401 on writes
text: On `idmc-api.<domain>`, `cdgc-api.<domain>` and `<pod>-mdm.<domain>` send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, `IDS-SESSION-ID: <sid>` and `X-INFA-ORG-ID: <orgIdV3>`. Bearer alone gets 401 on writes (GETs tolerated it); a catalog scan with a missing header or an empty `capabilityNames` list gets 500 `Login sessionID is missing` from the ccgf-auth-pep guard. A generic helper that sent only the v3 session header got 401 on `data360` where the JWT path succeeded.
evidence: Bearer-only writes 401; scan 201 with all three headers; 401 vs 201 between two helpers (2026-06-28 to 2026-07-26)

title: FRS, runtime selections, the licence service and the -ing plane take the v2 session in IDS-SESSION-ID
text: `https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/frs/api/v1/...` (or `/frs/v1/...`), `/runtime/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>/selections/ui` and `/license-service/api/v1/...` take the v2 `icSessionId` in header `IDS-SESSION-ID`. Sent `INFA-SESSION-ID`, the FRS and selections routes return the login HTML with status 200, which a script can mistake for success.
