The Database Ingestion plane on `<pod>-ing` also worked with `IDS-SESSION-ID`; the helpers sent `IDS-SESSION-ID`, `INFA-SESSION-ID` and `icSessionId` together there, so the minimal header was not isolated.
evidence: FRS moves and deletes, selections GET/PUT, licence reads and DBMI calls worked with IDS-SESSION-ID; login HTML with INFA-SESSION-ID (2026-09-28)

title: The profiling service is scriptable, and on some pods it needs the v3 session
text: `https://<pod>-dqprofile.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/profiling-service/api/v1` answered to `IDS-SESSION-ID` from September 2026. On one pod it returned 401 "Exception encountered while processing JWT" to the v2 `icSessionId` and worked with the v3 login `sessionId` in the same header (8 of 8 profile jobs completed); another pod accepted the v2 id. Make the helper pick the session per org. This overturns the July reading that the profiling routes are SPA-session-only.
evidence: 401 with the v2 id and 8/8 COMPLETED with the v3 id (2026-09-28); headless profiles with IDS-SESSION-ID (2026-09-24)

title: The v2 session dies 30 minutes after grant regardless of activity
text: Treat the v2 `icSessionId`, and JWTs derived from a session, as absolute 30-minute credentials: store the grant time with the session and log in again when it is older than 24 to 25 minutes (1,500 s), before a long batch starts; on an API 401 drop the cache and log in exactly once more. The 30-minute idle figure is documented for MDM SaaS sessions, a different plane.
evidence: Sessions died at 30 minutes during a long migration although calls kept flowing (2026-09-28)

title: A JWT expires 30 minutes after it is granted; re-mint it from the cached session
text: The vendor documents that the access token expires 30 minutes after the initial grant and must be regenerated. Re-mint it from the cached session (about 0.5 s, no password) when it is older than about 25 minutes or on any 401, instead of logging in again. Sizing example: 98,115 sequential writes at about 10 per second take about 2.7 h, so a token minted once covers only about 18% of the run.
evidence: Vendor Address Verification API guide p.9; bulk-ingest design review (2026-08-03)

title: Cache the long-lived identity session and the 30-minute JWT separately; each server keeps its own session
text: A colleague's MCP fleet reports the identity-service session lasting about 8 hours and the JWT 30 minutes, with a JWT refresh from the cached identity session taking about 0.5 s and no credential prompt. Cache both on disk with the org id and base URL (for example one file per server and role): cold start about 6 to 8 s, warm start about 0 s. Each MCP or product server holds its own session, so a 401 from one server only means that server needs its own login. Not probed here.
evidence: Colleague architecture document v1.0 (2026-07-16); shim behaviour (2026-07-26)

title: Session cache that held: one 0600 file per org, grant time, 25-minute refresh, one retry on 401
text: Cache `{sid, serverUrl, orgId, t}` in a mode-0600 file per org and reuse it across every script and browser run; log in again when it is older than 1,500 s. Keep the v3 session in its own cache (also about 25 minutes) and the CDGC JWT for about 20 minutes, renewing on 401. Serialize logins with a file lock and re-check the cache after taking the lock, treat an HTML 200 as an expired session, and on an API 401 drop the cache and log in exactly once more. Wrappers that return `(status, body)` without raising need callers that check the status.
evidence: Stable across the September tooling and a full org migration (2026-09-28)

title: Share one cached session under a file lock rather than a fresh login per agent
text: Parallel agents sharing an unguarded session file overwrite or expire each other's session and produce confusing 401s. The fix that held is one shared cache per org, written under a file lock and re-checked after locking, not a fresh login per agent or per script: the extra logins are themselves a lockout risk.
evidence: 401s from overwritten caches (2026-06-27); a lock attributed to per-script login volume (2026-08-20); no lockouts across dozens of sessions with one shared cache (2026-09-24)

title: Switching the org's authentication type to JWT changes what the login returns; stage clients first
text: An org administrator can set the org's authentication type to JWT (recorded as Administrator > Authentication > Authentication Type in June 2026 and as Administrator > Settings > General settings > Authentication type in a September plan). With it on, the v3 login `userInfo.sessionId` was a JWT (it starts with `ey`, about 1,700 characters) that CDGC GETs accepted as Bearer. A vendor thread said managed MCP needs the org on JWT, and the plan expected session-ID clients (`INFA-SESSION-ID`, `icSessionId`) to break after the switch; neither claim was verified, and later MCP calls succeeded with OAuth-client tokens and identity JWTs without the org's mode being recorded. Before flipping, move clients behind an `AUTH_MODE=session|jwt` flag, pause schedulers, and keep the switch reversible.
evidence: The login sessionId began with ey and was accepted as Bearer (2026-06-27); switch plan only (2026-09-03)

title: Session-ID REST authentication is deprecated: JWT becomes the default after the October 2026 release, JWT values are capped at 2,000 characters, and some clients must not use it (documented)
text: The Data Integration What's New notices of April and July 2026 say that session-based REST authentication has been deprecated since the October 2025 release and will be dropped in a future release, and that session-based stays the default until JWT becomes the default 'sometime after the October 2026 release' (the April notice had said October 2026, so the date has slipped once). The org administrator chooses the REST authentication type in Administrator settings (L-AUTH-032). With JWT on, the browser UI switches by itself and REST calls still send the session header, but its value is a JWT with a fixed expiry set in Administrator, so scripts must re-authenticate on a timer and on a 401 instead of relying on a long-lived session. From the October 2026 release JWT values are limited to 2,000 characters and longer ones are truncated: a JWT session value of about 1,700 characters was observed (L-AUTH-032), so check token length in clients that add claims or wrap tokens. Do not enable JWT authentication where API Manager or the REST V2 Connector calls IDMC APIs; API Center and, since April 2026, B2B Gateway support it. A related credential change in the same notices: source-control access to Bitbucket needs a Bitbucket API token, because app passwords stopped working on 2026-06-09. Design every script for both modes now: auth behind a session|jwt switch, refresh on a timer and on 401.
evidence: Vendor What's New important notices of April 2026 and July 2026 (including the July 'Upcoming change' on the 2,000-character limit), read 2026-10-02; a ~1,700-character JWT session value observed live (2026-06-27); an org switched to JWT by default not yet observed

title: IDS_086 is the only lock code; IDS_085, UI_10000 and a 400 mean the credential or the host is wrong
text: `IDS_086` "User account is locked. Contact your organization administrator." (401 on the v3 login) means locked. `IDS_085` "User name or password is not valid" (400 on the v3 login) means a bad or placeholder password, a truncated user name, or valid credentials sent to the wrong login domain; the v2 login answers the same case with `403 UI_10000` and the identity-service Login with 400. Once a lock ages out, a wrong stored password flips the code from `IDS_086` to `IDS_085`.
evidence: IDS_086 until an admin unlock (2026-08-18/19, 2026-09-28); IDS_085 at the wrong domain (2026-09-22); v2 403 UI_10000, v3 400 and identity 400 for one rejected credential (2026-08-18); truncated user name (2026-09-20)

title: IDS_085 at the wrong login domain is not a lockout; check the host before the password
text: Before concluding that an account is locked or its password changed, check that the login host matches the org's domain: an org provisioned on `dmp-us` returned `400 IDS_085` when its valid credentials were posted to `dm-us` and 200 at its own domain, while its pod host returned 404 for the login path. Only `IDS_086` means locked, and retries against the wrong host still count toward a lockout.
evidence: Own domain 200, other domain 400 IDS_085, pod host 404 (2026-09-22)

title: Rejected logins from every session add up, and each attempt during a lock can restart it
text: Failed logins from different sessions and tools count against the same account: at least 6 rejections across 3 sessions locked one account. Each new attempt during the lock can reset the cooldown, and one careful retry more than 40 minutes later was still locked. Stop every automated login, schedule no retries, and plan on an unlock rather than on waiting.
evidence: At least 6 failures locked the account (2026-09-28); a single retry after 40 minutes still returned 401 IDS_086 (2026-08-19)

title: Unlock with an admin or a password reset, then make one confirmed attempt
text: An org admin can unlock the user (Administrator > Users > the user > Unlock); a password reset also unlocks, either through "Forgot your password?" at `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/home` or Reset password in Administrator. A second admin is needed when the locked user is the only admin; otherwise open an Informatica support case. The org's lockout policy (Administrator > Organization > Security) may auto-unlock after a window, but sources disagree on whether locks expire and one was still active after 40 minutes. After the unlock, confirm the password in a browser once, then let one session make one attempt.
evidence: Reset unlocked the account and the next single login returned 200 within a minute (2026-09-28)

title: One credential, one designated session, one attempt
text: When a password is pasted to several parallel sessions, name one session to try it once, and nobody retries after an `IDS_085`. Three sessions each trying the pasted candidates produced at least 6 failures and a lock; after the reset, one session logged in once, a second confirmed from the shared cache, and from then on only one session logged in to that org.
evidence: At least 6 failed logins from 3 sessions caused the lock; the single attempt after the reset returned 200 (2026-09-28)

title: Automation holding a stale password re-locks the account right after every unlock
text: Cron pollers, health checks and helper scripts that log in every few minutes with a stale stored password re-lock the account immediately after each unlock. Correct the password in every config the automation reads, pause or fix the pollers, then ask for one unlock; with the stored copies corrected the unlock holds. One source adds that a poller holding the correct password cannot cause a lock; a later report attributes a lock to login volume alone (L-AUTH-040), so keep login volume low either way.
evidence: IDS_086 persisted until the stored password was corrected and one unlock issued; the next v3 login worked (2026-08-18)

title: Login volume alone was blamed for one lock: reuse one cached session everywhere
text: Cache the session with its grant time and share it across every script and browser run instead of logging in per call or per script. One lock was attributed to login volume rather than to a bad password: every enumeration and probe script opened fresh v3 and v2 sessions, a 696-object inventory completed, and the lock tripped mid-session. Keep browser automation serial.
evidence: Lock mid-session after a 696-object inventory (2026-08-20)

title: Host-script lockout guard: file lock, re-check, and a block file keyed to the creds fingerprint
text: Serialize logins with `fcntl.flock` on a lock file and re-check the session cache after taking the lock, because another process may just have logged in. When the server rejects a login (any 4xx other than 429), write a block file holding the SHA-256 fingerprint of the creds file; while the fingerprint matches, every process refuses to log in ("fix the creds or delete the block file"). A 5xx or 429 does not block, and an API 401 triggers exactly one re-login. Test it against a mocked network: after a rejected login, 10 further attempts must make 0 network logins, and changing the creds file must lift the block.
evidence: Mocked-network tests 11/11 (2026-09-28)

title: A service that logs in on its own must back off for hours after an auth rejection
text: A scheduler that ticks every few seconds locks the account within a minute if it retries a rejected login. After a 4xx answer other than 429, block logins for hours (a 6-hour default, 21,600 s); after a network failure or 5xx, block for 60 s; show the block on the service's health endpoint and clear it on a good login. To retry sooner, fix the creds and recreate the service. Test it in a throwaway container with `--network none` against a fake login server.
evidence: 14/14 offline tests; 20 retries during a block made 0 network calls (2026-09-28)

title: Rotate a password by updating every stored copy, clearing the guard, and verifying with one login
text: After a human changes the password: prompt for it without echo; write it in place into every creds file (same inode, backups kept, mode 600); delete the lockout block file and the session caches; verify with exactly one login; only then restart the dependent services. Inventory the touchpoints first: host creds files, service env files, catalog sources that store the user's password (the CDI lineage source keeps a user and password in its options), and MCP OAuth clients created with that password; each must be updated or recreated, or it fails or re-locks the account.
evidence: Rotation script and a cutover report listing four touchpoints (2026-09-29)

title: A user lockout does not stop the Secure Agent, only work that needs a user session
text: The Secure Agent authenticates with its own agent token, so already-scheduled tasks keep running while the interactive user is locked; REST job triggers, exports and UI work are blocked. Keep login-independent work going during a lock.
evidence: Schedules kept running during a lock (2026-08-19)

title: Automate with a native IDMC user; SSO-only users and login-name mismatches fail native login
text: If a login keeps returning "User name or password is not valid", the IDMC login name may differ from the e-mail address, the password may be a placeholder, or the user may be SSO-federated with no IDMC-native password; native REST login then needs a native user or an API-only user. Confirm the exact login once in a browser before any scripted attempt, stop after the first failure, and run automation as a dedicated native automation user rather than a personal or SSO account.
evidence: One credential was rejected by the v2 login (403 UI_10000), the v3 login (400) and the identity Login (400); it was attributed to an SSO password, although the domain may also have been wrong (2026-08-18); a later case resolved by a reset (2026-09-28)

title: Establish org, pod and domain from the login before any other call
text: Before any IDMC work, derive the org in three calls and re-derive it every session instead of caching it: the v3 login (`userInfo.orgId`, `userInfo.orgName`, `userInfo.sessionId`, `products[].baseApiUrl`), `GET /api/v2/org` (the v2 id, `orgUUID`, parent and sub-orgs) and `GET /api/v2/agent` (an empty `[]` leaves entitlement unresolved, not absent). Record the org name, both id shapes, pod, domain label and base URL; guessing the pod was recorded as the most common way to lose an hour.
evidence: Live logins on two orgs (2026-07-25/26); the first milestone of an org migration (2026-09-28)

title: Prove which org the session is in with a live read before any destructive call
text: Before any delete or import, read the org live and compare it with the intended one: `GET /session-service/api/v1/session/User` returns `name` and `orgId` (its host was not recorded), and `GET /api/v2/org` returns `id` and `orgUUID`. Destructive scripts assert the expected id (`GET /api/v2/org` must return `id == <orgIdV2>`) before their first write and print a receipt line with user, org name, v2 id and pod. When someone asks mid-run which org is being changed, this read is the answer.
evidence: Cleanup receipts began with the live user/org/pod read (2026-09-28)

title: One org has two id shapes: 6 characters on v2, 22 characters on v3 and identity
text: The v2 plane reports a 6-character org id (`<orgIdV2>`) and prefixes every v2 object id with it, followed by a type code (`0B` connection, `08` agent, `25` runtime environment; `0Z` was seen on mapping tasks). The v3 and identity planes use a 22-character id (`<orgIdV3>`, returned as `orgUUID` by `/api/v2/org`). Both are correct for the same org. Use the 22-character form for `X-INFA-ORG-ID`, for CAI URN paths and the anonymous CAI tenant, and for licence lookups (`GET /public/core/v3/license/org/<id>` with the 6-character id returns `V3API_016`).
evidence: Read live from both planes (2026-07-26); V3API_016 with the 6-character id (2026-09-28)

title: GET /api/v2/org returns the v2 id, orgUUID, parent and sub-orgs, but no job limit
text: `GET <serverUrl>/api/v2/org` with header `icSessionId` returns the v2 org id, name, `orgUUID`, parent, `subOrgs` and `subOrgLimit`, plus fields such as `maxLogRows` and `restApiSessionLimit`; it does not expose the monthly job limit. From a sub-org user, `GET /api/v2/org/<id>` returned `403 REPO_10404`, and `GET /public/core/v3/orgs/<id>` returned 404 on another org.

title: Sub-org membership is explicit per user and org switching is an admin action
text: If a login lands in a different org than the one you were asked to work in, stop: every documented org-switch path returned 404, so reaching another org is an admin action, not something to route around. A parent-org admin could not read a child org's agents (`403 APP_13407`), and a sub-org user could not read `/api/v2/org/<id>` (`403 REPO_10404`).
evidence: Probes as a sub-org user and as the parent-org admin (2026-07-26)

title: Check the parent org before concluding that a sub-org lacks an entitlement
text: Sub-orgs can use capabilities allocated by the parent. One sub-org showed a single engine and no licence reads over REST while its parent ran 22 engines; enabling the services on the sub-org's own agent delivered all 22, an assignment rather than a purchase. Licence allocation to sub-orgs is a UI step (the parent's Administrator > Sub-Organizations > Licenses), a sub-org's runtime environments can be inherited from the parent and show zero agents, and trial or embedded sub-orgs were reported to accrue zero billed IPU while their jobs succeeded.
evidence: Parent listed 22 sub-orgs; the sub-org agent went from 1 to 22 engines (2026-07-26); 0 billed IPU on a sub-org whose runs succeeded (2026-07-04)

title: Do not bind a sub-org connection to the parent's shared runtime environment as a shortcut
text: A sub-org connection bound to the parent's shared runtime environment creates fine (200), and its test error changes from `APP_105060` to `error [error [null]]`, which reads as progress but is not: an unroutable bogus host returns the identical error, so the result proves no reachability. Install an agent in the sub-org instead.
evidence: Bogus-host control returned the identical error (2026-07-26)

title: Two runtime environments in one org share every org-scoped object; isolation needs a second org
text: Catalog configuration, glossary, classifications, DQ rules, the MDM model and roles are org-scoped, so two runtime environments in one org share them by construction and there is nothing to mirror. Only RE-bound or duplicated objects can drift: agent versions, connections per environment (often name-mapped) and the mapping-task set. True isolation between environments needs a second IDMC org, which is a purchase.
evidence: Parity checks between two environments in one org reported in_parity (2026-07-06)

title: One writer per org: only a lead session logs in to and imports into each org
text: When several Claude sessions work the same program, name one lead that alone logs in to each IDMC org and alone imports or publishes; other lanes work host-side, on application repointing, or read-only, and coordinate by messages and board LEASE comments (owner, since, expires) with heartbeats and DONE-with-evidence posts. Announce every import first and never delete while an import runs.
evidence: An org cutover finished with no lockout and no duplicate import, after a morning in which 3 sessions had tried the same login (2026-09-28)

title: Make the shared IDMC client org-aware when two orgs are in play
text: Give the shared client one switch (an environment variable such as `IDMC_ORG=source|target`, else a switch file, else a default), a creds file, a session cache and a login host per org, and default it to the new org after a cutover so reads of the old org need an explicit login at its own domain. Scripts pinned to one org assert the selected org before any call, and a migration library can make the source org read-only (any non-GET raises unless explicitly overridden; export POSTs allowed). Flipping a host to the other org is then one write plus remapped id files.
evidence: About 19 host files and the MCP clients flipped at cutover; org-aware wrapper tests 11/11 (2026-09-28)

title: An org that looked walled had full access; the real blocker was the missing Secure Agent
text: A login landed directly in the org with its full privilege set (876 privileges, 38 roles), and connection create and delete both succeeded; the only blocker was that the org had no Secure Agent. Before calling an org inaccessible, log in, read the privileges and try a free create and delete.
evidence: Login plus connection create/delete (2026-07-25)

title: Create a user with POST /public/core/v3/users: the key is name, groups are plain id strings
text: `POST https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas/public/core/v3/users` with header `INFA-SESSION-ID` and body `{"name":"<login>","firstName":"...","lastName":"...","email":"...","groups":["<groupId>"]}` returns 201. The identity key is `name` (`userName` returns `400 V3API_007`); `groups` is a list of plain id strings, not `[{"id":...}]` objects and not `userGroupIds`; the body needs at least one role or group (a name-only body returns `V3API_IDSError_033`). Read back with `GET /public/core/v3/users`.

title: DELETE /public/core/v3/users/{id} returns 204
text: `DELETE https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas/public/core/v3/users/<userId>` with header `INFA-SESSION-ID` returns 204 and removes the user; confirm with `GET /public/core/v3/users`. 29 users were removed this way in one org cleanup. Back up the user list first, and keep the system and service users (L-AUTH-061).
evidence: 204 plus read-back, 29 users removed (2026-09-28)

title: There is still no proven in-place user edit: change a user by delete and recreate
text: PUT and PATCH on the users collection returned 405 in July 2026, and PUT/PATCH on the item were recorded as 405 too; in-place edit remains unproven after the September DELETE finding. To change a field over REST, delete and recreate the user (the Admin UI can edit in place). Snapshot the users before any batch delete and test the recreate body on one seat first: a wrong body once stranded 27 seats, which were restored from the snapshot.
evidence: 405 on PUT and PATCH (2026-07-05, 2026-07-25); 27 seats stranded then restored (2026-07-05)

title: Create groups and bind roles with POST /public/core/v3/userGroups; roles are role-id strings and cost nothing
text: `POST /public/core/v3/userGroups` with body `{"name":"<group>","roles":["<roleId>", ...]}` returns 200. Roles are plain role-id strings, not `[{"id":...}]` and not `roleIds`; guessed shapes silently dropped the role bindings, so read back with `GET /public/core/v3/userGroups?limit=200`. DELETE works; PUT and PATCH are untested. Groups and role bindings consume no seats and no IPU; only user seats are licensed.
evidence: 200 live; guessed bodies silently dropped bindings (2026-07-04, 2026-07-25)

title: Never delete CAI_Anonymous_<orgIdV3> or the service users that live automation uses
text: Processes deployed with anonymous access run through the org's `CAI_Anonymous_<orgIdV3>` user; deleting it breaks every `/active-bpel/public/rt/<orgIdV3>/<process>` URL. Keep it, the automation user itself, and any service user that a live process, catalog scanner or OAuth client depends on (search the hosts for the user names first). Anonymous endpoints are open to anyone with the URL: acceptable for a demo, not for production writes.
evidence: Kept through a 29-user cleanup (2026-09-28)

title: Roles and privileges are readable over v3; the privilege list is the REST proxy for entitlement
text: `GET /public/core/v3/roles` (for example 59 roles: 35 system and 24 custom; items carry `id` and `roleName`) and `GET /public/core/v3/privileges` (for example 897 effective privileges) return 200. Grep the privileges for a product's prefix before answering whether it is licensed, for example `create.dbmi.task`, `feature.cdam.*`, `create.mcp.CatalogSourceConfiguration` or `metering.admin`.

title: Roles that let one login deliver CDI, CAI, CDQ, CDGC, CLAIRE, migration and MCP work
text: A login that drives CDI, CAI, CDQ, CDGC governance and CLAIRE needs the Admin, Designer, Governance Administrator and CLAIRE GPT User roles; export and import additionally need the migration (export/import) and object-admin role. Managed MCP servers need the MCP Server and Deployed MCP Server asset privileges and the Execute and View Managed MCP Servers feature privileges, which the vendor guide says Admin and Designer hold by default (Operator can run servers but cannot create or set permissions on composite ones). Check these first in a new org.
evidence: Runbook prerequisite (2026-09-24); vendor MCP guide chapter 3 (2026-07-25)

title: Persona users with no role bindings give no separation of duties
text: Creating persona users (engineers, operators, platform admins, governance, MDM) does nothing for separation of duties if they hold no roles while one admin account holds everything. Bind roles per persona, through groups, especially when development and production runtime environments share one org.
evidence: User and role audit (2026-07-06)

title: For about 1,000 users plan SAML SSO with SCIM group provisioning, not native accounts
text: A 1,000-user access model concluded that native IDMC accounts do not scale to that size and recommended SAML SSO plus SCIM group provisioning, with roles bound to groups (groups and bindings are free; seats are licensed). Design recommendation; not tested.
evidence: RBAC scale model (2026-07-04)

title: PUT /public/core/v3/users/{id}/addRoles exists, but a successful add was never observed
text: A helper read the user with `GET /public/core/v3/users?q=userName=="<login>"`, took role ids from `GET /public/core/v3/roles` and called `PUT /public/core/v3/users/<userId>/addRoles` with body `{"roles":["<roleId>"]}` and header `INFA-SESSION-ID`. The only recorded answer was the error "license status is not enabled" for the Monitor and Operator roles in a shared org, which shows the route is live; a successful add was never observed.
evidence: Helper code plus one recorded licence error (2026-09-24)

title: In a shared org some UI roles are licence-locked for the demo user
text: In a shared presales org the demo user saw "insufficient permissions" on Monitor > All Jobs, Data Integration > My Jobs, Monitor > Application Integration and the Application Integration Console, and adding the Monitor or Operator roles failed with "license status is not enabled": the org's licence, not the user's roles, is the limit. Demonstrate with Monitor > Running Jobs, the Operational Insights dashboards and applications that read the job APIs directly.
evidence: addRoles licence error and UI permission messages (2026-09-24)

title: 403 MigrationSvc_038 is a permission gate; for Add-On Bundle templates it can persist
text: `403 MigrationSvc_038` "User does not have required permissions" on `POST /public/core/v3/export` is a permission gate, not a missing route or entitlement: an empty-body POST returns 400 (the route is writable), and granting the migration (export/import) and object-admin role, about a one-minute Administrator change, turned the 403 into 200. For Add-On Bundle templates such as `dsst__copy_data_new_tgt` and `dlt__copy_data` the 403 persisted for a non-admin user in some orgs and not in others (disputed); bundle content is system content, so create mapping tasks over the template rather than exporting it.
evidence: 403 then 200 after the role grant (2026-07-05/06); bundle-template 403 on 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-29 but not on 2026-09-23

title: A CAI 403 on invoke is a per-process access list; other role gaps have their own signatures
text: A 403 when invoking a published CAI process comes from that process's allowed users and groups (grant the Service Consumer role on the process); broad org roles, including the migration and admin roles, did not fix it. Other signatures of a role gap rather than a missing route: the CAI scheduler answering 401 while process lists answer JSON; MDM search returning `403 Authorization Client Error`; a CDQ dictionary host returning 401 on one pod (also recorded as not mounted there).
evidence: 403 persisted after a broad role grant (2026-07-06); CAI scheduler 401 beside JSON process lists (2026-07-26)

title: The login products[] list is a licensing label, not the entitlement map
text: The v3 login `products[]` list can name only "Integration Cloud" while the org is entitled to CAI, Database Ingestion, CDGC, MDM, DAM, CDQ, CLAIRE GPT and hundreds of connector types. Read entitlement instead from the identity-service Login (roles, `effectivePrivileges`, `feature.<cap>.*` flags), the licence service `EffectiveLicenses()`, `agentEngines[]` per agent, the runtime-environment service selections, the managed MCP registry, the console app switcher, and whether a real create call validates.
evidence: 59 roles, 897 privileges and 88 feature flags with products listing Integration Cloud only (2026-07-09); selections enabled for CAI, DBMI and governance (2026-09-23); CDGC writes in such an org (2026-09-28)

title: Deployed engines, not a 404, decide what an org can run
text: Never infer entitlement from a 404 or from `products[]`. The ground truth for deployed capability is `GET <serverUrl>/api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` with `agentEngines[].agentEngineStatus.appname` on every agent (a fully enabled agent ran 17 engines, a base agent 8); earlier "not provisioned" verdicts for Database Ingestion, DAM, the CAI Process Server and API Manager came from wrong paths. With no agent installed, entitlement is unresolved, not disproven.
evidence: agentEngines[] listed DBMI, DAM and CAI engines running while the 404s were wrong paths (2026-07-05)

title: Read effective licences from the licence service; its limits read -1 and hide the job cap
text: `GET https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/license-service/api/v1/OrgLicenseAssignment('<orgIdV3>')/EffectiveLicenses()` with `IDS-SESSION-ID: <v2 icSessionId>` and `Accept: application/json` returns `active[]` (id, name) and `limits{}`. The console calls it, and it confirmed MDM and CLAIRE GPT entitlements that `products[]` omitted. Every limit read -1 (32 in one org, 76 in another), including in an org that had just hit a 10,000 jobs/month cap, so the job cap cannot be read here.
evidence: Readouts in two orgs (2026-09-28); the console's licence call confirmed MDM (2026-07-06)

title: v3 license/org needs the 22-character id; there is no licence inventory route on some orgs
text: `GET /public/core/v3/license/org/<orgIdV3>` returned per-org licence detail (200; trial licences came without names and `customLimits=[]`), while the 6-character id returned `V3API_016`. There was no licence inventory route on a sub-org: `/public/core/v3/licenses` returned `404 No static resource`, `/api/v2/license` 404 (200 on another org) and `/api/v2/org/<id>/license[s]` 404. Read the inventory in Administrator > Organization > Licenses, or for a sub-org in the parent's Sub-Organizations > Licenses.

title: Establish entitlement ground truth in six reads and classify each capability
text: (1) Identity-service Login: roles, `effectivePrivileges`, `feature.<cap>.*` flags. (2) `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` on every agent: engines and their status. (3) Runtime-environment selections: which services are enabled. (4) Licence service `EffectiveLicenses()`: active licences. (5) v3 object counts per type, as content only, because the `q=type==` filter is not validated. (6) A free create call that validates. Then classify each capability as HEADLESS (REST works), UI-ONLY (provisioned, no REST write) or PURCHASE (engine and privilege genuinely absent).
evidence: Procedure used to correct about 90 false licence escalations (2026-07-06) and re-applied in September orgs (2026-09-23/28)

title: Audit logs: v3 securityLog is canonical; the v2 audit resources vary by org
text: `GET /public/core/v3/securityLog?limit=N` (N from 100 to 1,000) is the canonical audit log (200). `GET /api/v2/loginAudit` answered only on a parent or standalone org (404 on a sub-org). `GET /api/v2/auditlog` is disputed: one table records 404 ("superseded by securityLog") and another records it live on both orgs probed; it also did not record a job-cap change.
evidence: Conflicting live records (2026-07-25/26); no cap-change entry (2026-09-28)

title: API coverage is uneven: write is weakest, catalog and MDM are richest
text: The public API surface is incomplete and write coverage is its weakest part: catalog and MDM expose richer APIs than integration, while Data Integration exposes mainly operational APIs (schedule, monitor, logs, status). Routes fall into three tiers (documented public, undocumented but used by the UI, gated), and REST coverage is wider than MCP. Mapping design over API or MCP is not a documented public capability; the design gap is worked around by cloning tasks and by package import (see the CDI headless routes).
evidence: consistent with this KB's API route corpus and probes (see 12 - Reference Library)

title: IDMC REST has no PUT or PATCH; update only by POST to the id
text: The July 2026 route corpus counted GET 82, POST 37, PUT 0, PATCH 0 and DELETE 5 proven, and concluded that updates are POSTs to the id or delete and re-POST. A proven PUT on runtime-environment selections broke the rule. Was believed 2026-07-25 to 2026-09-27; overturned by L-AUTH-016.
evidence: Route corpus count (2026-07-26)

title: Never send a v3 session to a v2 endpoint; always keep two separate sessions
text: July notes held that a v3 sessionId sent to a v2 endpoint returns a misleading 200 HTML page or a 404, so two logins and two caches are mandatory. September wrappers ran v2 and v3 on one session value; the July case probably involved a JWT-form sessionId. Was believed 2026-07-05 to 2026-09-20; overturned by L-AUTH-020.
evidence: July field notes (2026-07-05 to 07-08)

title: The Data Profiling routes are SPA-session-only and not scriptable
text: July records called the profiling service an SPA session plane whose `IDS-SESSION-ID` is injected by the browser (a plain `INFA-SESSION-ID` GET returned login HTML). September calls with `IDS-SESSION-ID` created, ran and polled profiles headless. Was believed 2026-07-09 to 2026-09-23; overturned by L-AUTH-026.
evidence: July route table and status decoder (2026-07-09 to 07-26)

title: The IDMC session is a 30-minute idle timeout, so a cached session stays valid while calls keep flowing
text: Session helpers cached `session.json` on the assumption of a 30-minute idle timeout and reused it while active. Long September runs showed the v2 session dies 30 minutes after grant regardless of activity. Was believed 2026-07-05 to 2026-09-27; overturned by L-AUTH-027.
evidence: July helper design (2026-07-05 to 07-08)

title: Parallel agents should each log in and mint their own token instead of sharing a cache
text: The June fix for 401s from an overwritten shared cache was a self-minted token per helper. Per-script logins later contributed to a lockout, and a shared cache under a file lock replaced the pattern. Was believed 2026-06-27 to 2026-08-19; overturned by L-AUTH-031.
evidence: 401s stopped after self-minting (2026-06-27)

title: Repeated IDS_085 at login means the account is locked or its password changed
text: A session read repeated `IDS_085` answers as a lockout or a rotated password. The same day a login at the org's own domain returned 200: the credentials had been posted to the wrong domain. Was believed 2026-09-22 (part of one session); overturned by L-AUTH-035.
evidence: Overturned the same day by a 200 at the correct domain (2026-09-22)

title: Access to the org is a hard wall that only the account owner can clear
text: A README recorded an org as blocked behind an access wall only the owner could clear. The next day a login landed in the org with full privileges and a connection create/delete succeeded. Was believed 2026-07-24; overturned by L-AUTH-056.
evidence: README entry (2026-07-24)

title: /public/core/v3/users/{id} rejects GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE with 405
text: The July corpus called this route "the canonical proof" of no in-place edit and prescribed delete and recreate through the collection, although its own admin table listed GET and DELETE as supported. DELETE on the item returned 204 in September; PUT and PATCH remain unproven. Was believed 2026-07-25 to 2026-09-27; overturned by L-AUTH-058.
evidence: July endpoint tables (2026-07-25)

title: The login products[] list decides entitlement
text: Orgs whose v3 login listed only "Integration Cloud" were declared unable to catalog, run CAI or use MDM, and about 90 items were escalated as licence purchases. Privileges, engines, selections and successful writes showed the capabilities were entitled. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-09-21; overturned by L-AUTH-070.
evidence: Repeated false licence verdicts (2026-07-04 to 2026-09-21)

title: Read and run are headless; publish, deploy and serve are UI-only
text: A July framing held that everything can be read and the data plane run over REST, but publish, deploy and serve have no REST verb. September evidence moved several lines (CAI publish, Database Ingestion deploy, runtime-selection PUT, clone- and package-authored design objects); MDM model deploy and some governance actions still stand. Use the framing only as a starting hypothesis. Was believed 2026-07-09 to 2026-09-27 (overturned in part); overturned by L-AUTH-016.
evidence: July assessment verified 2026-07-09, recorded 2026-07-13

title: A 404 on a REST probe means the capability is not provisioned
text: Early July probes concluded that Database Ingestion, DAM, CLAIRE, the CAI Process Server and API Manager were not provisioned because guessed routes returned 404. The deployed engine list showed them running; the 404s were wrong paths or hosts. Was believed until 2026-07-05; overturned by L-AUTH-071.
evidence: Early July probe verdicts (2026-07-04)

title: Publish CAI assets headless with POST /active-bpel/asset/v1/publish on the -cai host
text: `POST https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/asset/v1/publish` with headers `INFA-SESSION-ID: <v3 session>`, `Accept: application/vnd.api+json` and `Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json` and body `{"data":{"type":"publish","attributes":{"assetPaths":["Explore/<project>/<folder>/<name>.PROCESS.xml"]}}}` returns 202 with the publish job id in `data.id`. The same call publishes service connectors (`.AI_SERVICE_CONNECTOR.xml`), app connections (`.AI_CONNECTION.xml`) and guides (`.GUIDE.xml`), including assets that an import package created. It is a documented vendor resource (Invoke guide ch.3), not a bypass. Supersedes L-CAI-097 and L-CAI-098.
evidence: 202 plus job id and item state SUCCESS, then live invokes: 4 processes on 2026-07-09, a 9/9 migration wave on 2026-09-28

title: Poll a publish or unpublish job and read every item: items fail inside a 200
text: `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/asset/v1/publish/<id>/Status` (same headers; `/unpublish/<id>/Status` for unpublish jobs; `/publish/<id>` returns job information) gives `data.attributes.jobState` (NOT_STARTED, RUNNING, IN_PROGRESS or QUEUED while it works, then SUCCESS, WARNING or ERROR) and `itemDetail[]` with `itemState`, `itemStatusDetail` and `assetPath`. The 202 and the 200 envelopes only mean the job was accepted: an item with state NOT_FOUND turns the job into WARNING and any item ERROR makes it ERROR. Poll every 4-5 s for up to about 3 minutes and stop a sequence at the first job that is not SUCCESS or WARNING. `GET` on the `/publish` starter itself returns 405 by design.
evidence: Status read-backs on every publish in two orgs (2026-07-09 to 2026-09-28); job and item semantics per Invoke guide pp.31-33

title: The asset path must be Explore/<project>/<folder>/<name>.<TYPE>.xml; resolve it from the v3 catalog
text: An asset path such as `<project>/<folder>/<name>` ends the job ERROR with item BAD_REQUEST "Invalid asset path." although the asset exists. Send `Explore/` + the v3 object `path` + `.<TYPE>.xml`, where TYPE is PROCESS, GUIDE, AI_CONNECTION or AI_SERVICE_CONNECTOR. Resolve it with `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='<TYPE>'&limit=200`, match the last `path` segment to the asset name, and refuse to publish when zero or several objects match. A project name containing a space published fine. This, not a missing designer registration, was the cause of the September "Invalid asset path" wall. Supersedes L-CAI-100.
evidence: BAD_REQUEST before and SUCCESS after the path fix (2026-09-24); 9/9 assets resolved by name and type and published (2026-09-28)

title: The publish body's data must be a JSON object: an array returns 500 ClassCastException
text: Sending `{"data":[{...}]}` to `asset/v1/publish` returns HTTP 500 with a ClassCastException. Send `data` as a single object whose `attributes.assetPaths` is the array of paths.
evidence: 500 ClassCastException with an array, 202 with an object (2026-09-24)

title: Accept: application/json on the asset/v1 routes returns 500 NotAcceptable
text: The asset/v1 publish family needs both `Accept` and `Content-Type` set to `application/vnd.api+json`. With `Accept: application/json` the call returns 500 NotAcceptable, which looks like a server fault but is content negotiation.
evidence: 500 NotAcceptable versus 202 on the same body (first seen 2026-09-09, re-confirmed 2026-09-22)

title: Publish in dependency order and stop at the first failure
text: Publish the AI_SERVICE_CONNECTOR first, then the AI_CONNECTION that references it, then processes without connection references, then processes that call the connection. One call accepts at most 199 asset paths and processes them in payload order. The field scripts published one asset per call and stopped at the first job that was not SUCCESS or WARNING, which keeps the cause of a failure obvious.
evidence: 9/9 SUCCESS in dependency order (2026-09-28); 199 limit and payload order per Invoke guide p.30

title: Unpublish with asset/v1/unpublish, dependents first: process, then app connection, then service connector
text: `POST https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/asset/v1/unpublish` with the publish headers and `{"data":{"type":"unpublish","attributes":{"assetPaths":["Explore/<project>/<folder>/<name>.<TYPE>.xml"]}}}` returns a job id; poll `/active-bpel/asset/v1/unpublish/<id>/Status`. Unpublish processes first, then app connections, then service connectors: unpublishing an asset that something still depends on gives item ERROR "... must be unpublished first. Dependent entry(ies): <names>" and jobState ERROR inside a 200. Maximum 199 per call. Unpublish before renaming a process or its API name, changing Run On or Applies To, or deleting it. Supersedes L-CAI-102.
evidence: Status read-backs in two orgs, including 59 legacy assets in one cleanup (2026-09-28/29); dependent-entry error per Invoke guide p.33

title: Delete CAI assets through FRS, and only after unpublishing them
text: FRS refuses to delete an asset that is still published or out of date (`FRS_082`). After unpublishing, delete in bulk with `POST https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/frs/v1/DeleteEntities` and `{"artifactIds":["<frsGuid>", ...]}` (header `IDS-SESSION-ID`; per item `FRS_200` deleted, `FRS_082` still published, `FRS_087` project not empty) or one at a time with `DELETE .../frs/api/v1/BaseEntities('<frsGuid>')` (204). `DELETE .../frs/api/v1/Documents('<id>')` returns 403. Read each id back: `FRS_070` means not found.
evidence: 81 of 83 legacy CAI objects removed with FRS_070 read-backs (2026-09-28); one integration's processes removed from two orgs (2026-09-29)

title: List CAI assets with their publication status
text: `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/asset/v1/status?MimeType=<process|screenflow|connection>` lists assets of a MIME type with their publication status (published, unpublished, out-of-date); the Invoke guide also documents a `PublicationStatus=` filter. Use it to find assets edited after their last publish and to make a publish driver idempotent.
evidence: 200 live with the MimeType filter (2026-07-25); PublicationStatus filter documented, not exercised

title: Publishing is not API activation: activate and deactivate in the console
text: The first publish of a process activates its API. If the API is later deactivated on the Application Integration Console APIs page, republishing does not reactivate it, and no verb activates or deactivates an API at any path found. When a published process does not answer, check the API status in Properties Detail and treat activation as a console step.
evidence: Invoke guide p.8; no activation verb found in probes (2026-07-25) [doc]

title: The runtime can serve the previous version for about 20 s after a publish
text: Right after a publish ends SUCCESS, calls can still reach the old version for a few seconds (about 20 s observed). A verifier should retry (for example up to 12 times, 10 s apart) before it declares a redeploy failed, or it will roll back a good change.
evidence: redeploy verifications (2026-09-28)

title: Renames, moves and Run On changes: unpublish, change, republish; recreate rather than rename by import
text: A published process must be unpublished before its name, API name, Run On or Applies To can change, and then republished. A process moved to another folder is republished from its new Explore path. Import-based renames of published processes hung; recreating the connector, connection and processes under the new names, publishing them, switching callers, then unpublishing and deleting the old assets worked. Callers that still use an old name get 404 from the runtime until they are switched.
evidence: 9-asset rename (2026-09-26); folder moves re-verified live (2026-09-24); Design guide p.203, Invoke guide p.9

title: A designer first-publish regression (cpfPublish 500) was bypassed with the bulk publish REST
text: After a platform client build change, the Process Designer Publish button failed for never-published assets: `POST https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/activevos-central/<orgIdV3>/app/florence-design/services/JSON/cpfPublish` returned 500 (`publishErrorResponse`) for first publishes and 200 for republishes, the UI said "unexpected error when publishing", and assets stayed "Validation in progress..". `asset/v1/publish` still worked, so publish over REST and give Informatica support the asymmetry evidence and the client build stamp. Supersedes L-CAI-099.
evidence: 200 versus 500 on identical calls (2026-07-08); 4 processes published over REST (2026-07-09)

title: Prove a platform regression with a same-session asymmetry test
text: To show that a failure is server-side, make the identical call with the same session and endpoint on a case that should work and on the failing case (for example republish versus first publish). A deterministic split, plus the vendor UI failing the same way, is the evidence a support ticket needs.
evidence: decisive 200/500 split reproduced with raw backend calls (2026-07-08)

title: asset/v1/update changes access, Run On, tracing and connection secrets (documented, untested)
text: `PUT <baseApiUrl>/active-bpel/asset/v1/update?assetType=Process` with `Content-Type` and `Accept` `application/json` and `INFA-SESSION-ID`, body `{"processes":[{"guid":{"$t":"<guid>"},"deployment":[{"key":{"$t":"Run On"},"value":{"$t":"cloud server"}}]}]}`, updates Allowed Users/Groups or Allow anonymous access (one or the other), API Gateway authorization, Run On and Tracing Level (None, Terse, Normal, Verbose); success is `{"status":{"$t":"SUCCESS"}}`. With `assetType=AppConnection` it sets sensitive attribute values, after which the connection must be republished. Needs the Admin, Deployer, Designer or Operator role. Never exercised here, so the host (base URL or `-cai`) is unconfirmed.
evidence: documented only: Design guide pp.210-212 and 415-418 [doc]

title: Clone a process with its connection and connector through v3 export and import
text: `POST /public/core/v3/export` with `{"name":"<n>","objects":[{"id":"<objectId>","includeDependencies":true}]}`, poll `GET /public/core/v3/export/<id>`, then download `GET /public/core/v3/export/<id>/package`. The zip holds `<name>.PROCESS.xml`, `.AI_CONNECTION.xml` and `.AI_SERVICE_CONNECTOR.xml` under `Explore/<project>/<folder>/`. Edit, recompute the changed files' SHA-256 lines in `exportPackage.chksum`, upload with `POST /public/core/v3/import/package` (multipart field `package`), start with `POST /public/core/v3/import/<jobId>`, poll to SUCCESSFUL, then publish: the import publishes nothing. To reach a different REST provider, clone the app connection with a new base URL. Needs the migration (export/import) role. Supersedes L-CAI-101.
evidence: clone imports SUCCESSFUL with checksumValid true (2026-07-04 and 2026-09-22); clones published and served (2026-09-24)

title: Rename a cloned process: the elements and attributes to change
text: In the cloned PROCESS file change `<types1:EntryId>`, `<types1:Name>`, `<types1:GUID>` and `<types1:DisplayName>` in the repository item, the `displayName=` and `name=` attributes of `<process>`, `PublishedContributionId` (`project:/spi.<NAME>/<NAME>.pd.xml`), and any renamed output fields together with the `to=` bindings that write them. Recompute the hashes and import; the org mints its own object id for the new asset.
evidence: import SUCCESSFUL, checksumValid true, PROCESS count up by one (2026-09-22)

title: Change a live process safely: export, swap only the target XML, re-hash, import OVERWRITE, publish, verify, roll back
text: (1) Find the IDMC object id with `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='PROCESS'` and export that one object (`includeDependencies:false`); keep the zip as the undo. (2) Replace only what changes (the whole `<process ...>...</process>` element, or single `<operation to="...">` expressions) with whitespace-tolerant regexes, because the export is pretty-printed, and assert exactly one replacement each. (3) Recompute only the changed files' SHA-256 lines in `exportPackage.chksum` (upper-case hex; spaces in paths appear as `\ `). (4) Import with `defaultConflictResolution: OVERWRITE`, publish, run side-effect-free verification cases, and re-import the saved zip in the same run if any case fails. Add new inputs as optional parameters so existing callers keep working.
evidence: two live processes changed and verified 10/10 and 15/15 cases, one attempt auto-rolled back by the verifier (2026-09-28)

title: Exporting a process by the GUID inside its XML gives MigrationSvc_034
text: v3 export takes the IDMC object id from `/public/core/v3/objects`. The GUID written in the process XML can differ from it (an import can mint a new object id), and exporting by that GUID fails with `MigrationSvc_034` (object resolution failed).
evidence: MigrationSvc_034 with the XML GUID, SUCCESSFUL with the object id (2026-09-28)

title: Author CAI assets from scratch as repository-item XML inside a hand-built import package
text: Each asset is an `<aetgt:getResponse>` wrapping one `<types1:Item>` with Name, MimeType, Description, VersionLabel `1.0`, State `CURRENT`, Entry (the asset XML itself), GUID (22 random alphanumerics) and DisplayName. Package the files as `Explore/<project>/<folder>/<name>.<TYPE>.xml`, add the real `<folder>.Folder.json` and `<project>.Project.json` copied from any genuine export of an object in that folder, an `exportMetadata.v2.json` that lists the folder, the project and each asset (`objectGuid`, `objectName`, `objectType`, `path`, `metadata.objectRefs` = dependency GUIDs, `additionalInfo.documentState: VALID`), `exportPackage.chksum` and a contents CSV. Import with OVERWRITE and `includeObjects:[<guids>]`, then publish in dependency order. Persist the GUIDs so a rebuild overwrites the same assets. Supersedes L-CAI-100 and L-CAI-101.
evidence: connector, connection and seven processes imported SUCCESSFUL and published (2026-09-25); the same assets migrated and published in a second org (2026-09-28)

title: Copy MIME types from a genuine export: the service connector's is spelled businesssconnector
text: Repository-item MIME types: `application/xml+businesssconnector` (three s) for AI_SERVICE_CONNECTOR, `application/xml+connection` for AI_CONNECTION, `application/xml+process` for PROCESS. A mistyped MIME type is an easy way to break a hand-built package; copy the values from a genuine export.
evidence: imports SUCCESSFUL with these values (2026-09-25)

title: Process inputs must be <parameter> elements; a <field> in <input> fails publish with a bare 'Publish Error'
text: Declare process inputs as `<parameter name="..." type="string">` inside `<input>`; outputs and temp fields are `<field>` elements. A `<field>` inside `<input>` imports fine, but the publish item fails with only "Publish Error". Mark optional inputs with `<options><option name="required">false</option></options>`.
evidence: failure isolated by bisecting variant bodies (2026-09-24); optional inputs used in later changes (2026-09-28)

title: Service connector XML: otherParams before httpHeaders, a body on POST, a form-encoded token call
text: In a `restSimpleBinding`, `otherParams` must come before `httpHeaders`, and a POST action needs a `<body>`. Bodies can be literal templates such as `<body>{$payload}</body>` or generated (`<body generateUsing="JSON" .../>`). Send an OAuth client-credentials token request as a form-encoded body (`Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), not as query parameters, so the client secret never sits in a URL; in the working builder the `&` separators of that body were written as `&amp;` inside the Entry XML.
evidence: token calls and upserts succeeded after the change (2026-09-25)

title: Test XQuery offline, and write regex-bearing XQuery with a file tool, never a heredoc
text: Process logic is XQuery/XPath 3.0 inside `<expression language="XQuery">`; functions seen working include `normalize-space`, `concat`, `string-join`, `tokenize`, `matches`, `replace`, `castable as xs:decimal` and `util:generateUUID()`. Test expressions offline first (for example with the Python elementpath library) against a case table. Shell heredocs and inline scripts altered backslashes (`\b` became a 0x08 byte, `\p` and `\s` vanished), so write such code with a file-editing tool and scan for control bytes (`grep -P '\x08'`) before deploying.
evidence: a 0x08 byte caught before a deploy (2026-09-28)

title: The CAI-native design routes do not author anything: use an import package
text: `POST /active-bpel/asset/v1/processes` returns 500 on any body; `asset/v1/import`, `/deploy` and `/save` returned 500, `designtime/v1/processes` 403 and `services/deploy` 404; `POST /public/core/v3/objects` is 405 (the catalog is read-only). None of them creates a process, connector or connection. The headless authoring path is a v3 import package (clone or from scratch) followed by `asset/v1/publish`. File listeners and human tasks were only ever authored in the designer; Kafka and AMQP event sources, event-bound processes and fault handling are authored by package (L-CAI-116).

title: A published service connector has no endpoint of its own: wrap it in a process
text: Publishing a service connector makes it usable by processes, not callable over HTTP. To call it headless, build and publish a process that uses it; to check the connector on its own, use its Test action in the designer.
evidence: no endpoint after publish; the designer Test returned the expected rows (2026-09-10)

title: MCP tool connections do not survive a migration import
text: An Application Integration TOOL_CONNECTION (a connection to an external MCP server) failed to import with `MigrationSvc_031` "Internal error" in three jobs, even after the package was fixed with the live URL and bearer token. Recreate it in the Application Integration designer (MCP connection form) and attach it to its MCP server object; the MCP_SERVER object itself imported.
evidence: three failed import jobs (2026-09-28)

title: Clones in a shared org can land in another user's project: search by exact type and id before calling them lost
text: Processes authored by clone sat in the project of the user who owned the clone source, and audits that looked only in the expected folder, or used a wrong type name (which returns 0 rather than an error), reported them missing. Query `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='PROCESS'` without a folder filter, confirm by id, then move them.
evidence: 5 processes found in another user's project and moved with ids preserved (2026-09-24)

title: The modern CAI designer lives under /aiUI and needs a headed browser for automation
text: ActiveVOS Central is deprecated; the designer is `https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/aiUI/products/applicationIntegration/main/Explore`, a nested SPA that rendered blank headless with a saved storage state. For a UI fallback use a fresh login and a headed browser (xvfb on servers), dismiss the service-switcher modal first, work inside the frame whose URL contains `bpmui-cai-app`, and pick the exact "Publish" button (not "Publish to API Center"). Make any UI driver idempotent by checking the publication status over REST first.
evidence: blank headless render (2026-07-07); UI publish driver built and exercised (2026-07-09)

title: Invoke an anonymous process at /active-bpel/public/rt/<orgIdV3>/<process>
text: `POST https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/public/rt/<orgIdV3>/<ProcessApiName>` with `Content-Type: application/json`, a JSON body that matches the input parameters and no auth header returns the outputs as JSON. The tenant segment is the 22-character v3 org id. The process must be deployed with anonymous access (`<deployment><rest><allowAnonymousAccess/></rest></deployment>`, the designer's Allow anonymous access). Smoke-test each process with one valid and one invalid payload.
evidence: live calls answered in 270-730 ms (2026-09-24 to 2026-09-28); hundreds of real anonymous runs in July

title: Invoke an authenticated process at /active-bpel/rt/...
text: `GET|POST https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/rt/<ProcessApiName>` (the vendor form) or `.../active-bpel/rt/<orgIdV3>/<ProcessApiName>` (the form that answered in the field) authenticates with HTTP Basic (an IDMC user name and password) or a session header: the Design guide documents `IDS-SESSION-ID: <v3 sessionId>`, and a field client sent `INFA-SESSION-ID` from the v3 login, cached it and retried once on 401/403. A process deployed for anonymous access answers 401/403 on this path; call it on `/public/rt/`. A process set to accept only API Gateway authorization needs an OAuth2 token from an API Manager client.
evidence: live 200 invokes (2026-07-06/07); a client fixed after 403 on every call to an anonymous process on the auth path (2026-07-08); Design guide pp.200-203

title: Discover deployed processes and their contracts
text: `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/rt` with a session header lists the deployed services; `.../active-bpel/rt/<orgIdV3>/<Process>/schema/input` returns a process's input contract. Append `?swagger` to an rt URL for its Swagger document and `?wsdl` to a SOAP URL (`/active-bpel/soap/<Process>`, anonymous `/active-bpel/public/soap/<Tenant>/<Process>`). Message events answer on `/active-bpel/public/rt/<Tenant>/<Process>/event/<MessageName>` (anonymous) or `/active-bpel/rt/<Process>/event/<MessageName>` (Basic).
evidence: list 200 with 54-68 deployed services (2026-07-06); swagger, SOAP and event forms documented (Invoke guide pp.12-14)

title: A 403 on invoke is the process's access list, not an org role
text: When an authenticated invoke returns 403 "User not authorized", the caller is not in the process's Allowed Users or Allowed Groups (users there also need the Run privilege). Granting broad org roles, including admin and migration roles, did not help. Set the access list in the designer (or with the untested `asset/v1/update`) and republish.
evidence: 403 persisted after an org role grant (2026-07-06); access semantics per Design guide pp.200-202

title: No access configuration means no service URL at all
text: If a process has neither Allowed Users/Groups nor Allow anonymous access, publishing generates no service URL, Swagger, OpenAPI or WSDL; the process can then run only as a subprocess, and it does not appear in API Manager.
evidence: documented: Invoke guide p.7, Design guide pp.200-203 [doc]

title: Send inputs as strings; unknown fields return 400 'extra'; nested webhooks need a bridge
text: The field callers sent every input value as a JSON string; a process with no inputs accepts `{}`, and an unknown property returns 400 "extra". A flat input schema rejects a provider's raw webhook (nested payload plus a signature header) with 400: either author the process to accept and verify the provider payload, or run a bridge that pulls authenticated events from the provider API, flattens them and invokes the process.
evidence: raw webhook 400 and bridge calls 200 (2026-07-08); 400 'extra' on an unknown field (2026-07-09)

title: CAI leaves empty-string outputs out of the response: read a missing key as ''
text: An output whose value is the empty string does not appear in the JSON response. Callers and verifiers must treat a missing key the same as `''`; a strict null-versus-empty comparison produced a false failure and an unnecessary rollback.
evidence: one verifier rollback caused only by null versus '' (2026-09-28)

title: Read invoke status codes as reachability markers
text: 200: the process ran. 500 carrying a downstream error (an invalid test key, a target rejecting the write): the process ran and reached the external system. 403 "User not authorized": the runtime access list blocked the caller. 404: no published process of that name for that tenant (unpublished, renamed, wrong org id or path). 400: the input contract does not match. 429: the rate window or the 10,000-activity limit. A smoke test should assert reachability rather than business success; an orchestration process that returns 200 plus a job id proves outbound CDI orchestration.
evidence: 500, 403 and 200 edge tests (2026-07-04); 404 on a renamed process until callers switched (2026-09-26)

title: Anonymous endpoints run as CAI_Anonymous_<orgIdV3> and are open to anyone with the URL
text: Processes deployed with anonymous access run as the org's system user `CAI_Anonymous_<orgIdV3>`; deleting that user in a user cleanup breaks every public endpoint. Anyone who has an anonymous URL can invoke the process, so anonymous access suits demos and side-effect-free decisions; for production writes use Allowed Users/Groups or API Gateway OAuth. Anonymous endpoints on `/active-bpel/public/rt/<orgIdV3>/<process>` answer an unauthenticated GET from the internet with HTTP 500, not 401, and the URLs are predictable from the org id and the process name: require authentication or front them with an API gateway before they sit in an application's request path (L-CAI-088). Newer evidence: L-CAI-163.
evidence: the user kept through a 29-user cleanup (2026-09-28); anonymous write endpoints flagged in an architecture review (2026-09-28); an unauthenticated GET probe answered 500 (2026-10-03)

title: CAI endpoint URLs embed the pod and the org id: make the base URL configuration in every caller
text: Moving processes to another org or pod changes every caller's URL (`https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/public/rt/<orgIdV3>/...`). Read the base URL from an environment variable in each caller (a code default that embeds the old org is a trap), switch it at cutover with one verify call, and keep the old value as the rollback.
evidence: callers switched with a 10-30 s container recreate; first decision through the new org in 343 ms (2026-09-28)

title: Derive the CAI host from the login base URL; a pod-literal string replace breaks after a move
text: Build `<pod>-cai.<rest-of-host>` from `products[].baseApiUrl` or `serverUrl` by inserting `-cai` after the first host label. Scripts that did `serverUrl.replace('<pod1>.<dom1>', '<pod1>-cai.<dom1>')`, or hard-coded a CAI host, silently kept calling the old pod after the org moved.
evidence: code review of the CAI builders during a cutover (2026-09-28)

title: CAI runs never appear in the Data Integration activity log
text: `/api/v2/activity/activityLog` reports mapping-task and taskflow runs; CAI process invocations are not there. Capture CAI evidence from the invocation responses (a row per call in your own table), from restadmin, or from Operational Insights.
evidence: runs absent from the activity log (2026-07-09)

title: Cloud-published processes run on the <pod>-cai runtime, not on an agent's Process Server
text: Processes published to the Cloud Server run on `<pod>-cai`; a Secure Agent's local process engine, and its embedded database, are not involved, so run history read on the agent shows 0 for them. `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/rt` lists what is deployed, and a 403 on some processes is their access list, not a license problem. Supersedes L-CAI-110.
evidence: 54 deployed services listed and a live 200 invoke; a wrong field returned 400 (2026-07-07)

title: List process instances and read a run's status with restadmin
text: `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/restadmin/processes` returns `{"process":[...]}` (200 live; the `/active-bpel/services/restadmin` variant returned 403). The Monitor guide describes these as process instances (runs), with filters `processState` (SUSPENDED, COMPLETED, RUNNING, COMPENSATABLE, FAULTED), `processName`, `processGroup`, `hideSystem`, `hidePublicTenant`, `processId`, `advancedQuery=getProcessProperty(...)`, and paging with `listStart` + `maxReturn` (default page size 20); `?processId=<runId>` returns one run. An empty list therefore does not show that nothing is deployed: use `GET /active-bpel/rt` for deployed services. The guide documents `IDS-SESSION-ID` for these calls.
evidence: 200 {process:[]} versus 403 on the services variant (2026-09-22); 200 live on two pods (2026-07-25); Monitor guide pp.101-104

title: Suspend, resume or terminate a process instance (documented PUTs)
text: `PUT https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/restadmin/processes/<processId>/suspend` (also `/resume` and `/terminate`) with `IDS-SESSION-ID` returns 204 per the Monitor guide; not exercised here. An older note advised retrying as POST on 405 because no PUT had been proven in IDMC; that premise is outdated (a PUT is proven on runtime-environment selections), so try the documented PUT first. The Job Management MCP server stops CDI jobs, not CAI instances. Supersedes L-CAI-111.
evidence: documented only: Monitor guide p.108 [doc]

title: Schedule processes natively with the restadmin scheduler
text: `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/restadmin/scheduler/schedules/?tenantContextId=<orgIdV3>` (header `INFA-SESSION-ID`) returns `{"schedulerInitialized":true,"scheduledItems":...}`. Create with `POST` to `.../scheduler/schedules` and `{"tenantContextId":"<orgIdV3>","name":"<n>","ipdService":true,"once":null,"intraday":{"executeEvery":{"value":30,"interval":"MINUTES"},"onlyBetween":null},"daily":null,"weekly":null,"monthly":null,"runOptions":"SKIP","serviceName":"<process API name>","inputDocument":null}` (204); update with `PUT` carrying `scheduleId`; delete with `DELETE` and `{"scheduleId":[<id>, ...]}` (one invalid id and nothing is deleted). `ipdService:true` is for Process Designer processes; BPEL services use `false` plus a SOAP `inputDocument`. The scheduler only fires the process: record run evidence inside the process. Supersedes L-CAI-104.
evidence: GET 200 with schedulerInitialized true (2026-07-09); create, update and delete documented (Monitor guide pp.62-67)

title: URN mappings and listener event sources on restadmin
text: `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/restadmin/urn/<orgIdV3>` reads all URN mappings (200 live). `PUT .../restadmin/urn/` adds or updates a mapping and `DELETE` removes one or more (documented; the Monitor guide shows `Authorization: Bearer <session_id>`). Listener-based event sources start and stop with `POST .../active-bpel/local/restadmin/eventconnection/start` and `/stop` (documented).
evidence: GET live (2026-07-25); the rest documented (Monitor guide pp.54-57, 122-123)

title: Every restadmin and invoke path has a Secure Agent twin under /process-engine
text: For processes deployed to a Secure Agent the same APIs answer on the agent host: `http(s)://<agentHost>:<port>/process-engine/restadmin/...` (processes, scheduler; tenant `$public`), invoke `/process-engine/rt/<service>`, anonymous `/process-engine/public/rt/<service>`, SOAP 1.2 under `/process-engine/soap/`. Local defaults are `http://localhost:7080/process-engine/` and `https://localhost:7443/process-engine/`.
evidence: documented: Invoke guide p.14, Monitor guide pp.62-108; the ports seen on agents (2026-07-04) [doc]

title: restadmin is live on dmp-us pods too; a scheduler 401 is a role gap
text: On a dmp-us pod, `<pod>-cai` returned real JSON for processes and URN mappings while only the scheduler returned 401, which isolates a missing role rather than an absent plane. The runtime-control plane is a platform feature on both host families. Supersedes L-CAI-106.
evidence: 200 JSON for processes and URN mappings on a dmp-us pod (2026-07-25)

title: Operational Insights export is GraphQL on /active-bpel/opsanalytics-das/metrics
text: `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/opsanalytics-das/metrics?query={processJobReport(start:"<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ>",end:"<...Z>"){time processName endpoint env originContext status executionCount executionTime averageExecutionTime}}` exports CAI job data (up to 13 months; optional `env`, `status` Completed or Faulted); `processRunsByNameEnv(start:"YYYY-MM-DD",end:"YYYY-MM-DD")` returns aggregates by process and environment (up to one month). Documented headers: `Authorization: Bearer <session_id>`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and `Accept: text/csv` for CSV (omit it for JSON). One active request per org, no pagination, UTC timestamps; the full schema is in Informatica KB article 000259754. A 400 on a malformed query proves the endpoint parses input; `/public/core/v3/operationalInsights` is 404 (wrong plane). Supersedes L-CAI-105. Newer evidence: L-CAI-159.
evidence: 400 on a malformed query (2026-07-25); Operational Insights guide pp.70-75 [disputed 2026-11-03 by L-CAI-159: the export answered 401 with Authorization: Bearer and 200 with the IDS-SESSION-ID header]

title: The 10,000-activity execution limit returns 429 and blocks new instances for 15 minutes
text: When a process execution exceeds the activity execution limit (default 10,000 BPEL activities, counted at BPEL level, not designer steps; count the "Executing [" lines in the process log), invocations return `{"error":{"code":429,"message":"The last execution of this process has exceeded the activity execution limit ..."}}` and no new instance is created for 15 minutes or until the process is republished. The cache is node-local, so one node can reject while another runs. At the limit a process is suspended (persistence Full or Persist; resuming it resets the count) or terminated (None, Brief, Final). The feature is tech preview. Keep loops bounded and pace high-volume traffic below the limit; a dedicated agent node keeps the counter away from other work.
evidence: documented: Invoke guide p.25, Monitor guide p.9; recorded as a known trap (2026-09-12) [doc]

title: Other CAI limits: rate window, 5 MB, 3,600 s, retention
text: REST and SOAP calls return 429 once the rate limit of the time window is exceeded. The Cloud Server accepts payloads and attachments up to 5,242,880 bytes (5 MB). A non-persistent process that runs longer than 3,600 s is terminated. With automated maintenance, completed instances stay 24 h and faulted ones 72 h in the Process Server database, and logs 30 days. Publish and unpublish accept at most 199 assets per call. Newer evidence: L-CAI-162.
evidence: documented: Invoke guide pp.12, 25-26, 30; Design guide (attachment size) [doc]

title: Run history of agent-deployed processes lives in the engine's embedded PostgreSQL
text: For processes that run on a Secure Agent's process engine, run history sits in the engine's embedded PostgreSQL on the agent host (database `activevos`, tables such as `aeprocess` and `aeplan`, default local port 5432, default user `bpeluser`). Read it over SSH with psql and land it in a warehouse. It is empty for Cloud Server processes; for cloud-side reporting use Operational Insights.
evidence: tables read on an agent host (2026-07-04)

title: Record CAI run evidence yourself: from the caller, inside the process, or with a Shell Service step
text: Neither the scheduler nor the Data Integration activity log records CAI runs for you. Write one row per call from the caller, or from the process itself (a service step that posts to your own endpoint or table). For agent-bound processes a "Run a Shell Command" step pinned to a Secure Agent can run a script, after a one-time UI enablement of the Shell Service (Console > Server Configuration > System Services > Shell Service) on that agent.
evidence: design notes from the Monitor and Design guides (2026-07-09); caller-side decision tables in use (2026-09-24 onward)

title: Model long-running external work as an async process
text: For callbacks from slow external work, build the process as accept, dispatch, suspend, resume on the callback (a message event), with a timer to back the timeout. Building and running such processes costs nothing beyond the metered downstream calls.
evidence: edge processes modelled on an existing async sample process (2026-07-08)

title: OData endpoints for CAI connections (documented)
text: `GET https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/odata/v4/<connection>` serves OData v2 and v4, and `/$metadata` returns the contract. Documented; not exercised.
evidence: documented only [doc]

title: Where a process runs: the Cloud Server, a Secure Agent or an agent group
text: The process Run On property selects the Cloud Server, a specific agent or an agent group; an app connection whose `<agent/>` element is empty runs on the Cloud Server. Processes that call only public cloud endpoints run on the Cloud Server and need no agent Process Server. Run on an agent when the process must reach private hosts, uses an event-based connector (run it on that connector's agent), signs with a keystore or private key, or uses the RSA encrypt/decrypt functions (key file on the agent). A Human Task step requires the Cloud Server. Run On is locked while the process is published: unpublish, change, republish.
evidence: 4 processes served from the Cloud Server at 350-730 ms while the agent Process Server was broken (2026-09-24); Design guide p.203 and the key and encryption notes

title: The Cloud Server cannot reach private networks
text: A process running on the Informatica Cloud Server cannot call a service on a private network (for example an internal transcription service). Deploy such processes to a Secure Agent process engine that has the network path, or expose the service.
evidence: internal service unreachable from the Cloud Server (2026-07-09)

title: Write to Salesforce from CAI with your own REST service connector and a Connected App
text: The built-in CAI Salesforce connector needs the ModifyMetadata permission, which breaks least privilege for an integration user. Build a REST service connector instead: a `Get_Token` action doing the OAuth 2.0 client-credentials grant against the org's token URL (outputs `access_token`, `instance_url`), and upsert actions doing `PATCH <instance_url>/services/data/v<nn>/sobjects/<Object>/<ExtIdField>/<value>` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (an idempotent create-or-update). Link parents through external-id relationship fields (`"<Parent>__r":{"<ParentExtIdField>":"<value>"}`). Build your own connector and connection rather than copying someone else's.
evidence: a Contact about 2 s after a sign-up; a child record 1.35 s after a database update (2026-09-25)

title: One generic Upsert_Record action, with the JSON payload built in XQuery
text: Give the connector one generic action whose inputs are `instance_url`, `access_token`, `sobject`, `ext_field`, `ext_id` and `payload` (body `{$payload}`), and let each process build the payload with XQuery: JSON-escape strings, emit numbers only when `castable as xs:decimal` (else `null`), map booleans from 'true', 't', '1' and 'yes', and omit a relationship entirely when its parent key is empty. One connector then serves every object.
evidence: three event processes upserting three objects through one action (2026-09-25 to 2026-09-28)

title: Connection attributes written with encrypted="false" are stored and exported in plaintext
text: An app connection whose attributes (client id, client secret, password, security token) were authored with `encrypted="false"` stores them in plaintext, and every later v3 export package that includes the connection carries them in plaintext. Marking the connector's attribute definitions `masked="true"` did not prevent it; the vendor guide says sensitive fields are not exported, which covers values stored as sensitive, not these. The exact headless form that stores an encrypted value was not established. Treat every export zip as a secret (0600, off shared folders), set secrets after import where possible (designer or the documented `asset/v1/update`), and rotate the credential after any migration.
evidence: client id and secret found in plaintext by package inspection (2026-09-28)

title: Change a connection secret headless by re-importing the connection with OVERWRITE, then republish
text: In July a connection-asset REST attempt returned 403 and processes rejected the key as an input, so connection secrets were recorded as UI-only.
