In September connections were rebuilt headless instead: regenerate the AI_CONNECTION XML with the new value under the same GUID, import it with OVERWRITE, republish the connection, and verify with one real call (a token request or an upsert). This route writes the value unencrypted (L-CAI-060). The documented `PUT .../active-bpel/asset/v1/update?assetType=AppConnection` is a second route, untested. Supersedes L-CAI-103.
evidence: builder re-run after a secret rotation and after a consumer-key fix, token and upsert calls green afterwards (2026-09-25/26)

title: invalid_client_id on the token call means the connection's consumer key does not match the Connected App
text: After a rebuild, a client-credentials token request that returns `invalid_client_id` means the connection holds the wrong consumer key for the Connected App. Fix the key, re-import and republish the connection, and re-test the token call before switching callers.
evidence: invalid_client_id until the consumer key was fixed (2026-09-26)

title: 'Foreign key external ID not found' means the parent record does not exist yet
text: A Salesforce upsert that links a child to its parent by external id fails with "Foreign key external ID not found" when the parent is missing. A real-time relay should retry, because the parent may land a moment later. For reconciliation, re-send the child without the relationship so its own fields are right, let the parent-creating job run, then re-link.
evidence: reconciliation matched 47/47 and 126/126 child records (2026-09-28)

title: A Salesforce duplicate rule can silently block Contact upserts from CAI and CDI alike
text: An active standard Contact duplicate rule blocked new Contacts from both the CAI real-time path and the CDI batch sync. Decide where deduplication lives (the IDMC match step, the CRM's own identity resolution), deactivate or adjust the CRM rule, and re-test both paths.
evidence: records reached Salesforce after the rule was deactivated (2026-09-26)

title: Process-engine JDBC drivers go in <agent_home>/apps/process-engine/ext
text: For CAI JDBC connections that run on an agent, the process engine loads driver jars from `<agent_home>/apps/process-engine/ext` when the connection's "JDBC Jar Directory" is left blank; otherwise point that field at any directory. Supply either the jar directory or the driver class name.
evidence: vendor JDBC connector guide ch.2; the directory confirmed on an agent (2026-07-26)

title: Enable the Process Server service headless through the runtime-environment selections PUT
text: In July every REST attempt to enable an agent service failed: `POST /api/v2/agent/service` gave 403 `APP_13401` or 500 `CMN_001` (router artifacts that bogus twins return too), `/api/v2/agent/selectiveservices` 500, `POST /api/v2/agent` with `agentEngines[].desiredStatus` was a silent no-op, `/public/core/v3/runtimeEnvironments` 404; the Administrator toggle (Runtime Environments > agent > Application Integration) was the only path. By September `GET https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/runtime/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>/selections/ui` and a `PUT` of the edited body, both with `IDS-SESSION-ID: <v2 icSessionId>`, changed service and connector selections headless (read back after the PUT; `INFA-SESSION-ID` returns the login HTML). Application Integration (the Process Server) is one of the service flags in that body. After enablement the agent downloads `package-process-engine` in about 2-3 minutes. Supersedes L-CAI-109.
evidence: July probes 403/500/no-op (2026-07-09); selections PUT 200 with read-back and engines RUNNING (2026-09-28); the Application Integration flag read enabled:true in the same body (2026-09-23)

title: enabled:true in the selections does not mean the Process Server runs
text: Application Integration can read `enabled:true` in the runtime-environment selections while the process engine restart-loops and never serves. Verify on the agent host (L-CAI-068) and in `GET <serverUrl>/api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>`, where the `process-engine` "Process Server" entry must read RUNNING/RUNNING. A restart loop shows as repeated RESTARTING events in `agentcore.log` (hundreds of events and over a thousand failed boots in two days in one case).
evidence: status endpoint 404 and RESTARTING loop until the repair, 200 and RUNNING after (2026-09-23/24)

title: Health-check the Process Server on the agent host, not on the cloud host
text: `GET https://localhost:7443/process-engine/status` (or `http://<agentHost>:7080/process-engine/status`) returns 200 with body `2` when healthy, and `/process-engine/rt` returns 401 (alive and auth-gated, not 404). Also confirm the java process launched from `apps/process-engine/*/conf`, the embedded PostgreSQL up with deployed BPEL plans (state 2), and agent details RUNNING. A 404 from a cloud host root says nothing about the Process Server. The agent polls the status itself every 60 s. Supersedes L-CAI-107.
evidence: 200 with 126 deployed plans (2026-07-04); 404 to 200 across a repair (2026-09-24)

title: The embedded PostgreSQL port 5432 is hard-coded and collides with any local Postgres
text: Every process-engine script uses `localhost:5432/activevos`, and `server_status.sh` is only `pg_isready -p 5432`. If another PostgreSQL listens on 5432 on the agent host, each start logs a false "PostgreSQL database has started"; `prepareDB.sh` then runs `db_init.sh` against that other database, fails, and deletes the engine's `data/PostGreSql` directory, so the deploy never completes. Check `ss -ltnp` for 5432 before enabling Application Integration on a shared host.
evidence: empty embedded data directory and no engine PostgreSQL process despite the 'started' log line (2026-09-23/24)

title: deploy.sh can delete the Tomcat context descriptor, and a missing keystore keeps port 7443 down
text: The engine's `deploy.sh` runs `[ -d conf/Catalina/localhost ] || mv host.name localhost` and then `rm -rf host.name`. If an empty `conf/Catalina/localhost/` already exists, the context descriptor `process-engine.xml` (allowLinking plus the `jdbc/ProcessEngine` resource) is deleted instead of moved; Tomcat then refuses the symlinked `WEB-INF/web.xml`, the webapp deploys empty in about 37 ms, and every request, including `/process-engine/status`, returns 404. Separately, if `conf/ae.keystore` and `ae.cacerts` are missing under `apps/process-engine/conf`, port 7443 never binds; copy them from `<peVersion>/conf/certs`.
evidence: observed on one agent (2026-09-23/24); 7443 bound after the keystore copy

title: Repair a restart-looping Process Server
text: (1) Back up `apps/process-engine/bin`, `conf` and `data` in one tar as the undo. (2) Change `localhost:5432/activevos` to a free port (for example 5433) in `<peVersion>/bin/*.sh` and in the context descriptor. (3) In the embedded PostgreSQL `user.conf` set that port and `listen_addresses = 'localhost'` (not `'*'`). (4) Stop the looping Tomcat and re-run Informatica's own `deploy.sh` with the LCM environment captured from the live process (schema created, Liquibase updated, exit 0). (5) Restore `conf/Catalina/localhost/process-engine.xml` from the backup. (6) Verify `/process-engine/status` 200 and agent details RUNNING/RUNNING.
evidence: RUNNING for the first time since its install and stable afterwards (2026-09-24)

title: Agent auto-upgrades re-ship the 5432 scripts: guard the port per agent directory
text: An auto-upgrade of the process engine installs a new version directory with the 5432 scripts again. A root cron job (every 10 minutes) that re-applies the non-5432 port keeps the fix. It patches one agent's install path, so a second agent that runs its own process engine needs its own copy pointed at its directory, and its own engine ports.
evidence: guard installed after the repair (2026-09-26); coexistence notes on a two-agent host (2026-09-29)

title: Make agent restarts safe for the Process Server: an orphan reaper and a port check
text: Install an orphan reaper as `ExecStartPre` and `ExecStopPost` in a systemd drop-in for the agent unit, plus a 5-minute check. It kills orphaned engine processes (including a surviving engine PostgreSQL) and refuses to start, loudly, while engine ports such as 7005 and 14479 or `*.mv.db` files are still held.
evidence: kill -9 of the agent core and its respawn loop, then a unit restart: 0 orphans and 20/20 engines RUNNING in about 6 min, CDC and CAI unaffected (2026-09-26)

title: Keep the process engine off on a second agent that shares a host
text: The on-agent process engine binds 7080/7443, internal ports (7005, 14479) and its embedded PostgreSQL. On a host that already runs an agent with a process engine (and possibly an application Postgres), a second engine clashes, and the first agent's start guard refuses while those ports are taken. If CAI runs on the Cloud Server, deselect the process engine on the second agent, and diff `ss -ltnp` before and after each service lands.
evidence: no port clash through a migration with two agents on one host (2026-09-28/29)

title: The process engine adds about 1.8-2 GB of RAM to an agent host
text: Adding the CAI process engine to an agent added roughly 1.8-2 GB of RAM (it ran with `-Xmx1536M`). Check free memory first, watch for a first-start crash loop, and raise the heap if it runs out of memory. For scale, an agent without CAI showed 8 base engines and a fully enabled one 17.
evidence: host sizing check (2026-07-04)

title: A stopped Process Server can be started from the agent host
text: When the engine binaries are already installed, a stopped Process Server can be started on the agent host (or toggled in the console) even though no REST call starts a service. Verify by the listening ports (7080, 7443) and agent details.
evidence: 7080 and 7443 listening after the start (2026-07-05)

title: CAI entitlement shows in agent engines and PROCESS objects, not in the login products list
text: The v3 login `products[]` can list only "Integration Cloud" while CAI is entitled and running. Proof comes from `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` listing `process-engine` ("Process Server"), PROCESS objects in `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='PROCESS'`, or `GET .../active-bpel/rt` listing deployed services. Application Integration comes with Integration Cloud rather than as a separate product. Supersedes L-CAI-108.
evidence: 54-68 deployed processes listed (2026-07-25); agent engine lists read (2026-07-05 and 2026-09-21)

title: Assets with duplicate runtime catalog rows or no runtime entry cannot be published, unpublished or deleted
text: Two stuck states need Informatica support, or at least a designer attempt. (a) The CAI runtime holds two catalog rows for one asset, so both publish and unpublish fault with "singleton sequence ... 2 items". (b) The asset has no runtime entry, so they fault with `AvrEntryNotFoundFault`. Either way the asset stays flagged published, FRS refuses to delete it (`FRS_082`) and its project cannot be emptied (`FRS_087`). Record them and move on.
evidence: two legacy assets left after a cleanup removed 81 of 83 (2026-09-28)

title: Two calls of the same upsert for one record within a second race, and the loser returns 500
text: When two callers (an application and a trigger relay) invoke the same CAI upsert process for the same record in the same second, one wins and the other gets HTTP 500, although the record is written. Make one caller responsible per record per event (or serialize and dedupe), and have sync-status views keep the latest SUCCESS per record rather than the latest attempt.
evidence: status view after the fix: upserted 76 to 79, errors 13 to 10 (2026-09-28)

title: A CAI 500 can simply be the target rejecting the write
text: CAI surfaces a downstream failure as a plain 500 from the process endpoint. Check the target system's response first; in one case every insert failed with Salesforce `STORAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` because the target org was full, and the process answered 500 for about two hours until space was freed.
evidence: 500s with STORAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED behind them (2026-09-28/29)

title: A publish can fail when the Process Server behind the target runtime is not running (hedged)
text: Recorded with the asset-path fix: publishes aimed at a runtime whose agent Process Server had never started failed. The processes that then went live ran on the Cloud Server, so the path format is the proven fix and the dead engine is a probable contributor for agent-bound assets. Check engine health (L-CAI-068) before blaming the publish call.
evidence: recorded as a contributing cause (2026-09-24); not isolated by a controlled test [hedged]

title: Call CAI from an application fail-open and record every decision
text: Call the runtime with a short timeout (about 6 s), send every input as a string, and fail open: a CAI outage must never block a sign-up or a payment and is recorded as `ok=false`. Write one row per call (process, subject, decision, ok, latency_ms, error, request, response) into an application table that the batch pipeline lands, so the decisions show up in analytics, and expose a health endpoint that makes one side-effect-free call. Run the push that creates a parent SaaS record (for example the CRM contact that later child upserts reference by external id) in a background thread and retry only transient failures there (HTTP 5xx and transport errors such as timeouts and connection resets) with a short backoff (2 s, 5 s, 10 s), persisting only the final outcome with the attempt count: a missing parent makes every later child upsert fail with 'Foreign key external ID not found' (L-CAI-063), so the parent is the one call worth retrying, and child upserts get no retry. The stored latency is then the last attempt's round trip, not the user's wait, so measure end to end separately. Before reading a daily CAI 500 rate as runtime flakiness, group the failures by the downstream error in the response body: a full target (STORAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, L-CAI-080) or a same-second double call for one record (L-CAI-079) is not fixed by retries.
evidence: inline decision latency about 350-730 ms on the Cloud Server; hundreds of decisions recorded (2026-09-24 to 2026-09-27); per-call rows over 24 h windows: bursts of 500s on the upsert process traced to the CRM rejecting inserts (21 of 24 calls in one day failed, each after all 4 attempts) (2026-10-01)

title: Near-real-time SaaS upserts: database trigger, NOTIFY, a thin relay, then a CAI process
text: An AFTER INSERT/UPDATE trigger builds the payload in the CAI input shape and fires `pg_notify('<channel>', payload)`; a small relay LISTENs and posts each event to the matching CAI upsert process. Retry after 3, 6 and 12 s on retryable SaaS answers (parent not landed yet, DUPLICATE_VALUE, UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW, REQUEST_LIMIT, 5xx) and skip events beyond a burst limit (for example 200 per 300 s), because the scheduled batch reconciles anyway. Keep the business rule in the trigger (for example emit only after a fee has settled) and the SaaS logic in CAI.
evidence: database write to CRM in 1.35 s (2026-09-25); reconciliation matched 47 and 126 records (2026-09-28)

title: CAI is the real-time leg: about 0.2-2 s from an application call to a SaaS record
text: Measured from the application call through a CAI process to a Salesforce record: 0.2-2 s (932 ms on a clean run; a contact-upsert process later averaged 1.37-1.43 s round trip, fastest 0.59-0.97 s, and application insert to CRM record averaged 1.9 s), against minutes for batch mapping lanes and 15-35 s for CDC into a warehouse. Inline decision processes on the Cloud Server answered in about 270-730 ms early on and averaged 77-114 ms later (fastest 41 ms; p50 266 ms over a week). Report averages over successful calls only: 27 failures ('500 after 4 attempts' while the CRM was full) pulled one average from about 1,130 ms to about 810 ms (L-METHOD-049).
evidence: Measured runs (2026-09-24 to 2026-09-29); per-call rows over 24 h windows and 7 days of the process call log (2026-10-01 to 2026-10-03)

title: Find every writer of a target field before changing a rule
text: One SaaS field can be written by several Informatica steps: a CAI cleanse, a CAI upsert and a batch mapping task that runs minutes later. Fixing only the real-time step is undone by the next batch run. List all writers, apply the same rule in each (prove the batch change with a full old-versus-new diff), and verify after the next batch run.
evidence: batch diff 701/701 rows with 0 changed columns, 12/12 synthetic cases, 15/15 name cases read back from the CRM (2026-09-28)

title: Naive title-casing in CAI logic breaks real names
text: Word-by-word title-casing lower-cases deliberate internal capitals (McDonald-style names) and a naive first/last split puts only the first word of a compound given name into FirstName. Keep deliberate internal capitals, capitalise after apostrophes (straight and curly) and hyphens, keep lower-case particles (de, la, van) in mid-name, take the last name as the last word plus a suffix (Jr., III) plus the particles just before it, and accept optional typed first and last name inputs. A rule that held without damaging correctly typed values: INITCAP each word with space, hyphen, straight and curly apostrophe as delimiters; keep the typed word when it matches `^\p{Lu}\p{Ll}+(\p{Lu}\p{Ll}{2,}){1,2}$` (deliberate inner capitals); keep a typed lower-case particle in mid-name when the name has more than two words (da das de del della der di do dos du la le van von den ter ten bin ibn al el); otherwise INITCAP, so ALL CAPS and random case are still fixed. For addresses: collapse runs of spaces, title-case street and city only when the value was typed all lower-case (keeps 'NE', 'McKinney'), and upper(trim()) the state. Put the same rule in every writer of the name (every target of the golden mapping, L-CDI-104, the real-time CAI path and the CRM sync): with two different rules the passes flip names back and forth. Bracketed tombstones such as '[erased]' get re-cased by the cleanse, so match tombstones case-insensitively downstream.
evidence: defect list from a scripted story run and a 10-case verification set (2026-09-28); re-import plus a time-travel diff around the first run: 830/830 and 875/875 rows with 0 unintended changes, and typed names held in the database, the login, the CRM and the warehouse for 23 h of lanes (2026-10-03)

title: Migrate CAI between orgs: publish in order, verify on the target runtime, then switch callers
text: The v3 import publishes nothing, so after it publish in the target in dependency order (connectors, app connections, processes without references, processes with references). Verify against the target's public runtime base with side-effect-free cases plus one real SaaS read-back that proves the app connection's credentials, and only then switch callers in a separate step (base-URL environment variables plus a container recreate). Keep the old org's processes published until the switch is verified.
evidence: wave 1 9/9 SUCCESS, 15/15 and 4/4 verification cases, callers switched 11 minutes later (2026-09-28)

title: Split integration by purpose: the API layer runs the application in real time, IDMC owns everything that feeds or serves analytics, and only API-shaped edges go through CAI
text: A division that kept roles clear where an API-led platform (an API gateway product such as MuleSoft) and IDMC run side by side. The API layer owns the doors into the application: every button's API from web, mobile, point-of-sale and staff tools into the operational database, application logic such as payment ledger legs, and the real-time app-to-CRM record sync. IDMC owns everything that feeds or serves analytics: CDC and CDI bring source data natively into the warehouse (raw to gold, DQ, catalog, golden records) and never pass through an app API where a native connector exists; CDI keeps the batch golden sync to the CRM; CAI carries only the analytics integrations that are API- or event-shaped (API-usage events into the warehouse, golden-record activation back into the apps by calling the app's own API). Keep a real-time data-quality check (cleanse + validate + decision) as an IDMC service (a CAI process) that the API layer calls fail-open (L-CAI-082), so the DQ rules exist once. Never route BI or analytics data through the API layer (it bypasses lineage, governance and DQ), never make an application's critical path wait on a batch job, and let golden data flow back into the app database through one writer. Facts that shaped it: CAI calls are not jobs, so moving work between CAI and the API layer saves no jobs (L-IPU-044); batch jobs count against a monthly job cap; anonymous CAI endpoints in the app path were a security gap (L-CAI-038). Audit an existing build for crossings (CAI processes in the app's request path, clients that bypass the gateway, gateway logs written straight to the warehouse, two writers of golden data into the app, custom loaders that belong to neither side), record the decision per edge in the architecture inventory, and move edges one at a time with the old path as rollback; before moving a flow, confirm the API platform has runtime capacity (an expired trial with no production capacity blocked one move). Within CAI, use it for HTTP/REST/SOAP edges (outbound SaaS and model APIs, inbound webhooks, admin APIs, managed public APIs), and keep database wire protocols, message buses and outbox relays, WebSockets, media streams, presigned object-storage URLs, SMTP and the hottest server-side paths direct, for latency and because CAI meters per invocation.
evidence: Edge-by-edge inventory with code evidence (2026-07-01); an architecture audit of every hop against the split found five crossings (6 CAI processes, one bypassing client and one direct warehouse loader on the wrong side) and gave each a migration item; the real-time CAI leg measured 0.2-2 s against minutes for batch lanes (2026-10-01 to 2026-10-03)

title: Phase CAI adoption from low-risk async edges to payments last, with flags and fallbacks
text: Validate each phase in every environment (dev-green is not prod-green): foundations and a reachability spike, a zero-risk async slice, inbound webhooks (payment webhooks last, keeping signature checks over the raw body), outbound orchestration, then selected internal edges. Put each edge behind a feature flag with a direct fallback and a circuit breaker, start with low-volume edges because IPUs are per invocation, and remember that process logic is portable metadata while agents, connections, secrets and network reach vary per environment.
evidence: phased plan document (2026-07-01)

title: Shadow-evaluate a CAI decision process against real history before cutover
text: Replay a large sample of real historical events through the process and compare its decisions with what the application actually did; run it in advisory mode (the application still owns the side effect) until parity is proven and QA signs off.
evidence: 1,000 historical payments matched 1000/1000 (2026-07-08)

title: Keep outbound money and LLM calls from CAI behind an explicit spend gate
text: Split edges that call paid services into a safe half (webhook ingest, reconcile, read-only checks) and a gated half (live charges, model calls at volume). Validate with test-mode keys only; the live outbound half needs explicit human approval and QA sign-off, and it migrates last.
evidence: gate design (2026-07-04)

title: A CAI process can orchestrate CDI jobs and return the run id
text: A process that calls the CDI job API (`POST /api/v2/job`) can start a mapping task and return its run id, which gives REST-triggered orchestration through CAI. Keep the task ids it uses current: pointing at deleted tasks made the process return 500.
evidence: 200 with a run id and 208 rows landed; stale task ids gave 500 (2026-07-07)

title: Data Integration taskflows publish through a different path from CAI processes
text: Data Integration taskflows do not use the CAI designer publish service: they were created and published (`publicationStatus=published` read back) while CAI first publish was broken. The reverse also holds: API-created or FRS-copied advanced taskflows failed to publish (`AvrEntryNotFoundFault`, "File format was not recognized") while CAI assets published fine.
evidence: taskflow published during the CAI regression (2026-07-09); advanced-taskflow publish failures (2026-09-25)

title: API Manager was entitled, but managed-API and policy authoring had no REST (July 2026)
text: With API Manager entitled, its engine (`DataServiceApiMgmt`) running and dozens of API Manager privileges granted, managed-API and policy authoring still had no public REST (probes 404) and no object to clone (`MANAGED_API` count 0); authoring was the API Manager canvas. Re-probe before relying on this.
evidence: 404 probes and a zero MANAGED_API count (2026-07-04)

title: A process created in a sub-organization cannot be saved and published after switching in from the parent
text: Per the Invoke guide, if you switch from a parent organization to a sub-organization, you cannot save and publish a process that was created in the sub-organization. Log in to the org that owns the asset.
evidence: documented: Invoke guide p.8 [doc]

title: What one CAI 'API call' is for metering
text: A CAI API call is one execution of a process, subprocess, guide or OData endpoint on the Process Server (each subprocess call adds one), not one outbound HTTP call, and CAI also accrues a separate compute-hours meter. The same feed meters differently as a CAI process (per call) or as a CDI mapping with a REST connector (compute hours), so confirm the build style before sizing.
evidence: Cloud Services Measurement Guide and rate card review (2026-09-11)

title: CAI publish has no REST verb; a human must click Publish in Application Integration
text: Believed because `POST .../objects/<id>/publish`, `/publish` and `/appint/v1/process/publish` returned 404 and the legacy `active-bpel/asset/publish` returned 403; a bootstrap reference kept listing publish as UI-only until late July. The probes used the wrong path and the pod host instead of `<pod>-cai`. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-26; overturned by L-CAI-001.

title: Publishing CAI over REST is an undocumented bypass, and a 403 on asset/publish means there is no API
text: The first headless publishes were framed as a bypass around the broken designer. The vendor Invoke guide documents `asset/v1/publish` and `/unpublish` as supported bulk resources; the 403 came from `asset/publish` (no `/v1/`) on the pod base host. Was believed 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-CAI-001.
evidence: framing in July notes; corrected from the vendor PDF (2026-07-25)

title: CAI first publish is blocked until Informatica fixes the designer build
text: During the cpfPublish regression, first publishes were thought to be impossible until a vendor fix. The documented bulk publish REST published the same assets the next day. Was believed 2026-07-08 to 2026-07-09; overturned by L-CAI-013.
evidence: designer 500 on first publish (2026-07-08)

title: Migration-imported CAI assets need one UI Save in Process Designer before they can be published
text: The theory was that a v3 import fills the Explore catalog but not the designer's runtime repository, so publish answered BAD_REQUEST "Invalid asset path" until someone saved each asset in the designer (or rebuilt it with the OpenAPI 3.0 wizard). The paths sent were `<project>/<folder>/<name>`; with `Explore/<project>/<folder>/<name>.<TYPE>.xml` imported and even hand-built assets publish headless. Was believed 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-24; overturned by L-CAI-003, L-CAI-020.
evidence: BAD_REQUEST 'Invalid asset path' on imported connectors and processes (2026-09-09 to 2026-09-22)

title: CAI process authoring is UI-only because POST /public/core/v3/objects returns 405
text: Held twice: in early July, and again in September before the migration-clone route was rediscovered. Processes are authored headless by cloning through a v3 export and import, or from scratch in a hand-built package. Was believed 2026-07-04; again 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-CAI-016, L-CAI-020.
evidence: 405 on the v3 objects catalog

title: Unpublish CAI assets in the same order as publish: service connector, app connection, process
text: A limits table carried the publish order for unpublish too. The vendor example (a connector unpublish failing on "Dependent entry(ies)") and every field cleanup show the reverse: dependents first. Was believed 2026-07-25 to 2026-09-28; overturned by L-CAI-007.
evidence: limits-table row citing Invoke p.35 (2026-07-25)

title: Secrets inside a CAI app connection can only be set in the UI
text: A connection-asset REST call returned 403 and processes rejected the key as an input, so one UI edit per connection secret was planned. Rebuilding the connection and importing it with OVERWRITE changed secrets headless in September. Was believed 2026-07-08 to 2026-09-25; overturned by L-CAI-061.
evidence: 403 and rejection verified three ways (2026-07-08)

title: A CAI process cannot be scheduled natively, so scheduling needs a DI taskflow or browser automation
text: The process Start binding offers only REST/SOAP and Event, so native scheduling looked impossible. Scheduling is a separate layer: the restadmin scheduler schedules REST-bound processes. Was believed 2026-07-09; overturned by L-CAI-045.
evidence: Start binding options inspected (2026-07-09)

title: Operational Insights has no API plane
text: REST-shaped probes found nothing. The documented export is GraphQL on `/active-bpel/opsanalytics-das/metrics` on the `-cai` host. Was believed to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-CAI-049.
evidence: REST probes on the wrong host family

title: The CAI restadmin plane exists only on the dm-us host family
text: Generalised from one pod. restadmin answered with real JSON on a dmp-us pod as well. Was believed to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-CAI-048.
evidence: belief from one pod

title: A Process Server 'validation failed' (404 on the status probe) means the engine is broken
text: The probe had hit a cloud host root. The on-agent status endpoint returned 200 with over a hundred deployed plans. Was believed 2026-07-04; overturned by L-CAI-068.
evidence: 404 on a cloud host root (2026-07-04)

title: CAI is not provisioned or not licensed on the org
text: Read from the login `products[]` list, from probes taken before any assets existed, and later from an agent that seemed to lack a Process Server runtime. Engine lists, PROCESS objects and the deployed-service list proved CAI entitled and running. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-05; again 2026-09-21; overturned by L-CAI-077.
evidence: products[] misread and early probes (2026-07-04, 2026-07-05, 2026-09-21)

title: Enabling the Process Server on a Secure Agent is a UI-only Administrator toggle
text: All July REST attempts to enable agent services failed or were router artifacts. The runtime-environment selections GET/PUT with `IDS-SESSION-ID` now changes service selections headless. Was believed 2026-07-09 to 2026-09-27; overturned by L-CAI-066.

title: CAI has never run in the org, and publish and run are UI-only (/active-bpel/rt 404, /process-engine/rt 401)
text: Concluded from probes on the wrong host and from an empty run-history table on the agent. Cloud-published processes run on `<pod>-cai`, where dozens were deployed and invocable. Was believed to 2026-07-07; overturned by L-CAI-042.
evidence: 404/401 probes and an empty agent-side table (to 2026-07-07)

title: No PUT is proven anywhere in IDMC, so documented restadmin PUTs should be retried as POST on 405
text: A July verdict table built its advice on "zero PUT proven". A PUT was later proven on runtime-environment selections; the restadmin PUTs themselves remain documented and unexercised. Was believed 2026-07-25 to 2026-09-28; overturned by L-CAI-044.
evidence: July verb census (2026-07-25/26)

title: Mint the CDGC Bearer JWT from the identity service with client_id=cdlg_app
text: `POST https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/api/v1/jwt/Token?client_id=cdlg_app&nonce=<random>&access_code=` with headers `IDS-SESSION-ID: <sessionId>` and `Cookie: USER_SESSION=<sessionId>` and an empty body returns `{"jwt_token": "..."}` (about 2,100 characters). The session id is the v3 login `userInfo.sessionId` (or the identity-service `Login` sessionId). A JWT lives 30 minutes from grant while the identity session lasts hours, so cache the JWT for about 20 minutes and re-mint it on any 401. A GET form (`?client_id=<id>&nonce=<uuid>` with `IDS-SESSION-ID`) is also recorded; `client_id=idmc_api` is the value used for managed MCP servers.
evidence: Every catalog-source, glossary, link and scan call of a two-org rebuild used it (200s); search with it returned 5,089 assets

title: Send the three identity headers on every CDGC call
text: CDGC routes sit behind `ccgf-auth-pep`. Send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, `IDS-SESSION-ID: <sessionId>` and `X-INFA-ORG-ID: <orgIdV3>` (plus `Content-Type`/`Accept: application/json`) on every call; search also needs `X-INFA-SEARCH-LANGUAGE: elasticsearch`. Some GETs tolerate Bearer only, but runs, creates and updates do not: a missing header shows up as 401, as 500 "Login sessionID is missing" from ccgf-auth-pep (or 406) on a scan run, or as a runtime-environment validation failure on catalog-source create (Informatica KB 000221244).
evidence: Bearer-only run = 500; with the three headers = 201 + jobId; creates validated only with IDS-SESSION-ID

title: A helper that sends only the v3 session header gets 401 on data360
text: Calling data360 through a generic helper that sends only `INFA-SESSION-ID` returned 401, while the same call with the minted Bearer JWT plus `IDS-SESSION-ID` and `X-INFA-ORG-ID` succeeded. Route every data360/ccgf call through one CDGC auth helper that owns the JWT cache.
evidence: 401 through the generic helper vs 201 through the CDGC helper on the same run call

title: With JWT-on-login enabled, the v3 sessionId itself can serve as the CDGC Bearer
text: When Administrator > Authentication sets the org's authentication type to JWT, `POST /saas/public/core/v3/login` returns a JWT in `userInfo.sessionId` (starts with `ey`, about 1,700 characters). CDGC accepted that value as `Authorization: Bearer` (with the same value in `IDS-SESSION-ID` and the org id in `X-INFA-ORG-ID`) for reads and for content/publish writes. Where the org is not on JWT-on-login, mint the Bearer through `jwt/Token` (L-CDGC-001).
evidence: sessionId began with ey and was accepted by CDGC GETs (2026-06-27) and by reads plus publish writes (2026-08-20)

title: Host map: which CDGC plane answers on which host
text: `idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com` serves `/data360/search/api/v1/search`, `/data360/search/v1/assets...`, `/data360/content/v1/assets...`, `/data360/executable/v1/...`, `/data360/observable/...`, `/data360/catalog-source-management/v1/...` and `/data360/marketplace/api/v1|v2/...`. `cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com` serves `/ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources...`, `/ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/publish`, `/ccgf-searchv2/api/v1/search` and `/cdmp-marketplace/api/v1/provisioning/*` (the executable run path and Marketplace dataAssets also answered there). `ccgf-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com` served `/ccgf-orchestration-management-api-server/...` to a browser session. `<pod>-cdgc.<domain>` has no DNS, and the platform pod host does not serve data360: a 404 there is a wrong-host result, not a missing feature.
evidence: 200/201/207 per route between 2026-06-28 and 2026-09-29; DNS failure for <pod>-cdgc (2026-07-26)

title: Zero-byte or twin-identical 200s on data360 are gateway artifacts, not a capability or licence verdict
text: On some orgs every `data360/*` and `cdmp-marketplace/*` path answers 200 with `Content-Length: 0` and no Content-Type, and a bogus twin path gets a byte-identical 200. That proves nothing: the plane is only partially mounted (some paths 404, others zero-byte 200). Run a bogus-twin control on every data360 probe and assert on body shape. In the observed case the org held CDGC privileges, so it was a deployment question, not an entitlement ticket; `cdgc-api` of another domain answered a clean 401 to the foreign-org token, which proves that route is real elsewhere.
evidence: Five hypotheses tested live (verb, host, header set, entitlement, path); bogus twins identical across 9 combinations

title: CDGC entitlement truth: RE services, agent engines, privileges and a real create, never products[] or guessed 404s
text: Do not conclude CDGC is unavailable from the login `products[]` list (it often shows only "Integration Cloud") or from 404s on guessed paths. Check the runtime environment's service selections (`Data Governance and Catalog` enabled:true in `GET .../runtime/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>/selections/ui`), the agent engines `Metadata_Platform_Service` and `Metadata_Foundation_Agent` RUNNING (`GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>`), privileges such as `create.mcp.CatalogSourceConfiguration`, `execute.mcp.CatalogSourceConfiguration` and `create.PROFILE` with the Governance Owner/Administrator roles, and whether a real catalog-source create validates. An empty catalog means unpopulated, not unentitled.
evidence: Catalog sources created and scans COMPLETED, glossary written, on an org whose login listed only Integration Cloud

title: Roles for one login that delivers CDI, CAI, CDQ, CDGC and CLAIRE work
text: A login that drives governance and CLAIRE as well as integration needs Admin, Designer, Governance Administrator and CLAIRE GPT User. In the UI the stakeholder picker stays empty unless the governance roles (Data Owner, Data Steward) are populated in Administrator first.
evidence: Runbook prerequisite for repeating a full build in a new org; UI playbook

title: Governance is org-scoped, not runtime-environment-scoped
text: Catalog sources, the published glossary, CLAIRE classifications, DQ rules and the MDM model belong to the org. Two runtime environments in one org share one governance layer by construction; only RE-bound objects (agents, per-environment connections, task sets) and the warehouse each catalog source targets differ. Isolating governance between environments needs a second org.
evidence: Live probe: identical governance objects across two REs of one org; the governance diff was empty

title: Every CDGC route is probe-derived: no vendor CDGC API guide was held
text: No Informatica CDGC REST guide was available, so every data360/ccgf route in this KB comes from live probes and browser network captures, not vendor documentation. Treat them as lower confidence than vendor-documented CAI or CDQ routes, record host, header, verb, code and date for each verdict, and re-probe when the platform build changes.
evidence: Provenance review of the endpoint corpus

title: Metadata Command Center is REST-driven; INFACore is a client-side SDK with no server endpoint
text: INFACore is a pip-installable Python/CLI SDK that authenticates to IDMC and drives a Secure Agent. It has no server-side endpoint, so a probe for an "INFACore service" 404s even when INFACore is usable; do not gate work on that 404. Drive catalog work through MCC's backing REST: catalog-source management plus the executable and observable routes.
evidence: MCC catalogsources GET 200 while INFACore probes 404

title: MCC configures and runs; Data Governance and Catalog shows the content
text: Metadata Command Center (MCC) is where catalog sources are registered, configured, run and monitored (Monitor > job > per-capability tasks and logs) and where lineage connection assignment lives (Configure > Lineage). Data Governance and Catalog (DGC) is where assets are searched and browsed and where lineage, glossary, classifications, DQ and stakeholders are shown. Its Customize/admin pages show "nothing to display" even when the catalog is full: drill Explore > source > schema > tables before calling a scan failed. Data Marketplace is a third app.

title: The CDGC asset and search APIs rate-limit with 429: walk them sequentially
text: data360 asset reads and searches answer 429 when called too fast. Run tree walks (Resource > Database > Schema > Table/View > Column, plus each column's classifications) one call at a time with an adaptive pace: start near 0.8 s between calls, add about 0.3 s and sleep about 15 s on each 429 (cap near 4 s), ease back slowly on success, and re-mint the JWT on 401. A Salesforce source holds the whole org schema (hundreds of objects, tens of thousands of fields), which exceeds a practical call budget, so walk only the objects you need.
evidence: Coverage-feed code with adaptive pacing and 429/401 handling

title: Create a catalog source: multipart part dataSource on ccgf-catalog-source-management
text: `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources` (no trailing slash: a trailing slash gives 404) as `multipart/form-data` with exactly one part named `dataSource` (`Content-Type: application/json`) holding the definition. Headers: Bearer JWT, `X-INFA-ORG-ID` and `IDS-SESSION-ID` (without `IDS-SESSION-ID` the runtime-environment validation fails). A plain JSON body returns 415; a definition without `custom` and `endOfLife` returns 500 "Custom flag cannot be null". Success returns the source with its new `id`; read it back with `GET .../datasources/<id>`. No MCC step is needed to register a source.
evidence: 415, then 500, then success; 5 sources created and verified by GET in one dm-us org (2026-09-28/29), 3 in a dmp-us org (2026-09-24/25)

title: Build a create body by cloning a working source of the same type and remapping every id
text: GET a working source of the same type and keep `name, description, type, endOfLife, custom, overrides, typeOptions, capabilities, typeCapabilities, globalConfigOptions, customAttributes`. Drop `id, createdBy, lastModifiedBy, createdTime, lastModifiedTime, seedVersion, clonedCatalogSourceId, modelVersion` (and `isDeleted`). Remap the connection id (`typeOptions` > `ConnectionId`), the runtime environment (`globalConfigOptions` > Execution > Runtime Settings > `Runtime Environment`) and any catalog id, then string-scan the JSON and assert that no old-org or old-connection id remains. A clone helper that captured but never swapped its connection argument once created a source still bound to the old warehouse.
evidence: Created sources verified by GET with no source-org ids left; the earlier clone bug found by read-back

title: List catalog-source types with GET datasourceTypes
text: `GET .../ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasourceTypes` lists the types the org can create (for example PostgreSQL, Google BigQuery, IICS). Confirm the type exists before cloning a definition. The older `GET /data360/catalog-source-management/v1/catalogsourcetypes` still returns 404; in July 2026 that 404 was read as "types can only be picked in the MCC wizard". Each listed type carries `iicsConnectionTypes`, `optionGroups` and `documentationInfo` (for PostgreSQL: `sourceSystemVersions` '10.x through 14.x', authentication modes Database and Kerberos, Data Quality exception management 'Yes'; page with `?offset=0&limit=200`). `GET .../api/v1/type/<TypeName>/capability/<CapabilityName, URL-encoded>/configuration` (for example `type/PostgreSQL/capability/Data%20Quality/configuration`) returns that capability's option groups, each option with its `name`, `dataType`, `required`, `defaultValue`, `staticValues` and `conditions` (the typeCapabilities layer, L-CDGC-143): for Data Quality the `Data Quality Scope` group offers `Sampling Type` (All Rows, Limit N Rows as the default, or Custom Query), `No of rows to limit` (default 1000), `Sampling Query` and `Runtime Environment`; Data Classification returned no option groups at the type level, so there is no classification auto-accept threshold to set there (L-CDGC-061). Build catalog-source bodies from these reads rather than guessing option keys.
evidence: Types listed before the creates of 2026-09-24; both routes 200 with the catalog identity headers, and the PostgreSQL type with its Data Quality and Data Classification configurations read (2026-10-03)

title: List and read catalog sources
text: `GET .../ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources?offset=0&limit=100` returns `datasources[]` (id, name, type and more) and `GET .../datasources/<id>` returns the full definition, which doubles as the before-state backup. The data360 form `GET https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/catalog-source-management/v1/catalogsources` also returned the sources with `totalElements` on the orgs tested.
evidence: totalElements=4 (2026-06-28); 15 existing sources listed (2026-09-24); 200 on a dm-us org (2026-09-28)

title: The catalog-source list can come back empty: keep your own name-to-id map
text: The list call has returned 0 items while MCC showed the sources: once before the full header set was sent, and once for a service login after a wave of renames. Keep a local map of source names to ids from the create responses, cross-check the UI, and never let a script conclude "missing" from an empty list. The renames in that case had to be finished in the DGC UI (ids unchanged); renaming by PUT was not tried.
evidence: 0 items vs 4 in the UI (2026-06-27); empty list for the service login (2026-09-26)

title: The data360 catalog-source-management prefix is not reliably routed: create, update and purge on the ccgf plane
text: The same `data360/catalog-source-management/v1/catalogsources` prefix answered 200 in July 2026, returned an empty-body 404 identical to its bogus twin on idmc-api, the pod host and cdgc-api for one org on 2026-08-20 (while search with the same JWT returned 200), and answered 200 again on that org on 2026-09-28. Treat it as a secondary read path. Create, update and purge through `ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources`, and re-probe before building on the data360 form.
evidence: 200 (July); empty 404 with identical bogus twin (2026-08-20); 200 (2026-09-28)

title: Update a catalog source: GET, back up, edit, multipart PUT
text: `GET .../ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>`; save the JSON as the undo file; edit it; strip the read-only fields (`id, createdBy, lastModifiedBy, createdTime, lastModifiedTime, seedVersion`, and for a clone `clonedCatalogSourceId, modelVersion`); send it as multipart part `dataSource` with `PUT .../datasources/<id>` (fall back to PATCH if PUT is refused). Include filters, the Metadata Change Option, profiling filters and lineage filters were changed this way and took effect on the next scan, so a source's object selection and capability configuration are no longer MCC-only.
evidence: Filter and change-option edits took effect on the next scans (2026-09-25 bisect helper; 2026-09-28/29 update helper)

title: Anatomy of a catalog-source definition
text: A GET returns: `type` (e.g. `PostgreSQL`, `Google BigQuery`, `IICS`, `Salesforce`, `Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse`); `typeOptions.configurationProperties[]` option groups of `{key, values[], additionalMetadata}` (a database or SaaS source carries `ConnectionId` = the v2 connection id; an IICS source carries `IICS URL`, `IICS User`, `IICS Password`); `capabilities[]` of `{capabilityName, configurationProperties[]}` (Metadata Extraction has group "Metadata Extraction OptionGroup" with `Metadata Change Option` Retain|Delete and `Type of scan` Full; Data Profiling can carry group "Data Profiling Scope"); `typeCapabilities[]` holding per-capability filters ("Metadata Filter Config", "Profiling Filter Config", "Lineage Discovery Filter Config"); `globalConfigOptions[]` with `Execution` (group "Runtime Settings" > `Runtime Environment` = `<reId>`; group "Metadata Sync Settings" > `Mode of Execution` = `Full Sync`) and `Configuration` (group "Metadata and Data Filters" > `Filter Options` = `Filter Conditions`); plus `custom`, `endOfLife`, `overrides[]`, `customAttributes`.
evidence: GET bodies of five sources of four types (2026-09-28/29)

title: Create validates the runtime environment; readyToRun=false never blocked scans
text: The create call validates the runtime environment named in `globalConfigOptions` Execution. In June 2026 it returned 500 "Error while validating Runtime Environment detail [<reId>] under global config option [Execution]" while the RE-nested `readyToRun` was false, and restarts or a brand-new RE did not clear it; the same session noted the calls probably lacked `IDS-SESSION-ID`/`X-INFA-ORG-ID`. In September 2026 creates validated once `IDS-SESSION-ID` was sent. `readyToRun=false` never blocked scans of existing sources or mapping-task runs. On a validation failure, re-send with the full header set before touching the RE.
evidence: 500 on create (2026-06-27); scans ran with readyToRun=false (2026-06-28); creates validated with IDS-SESSION-ID (2026-09-24)

title: Catalog PostgreSQL with the native connector, not JDBC
text: JDBC-based PostgreSQL scans cannot read the system catalogs (`Object(s) [pg_sequence/pg_constraint/pg_foreign_server/...] not found`), finish COMPLETED WITH ERRORS and miss sequences, constraints and foreign keys. Native PostgreSQL scans (connectorGuid `com.informatica.adapter.postgres`) read them, parse PL/pgSQL function bodies and finish Success. Use the native connector for cataloging (it is also the one DBMI/CDC needs) and retire JDBC catalog sources.
evidence: Native Sync logs Success with failed:0; JDBC runs COMPLETED WITH ERRORS

title: Catalog scanners read JDBC drivers from their own folders
text: A JDBC driver jar that makes the connection Test pass (`<agent_home>/ext/connectors/thirdparty/informatica.jdbc_v2/common/`) is not seen by the catalog scanners. Also place it under `Metadata_Foundation_Agent/.../data/browse/drivers/` (plus a per-database subfolder) and `Metadata_Platform_Service/.../lib/drivers/` (and `Database_Ingestion/.../dbmi_libs/libs/` for DBMI), then restart the agent.
evidence: Connection test and scan both succeeded only after placement in all folders

title: Microsoft Fabric catalog-source type, and types without a Data Quality capability
text: The type for a Fabric warehouse is "Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse" (connectorGuid `com.informatica.adapter.fabricdw`), one of three native Fabric types in the MCC picker; no extra entitlement was needed. A type's `typeCapabilities` may not include Data Quality at all: in one org the Fabric source could not be DQ-scored while the PostgreSQL sources could.
evidence: MCC picker listing; typeCapabilities inspection

title: PostgreSQL catalog filters are schema.*, because the scanner adds connection and database
text: A scan that fails with "None of the Assets met filter criteria" usually has filters written as `db.schema.*` (for example copied from a Snowflake source). The PostgreSQL scanner prefixes `<connection>.<database>.` itself, so the filter value must be `schema.*` (e.g. `public.*`). For warehouse sources, confirm the expected form per type: one BigQuery profiling filter was written with both `<dataset>.*` and `<project>.<dataset>.*`.
evidence: Two runs FAILED on db.schema.*; COMPLETED after the change

title: Scope a scan with the Metadata Filter Config option group
text: In `typeCapabilities` > "Metadata Extraction", add one `configurationProperties` group named "Metadata Filter Config" per pattern, with `Filter Pivot` = ["Include Metadata"], `Filter Type` (e.g. ["Data Integration"] for an IICS source, or the dataset/schema type for a database or warehouse), `Filter Value` = ["<path pattern>"] and `Filter Conditions` = ["All Types"]. Include-filter warehouse sources to their live datasets so CLAIRE does not answer from stale copies in other datasets. To isolate a failing object, a bisect helper can set one pattern, PUT, scan Metadata Extraction only, print the task statuses and restore the saved original.
evidence: Bisect runs on a failing IICS scan; CLAIRE answered from stale copies until the include filter was set

title: Set Metadata Change Option = Delete before a rescan, or removed and renamed objects stay
text: With the default `Retain`, a rescan keeps catalog objects that no longer exist in the source: a renamed database or schema leaves both trees, and deleted objects linger (and confuse CLAIRE). Set `Metadata Change Option` to `Delete` in `capabilities` > "Metadata Extraction" > "Metadata Extraction OptionGroup" (multipart PUT, L-CDGC-020) before rescanning, and extend a warehouse source's include filter to any datasets added since (e.g. CDC or real-time views) so they are cataloged too.
evidence: After Retain->Delete and a rescan, 0 stale assets were left (2026-09-29); a renamed database left only the new tree (2026-09-26)

title: IICS catalog source for CDI lineage: project include filter plus Lineage Discovery
text: A source of type `IICS` catalogs Data Integration assets for lineage. Set its Metadata Filter Config to Include / `Data Integration` / `<project>` / `All Types`, enable Metadata Extraction plus Lineage Discovery (without Lineage Discovery there are no connection-assignment recommendations and no stitched lineage), and rescan after adding new task types or lanes. Run it on a runtime environment you control, not a shared demo runtime.
evidence: Connection-assignment recommendations appeared only with Lineage Discovery enabled

title: The IICS catalog source stores a user password: rotation breaks it and its JSON is secret-bearing
text: An IICS source keeps `IICS URL`, `IICS User` and `IICS Password` in `typeOptions` and signs in as that user, so its scans fail when that password rotates. Use a dedicated service login you own (never a personal or borrowed login) and put the source on the rotation checklist. A GET returns the password option as a long opaque string (about 300 characters, probably encrypted; not verified), so treat saved source JSON backups as secret-bearing files.
evidence: Cutover rotation list item; inspection of saved GET bodies (value length only, never printed)

title: A Salesforce catalog source on a legacy v2 Salesforce connection cannot scan
text: A Salesforce source bound to a connection of the legacy v2 Salesforce type fails with "no permissions to access connections which are selected". Putting the connection's federated id into `ConnectionId` was rejected too. Use a connection of the current Salesforce connector type for catalog scans, or accept the lineage gap. The same source on the same connection scanned a day later (L-CDGC-142). Was believed 2026-09-29; overturned by L-CDGC-142.
evidence: Scan refused with that message; the federated-id variant refused as well

title: Salesforce catalog source for lineage: ViewSetup and ViewRoles, then assign the connection
text: The Salesforce integration user behind the connection needs ViewSetup and ViewRoles. After the scan, assign the IDMC Salesforce connection in MCC > Configure > Lineage > Assign Connections so mapping tasks stitch to the Salesforce objects. The source holds the whole org schema (hundreds of standard objects), so downstream tooling should filter to the objects it uses.
evidence: CLAIRE showed a custom object with 23 upstream assets across 5 hops

title: Scope warehouse sources: profiling a whole 26-dataset project took about two hours
text: Scope a BigQuery source to the datasets you need with an include filter: profiling a whole 26-dataset project took about two hours. For scale, a native PostgreSQL scan of one application database took about 51 minutes in June 2026.
evidence: Measured scan durations

title: Run a scan: POST data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id> with a non-empty capabilityNames
text: `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<catalogSourceId>` with the three identity headers and `{"capabilityNames":["Metadata Extraction","Data Profiling","Data Classification","Lineage Discovery"]}` (only capabilities configured on the source) returns 201 (200 also seen) with `jobId` and `trackingURI`. Errors: empty list = 500 "no capability is being chosen"; wrong body shape = 400 "Failed to read request"; missing header = 500 ccgf-auth-pep "Login sessionID is missing" (or 406); 406 "Job is in progress" = a run of that source is already active; GET or DELETE = 405. The same body worked on `/data360/catalog-source-management/v1/catalogsources/<id>/sync` and on the `cdgc-api` host. Every scan is IPU-metered.
evidence: 201 + jobId in June, July and September 2026 on three orgs

title: Capability names are the UI display names, e.g. Metadata Extraction
text: Use display names in `capabilityNames` and in definitions: "Metadata Extraction", "Data Profiling", "Data Classification", "Lineage Discovery", "Data Quality", "Data Observability". The UI also lists Relationship Discovery and Glossary Associations (exact API names not captured). Enum-style names such as `CATALOG_EXTRACT` from a July 2026 reference example are not what the proven runs used. Job task hierarchies also show internal steps such as "Auto Classification" and "Bulk Ingestion".
evidence: Runs accepted with display names (2026-08-20, 2026-09-24..29)

title: One source can run every capability in one scan; Data Quality also runs alone once its Scope groups carry a runtime environment
text: A source configured with Metadata Extraction, Lineage Discovery, Data Profiling, Data Quality and Data Observability produces catalog, lineage, profiles, DQ results and observability in one run when all are listed in `capabilityNames`. Data Observability depends on profiling and is skipped when profiling fails. Submitting `{"capabilityNames":["Data Quality"]}` alone returned 406 in July, but it runs on its own (Rule Profiling, Batch Profiling and Score Propagation, about 15 min for a warehouse source) once the source's `typeCapabilities` carry the Data Profiling Scope and Data Quality Scope groups with a runtime environment (L-CDGC-143).
evidence: One run produced catalog, profiling and DQ per source (2026-06-27); DQ-only run 406 (2026-07-09); DQ-only runs COMPLETED with Score Propagation after the Scope groups were added (2026-09-30)

title: Poll one job at observable/v1/jobs/<jobId>; list jobs at observable/api/v1/jobs
text: Poll one job: `GET https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/observable/v1/jobs/<jobId>?expandChildren=TASK-HIERARCHY` returns `status` (CREATED, QUEUED, SUBMITTED, STARTING, RUNNING, then COMPLETED, PARTIAL_COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED or ABORTED) and `tasks[]` with each capability's `name` and `status`. List jobs: `GET .../data360/observable/api/v1/jobs?limit=N` (the `/api/` infix is required on the list; the list form without it 404s) with `metadata.totalElements`. The run response's `trackingURI` points at the single-job route. Poll every 20-40 s.
evidence: List 200 with totalElements=463 (2026-07-10); single-job polls to COMPLETED (2026-06-28, 2026-09-24, 2026-09-29)

title: A failed scan start can be transient: wait 60-90 s and retry once
text: When the run call fails for a source that has no active job, wait 60-90 s and retry once before investigating; a queue helper that did this cleared failed starts. Do not loop: a 406 means a job holds the lock (L-CDGC-040).
evidence: Queue helper retry succeeded on the second attempt

title: A started scan is not a governed catalog
text: 201 or 406 only mean a run was accepted or is active. Report success only when every capability task in the job hierarchy is COMPLETED and sampled assets show the results you expect: `core.profiled=True`, a `lastProfiledState` other than "Not Profiled", non-empty `patternStatistics`, classifications, and a fresh `lastScanned`. Report metadata extraction separately from profiling, DQ, lineage, observability and classification. PARTIAL_COMPLETED (UI "Completed with Errors") means published with some assets skipped: read the task log.
evidence: About 3,900 assets indexed while every sampled column was unprofiled (2026-06-28)

title: No REST cancel for a running scan, and a stuck job locks the source
text: Every cancel variant tried returned 404 or 405, including `POST .../data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id>/cancel` (404). Cancel in MCC (Catalog Sources or Monitor). While a stuck job holds the source's lock, every run returns 406 and a delete returns 400 "Job is in progress ... cancel current job", so automation that loops "run until accepted" never succeeds.
evidence: 404/405 on every cancel variant; 400 on DELETE while locked

title: Verify a scan from the agent's scanner Sync log
text: When status APIs are unclear, read `<agent_home>/apps/Metadata_Foundation_Agent/data/workspaces/<source>-<uuid>/logs/<jobId>_Sync.log`. Success markers: `Metadata extraction application completed`, `ProcessEnd status:Success`, counters with `failed:0`, `BULK_CONTENT_PUBLISHER "Writing N records"`, and a `BulkIngestionResponse` ingestionTaskId with Success. Confirm no scanner processes remain before calling a job stuck. A literal "not found" in these logs can be text inside a cataloged function body (e.g. a `RAISE EXCEPTION`), not an error.
evidence: Sync-log markers proved four sources published (411 tables, 3,620 columns, 481 FKs)

title: Benign COMPLETED WITH ERRORS on PostgreSQL, and orphan RUNNING rows after a delete
text: A PostgreSQL scan under the LENIENT strategy reports COMPLETED WITH ERRORS (e.g. 15/24 tasks) when it skips C-language extension functions (e.g. pgcrypto: "Only supported languages SQL, PL/pgSQL"); tables, columns, profiles and DQ are still ingested. After a source is deleted, Monitor can keep showing its `*_sync` job rows as RUNNING: with no scanner process and a completed Sync log they are display orphans.
evidence: All tables and columns ingested despite the status; 0 scanner processes behind the RUNNING rows

title: Diagnose PARTIAL_COMPLETED profiling and exclude the failing table
text: If Data Profiling ends PARTIAL_COMPLETED, one table failed. The observable job API exposes no error detail (MCC shows e.g. "3 objects discovered, 1 profiled, 2 failed"); `<agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/logs/s_cp_*_session.log` names the table. Causes seen: pgvector columns, a BigQuery column named `rows` (the generated profiling SQL chokes on it) and transient BigQuery 503s. Fix: add a "Profiling Filter Config" group that excludes the table (`Filter Type` Tables, `Filter Value` schema.table) to the Data Profiling type capability, PUT the source back and re-run Data Profiling only; the table stays in the catalog. The include form of that group uses `Filter Pivot` "Include Metadata".
evidence: Profiling re-runs completed after the excludes (2026-09-24); empty error detail on a 9-second failure (2026-07-09)

title: Only Data Profiling launches the native DTM: profiling-only failures point at the agent
text: Metadata Extraction, Lineage, Data Quality and Classification run in the Java scanner and cloud services; Data Profiling launches the native `pmdtm` engine on the agent. If metadata is cataloged but zero columns are ever profiled, read the pmdtm exit code on the agent: 127 = a native library failed to load (e.g. `libidn.so.11` on Debian 12), 134 = SIGABRT, 137 = OOM. It was not a stuck job, readyToRun or auth. A source without the Data Profiling capability never profiles, and the native PostgreSQL connector skips json, enum and array columns (cast them in views added to the scope).
evidence: Exit-127 count matched the unprofiled sources; the library fix restored profiling

title: Turn the agent's Metadata services on only for the scan window, and scan one source at a time
text: On-agent scans run in `Metadata_Foundation_Agent` and `Metadata_Platform_Service` (with DIS and Connector_Service), which cost several GB of RAM and a lot of CPU on a small host. Select them on the runtime environment just before the scan window (`PUT .../runtime/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>/selections/ui`; each PUT can roll engines to newer versions and queue work for about 5 minutes), scan sources one after another (profiling only where needed), then deselect them.
evidence: Deselecting after the window: MemAvailable 10.1 -> 13.8 GB and CPU pressure 16-19% -> ~10% on a 32 GB host

title: An IICS source rescan failed at Catalog Source Extraction after a file-based lane was added (open)
text: After flat-file based tasks were added to a cataloged project, rescans of the IICS source failed at the Catalog Source Extraction step while the earlier lineage assets stayed intact. Root cause not found as of 2026-09-26. Rescan once in a quiet window, read the extraction task, and bisect the include filter (L-CDGC-027) to isolate the object.
evidence: Repeated FAILED status at the extraction step

title: REST DELETE purges a catalog source's metadata; the definition needs an MCC UI delete
text: `DELETE https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>` starts a bulk purge job that removes the harvested metadata, but the catalog-source definition stays listed: delete it in MCC > Catalog Sources and keep an id list for that UI step. Back up the source JSON (GET) and harvest its GUID-keyed links first (L-CDGC-084). History: in June 2026 a DELETE on the data360 prefix returned 400 "Job is in progress" (route live, lock held); in August 2026 it returned an empty 404 on one org.
evidence: Purge jobs COMPLETED; the definitions were still listed afterwards

title: A catalog source that holds a connection blocks the connection delete
text: `DELETE /api/v2/connection/<id>` returns 403 `REPO_10242` while mappings reference the connection. Once those are gone, a generic "asset used by another asset" means a catalog source still holds it: purge the source (or repoint it) before deleting the connection.
evidence: Error progression REPO_10242 -> used by another asset

title: Repoint a moved database by updating the connection in place: catalog sources stay bound
text: When a source database moves, update the existing connection with `POST <serverUrl>/api/v2/connection/<id>` (full body, secrets re-supplied, because GET masks them) instead of creating a new connection. Catalog sources and mapping tasks that reference the connection id stay bound, and scans that failed after the move recover on their next run.
evidence: 4/4 connection tests SUCCESS with ids preserved; failed scans recovered

title: Create a glossary domain through data360 content
text: `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/content/v1/assets` with the identity headers and `{"core.classType":"com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.Domain","summary":{"core.name":"<name>","core.description":"<description>"}}`. The response carries `core.identity` (the internal UUID used in later calls) and `core.externalId` (`DOM-<n>`). A status of 300 or more is a failure; read the domain back by search.
evidence: Domains created in two orgs and read back by search

title: Create business terms headless with data360/content/v1/assets
text: Same route and headers as a domain, with `{"core.classType":"com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.BusinessTerm","summary":{"core.name":"<name>","core.description":"<definition>"},"parent":{"core.identity":"<domainIdentity>"}}`. Terms land in lifecycle Published with externalId `BT-<n>`; a term without `parent` was also accepted (2026-09-24). The term Hierarchy (term > subdomain > domain) resolves from the parent (reads show `__meta.parentLocation`), so no extra write is needed for it. The old `glossary/v1/terms` and `businessTerms` paths stay 404.
evidence: 6 terms (2026-09-24); 33 terms in each of two orgs (2026-09-28/29), all Published

title: Make glossary scripts idempotent and reversible
text: Search before create: ES `term` on `core.classType` (Domain or BusinessTerm), match `core.name`, and for a term require the domain identity inside `core.location`. Keep a registry file (key > identity, externalId, source id) written after each create; on re-run reuse what exists; an `--undo` mode deletes registry items in reverse order. Write an undo JSON of every description you replace before the PATCH. Rebuild a glossary in another org from a read-only export of the source org, because glossary content does not travel in the v3 package (L-CDGC-071).
evidence: Re-runs created nothing twice; undo files used for the renames

title: Rename or redefine terms and domains with PATCH by external id
text: `PATCH https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/content/v1/assets/<externalId>?scheme=external` (slash-free ids such as `BT-<n>` or `DOM-<n>`) or `.../assets/<identity>?scheme=internal`, body `[{"operation":"replace","segment":"summary","attributes":{"core.name":"<new name>","core.description":"<new definition>"}}]`. Save the old values first. Catalog readers (CLAIRE, read-back feeds) pick the change up on their next refresh; no UI rename is needed.
evidence: Several terms and one domain renamed and redefined, confirmed on read-back

title: Write the data dictionary: PATCH asset descriptions
text: Harvest the source first so the column assets exist, resolve each column's `core.identity` by search (L-CDGC-057), then `PATCH .../data360/content/v1/assets/<identity>?scheme=internal` with `[{"operation":"replace","segment":"summary","attributes":{"core.description":"<text>"}}]`. The same works for catalog-source Resource, Database and Schema assets (curated descriptions). Keep the previous descriptions in an undo file.
evidence: 14 column descriptions (2026-09-24); 11 curated container descriptions (2026-09-28), visible on read-back

title: A scan can overwrite curated descriptions when the source object has none
text: A later scan may replace catalog-side descriptions with the source's blank description. Also set descriptions in the source system (warehouse dataset, table and view descriptions; CRM field help) so rescans carry them, and re-run the idempotent curation script after every scan of that source.
evidence: Curated descriptions reverted after a scan

title: Link a term to an asset headless: PATCH segment glossary
text: `PATCH https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/content/v1/assets/<assetIdentity>?scheme=internal` with `[{"operation":"add","segment":"glossary","items":[{"core.identity":"<termIdentity>"}]}]` returns 200 or 204. Resolve the asset identity from its externalId by search first (L-CDGC-057) and log each pair (term|externalId > linked, missing-asset or error) so re-runs skip finished links. This overturns the July 2026 verdict that term-to-column binding was UI-only.
evidence: 11 links (2026-09-24), 47 links (2026-09-28) and 42 links in a second org (2026-09-29), each visible on the asset

title: Resolve identities with an ES terms query on core.externalId: slash ids break GET-by-path
text: Asset external ids contain slashes, e.g. `<catalogSourceId>://<db>/<schema>/<table>/<column>~com.infa.odin.models.relational.Column`, so a GET or PATCH with one in the URL path fails with 400 (encoded slashes) or does not resolve. Resolve with `POST .../data360/search/api/v1/search` and `{"query":{"terms":{"core.externalId":["<externalId>"]}}}` (or `term`), take `hits.hits[0].sourceAsMap["core.identity"]`, and address `.../assets/<identity>?scheme=internal`. Slash-free external ids (`DOM-<n>`, `BT-<n>`, classification ids) do work in the path with `?scheme=external`.
evidence: 400 on the path GET; every link, classification and description update of two orgs resolved its identity by search

title: External ids embed the catalog source id, and domain numbers differ per org
text: Every harvested asset's externalId starts with its catalog source id: the root is `<csId>://<csId>~core.Resource`, then `...~com.infa.odin.models.relational.Database|Schema|Table|View|Column`. Recreating a source (another org, or delete and recreate) gives new ids, so map old to new by replacing the source-id prefix, and try both the `Table` and the `View` suffix because the same object can be cataloged as either. `DOM-<n>` numbers and internal identities also differ per org: read them from per-org configuration, never hard-code them.
evidence: A target dry run found 33 terms and 6 classifications once the ids came from per-org config

title: DELETE of a Published term can report success while the term stays
text: `DELETE .../data360/content/v1/assets/<identity>?scheme=internal` on a Published business term returned "deleted" while the term stayed in search. Verify every delete with a search read-back. If a term persists, rename it "<name> (retired duplicate)" with a pointer to its replacement, move it out of Published, or remove it in the UI. Domain and term deletes during a later cleanup were reported done, so the outcome may depend on lifecycle state; the read-back is the only reliable signal.
evidence: Term still searchable after the API reported it deleted

title: Apply a data-element classification manually: PATCH segment dataClassification
text: Classifications are `core.DataElementClassification` assets: page an ES `term` query on `core.classType` = `core.DataElementClassification` and key the hits by `core.name` (e.g. "Email", "Phone Number USA"). Apply one with `PATCH .../data360/content/v1/assets/<columnIdentity>?scheme=internal` and `[{"operation":"add","segment":"dataClassification","items":[{"core.identity":"<classificationIdentity>"}]}]`; the asset page then shows "Data Element Classifications Accepted". Only classifications that exist in the org can be applied (there may be First Name but no Full Name). Use this when Auto Classification infers nothing or to curate a reviewed list.
evidence: UI showed 'Data Element Classifications Accepted (1) Email' (2026-09-24); 6 classifications applied in each of two orgs

title: Bulk-accepting CLAIRE-generated classifications has no public data360 REST path
text: CLAIRE-generated data-element classifications carry `core.generatedClassification`; nothing on the data360 plane flipped them to `core.acceptedClassification`: `POST /data360/classification/api/v1/accept`, `/dataclassification/.../accept`, `PUT .../status` and `/catalog/.../accept` all 404, `POST /public/core/v3/objects` 405, per-object PATCH 404 (37+ variants). In that tenant the UI auto-applied them and offered only a per-item Dismiss (X). The bulk lever is the catalog source's Data Classification capability (auto-accept threshold) applied on a re-scan. Not re-probed in September 2026 against the content-API segments; manual curation (L-CDGC-060) and the browser-captured Classification Promotion job (L-CDGC-063) are the known partial routes.
evidence: 404/405 on 37+ variants on the data360 and catalog-source planes; browser check of the UI controls

title: CLAIRE-generated classifications are not the built-in Data Element Classifications
text: CLAIRE generates custom classifications, often one per column name (e.g. "Booking Identifier"), that do not map to the roughly 230 built-in Data Element Classifications (regulatory PII such as passport, tax id and IBAN, plus Email, Name, Gender, Address). Promote only exact matches; bulk-promoting business-name classes as PII corrupts governance. A wrong promotion was reverted with curationStatus REJECTED.
evidence: Thousands of generated classes vs about 230 built-in targets; 4 exact matches; one wrong promotion reverted

title: Classification Promotion job on the ccgf-api host (browser-captured once)
text: The UI promoted classifications with `POST https://ccgf-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-orchestration-management-api-server/api/v1/management/job` with type 'Classification Promotion', which returned 200 + jobId; the undo was `POST .../ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/publish` with curationStatus REJECTED. It was seen once, from an authenticated browser session; the body is not recorded, it was never re-proven headless, and a same-day browser check of another tenant found only Dismiss (L-CDGC-061). Earlier 404s on idmc-api were on the wrong host.
evidence: 200 + jobId once (2026-07-09); conflicting UI observation the same day

title: Classification is not profiling, and Auto Classification can infer nothing
text: CLAIRE classifies from names and metadata, so it also covers empty tables; profiling computes statistics from rows (`core.average`, `minValue`, `maxValue`, `distinctCount`, `nullPercentage`, `patternStatistics`, `inferredDataType`), so it covers only tables with data. Expect classified counts well above profiled counts. In another org, Auto Classification inferred nothing even with fresh profiles: curate manually (L-CDGC-060).
evidence: 2,582 of 3,136 columns classified vs 671 profiled (2026-06-28); 0 inferred (2026-09-24)

title: ccgf-contentv2 publish: the 207 Multi-Status write plane; an empty items list means nothing was written
text: `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/publish` with the identity headers (one capture also sent `X-INFA-PRODUCT-ID` with any value) returns 207 Multi-Status + job id; read each item's status in the 207 and re-GET. Proven for a term-to-column relationship (type `IClassTechnicalGlossaryBase`, `curationStatus` ACCEPTED, item 201, link count 0 -> 1 on read-back) and for REJECTED curation. A data-flow lineage edge published in one test came back as 207 with `items: []` and changed nothing; RELATIONSHIP items with `core.DataSetDataFlow` or `core.DirectionalDataFlow` are written (L-CDGC-179). For term links today, prefer the content PATCH segments (L-CDGC-056).
evidence: 207 with item 201 and a read-back link (2026-07-09); 207 with items:[] for lineage edges (2026-08-20)

title: Steward and data-owner (stakeholder) assignment had no REST write
text: Asset stakeholder attributes (`core.assignedStakeholders`, `core.stakeholders`) are read-only over REST: stewardship, stakeholder and responsibility paths 404, `/data360/asset/v1/*/stakeholders` 404/405 (PUT 405) across 100+ variants, per-object PATCH 404, and there is no stakeholder object to clone. `PUT /dataCollections/<id>` with stakeholder ids echoes 200 but does not persist. Assign in MCC > Associations > Stakeholders > Assign Stakeholders (roles must exist in Administrator) and keep ownership as code (a RACI table) as the authoritative store. Not re-probed with the September 2026 content-API segments.
evidence: 404/405 across 100+ variants; echo-only 200 disproved by re-GET

title: DAM policy authoring has no REST plane on the probed orgs; demonstrate the controls as pushdown
text: Data Access Management can be entitled and running (`feature.cdam.*` flags, `Data_Access_Management_Agent` engine RUNNING) while its policy API (`cdam-policy-api`, about 40 `/data360/dam/v1/policies` variants) 404s on every verb, `<pod>-dam` has no DNS and the DAM policy census is 0. Build the first policy in the UI. The verdict is org-scoped: a third-party tool fleet ships policy tools, so ask which path they call before calling it a platform wall. Meanwhile the three control types (access control, row filter, de-identification) can be demonstrated as warehouse views or table functions that compute the same result.
evidence: 404 on about 40 variants with the engine RUNNING; pushdown views returned the expected masked, filtered and generalized rows

title: Governance-as-code for policies and PII inventories
