text: When native policy or classification writes are walled, publish governance as versioned files: a policy catalog (name, legal basis, mandated control, enforcement, owner) linked to datasets through the PII classification, and a PII data-entity inventory built from the CLAIRE catalog export plus a live schema pass (the catalog reflects only the last scan; a schema pass found tables and columns it missed). Bind protection to classification tags rather than raw columns so new columns inherit it, and test with assertions (every PII entity governed, every link points at a real policy).
evidence: Assertion suites passed; the schema pass caught 24 columns the catalog lacked

title: Propagate PII classifications down lineage with a worklist script
text: Where derived columns (downstream marts, a second warehouse) lack classifications, walk lineage from classified source columns, propose the same class for each derived column, review the worklist and apply it (today with the dataClassification PATCH, L-CDGC-060).
evidence: 155 propagated classifications proposed

title: QuickLook is a client-side browser extension with no server enablement
text: QuickLook (in-context glossary definitions) is a per-user Chrome/Edge extension. `/data360/quicklook/*` 404s and there is no server enablement surface; it needs a per-analyst install and sign-in. The org-side prerequisite is a browsable catalog with published terms.
evidence: 404 while a positive control on the same host and auth returned 200

title: CDGC content does not travel in a v3 migration package
text: A v3 export of a catalog-asset identity returns 400 `MigrationSvc_034` "Object resolution failed", and `POST /public/core/v3/objects` is 405 (the v3 object catalog is read-only). Catalog sources, glossary domains and terms, links, curated descriptions, classifications and stakeholders are not carried by export/import, and the migration role does not change that. Rebuild them in the target through the ccgf and data360 APIs from a read-only export of the source org (L-CDGC-104).
evidence: 400 MigrationSvc_034 (2026-07-04); a 223-object package carried no CDGC content (2026-09-28)

title: Make CLAIRE GPT answer business questions from the glossary
text: Create a glossary domain whose description states what the company does and its goal; add a term for every business concept (and one that explains legacy technical names); link each term to its physical assets; write curated descriptions on catalog sources, databases and schemas; and set descriptions in the source system too, so rescans keep them. Script it idempotently with undo files, then test with a fixed question set phrased as "the business term X". Prompt rules are in the CLAIRE folder.
evidence: 18 of 18 test questions answered correctly

title: Search the catalog: POST data360/search/api/v1/search with an Elasticsearch body
text: `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/search/api/v1/search` (optionally `?knowledgeQuery=*&segments=all`) with Bearer JWT, `X-INFA-ORG-ID`, `IDS-SESSION-ID` and `X-INFA-SEARCH-LANGUAGE: elasticsearch`; the body is raw Elasticsearch DSL, e.g. `{"from":0,"size":200,"query":{"term":{"core.classType":"com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.BusinessTerm"}}}`, `{"query":{"terms":{"core.externalId":["<id>"]}}}` or `{"query":{"match_all":{}}}`. Results are in `hits.hits[].sourceAsMap` (`core.identity`, `core.externalId`, `core.name`, `core.location`, `core.description`) with `hits.total.value`, which caps at 10000 with `relation: "gte"`. GET is 405.
evidence: 200 with real hits from 2026-06-28 to 2026-09-29 (e.g. 369 table hits for one term; 10000+ for match_all)

title: data360/search/v1/assets works once knowledgeQuery and segments are sent
text: `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/search/v1/assets?knowledgeQuery=<query or *>&segments=all` (or a list such as `summary,systemAttributes,dataClassification`) with body `{"from":0,"size":<n>}` returns `hits[]`, each with `core.identity`, `summary`, and `systemAttributes` (`core.classType`, `core.origin` = the catalog source id). The total is a quick harvest check. The July 2026 "400 MissingServletRequestParameter forever" on this path was the missing `knowledgeQuery` query parameter. For exact filters prefer the Elasticsearch endpoint (L-CDGC-073).
evidence: 5,089 cataloged assets returned (2026-09-24); coverage probes (2026-09-28)

title: Read one asset with chosen segments; walk the tree through neighborhood
text: `GET https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/search/v1/assets/<identity>?scheme=internal&segments=<list>`; segments include `summary`, `systemAttributes`, `selfAttributes`, `customAttributes`, `neighborhood`, `dataClassification` or `all`. `scheme=external` works for slash-free external ids. `neighborhood` lists typed edges (ParentChild confirmed) to walk Resource > Database > Schema > Table/View > Column. A classification asset's `selfAttributes.core.sensitivity` is CDGC's own rating (e.g. Email = MEDIUM), which lets a script count PII columns as those whose classification is MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL.
evidence: Coverage walks over three sources of two types

title: An unknown field in a search query returns 500, not 400
text: The search API answers 500 for an unknown field name, which reads like an outage (a false red). Use exact field names: `core.profiled=True` for profiling status (200 with real counts), and `core.generatedClassification` / `core.acceptedClassification` for classification (the direct `/data360/classification/api/v1/classifications` read 404s).
evidence: Wrong field = 500; `core.profiled` = 200 with 1,755 profiled / 9,070 not

title: Measure coverage from search counts and state the grain
text: Count hits with `core.profiled=True` for profiling coverage and with `core.generatedClassification` present for CLAIRE coverage; use `core.Resource` hits and per-class aggregates to count sources, tables, columns, keys and schemas; check `lastScanned` to prove a scan ran rather than a configured-only source. Asset-grain and column-grain counts differ (e.g. 1,755 profiled assets vs 671 profiled columns) and the search total caps at 10,000, so name the grain and aggregate per class.
evidence: Counts reconciled against scanner logs and per-source totals

title: Page with a stable sort and dedupe; free-text results are not stable handles
text: Search is Elasticsearch-backed and relevance-ranked. Deep paging with `from`/`size` and no stable sort returned overlapping pages (114 duplicates and 114 missing rows in a 7,464-column extract). Request one page larger than the per-source total or add a stable sort key, dedupe by `core.identity`, and reconcile the distinct count with the known total. The same free-text query can return different hits and order across runs, so never cache "the top hit" as a handle: resolve by exact externalId or name at use time.
evidence: Distinct count matched 7,464 after the fix (2026-07-13); differing hits across runs (2026-07-26)

title: 'classType filter ignored': a filter parameter was, but an ES term query on core.classType filters
text: A third-party tool fleet reported that its `classType` filter parameter is accepted and has no effect, which returns plausible wrong results; the outcome of a `filterSpec` body probe on `search/v1/assets` is not recorded. In contrast, an ES `term` query on `core.classType` inside the `search/api/v1/search` body returned only that class (a RuleInstance census; BusinessTerm, Domain and DataElementClassification lookups). Use the ES term query, and still check `core.classType` on each hit.
evidence: RuleInstance census returned 8 rule instances (2026-07-09); class lookups drove two glossary rebuilds (2026-09-28/29)

title: In the UI, AI 'Query' search can return 0 while Keyword search works
text: In some orgs the default CDGC AI search (type=Query) returns 0 results for everything while Keyword search (`cgsearch/<id>?query=<term>&type=Keyword` in the UI) works. Use Keyword search for demos and scripted UI checks until AI search is confirmed in that org.
evidence: 66 Keyword results vs 0 Query results for the same term

title: ccgf-searchv2 accepts only a subset of Elasticsearch queries
text: `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-searchv2/api/v1/search` with `x-infa-search-language: elasticsearch` worked for read-back checks, but only with `multi_match`, `term`, `match_all` and `bool` (plus `aggs`), not `query_string`, `wildcard` or `match`. Prefer `data360/search/api/v1/search` (L-CDGC-073).
evidence: Read-back verification runs

title: Census DQ rule instances in the catalog; rule occurrences had no create API
text: `POST .../data360/search/api/v1/search` with `{"query":{"term":{"core.classType":"com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.RuleInstance"}},"size":200}` lists rule instances; scores appear only on instances whose occurrence actually ran. The CDGC rule occurrence (the scoring bind) could only be created in the CDGC DQ wizard, reading scores meant scraping the asset's Score tab, and six identical occurrences once scored 1 of 6. Build scorecards on the Data Profiling service instead (DQ folder). Was believed 2026-07-09; overturned by L-CDGC-144.
evidence: 8 rule instances, 1 scored; MCC job error text

title: Export governance intelligence per entity and reconcile every count
text: To move catalog intelligence out of CDGC (migration, backup, another catalog), extract per-entity rows: column > classification, term > asset links, lineage edge pairs with both endpoints, rule > column bindings. Page every query to completion and reconcile each class count against a separately measured inventory; a first pass that returns counts plus samples, or caps a bucket (e.g. 500 of 1,526 classification types), silently loses most of the data. Carry CLAIRE classifications over as data: a rule-based classifier in another catalog does not reproduce them.
evidence: All 10 counts matched the inventory after the per-entity re-extract

title: Harvest GUID-keyed links and classifications before purging or replacing a source
text: Term links and accepted classifications attach to the asset GUIDs of one catalog source. Before deleting or replacing a source, export a name-keyed manifest (asset path > terms, classifications) so they can be re-applied once the replacement is scanned; when names differ between the retired and live sources, match assets by column-set Jaccard similarity.
evidence: 52 links and 231 classifications were keyed to a source about to be retired

title: No lineage-graph REST: read lineage through MCP get_asset_details
text: `/data360/lineage/*` (25+ variants) returned 404 from every client in July 2026, so the interactive graph is UI-only (DGC > asset > Lineage tab, with a Data Element level). The CDGC Metadata Search MCP action `get_asset_details` returned lineage together with profile and descriptions and was the only programmatic lineage read found; the asset `neighborhood` segment exposes typed edges (ParentChild confirmed; data-flow edge types not verified). Not re-probed in September 2026. Was believed 2026-07-25 to 2026-10-07; overturned by L-CDGC-156, L-CDGC-181.
evidence: 404 from the laptop and from an agent VM on 25+ variants

title: Column-level CDI lineage: an IICS source, physical sources and connection assignment
text: Catalog the physical systems (e.g. PostgreSQL and BigQuery sources with Metadata Extraction, Data Profiling and Data Classification) and an IICS source over the project's Data Integration assets with Lineage Discovery (L-CDGC-029). In MCC > Configure > Lineage for the IICS source, accept CLAIRE's connection-assignment recommendations (the UI calls `POST .../ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/assignment/recommendation/catalog-source`; scores of 71-100% seen) or assign connections by hand. Result: column-level lineage source table > mapping task > landing table > next task > raw table. A "Lineage Discovery Filter Config" group (`Filter Pivot` Include, `Filter Type` "Catalog Source Name", `Filter Value` = source names) limits which sources it stitches to (set by PUT; effect not recorded). After the IICS source is scanned in a new org, its task references to source and target connections can stay unresolved (`core.resolvedStatus` empty, CLAIRE answering '0 upstream assets'). The pending fix is an asset of class `core.ConnectionAssignmentRecommendation` (find it with an Elasticsearch `term` on `core.classType`) that names the target catalog source, a score (100 seen), the number of objects it covers (966 seen) and action NONE. The accept call is `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/assignment/connectionAssignment?operationType=ASSIGN` (live: 422 for a malformed body, 500 for a bogus twin); a body shape read from the catalog UI bundle and not yet executed is `{sourceRootAsset:{externalId, origin, location}, targetRootAsset:[{externalId, origin, isCaseSensitive, location}], initialAssignment:true, modifyAssignment:false}` (UNASSIGN reverses), with candidates from `GET .../ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v2/connections/endpointsQuery/<referenceDataSourceId>?recommendations=true` (an Elasticsearch query to run on the search API). Until that is proven, accept in the UI: Metadata Command Center > Explore > Catalog Sources > click the ROW of the IICS source (not its name) > right pane 'Related Catalog Sources' > the recommendation card ('1 Pending', '100 % Recommendation') > Accept; then re-run Lineage Discovery headless and check `core.resolvedStatus`. A Lineage Discovery run can also auto-accept (L-CDGC-140), which is necessary but not sufficient for job-level lineage (L-CDGC-148). Was believed 2026-09-30; overturned by L-CDGC-159.
evidence: Lineage rendered end to end on a landing table (screenshot evidence); the recommendation asset read over search, the accept route 422 against 500 for its bogus twin, and the card path walked by a browser harness (2026-09-29/30)

title: Database scans derive lineage only from view SQL (and CDI mappings through an IICS source)
text: A database scan derives data-flow lineage from a view's SQL, not from base tables: a table materialized by a CDI mapping gets only containment from the database scan (its logic lives in the mapping, visible only through an IICS source). A view's lineage appears only when the view is inside the Metadata Extraction include scope, Lineage Discovery is enabled and the source is rescanned; Metadata Extraction alone did not even catalog a newly added view (0 nodes right after a successful scan). Keep a record that must show fan-in lineage as a view or a mapping target. Relationship Discovery (similar columns and join keys, containment-score threshold of 0.4 or more) is not lineage.
evidence: 0 nodes and 0 edges after a Metadata-Extraction-only scan; an existing view's upstream edges derived automatically

title: Grey 'referenced' lineage nodes mean an unassigned connection
text: Upstream nodes shown as grey "referenced" stubs in the Lineage tab turn into real assets once their connection is assigned in MCC > Configure > Lineage > Assign Connections (for PostgreSQL the endpoint class is Database).
evidence: UI playbook grounded in the vendor docs and a live org

title: Prove lineage from warehouse metadata when the graph cannot be read
text: When the lineage graph cannot be read programmatically, prove resolution source > bronze > silver > gold with probe fields: check each key column exists at every layer in the warehouse INFORMATION_SCHEMA and cross-check the documented mapping edges. Governance overlays (worst failing DQ rule per node; a marketplace-requestable flag per node) can be built from catalog exports plus governance views, with no native overlay API.
evidence: 3 of 3 probe fields resolved at every layer

title: CLAIRE lags fresh scans, goes blind while a source scans, and trips on duplicate sources
text: CLAIRE GPT answers from the catalog index. Newly created or rescanned sources were unanswerable for hours; about 30 minutes after a migration, glossary and PII questions passed while lineage and NL-to-SQL still failed (probably index lag). While a source's scan is RUNNING, CLAIRE returns "no relevant information" for its assets, so do not rescan within about 40 minutes of a demo. Legacy duplicate sources with the same table names and stale copies in other datasets make CLAIRE pick the wrong asset: purge them and include-filter the live sources, then retest before switching a demo to a new org.
evidence: Parity test after a migration (2026-09-29); answerability times (2026-09-24); blind during a scan (2026-09-26)

title: Mapping tasks are not catalog assets, and SQL inside a task hides lineage
text: CDI mapping tasks are not catalog assets, so CLAIRE finds nothing for a task name. Business logic kept in a source custom-query string is invisible to lineage below table level and shows as a two-box canvas; visual transformations (Joiners, Expressions, Aggregators) are what give column-level lineage.
evidence: CLAIRE 'no information found' for task names; audit of a copy-data pipeline

title: Create and read Marketplace data assets (data products) over REST
text: `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/marketplace/api/v1/dataAssets` with the identity headers creates a data asset (201, status PUBLISHED); `GET` lists them with `totalCount`; a bad body gives 400 (the verb exists). The same create also answered on `cdgc-api`. The asset's `technicalAssetName` points it at the governed physical asset. `PUT` is vendor-documented and an idempotent update was reported; `.../dataAssets/<id>/dataElements` GET/POST/PUT are documented only.
evidence: 201 and GET totalCount=5 all PUBLISHED (2026-07-04); another product created and read back (2026-08-20)

title: Marketplace v1: collections, categories, terms of use and orders
text: On `idmc-api` with the three identity headers: `GET|POST /data360/marketplace/api/v1/dataCollections` (201, PUBLISHED, with a category), `categories` (200/201), `termsOfUse` (201; `type` CONSTRAINED, NEUTRAL or PERMISSIVE, `acknowledgement` BOOLEAN, `status` ENABLED) and `orders` (201, status PENDING until fulfilled). Re-GET after every write.
evidence: 201s with re-GET confirmation

title: Marketplace v2: data-collections, delivery-targets and orders
text: `https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/marketplace/api/v2`: `GET /data-collections` (200), `GET|POST /delivery-targets` (POST 201 creates a delivery target for a collection) and `POST /orders` (201). Delivery templates are not on this plane: `/api/v2/delivery-targets/templates` is the wrong place (GET 400, POST 405).
evidence: POST 200/201 on targets and orders (2026-07-09); v2 collections totalCount 5 (2026-07-10)

title: Provisioning reads on cdgc-api give the template, format and method ids
text: `GET https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/cdmp-marketplace/api/v1/provisioning/deliveryTemplates` (also `deliveryFormats` and `deliveryMethods`) returns `objects[]` with the UUIDs that delivery targets and orders need; the routes were found by browser network capture. The bare `/provisioning` returns 500 (wrong request shape, not an absent service) on both cdgc-api and idmc-api.
evidence: 200 with live objects on two dates

title: Creating a Marketplace delivery template is UI-only: automate it in a headed browser
text: Every REST verb on template creation returned 405. The Marketplace app (`https://cdmp-app.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/`, reached by SSO after login) stalls headless because its bootstrap makes cross-origin calls, so drive it in a headed browser (xvfb on servers). In Setup > Delivery the dropdowns are react-select (options match `[class*='-option']`; `role=option` belongs to a background grid, and Escape closes the modal), and fields carry `data-testid` values such as `field_deliveryType`, `field_deliveryFormatIds` and `field_deliveryMethodIds`.
evidence: Template created by browser automation and an order fulfilled through it (2026-07-09)

title: The Marketplace provisioning chain end to end
text: Delivery Format + Delivery Method > Delivery Template (an Automatic template grants access with no manual task) > a Delivery Target per data collection > an Order, which fulfils (COMPLETE) and grants the consumer access (AVAILABLE). Orders placed before any delivery target exists stay PENDING and do not recover, so create targets first. Approval and access-key verbs on orders (approve, PATCH, DELETE) returned 405.
evidence: Order COMPLETE with access AVAILABLE; earlier orders stuck PENDING

title: Marketplace ratings, stakeholders, comments and consumer chat are UI-only
text: `POST` or `PUT /data360/marketplace/api/v1/dataAssets/<id>/ratings` returns 405, the stakeholder and comment sub-resources return 405, and consumer chat has no REST. `PUT /dataCollections/<id>` with stakeholder ids echoes 200 without persisting. The split is by design: producer and publish APIs are REST, consumer collaboration is UI.
evidence: 405s; re-GET showed no stakeholders after the echo-only 200

title: MCP for Marketplace: the Data Provisioning server
text: The managed Data Provisioning MCP server offers `list_data_collections`, `list_delivery_targets` (which returns collection detail, not a target list) and `checkout_data_order` (dataCollectionId, justification, targetRef), which raises a governed access request. A small local stdio MCP shim over the public API can expose the same three actions to Claude.
evidence: Vendor MCP catalog; a local shim registered and used

title: MCP for CDGC: Metadata Search actions, the September registry, and empty answers for uncataloged assets
text: The CDGC Metadata Search server offers `search_metadata` (natural-language query > asset ids and core attributes; it wraps the search endpoint, which is richer with raw DSL) and `get_asset_details` (`id`, `scheme` > full metadata including lineage and profile). A September 2026 registry enumeration also listed `cdgccatalogdiscovery`, `cdgcsearchmetadata`, `cdgcdataqualityscore` and `cdgccatalogenrichment` (three glossary/classification write tools, not exercised in these sources). Catalog-keyed DQ agent tools return SUCCESS with an empty `END_OF_ANSWER` for assets that are not cataloged, so scan first. The MCP layer is not monetized in preview, but the backing calls still bill.
evidence: Vendor catalog (2026-07-25); registry listing (2026-09-22..28); repeated empty answers for uncataloged assets (2026-09-22..24)

title: No IDMC connector reads CDGC metadata: catalog feeds are external scripts
text: CDI has no connector that reads CDGC catalog metadata, so a feed that lands catalog facts (coverage, classifications, glossary) in a warehouse must be a script over the REST APIs: read-only, one scheduled writer, credentials in a 0600 file. Treat the catalog as eventually consistent with its sources (a freshness contract such as structure within a day, profiles and DQ within an hour) and read the operational store when you need live truth.
evidence: Coverage feed code; exporter runbook

title: CDGC is the most headless IDMC family; know the few walls left
text: In the July 2026 scorecard, catalog search, scan execution, profiling runs and lineage discovery were REST end to end while other families authored only by clone or ended in a UI click. September 2026 widened CDGC further: catalog-source create and update, glossary domains and terms, term links, dictionary descriptions and manual classification are all headless. Walls left: deleting a source definition, scan cancel, bulk CLAIRE accept, stakeholder assignment, DAM policies, delivery templates, and lineage-graph reads (MCP only).
evidence: July scorecard plus the September 2026 proofs cited in this folder

title: Scans cost IPUs; configuration, search and content writes are author-time
text: Firing a scan is IPU-metered; the July 2026 phrase "no IPU for metadata operations" referred to reads and configuration. Catalog-source create and update, search, glossary and content writes are author-time work. Budget scans (profiling large warehouses is the expensive part), scope them with filters, and never loop run-until-accepted.
evidence: Metering notes across July and September 2026

title: Migrate CDGC between orgs: recreate, scan serially, rebuild the glossary, purge legacy, retest CLAIRE
text: CDGC does not travel in the v3 package (L-CDGC-071). In the target: recreate each catalog source with the same name (multipart create with custom and endOfLife, connection and RE ids remapped); select the agent's Metadata services only for the scan window; scan one source at a time and link terms after each; recreate glossary domains, terms, links, curated descriptions and classifications through data360 content from a read-only export of the source org; purge legacy sources that duplicate asset names; deselect the services; retest CLAIRE after the index settles. Plan the UI steps (definition deletes) and known gaps (legacy connection types) up front.
evidence: 5 sources, 33 terms, 42 links, 6 classifications and 11 descriptions rebuilt in a target org; scans COMPLETED or PARTIAL_COMPLETED

title: API Manager hosts return nginx 503 on every path: an artifact, not a verdict
text: In the governance family's neighbour service, `<pod>-apigw` and `<pod>-apim` both answer nginx 503 for every path, including bogus ones: a load balancer with no backend attached. That is an artifact and carries no per-path meaning. `/public/apim/v1/apis` (and variants) 404 while the DataServiceApiMgmt engine ran; the developer portal `/public/api/v1/apiPortal` 404s and is the one likely true entitlement gap (inferred from an absent privilege, weak evidence).
evidence: 503 on real and bogus paths on both hosts

title: List executables on the executable plane
text: `GET` (and `POST`) `https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/executable/v1/executables?type=<type>` returns the executables list (200) with the identity headers. The accepted `type` values are not recorded; PUT, PATCH and DELETE are untested.
evidence: 200 live

title: Governance and usage dashboards from catalog counts and warehouse governance views
text: A governance dashboard that works headless combines: an open-issues notice board (DQ violations, policy gaps, staleness) ordered by severity and age; DQ rules by dimension; catalog coverage widgets from search counts (tables indexed, columns profiled and classified, glossary terms, keys, Marketplace products); and a KPI row (open and critical counts, DQ pass rate). Asset-growth analytics come from periodic snapshots of per-table row, column and byte counts by layer. User adoption (who searches, opens or curates) needs an IDMC audit-log activity feed exported to the warehouse, which does not land by itself. Native CDGC custom widgets are UI personalization; this pattern is shareable and read-only.
evidence: Dashboards live with all SQL pre-validated; 6 snapshots showed catalog growth

title: Build deterministic fallbacks for CLAIRE GPT skills that have no REST
text: CLAIRE GPT chat has no REST chat API on the probed orgs (it was driven through the web UI), so for demos and checks build deterministic, credit-free fallbacks over the live catalog and warehouse: discovery through `POST /data360/search/api/v1/search`, NL-to-SQL through a curated intent matcher with pre-validated queries, and document research through curated pointers to proven API mechanics. Validate the native CLAIRE answers against these once they run.
evidence: Harness passed 3 of 3 skills; answers matched live warehouse queries

title: Scans can only be triggered from the UI: the ccgf-auth-pep 500 is a platform auth bug
text: A Bearer-only run call answered 500 'Login sessionID is missing' and was read as a platform fault, so scans were said to be UI-only (a later note also claimed no REST scan or profile trigger exists). The 500 came from a missing header and an empty capabilityNames. Was believed 2026-06-27 to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-CDGC-034 (Run a scan: POST data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id> with a non-empty capabilityNames).
evidence: Was believed 2026-06-27 to 2026-07-25; overturned 2026-06-28 by L-CDGC-034

title: Every run returning 406 with zero profiled columns means a stuck scan holds the source lock (root cause)
text: A stuck job does return 406, but it did not explain why every source failed identically; the native-library crash of the profiling engine did. Was believed 2026-06-28; overturned by L-CDGC-044 (Only Data Profiling launches the native DTM: profiling-only failures point at the agent).
evidence: Was believed 2026-06-28; overturned 2026-06-28 by L-CDGC-044

title: The CDGC search API needs an undiscovered query parameter; verify assets in the Explore UI instead
text: The documented search path kept returning 400, which led to UI-only verification. The Elasticsearch endpoint with X-INFA-SEARCH-LANGUAGE works. Was believed until 2026-06-28; overturned by L-CDGC-073 (Search the catalog: POST data360/search/api/v1/search with an Elasticsearch body).
evidence: Was believed until 2026-06-28; overturned 2026-06-28 by L-CDGC-073

title: data360/search/v1/assets is a dead end (400 MissingServletRequestParameter forever)
text: The path was recorded as unusable. It works once the knowledgeQuery (and segments) query parameters are sent. Was believed 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-CDGC-074 (data360/search/v1/assets works once knowledgeQuery and segments are sent).
evidence: Was believed 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-25; overturned 2026-09-24 by L-CDGC-074

title: The CDI object chain: mapping (DTEMPLATE) -> mapping task (MTT) -> linear or advanced taskflow -> schedule
text: A mapping is the design (v3 type `DTEMPLATE`, inner `documentType:"MAPPING"`; v2 `/api/v2/mapping` for read and delete). A mapping task is its runnable instance with parameters (v2 `/api/v2/mttask`, v3 `MTT`, FRS document type `MCT`). A linear taskflow is v2 `/api/v2/workflow` (v3 `WORKFLOW`), and an advanced taskflow is v3 `TASKFLOW`. A schedule (v2 `/api/v2/schedule`) is org-level and bound through `scheduleId`. Everything a pipeline runs is ultimately a mapping task started with `POST /api/v2/job`.
evidence: v2 and v3 reads of every object type; 160 MTTs and 10 taskflows inventoried

title: A fresh org already holds about 160 stock template assets; count real tasks with /api/v2/mttask
text: `GET /public/core/v3/objects` on a new org lists many stock add-on assets. They are templates, not user work. Count real tasks with `GET /api/v2/mttask`. `/api/v2/diTask` returned 404.
evidence: v3 object type counts (MAPPLET 48, DTEMPLATE 44, DMAPPLET 20, CLEANSE 18, DICTIONARY 15, PARSE 7) with 0 user mappings

title: Add-On Bundle Data Transfer templates are parameterized mappings you can wrap in tasks directly
text: The Copy Data templates under `Add-On Bundles/Data Transfer Templates` have `fixedConnection=false` and `connParam=true` on `$Source$` (`EXTENDED_SOURCE`) and `$Target$` (`TARGET`): `dsst__copy_data_new_tgt` (auto-creates the target), `dsst__copy_data_existing_tgt`, `dsst__copy_with_lookup_*`, `dlt__copy_data` (incremental-key filter parameters) and `INFA_Generic_Cloud_Service_Mapping`. A mapping task over one of them supplies its own connections, objects or `customQuery`, so no UI-authored mapping is needed. Each template shows `tasks=0` until used.
evidence: first genuine runs 2026-09-23; 46/46 SUCCESS per hourly cycle

title: Bundle templates are system content: FRS delete:false, export 403 MigrationSvc_038, import with REUSE
text: A v3 export of an Add-On Bundle template (e.g. `dsst__copy_data_new_tgt`, `dlt__copy_data`) can return `403 MigrationSvc_038` "User does not have required permissions". It reproduced in some orgs and dates and not in others. User-owned mappings and bundle rule specs exported fine. FRS reports `delete:false` on bundles even for an admin. When migrating tasks built on a bundle template, import with REUSE so the target's own copy is used.
evidence: 403 on bundle export for a non-admin user; FRS delete:false; import reported "Reuse existing object"

title: A target org reuses its own build of a bundle template; a TmplPatternRuleImpl failure passed on rerun
text: After an org-to-org import, tasks bind to the target's copy of the bundle template, which can be a different build from the source's. One task failed once with "Cannot propagate link rule of type TmplPatternRuleImpl between Expression and IUpdateStrategyNode5" and succeeded on a plain rerun. Rerun before debugging, and validate each task once after an import.
evidence: one failure, then a successful plain rerun

title: A mapping task carries no field array; field overrides over v2 return 400
text: Exported mapping tasks contain no field array: fields live in the mapping referenced by `mappingId`. So precision or type changes cannot be made on a template-based task. Use a source view or SQL that casts, change the mapping itself, or use a JSON-typed target column for long text.
evidence: inspection of exported task packages; `overriddenFields` → HTTP 400

title: Tasks over ordinary mappings are schema-bound; a task-level connection swap does not reach the mapping
text: A task built on an ordinary (user-authored) mapping has `connectionParameterized:false` and `objectParameterized:false`. Changing only its connection yields an invalid task, and a task-level `sourceConnectionId` does not propagate into the mapping. Check a mapping's real binding in its export, not its name. Clone a template-based task, or edit the mapping's objects and fields.
evidence: the task became invalid after a connection-only swap; an import log showed the original connection

title: The v2 mapping-task list omits frsGuid and scheduleId; read each task's detail
text: `GET /api/v2/mttask` and `GET /api/v2/task?type=MTT` return names and ids but not `frsGuid` and not `scheduleId`. Anything that needs the v3 id, or needs to know whether a task has its own schedule, must `GET /api/v2/mttask/<id>` for every task.
evidence: a scan of 159 task details found a task-level binding the list did not show

title: Resolve ids across planes: frsGuid, name match for workflows, assetFrsGuid, v3 lookup by path
text: A v2 task's v3 id is its `frsGuid` (from the detail GET). v2 workflows carry no `frsGuid`: list v3 `type=='WORKFLOW'` objects and match the last path segment to the name, requiring exactly one hit. A v2 mapping's v3 id is its `assetFrsGuid`. `POST /public/core/v3/lookup {"objects":[{"path":"<project>/<folder>/<name>","type":"MTT"}]}` resolves by path. Cache name → GUID per org.
evidence: workflow placement and a taskflow generator depended on it; deletes resolved this way on 2026-09-28

title: Address tasks by id, never by name
text: An org with older content held tasks with the same names in other folders, so any lookup by name (to run, bind, delete or map ids) can hit the wrong object. Record ids at creation or import time, and resolve names only within the intended folder or among the objects created by one import.
evidence: 15 task names also existed in unrelated folders of the same org; 0 workflow task ids pointed at them after the check

title: The v3 objects type filter is not validated: an unknown type returns 0
text: `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='<X>'` returns an empty list, not an error, when `<X>` is not a real type name. Sweep candidate type names, or list everything unfiltered and group by type on the client.
evidence: an audit filtering `type=='DBMI'` missed 23 `DBMI_TASK` objects

title: v2-created mapping tasks do appear in the v3 objects list
text: By 2026-09-25/29 the v3 objects list returned every v2-created mapping task (type `MTT`). An earlier sweep that saw none was probably a filter or paging artifact. When a v3 count looks like zero, cross-check with `GET /api/v2/task?type=MTT` before concluding anything, including that an org was wiped.
evidence: a live v3 read listed 160 MTTs and 10 taskflows

title: Attribute tasks to runtime environments with GET /api/v2/mttask
text: `GET /api/v2/mttask` returns `runtimeEnvironmentId` per task, so it is the source for "which tasks run on which runtime". v3 objects are org-scoped and carry no runtime field.
evidence: per-runtime inventories of production and pre-production task sets

title: Task reads by type: /api/v2/task?type=, /api/v2/workflow, /api/v2/taskflow
text: `GET /api/v2/task?type=<X>` lists tasks by type (403 for `MI_TASK`, and 403 "DVT is not a valid task type" for `DVT`: use each service's own API). `GET /api/v2/workflow` and `GET /api/v2/taskflow` read workflows and taskflows (200).
evidence: 200 and 403 answers, live

title: v2 task resources mount per pod and per licensed engine
text: `/api/v2/dss`, `dtemplate`, `dmask`, `dreplicate`, `plan` and `fileListener` mount per pod and per licensed engine, not per org. They were the biggest source of false "not entitled" calls. Never generalize a v2 inventory from one org.
evidence: live A/B: 200 on one dm-us org, 404 on a dmp-us sub-org holding 876 privileges

title: Move tasks into a folder with FRS MoveEntities; ids, schedules and history survive
text: New v2 tasks and workflows are created in `Default`. Move them with `POST https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/frs/api/v1/MoveEntities` (or `/frs/v1/MoveEntities`), header `IDS-SESSION-ID: <v2 icSessionId>`, body `{"xferSpec":{"targetLocationId":"<folder frsGuid>","sourceSpecArr":[{"sourceEntityId":"<frsGuid>","mergeTags":""}]}}`, at most 25 ids per call. The v2 id, `mappingId`, schedule bindings and run history are unchanged. v3 `/objects/{id}/move` is 404. `CopyEntities` takes the same `xferSpec`. Data Quality profiles could not be moved.
evidence: `XFER_200` "Operation succeeded on 10 artifacts"; FRS_200 per item; runs unchanged afterwards

title: No headless browse of connection objects: know the connector's object path format
text: v2 `/api/v2/connection/{id}/objects|source|metadata|objectbrowse|objectcategories`, `/api/v2/mttask/objectDetails|browseObjects` and `/metadata/objects` all returned 404. So did v3 `/public/core/v3/connections[/{id}/objects|objectsList|metadata]` ("No static resource"). An older reference lists `GET /api/v2/connection/source/<connId>` as a source-metadata browse (200 or 403 per connection, July 2026). Write object paths from the connector's known format instead of browsing.
evidence: exhaustive 404s across v2 and v3 browse shapes

title: v2 object-id type codes and FRS document types
text: A v2 id is 20 characters: the 6-character v2 org id, a 2-character type code, then a 12-character sequence. Observed codes: `0Z` mapping task, `0N` workflow, `D0` schedule, `17` mapping, `0B` connection, `08` agent, `25` runtime environment. v3/FRS ids are 22-character base-62 GUIDs. FRS reports a mapping task as document type `MCT`, the same code an advanced taskflow's Data Task uses for "Task Type".
evidence: ids observed across two orgs; FRS move receipts

title: Job-history counts include runs of objects that no longer exist
text: Job totals in the monitoring views can be dominated by old runs of deleted objects. Filter by object and date before using job counts as evidence.
evidence: 930 of the last 1,000 job-history rows belonged to deleted test objects

title: POST /api/v2/mapping is not a create surface; v3 objects POST is 405
text: No REST call creates a mapping design directly. Do not debug the body. Author through import packages instead (a cloned or synthesized DTEMPLATE, then a v2 task over it). The vendor previewed a mapping-design API for about late 2026, GA about 2027 (documented in a July 2026 conversation, unproven).
evidence: 400 HTML "Internal error, please contact technical support"; `/api/v2/Mapping` 404; `POST /public/core/v3/objects` 405; `/public/core/v3/mappings` 404; still true 2026-09-29

title: Route 1: tasks over the copy-data template with customQuery SQL move data fully headless
text: Take one working task over `dsst__copy_data_new_tgt`. `GET /api/v2/mttask/<templateTaskId>`, change the name, `$Source$.customQuery` (or source object) and target object, then `POST /api/v2/mttask` to create, or `POST /api/v2/mttask/<id>` to update, and run with `POST /api/v2/job`. Landing, raw, staging, gold, DQ marts, reverse-ETL, SaaS upserts, flat-file ingest and evidence snapshots were all built this way. The cost: empty two-box canvases, logic invisible to lineage, and about 20 s plus one job per task.
evidence: hourly cycles 46/46 SUCCESS, ~1.5M rows per cycle; later 159 tasks ran for days

title: Clone a template mapping task over v2: which fields to strip and which parameters to set
text: Drop `id, orgId, createTime, updateTime, createdBy, updatedBy, frsGuid`. Set `name`, `description`, `shortDescription` and `sessionProperties={}`, and pop `id` in every `parameters[]` entry. `$Source$`: `sourceConnectionId`; `customQuery` (or pop it); `sourceObject = objectName =` `'DUMMY_Source'` or `'<schema>/TABLE/<t>'`; each `extendedObject.object`/`objects[]` entry gets `{name, label, dbSchema:""}`. `$Target$`: `targetObject = targetObjectLabel = newObjectName = objectName = objectLabel = '<dataset>/<table>'`, `tgtObjectAttributes={"parent":"<dataset>"}`, `runtimeAttrs={}`, `oprRuntimeAttrs={"writeMode":"Bulk","writeDisposition":"Write truncate"}`, `truncateTarget=false`. `POST /api/v2/mttask` and require 200.
evidence: 159 tasks built this way; probe tasks created and deleted with zero residue

title: customQuery runs in the dialect of the source connection
text: The SQL in `$Source$.customQuery` runs on the source connection, so it must use that engine's dialect (GoogleSQL for BigQuery) even when the target is another warehouse. Half-translated queries that mix dialect-specific functions (`QUALIFY`, `REGEXP_CONTAINS` with raw strings) fail in both. Translate with an explicit map when the SQL must run elsewhere.
evidence: BigQuery 400 "Syntax error: Unexpected "[" ... escape with backtick"; gone after the fix

title: Non-ASCII in a BigQuery customQuery fails the reader with "missing CR"
text: Before storing SQL in a task, drop `--` comment lines and trailing comments, remove non-ASCII characters and strip the trailing `;`. In practice the only non-ASCII characters were in comments.
evidence: the task failed with "IOException: missing CR" until an em dash in a comment was removed

title: Route 2 via the iics CLI: clone an exported mtTask.json and re-import it
text: A mapping task's source SQL and target table are plain editable fields in its exported `mtTask.json` (`customQuery`, `targetObject`), and one pass-through template mapping can serve many tasks. Export one working task, clone it per output (new `customQuery`, target, name and `frsGuid`), recompute checksums, and import with the Informatica `iics` CLI (`-r us` region, `type==MTT` filters, `--sync=true`). Then run with `POST /api/v2/job`.
evidence: 18/18 cloned tasks listed by the CLI and ran state=1

title: Route 3: package-clone a working mapping and rebuild its field arrays by position
text: Clone a live mapping through a v3 export. For a new output shape, rebuild the source and target field arrays by position from the live target schema, with fresh `$$ID`/`##ID` references and correct `platformType`/`javaType`/`nativeType`/`precision` per column (renaming is not enough). Swap `customQuery`, repoint the target object, recompute SHA-256 lines and import. Then `POST /api/v2/mttask` and run.
evidence: 14/14 new-shape marts ported with exact parity (set difference 0)

title: A mapping's IMF lives in bin/@N.bin as JSON text, not a compiled binary
text: In a v3 export of a mapping (`.DTEMPLATE.zip`), the file named by `mappingTemplate.json`'s `templateId` holds the mapping definition as text JSON: IMF with `content` and `metadata.$$classInfo`. In the exports seen that was `bin/@3.bin`, and `bin/@2.bin` was a preview JPEG. `mappingTemplate.json` `references[]` holds the connection references. Exported user mappings are `fixedConnection:true` and schema-baked, so retargeting one means editing sources, targets and field graphs in the IMF, not only a connection id.
evidence: export SUCCESSFUL, file contents inspected; the format was later used to synthesize 11 mappings

title: Swap a connection GUID in place (22 characters) and re-hash only the path-keyed lines
text: A connection swap inside a cloned mapping's IMF can be an in-place replacement: IDMC GUIDs are 22 characters, so offsets are preserved. After editing, recompute only the path-keyed SHA-256 lines of the changed entries in `exportPackage.chksum`. The opaque GUID-keyed lines could stay stale and the import still reported `checksumValid:true`.
evidence: import `checksumValid:true`; the cloned mapping ran SUCCESS 52/52

title: The objectRefs trap: an objectRef without a matching entry fails the import with MigrationSvc_031
text: Every GUID in an object's `metadata.objectRefs` (in `exportMetadata.v2.json`) must resolve. Adding a new connection GUID to `objectRefs` with no matching entry failed with `MigrationSvc_031`, and a dangling objectRef gives `MigrationSvc_031` with empty details. Two ways work: leave `objectRefs` naming the original connection and let the swapped GUID resolve in the target, or add an `exportedObjects` entry for the connection (`objectType:"Connection"`, `path:"/SYS"`, `repoInfo.repoHandle:<v2 connection id>`), as synthesized packages do.
evidence: MigrationSvc_031 with the extra ref, a clean import without it (2026-08-19); SUCCESSFUL imports after remapping (2026-09-28/29)

title: Checksum rules for an edited package (MigrationSvc_073)
text: `exportPackage.chksum` holds one `path=SHA256HEX` line per file: upper-case hex, with spaces in paths escaped as `\ `. Replace only the lines of files you changed, including the line for `exportMetadata.v2.json` itself; otherwise the import fails with `MigrationSvc_073` "package has been modified". Keep every other line byte-identical, and drop the matching rows of the contents CSV when you remove an object.
evidence: `checksumValid:true` and SUCCESSFUL imports after each edit

title: Package edits did not retarget a mapping to a different connector type
text: A mapping cloned through an export package kept its original source/target connection binding after the package was edited to point at a different connector type (one cloud warehouse to another). Retargeting an existing mapping across connector types was not achieved headless and was not retested after the IMF format became understood. Synthesize a new mapping for the other adapter (L-CDI-033), or author it once in the UI.
evidence: the compiled definitions of 22 cloned "twin" mappings still referenced only the original warehouse connection

title: From-scratch import packages are accepted when metadata and checksums are right
text: A package you build yourself imports fine if it has: - the object files under `Explore/<project>/<folder>/`; - the real `<folder>.Folder.json` and `<project>.Project.json`, copied from any genuine export in that folder, or `exportedObjects` entries with the real project and folder GUIDs; - an `exportMetadata.v2.json` listing folder, project and each object (`objectGuid`, `objectName`, `objectType`, `path`, `metadata.objectRefs`, `additionalInfo`); - a correct `exportPackage.chksum`. `400 MigrationSvc_030` is what an empty or invalid multipart gets.
evidence: generated mapping, CAI and taskflow packages imported SUCCESSFUL, `checksumValid:true`

title: Route 5: synthesize real multi-transformation mappings as IMF JSON and import them
text: Write a JSON spec of nodes (`source` query or table, `expression`, `filter`, `router`, `joiner`, `aggregator`, `sorter`, `target`) and links. Generate the IMF template JSON, package it as a DTEMPLATE, and import it (REUSE first, OVERWRITE to rebuild under the same GUID). Wrap it in a v2 task with `{mappingId, runtimeEnvironmentId}`, move it into the folder, run it and check parity. The mappings show real transformations on the canvas. Proven: warehouse query/table sources, BigQuery targets, Expression, Router, Joiner and Aggregator, plus PostgreSQL-source ingest mappings in parity runs.
evidence: 11 mappings imported SUCCESSFUL, two-way EXCEPT DISTINCT = 0 against the live SQL, and an idempotency double run

title: The synthesized DTEMPLATE package layout
text: The outer zip holds `Explore/<project>/<folder>/<name>.DTEMPLATE.zip`, `exportMetadata.v2.json` and `exportPackage.chksum`. The inner zip holds: - `mappingTemplate.json`: `[{"@type":"mappingTemplate","id":"@1","name","assetFrsGuid":"<22-char guid>","templateId":"@2","documentType":"MAPPING","fixedConnection":true,"valid":true,"references":[{"@type":"reference","refObjectId":"@<conn guid>","refType":"connection"}]}]`; - `fileRecord.json`: `[{"@type":"fileRecord","id":"@2","type":"IMFOBJECT","size":<n>,"additionalInfo":"com.informatica.metadata.template.common.Template"}]`; - `bin/@2.bin` (the IMF JSON) and `metadata.meta`. `exportMetadata.v2.json` lists the DTEMPLATE (`objectRefs` = connection guids), the Project, the Folder, and each Connection (`path "/SYS"`, `repoInfo.repoHandle` = its v2 id).
evidence: every generated package imported SUCCESSFUL

title: IMF content: transformation classes, $$classInfo, adapters, link rules, type map
text: - **Structure.** The IMF has `content` = a `Template` (`$$class`, `documentType:"MAPPING"`, `name`, `links:[TmplLink]`, `transformations:[...]`) and `metadata.$$classInfo` = `{<n>: "com.informatica.metadata.template...<Class>"}`. Every object carries `$$ID` and `$$class`; references are `{"##ID","$$class"}`. - **Transformations.** `TmplSource`/`TmplTarget` each carry a `BaseAdapter` (`connectionId:"saas:@<conn frsGuid>"`, `objectType` `QUERY` or `SINGLE`, a `DataObject` with `BaseAdapterField`s, `ReadOptions`/`WriteOptions`, `oprRuntimeAttributes`). The others are `TmplExpression` (OUTPUT/VARIABLE fields), `TmplRouter` (`GroupFilterCondition`s), `TmplFilter`, `TmplJoiner` (`JoinCondition`s, `joinType`), `TmplAggregator` (group-by fields) and `TmplSorter` (`SortEntry`s). - **Groups and links.** Groups hold ports. `TmplAllRule` passes every field through; `TmplNameRule` entries select or rename fields on a link. - **Type map.** Platform types come from `smd:com.informatica.metadata.seed.platform.Platform.typesystem/<string|bigint|decimal|double|date/time>`.
evidence: proven node types ran; exemplars harvested from real mappings

title: Harvest real mappings read-only from another org as exemplars
text: If the org you build in has no real mappings to copy, export (read-only) the mappings of an org that has them, covering Joiner, Aggregator, Router, Expression and Lookup patterns. They give the exact IMF shape of each transformation and adapter for a generator.
evidence: an export of 78 real mappings used as IMF exemplars

title: Create a mapping task over a real mapping with a minimal v2 body
text: After importing the mapping, find its v2 id with `GET /api/v2/mapping` (match by name inside the intended folder). Then `POST /api/v2/mttask {"@type":"mtTask","name":"mt_<x>","description":"...","mappingId":"<v2 mapping id>","runtimeEnvironmentId":"<reId>"}`. Reuse the task if the name already exists, and assert the org first. The task lands in `Default`: move it with FRS MoveEntities, then run it with `POST /api/v2/job`.
evidence: 11 tasks created, HTTP 200 each

title: In a synthesized mapping the BigQuery write disposition must sit in oprRuntimeAttributes
text: A BigQuery target's truncate or append behaviour comes from its adapter's `oprRuntimeAttributes` (`RuntimeAttribute` `writeDisposition` = "Write truncate" or "Write append", `writeMode` = "Bulk"). `WriteOptions.truncate` alone is ignored: the session log says "Write append" and every run appends.
evidence: session logs before and after; two mappings re-imported OVERWRITE with the fix

title: Fields declared JSON fail in BigQuery Simple mode; declare them STRING
text: A mapping that declares JSON-typed fields on a BigQuery Simple-mode connection fails, on both source tables and target columns. Declare those fields STRING in the mapping. A pre-created JSON target column still receives the text through Bulk loads. Keep the connection in Simple mode (Hybrid breaks mappings; L-CDI-156).
evidence: "The mapping failed because the table contains [JSON] data type that is incompatible with the [Simple] connection mode" (2026-09-29); "JSON incompatible with Simple connection mode" (2026-07-09); runs succeeded with STRING declarations

title: A JDBC V2 target writes into the database bound on its connection; the object's schema is ignored
text: A synthesized mapping whose JDBC V2 target object named a scratch schema wrote into the database the connection is bound to, ignoring that schema. Parity and scratch runs against such targets need their own connection, and a run-time assertion that no parity task points at a live database. To point parity or scratch runs at another database, clone the connection (`GET /api/v2/connection/<id>`, change the name and the JDBC URL's database, `POST /api/v2/connection` without the id, test it) and bind the scratch mapping to that clone; never change the live connection's URL for a test.
evidence: a parity probe wrote 1,723 rows into the live table; no data lost because the content matched; parity runs against a scratch database still landed in the live database until a separate scratch connection was used (2026-09-29)

title: Route 4: author one mapping in the designer (automated), then clone it
text: When no headless route has proven a transformation or adapter, author one mapping in the Data Integration designer and clone the variants. Automation that worked: - drive Playwright from a host outside any transparent proxy (behind one, the design SPAs rendered blank); - enter SQL with CodeMirror `setValue(...)` plus `save()`, and never press Escape before the commit; - react-select options match `[class*='-option']`; - if a large query (about 6 KB) hangs the field-derive spinner, adopt the persisted `Mapping<N>` by GUID and delete orphans with `DELETE /api/v2/mapping/<id>`. Cost: 30–75 minutes per mapping.
evidence: 16 marts authored this way, each with exact parity

title: BigQuery full pushdown could not be enabled over REST
text: `POST /api/v2/mttask/<id>` with `sessionProperties {"Pushdown Optimization":"Full"}` persists, but pushdown does not happen, and `optimizationPlan` accepts any string, unvalidated. Capture the UI's save request once (an XHR log) to learn the real property name and value. Until then, heavy warehouse logic runs as query sources. Setting the temporary-view property and `enableCrossSchemaPushdown` as well, with no write disposition on the targets, made the same kind of mapping push down (OPT_63367 in the session log). Was believed 2026-09-29 to 2026-09-30; overturned by L-CDI-202.
evidence: read-back showed the property; the session log showed no pushdown, and the run died with a reader GC-overhead OOM (baseline 62 s, 0 errors)

title: Full pushdown runs only when source and target share an ecosystem; the session log is the proof
text: One mapping runs with full pushdown (SQL ELT) when source and target are in the same ecosystem (proven BigQuery to BigQuery), and in agent mode when they cross ecosystems (to another warehouse, a database or a SaaS). The generated warehouse SQL in the session log is the proof that pushdown happened (L-CDI-202). Group targets by ecosystem when consolidating, and keep pushdown only where it measures faster: it writes a mapping's targets one after another (L-CDI-203). Newer evidence: L-CDI-305.
evidence: Documented in the CDI guides; live-proven on a 5-target BigQuery-to-BigQuery mapping whose session logs showed OPT_63367 and one INSERT INTO per target (2026-10-01)

title: Every connector a mapping uses must be on the one runtime environment that runs it
text: With the source connector on one agent and the target connector on another, a task failed within about 2 s. A session abort at "Importing Connection: <conn>" (`trepcnx.cpp:296`) means the task's runtime cannot use that connection: it is bound to another runtime environment, or that connector's package is missing on the agent. Colocate connectors on one runtime, or give the other side its own task.
evidence: state 3 in ~2 s, 0 rows, "DTM process terminated unexpectedly"; the agent package inventory plus a binding check

title: APP_13400 "Compute capacity exceeded" comes from a throttled target warehouse
text: `APP_13400 Compute capacity exceeded` on a connection fetch came from the warehouse's capacity throttle, not from IDMC. Tasks against the throttled warehouse ran but wrote 0 rows with "DTM process terminated". Fix capacity: pause the jobs hitting it, then suspend and resume the capacity.
evidence: the capacity throttle on the warehouse side; tasks wrote 0 rows until capacity was restored

title: Minimal task bodies fail APP_13507; APP_13533 means no mappingId; update is POST /{id}, PUT is 405
text: `POST /api/v2/mttask` over a Copy Data template with a minimal body fails with `APP_13507`. The body needs the full `$Source$` (`EXTENDED_SOURCE`) and `$Target$` (`TARGET`) parameter objects, so clone a working task. `403 APP_13533 "specify a mapping id"` means a mapping was being authored through the task API. Updating is `POST /api/v2/mttask/<id>` (the v2 idiom), and `PUT` returns 405.
evidence: APP_13507 on a minimal body; 403 APP_13533 without a mappingId; PUT 405 on both paths

title: Value-less template parameters need uiProperties.required=false and placeholder values
text: On a task over `dsst__copy_data_new_tgt`, value-less STRING parameters such as `$p_tgt_excluded_fields$` and `$p_filter_src$` without a `uiProperties.required` key are treated as required, and the task is rejected with `APP_13506`/`APP_13507`. Set `uiProperties.required="false"` and placeholders (`$p_filter_src$=TRUE`, `$p_tgt_excluded_fields$=NONE`). `errc=-1` under `schemaMode:"async"` means validation was deferred, not failed; `valid=true` is authoritative.
evidence: task create + validate returned `valid=True` and ran on the agent

title: Target write options go in $Target$.oprRuntimeAttrs; runtimeAttrs is ignored
text: In a task over a Copy Data template, BigQuery write options are read from `$Target$.oprRuntimeAttrs`, e.g. `{"writeMode":"Bulk","writeDisposition":"Write truncate"}`. Values placed in `runtimeAttrs` are silently ignored for BigQuery; JDBC V2 targets use `runtimeAttrs` for "Pre SQL" (L-CDI-171).
evidence: truncation was honoured only after the attributes moved

title: Set fetchMode RUNTIME or new target columns silently land NULL
text: A mapping task keeps the field list it had when it was created. If the target table or the source query gains columns later, the task silently writes NULL into them. Set `fetchMode:"RUNTIME"` on `$Source$` and `$Target$` so field metadata is read at run time, or rebuild the task after the schema changes.
evidence: NULL columns observed after columns were added; populated after the change

title: Silent no-op: a target-parameter POST returns 200 but the task keeps its mapping's targets
text: Updating a task over a real (fixed-connection) mapping by POSTing changed target fields (`targetObject`, labels, `newObjectName`, connection) returns HTTP 200, but the task re-derives its targets from the mapping on every read and run. To retarget, change the mapping: rebuild or edit its package with the new targets and re-import it with OVERWRITE under the **same GUID**, then re-read the task. Tasks over Copy Data templates are different: their `$Target$` is task-owned and target changes stick. Always read back after any write.
evidence: 10 task POSTs → 200 with read-backs unchanged; after the mappings were re-imported OVERWRITE, the tasks showed the new targets (2026-09-29); a cross-connector `targetConnectionId` change reverted silently (2026-07-04)

title: Switch an existing task between Write truncate and Write append
text: `GET /api/v2/mttask/<id>`. If `$Target$.oprRuntimeAttrs.writeDisposition` already equals the wanted value, stop. Otherwise set `{"writeMode":"Bulk","writeDisposition":"Write append"}` (or "Write truncate"), drop `orgId, createTime, updateTime, createdBy, updatedBy`, and POST the body back to `/api/v2/mttask/<id>`.
evidence: append-only snapshot tasks ran on every scheduled cycle after the switch

title: Delete mapping tasks and mappings with v2 DELETE and read the delete back
text: `DELETE /api/v2/mttask/<id>` → 200, and a read-back 403 means gone. Resolve the v2 id from a v3 id through `frsGuid`, never by name. `DELETE /api/v2/mapping/<id>` → 200, only when the mapping's `tasks[]` is empty (resolve it through `assetFrsGuid`). `/api/v2/dtemplate/<id>` is the wrong path (404 HTML), and a v3 objects DELETE returned 404. Delete tasks before mappings, with an export backup first.
evidence: 200 per delete; read-back 403; mapping counts dropped (123 → 61 on one cleanup)

title: REPO_52013 on delete means the task is bound to a schedule, so it is live
text: A v2 DELETE of a mapping task that has its own task-level schedule fails with `REPO_52013`. Treat it as proof the task is live, not an orphan: find the binding in the task detail (`scheduleId`), check who reads its output, and unbind deliberately only if the task really should go.
evidence: a prune attempt hit REPO_52013 on a task that looked unreferenced

title: Tag objects in batches of 50; projects and folders cannot be tagged; imports drop tags
text: `POST /public/core/v3/TagObjects` with `[{"id":"<frsGuid>","tags":["<tag>"]}, ...]`, at most 50 per call. Read the status of every item (200/201/204/207). Items of type Folder or Project fail ("of type: [Folder]"), so let the project name mark the scope. Imports do not carry tags: re-tag after every import.
evidence: 189 objects re-tagged after an import and read back

title: Create the project and folder over v3 idempotently and cache their ids per org
text: Find the project with `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='PROJECT'`, or create it with `POST /public/core/v3/projects {"name","description"}` (200/201 → id). List folders with `q=type=='FOLDER' and location=='<project>'`, and create one with `POST /public/core/v3/projects/<projectId>/folders {"name","description"}`. Cache the ids per org: ids from one org must never be used in another.
evidence: folder create 201; repeated builds found and reused it

title: Run a task or linear taskflow with POST /api/v2/job; readyToRun=false does not block it
text: `POST <serverUrl>/api/v2/job`, header `icSessionId`, body `{"@type":"job","taskId":"<taskId|wfId>","taskType":"MTT"|"WORKFLOW"}` → 200 with a `runId`. It works even when the runtime-environment list reports `readyToRun=false`: that flag is stale on the list, and only mattered for catalog-source operations. No publish is needed to run an imported task.
evidence: 200 + runId on thousands of runs; runs completed with the runtime-environment list reporting readyToRun=false

title: Start jobs by v2 taskId; taskFederatedId works only with the task's own federated id in the same org
text: The v2 `taskId` with `taskType:"MTT"` always worked. `{"taskFederatedId":"<federated id>","taskType":"MTT"}` also started runs in one org, with the federated id resolved from the task in that org. Sending another value (an id from a different plane or org) returned `403 REPO_19035` or `UI_13429`. The exact cause of the August failure was not isolated. Prefer `taskId`.
evidence: `taskFederatedId` runs appeared as REST_API_V2 in the activity log in one org (2026-09-22); 403 REPO_19035 when another value was sent (2026-08-19)

title: UI_13404, UI_13429 and REPO_19035 on job start: wrong object type, stale id or another org
text: - `POST /api/v2/job` with a Database Ingestion or Mass Ingestion task, a profile, or an undeployed object gives `403 UI_13404` "Object identifier is not valid or missing" for every `taskType`. Run those through their own services. - A federated id that no longer resolves gives `403 UI_13429`. - `GET /api/v2/mttask/<id>` on an id that is not a mapping task, or that belongs to another org, gives `403 REPO_19035` "task does not exist".
evidence: the recorded 403 answers for 5 taskType variants and several object types

title: Poll the activity log by runId until the run is terminal
text: After `POST /api/v2/job`, poll `GET /api/v2/activity/activityLog?taskId=<id>&rowLimit=1` every 5–10 s until `row[0].runId == runId` and `endTime` is set. State 1 = SUCCESS, 2 = WARNING (rows rejected), 3 = FAILED. Keep `successTargetRows`, `failedTargetRows`, `errorMsg` and the activity id. Time out at about 60 min per task and 2 h per taskflow. Never take the first row blindly: it can be the previous run.
evidence: the standard run path of every lane since 2026-09-23; a false failure when rows[0] was used instead

title: A WARNING run that wrote 0 rows is a failure
text: State 2 (WARNING) means some rows were rejected. If `successTargetRows` is also 0, nothing was written: count it as FAILED in orchestration and alerts. A WARNING that wrote rows (e.g. one rejected SaaS row) can stay non-blocking.
evidence: orchestration code mapping state 2 + 0 rows to FAILED; a WARNING with 509/510 rows stayed non-blocking

title: Tasks inside a linear taskflow log under the taskflow's entry (entries[])
text: When a linear taskflow runs, `GET /api/v2/activity/activityLog?taskId=<childTaskId>` does not show that run. The children are the `entries[]` of the taskflow's own row (`objectName`, `state`, `successTargetRows`, `errorMsg`, `startTimeUtc`, `runId`). Mirror child states from `entries[]` after the taskflow finishes; children missing after a stop did not run (`stopOnError`). Outer activity-log rows are batches, so flatten `entries[]` for per-run rows.
evidence: monitoring code changed to mirror children from the workflow entry; the console fix verified

title: The activity monitor says what is running and which child step it is on
text: `GET /api/v2/activity/activityMonitor` (add `?details=true` for taskflows) lists running jobs with `taskName`, `taskId`/`objectId` and `subTaskName` or `currentTaskName`. 0 rows means nothing is running. Use it before starting a task that may already be running, to adopt a schedule-started taskflow, and to show live progress. Do not trust derived "jobs running" gauges.
evidence: used before every lane start; a derived gauge read 17 while the monitor had 0 rows

title: US pods stamp local UTC-4 times with a Z; use the *Utc fields
text: On the US pods seen, v2 `createTime`/`startTime` and activity-log `startTime`/`endTime` are pod-local (UTC-4) but labelled `Z`. Use `startTimeUtc`/`endTimeUtc` for elapsed-time, freshness and completion logic. Schedules take both `startTime` (pod-local) and `startTimeUTC` (L-CDI-073).
evidence: a 4-hour offset between `startTime` and `startTimeUtc` on two pods

title: The agent's DIS session logs are exact run evidence
text: Each mapping-task run writes `<agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/logs/s_mtt_<taskId>_<n>.log`: - `TM_6014` marks the session start; - `PETL_24012` marks a successful end and `PETL_24013` a failure; - `WRT_8036 Target: <table>` names the target and `Applied Rows [N]` gives the count; - `DATABASENAME=` gives the source database; - "Session run completed successfully" is the verdict. Parsing them gives exact timing, concurrency and row evidence without API calls.
evidence: a 14/14 exact landing parity table and 12/12 and 5/5 lane parity built from these logs

title: Before re-arming a job paused for an IDMC run, confirm nothing is running
text: Jobs paused to avoid colliding with an IDMC run are easily orphaned. Before un-pausing, confirm the activity monitor shows 0 running jobs and no `pmdtm`/DTM process is alive on the agent host. Run the re-armed job once by hand, keep backups of the crontab and manifests, and update baseline counts so drift checks do not false-alarm.
evidence: an orphaned pause found; the activity monitor at 0 and no DTM process confirmed

title: Verify the production scheduler really calls IDMC; keep the legacy path behind a default-off flag
text: A pipeline can pass every on-demand IDMC run while production output still comes from legacy code on a cron. Inspect the live scheduler and the driver it calls, and cross-check activity-log run counts, before claiming "runs on IDMC". When IDMC becomes the sole engine, fail loudly on IDMC errors, keep the old runner only behind a default-off emergency flag, and banner the old SQL as superseded.
evidence: a production cron still ran the retired SQL every 15 minutes while every on-demand IDMC run was green

title: Watch run health per taskflow and alert on state change; a healthy container is not a healthy pipeline
text: Run a small watcher (e.g. every 15 min) that reads the activity log for each important taskflow and alerts only when a flow changes state (fails, stops running, recovers). When one host drives two orgs, run one watcher per org with separate state files. Container health checks only prove a process and a port. Judge pipelines by run completions, row growth and freshness.
evidence: a watcher added after a broken connection failed hourly runs silently; a pipeline container reported healthy for 38 h while every cycle failed

title: The managed Job Management MCP server wraps run, status and stop
text: The managed Job Management MCP server exposes `run_mapping_task` (wraps `POST /api/v2/job`), `get_job_status` (wraps the activity log, one job) and `stop_running_job`. It can also run taskflows and replications. REST is equivalent and returns full history. No managed MCP verb authors a mapping or a mapping task.
evidence: Documented, not live-proven: reference corpus action list; REST equivalents proven

title: Linear taskflows are created and updated headless with /api/v2/workflow and need no publish
text: `POST /api/v2/workflow {"@type":"workflow","name":"wf_<app>_<lane>","description":"...","tasks":[{"@type":"workflowTask","taskId":"<taskId>","type":"MTT","name":"<task>","stopOnError":true,"stopOnWarning":false}, ...]}` creates a linear taskflow (tasks in execution order). It can reference a schedule and runs as soon as it exists. To update: `GET /api/v2/workflow/<wfId>`, keep its `scheduleId`, and `POST /api/v2/workflow/<wfId>` with `id`. Run it with `POST /api/v2/job {"taskType":"WORKFLOW"}`. It runs strictly in sequence.
evidence: 8/8, 50/50, then 62/62 tasks per scheduled cycle; 10 workflows migrated with no publish step

title: Advanced taskflows generated or copied by API import but cannot be published
text: Advanced taskflow XML can be generated and imported with OVERWRITE: - a `parallel` container per wave; - Data Tasks as `ICSExecuteDataTask` services inside `eventContainer`s; - a temp field per task with a `processObject` dependency; - the step title equal to the field name, and no inner description. But a taskflow created by the API, or copied with FRS CopyEntities, could not be **published** through `active-bpel/asset/v1/publish` with its `.TASKFLOW.xml` path. Its REST/SOAP run URL is minted only by a designer Publish (July). Use linear taskflows, or a controller that runs tasks concurrently.
evidence: publish faults `AvrEntryNotFoundFault` / "File format was not recognized"; July: imported taskflows stayed documentState INVALID

title: POST /api/v2/job rejects advanced taskflows (403 UI_13430)
text: The v2 job resource starts Data Integration tasks and linear workflows (`taskType` `MTT`/`WORKFLOW`). An advanced taskflow was rejected with `403 UI_13430`: it runs from its published endpoint. Run the member tasks in waves, or build the flow as a linear taskflow.

title: Replace an unpublishable taskflow with RunAJob dependency waves and a native schedule
text: Fire each task with `POST /api/v2/job` in dependency waves derived from the tasks' source reads. After each wave, barrier-poll the activity log until every run is terminal, matching runs by `runId`. Pre-truncate targets whose connector ignores truncate, fail loudly on any state 3, and offer dry-run and resume-from-wave. A published taskflow's run-URL trigger script should use distinct exit codes (success, failed, timeout, URL not configured) so callers can fall back.
evidence: 22 tasks in 5 waves, exit 0, gold matching the baseline exactly

title: Create a v2 schedule with an explicit body: startTime pod-local plus startTimeUTC
text: `POST /api/v2/schedule {"@type":"schedule","name":"<tag>_<app>_<cadence>","description":"...","interval":"Hourly"|"Daily"|"Minutely","frequency":<n>,"timeZoneId":"GMT","startTime":"<pod-local time>Z","startTimeUTC":"<true UTC>Z","weekDay":false,"dayOfMonth":0,"mon":true,...,"sun":true}`. On a UTC-4 pod, local = UTC − 4 h (the API read `startTime` as pod-local and set `startTimeUTC = startTime + 4 h`). Read `startTimeUTC` back. Create migration schedules unbound, and make the create idempotent by name.
evidence: the first target runs fired at the expected UTC minutes; startTimeUTC read back

title: UI_10612 without day flags on an hourly schedule; UI_10621 off a 5-minute boundary
text: `POST /api/v2/schedule` with `interval:"Hourly"` fails with `UI_10612` unless the day-of-week flags (`mon`…`sun`) are set. The start minute must be on a 5-minute boundary, otherwise `UI_10621`.
evidence: UI_10612 without the flags, created with them; UI_10621 on an off-boundary minute

title: Bind and unbind schedules by POSTing the workflow or task with scheduleId (null unbinds)
text: `GET /api/v2/workflow/<wfId>`, drop `createTime/updateTime/createdBy/updatedBy`, set `scheduleId` to `"<scheduleId>"` (bind) or `null` (unbind), `POST /api/v2/workflow/<wfId>`, then GET it again and compare. The same works at task level on `/api/v2/mttask/<id>`, with no taskflow needed. Prove the verb on a low-risk workflow first, and snapshot every binding as the rollback baseline.
evidence: read-backs showed None after an unbind and the new id after a bind, in two orgs; 18 tasks bound at task level ran with a scheduler context (2026-07-09)

title: Ending a schedule: set endTime and endTimeUTC; a v3 disable PATCH returns V3API_007
text: `endTime` is read as pod-local even when written with `Z`: an `endTime` of "23:40Z" meant 03:40Z on a UTC-4 pod, and the lane kept running and failing. Set both `endTime` and `endTimeUTC` on a :05 boundary, and confirm no run fires after it. `PATCH /public/core/v3/schedule/<id> {"status":"disabled"}` returned `400 V3API_007`. Unbinding (`scheduleId:null`) is the simpler stop.
evidence: a schedule ran 4 hours longer than intended until both fields were set; the last run came just before the fixed end

title: At cutover, scan every task's detail for a task-level schedule
text: Mapping tasks can be bound to a schedule directly, and the v2 task list does not return `scheduleId`. Before a cutover, or before moving or deleting schedules, scan every task's detail as well as every workflow. Otherwise a task keeps running in the old org.
evidence: a task-level binding missed by a workflow-only unbind ran once more in the old org; a scan of 159 details found only that one

title: REPO_17314: taskflows that share tasks cannot overlap
text: Starting a linear taskflow while another taskflow that runs the same tasks is running fails with `REPO_17314` "Another instance of the Linear Taskflow is currently running". Two orchestrators firing the same tasks get the same error. Keep on-demand subset lanes out of a quiet window around the scheduled full run (e.g. 7 minutes before to 1 minute after), make lanes mutually exclusive, or remove the subset taskflows.
evidence: the collision retired a cron runner; the quiet-window fix held

title: Never clone a new schedule from another application's schedule
text: Builders that created a schedule by GETting an existing schedule, stripping `id/orgId/createTime/updateTime/createdBy/updatedBy/startTimeUTC` and renaming it broke when that template schedule was deleted. Create schedules from an explicit body.
evidence: builders' schedule paths raised after the template schedule was deleted with its application

title: A schedule whose start date lies years ahead never fires
text: A task can look scheduled while its schedule's start date lies far in the future, so it never runs. Read each schedule's start time and next run before claiming scheduled operation.
evidence: a schedule starting in 2037; data moved only on manual runs

title: Delete a schedule; a deleted schedule's GET returns an empty 200 shell
text: `DELETE /api/v2/schedule/<id>` → 200. A GET of the deleted schedule returns an empty 200 shell, so confirm with `GET /api/v2/schedule` (the list). Unbind or delete schedules before deleting the tasks bound to them (`REPO_52013`).
evidence: read-backs during a cleanup

title: Run an agent-side script from a taskflow with a Command Task (documented, not done headless)
text: To run a shell script natively on a schedule, create a Command Task (runtime environment = the agent's; Script File = an executable path on the agent), add it as a taskflow step, set Allowed Users, and publish and schedule the taskflow. Canvas automation of this was fragile (nested iframes, SVG edge drags, allowed users not persisting). Advanced taskflow publish is walled headless (L-CDI-070).
evidence: Documented, not live-proven: a design; canvas automation fragile; not completed headless

title: The pipeline generator contract: plan + SQL -> tasks idempotent by name -> folder -> taskflows -> schedules
text: **Inputs:** a directory of SQL files (one per curated table), a spec (`name, sql, target, reads, kind`, optional `materialization: view`), a landing table list and a mode (live|shadow). **Order of work:** 1. Ensure the project and folder. 2. Upsert one landing task per source table, then the raw layer (a task, or a view for long-text tables). 3. Upsert the medallion tasks in topological order of `reads`, with views emitted as DDL. 4. Add the special shapes (reverse-ETL, SaaS, files, snapshots). 5. Write the plan file. 6. Build one linear taskflow per lane (keeping its schedule), and bind schedules created unbound.
evidence: generators re-run many times in shadow and live modes without duplicates; 159 tasks built

title: Idempotent task upsert: look up by name, update in place with id and frsGuid
text: Cache `{name: id}` from `GET /api/v2/task?type=MTT` once per run. If the name exists: `GET /api/v2/mttask/<id>`, set `body.id=<id>` and `body.frsGuid=<current frsGuid>`, and `POST /api/v2/mttask/<id>`. Otherwise `POST /api/v2/mttask`, record the new id, and move and tag the new object. Require 200, and fail with the first 300 characters of any other answer.
evidence: repeated generator runs rewrote the same tasks and never duplicated one

title: Rewrite logical dataset names to physical ones per mode (live or shadow)
text: Write mapping SQL against logical dataset names (`raw.`, `staging.`, `<gold>.`). At build time rewrite each one to `` `<cloud-project>`.<physical>. `` with a regex that skips names already qualified: `(?<![\w`.])<logical>\.`. A shadow mode maps every logical dataset to a shadow twin, so the whole chain can be built, run and compared without touching what apps read. Keep one mapping dict per mode.
evidence: a shadow build produced a full parallel chain for parity tests

title: Generate the STRING raw layer from column metadata; long-text tables get a view instead
text: For each landed table, generate a SELECT over the typed landing table: - `JSON_VALUE(col)` for JSON columns; - `FORMAT('%.<scale>f', col)` for scaled numerics; - `FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S+00:00', col, 'UTC')` for timestamps (the `%E6S` form when microseconds are non-zero); - `CAST(col AS STRING)` otherwise.
