Splitting into a hot task (7 tables users watch; cycle 5 s, flush 2 s) and a cold task (7 back-office tables; cycle 10 s, flush 5 s), each with its own publication and slot, brought source-to-BigQuery latency to 10-22 s.

title: Move a CDC stream to another org on the same slot: stop the old job, start the new one, keep the old for rollback
text: Deploy the new org's task ahead of time without starting it. At the switch, stop (do not undeploy) the old job, then start the new job on the same slot and publication. A CDC_COMBINED task with LATEST re-runs the initial unload into the existing target tables and then streams, and the merge apply keeps parity. Verify one consumer, 0 errors, and a source audit maximum equal to the warehouse's. Rollback = stop the new job and resume the old one on the same slot.
evidence: about 70 s to the first target write and 3 min 13 s until all 13 tables were in continuous CDC (2026-09-28)

title: An imported DBMI task keeps the source's slot and publication names, and its first start re-runs the initial load
text: A DBMI task imported from another org carries the source's replication slot and publication; change them, or reuse them deliberately, before deploying. On its first start a CDC_COMBINED task with cdcStartPoint LATEST re-runs the initial load, rewriting the target tables before it streams.
evidence: import read-back and the 3-minute re-baseline (2026-09-28)

title: Split a running CDC task onto new slots; drop the old slot only after the old job is gone
text: Create the new publications (`FOR TABLE` per split; add `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` and SELECT for any newly captured table) and their slots; create and deploy the new tasks without starting them; stop the old job and start the new ones; watch lag and errors; then undeploy the old job and drop its slot. Dropping the old slot ends the rollback path onto it, so do it only after the new tasks are verified.
evidence: split executed 2026-09-29: new tasks live at 03:11Z, old slot dropped at 03:31Z

title: Never set datatype rules on a BigQuery-target CDC task
text: DBMI datatype change rules (`datatypeChangeRules`; five spellings of `timestamptz` to STRING over three redeploys) did not take effect for a BigQuery target, and a half-applied rule (staging `_EXT` column STRING, target column TIMESTAMP) made the MERGE fail non-retriably, so the job died silently for about 2 hours. Recover by redeploying with `datatypeChangeRules=[]` (a new job id). Supersedes L-DBMI-049.
evidence: 2-hour outage and recovery (2026-09-26)

title: DBMI misreads PostgreSQL fractional seconds that end in zero
text: PostgreSQL text trims trailing zeros (`.46035`) and DBMI stores it as `.046035`, so about 10% of timestamps are off by less than 1 s, on both the initial-load and the CDC path; whole seconds and minute or day aggregates are right. Fix it downstream: in the views over the CDC tables, take an exact batch copy's timestamp when it is within 1 s of the CDC value. Worth a support case.
evidence: parity 0/0 on the affected marts after the view fix (2026-09-26); still present after an org move (2026-09-29)

title: DBMI skips no-op UPDATEs: test CDC with a real change and revert it
text: An UPDATE that changes nothing is not replicated, so it proves nothing. Make a real change and revert it (for example shift a timestamp by one microsecond and back) and time both directions.

title: Deletes replicate: purge test rows at the source and the CDC copy follows
text: Source row deletes are applied to the CDC target, so purging test records at the source (after archiving them) also cleans the CDC dataset and any views over it; no separate warehouse cleanup is needed.
evidence: CDC dataset clean after a source purge (2026-09-26)

title: `session_replication_role=replica` silences triggers, but CDC still captures the change
text: A bulk fix run in one transaction with `SET session_replication_role = replica` suppresses ordinary triggers (for example `pg_notify` relays that would flood a real-time integration), while the changes are still written to WAL and captured by logical CDC within the normal latency. Take backups and an undo script first. Pre-flight before any bulk UPDATE on a CDC source table: list its triggers (`SELECT tgname, pg_get_triggerdef(t.oid) FROM pg_trigger t JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = t.tgrelid WHERE c.relname IN ('<table>', ...) AND NOT tgisinternal`); a per-row `pg_notify` trigger feeding a real-time relay would turn a ~590-row key backfill into ~590 CAI-to-SaaS upserts. Then, in ONE explicit transaction: `SET LOCAL session_replication_role = replica`; `SHOW session_replication_role` and abort unless it returns `replica` (SET LOCAL has no effect outside a transaction block, for example on an autocommit connection); create backup tables of the old values; run the UPDATE; commit. Setting the parameter needs a superuser (or a role granted SET on it); if the SET fails, roll back before changing anything, and keep an undo script that restores from the backup tables.
evidence: changes reached the warehouse in about 30 s without firing the relay (2026-09-28); a trigger inventory before a ~587-row backfill found a per-row NOTIFY trigger feeding the CAI relay, and the backfill was re-guarded with SET LOCAL plus a SHOW check (2026-10-01)

title: CDC watchdog: job state, slot lag, end-to-end freshness, bounded auto-resume
text: Every 5 minutes: check that `GET /dbmi/api/v1/task/<taskId>/job` says `running`; check that the slot exists and `pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn)` is below a threshold; check that the newest source audit row older than 5 minutes is in the warehouse. Auto-resume a failed job (`job/resume`) only when the task log shows a transient warehouse error (`Retrying the job may solve the problem`, `100032`, `backendError`, `rateLimitExceeded`) and no schema or type error (`Value of type`, `cannot be assigned to`, `does not exist`, `Permission denied`), at most 3 times per rolling hour. Alert only on state changes, write one health row per check, and pause the watchdog explicitly during planned redeploys. After an agent-host reboot, deployed CDC jobs report `awaiting_auto_restart` and return to `running` by themselves (about 20 minutes after boot in one case, with slot lag back to 0 and no manual resume): treat `awaiting_auto_restart` as transient for at least 30 minutes after an agent restart before resuming or alerting, and never drop or recreate the slot meanwhile (L-DBMI-016).
evidence: built after one job died silently for 2 hours and another stopped on a transient 100032 (2026-09-26); two CDC jobs passed through awaiting_auto_restart back to running after one host reboot (2026-09-30)

title: Measure CDC landing latency per table: `APPENDS()` for inserts, change counters against `__TABLES__` for updates
text: Read each row's landed time from BigQuery's `APPENDS()` change-history function on the CDC tables and compare it with the source commit time. DBMI did not persist its commit timestamp (`OP_CMT_TIME`) and `track_commit_timestamp` was off, so the source row's `created_at` served as the commit proxy. A cheaper check compares the newest source `created_at` with the table's `last_modified_time`. Two methods. (1) Inserts: per row, BigQuery `APPENDS()` `_CHANGE_TIMESTAMP` minus the source `created_at`, excluding rows copied by the initial load. (2) Update-heavy traffic, where insert-based probes see nothing: sample PostgreSQL `pg_stat_user_tables` every 2 s (`n_tup_ins + n_tup_upd + n_tup_del` per table) and note when each counter first moves; poll `<dataset>.__TABLES__` `last_modified_time` every 3 s; the first last-modified after the change is the apply time. A cycle applies tables one after another (L-DBMI-019), so report every table, not one, and prove catch-up separately (an audit table's max id equal at the source and in the warehouse). Measured: one task 15-35 s per table; after the hot/cold split 10.7-22.7 s; over 24 h with the split, inserts on five tables landed in an average 25.9 s (fastest 10.0 s, n=305; 20.5 s on the hot table, 26.6-28.9 s on four transaction tables), with a 10-11 s floor on every table; new-entity inserts alone averaged 22.1 s (median 21.2 s, p90 29.7 s, worst 56 s, n=61). Views defined over the CDC tables are evaluated at query time, so a record is visible in them the moment it lands: report them as the CDC figure, not as an extra hop (L-CDI-206).
evidence: p50 about 20 s (2026-09-27); the counter-versus-__TABLES__ method before and after the hot/cold split (2026-09-28/29); APPENDS() minus created_at over 24 h windows on two days plus three traced records at 13-21 s (2026-10-01)

title: Where DBMI task logs live on the agent
text: Task logs are under `<agent_home>/apps/Database_Ingestion/logs/tasks/`, named like `*_<jobId>-CDC_COMBINED-*.log`, and are root-readable only; grep ` ERROR ` in the newest file before resuming a job. A running job's PowerExchange processes show as `PwxAgent_dbmi_<task>_<job>` under the agent's OS user. Per-table progress is logged in the newest `<task>_<jobId>*.log` as `transition event [<EVENT>]. Details: [table=<schema>.<table>`: `M4_UNLOAD_COMPLETE` marks the end of a table's initial unload and `NORMAL_CONTINUOUS_CDC_TABLE` marks it streaming. A start, restart or task split is complete when every table's latest event is NORMAL_CONTINUOUS_CDC_TABLE and the file has no ` ERROR `, ` SEVERE ` or ` FATAL ` lines (`grep -oE 'transition event \[[A-Z0-9_]+\]. Details: \[table=[a-z_.]+' <log>` lists them). Prove an old job is gone by its log's last write time and zero `PwxAgent_dbmi_<task>_<job>` processes, and prove there is one consumer on the slot.
evidence: used by the watchdog and the split watch (2026-09-26 to 2026-09-29); 13 tables reached NORMAL_CONTINUOUS_CDC_TABLE 3 min 13 s after a new job started (initial unload included), and a hot/cold split took 14 tables to continuous CDC with 0 errors (2026-09-28/29)

title: Failed probe jobs linger in Running Jobs until undeployed
text: Failed DBMI probe instances stay in Monitor > Running Jobs until they are undeployed (in the UI or with `job/undeploy`); clean them up before demos and before deleting the tasks.
evidence: Running Jobs clean after undeploying three probes (2026-09-24)

title: Initial-load (UNLOAD) tasks fail import validation with 403 FORBIDDEN when the target agent has no DBMI engine
text: Importing UNLOAD tasks failed with 'Cannot validate vendor for task with type UNLOAD because of the following error: Response: 403 FORBIDDEN. Access denied.', and because an import is all-or-nothing the other 180 objects in the package were skipped. The likely cause was that the target agent had no Database Ingestion engine yet (not proven). Enable the engine first, or drop these tasks from the package and create them with task/create later.
evidence: 5 vendor-validation errors plus 180 'skipped because of previous failures' (2026-09-28)

title: A BigQuery DBMI target needs the Simba BigQuery JDBC driver set on the agent, then a restart
text: A deploy fails with 'Failed to load driver class com.simba.googlebigquery.jdbc.Driver' until the Simba BigQuery JDBC set is installed: about 73 jars in `<agent_home>/apps/Database_Ingestion/ext/connectors/thirdparty/`, and `GoogleBigQueryJDBC42.jar` also in `<agent_home>/apps/Database_Ingestion/<version>/dbmi_libs/libs/`, owned by the agent's OS user. Restart the agent afterwards, because the classloader caches the classpath at start. Copying the set from another agent that already ran DBMI to BigQuery worked.
evidence: deploy failure, then success after the copy, the restart and a key fix (2026-09-28)

title: Give DBMI its own BigQuery connection and probe the private-key format per engine
text: On one pod the CDI BigQuery V2 connector accepted the service-account key only without its header lines, while DBMI's Simba driver rejected that form with '[Simba] Invalid PKCS#8 data' and accepted a PEM form. Keep one BigQuery connection per consumer (a CDI one and a DBMI-only one) and find each format with a probe loop: set the key (v2 GET, edit `connParams.privateKey`, POST back), run `GET /api/v2/connection/test/<connId>`, then `task/deploy` and poll; keep the first form that passes both. Never paste a key with raw newlines into a hand-written JSON string.
evidence: five key forms tested against both consumers; no single form passed both on that pod (2026-09-28)

title: Which PEM form the Simba driver accepts is disputed
text: The run reports say DBMI took the 'escaped PEM' (literal backslash-n), but the script that created the DBMI-only connection applied a replace that is a byte-for-byte no-op, so the value sent was most likely the unmodified PEM from the key file (JSON-encoded normally). An earlier finding on another pod said the v2 connection API needed escaped newlines for CDI as well. Treat the exact form as unknown and probe it on each pod.
evidence: reports vs the script source (2026-09-28); earlier pod finding (2026-09-22/25)

title: A BigQuery DBMI target stages through GCS: the connection's service account needs bucket rights
text: DBMI loads BigQuery through a GCS staging bucket (`target.bucket`, `target.directory`, `targetBucket`, `targetDirectory`). Grant the connection's service account write, list and delete on that bucket (for example a bucket-scoped storage admin or object admin role) and verify with a real write, list and delete before running the task. A service account without `storage.buckets.create` cannot create the bucket, so create it separately.
evidence: grant verified with write/list/delete (2026-06-29); a load waited on the missing bucket (2026-09-22)

title: A relational DBMI target needs no cloud staging; `selectionRules` take include and exclude
text: A PostgreSQL target is written through a local file and JDBC COPY, so no bucket is needed; an initial load (UNLOAD) of 24 tables and 682,385 rows completed in 43 s. `selectionRules` honor both forms, for example `[{"include":"*"},{"exclude":"<table>"}]`.
evidence: job completed in 43 s with the row counts read back (2026-09-22)

title: UNLOAD edge cases: character primary keys and dropped NOT-NULL columns
text: Tables whose primary key is a character type failed the initial load with `VerifyValueException: Field Schema.column value error: no columns` (a read-side failure; bigint-keyed tables in the same task loaded). On a PostgreSQL target the COPY also dropped some NOT-NULL text columns of internal control tables, causing NOT-NULL violations. Exclude such tables, or add a numeric surrogate key at the source.
evidence: agent task log stack and the reruns with exclusions (2026-09-22)

title: DBMI offered no Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse target (July 2026)
text: The DBMI CLI rejected a Fabric target with `No enum constant com.informatica.dbmicli.domain.Vendor.FABRIC`. Recheck the target list for your release; otherwise use CDI mapping tasks (the Fabric DW connector is a valid mapping target) or land files for Fabric to read.
evidence: dbmicli error text (2026-07-06)

title: The DBMI command-line client ships with the agent
text: Run `<agent_home>/apps/dbmicli/dbmicli.jar` with the agent's bundled JDK (`JAVA_HOME=<agent_home>/jdk`) and log in at the domain host (`<domain>.informaticacloud.com`), not the pod host. Task definitions are YAML (source connection and schema, table list, target connection and schema).
evidence: dbmicli login OK (2026-07-06)

title: DBMI entitlement is proven by agent engines and privileges, not by a 404
text: Check `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` for the `Database_Ingestion` and `MassIngestionRuntime` engines in RUNNING state and the `create.dbmi.task` / `execute.dbmi.task` privileges, and enable the Mass Ingestion (databases) service on the runtime environment. A 404 on a DBMI path means the wrong host or path, not a missing license. Supersedes L-DBMI-046.
evidence: engines RUNNING and privileges present while every probed path returned 404 (2026-07-05 to 2026-07-09)

title: Where CDC lives in IDMC and what it competes with
text: CDC runs on the integration and ingestion runtime (Database Ingestion and Replication with PowerExchange readers), not on the Data Quality service. Cloud-native tools (AWS DMS, GCP Datastream, Databricks Lakeflow Connect, Snowflake Openflow, Fabric Mirroring) also do log-based CDC but only replicate rows; Informatica's distinct edge is mainframe and legacy CDC (DB2 z/OS, VSAM, IMS, IDMS, Adabas through PowerExchange).
evidence: fact-checked against vendor sources (2026-08-14)

title: Watermark MERGE makes batch incremental, but tables without `updated_at` need log-based CDC
text: A watermark-based incremental MERGE (read the watermark, MERGE rows newer than the watermark minus a lookback, write back MAX(ts)) cut one scan by 97.4% and stays idempotent, but a timestamp watermark cannot see UPDATEs or DELETEs on tables with no `updated_at`. Use log-based CDC for mutable tables, or add an application-maintained `updated_at`.
evidence: second MERGE run touched 6,804 rows instead of a full reload (2026-07-04)

title: A running CDC job kept working when the org's monthly job limit stopped every CDI run
text: When an org exceeded its monthly job limit, every CDI mapping-task start failed within seconds, while a running DBMI CDC job (and the CAI runtime) kept working, probably because a continuous job is started once rather than per cycle. Prefer CDC for per-event freshness and budget the batch jobs.
evidence: CDC healthy through a job-cap outage of several hours (2026-09-28)

title: DBMI authoring is a UI wizard because every mi/dbmi REST path 404s
text: Early probes of `/saas/public/mi/v2/*`, `/dbmi/v1/tasks`, `/data360/mi/v1/tasks`, `/api/v2/miTask` and `/public/mi/v1/tasks` on the pod host all failed, and `MI_TASK` counted 0, so authoring was recorded as UI-only. Every probe had used the platform host; DBMI answers on `<pod>-ing`. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-DBMI-001.
evidence: 404s on the platform host (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-25)

title: A DBMI 404 means the entitlement is missing and needs a purchase
text: 404s on DBMI paths were read as an unprovisioned license. The engines were deployed and the privileges present; the 404s were wrong-host or wrong-path results. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-05; overturned by L-DBMI-041.
evidence: 404s read as missing entitlement (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-05)

title: DBMI deploy and run have no public REST verb
text: A 26-probe matrix (mftsaas jobs and deploy variants, `/dbmi/api/v1/tasks/<id>/deploy` without the `public` segment, v3 objects deploy/activate/publish, disServiceController) found no deploy handler, and on one agent build the task GET surface answered 'No static resource'. The verb lives at `/dbmi/public/api/v2/task/deploy/<taskId>` on `<pod>-ing`; the probes missed the `public` segment or used the wrong host or header. Was believed 2026-09-22 to 2026-09-23; overturned by L-DBMI-003.
evidence: 20x 404 and 6x login-HTML 200 in the probe matrix (2026-09-22); 'No static resource' (2026-09-23)

title: Author the first DBMI task in the UI wizard, then clone it
text: With no REST create known and the task designer hanging under eight UI-automation approaches, the plan was a manual authoring session for the first CDC task. task/create from a JSON body replaced it. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-09-21; overturned by L-DBMI-003.
evidence: designer hung in Loading (2026-07-09)

title: A datatype rule (timestamptz to STRING) fixes the fractional-seconds defect
text: The first remedy for the fractional-seconds defect was a DBMI datatype rule landing timestamps as strings. The rules never took effect for a BigQuery target, and a half-applied rule killed the job; the fix moved to the views. Was believed 2026-09-26 (hours); overturned by L-DBMI-023.
evidence: candidate fix recorded, then five failed spellings and an outage (2026-09-26)

title: Data Quality authors and measures; a CDI mapping on a Secure Agent executes
text: IDMC Data Quality is licensed and metered separately but has no production run engine or mapping designer of its own. To cleanse, parse, match/deduplicate or verify addresses on real data, add the DQ assets to the matching transformations in a Data Integration mapping that runs on a Secure Agent (CDQ April 2026 Introduction pp.6-7: design and run the mappings in Data Integration). DQ alone can author assets, test them on sample rows at design time, profile and score, and schedule a single profiling task; it lacks taskflow orchestration and writes no cleansed data to a target (only exception/reject rows). Advanced DQ (match, address, parse) is not pushdown-eligible and runs on the agent; MDM SaaS has its own cleanse/match/merge. Plan and size DQ with a CDI mapping around it.
evidence: Page-cited vendor docs (CDQ Introduction April 2026 pp.6-7; IICS Getting Started pp.6-7); used as a locked planning decision on 2026-09-17

title: Say precisely what Data Quality can do without CDI
text: DQ asset editors test rules on sample rows at design time, so say that DQ alone cannot run on production data, not that it has no engine. DQ alone can schedule one profiling or DQ task but has no taskflow orchestration; profiling is standalone, while viewing the scorecard dashboard needs CDGC and a governance role; DQ alone extracts exception/reject rows (Exception Management) but writes no cleansed data to a target; CDGC lineage is CLAIRE-generated with confidence thresholds or added manually, not purely automatic.
evidence: Find-and-verify pass over 15 claims

title: The DQ runtime lives inside the Data Integration Server on the agent
text: Enabling Data Quality on a Secure Agent adds no separate DQ service directory: the DQ runtime is part of the Data Integration Server (the DIS version bumps when DQ is enabled), with the DQ libraries under `<DIS>/.../ICS/main/DQ`. Troubleshoot DQ transformation runs through the DIS logs.
evidence: DQ libraries found under the DIS ICS/main/DQ directory after enabling DQ

title: A CDI task that runs SQL imitating DQ is not IDMC Data Quality
text: If a mapping task only pushes down SQL written to mimic cleansing or match/merge, IDMC ran a job but the DQ logic is still SQL. Genuine IDMC DQ means the logic lives in DQ assets and transformations (Cleanse, Standardizer, Parser, Match/Merge or Deduplicate, Rule Specification, Profiling) executed by the engine. Read the mapping or its customQuery before claiming that DQ runs in IDMC, and label every status by evidence layer (IDMC-native versus SQL equivalent).
evidence: Mapping SQL inspection: comments described the SQL as an analog of CDQ cleanse and match/merge

title: The six Data Quality capabilities a complete demonstration covers
text: (1) Profiling (completeness, conformity, consistency, accuracy, duplication); (2) standardization and cleansing (address, phone, formats); (3) deduplication (identify and merge); (4) parsing and enrichment (parse free text; enrich, for example ZIP to geography from reference data); (5) rule-based DQ applied continuously in transit; (6) AI-pipeline readiness (remediate before vectorization, embed only valid records). With only entitled features, use a reference-data lookup for geo enrichment instead of a licensed address verification service.
evidence: A demonstration mandate and its build plan

title: CDQ dictionaries have a write-only REST API on the dedicated `<pod>-dqcloud-api` host
text: POST `https://<pod>-dqcloud-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/quality/public/v2/dictionaries/` with Content-Type: application/json and Authorization: Bearer `<jwt>` (or IDS-SESSION-ID) and body {name (max 125 chars), description, columns[] (max 42, unique, max 64 chars each), path (project folder)} returns 201 with the dictionary id. Documented: DELETE `.../dictionaries/<id>` (204); `.../dictionaries/<id>/rows` with POST to add, PUT to replace and DELETE to clear, body {cols[], rows[[...]]}, at most 10,000 rows per call (413 above); POST `.../dictionaries/<id>/finishUpload` is mandatory to commit pending row operations (424 if skipped); 409 on state conflicts. There is no GET or PATCH anywhere, so keep the id from the create response or take it from the UI URL. The API host is the DQ app host with -api appended (`<pod>-dqcloud` becomes `<pod>-dqcloud-api`).
evidence: 201 on create, live on a dm-us pod; the rest per the CDQ API Reference (April 2026)

title: A dictionary accepts UI edits or API edits, never both: Convert to API first
text: A dictionary has one editing environment at a time. For a dictionary authored in the UI, someone must click Convert to API (Definition or Configuration tab) before REST can write it; Convert to UI switches it back, and the create response's customAttributes carry a MODE attribute naming the environment that may update or delete it. A dictionary created through the API presumably starts in API mode, since the documented flow creates it and adds rows over REST. Dictionaries sourced from Reference 360 are editable only in Reference 360. No receipt of the Convert click has been captured.
evidence: Vendor CDQ Dictionaries guide and API Reference (April 2026); UI receipt not captured

title: The `<pod>-dqcloud-api` host is not mounted on every pod
text: The dictionary host answered on one dm-us pod and failed on a dmp-us pod; one record says 404 (not mounted), another says 401 (a role gap). The vendor examples all use dm-us pods. Resolve the host by DNS and make one authenticated call before designing on it.
evidence: Conflicting records: 404 versus 401 on a dmp-us pod; 200 on a dm-us pod

title: The CDQ public REST API is dictionaries-only: no rule, rule-spec, scorecard or profile endpoints
text: The April 2026 CDQ API Reference covers only the Dictionary API. Probed and rejected: /data360/dq/v1/ruleSpecifications (404 on every verb), /public/dq/v1/rules and /api/v2/dqRule (404), /quality/public/v2/scorecards (GET and POST 404) and /data360/businessDataset/v1, the CDGC rule-occurrence scoring object (POST 404). Rule specifications are readable through GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='RULE_SPECIFICATION' and authored in the rulebuilder or by migration clone; profiles and profile rule occurrences live on the separate `<pod>-dqprofile` service.
evidence: Official docs with zero hits for rule or scorecard endpoints; 404 on all probed variants (2026-07-05 to 2026-07-25)

title: Rule specifications can be authored headless by cloning a template through v3 export/import
text: Direct create fails (POST /public/core/v3/objects returns 405 Method not supported; every /data360/dq/* rule path returns 404), but a same-type template can be cloned: POST /saas/public/core/v3/export {`"objects":[{"id":"<frsGuid>"`}]} and download the package; give the object a new GUID and name; recompute the SHA-256 of every edited file; POST /saas/public/core/v3/import/package as multipart/form-data (200 checksumValid=true); POST `/saas/public/core/v3/import/<id>` to start and poll it to SUCCESSFUL; then confirm with the v3 objects census on RULE_SPECIFICATION. The clone inherits the template's expression logic, so making each rule implement its own check still needs the rulebuilder canvas.
evidence: Export 200, edit and re-hash, import/package 200 checksumValid=true, import SUCCESSFUL; RULE_SPECIFICATION count went 4 to 11 to 12

title: Moving rule specifications between orgs: package them and check their dependencies
text: Rule specs travel as RULE_SPECIFICATION objects in a v3 export/import package, imported with REUSE on name conflicts. Check for cross-pod version mismatch, whether the functions they reference are licensed in the target, and that every dictionary they read exists in the target; passwords are not exported; verify the rule count after import. Rule specs from Informatica bundles must exist in the target (or be imported with REUSE) before profiles that bind them can be re-bound. Exporting a bundle rule spec succeeded in an org where exporting an Add-On Bundle mapping template had been refused with 403 MigrationSvc_038 in another org, so test bundle-object export per org.
evidence: Rule-spec and bundle-rule exports SUCCESSFUL (2026-09-23); rules invisible in the target until migrated (2026-09-12); re-bound after import (2026-09-28)

title: A rule specification can be exposed as a request/response API through API Center
text: In Explore, Actions > Enable for APIs on a rule specification (API name up to 100 characters) sends an enablement request; import the API-enabled rule into API Center, design and publish an endpoint, and external applications then invoke it for real-time or incremental checks. This gives per-request verdicts only, with no scorecard and no results table. A mapplet that contains a Rule Specification transformation can be API-enabled in a similar way.
evidence: Vendor DQ Assets guide (April 2026) chapter 21; untested

title: Data Quality for Fabric (DQF) is a profiling-only preview, not a scoring path
text: DQF (April 2025) is a preview run from the Microsoft Fabric UI that profiles Fabric data; it has no rules, no scorecards and no REST, API or RunAJob surface. For DQ scores on Fabric data, a CDI mapping task that evaluates rules is stronger.
evidence: DQF April 2025 guide: zero hits for rule, scorecard or API

title: Data Preparation had no REST plane on the probed orgs
text: /dataprep/projects and /prep/v1/projects returned 404 on GET and POST, and `<pod>-prep` and `<pod>-dataprep` had no DNS on at least one pod. Treat Data Preparation as UI-only (or absent) there, and meet parsing needs with a parse asset in a mapping or with deterministic code.

title: Address verification: batch REST at 1,000 addresses per call versus one per MCP call
text: POST `<baseApiUrl>/dataquality/addressverification/api/v1/process` (Bearer identity JWT) verifies, standardizes and geocodes addresses in 240+ countries, up to 1,000 addresses per call and 100 suggestions in interactive mode; GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE return 405. The job token expires in 5 minutes; free resubmits are 2x in interactive mode and 9x in QuickCapture. The managed MCP action verify_address handles one address per call.
evidence: Vendor Cloud Address Verification guide (July 2025)

title: Verify addresses from a pipeline through the managed MCP server dqverifyaddress: pre-merge input, real test addresses, a hash cache and a first-check timestamp
text: The Cloud Address Verification service is exposed as the managed MCP server with context dqverifyaddress and tool verify_address (Interactive mode). Call it from a small pipeline for new records only, cap the calls per run and per day, and store the result code per record in a warehouse table (codes seen: VERIFIED, VERIFIED_CORRECTED, LOW_CONFIDENCE_MATCH, STREET_NOT_FOUND, HOUSE_NUMBER_NOT_FOUND, NO_ADDRESS). E-mail and phone verification and geocoding need their own servers and licences; without them, use CDQ format flags. (1) Feed it from the per-record pre-merge layer, not the de-duplicated golden view: an enrichment job that read the golden view never verified the addresses of records that match-and-merge had folded into a survivor (44 skipped); MERGE (upsert) the results. (2) Test data needs real addresses: invented streets are correctly answered STREET_NOT_FOUND or HOUSE_NUMBER_NOT_FOUND (547 of about 600 synthetic records), so the verified rate stays low however often you re-check; draw from a small pool of real public addresses (civic buildings, libraries, arenas; never private homes) and derive messy variants (lower case, missing suffix or direction, spelled-out suffix, wrong ZIP): 25 of 25 returned VERIFIED and 9 of 10 variants VERIFIED_CORRECTED. A mix of about 72% clean, 24% messy and 5% invented keeps both the correction and the exception story; check shared pool addresses for collisions on the person match key before assigning them (L-MDM-072). Enrichment that deliberately skips test identities must still be proven on a real record. (3) Cost: cache results by a normalized-address hash (results were reusable for 30 days, so re-checks cost 0 calls) and key the work queue on that hash (L-DQ-018). (4) Timestamps: if re-checks MERGE into the results table, keep a first-verified timestamp that is set once (`first_checked_at = COALESCE(target.first_checked_at, target.checked_at)` on update) and count a latency sample only when the first check lands within a few minutes of the record's creation; overwriting the only timestamp turned a 33 s 'record to verified' metric into 26-54 hours. Lost first-check times can be recovered with time travel within about 7 days (L-CDI-161). (5) Swap the job's code under the same `flock` the job takes, after checking the live files' checksums, with a backup and an undo script. Measured with a 20 s polling job: source insert to first check about 33-34 s average (24-44 s, fastest 27 s), a few minutes more until visible in BI. Newer evidence: L-DQ-160.
evidence: 583 calls and 0 errors on the first run; invented addresses 344 STREET_NOT_FOUND and 203 HOUSE_NUMBER_NOT_FOUND, a real-address seed 25/25 VERIFIED and 9/10 variants VERIFIED_CORRECTED, 51 re-checks with 0 calls, 735 first-check times restored by time travel, and after the switch to the pre-merge layer 43 new records verified with 37 calls and 0 errors (2026-10-01)

title: MCP address-verification calls are not IDMC jobs
text: Calls to the dqverifyaddress MCP tool do not appear in the IDMC activity log and do not count against the org's monthly job limit. Describe such enrichment accordingly, and budget IPUs for the backing service.
evidence: Absent from the activity log while running every minute

title: A verification queue that picks only 'not yet enriched' rows never re-verifies a changed address
text: A downstream verification job that selects only records missing from its results table will not re-check a record whose address was added or changed later (for example a record first captured with NO_ADDRESS). Key the work queue on a hash of the address fields, or on the last-modified time.
evidence: Gap found in an end-to-end proof

title: Data Profiling profiles can be created, updated, executed and polled over REST
text: Base `https://<pod>-dqprofile.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/profiling-service/api/v1`, header IDS-SESSION-ID (a v3 session on some pods). List with GET /profile?limit=200; read with GET `/profile/<id>`; create with POST /profile using a body cloned from a known-good profile on the same connection type; update with PUT `/profile/<id>`; run with POST `/profile/<id>/execute` {} which returns 200 {profileJobId}; poll GET `/job/<profileJobId>` until the status leaves RUNNING, QUEUED, SUBMITTED or STARTING (COMPLETED means done; errorMessage on failure). Reads on the same host: run history one run at a time with `GET /runDetail/<profileId>/<runKey>` (runKey 1 to the profile's `lastRunKey`; each record carries `startTime` in epoch ms, `status`, `rowsProcessed`, `numberOfColumns` and `numberOfRules`), because the `/runDetail/<id>/filter` form answered 400 `PROFILE_SVC_00093` 'Invalid request - Provided argument does not match the expected type' to both POST and GET on one pod; `/ruleOccurrence/...ForProfile_V2_Token/<uuid>` (bindings), /ruleOccurrence/ruleType (the six dimensions) and `/metric-store/api/v1/odata/Profiles('<uuid>')/Columns`, /Insights, /Patterns, /ValueFrequencies. Profiling query CRUD is vendor-documented in a separate guide whose paths are not held. A run that dies with the agent (engines killed mid-run) can leave `lastRunKey: null`, so 'never run' does not prove that no profiling DTM ran; the agent names its profiling DTM sessions `s_profiling_<profileKey>_<run>_<n>`, which maps a running or crashed `pmdtm` process back to its profile.
evidence: 8 profiles executed to COMPLETED 'No errors encountered' in one org (2026-09-24) and 8/8 in another (2026-09-28); reads returned 200 on two pods (2026-07-25); runDetail/<id>/1 read back COMPLETED (33,277 rows, 39 columns), the /filter form 400 PROFILE_SVC_00093, a killed 181-column run left lastRunKey null (2026-10-03)

title: The `<pod>-dqprofile` service may need the v3 login session
text: On one dm-us pod the profiling service answered 401 'Exception encountered while processing JWT' to the v2 icSessionId sent in IDS-SESSION-ID, while the v3 login sessionId (POST `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas/public/core/v3/login`, field userInfo.sessionId) in the same header worked; another org accepted the v2 id. Make the profiling helper org-aware, or always send the v3 session. An HTML body with status 200 means the identity single-page app answered: the header or plane is wrong.
evidence: 401 with the v2 session; 8/8 profile jobs COMPLETED after switching to the v3 session

title: POST /profile with client-side ids fails with 500 'Row was updated or deleted'
text: When creating or updating a profile through the Data Profiling REST API, omit every id field (profile, source, runtimeOptions, rule blocks, profileable fields). Supplying client-side ids returns HTTP 500 'Row was updated or deleted'.
evidence: 500 with ids; success without them

title: PROFILE_MDL_00006: int4 and char(n) columns are rejected as profileable fields
text: Binding a profileable field or a rule occurrence to a Postgres int4 or character(n) column returns PROFILE_MDL_00006: skip those columns or profile a view that casts them. When building fields from information_schema, map text, varchar and uuid to NSTRING, numeric to DECIMAL (with precision and scale) and timestamps to TOOLKIT_DATETIME (timestamp or timestamp_with_time_zone); the builder skipped jsonb and array columns (whether the service accepts them is untested).
evidence: PROFILE_MDL_00006 on int4 and char(n) columns (2026-09-24); the builder's type map (2026-09-27)

title: Rule occurrences are bound inside the profile body: one rule block per rule spec, one MAPPLETFIELD per column
text: To bind a rule specification to columns, add it once to source.rules[] ({name, description, frsId, inFields[], outFields[], ruleType 'RULE_SPECIFICATION'}) and add one profileableFields[] entry per bound column with fieldType 'MAPPLETFIELD', the rule's frsId, scoreCardId null, a fresh assignmentIdentifier, inputFieldMappings [{dataSourceFieldName `<column>`, inFieldName `<rule_input>`}] and outputFieldMappings [{columnKey 40000+n, outFieldName `<rule_output>`, datatype 'string'}]; data columns are DATASOURCEFIELD entries with columnKey 10001+i. To change the rules, GET the profile, reset source.rules and keep only the DATASOURCEFIELD entries, append the new blocks, PUT it back, and run the profile again.
evidence: Profiles updated with 3-4 rule occurrences each and executed to COMPLETED

title: The platform job API cannot run a profile: 403 UI_13404
text: POST /saas/api/v2/job with a profile id returns 403 UI_13404 'Object identifier is not valid or missing' for every taskType tried (Profile, PROFILE, DSS), and /public/core/v3/jobs and `/v3/profile/<id>/run` return 404. Run profiles with POST `/profiling-service/api/v1/profile/<id>/execute` on `<pod>-dqprofile` instead.

title: Profiles travel between orgs in v3 export/import packages
text: POST /public/core/v3/objects for a Profile returns 405, but profiles move inside v3 export/import packages like other assets, so a profile authored once can be migrated or cloned headless.
evidence: Profiles present in the target after a package import

title: Profiles imported from another org arrive with 0 rule occurrences
text: After a v3 import, profiles came over without their rule occurrences: re-bind the rule specifications by the target's frsIds and run them again. Bundle rule specs must already exist in the target (import with REUSE), and project, folder and rule-spec id caches must be kept per org so that target objects never receive source-org ids.
evidence: Imported profiles re-bound; 8/8 profile jobs COMPLETED

title: Exported Profile objects hard-code their column list
text: A v3 export of a Profile yields a .PROFILE.json with connectionId, a hard-coded source.fields[] list and runtimeOptions, so pointing it at another table means rewriting the field list. Cloning through the REST body (GET a template profile, edit it, POST it) is simpler for new tables.
evidence: Export package inspected

title: Bulk profile imports: clear the target folder and skip empty object references
text: If a bulk profile import fails, delete the profiles already in the target folder (GET and DELETE on `/profiling-service/api/v1/profile/<id>`), confirm the list is empty and import again, unchecking any profile whose zip entry has an empty object reference. If a profile's column path is missing on the target connection, put the folder path in the source connection before exporting and importing.
evidence: Vendor Cloud Data Profiling guide (October 2025) pp.159-160; untested

title: Data profiles cannot be moved between folders (FRS_108): recreate them
text: FRS MoveEntities refuses data profiles (FRS_108) and the profiling API answers 'cannot move profile'. Recreate the profile directly in the target folder through the profiling REST API (frsProjectId and frsFolderId in the body), run it to COMPLETED, then delete the old one.
evidence: Recreated profiles ran to COMPLETED; disputed 2026-11-02 by L-DQ-124 (15 profiles moved with FRS_200; FRS_108 only on orphan profile documents)

title: API-updated profiles may show 'updated source metadata / unsaved changes' in the UI
text: After API-side updates, some data profiles open in the Data Profiling UI with an 'updated source metadata / unsaved changes' banner; saving them once from the UI clears it. Check before a demo.
evidence: 4 of 8 profiles showed the banner; all were clean after one UI save

title: No REST read of per-rule profile pass rates was found
text: Every guessed result path for the per-rule pass rates of a profile returned 'not implemented', and CDQ rule runtime scores were already unreadable over REST in July 2026. The console shows the scores (View Scorecard, and Results > Rules). Keep any app-facing DQ numbers in your own warehouse tables.
evidence: All guessed result paths 'not implemented' (2026-09-24); empty or 404 score reads (2026-07-13)

title: Keep 200 or fewer rule occurrences per profile; publishResults is internal
text: With more than about 200 rule occurrences on a profile, the scorecard job fails with a read time-out on an internal /profiling-service/internal/api/v1/ruleOccurrence/publishResults call while the profile results page still renders: keep at most 200 occurrences, re-import or trim, and re-run. The internal/ segment (seen only inside that error message, on an operations domain) means unsupported, so never call it.
evidence: Vendor Cloud Data Profiling guide p.160

title: Profiling needs the Amazon S3 V2 connector on the runtime environment when its results store is S3
text: In one org the profiling results warehouse was an Informatica-managed, immutable Amazon S3 V2 connection, and profiles (and the scorecards produced by running them) could not run until the Amazon S3 V2 add-on connector was enabled on the runtime environment. Symptom: GET `/api/v2/connection/test/<id>` returns 403 APP_105060 'Unable to fetch Connector attributes [com.infa.adapter.amazons3]'. Fix: Administrator > Add-On Connectors > Amazon S3 V2 > enable and assign to the runtime environment (the connector was already entitled org-wide).
evidence: 403 APP_105060 until the S3 V2 adapter was enabled

title: Profiling may use ADLS Gen2 or GCS as its results store (S3 not required)
text: A later note says a Data Profiling setup accepts ADLS Gen2 or GCS as the results warehouse and can profile a Postgres connection directly, so S3 is not required. It was not re-tested and conflicts in emphasis with L-DQ-033: if a profile fails with APP_105060 naming amazons3, enable the S3 V2 connector first, then check which store the org uses.
evidence: Peer session note, not re-tested

title: The Data Profiling wizard chokes on system and backup schemas
text: The wizard fails ('too many tables') when enumerating system or backup schemas (pg_catalog, information_schema, archive copies). Scope the connection's Schema field (not just the profile) to business schemas, and tick at least one column on the Columns tab or Save errors.
evidence: Wizard error on system schemas

title: Profiling exits 127 on Debian 12 because pmdtm needs libidn.so.11: symlink it to libidn.so.12
text: pmdtm (under ICS/main/bin/rdtm/) links libpmcurl.so, which needs libidn.so.11; Debian 12 (and RHEL/Rocky 8/9) ship only libidn.so.12, so every profile dies at launch with 'error while loading shared libraries: libidn.so.11' (exit 127) while metadata extraction still works. libidn 1.x is ABI-compatible: fix it durably with a system symlink in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, a copy in a compat directory registered in /etc/ld.so.conf.d plus ldconfig, and the compat directory on LD_LIBRARY_PATH in agent_start.sh, then restart the agent; verify with env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH ldd pmdtm. The same fix cleared a DTM exit 134.
evidence: 1,965 libidn misses equalled 1,965 exit-127s before the fix and 0 after; profiled columns went from 0 to 671 within an hour

title: Zero profiled columns: read the pmdtm exit code before chasing jobs, readyToRun or auth
text: When scans complete and metadata is present but no column is profiled, check how pmdtm died on the agent host: 127 means a native library failed to load, 134 SIGABRT, 137 an OOM kill. Every source failing identically is the tell. Stuck-job 406 locks, readyToRun=false and ccgf-auth-pep 500s did not explain it; the missing library did.
evidence: The exit-127 count matched the libidn misses; the fix restored profiling

title: Only Data Profiling uses the native pmdtm engine
text: In a CDGC catalog scan, Metadata Extraction, Lineage, Data Quality and Classification run in the Java scanner, the DQ engine and cloud services, while Data Profiling launches pmdtm on the agent; Data Observability depends on profiling and is skipped when profiling fails. A scan where only profiling fails points at the agent's DTM, not at the source database.
evidence: The other capabilities COMPLETED while profiling failed

title: 'DTM process terminated unexpectedly' on every profile: look for dangling plugin XML files
text: Profiling uses a Java transformation (pmjtx). When every profile run fails with 'Internal error. The DTM process terminated unexpectedly' and Data_Integration_Server/logs/s_profiling_*_import.log stops at 'Post validation on imported plug-ins... Error encountered while Parsing file', look for dangling *.xml symlinks in the rdtm plugin folders (DIS parses every XML file there): rename the dead files and restart the agent. Unchecking 'Enable CLAIRE capabilities' in the profiling-task wizard also sidestepped the same Java-transformation defect.
evidence: Import-log parse error while non-profiling mappings succeeded; the blocker was recorded as resolved on 2026-09-16

title: The native PostgreSQL connector cannot profile custom enums, json, arrays or tsvector
text: Catalog-source profiling logs 'native type system does not support the data type [`<ENUM>`]' for custom enums and 'could not identify an equality operator for type json' for plain json, and skips arrays and tsvector; jsonb profiled fine on that path. The scan can report success while those columns carry no profile.
evidence: Profiling logs, 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-26

title: Casting views recover json and enum columns, but price the work first
text: Create a read-only schema of views that cast unsupported columns to text (enum::text, json::text), add it to the catalog source's object selection, and roll back with DROP SCHEMA `<schema>` CASCADE. The object-selection change was a UI step in June 2026 (catalog-source filters can now be edited through the datasources multipart PUT, untested for this purpose). On a real corpus the views recovered only about 0.25% of columns, because most unprofiled columns sat in empty tables.
evidence: COUNT(DISTINCT) succeeded through the views (2026-06-28); about 0.25% of columns recovered (2026-07-26)

title: Profiling coverage that looks catastrophic can be complete: empty tables never profile
text: Profiling samples rows, so a table with NumberOfRows = 0 never profiles and core.profiled stays false, correctly. Compute the profiled percentage against tables that hold rows before reporting a coverage problem: in one catalog 97.9% of the unprofiled columns were in empty tables, and the ~21% headline simply tracked each source's share of non-empty tables.
evidence: Coverage analysis, 2026-07-26

title: A catalog source without the Data Profiling capability never profiles
text: A catalog source configured only with Metadata Extraction and Lineage Discovery never produces profiles, however often it is scanned. Add the Data Profiling (and Data Classification) capability to the source; one source can then run Metadata Extraction, Lineage Discovery, Data Profiling, Data Quality and Data Observability in a single run of POST `https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id>` with the capabilities listed explicitly in capabilityNames (an empty list gives a misleading 500).
evidence: A source with only two capabilities never profiled; one run produced catalog, profiling and DQ results per source (2026-06-27)

title: Running only the Data Quality capability returns 406, and failed profiling jobs expose no error over REST
text: POST `/data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id>` with {"capabilityNames":["Data Quality"]} returned 406 (not runnable on its own). A Data Profiling run that failed in 9 seconds exposed no error detail through the observable job API; only the Metadata Command Center UI showed the reason (for example '3 objects discovered, 1 profiled, 2 failed'). Was believed 2026-07-09; overturned by L-CDGC-143.
evidence: 406; empty error detail on the observable job

title: Diagnose PARTIAL_COMPLETED catalog profiling from the agent session logs, then exclude the table
text: Poll GET `https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/observable/v1/jobs/<jobId>?expandChildren=TASK-HIERARCHY` to see each capability's child tasks. If Data Profiling ends PARTIAL_COMPLETED, find the failing table in `<agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/logs/s_cp_*_session.log` (causes seen: pgvector columns, a BigQuery column named rows, transient BigQuery 503s), add a Profiling Filter Config row (Exclude, Tables, schema.table) to the source's Data Profiling capability, PUT the source back as multipart, and re-run Data Profiling only; the table stays in the catalog.
evidence: Profiling re-runs completed after the excludes

title: Measure profiling coverage with exact search facets
text: Count POST /data360/search/api/v1/search hits (header X-INFA-SEARCH-LANGUAGE: elasticsearch) with core.profiled=True for profiling coverage and core.generatedClassification for CLAIRE classification; a wrong field name returns 500, which was once misread as 'profiling is broken'. Column grain and asset grain differ (671 profiled columns versus 1,755 profiled assets in one catalog), so state the grain of each KPI.
evidence: 200 with real counts; 500 on a wrong facet

title: Classification is not profiling
text: CLAIRE classification (core.generatedClassification) infers a column's category from names and metadata, so it also covers empty tables; profiling computes statistics from rows (core.average, minValue, maxValue, distinctCount, nullPercentage, standardDeviation, patternStatistics, topNValueFrequenciesSample, inferredDataType). Expect classified counts to exceed profiled counts.
evidence: 2,582 of 3,136 columns classified versus 671 profiled in one catalog

title: Two DQ scorecards exist: build on the Data Profiling scorecard, not the CDGC BusinessDataset one
text: The CDGC Data Quality scorecard (data360; BusinessDataset + RuleOccurrence + DATA_QUALITY_SCORE) scores catalog assets and was the UI-only/404 wall. The Data Profiling scorecard on `<pod>-dqprofile` scores a profile's source, is simpler, and its design objects are exportable. Build scorecards on Data Profiling.
evidence: Inspection of a working training org, with screenshots

title: Data Profiling scorecard: rule specs with dimensions, rule occurrences on the Metrics tab, run, View Scorecard
text: Create a profile; add rule specifications on the Rules tab; on the Metrics tab (Menu > Scorecard Metrics) promote them to rule occurrences with a dimension (Accuracy, Validity, Completeness, Consistency, Uniqueness, Timeliness, or a custom Dimension value from Metadata Command Center, up to 12), thresholds (Good, Acceptable, Not Acceptable), target, measuringMethod 'InformaticaCloudDataQuality', criticality, ruleFRSId and mappletColumnId; run the profile again; View Scorecard opens the scorecard dashboard in Data Governance and Catalog. Prerequisites: passing rows output Valid, True, 1, Yes or Ok; only rule specifications can back occurrences; with several outputs the first of isValid, isTrue, out_valid, out_status, PrimaryRuleSet is used; the viewer needs the Governance User role, and DQ plus CDGC must be available on the pod. A profile's Insights tab lists CLAIRE-recommended rule specifications, each scored High, Medium or Low: use it as the starting rule list before adding rules on the Rules tab. The internal reads (profiling-service `/profile/<uuid>`, `/runDetail/<uuid>/...`, `/ruleOccurrence/...ForProfile_V2_Token/<uuid>`, metric-store `Profiles('<uuid>')/...`) take the profile's internal uuid, which differs from the repository handle in the browser URL: take it from `GET /profile?limit=200` (match on name), never from the address bar.
evidence: Training-org structure and data model confirmed, run-to-score inferred (2026-07-09); vendor Cloud Data Profiling guide (October 2025) pp.86-90; UI inspection of 36 authored profiles plus internal REST reads where the uuid differed from the URL handle (2026-07-09)

title: No REST endpoint emits a DQ scorecard: it comes from running a profile with rules
text: A scorecard is produced by running a profile that has rules attached. Rule-occurrence pass/fail renders on the Data Profiling Results tab (Rules view) without CDGC; the scorecard dashboard needs CDGC and the Governance User role. For portable artifacts use Export Profile Results (Excel); for dashboards, land the rule results in your own table.
evidence: No scorecard REST endpoint exists; the Rules view rendered without CDGC

title: CDGC catalog rule occurrences scored 1 of 6, and reading the scores was UI-only (July 2026)
text: On one dm-us org, six identically authored CDGC rule occurrences produced one score and five failures, with no UI lever to fix it; authoring occurrences and reading their scores were UI-only (scripts had to scrape the asset's Score tab). Do not loosen a gate to accept a partially completed scan (1/19 coverage) as green. Was believed 2026-07-09; overturned by L-DQ-097, L-CDGC-144.
evidence: MCC job error text; 400 and 406 probes

title: CDGC rule occurrences had no create API, and some catalog source types lack the Data Quality capability
text: The CDGC rule-occurrence object that computes a catalog DQ score could only be created in the CDGC DQ wizard (no create API found), and a catalog source type's typeCapabilities may not include Data Quality at all (in one org only PostgreSQL sources were scorable, not the warehouse source). DQ and profiling runs themselves were headless on the executable and observable routes. Was believed 2026-07-09; overturned by L-CDGC-143, L-MCP-086, L-DQ-097.
evidence: typeCapabilities inspection; no create route found

title: Seed an org that has no profiles by importing a profile package
text: An org with zero profiles has nothing to clone. Export a profile that carries rule occurrences, plus its rule specs, from an org that has them; import it into the target and retarget the source connection; re-bind the occurrences to the target's rule-spec frsIds; run it. After that, one working profile is enough to clone the rest through POST /profile.
evidence: Planned on 2026-07-09; import, re-bind and run proven on 2026-09-28 (8/8 COMPLETED)

title: Score DQ natively with a CDI mapping task that writes a scorecard table
text: A CDI mapping task that evaluates the governed DQ rules and writes a scorecard table is a genuine IDMC-native path to DQ scores: it runs on the DIS engine and shows SUCCESS in the v2 activity log, independent of CDGC rule-occurrence limits, and it matches the positioning that DQ needs CDI to run.
evidence: Activity log SUCCESS; 19 rules landed in the scorecard table

title: The warehouse scorecard pattern: dq_results per rule, dq_scorecard per dimension, a daily snapshot
text: dq_results holds one row per rule, with rule (unique), checked, failed, dimension and run_at, built as a UNION ALL of per-rule SELECTs over staging models. dq_scorecard rolls it up by dimension plus an 'overall' row: rules, checked, failed, pass_rate = round(1 - failed/greatest(checked,1), 4) and a status (green at 0.99 or above, amber at 0.90 or above, else red). Add a daily snapshot table (Write APPEND with a NOT EXISTS guard so it writes once per UTC day, using the same rule logic as dq_results), a per-entity completeness worklist, reconciliation buckets, match pairs, and a clean-only gate view that downstream activation reads. Each mart is a mapping task over the Copy Data template with its SQL in customQuery, in an hourly taskflow.
evidence: Hourly production run with 15 dimensions, 23 rules and about 560k checks (2026-09-24); SQL restructured so each business rule counts once (2026-09-27)

title: One governed rule catalog scored by two engines and reconciled by a parity harness
text: Keep one rule catalog as data, where each rule carries its violation query for every engine that scores it (for example the operational database and the warehouse). Score with both, reconcile with a parity harness (a difference is either real drift or a rule bug), publish to dashboards, alert on it, and validate against the golden-record layer. Scheduled scoring exits 0 even when the verdict is red: red is a data verdict, not a job failure.
evidence: Parity 17/19, with 2 real drifts found

title: Turn red DQ scores into steward tickets from the warehouse scorecard
text: Native CLAIRE auto-rule generation comes out of a CDGC profiling scan and is reviewed in the UI. The headless equivalent: materialize the scorecard in the warehouse (a fail count per rule), run a red-score loop that flags any rule with failures, route it to a steward by domain through a steward-queue view, and file a ticket.
evidence: Loop proven with 7/7 green rules (0 tickets filed); the steward-queue view was live

title: Compute DQ pass rates on deduplicated, test-excluded records, and count each business rule once
text: Rule checks over raw sign-up rows (including test accounts and duplicates) inflate duplicate counts and distort completeness, and a headline weighted by raw rows does not match the per-customer numbers elsewhere. Define customer checks over the unique customers and the duplicate check over the records actually merged, exclude test identities, merge rules that test the same property of the same rows (one 'address complete' rule, not four), and publish one view that both BI and CLAIRE read.
evidence: Numbers tied out after the view (2026-09-28); rules restructured so each business rule counts once (2026-09-27)

title: Gate DQ rules on activity: at small n, zero rows is NO_ACTIVITY, not BROKEN
text: A health rule that flags an expected-data table with 0 rows as BROKEN false-alarms when nothing has happened yet. Give each rule an activity driver (for example, judge reviews only when completed transactions exceed a floor) and report NO_ACTIVITY below it; tables without a gate still flag BROKEN. If the rule SQL is replicated into an IDMC mapping customQuery, keep both bodies byte-identical.
evidence: The false positive was fixed and the replica synced

title: Prove a DQ detector is falsifiable: seed a violation, watch it go RED, remove it
text: A GREEN verdict means little until the detector has been shown to go RED on a real violation. Seed a known violating record, confirm that the rule flags it and that the run exits non-zero, then remove the seed and confirm GREEN. Keep such detectors read-only.
evidence: Seeded violation turned RED with exit 1; removing it restored GREEN

title: Keep synthetic rows out of gold and golden layers, and assert zero leakage
text: Filter synthetic and test identities at the staging step of the golden layer so that it is real-only by construction, then assert in the pipeline that the count of synthetic markers is 0 in every gold and golden table, and exit non-zero on any leak.
evidence: Zero-leak assertion on both the gold and golden tables, failing loudly

title: Measure production DQ through views that exclude synthetic test rows
text: When test suites keep filling a live database with deliberately invalid fixtures, repairing the data never converges. Create a schema of views that shadow each checked table with the synthetic rows removed (test e-mail domains, prefixes, mock ids) and run the unchanged rules with SET search_path = `<dq_schema>`, public. Document any baseline-waived rules with their reason.
evidence: DQ lane green with no effective failures

title: Re-seeding test data moves which DQ rule fails
text: With production-scoped DQ, each reseed of test fixtures can introduce a new synthetic e-mail domain that trips a different identity rule. Confirm that the new domain has no real users, add it to the synthetic exclusion list symmetrically for every compared system, and expect the pattern to recur.
evidence: 0 real users on the excluded domains

title: Validate DQ rule value lists against live distinct values
text: A rule with a hard-coded allow-list can pass today and false-flag later when real values differ from the assumed vocabulary (for example vendor statuses versus the application's own enum). Compare the list against SELECT DISTINCT on the live column before trusting it.
evidence: Rule fixed before resolved records aged into false breaches

title: Flag never-populated tables from live row counts
text: Compute a data-health mart from live table row counts (for example the warehouse's own table metadata) rather than from a hard-coded list, and flag tables with zero or stale rows as dormant or broken features to troubleshoot.
evidence: A dynamic mart of about 21 curated rows

title: Never drop a row silently: a structured reject sink
text: Send every failed row to an error table with the run id, source entity, business key, a reject reason in the form 'rule id | code | offending value' (for example CQ-002 | INVALID_EMAIL_FORMAT | EMAIL='x@example.com') and the full raw record as JSON. Choose per rule between reject and flag/warn, and keep domain value lists in a reference table rather than a hard-coded IN-list.
evidence: Third-party reference design (CDC to SCD2 to star over CDI + CDQ + CDGC); not live-probed

title: A reject-rate circuit breaker, and dedup lookups so that re-runs are safe
text: If the reject rate exceeds a threshold (for example 10%), fail the quality task and abort the taskflow: a mass reject means the source contract changed. Make re-runs safe with a lookup against the fact on the natural key followed by a filter ISNULL(LKP_SK); without it, re-processing a file doubles the facts.
evidence: Third-party reference design; not live-probed

title: A match rule on surname plus street number pairs different people
text: A fuzzy match rule keyed on surname + street number merged people with different first names and e-mails at 100% confidence. Tighten it (add the e-mail domain or phone) or present it deliberately as a household match, and decide before showing match-and-merge results.
evidence: Merged pairs listed on a review dashboard

title: Make cleansing visible in a demo: generate realistically messy inputs within the API contract
text: If synthetic traffic arrives already clean, before/after cleansing views show no difference. Make most generated inputs messy in realistic ways (ALL CAPS or lowercase names, extra spaces, bracketed or dotted phone formats, mixed-case e-mail) while staying inside the input validator, keep a share clean, and put the rate behind a knob.
evidence: Offline simulation: 69.2% messy, 100% passing the validator

title: Call the managed Data Quality agent: Bearer JWT plus IDS-SESSION-ID, a nested tools/call, poll for updates
text: The endpoint is `https://mcp.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/mcp-servers/public/dataqualityagent`. Send Authorization: Bearer `<jwt>` (an identity-service JWT minted with client_id=idmc_api) plus IDS-SESSION-ID and MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18, or use an OAuth client token. tools/call uses a doubly nested envelope (the arguments are a full inner JSON-RPC tools/call), and results are asynchronous: poll get_skill_execution_updates {conversation_id, message_id, cursor, events, reasoning} until pagination.has_more is false. The tools are data_profiling, data_quality_analysis, data_quality_rule_recommendation, data_quality_rule_generation, data_quality_cleansing, request_upload_url and get_skill_execution_updates.
evidence: Login 200, JWT minted, all five DQ skills reachable

title: The DQ agent's profiling, analysis and rule skills need a CDGC-cataloged asset
text: data_profiling, data_quality_analysis and data_quality_rule_recommendation (and rule generation on table assets) work only on CDGC-cataloged assets keyed by the catalog asset id (a pivot UUID, passed as external_id). On a raw connection or an uncataloged table they return STATUS SUCCESS with an empty END_OF_ANSWER, ask for the asset id, return an ARTIFACT error, or fail at the summarize step ('An error occurred while processing data profile request'). Catalog the source first, or use the file-based data_quality_cleansing; the classic Data Profiling service needs no catalog at all. The hosted agent cannot reach a private database directly.
evidence: Repeated empty END_OF_ANSWER answers and summarize errors, 2026-09-12 to 2026-09-24

title: File-based profiling and cleansing works headless through data_quality_cleansing with an HTTP/1.1 upload
text: Call request_upload_url {filename, size_bytes, content_type, description, display_name} to get a single-use presigned PUT url, its required_headers and a conversation_id, then upload with curl --http1.1 -H "Expect:" --data-binary `@<file>`. With HTTP/2 or an Expect: 100-continue preflight, the preflight consumes the single-use URL and the body PUT gets 409; there is also a transient 409 race on a fresh URL, so wait about a second, use a unique filename each time and mint a new URL on each 409 (7 x 409 then 201 was seen). Then call data_quality_cleansing with {prompt, name, `artifacts:[<file>`], conversation_id}. csv, xlsx and parquet are accepted, and no catalog is needed.
evidence: STATUS SUCCESS with a server-side profile on several datasets

title: Two calls make CLAIRE generate a cleansing transform: prescriptive first, 'Yes, proceed now' second
text: Call 1 is a prescriptive data_quality_cleansing prompt that names each fix you want (CLAIRE captures this usage context and proposes rules). Call 2 is 'Yes, proceed now. Using the usage context you captured, generate the actual cleansing ...' sent with only {prompt, conversation_id} and no artifacts. A generic 'analyze/profile' first call plus re-sent artifacts gave an empty second call (profile only).
evidence: Empty second call with the generic prompt; a full transform with the prescriptive pair

title: CLAIRE prompts reject angle brackets: send plain ASCII prose
text: The DQ agent's prompt validation rejects '<' and '>' with JSON-RPC -32602 'Angle brackets ... prohibited', so '->' arrows fail; some shims also reject non-ASCII characters and HTML. Write prompts in plain ASCII prose.
evidence: -32602 error

title: Apply CLAIRE's generated cleansing code with a small generic harness
text: The follow-up answer carries a Python transformation in the IDMC Python-transformation dialect, JSON-escaped under a 'Script' key: Pre-Partition definitions, Main per-row code, Post-Partition DataFrame rules, and an Output block ending in generateRow(). Extract the longest Script value, ast.parse it, and split it at '# Main Python Code', '# Post-Partition' and '# Output Code'. Run Pre once, bind each input column as the same-named variable ('' becomes None) and run Main per row, then run Post and write the *_out columns as the cleansed file and the rows with a rule_name as the rule-hit report. 'Testing got failed' progress lines are self-correction attempts. Treat the code as untrusted: review it and run it isolated.
evidence: Unmodified CLAIRE code executed on 3 datasets (45 to 43 rows with 33 cleansed; 439 of 2,000; 595 to 594)

title: CLAIRE profile statistics cover the whole upload; 'Rows: 500' is only the preview
text: valueCount in the file-based profile equals the full upload size; the 'Rows: 500' line is the data-preview size, not the sample that the statistics were computed on.
evidence: valueCount matched the uploaded row counts

title: The DQ agent stalls after the preview on an all-empty column: drop it
text: A profiling or cleansing run that stops after the preview (PARTIAL) often has a 100% empty column. Drop all-null columns from the upload, report their null rate from the database instead, and run again. Run datasets one at a time; that also cleared transient upload 409s.
evidence: PARTIAL became SUCCESS after dropping a 99.99%-null column

title: Check CLAIRE's generated rules against its own findings before applying them
text: Generated code can contradict CLAIRE's issue catalog (for example zero-padding a value it classed not_fixable), passes not_fixable values through for stewardship, and its ingest can coerce numeric-looking strings such as ZIP codes and phone numbers to floats. STATUS SUCCESS can arrive after all five internal self-test attempts failed, and representation changes (a removed thousands separator) can go unflagged by its violation mask. Validate the script, and review each rule against the data and the issue list.
evidence: Rule-hit report review; a call-2 log with 5/5 failed self-tests and STATUS SUCCESS

title: DQ agent rule generation drafts rules but does not save or run them
text: data_quality_rule_generation extracts and plans rules and then stops: nothing is saved as a console asset, bound or executed, so no scorecard or pass rate appears, and no MCP verb saves a DQ console asset. Put executable DQ logic in a rule specification (UI or package clone) bound to a profile or mapping, and surface results from its output. One run reported rules persisted to a CLAIRE workspace; that is unreconciled.
evidence: No asset created after the runs

title: Rule recommendation through MCP pauses on a HUMAN_PROBE and needs a current asset id
text: The data_quality_rule_recommendation flow returns a HUMAN_PROBE item that must be answered ('yes', with the same skill and conversation_id, then poll again) before it returns rules; a run on a cataloged Postgres table returned 10 recommended rules, 4 of which matched already-published rules. Catalog asset ids can change after rescans or renames, so resolve the asset id again before each run.
evidence: 10 rules returned after the probe was answered

title: Uploading data to the hosted DQ agent is egress: sample it, go one dataset at a time, log it
text: File-based CLAIRE profiling sends the file to Informatica's cloud. Use small synthetic or sampled data with no real PII, one dataset at a time, and keep an egress ledger (dataset, rows, bytes, retries included). The local apply step has zero egress. Newer evidence: L-DQ-157.
evidence: An egress ledger was kept (about 1.6 MB of samples in one project)

title: A stale conversation_id fails with 'No conversation found'; reuse the upload's conversation
text: Passing an unknown or expired conversation_id to a DQ agent skill returns 'No conversation found for the provided conversation id. Please pass a valid conversation id or omit it to create a new conversation.' Omit it to start fresh. After request_upload_url, run the first cleansing call in the conversation_id that the upload mint returned.
evidence: Error text captured (2026-09-03); the upload-then-cleanse flow (2026-09-21)

title: Native CDQ rule authoring is UI-only
text: Believed from POST /public/core/v3/objects returning 405 and 404s on /data360/dq/*, so automated test lanes could only run headless checks around IDMC DQ. Overturned by the migration clone of a template rule spec; only new rule logic still needs the rulebuilder canvas. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-07; overturned by L-DQ-010.
evidence: 405 and 404 probes

title: CDQ has no REST write path at all
text: A rule-authoring finding was generalized to the whole service. The documented Dictionary API (with create proven live) overturned it; rule logic and scorecards remain outside the public CDQ API. Was believed until 2026-07-25; overturned by L-DQ-006.
evidence: Early belief

title: Data Profiling has no API; it only rides a catalog scan
text: Believed from the absence of a local guide. Live reads on `<pod>-dqprofile` (2026-07-25/26), the vendor's documented CRUD and the later create/execute proof (2026-09-24) overturned it; 'documented, paths not held' was the honest answer for query CRUD. Was believed until 2026-07-25; overturned by L-DQ-019.
evidence: Early belief

title: Data Profiling routes are SPA-session only
text: The routes were recorded as internal single-page-app routes needing the web app's injected IDS-SESSION-ID, with a plain INFA-SESSION-ID GET returning the identity HTML shell. IDS-SESSION-ID carrying a login session (the v3 session on some pods) works for create, update and execute. Was believed 2026-07-09 to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-DQ-020.
evidence: Network capture and HTML answers (July 2026)

title: Profile execution has no public REST verb
text: Concluded from POST /api/v2/job returning 403 UI_13404 and 404s on guessed dqprofile run paths; POST `/profiling-service/api/v1/profile/<id>/execute` ran 8/8 profiles to COMPLETED on 2026-09-24 and again on 2026-09-28. Was believed 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-21; overturned by L-DQ-019.

title: Binding rules to a profile (rule occurrences) is UI-only
text: A runbook listed rule-to-profile binding and the profile run as UI- or Playwright-only; both were done over REST on 2026-09-24 (MAPPLETFIELD entries in PUT `/profile/<id>`, then execute). Dimensions still come from the rule spec. Was believed 2026-09-13; overturned by L-DQ-023.
evidence: Runbook assertion

title: Profile authoring is UI-only (POST /v3/objects = 405)
text: The 405 on the v3 objects collection was read as 'profiles cannot be authored headless'; profiles travel in v3 packages (2026-09-28) and are created with POST /profile from a template body (2026-09-24). Was believed 2026-09-20; overturned by L-DQ-025.

title: The DQ agent upload PUT fails with a permanent 409 (a per-user preview cap)
text: The 409 survived a fresh JWT, a 15-minute wait and files under 1 MB, and was blamed on an upload cap. It was the HTTP/2 or Expect: 100-continue preflight consuming the single-use URL, fixed with curl --http1.1 -H "Expect:", unique filenames and re-minting. Was believed 2026-09-04; overturned by L-DQ-072.
evidence: Persistent 409s

title: Empty profiling was a stuck-job 406 lock, readyToRun=false or ccgf-auth-pep 500 errors
text: Several days of zero profiled columns were attributed to job locks, runtime-environment flags and auth errors; none explained why every source failed identically. The missing libidn.so.11 (pmdtm exit 127) did. Was believed June 2026 (to 2026-06-28); overturned by L-DQ-037.
evidence: Competing explanations

title: Low profiling coverage (~17%) is caused by the connector skipping json/enum/array; casting views take it to ~100%
text: Coverage of about 17% was attributed to the native PostgreSQL connector skipping json, enum and array columns, and casting views were expected to lift it toward 100%. Later analysis showed that 97.9% of the unprofiled columns sat in empty tables and that the views recovered only about 0.25%. Was believed 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-09; overturned by L-DQ-042.
evidence: Coverage counts (July 2026)

title: CDGC catalog scans and profiling are UI-initiated; there is no REST trigger
text: Recorded from 404s on guessed /data360/scan/*, /profile/* and /job/* routes. The scan trigger is POST `https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id>` with explicit capabilityNames, used in June 2026 and proven again on 2026-09-24, and polled on the observable jobs route. Was believed 2026-07-05; overturned by L-DQ-043.
evidence: 404 probes on guessed routes

title: Reach a firewalled agent VM through a cloud IAP jump host
text: When direct SSH to the agent VM is blocked (source-IP allowlists, rotating egress), hop through a jump VM: `gcloud compute ssh <jump-vm> --zone <zone> --tunnel-through-iap --account=<user> --command "ssh -i <key-file> <user>@<vm-ip> 'sudo bash -s'"`, with the script base64-encoded inline. Move large files with `gcloud compute scp` to the jump host first, then `scp` them on. Pin `--account` (or `CLOUDSDK_CORE_ACCOUNT`) on every call: a peer session can switch the global gcloud account, and the hop then lands as a user without the key (`Permission denied (publickey)`).
evidence: Used by several lanes when direct SSH and the cloud run-command channel were blocked or jammed

title: Never pipe stdin through gcloud compute ssh on Windows
text: On Windows, `gcloud compute ssh` shells out to plink.exe rather than OpenSSH, and piping a script on stdin through it injects a stray "y" (the host-key prompt answer) into the stream. Copy the script with `gcloud compute scp` or inline it base64-encoded in `--command`, then run it. IAP tunnels from Windows are also slow, so run long ones in the background.
evidence: Repeated observations on a Windows workstation

title: Azure run-command invoke: root, a per-VM singleton and a 4 KB output tail
text: `python -m azure.cli vm run-command invoke -g <rg> -n <vm> --command-id RunShellScript --scripts @file.sh --query "value[0].message" -o tsv` runs as root through the Azure control plane, needs no SSH key and is the break-glass path when SSH times out. It is a per-VM singleton: concurrent sessions get `Conflict: Run command extension execution is in progress`, sometimes for more than 5 minutes (retry with 25-60 s backoff). Output keeps only the last ~4 KB, so print small filtered results and write big dumps to a file on the VM to read back in chunks. `HOME` is `/root`, so `~` paths resolve wrong (use `sudo -u <user>` or set `HOME=/home/<user>`). Pass scripts as `--scripts @file` (inline multi-line scripts get mangled and a Windows command line caps at 32 KB); output arrives as `[stdout]...[stderr]...` inside `value[0].message`.
evidence: Conflicts and truncated output seen repeatedly across a week of shared use

title: Managed run-commands run beside a jammed singleton, but are capped and may be undeletable
text: `vm run-command create -g <rg> --vm-name <vm> --name <n> --script "..."` creates a named child resource that does not share the invoke singleton; read its output with `vm run-command show -g <rg> --vm-name <vm> --run-command-name <n> --instance-view --query instanceView.output -o tsv` (create returns no output, so fold create and show into one call). Output is tail-capped at ~4 KB and front-truncates, so a big base64 blob loses its head (chunk with `split -b 3000`, or use `--output-blob-uri`).
