Managed run-commands are capped at 25 per VM, and a `CanNotDelete` resource lock stops them from being deleted (`ScopeLocked`), so the slots eventually fill; then fall back to invoke. `docker exec -i <container> python manage.py shell < /tmp/x.py` works through a managed run-command.
evidence: Managed run-commands ran while invoke stayed locked; all 25 slots were full on a locked VM

title: A process started through run-command dies on reboot: use systemd
text: A process launched with Azure run-command lives in the run-command extension's transient cgroup (a `...RunCommandLinux.slice` scope), not under systemd: nothing supervises it, it is exposed to the extension's lifecycle, and it does not survive a reboot. Start the Secure Agent and any daemon through its systemd unit and check the cgroup (`/system.slice/<unit>.service`) after starting.
evidence: An agent ran in the extension scope for hours until moved under its systemd unit (cgroup inspection)

title: Launch long remote jobs detached and poll a log
text: Write the whole sequence to a script, ship it on its own, start it with `setsid` (or `nohup ... </dev/null > log 2>&1 &`) so it survives SSH and IAP drops, then poll the log for a done marker with short, independent calls. Do not ship and background in the same remote command (the pipe wrote 0 bytes). An orchestrator finalizes only on an explicit DONE sentinel, confirmed process death or a wall-clock limit, never on the end of an SSH output stream, and marks unrun lanes as not evaluated rather than failed. Newer evidence: L-METHOD-148.
evidence: Clean-slate redeploys completed despite SSH drops; 0 gap-filled lanes after the orchestrator fix

title: Move code to a VM as base64, never through heredocs, scp or remote editors
text: Heredocs, scp, terminal editors and inline run-command scripts mangle backslashes and strip quotes in regexes and nested f-strings. Write the file locally, base64-encode it, send the text, decode it on the VM (`base64 -d > file` or python3) and verify with a checksum or `od -c` before running it. Avoid inline f-strings with nested quotes in commands shipped over SSH.
evidence: Scripts ran unmodified after base64 transfer; SyntaxErrors before

title: Human cloud logins lapse; keep service-account paths for headless work
text: A human gcloud token can hit a reauthentication window ("Reauthentication failed, cannot prompt") that no background session can refresh, and a warehouse-only service account cannot SSH; a service account that holds IAP-tunnel and SSH rights on the jump VM can (`gcloud compute scp|ssh <jump-vm> --account=<service-account> --tunnel-through-iap`, the account pinned on every call, L-ENV-009), and it ran dozens of remote runs while the human login was lapsed (the exact roles were not recorded). Check the human login with a timeout (`timeout 15 gcloud auth print-access-token`) instead of hanging; for warehouse work use a service-account key stored on a VM inside a throwaway container that mounts it read-only; plain SSH with an already-registered OS Login key kept working while the gcloud user token was lapsed. Management-plane actions (snapshots, instance resets) still need the human login. Hop pattern that held: tar the script and its files locally, `gcloud compute scp` the tarball plus a small hop script to the jump VM (up to 4 tries 10 s apart), run `gcloud compute ssh <jump-vm> ... --command 'bash /tmp/<hop>.sh' </dev/null`, and let the hop script copy on to the target VM with plain `scp`/`ssh` (`-o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=20`), run and clean up; filter gcloud's banner lines out of the output.
evidence: Queries across 29 datasets ran through the service-account path while the human login was lapsed; dozens of remote runs through a service-account IAP hop while the human login was lapsed (2026-09-29 to 2026-10-01)

title: gcloud's active account is global state: pin the account on every call
text: `gcloud auth activate-service-account` makes the service account the active account for every later command on the machine, so SSH and IAP commands that need the human account fail until `gcloud config set account <human>` is run again, and scheduled jobs that self-heal by activating a service account silently flip it for everyone. Pin `--account=<user>` or `CLOUDSDK_CORE_ACCOUNT` per call instead of relying on the global setting.
evidence: SSH failed after a service-account activation until the account was reset; a peer's switch broke an IAP hop

title: Run warehouse and database reads where the key and the client already live
text: If the host lacks the warehouse client or the key, run the script inside a container that has both: `sudo docker exec -i <container> python -` with the script on stdin. For a private PostgreSQL reachable only from one VM, use the database or app container so the password never leaves it: `sudo docker exec -i <pg-container> sh -c 'PGPASSWORD=$POSTGRES_PASSWORD psql -U <user> -d <db> -f -'`, feeding SQL through a quoted heredoc (`<<'EOSQL'`) so `$` and backslashes survive. Strip a SQLAlchemy driver suffix (`postgresql+psycopg://`) before handing a `DATABASE_URL` to psql, and cast JSON columns to `::text` before `count(distinct ...)`.
evidence: Reads confirmed through a controller container and a database container

title: Corporate egress rotates, so IP-pinned firewall rules go stale
text: Outbound traffic can leave through a proxy pool whose address changes mid-session (different /24s). Symptoms: SSH and admin ports that worked minutes ago time out while the public app still returns 200, and a rule you just added seems to do nothing. Sample egress per destination (an echo service may be on a bypass list), confirm ownership with RDAP (`https://rdap.arin.net/registry/ip/<ip>`), and prefer a jump host, a tailnet or a control-plane channel over allowlisting a shared proxy range (a /24 is a compromise worth flagging). If you do widen a rule, add whole ranges additively, and relaunch subagents after the fix rather than resuming them, because their cached results are the failed ones. ICMP is often blocked, so ping loss does not mean down.
evidence: Egress rotated mid-session during an agent install and throughout a week of VM work

title: Reachability is not authentication: know which one failed
text: An `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_...` banner means the port is open; `Permission denied (publickey)` means the port was never the problem; a timeout means network or firewall. `ssh -v` lists "Authentications that can continue": if it says only `publickey`, no pasted password helps. A provider's web console connects from the provider's infrastructure, so narrowing port 22 to user IPs silently breaks it (`Timed out while waiting for handshake`); keep it reachable before narrowing. Account-level SSH keys at a provider apply only to newly created instances. A long key pasted into a terminal can wrap and write a broken `authorized_keys` line that sshd silently ignores: split it into two shell variables, rejoin with `printf`, keep the directory 700 and the file 600, and verify with `ssh-keygen -lf`.
evidence: Environment-trap rules recorded during an agent install

title: Verify the fix and your own access; trust the provider API over its CLI
text: After changing a firewall, a unit file or a permission, re-test the thing that was broken and the access you rely on; confirm a firewall actually filters by probing a port you did not allow; close anything opened temporarily in the same session. A CLI can hold its own stale stored credential and return `401 Unable to authenticate you` while the token you were given is valid: test the token against the provider's REST API before believing the CLI. Some clouds have no remote-exec API at all (console, exec and run routes 404; user data immutable, 405), so plan SSH or the provider's web console for an agent install.
evidence: Environment-trap and bootstrap rules

title: False 'site down' readings from DNS, SNI and TLS
text: A sandbox or corporate VPN that blocks outbound DNS (port 53) makes healthy hosts look down: pin the address with `curl --resolve <host>:443:<ip> https://<host>/`, use DNS-over-HTTPS, or check from the host itself. A reverse proxy with SNI virtual hosts and no catch-all answers an IP-only probe with an immediate TLS internal_error, and `curl -k https://localhost/...` can return 000 for the same reason (test with the right Host header from inside the proxy container). A zone wildcard record pointing at another server swallows a new subdomain until it gets its own explicit record. Allow about 10 s for slow root pages. Address translation adds two more false readings. No hairpin: a VM, or a container on it, that calls its own public IP or hostname can fail because the cloud does not route that traffic back to the same VM; a server-side OIDC token exchange through the public identity-provider URL failed while browsers worked, so use the internal service URL for back-channel calls, keep the public issuer for browsers and accept both issuers, and give a Secure Agent connection to a database on the same host localhost or the Docker network alias, never the public name. Docker SNAT: with `userland-proxy`, requests to the public IP from the host itself arrive with the bridge gateway as their source, so a reverse-proxy source-IP allowlist answers 403 in local tests while real clients keep their own IP: test allowlists from a genuinely external client.
evidence: False 'down' readings corrected with --resolve and Host-header probes; a back-channel token exchange failed through the public address and passed on the internal URL, and proxy logs showed the bridge gateway as the source of local calls (2026-09-09)

title: Bursts of cloud management calls from a proxied laptop get reset
text: Management-plane PATCH calls sent in tight bursts from behind an enterprise proxy were intermittently reset, while isolated calls with retries succeeded. Space bulk management calls out and retry each one.
evidence: Intermittent resets during a tagging pass

title: git-bash swallows az: call python -m azure.cli
text: Under git-bash the `az.cmd` wrapper can lose its stdout handle: `-o json` output and file redirects come back empty (0 bytes) with exit code 0, so a failed create looks successful. Call the CLI as a module (`python -m azure.cli <args>`), set `AZURE_CORE_USE_PAGER=false` and `PYTHONUTF8=1`, never treat an empty result as "no data", and read the resource back after creating it. Do not write az JSON to a POSIX temp path and read it with Windows Python; parse stdin instead. Newer evidence: L-ENV-127.
evidence: A VM create 'succeeded' while only an empty resource group existed; the module form showed the real error

title: MSYS path conversion rewrites leading-slash arguments
text: git-bash converts arguments that look like POSIX paths into Windows paths: `/api/v2/connection` passed to a helper script, or `/subscriptions/...` passed to `--ids`, arrives mangled. Export `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` only for the IDMC REST helpers that take path arguments; never set it globally, because it breaks the az launcher and the gcloud/bq wrapper scripts. For az, use the `-g` / `-n` forms instead of `--ids`.
evidence: Mangled REST paths fixed after the export; the az launcher broke with the variable set globally

title: Scripts that shell out to bash wrappers can false-RED under git-bash
text: A Python gate that calls `bash <wrapper>.sh` from git-bash can have its `/c/...` drive paths rewritten into bogus Windows paths, so the wrapper fails and the gate reports RED while the data is fine. Run such gates from cmd or PowerShell, or call the tool directly without a shell wrapper.
evidence: The same gate went green from PowerShell

title: git-bash mangles brace JMESPath queries and cmd builtins
text: git-bash brace-expands `az ... --query '{a:b}'`, which gives "invalid jmespath_type" errors: use `-o tsv` with a brace-free query (`--query 'value[0].message'`), `-o table`, or omit `--query` (`-o none`). Calling cmd builtins such as `cmd //c "mklink /J ..."` from git-bash can fail with "The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect" even with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`: write the command into a `.bat` file and run that (directory junctions need no elevation).
evidence: The .bat approach succeeded where direct calls failed

title: %VAR% does not expand in bash
text: Writing to `%LOCALAPPDATA%/...` from bash created a folder literally named `%LOCALAPPDATA%` inside the working tree, and a plaintext cloud key landed in it. Use `$LOCALAPPDATA` (or `cygpath`) or an absolute path, and after such a mistake search for stray literal folders and key files.
evidence: A stray literal folder holding a key was found during a cleanup and quarantined for rotation

title: Windows MAX_PATH makes deep paths look missing
text: Paths longer than the Windows MAX_PATH limit (260 characters) make `os.path.exists()` return false negatives. Use the `\\?\` extended-length prefix, or `cd` into the directory and work with short relative names.
evidence: False negatives on deeply nested folders

title: Windows Cloud SDK traps: spaces in the SDK path, pscp, console encoding
text: Stock `gcloud` and `bq` launchers break when the Cloud SDK path contains a space: wrap them to call the SDK's bundled Python directly (`<sdk>/platform/bundledpython/python.exe <sdk>/bin/bootstrapping/bq.py`, `<sdk>/lib/gcloud.py`) with `CLOUDSDK_ROOT_DIR` exported. `gcloud compute scp --recurse` (pscp) can fail on local paths with spaces: copy files one by one. The Windows console's cp1252 encoding breaks Python writers on emoji and other non-ASCII text: set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` (and `PYTHONUTF8=1`), and pass payloads through files rather than heredocs, where apostrophes also break. Minimal VM images can lack `python3-venv`.
evidence: The wrappers worked; per-file copy succeeded; writer failures reproduced and fixed

title: The agent shell mangles backslashes in heredocs, sed and inline Python
text: Code passed through shell heredocs, sed or `python -` strings lost its backslash escapes: `\b` in a regex became a literal backspace byte (0x08), `\p` and `\s` disappeared, and a `replace()` meant to escape newlines became a byte-for-byte no-op. Write regex-bearing files with the file-editing tools, use forward slashes in paths, quote heredocs (`<<'EOF'`) so `$` and backslashes reach the remote shell unchanged, and scan for control characters (`grep -P '\x08'`) before deploying. Windows-authored scripts break on Linux hosts in three more ways: Python `open(p, 'w')` on Windows writes CRLF, so a shell script written that way fails on the agent host with `$'\r': command not found` (write with `newline='\n'`, or `newline=''` to keep the source's endings, keep the live file's newline style when patching, and check with `bash -n` before deploying); Git Bash `grep -c $'\r'` miscounts carriage returns (count them on the bytes in Python); and a write to a file with the Windows Hidden attribute fails or drops the attribute (`attrib -h` first, `+h` after). Inside quoted heredocs the shell still turned `\\` into `\`: write scripts with the file tools and use `chr(92)` where a script must emit a backslash.
evidence: A 0x08 byte found in an expression about to be deployed; an od -c dump showed the no-op replace; a deployed shell script failed on CRLF and was fixed with newline='\n' and bash -n, and a rewritten config file lost its hidden attribute (2026-10-01 to 2026-10-03)

title: Workflow scripts must be ASCII, and ${VAR} inside an agent prompt is interpolated
text: Files passed as a workflow `scriptPath` are read with a legacy encoding, so non-ASCII characters break them: keep them ASCII. Workflow scripts are JavaScript, so a literal `${VAR}` or a stray backtick inside an agent prompt template is evaluated as interpolation (`ReferenceError: VAR is not defined`): escape it as `\${VAR}` or reword.
evidence: Failures on a non-ASCII script and on an unescaped template variable

title: Run automation from a private scratch directory
text: Other sessions writing scripts into a shared folder such as `%TEMP%` can leave files like `inspect.py` that shadow standard-library modules and break imports (Playwright stopped importing). Run automation from a private scratch directory.
evidence: The import broke until the stray file was avoided

title: Always sudo docker when the login user is not in the docker group
text: Non-sudo `docker ps` or `docker info` from a user outside the docker group silently returns 0 containers and an empty DockerRootDir, which looks exactly like "the stack is down". Check container state with `sudo docker ...` only.
evidence: A false '0 containers' reading mid-incident; sudo showed 26 of 29 containers up

title: Bind mounts are resolved at container start: recreate after fixing a mounted file
text: If a container mounts a credential or config file that was missing or wrong at start, fixing the file on the host does not reach the running container: run `docker compose up -d --force-recreate <service>` (a plain `docker restart` does not reload `env_file` either) and check the logs. When the mount source does not exist, Docker creates an empty directory in its place, the container still shows Up (healthy), and the app fails with `[Errno 21] Is a directory`; recreate every container that mounts it, not only the first one.
evidence: A pipeline was dead for 38 hours behind healthy containers; two sibling containers kept failing until also recreated

title: Write bind-mounted files in place so the container sees the change
text: Replacing a file (write a temp file and rename it, or delete and recreate) gives it a new inode, and a container that bind-mounts that single file keeps the old inode and never sees the change. For bind-mounted configs and env files open the file `r+`, `seek(0)`, write, `truncate()` (or pipe through `sudo tee` when permissions require). If a mounted directory is replaced on the host, the container keeps serving the old one until it is restarted.
evidence: A reverse-proxy config change that never took effect; every later flip used in-place writes

title: Baked versus mounted: what goes live when
text: Files copied into an image (`COPY` in the Dockerfile) go live only after that service is rebuilt; bind-mounted files change immediately; services behind compose profiles are built only with `--profile`, otherwise `run` uses a stale image; build contexts cache aggressively, so use `build --no-cache <svc>` when source changed. Fixes made in a running container's writable layer survive a restart but not a rebuild or force-recreate: put them in the repository or image and record the commit. Mapping and taskflow definition files baked into an image are read from the image layer, so a volume mount over them does not take effect.
evidence: Stale images and unchanged pages until rebuilt; fixes lost after rebuilds

title: Cloud default usernames in mount and key paths break portability
text: Absolute host paths such as `/home/<cloud-default-user>/<key>.json` in compose volume mounts work on one cloud (the default admin user differs: Azure images use one name, EC2 uses `ec2-user` or `ubuntu`, GCP derives it from the account) and break on another: the path does not exist, Docker creates an empty directory, the container starts and jobs fail. Use compose-project-relative paths (`./config/key.json`), Docker secrets or a secret manager, and audit every volume source (`docker compose config`) before moving a stack across clouds.
evidence: A stack moved between clouds failed silently on a cloud-specific key path

title: A containerized Secure Agent registers under the container hostname
text: When the Secure Agent runs in a container, it registers in the org under the container's hostname; without `hostname: <agent-name>` in the compose file, the container id becomes the agent name. Agents running as native OS processes do not appear in `docker ps`: inventory hosts by the agent directory and by Java processes such as `Data_Integration_Server` or `Metadata_Platform_Service`. Agent state kept in Docker named volumes exists only in OS-disk snapshots, not in file-level backups, so snapshot or extract it before deleting a VM or the agent is silently de-registered.
evidence: A 27 GB agent volume existed only in an OS-disk snapshot; an undocumented agent was found by process inventory

title: Make Docker wait for its data disk, which also makes a hard reset safe
text: If Docker's data-root is on a separate mount, add a systemd drop-in with `RequiresMountsFor=<mount>` to `docker.service`; enabling docker alone raced the mount and the stack did not start after a reboot. With the drop-in, `gcloud compute instances reset <vm>` is a safe recovery when a VM is IO-saturated and sshd no longer returns its banner (the reset needs an operator cloud login, not the VM's service account). Newer evidence: L-ENV-101.
evidence: A reboot outage fixed on four VMs; a banner-dead VM recovered by reset

title: Services keep their old environment until restarted through their launcher
text: A daemon that launches a configurable program via an env var keeps its old environment when the file or the variable changes, which can make every request fail instantly ("unrecognized arguments"): restart it through its launcher and verify with one real run. Never restart a service that tails and finalizes runs while a run is active.
evidence: Runs completed after a launcher restart

title: The dbt image's entrypoint always runs dbt build
text: The official dbt Docker image's ENTRYPOINT runs `dbt build`, so a "compile" through the default entrypoint silently rebuilds live models. Override it (`docker run --entrypoint dbt <image> compile ...`) when harvesting compiled SQL, for example as a mapping spec.
evidence: Live tables rebuilt by an intended compile-only run

title: In server scripts use absolute paths after cd, and back files up before writing
text: A shell script on a server that changed directory and then wrote to a relative path truncated a live compose file. Use absolute paths for every write, back the file up first, and check it afterwards.
evidence: The compose file was restored from its backup

title: Exit codes and redirects that hide failures
text: Piping a test runner through `tail` makes the pipeline's exit status tail's (0): capture the runner's own exit code. `sudo cmd > /root-owned/log` runs the redirect as the caller, so every cron fire fails with Permission denied (use `sudo sh -c 'cmd > log 2>&1'` and prove the fix with one autonomous fire). `exec > >(tee /var/log/x)` without write permission fails quietly and can mask later failures. A hard-coded shared `/tmp` path created root-owned by one cron breaks later non-root runs: use per-UID temp dirs (`/tmp/<name>.$(id -u)`) with a writability check. Backgrounded Python writes nothing to its log until exit unless run with `python -u`. Use `grep -F` for literal dotted keys. Newer evidence: L-ENV-115.
evidence: A gate reported rc=0 over 53 collection errors; a watchdog cron failed silently until the redirect moved inside sudo

title: Bound long jobs and HTTP calls with hard deadlines
text: A sync or ingest script run by cron can hang (a stuck connection or lock) and silently block every downstream refresh for hours: wrap it in `timeout <n>` plus a lock that expires, emit a heartbeat and alert on a stale one. Python `urlopen(timeout=...)` bounds the connect and each socket read, not the whole transfer: wrap request plus read in a watchdog with a hard deadline and retry only no-response results. An endpoint sweep that reads every body hangs on server-sent-event streams: skip stream paths as well as stream content types.
evidence: A 12-hour silent stall; a sweep finished in 119 s instead of hanging

title: After a rename, a backup can keep 'succeeding' with a tiny dump
text: A backup script that targets a container or directory by its old name kept exiting OK after a rename while dumping nothing (a 20-byte dump, a 192-byte tar of a symlink). Monitor backup size against a floor, update backup targets as part of every rename, and take a manual dump before risky work. Newer evidence: L-ENV-113.
evidence: A 20-byte nightly dump reported OK

title: Read big cloud-storage objects with bounded byte ranges only
text: Spot-check large archive objects with a bounded range read (`gsutil cat -r 0-5242879 gs://<bucket>/<object>`). Never stream with `gcloud storage cp <object> - | head -c N`: gcloud retry-loops on the broken pipe and re-downloads the whole object; on a 143 GB object this IO-saturated the VM until sshd stopped returning its banner and the host needed a reset.
evidence: A VM reset was required to clear the IO saturation

title: A read-only host watcher when two Secure Agents share one VM
text: Log one line a minute: MemAvailable, free swap, load, free disk on the data volume, each agent unit's memory and active state, each agent user's summed RSS and Java process count, the ports the second agent listens on with a clash check against the first agent's critical ports (7080, 7443, 8443, 7005, 14479, 5432), app container health, and each agent's service-status line and recent ERROR count. Stop it after a few hours. It shows capacity trouble before jobs fail.
evidence: The watcher log was kept through a cutover

title: BigQuery CLI defaults, spend caps and schema propagation
text: `bq query` returns 100 rows by default and silently truncates client-side joins and counts: pass `--max_rows=100000` or aggregate in SQL. Cap automated spend with `maximum_bytes_billed=<bytes>` under the query section of `.bigqueryrc` (test with one oversized and one normal query). Right after replacing a table's schema, a dependent statement can fail with "Unrecognized name: <new column>": sleep briefly (about 15 s) and retry once. Probe an estate read-only: `bq show <project>:<dataset>` answers 'Not found' (404) when a dataset does not exist and 'Access Denied' (403) when it exists but you cannot read it (calibrate with a made-up name first); `POST https://cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<project>:testIamPermissions` with the permissions you care about returns the granted subset, for the operator account and, from the VM through the metadata-server token, for the VM's attached service account; metadata reads (`__TABLES__`, datasets.list and get) bill 0 bytes. The project quota `QueryUsagePerDay` defaults to 200 TiB a day and per-user usage is unlimited, so there is no effective cap: set `maximum_bytes_billed` on every automated job and a default table expiration on sample datasets (a custom daily quota needs `serviceusage.quotas.update`).
evidence: Counts changed after adding --max_rows; a 12 GB scan was rejected by the cap; 404 versus 403 probes, testIamPermissions for two identities and the default QueryUsagePerDay read through the Service Usage API in one project (2026-10-03)

title: Query a Microsoft Fabric warehouse directly for verification
text: Get a service-principal token from `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token` with scope `https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/.default`, and connect with pyodbc and ODBC Driver 18 (server `<workspace>.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com`, the token passed as the access-token connection attribute, `Encrypt=yes`). Load with multi-row `INSERT ... VALUES` batches (about 200 rows per statement) rather than executemany, and count with a real `COUNT(*)` (`sys.partitions` returned 0). Clients built on go-mssqldb (for example a BI tool's native SQL Server datasource) failed Fabric's Entra TDS handshake with "Read: EOF"; serve such tools through a small JSON sidecar. A Fabric capacity bills while Active even when idle: pause it when not in use.
evidence: CREATE, INSERT, SELECT and DROP succeeded over ODBC 18; 34,145 rows loaded in about 2 min; an idle F2 cost about $262 a month

title: Tokens in git remote URLs leak; use a credential helper and short-lived tokens
text: A token embedded in a git remote URL sits in plaintext in `.git/config`, shows in process listings and is printed by `git remote -v` into any session log. Use a credential helper that reads a 0600 file, or mint a short-lived token, push, revoke it and scrub it from the remote URL (a `trap ... EXIT` makes the revoke unconditional). Self-hosted GitLab tokens can contain a `.`, so extract them with `sed -n 's/^PATOKEN=//p'` rather than a `glpat-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` regex that stops at the dot and yields a truncated token that fails with 401.
evidence: A remote-URL token was printed into a session log and rotated; the successor was revoked after the push

title: A .gitignore does not untrack committed files, and removing a key file does not revoke it
text: A `.gitignore` rule does not remove a file that is already tracked: run `git rm --cached`, commit, and rotate anything that reached history (gateway identity files, literal service keys in config). A committed service-account key stays valid until the key itself is deleted (`gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete`); moving the file or rewriting history is hygiene, not the fix. After rotating, confirm in the cloud audit logs that the old key id shows no further use.
evidence: The old key id showed zero activity after rotation; a registration file was untracked and its secret queued for rotation

title: Scrub git history properly: tags, orphan commits, example files, inspect output
text: Secrets hide beyond `.env`: redact `docker inspect` `Config.Cmd`, `Args` and `Entrypoint` as well as `Env` (command-line passwords survive env-only redaction); scan `.example` files and backups (`*.bak`, `config.json.bak-*`), because generated examples can retain real values; scan every file type. Git tags and any other ref pin pre-scrub commits: after scrubbing a branch, delete or recreate every tag on the old commits and verify that no branch or tag on any remote still reaches the old secret SHAs; rebuilding scrubbed branches as orphan commits makes old blobs unreachable. Scan with a battery (a secrets scanner in no-git mode, literal regexes, a high-entropy quoted-assignment rule), know its false positives, and add an independent critic scan.
evidence: An independent clean-room scan caught two secrets that the capture's own gate had missed

title: Commit host tooling without secrets
text: Keep credentials in separate files read at run time (creds, session caches, key JSON) and gitignore them with logs, locks and caches; commit an example config instead of a helper that embeds credentials; run a staged secret-scan gate on the tree before every commit, anchoring PEM detection at line start (code that strips PEM headers otherwise false-positives).
evidence: Secret scan clean on the committed tooling

title: Store a credential in a secret manager by streaming it, and verify by hash
text: Create the secret by streaming the existing credential file into the secret manager without printing it (labels for app and purpose, automatic replication), then verify that the stored version is byte-identical by comparing length and SHA-256, never by displaying it. Keep one vault item per role, so a 403 becomes a choice of login rather than a debugging session.
evidence: The stored version matched in length and SHA-256

title: Old .env backups keep old credentials and are often world-readable
text: Dated `.env` backups accumulate older credentials and are often created world-readable (0644). Restrict them to 0600 at once, copy them to the approved backup location (or confirm every value has been rotated), then delete them from the host.
evidence: Eight backups changed from 0644 to 0600

title: Rotate a shared credential in one coordinated window with every consumer listed
text: Before rotating, list every consumer: service env files, host creds files, IDMC connections, CDC tasks, BI data sources, admin tools, pipelines, secret-manager copies, catalog scanners that store the password, and OAuth clients that store the user's password (those must be recreated). Rotate after critical events such as demos rather than before; change the credential at the source, update every consumer within minutes, clear the lockout-guard block, verify with exactly one login, restart the consumers and run the end-to-end rehearsal.
evidence: Rotation plans with full consumer lists; a rotation script re-armed the login guard with one verified login

title: Sequester loose secret files reversibly; move live-wired ones only with their consumers
text: Move standalone secret files (install tokens, API tokens, credential bundles, installer JSON with a live token) out of the working tree into a dated archive folder with a README that recommends rotation, leave a `.SEQUESTERED.txt` stub where each one was, and log every move in an UNDO log. Credentials that running tools read (for example an MCP server's config pointing at a creds file) stay in place until their consumers are repointed in the same change; rotate them instead. To cut runtime coupling to another environment, move its credential files to a quarantine folder (reversible) and verify the app still serves.
evidence: Five loose secret files sequestered with stubs; a backend stayed healthy with another environment's keys quarantined

title: Export packages and design objects can carry plaintext secrets
text: Connection passwords are masked in v3 exports, but a CAI app connection whose attributes were written with `encrypted="false"` stores client ids, client secrets and passwords in plaintext, and every export package that contains it does too. Mark secret attributes masked or encrypted when authoring; treat every package zip as a secret (store it 0600, off shared folders and tickets, and leave a README where it used to be); never print package contents into logs; rotate the affected credential after a migration.
evidence: Package inspection found an OAuth client secret in plaintext

title: Service-account keys never expire by default
text: User-managed service-account keys (for example the one an IDMC warehouse connection uses) never expire unless configured to, so old keys accumulate. List them (`gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=<sa-email>`), check which hosts use a key before deleting a VM, rotate before making a repository public or moving hosts, and delete old keys once the rotation is verified. Where org policy blocks key creation (keys come out 0 bytes), grant roles to the VM's attached service account instead. Keys also die with their project: after a Google Cloud project is deleted, every user-managed key minted in it fails with `403 CONSUMER_INVALID` although the key file still parses, and a gcloud configuration whose `core/project` names the deleted project fails through the dead quota project. When you inventory keys, confirm the owning project still exists (the project id is in the key's `client_email`, which is also the `clientEmail` of an IDMC BigQuery V2 connection) with `gcloud projects describe <cloud-project>`, check `gcloud config get-value project` on every workstation and VM, and remove inert keys from hosts, secret stores and connection definitions.
evidence: Two never-expiring keys found; the old one had leaked and was in use from three hosts; 403 CONSUMER_INVALID from on-host keys and from a BigQuery key held for IDMC after their project had been deleted (2026-09-07)

title: Set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, or run from cmd, for the bq and gcloud wrappers
text: An early fix for false gate failures set `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` for the bq/gcloud wrapper calls. Later tooling maps and the September az work showed the wrappers and the az launcher break with it set: export it only for IDMC REST helpers, never globally. Was believed 2026-07-04; overturned by L-ENV-017.
evidence: Early gate fix

title: Allowlisting the corporate proxy's /24 is a durable way to reach a VM
text: A plan listed SSH through a proxy /24 allowlist as the reach path to the agent VM. The egress address kept rotating out of the allowlisted range mid-session, and the durable paths became the cloud run-command channel and an IAP jump host. Was believed 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-21; overturned by L-ENV-011.
evidence: Plan environment table

title: docker exec with a redirected script does nothing through run-command
text: An earlier note said `docker exec -i <container> ... < /tmp/x.py` no-ops when sent through run-command. It worked through a managed run-command on 2026-09-23 (it created tracker comments); the earlier failure was most likely a different problem in that call. Was believed to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-ENV-004.
evidence: Earlier note

title: Grafana provisioning and datasource traps
text: File-provisioned dashboards win over UI saves (edit the file; a same-uid DB copy is shadowed; `editable:false` titles change only after a full provider cycle); file-provisioned alert rules reject API updates (PUT 500; edit the rules file and call `POST /api/admin/provisioning/alerting/reload`); the Infinity datasource returns empty results for hosts outside `allowedHosts` or without `parser: "backend"`, and panels missing `url_options` crash in the browser while the API query succeeds; the BigQuery plugin rejects `format: "time_series"` (use `"timeseries"`); behind a sub-path all API calls need the sub-path, and BusyBox `wget` in the container cannot send PUT or DELETE; audit panels in parallel through `POST /api/ds/query`. More traps: the BigQuery datasource health check shows 403 when the Cloud Resource Manager API is disabled in the project, yet real queries work (judge the datasource with `POST /api/ds/query`, not the health button); the provisioning directory is often bind-mounted read-only into the container, so write dashboard JSON to the host-side directory and call `POST /api/admin/provisioning/dashboards/reload`; an e-mail admin login breaks URL-embedded credentials (use `curl -u '<user>@example.com:<pw>'`), and wrong admin credentials fall back silently to the anonymous Viewer (GETs succeed, POST and DELETE answer 'Permissions needed'). Apps that read IDMC-built marts directly: a summary endpoint that ran about 14 sequential COUNT(*) queries took about 10 s on every cold cache; collapse the counts into one query, prime the cache at startup, do not wire page controls inside that call's success handler, and validate LIMIT parameters (a negative value surfaced as HTTP 500).
evidence: 420 panels audited; provisioning fixes held across provider cycles; a panel query returned 48 rows through /api/ds/query while the health check showed 403, and the provisioning reload from the host path worked (2026-09-10)

title: Identity-provider and connection-pool traps in test logins
text: Keycloak users created by CLI need required actions cleared, a non-temporary password and names before a password grant works; confidential clients need the client secret for password grants (a 401 otherwise looks like a broken user); a `+` in a form-encoded username becomes a space unless URL-encoded; RBAC deny tests need a user holding only the role under test. pgbouncer in transaction mode handed out read-only sessions until `SERVER_RESET_QUERY_ALWAYS=1`, and it rejects some startup parameters, so harnesses that set them connect to Postgres directly.
evidence: Personas minted tokens after the fixes; passing tests went from 250 to 398 after the pool fix

title: Postgres and API code traps met while testing apps
text: `psql -c "SET ..." -f file.sql` runs the SET in a separate session (put SET inside the file); a streaming handler that holds its auth DB session gets killed by idle-in-transaction timeouts (authenticate in a short-lived session); sweep orphan child rows with one catalog-driven pass over `pg_constraint`; `SELECT FOR UPDATE` loses its protection at an intermediate commit (use a transaction-scoped advisory lock); `boolean::text` is 'true'/'false' and enums need `::text` before `ILIKE`; two routers binding the same path silently shadow each other; `uvicorn --reload` runs one worker and serializes load; `httpx.Client` is not thread-safe (one client per thread, with timeouts).
evidence: Each fix verified by the failing test or race going green

title: Office files and PDFs on Windows
text: A workbook open in Excel cannot be replaced (`WinError 5`; write a sibling and promote it later) and a document open in Word raises PermissionError on rebuild; Excel COM `Workbooks.Open` can fail with `0x800A03EC` in some sessions only (a missing system-profile Desktop folder is a strong candidate; set `fullCalcOnLoad` or recalc from a working session); openpyxl never computes formulas and writes `=`-prefixed text as formulas; `pdftotext -layout` can swap table columns (extract by coordinates or read the page image).
evidence: Each reproduced on a Windows workstation

title: Miscellaneous app-platform traps
text: A capped mail catcher never increases its total, so test delivery by the newest message's timestamp; an OpenMetadata ingestion SDK must match the server version and sits in its own virtualenv, and table profiles are read from the time-series profile endpoint; the community edition of a self-hosted issue tracker had no OIDC, and repurposing its GitLab OAuth provider file to speak Keycloak worked without image changes; BigQuery ML rejects several `CREATE MODEL` statements in one script; a production data-cleanup policy defines test data by predicate, purges every surface symmetrically and runs as the final lane of each QA run.
evidence: Each verified in the app estates of July 2026

title: An IPU is one fungible consumption credit spent across eligible services
text: The CPDS defines the Informatica Processing Unit as 'a unit of capacity that can be used across eligible Cloud Services'. A subscription is one pool (aggregated across the customer's orgs and sub-orgs), and each service draws it down per its own scalar (compute hours, rows, GB, API calls, daily assets, events, queries) at a published, usually tiered, IPU-per-metric-unit rate. Consumption is measured monthly. Cross-service rules: a job that uses another service's components is charged at the highest applicable rate, and a natural-language query that triggers another service also consumes that service's IPUs. Compute Units assume a minimum of four CPU cores. New eligible services are activated for the pool automatically.
evidence: Documented (CPDS v39.1, pricing pages, accessed 2026-09-03)

title: Subscription shapes: IDMC IPU (monthly), Flex IPU (annual), Unlimited Flex, Overage Protection
text: IDMC - IPU: the subscribed IPUs are consumed across a monthly period, nothing carries over, and exceeding the quantity means subscribing to more IPUs for the rest of the term. IDMC - Flex IPU: consumed across an annual period, no carry-over, and consumption beyond it without more IPUs is charged the overage fee in the Order. Unlimited - IDMC - Flex IPU: no maximum quantity, for deployment in a single parent org. IPU and Flex IPU must be provisioned separately and may not be deployed in the same org. Overage Protection (IPU only, not Flex) triggers a joint review when consumption exceeds the subscription by up to 25% in any two consecutive months or three of five, or by 100% in one month, with quarterly reviews.
evidence: Documented (CPDS v39.1 product notes)

title: Published consumption rates for the main services (CPDS v39.1, tier 1)
text: These are public rates, not prices: Data Integration 0.16 IPU per compute hour for the first 2,000 hours a month, then 0.025; Data Quality 0.38 then 0.152; Advanced (elastic) DI 0.19; SQL ELT (advanced pushdown) 0.048 IPU per million rows for the first 100M; Application Integration 1.453 IPU per thousand API calls for the first 20K (tiering down to 0.015); API Center 13.33 per million calls; Database Ingestion CDC 6.5 per million rows for the first 15M; bulk database or application ingestion 0.1 per GB for the first 2 TB; file ingestion 0.03 per GB; DGC Scanner 0.32 per compute hour; CLAIRE GPT 50 per thousand queries. Advanced Serverless variants cost more per unit (DI 0.16 -> 0.28). The rate card converts usage to IPUs; what an IPU costs is set in the customer's Order. Re-verify against the current CPDS before quoting. Newer evidence: L-IPU-063.
evidence: Documented (CPDS v39.1 matrix, rate-card file)

title: The Measurement Guide defines the metered unit; the rate card gives the multiplier
text: For Data Integration jobs (mapping task, mapping, synchronization, data transfer) one compute hour is one job running one hour on the integration service using up to four CPU cores; jobs are measured to the second with no minimum, and more than four cores pro-rates (for example 45 minutes on 6 cores = 1.125 compute hours). Serverless compute hours are the serverless compute-unit factor times elapsed time. A CAI 'API call' is one execution of a process, subprocess, guide or OData endpoint (each subprocess call adds one), not one outbound HTTP call, and processes on a Secure Agent also accrue compute hours. The same feed therefore meters differently as a CAI process (per call) or as a CDI mapping with a REST connector (compute hours): confirm the build style before sizing.
evidence: Documented (Measurement Guide 39.1); guide and rate card reviewed 2026-09-11

title: Development, taskflow orchestration and reads are free; runs, previews and scans are metered
text: The Measurement Guide says development in any org incurs no compute hours except when it invokes test or run jobs; UI data preview does incur compute hours; Taskflow and Linear Taskflow orchestration of other jobs incurs no compute hours (the tasks it runs do). Recorded as 0 IPU in practice: creating or editing mapping tasks, connections, schedules and catalog-source configs, migration clones and imports, connection create/test/delete, user groups and role bindings, and metering-export reads. Billable: task runs, catalog scans and profiles, DaaS lookups, serverless runtime hours, and every backing service call behind a managed MCP tool (MCP itself was not metered during the preview, so an agent looping on prompts can burn real IPUs while the MCP line reads zero). Do not stall author-time work behind a spend gate.
evidence: Documented (Measurement Guide); observed 0-IPU author-time work (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-26)

title: Outside the IPU pool: MDM SaaS (records), Operational Insights (instance), connectors (tiers)
text: MDM SaaS (Customer 360 and the other 360 apps) is licensed by unconsolidated records per data domain, not IPUs. It bundles Data Integration (Business 360 connector, full transforms), Data Synchronization with unlimited Secure Agents, ingestion of Business 360 events, DQ assets, Application Integration, API Gateway, 100 named users, sandboxes and hierarchy management, but only where MDM is the sole source or target; Address Verify still needs a Premium Address pack or IPUs, and integration between non-MDM systems, standalone ingestion, standalone CAI/API Center and all of CDGC use the IPU pool. Operational Insights is subscribed per instance. Connectors are tier-licensed (Tier A included; Tiers B, C and D per end point) and do not draw from the pool.
evidence: Documented (CPDS v39.1 pp. 7 and 28, effective 2026-06-05)

title: Data Integration and Data Quality meter separately but draw one pool
text: DI and DQ have distinct meters (both compute hours), and both draw the same IPU balance with no double metering. DQ has no run engine of its own: DQ assets run inside a CDI mapping on the agent, billed as DQ hours. Adding CDI to a DQ deal grows consumption from the same pool rather than competing for budget.
evidence: Vendor metering documentation (2026-08-14)

title: Classify each flow before sizing IPUs, and ask for counts and sizes, not runtimes
text: A live database source with ongoing changes = CDI plus CDC (one Database Ingestion and Replication task does the initial snapshot and the change capture). One-time batch reads, file drops, ETL and DQ = CDI (DQ bills as DQ hours inside a CDI mapping). Application writes and API ingests = CAI API calls. A BI tool live-querying the warehouse = no IPU. Ask for records per month and row size, files per month and file size, calls per month and complexity, never for runtimes. Work volumes down from business drivers (sites x active customers x activity per customer x cadence), not from discovery sample files: in one engagement the sample-derived anchor was about 3x too low and published industry benchmarks matched the driver-derived figure. Give the customer three plain input columns that mirror the calculator's own questions ('What the calculator asks for', 'How much per month', 'How big / how complex') plus a computed output column they never fill in; for compute-hour lines ask for the calculator's complexity level (Simple, Moderate, Complex), never a runtime; define a record as one row and its size as the KB it takes, not a column count. Report steady state (about 36 IPU a month in that case) and a peak band that combines growth, a faster cadence and batched versus unbatched API writes (about 100 to about 147, L-IPU-009), and check feasibility against the target API's own concurrency limits.
evidence: Sizing worksheet method (2026-09-21); one sizing engagement recomputed with the calculator's engine and checked against industry benchmarks (2026-09-21)

title: At small volumes, run counts and API-write batching drive IPU, not gigabytes
text: Below about a gigabyte a month, ingestion is close to 0 IPU and scheduled compute hours for DQ and ETL dominate. For API-write-heavy targets, batching is the lever: one call per document with nested lines instead of one call per line (about 4x), then bulk batches, moved one flow from about 20 to about 4.8 to about 0.1 IPU per month; a whole small pipeline came to about 24-36 IPU per month pooled. Present the value as orchestration and data quality, not volume.
evidence: Calculator re-implemented and run on a worked example (2026-09-21)

title: Estimator traps: a service name that does not match the rate card prices at 0 with no error
text: Estimators that look up the service string on the rate card (for example an Excel MATCH) silently price a line at 0 when the name differs: the rate card abbreviates the CDC lines ('App Ingestion and Replication - Change Data Capture', 'DB Ingestion...') while the Measurement Guide uses full names. Keep separate constants for the rate-card name and the metering name, and recalculate in Excel to catch zeros.
evidence: A CDC line priced at 0 (2026-08-03)

title: Continuous CDC moves the cost into IDMC consumption
text: Moving from batch to continuous CDC keeps warehouse cost small (and cappable) but makes IDMC the growing cost line, because continuous ingestion keeps consuming IPUs (CDC meters per million rows, front-loaded: 6.5 for the first 15M). Model CDC explicitly, in IPUs per month from the expected change volume.
evidence: Planning estimate (2026-06-28)

title: BI live queries and pure warehouse SQL consume 0 IPU
text: A BI tool live-querying curated warehouse views (for example with a read-only service account) needs no IDMC step and consumes 0 IPU, and marts built purely by warehouse SQL outside IDMC also consume 0 IPU. IPU is consumed by IDMC task runs (pushdown included), CAI and the other metered services.

title: Serverless runtime trades IPUs for operations; a Secure Agent has no runtime-hour charge
text: A Secure Agent carries no IPU charge for being up (jobs on it still meter their compute hours, and you pay for the host). Serverless and Advanced Serverless variants cost more IPUs per unit (for example DI 0.16 -> 0.28 per compute hour) and serverless runtime environments bill per runtime-hour; they also cannot reach private data outside their own cloud account.
evidence: Vendor runtime docs (2026-07-26); CPDS matrix

title: Target-side capacity bills separately from IPUs
text: Warehouse or target capacity is its own bill. A pay-as-you-go Microsoft Fabric capacity bills per second while Active, idle or not, and costs nothing only while paused (July 2026, East US 2 public pricing: an F2 was about $0.36 per CU-hour, about $262 a month 24x7). For parity tests or demos keep a small capacity paused, resize up only for the window, then scale back and pause.
evidence: Azure pricing read (2026-07-04)

title: A monthly IPU quantity read as annual (or the reverse) is wrong twelvefold
text: Tools that store an IPU quantity or its cost as a bare number invite a 12x error: one estimate reported a monthly commitment as a yearly figure. Keep the unit in variable names and outputs, and model consumption as IPUs per month.
evidence: Error caught in a one-pager (2026-08-17)

title: Size with the published consumption rates; what an IPU costs comes from the customer's Order
text: Explain and size consumption only with the published rates (the CPDS IPU-per-unit rates). What an IPU costs, any volume terms and overage or Flex rates are set in the customer's Order, so send commercial questions to the Informatica account team instead of quoting figures in technical material.
evidence: Pricing-reference review (2026-09-03)

title: Treat job runs as spend: get and record explicit approval before burning IPUs
text: Every run consumes IPUs, so real runs stay on demand and minimal until the org owner explicitly approves IPU use; record the approval verbatim in the tracker. In a shared org every IPU spent draws on the owner's entitlement, so note that in the approval record. Prefer an on-demand run over raising schedule frequency for demos.
evidence: Approval recorded in the tracker (2026-09-23)

title: Read IPU consumption headless with the async ExportMeteringData job
text: `POST <serverUrl>/public/core/v3/license/metering/ExportMeteringData` (header `INFA-SESSION-ID`) with `{"jobType":"SUMMARY","startDate":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z","endDate":"2026-07-26T00:00:00Z"}` (jobType `SUMMARY`, `ASSET` or `PROJECT_FOLDER`) returns 201 and a job id. Poll the job until SUCCESS (about 3-4.5 minutes), then GET `.../<jobId>/download` for a ZIP with one CSV per org (read it as bytes). CSV header: `OrgId,MeterId,MeterName,Date,BillingPeriodStartDate,BillingPeriodEndDate,MeterUsage,IPU,Scalar,MetricCategory,OrgName,OrgType,IPURate` (the period columns are `BillingPeriodStartDate` and `BillingPeriodEndDate`). Dates need full ISO-8601 with a zone (a bare `2026-06-01` gives 400 V3API_007) and `jobType` alone gives 400 LS_147. It needs no extra entitlement and the reads cost 0 IPU. The poll path is recorded two ways: `GET /public/core/v3/license/metering/ExportMeteringData/<jobId>` and `GET /public/core/v3/license/metering/jobs/<jobId>`. Windows: a `PROJECT_FOLDER` export over 33 days was refused with 400 `LS_298` ('... can not be apart 30 days') and created no job, while `SUMMARY` accepted the same 33 days (and longer windows): split detail exports (PROJECT_FOLDER, and plan ASSET the same way) into windows of 30 days or less. A trial org returns the header only (L-IPU-023).
evidence: 201 -> SUCCESS -> ZIP on three orgs (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-26); SUMMARY 201 then SUCCESS in about 4.5 min with the corrected header, PROJECT_FOLDER over 33 days 400 LS_298 within a second (2026-10-03)

title: The metering summary GETs return 404; use the export
text: `GET /public/core/v3/license/metering/MeteringUsageSummary`, `AssetUsageSummary`, `/metering/summary` and `/consumption-summary` answered 404 'No static resource' on orgs where the async export worked. Do not read that 404 as 'metering is not entitled'.
evidence: 404 on every summary path (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-26)

title: Trial and embedded sub-orgs accrue zero billed IPU even when jobs run
text: A sub-org on a trial or embedded model ran a daily 22-mapping pipeline successfully while the metering export stayed header-only (0 records, IPU total 0.0). A $0 cost verdict from such an org is trial-conditional; the real rate is only in the Order. Check the org type and entitlement model before expecting non-zero IPUs, and estimate with a labelled proxy meanwhile (L-IPU-024).
evidence: 0-row metering CSV with successful runs (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-09)

title: Build a labelled IPU proxy from the activity log when billed IPU reads 0
text: `GET <serverUrl>/api/v2/activity/activityLog?rowLimit=1000&offset=<n>` returns runs (flatten `entries[]` for taskflows) with `startTimeUtc`, `endTimeUtc`, task type and row counts. Top-level rows carry `objectId`, `objectName`, `type` (MTT, WORKFLOW, MAPPING), `runId`, `state`, `startedBy` and `runContextType` (`REST_API_V2` or `SCHEDULER`) but no `runtimeEnvironmentId` and no `agentId`: `agentId` sits only in each row's `entries[]`, so map `entries[].agentId` to its runtime environment, or attribute by object-name prefix. The log pages 1,000 rows per call and about 3,700-3,800 rows covered the last ~4 days; count jobs as task rows plus taskflow rows plus each taskflow's children (2,329 rows were 2,775 jobs). Compute processing hours per run, apply an editable rate (for example 1.0 IPU per processing hour, or the DI 0.16 compute-hour rate), and group by day, task type and environment. Label every proxy row `estimate=true, billed=false, basis=activityLog-duration, model_version=proxy-v1`, and emit it next to the billed rows from the export so dashboards switch to billed data when it appears.
evidence: Proxy 3.92 IPU vs 3.95 processing hours over 200 runs (2026-07-04); 3,700 rows read in 4 pages: 0 top-level rows had runtimeEnvironmentId or agentId, 4,115 of 4,121 entries had agentId (2026-10-03)

title: An IPU meter that cannot read the activity log reports 0 instead of failing
text: An estimator that reads the activity log emitted a success status with 0.0 consumption when the log call returned 403 or nothing. Treat zero or unsampled consumption as unknown, not green, and fail on collector errors.
evidence: False green reproduced and fixed (2026-07-07)

title: Near-zero metered usage means nothing has ever run in the org
text: A metering export whose only line is a trivial API Center charge (for example 0.0000133 IPU) independently confirms that no integration job has ever executed in the org; use it as corroborating evidence before diagnosing 'broken' runs.
evidence: Metering export on a new sub-org (2026-07-26)

title: The Administrator Metering console shows usage; reporting is not instant
text: Usage is tracked automatically in the product: the Administrator Metering console shows consumption, administrators can set consumption threshold alerts, and usage is measured monthly. Row-metered pushdown (SQL ELT, PowerCenter pushdown) is visible within about 15 minutes of job completion; several inventory-style meters (catalog, governance, scanner) are counted per day. Billing periods need not align with calendar months (a period can end mid-month), so read `BillingPeriodStart`/`BillingPeriodEnd` rather than the calendar.
evidence: Documented (Measurement Guide, pricing pages)

title: Administrator CSV exports give the agent, licence and connector-endpoint inventory
text: The Administrator console's CSV downloads (the menu path was not recorded) produced: Agents (UUID, Agent Group Name, Agent Name, Available Processors, Created On, Updated On, Status, Version, Agent ID); License (UUID, License Type Name, Service Name, Edition Name, Category such as Mappings / Packages / Connectors / Bundles, License Type such as SUBSCRIPTION, Expiration Date); CAI Connections (UUID, Connection Name, Connector Type, Publication Status, OData Enabled, Runs On Agent Only); Unique Endpoints (UUID, Connection, Connection Type, Pricing Tier, connector property, Service URL, Database, Schema, Host, Username, Created, Last Used, Days Since Last Used). The License export is the licence inventory that REST does not offer, and Unique Endpoints with its Pricing Tier column is the input for connector tier licensing per end point. Treat these files as customer data.
evidence: Export files taken from two orgs (2026-09-09)

title: There is no licence inventory API; one per-org licence read exists
text: `/public/core/v3/licenses` -> 404 'No static resource'; `/api/v2/license` -> 404 on a sub-org (200 on another org); `/api/v2/org/<id>/license[s]` -> 404; `/api/v2/org/<id>` -> 403 REPO_10404 from a sub-org user. `GET <serverUrl>/public/core/v3/license/org/<orgIdV3>` returns per-org licence detail (200) when given the 22-character v3 org id (the 6-character v2 id gives V3API_016); TRIAL licences came back without names and `customLimits: []`. Read the licence list in Administrator > Organization > Licenses (for a sub-org, the parent's Sub-Organizations > Licenses) or its CSV export (L-IPU-028).
evidence: 404s on two orgs (2026-07-25/26); license/org 200 with the v3 id and V3API_016 with the v2 id (2026-09-28)

title: Read the org's active licences and limits from the licence service's EffectiveLicenses()
text: `GET https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/license-service/api/v1/OrgLicenseAssignment('<orgIdV3>')/EffectiveLicenses()` with headers `IDS-SESSION-ID: <session>` and `Accept: application/json` (the call the console itself makes) returns `active[]` (each `{id, name}`; one org listed 469 active licences, including CLAIRE GPT, clairegpt.core and ai.agent.engineering.designer while the login `products[]` said only Integration Cloud) and `limits{}` (licence id -> value). Every limit read -1 in two orgs (32 and 76 limits), including one that had just hit a monthly job cap, so this call does not reveal the cap (L-IPU-041).
evidence: active[] read (2026-07-09); limits all -1 in two orgs (2026-09-28)

title: Entitlement ground truth: privileges, feature flags, licences, engines and selections, never products[] or a bare 404
text: The v3 login `products[]` may name only the base entitlement ('Integration Cloud') while CDGC, MCC, CDQ, DAM, Data Prep, DBMI, CAI, MDM, CLAIRE GPT and API Manager ride under it. Verify each capability against: the identity-service Login (roles, `effectivePrivileges`, `feature.<cap>.*` flags; L-IPU-032); `EffectiveLicenses()` `active[]` (L-IPU-030); the engines deployed on each agent (`GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>`); the runtime-environment selections (what can be enabled); and real design objects of the type in `GET /public/core/v3/objects`. A bare 404 on a guessed path means wrong path or host; `objects?q=type=='X'` returning 0 proves nothing (the filter is not validated); the connector catalog is not entitlement. With no agent installed, entitlement is unresolved, not disproven. This retired about 90 false 'buy a licence' escalations on one org.
evidence: Capabilities proven usable on orgs whose products[] said only Integration Cloud (2026-07-04 to 2026-09-24)

title: Read privileges and roles to answer 'is this licensed?'
text: `POST https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/api/v1/Login` returns the user's `effectivePrivileges`, roles and `feature.*` flags; `GET <serverUrl>/public/core/v3/privileges` (for example 897 effective privileges) and `GET /public/core/v3/roles` (for example 59) return 200 too. Count privileges by product prefix (MDM/B360, CDGC/catalog, Marketplace, API Manager/apim, DBMI such as `create.dbmi.task`, DQ/VERIFIER, DAM/cdam, CLAIRE GPT, metering such as `metering.admin`) and list roles such as Customer360, CLAIRE GPT User or Data Marketplace Admin, then combine with the agent engine list.
evidence: Privilege counts on two orgs (2026-07-06, 2026-07-25)

title: Licensed, entitled, selected and running are separate layers
text: Licensed: the contract record (Administrator > Licenses, its CSV export, `EffectiveLicenses()` `active[]`). Entitled in the org: the privileges, feature flags and the services or connectors the runtime environment lets you select. Selected on a runtime environment: `enabled: true` in the selections. Deployed and running: `agentEngines[]` RUNNING, and resolvable only when a connection test or job passes. Each fails with a different signature; most 'licensing' problems turn out to be the selection or engine layer (no service selected, or the agent not ready).
evidence: Layer misdiagnosed on an org that held 321 licences (2026-07-26); selections made headless (2026-09-28)

title: Check the parent org first: allocation is often an assignment, not a purchase
text: A sub-org exposing a single engine looked unlicensed. The parent org enumerated 22 sub-orgs and its shared agent ran 22 engines (DI, Metadata Foundation and Platform, Database Ingestion, process-engine); enabling services on the sub-org's own agent then delivered all 22 engines with no reinstall. Probe the parent before calling anything a purchase.
evidence: Parent login and engine read; 1 -> 22 engines (2026-07-26)

title: Sub-org licence allocation is UI-only
text: Licences are allocated down to a sub-org in the parent org: Administrator > Sub-Organizations > Licenses. No REST verb was found and no receipt text has been captured.
evidence: UI-only walls list (2026-07-26)

title: Sub-orgs inherit entitlements from the parent org
text: A sub-org may show a narrow `products[]` in its own login and still use capabilities entitled on the parent. Check the parent org id and its entitlements. Trial or embedded sub-orgs accrue zero billed IPU even when capabilities run (L-IPU-023).
evidence: Sub-org runs succeeded with 0 billed IPU (2026-07-04)

title: An absent privilege is weak evidence of a missing SKU
text: The API developer portal was flagged as the one likely genuine entitlement gap in the API family: API Manager privileges were present, no Developer Portal privilege existed among about 660 privileges (only B2B partner-portal ones), and `GET /public/api/v1/apiPortal` returned 404. That rests on an absent privilege, which is weak evidence; confirm in Administrator whether a distinct developer-portal add-on exists before escalating.
evidence: Privilege facet and a 404 only (2026-07-04, 2026-07-25)

title: CLAIRE GPT was entitled although no agent engine served it
text: CLAIRE GPT looked like the one genuine purchase: no agentic engine among an agent's 17, and probes of `/data360/claire-gpt/*`, `copilot`, `agent/v1` on the wrong hosts returned 404. `EffectiveLicenses()` listed CLAIRE GPT and clairegpt.core as active, and a live query on the service's own host returned 201. CLAIRE GPT is a cloud service, so its entitlement shows in licences and privileges, not in agent engines.
evidence: EffectiveLicenses active entries plus a live 201 (2026-07-09)

title: In a shared org, some UI roles can be licence-locked for a demo user
text: A shared org's demo user could not see Monitor > All Jobs, Data Integration > My Jobs or the Application Integration Console ('insufficient permissions'), and adding Monitor or Operator roles failed with 'license status is not enabled'. Work around it with Monitor > Running Jobs, the Operational Insights dashboards, or apps that read the job APIs directly.
evidence: addRoles error text (2026-09-24)

title: Database Ingestion priced as a fixed floor plus 24x7 runtime is unverified
text: One July source described DBMI pricing as a fixed floor plus 24x7 runtime rather than volume, and advised against CDC when batch met the cadence. That structure came from a tracker task title and was never verified; the CPDS meters Database Ingestion CDC per million rows processed (tiered) and bulk loads per GB. Size CDC from the CPDS rates.
evidence: Tracker task-title claim (2026-07-05) vs CPDS v39.1 matrix

title: A monthly job limit (seen at 10,000 jobs) stops every Data Integration job and cannot be read over the API
text: An org can carry a monthly job limit. At the cap every Data Integration start (mapping tasks, taskflows, DQ, reverse-ETL, read-backs) fails within about 5 s with 'You have exceeded your monthly limit of 10,000 jobs.', while an already running DBMI CDC job, CAI processes and address verification through its MCP tool keep working. The limit, its reset date and the month-to-date count are not readable: `GET /api/v2/org` shows only `maxLogRows`, `subOrgLimit` and `restApiSessionLimit`; the v3 licence lookup shows `customLimits: []`; `EffectiveLicenses()` shows every limit as -1; the v2 audit log recorded nothing when the cap was lifted; and the activity log retained only about 3-4 days. The cap was lifted about 8.5 hours later by Informatica (reset or raise unknown). Count jobs yourself and ask Informatica or check Administrator > Licenses before relying on a cadence.
evidence: Error text on every run 04:24-11:55Z, jobs succeeding again from 12:39Z (2026-09-28); API reads in two orgs

title: Job arithmetic: one job per task run plus one per taskflow run
text: Count 1 job per task run and 1 per taskflow run. A 16-20-task event lane costs 17-21 jobs per user event; a 62-task full lane costs 63; a 5-task taskflow every 5 minutes is 5 x 288 = 1,440 jobs a day (about 10,000 a week). An event-driven pipeline (per-sign-up and per-event lanes, a full lane every 4 hours, a 5-minute feed) came to about 3,200-3,600 jobs a day, roughly 100,000 a month, against a 10,000-a-month cap, while all hourly schedules alone were about 650 a day; back-to-back event lanes under test traffic burned about 4,000 jobs in one day. On a trial org whose licence page hides the limit, an economy cadence still burned 520-557 jobs a day (about 16-17k a month); a two-hour fast window cost about 280 jobs and three story-test rounds 150-300. What saved jobs: folding 11 SaaS tasks into one mapping (about 175 a day, L-CDI-170) and reading the CDC replicas instead of re-ingesting (3 jobs per lane run). What did not: moving CAI work elsewhere (CAI calls are not jobs, L-IPU-044) and pushdown (one job per run either way). Count from each source, not one log: the activity log for tasks and taskflows (top-level rows plus taskflow children, L-IPU-024), the profiling service's run history for profiles and the catalog jobs API for scans (L-IPU-055).
evidence: Activity-log counts over four days, about 10,011 jobs (2026-09-25 to 2026-09-28); ledger readings 722 -> 763 -> 806 jobs across one test wave and 1,650 -> 1,944 over a 2-hour round, projecting 12-16 days to the hard cap (2026-10-01 to 2026-10-03)

title: Budget jobs per lane and put a quota breaker in anything that triggers jobs
text: Levers: coalesce events into one lane run (a minimum gap between event lanes), run the full lane less often, slow high-frequency feeds (5-minute to hourly saved 1,440 jobs a day), consolidate many small tasks into fewer mappings, freeze test traffic before a demo, and prefer CDC or CAI for per-event freshness. Breaker: on the quota error, pause the job-triggering lanes for a backoff (60 min), let one probe through, clear on success, send at most one alert per 24 h, and expose 'blocked until' on the health endpoint. Before a cutover into a trial org, confirm its job limit or cut over with a budgeted cadence. Keep your own monthly job ledger, because the cap and its count cannot be read (L-IPU-041) and the activity log keeps only a few days: every ~10 minutes page `GET /api/v2/activity/activityLog?rowLimit=1000&offset=<n>` (newest first) and insert each entry into a ledger keyed by the entry `id` (idempotent); stop paging when a page inserts nothing, reaches the previous month or returns fewer than 1,000 rows. Count each top-level entry as one job and each child of a taskflow entry as one more (a stand-alone task's own sub-entry is its session, not a second job). Derive month-to-date jobs, the last 24 h, the top sources, the projected month end (jobs + jobs_24h x days left) and the days left before the hard threshold, expose them on a health endpoint, and shed load in two steps: SOFT at about 85% (for example 8,500 of 10,000: coalesce event lanes to a long gap, slow periodic feeds) and HARD at about 95% (start no automatic batch lane until the month resets), with one alert per level per month; CDC and a database-trigger -> CAI relay keep running. Assume a new or trial org is capped even when its limits read -1. Projections matter more than the month-to-date count: one day at a heavy test pace (557 jobs) projected about 17,500 for the month. For reset-window ambiguity see L-IPU-059.
evidence: Breaker deployed; lanes paused instead of failing per event (2026-09-28); the ledger and thresholds in an orchestrator from 2026-09-29: 3,369 jobs month-to-date and 1,392 in 24 h through a migration week, about 220 a day after consolidation, a 557-job day projecting about 17,450 (2026-10-01)

title: What counts against the job limit is not what bills IPUs
text: Taskflow runs count as jobs even though taskflow orchestration incurs no compute hours (L-IPU-005). Calls to the address-verification MCP tool do not appear as IDMC jobs and do not count against the job limit, though they still consume the service's metered units. CAI processes and a running CDC job kept working at the cap. Budget jobs and IPUs as two separate ledgers.
evidence: Activity log and cap behaviour (2026-09-28); Measurement Guide

title: IPU metering needs an org-admin Consumption API entitlement; actuals are UI-only
text: Every metering GET returned 404 'No static resource' on a trial org, so a support request to enable a Consumption/Metering API was planned and actuals were called UI-only. The async ExportMeteringData job worked with no new entitlement. Was believed 2026-07-04 (same day); overturned by L-IPU-021.
evidence: 201 + job id from the export (2026-07-04)

title: Licensing and consumption have no API at all
text: Because every obvious licence path returned 404 from the sub-org and the parent, licensing was declared UI-only in its entirety. Consumption is readable through the metering export; only the licence inventory stays UI-only (with one per-org read and the EffectiveLicenses call). Was believed until 2026-07-26; overturned by L-IPU-021.
evidence: 201 + ZIP download (2026-07-26)

title: Connectors draw from the IPU pool
text: Earlier phrasing had connectors consuming pool IPUs. Per the CPDS, connectors are tier-licensed per end point and are not IPU-metered. Was believed until 2026-09-03; overturned by L-IPU-006.
evidence: CPDS v39.1 pp. 7 and 28

title: About ten IDMC capabilities are licence-blocked and must be purchased
text: DBMI, native CDQ, the MDM SaaS runtime, API Manager/Portal, DAM, Data Prep, Data Validation, CAI Process Server and more were treated as purchases because the login `products[]` listed only Integration Cloud and guessed REST paths returned 404 (a July 5 probe also read 404s for Metering, DBMI, DAM and CLAIRE GPT as honest licence labels). Engine, privilege and object ground truth showed them entitled; the real walls were UI-only authoring steps and wrong hosts (DBMI answers on `<pod>-ing`). Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-06; overturned by L-IPU-031.
evidence: Live engine and privilege re-verification (2026-07-06)

title: The org has only Integration Cloud (CDI) because the login products list says so
text: `products[]` naming only Integration Cloud was read as the whole entitlement, twice, months apart. Identity-service roles, privileges and feature flags, deployed engines and the runtime-environment selections showed most of the suite entitled. Was believed until 2026-07-04 (and again 2026-09-21/22); overturned by L-IPU-031.
evidence: 59 roles, 897 privileges, 88 feature flags and 200 authored objects on one org (2026-07-04); CAI/DBMI/CDGC selectable on another (2026-09-23)

title: A sub-org showing one engine may need an entitlement purchase
text: A sub-org exposing a single engine was taken as a sign the engines might not be owned at all. The parent's shared agent ran 22 engines and enabling services delivered them all. Was believed 2026-07-26 (before the parent check); overturned by L-IPU-034.
evidence: Parent login and engine read (2026-07-26)

title: CLAIRE GPT is genuinely absent: no agentic engine among the agent's engines
text: The absence of a CLAIRE engine on the agents and 404s on guessed CLAIRE paths were read as a missing entitlement. EffectiveLicenses and a live query proved it entitled and working. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-09; overturned by L-IPU-038.
evidence: Live 201 and active licences (2026-07-09)

title: Enumerate the org's managed MCP registry before declaring an MCP wall
text: GET `https://hdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/a2e-mcp-asset-mgmt-svc/api/v1/mcp-servers?type=MANAGED` with IDS-SESSION-ID: `<v3_session>` lists every managed MCP server of the org with id, name, serverEndpointUrl and context (for example jobmanagement, connectionmanagement, secureagentmanagement, diassetpromotion, cdgccatalogenrichment, cdgcsearchmetadata, cdgcdataqualityscore, dataqualityagent, dqverifyaddress, dataexplorationagent, datamanagementorchestrator, troubleshooting, logmanagement). One org exposed 19 servers with about 140 tools. A verdict based only on the MCP servers wired into the current session, or on GET /public/core/v3/mcpServers, is wrong: run tools/list against each server's serverEndpointUrl first-hand.
evidence: 19 servers enumerated and tested with one read-only login (2026-09-23); registry reads in two orgs (2026-09-28)

title: What the managed MCP servers can and cannot do
text: Seen in one org's registry: jobmanagement (run mapping, synchronization, replication, linear and published taskflows, masking; monitor, stop, terminate), connectionmanagement (create, update and test connections), secureagentmanagement (update_runtime_environment_selections enables services and connectors), diassetpromotion (export and import of asset definitions), cdgccatalogenrichment (glossary, classification and business-metadata writes), cdgcsearchmetadata and cdgccatalogdiscovery (natural-language search, get_asset_details with lineage), cdgcdataqualityscore (get_asset_score), dataqualityagent (the DQ agent), dqverifyaddress, searchcustomer (MDM fuzzy match), dataprovisioning (checkout_data_order), usermanagement (users, roles, groups), ipumanagement (metering exports), troubleshooting, logmanagement and auditmanagement (read-only diagnostics), datamanagementorchestrator (orchestrate) and dataexplorationagent (data_explore). The writes that the old 'MCP can't write' list denied (connections, connector enablement, glossary, roles, imports) all exist.
evidence: Tool lists read first-hand with tools/list per server

title: No managed MCP verb authors a new CDI field mapping, deploys a DBMI task or publishes a CAI process
text: Across all 19 managed servers (about 140 tools), including datamanagementorchestrator.orchestrate, no verb authors a brand-new CDI mapping definition, deploys a Database Ingestion task or publishes a CAI process: diassetpromotion import lands asset definitions only, and jobmanagement runs only tasks that are already deployed or published. Use REST: package synthesis and import for mappings, task/deploy and job/start on the `<pod>-ing` DBMI API, and POST /active-bpel/asset/v1/publish on `<pod>-cai`. Newer evidence: L-MCP-130.
evidence: Full enumeration of the managed registry with one read-only login

title: The April 2026 managed catalog: five servers and eleven actions (argument reference)
text: Address Verification: verify_address (validate, standardize, geocode; persists nothing). CDGC Metadata Search: search_metadata (knowledgeQuery, a natural-language string) and get_asset_details (id, scheme; includes lineage, profile and descriptions). Customer Identification: search_master_record (fuzzy match to a business id) and get_master_record_details (the golden record). Data Provisioning: list_data_collections (limit, search), list_delivery_targets (id, segments; returns collection detail, not targets) and checkout_data_order (dataCollectionId, justification, targetRef; raises a governed access request). Job Management: run_mapping_task, get_job_status, stop_running_job (CDI jobs only, not CAI instances).
