In September these appear as the contexts dqverifyaddress, cdgcsearchmetadata, searchcustomer, dataprovisioning and jobmanagement among 19 servers.
evidence: Vendor guide 'Getting Started with Informatica MCP Servers - Headless Data Management' (April 2026) pp.7-8

title: Three different things get called 'IDMC MCP servers': ask which class and which release
text: (1) Informatica-managed servers (5 in the April 2026 guide; 19 in one September 2026 registry); (2) CLAIRE/AI-agent servers reached on the CLAIRE API host (`<claire_api_url>/claire-orchestrator-ai-agent/api/v1/mcp`), which appear as tools in the host app, not in the org registry; (3) custom fleets built over the same REST APIs (one reference fleet: 9 servers, about 110 tools). When someone quotes a number, ask which class, which release and when it was enumerated.
evidence: Vendor guide; a reference fleet document (2026-07-16); a September registry count

title: MCP is a calling convention, not a network position
text: An MCP server cannot reach a private database that only a Secure Agent can reach, so MCP never replaces the Secure Agent, and editing an MCP proxy's code cannot bypass a server-side check. MCP sits on the same service APIs, so its read/write boundary matches REST's. Judge a server by its action list, not by the word 'MCP'.
evidence: Vendor MCP guide (April 2026); consistent with every probe since

title: HTTP verbs do not apply to MCP, and REST is usually richer
text: Every MCP call is an HTTP POST of a JSON-RPC body to one server endpoint naming an action; read/write intent lives in the action name, so REST verb matrices do not apply. About 7 of the April 2026 release's 11 actions were thin REST wrappers, and REST was richer (Elasticsearch DSL versus one natural-language string, 1,000 addresses per call versus 1, full activity history versus one job). In July, MCP added two things REST lacked: lineage via get_asset_details and fuzzy identity match via search_master_record. With the 19-server registry and the file-based DQ agent, 'only two' is probably outdated.
evidence: Action-by-action comparison

title: Managed MCP servers speak protocol 2025-06-18 over streamable HTTP and bill as their backing services
text: Informatica-managed MCP servers use MCP protocol version 2025-06-18 over streamable HTTP (not stdio); your AI app is the host and each agent a client, with one connection per server; Informatica calls tools 'actions'. Calls are billed as the underlying service API's IPUs. OAuth uses client credentials with a 5-minute default token lifetime (5 to 1440 minutes).
evidence: Vendor guide (April 2026)

title: Managed MCP servers are documented and shipping
text: The April 2026 guide documents shipping managed servers (then five servers, eleven actions, protocol 2025-06-18 and three auth methods); by September 2026 an org registry listed 19.
evidence: Vendor guide (April 2026); a September registry

title: The CLAIRE agent MCP server is read-only: it cannot provision agents, connections or assets
text: The CLAIRE orchestrator MCP server can read org metadata but could not register agents, create connections or author assets. Do not plan provisioning through it; use REST or the managed operations servers (connectionmanagement, secureagentmanagement, diassetpromotion) instead.
evidence: Read-only responses only

title: AI Agent Engineering MCP capacity can be present even when the v3 object census shows zero
text: A count of 0 for AI_AGENT, GENAI_AGENT and MCP_SERVER in GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type==... was read as 'AI Agent Engineering is not entitled', but the type filter is not validated (fake types also return 0) and an org registry later listed 19 managed servers. Re-check per org through the hdm registry and the AI Agent Engineering pages before building workarounds.
evidence: A registry of 19 servers; hedge: not directly re-probed on the org where the census was 0

title: AI Agent Engineering 'Fetch Actions' for an MCP tool can fail with 401 from IDMC itself
text: In AI Agent Engineering, New Tool > MCP Tool > Token Authentication (prefix 'Authorization:Bearer ') > Fetch Actions made POST a2e-flow-mgmt-svc/api/v1/mcp/fetch-actions return 401 from IDMC; the request never reached the MCP server (its access log stayed empty) and Save was a no-op, although the user held Admin plus Designer. That is most likely an entitlement or licence limit of that org. In a new org, test a trivial MCP tool connection before building an agent (a reusable template is the Agent Hub 'Business Insights AI Agent using CDGC Metadata Discovery'; swap its execute tools for MCP tools).
evidence: 401 with an empty server access log

title: MCP tool connections do not migrate: recreate them in the Application Integration designer
text: Recreating works only on an org that was in the AI Agent Engineering private preview; newer orgs do not offer the connection type at all. Original text: Importing a TOOL_CONNECTION (an Application Integration connection to an external MCP server) failed with MigrationSvc_031 'Internal error' in several jobs, even with the live URL and bearer token supplied; it is not offered under Data Integration New Asset. Recreate it in the Application Integration designer (MCP connection form), re-enter the token and attach it to the MCP server object. A migration scope selected by tag also misses untagged MCP_SERVER and TOOL_CONNECTION objects, so cross-check the project folder and export the stragglers separately. Was believed 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-29; overturned by L-MCP-081.
evidence: Three failed import jobs; package cross-check by a second session

title: Prototype an agent deterministically over MCP tools when the agent engine is not licensed
text: Without the licensed agent engine, build a deterministic agent: a rule-based planner (understand, retrieve via MCP tools, rank and explain, consent-gated handoff) with no LLM calls, composed from live read-only skills over golden records and catalog metadata. It costs no credits and keeps the same tool contract, so moving to the licensed engine later is the only delta.
evidence: Deterministic planner working with no LLM credits

title: A self-hosted MCP server over governed data: read-only tools and a hard denylist
text: Expose read-only tools over published rows only, enforce a hard field denylist (encrypted fields, API keys, e-mail, phone) inside the server, expose no write tools, read live first with a snapshot fallback, and stamp every answer with its source. Tools that shell out to a CLI break on hosts where that CLI is not installed.
evidence: An early build failed on sensitive columns and on a missing CLI; fixed with a server-side denylist and a snapshot fallback

title: Expose databases to an AI agent through MCP Toolbox for Databases with read-only identities
text: Run MCP Toolbox for Databases as your own MCP server with tools such as `<x>_pg_list_tables`, `<x>_pg_execute_sql`, `<x>_bq_list_dataset_ids`, `<x>_bq_list_table_ids`, `<x>_bq_get_table_info` and `<x>_bq_execute_sql`. Give it read-only identities (a Postgres role with default_transaction_read_only and a 30 s statement timeout; a GCP service account with bigquery.dataViewer and bigquery.jobUser) and verify that DELETE and CREATE are rejected. Toolbox runs as uid 65532 (chown its config and key files); its /api endpoints are disabled, so clients use JSON-RPC on /mcp (tools/list, tools/call); put it behind TLS with bearer or Basic auth.
evidence: Reads work; DELETE and CREATE rejected

title: Wrap a REST flow such as Data Marketplace ordering as a small stdio MCP server
text: A local stdio MCP shim can expose list_data_collections, list_delivery_targets and checkout_data_order over the public Marketplace API with self-refreshing session auth, registered in Claude Code at user scope, so an agent can place governed data orders conversationally.
evidence: Shim registered and used

title: MCP OAuth clients can be created headless through a2e-mcp-asset-mgmt-svc oauth2clients
text: POST `https://hdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/a2e-mcp-asset-mgmt-svc/api/v1/oauth2clients` with IDS-SESSION-ID: `<v3_session>` and body {providerType 'IDMC_MCP', clientName, description, credentials {username, password}, accessTimeout `<minutes>`, enabled true, mcpServers [{id, name, serverEndpointUrl, context, serverPolicy null}, ...]} returns 201 with clientId and clientSecret. Other shapes did not create a client (mcpServersDetails, mcpServerIds, servers, resources). List with GET ...?type=IDMC_MCP&page=1&size=50&sortBy=lastModifiedDate&sortOrder=desc&grantType=client_credentials (content[]); delete with DELETE `.../oauth2clients/<clientId>`. The route was found by recording the UI's own requests while a client was created.
evidence: 201; a gateway then got a 24 h token and listed 83 Informatica tools; verify_address answered Status Ok

title: An MCP OAuth client secret is shown once: write it straight to a 0600 file, recreate the client if it leaks
text: The create call (like the UI wizard) returns the client secret once. Write it with os.open(path, O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, 0o600) into an env file holding IDMC_CLIENT_ID, IDMC_CLIENT_SECRET, `IDMC_TOKEN_URL=https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/authz-service/oauth/token` and `MCP_BASE=https://mcp.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/mcp-servers/public/` without printing any of it, and mask the password in echoed errors. If even a prefix of the secret reaches a log, delete the client and recreate it; disabling a client stops token issuance without deleting it.
evidence: A secret prefix reached a local log once; the client was deleted and recreated

title: MCP OAuth token lifetime is set in minutes: raise it for daemons
text: The access-token timeout defaults to 5 minutes in the UI, with a range of 5 to 1440 minutes; accessTimeout 1440 in the create body gave tokens with expires_in 86,400 s (24 h). Five minutes is too short for a background job or a gateway, so raise it deliberately, and scope each client to the servers its consumer needs. (One note recorded accessTimeout in seconds; the unit is minutes.)
evidence: A gateway logged 'token refreshed' with 86,400 s; vendor guide pp.17-18

title: An MCP OAuth client stores its creator's password: recreate it when that password rotates
text: The client is created with the user's username and password in its credentials, so a password change breaks it. Recreate the client and copy the new secret to every consumer (gateways, cron jobs, scripts), and keep the consumer list next to the client name.
evidence: Cutover rotation checklist

title: The MCP OAuth client lifecycle in the UI
text: Configuration > MCP Server Authorization > Add OAuth Client: Authentication (IDMC username and password), Details (name, description, token timeout), Resources (which MCP servers), then Generate Credentials, which shows the client ID, the secret and the auth header value (base64 of id:secret) once. Regenerate Secret re-authenticates first; Disable stops token issuance without deleting (the right response to a compromise); Edit changes the name, description, timeout or server scope; Download CSV lists every client with status, servers and last update, ignoring on-screen filters.
evidence: Vendor guide (April 2026) pp.17-18

title: Three ways to authenticate to managed MCP servers, and the privileges they need
text: Session ID: IDS-SESSION-ID: `<sessionId>`. JWT: Authorization: Bearer `<jwt>`, minted like the data360 token (30 minutes). OAuth 2.0 client credentials: Authorization: Bearer `<token>` from `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/authz-service/oauth/token`, recommended for production because the agent never holds a user's IDMC credentials; a federated variant uses an IdP-issued JWT and needs the org on SAML with SAML users and the IdP's authorization server registered through the Administrator REST 'Identity providers' resource. The feature privileges Execute Managed MCP Servers and View Managed MCP Servers, and the asset privileges MCP Server and Deployed MCP Server (for composite servers), are held by Admin and Designer by default; Operator can run but not create composite servers.
evidence: Vendor guide pp.12-20; the token URL was used by a working gateway on 2026-09-28

title: Mint the identity JWT from a login session and cache both tiers
text: Get a session from POST `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas/public/core/v3/login` (userInfo.sessionId) or POST .../identity-service/api/v1/Login (read userInfo.sessionId, sessionId or session_id), then GET `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/api/v1/jwt/Token?client_id=idmc_api&nonce=<fresh_uuid>` with IDS-SESSION-ID: `<sessionId>` to get jwt_token (about 2,100 characters); the documented form is a POST that also sends Cookie: `USER_SESSION=<sessionId>`. client_id=idmc_api worked for the managed MCP servers, cdlg_app for the CDGC API. The JWT lasts 30 minutes from grant and the identity session about 8 hours: cache both and re-mint the JWT from the session before expiry.
evidence: JWT minted and MCP calls returned 200 (2026-09-21); two-tier refresh in working shims

title: Each MCP server holds its own session; IDS_085 with 400 means a valid credential on the wrong pod
text: A 401 on one MCP server says nothing about the others, because each server (and each server in a custom fleet) logs in independently. IDS_085 'User name or password is not valid' with HTTP 400 usually means the right credential sent to the wrong domain or pod, not a bad password: check the host before resetting anything.
evidence: Independent 401s per server; IDS_085 resolved by using the correct login host

title: MCP looks free during preview, but the backing services bill IPUs
text: MCP usage is not separately metered during the AI Agent Engineering preview, but every backing CDGC, CDI, Marketplace or MDM call bills IPUs at the normal service rate card. An agent looping on an orchestration prompt can generate real consumption while the MCP line reads zero: budget the underlying service, not the MCP layer.
evidence: Vendor guide p.7

title: Using MCP may require switching the org's REST authentication to JWT (vendor statement, unverified)
text: Informatica staff stated that MCP needs the org's REST authentication type switched from Session ID to JWT (Administrator > Settings > General settings > Authentication type), which breaks every client that authenticates with INFA-SESSION-ID or icSessionId until it moves to Bearer JWT. The vendor guide says session ID or JWT works depending on the org's configuration, and later calls succeeded with Bearer JWT plus IDS-SESSION-ID and with OAuth tokens; whether that org's toggle had been flipped is not recorded. Check the setting before changing it, and never flip it under a live workload.
evidence: Vendor statement and an enablement plan; untested

title: Call an MCP server over streamable HTTP: initialize, initialized, then tools
text: POST the endpoint with JSON-RPC {`"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"<client>","version":"1"`}}} and Accept: application/json, text/event-stream; keep the Mcp-Session-Id response header and send it on every later call; post {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}, then tools/list and tools/call. Answers may be SSE: parse the 'data:' lines.
evidence: tools/list returned 89 tools through a gateway

title: Read each server's endpoint from the registry instead of building it
text: Two managed-server host patterns were recorded: `https://a2e-prod-<pod>-mcp.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/mcp-servers/public/`... in July-era examples, and `https://mcp.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/mcp-servers/public/<context>` as serverEndpointUrl in the September registry. Take serverEndpointUrl from the registry (or from the server's Configuration tab code block) rather than constructing it.
evidence: Registry reads (2026-09-28); vendor and July examples

title: Informatica agent tools return a JSON-RPC envelope inside the text content
text: An agent tool's result.content[].text can itself be a JSON-RPC message whose result.content[].text is another one: unwrap up to three levels (or read result.structuredContent) before parsing. If a tool rejects a JSON-RPC-shaped (nested) argument with a validation error, retry with the plain argument object.
evidence: Unwrap and fallback logic in a working client

title: A local MCP gateway holds the OAuth client and proxies the managed servers
text: Run one small gateway container that holds the org's OAuth client credentials (a 0600 env file), refreshes the token and exposes the managed servers' tools through one local streamable-HTTP endpoint with server-prefixed names (for example address_verify_address). Scripts and cron jobs then need no IDMC credentials. Moving to another org means recreating the client there, swapping the env file and the MCP base URL, rebuilding with a new image tag, and keeping the previous tag for rollback.
evidence: An org switch through the gateway: 83 Informatica tools; verify_address answered Status Ok

title: A local MCP shim failing with KeyError 'userInfo' is a failed login, not an MCP fault
text: A shim that logs in and reads response['userInfo'] without checking the status throws KeyError 'userInfo' whenever the login fails (wrong host, wrong org, stale password). Override the login URL, JWT URL, MCP URL and credentials through environment variables instead of hard-coding them, surface the login error code (IDS_085 for the wrong domain or pod, IDS_086 for a locked account), and stop after one rejected attempt.
evidence: The error disappeared after the shim was re-pointed by environment override

title: A CLAIRE orchestrator MCP that lists zero tools may be a mis-pointed local config
text: The CLAIRE agent MCP endpoint (claire-orchestrator-ai-agent) listed 0 tools, or only new_conversation and working, for an org, and the local MCP config turned out to point at a different org than the one under test. Check which identity URL, user and org a local MCP server logs into before drawing conclusions, enumerate the org's managed registry (its datamanagementorchestrator exposes orchestrate), and test CLAIRE GPT through a scripted web UI session when the MCP route stays empty.
evidence: 0 tools listed; config inspection; orchestrate listed live in the managed registry

title: CLAIRE agent MCP: the four-step call sequence
text: (1) new_conversation (no arguments) as the very first action of every chat session, before any skill call, and not again mid-conversation unless deliberately resetting. (2) OrchestratorSkill, or MdmOrchestratorSkill for mastered entities, golden records, hierarchies and match/merge, with one natural-language prompt (the only required argument); it returns immediately because it is a submission. (3) working with no arguments, polled at about 1-second intervals; it is cursor-based and returns only what queued since the last call, so never skip calls. (4) Stop on a sentinel.
evidence: Live tool schemas read from a connected CLAIRE MCP server

title: CLAIRE poll sentinels and what to do with each
text: ANSWER: is the final JSON with responseType=FINAL_BUNDLE carrying artifact, plan and human_probe: render it and stop. PROBE: means CLAIRE needs clarification (usually a vague prompt): ask the human and stop. done means finished: stop. Error: `<msg>` means report it and stop; do not retry blindly. 'Still working...' means poll again silently. Any other text is live progress: show it verbatim and keep polling.
evidence: Live tool schemas

title: CLAIRE argument rules that silently lose context
text: Omit conversation_id on the first call and never invent one: the server mints it at response.context.conversation_id. Pass that exact value on every follow-up, because omitting it silently starts a new session and drops all prior context. Use conversation_id or history (a list of {role, content}), never both. artifacts may contain only names CLAIRE already returned. Vague prompts come back as a HUMAN_PROBE; reasoning=true exposes why (REASONING_TRACE items) and events=true exposes what ran (EXECUTION_INSIGHT items).
evidence: Live tool schemas; testing confirmed the context loss

title: The CLAIRE working action takes no arguments
text: The live schema of working is properties={}: it is cursor-based server-side polling and must be called without conversation_id. This corrects a published skill signature and an earlier catalog row that passed it.
evidence: Inspection of the working schema (properties={})

title: working is a temporary polling shim: isolate polling, and expect loop bugs
text: The server documents working as a local polling shim that will be removed once native progress streaming ships, so put polling behind one function and the swap becomes a single edit. Most integration bugs are loop bugs, not auth bugs: a self-generated conversation id, dropping it on the second call, passing arguments to working, surfacing 'Still working...', or stopping before a sentinel.
evidence: Server self-description in the live tool schema

title: Claude Desktop keeps MCP servers alive across chats
text: New Chat in Claude Desktop does not reset CLAIRE's server-side context, because the MCP server keeps running across chats; that is why new_conversation must be the first action of every chat. Skipping it leaks context between conversations.
evidence: Live behaviour

title: Render the CLAIRE ANSWER bundle by viewType
text: GridView: headers from schema_definitions[].label in order, rows mapped by fieldName position, key_insights as a callout below. DataExploreResult (or null): the same grid with null cells as an em dash, execution_context.generated_sql in a sql code fence, then 'Rows: `<row_count_total>` | Execution time: `<execution_time_ms>ms`'. PropertiesView: a two-column Property | Value table with subheadings per group. GraphView: arrows for direction, one node per line, indented branches. AnalyticsView: the most important metric in bold, with minimal commentary. TreeView: an indented tree. BlockText: display as-is.
evidence: Contracts verified against live responses

title: Wire a local CLAIRE agent MCP server into Claude
text: The endpoint is a path on the CLAIRE API host: `<claire_api_url>/claire-orchestrator-ai-agent/api/v1/mcp`. The config keys claire_api_url, identity_url, username, password and client_id come from config or environment, never inline or in chat. Auth: POST `<identity_url>/api/v1/Login` for a sessionId, then GET `<identity_url>/api/v1/jwt/Token?client_id=<id>&nonce=<uuid>` with IDS-SESSION-ID for jwt_token (a fresh nonce per request; a 30-minute token that the shim refreshes itself). Register the shim with claude mcp add; the skill (how to call) and the MCP server (the callable) are two separate registrations.
evidence: Shim working in sessions; live schemas

title: Keep Informatica's claire-idmc-agent skill as the transport
text: Informatica publishes a claire-idmc-agent skill (SKILL.md, a Python MCP shim and a setup script) that operates the CLAIRE agent server: skill selection, the poll loop and the seven viewType rendering contracts. A judgement skill can absorb its operating contract, but the shim must still be registered for the tools to exist: keep both.
evidence: Shipped skill reviewed

title: CLAIRE only sees what is cataloged
text: The CLAIRE agent (through MCP or CLAIRE GPT) answers from the CDGC catalog and the MDM repository; runtime connections and tables that were never scanned into CDGC return nothing. Catalog the source first.
evidence: Empty CLAIRE answers for uncataloged connections

title: Managed agent servers use submit-then-poll with get_skill_execution_updates
text: The managed agent-style servers (dataqualityagent, with the same shape for the orchestrator and exploration agents) return context.conversation_id and context.message_id immediately. Poll get_skill_execution_updates {conversation_id, message_id, cursor, events, reasoning}, feeding back pagination.cursor and waiting pagination.poll_interval_ms (about 1.5 s), until pagination.has_more is false and the status is SUCCESS, PARTIAL_SUCCESS or FAILED. A HUMAN_PROBE item stops the loop: answer it with the same skill ({prompt 'yes', conversation_id, deferred true}) and poll the new context. Item types are EXECUTION_INSIGHT, REASONING_TRACE, ARTIFACT (payload.summary and payload.data), HUMAN_PROBE and END_OF_ANSWER.
evidence: A full frame transcript of a rule-recommendation run with its probe answered (2026-09-27); a shim polling loop (2026-09-21)

title: A custom MCP fleet changes ergonomics, not capability
text: Wrapping the REST surface in your own MCP servers buys discoverability, session handling, role selection and parallelism, but no capability the API lacks. Split servers by product to keep each tool list small (a specialist sees 15-46 tools instead of about 110) and to isolate a broken plane; the trade-off is that every server logs in independently. Treat any fleet's tool inventory as its author's code, not as a product spec.
evidence: A reference fleet document; not probed

title: Design patterns from a working custom IDMC MCP fleet
text: Split servers per product; keep servers stateless with an on-disk session cache (a cold call takes 6-8 s, a warm one about 0 s); keep two token tiers, the identity session (about 8 h) and the JWT (30 min) auto-refreshed from it, and cache both; store credentials as one vault item per role, so that a 403 becomes a login choice; call a tool directly for simple queries (3-5 s) instead of spawning an agent (about 8 s).
evidence: Measured timings reported in the fleet document

title: Do not spawn a sub-agent for a simple single-domain query
text: A direct tool call answers a single-domain question in about 3-5 s, versus about 8 s through a sub-agent; parallel sub-agents only pay off on multi-domain fan-out (about 28 s versus 60 s sequential) or phased workflows. No methodology was given, and parallel agents also multiply IPU billing on the backing calls.
evidence: Reported, not measured here

title: Hold MCP credentials in a secret manager, one vault item per role
text: MCP servers should hold no plaintext credential: read it from a secret manager at start (for example op read '`op://<vault>/<item>/<field>`', about 2-3 s with a biometric prompt). Keep one item per role (parent org, governance sub-org admin, MDM analyst, MDM developer) so that 'why does this 403' becomes a login choice rather than a debugging session.
evidence: A reference fleet document

title: REST versus MCP: choose per capability
text: Prefer MCP for natural-language catalog search, lineage (get_asset_details), fuzzy identity match (searchcustomer), the file-based CLAIRE DQ agent (MCP-only) and conversational run/monitor. Prefer REST for bulk or history (Elasticsearch DSL, 1,000 addresses per call, full activity logs), package-based authoring, DBMI deploy and CAI publish (no MCP verb), Data Profiling profiles and dictionaries (no MCP server), schedules and metering exports. Both sides offer connections, runtime-environment selections, glossary and classification writes, users and roles, and export/import.
evidence: The REST-versus-MCP delta (2026-07-25) updated with the 19-server registry (2026-09-23)

title: CLAIRE GPT lives on its own hosts: check EffectiveLicenses and a live query, not data360 404s
text: Probes of /data360/claire-gpt/*, /copilot/* and /ai/* on `idmc-api.<domain>` returned 404 and were misread as 'not entitled'. CLAIRE GPT is served at `claire-gpt.<domain>.informaticacloud.com` (the UI), with a conversation API on `claire-gpt-api.<domain>`. The v3 login products[] list can show only 'Integration Cloud' while it works: check the identity-service login's EffectiveLicenses (CLAIRE GPT, clairegpt.core, ai.agent.engineering.designer), effectiveRoles and feature.clairegpt.* flags, then prove it with one live question (HTTP 201 with a grounded answer). Engine evidence and licence evidence conflicted in July; reconcile per org.
evidence: Live chat HTTP 201 with a grounded catalog answer, and EffectiveLicenses listing CLAIRE GPT (2026-07-09); 70 tested runs in another org (2026-09-28/29)

title: CLAIRE GPT has no public chat REST API: use the UI
text: CLAIRE GPT's conversational skills (discovery, NL-to-SQL with Show Code, documentation research, mapping generation) are used through the Agentic Data Management chat UI. No REST create or chat route exists under /data360/claire-gpt/* (all 404), and the conversation API observed behind the UI (`claire-gpt-api.<domain>/.../claire-conversation-session/api/v2/conversations`) is internal and undocumented. At volume CLAIRE GPT consumes LLM credits; single author or demo queries are small.
evidence: Live UI query HTTP 201 with a Reasoning step and a grounding card; 404s on the data360 routes

title: CLAIRE GPT mapping generation is UI-only
text: 'Generate a mapping' works inside the Data Integration designer canvas, and the result must be saved there; /saas/public/core/v3/copilot returns 404 and there is no headless route. In the CLAIRE GPT chat, 'create a mapping that reads ... writes ...' failed to resolve catalog names ('Unable to locate either table'). Headless mapping authoring goes through packages instead.
evidence: 404s on the copilot and mapping routes (2026-07-04); a failed chat prompt (2026-09-28)

title: CLAIRE GPT NL-to-SQL and Show Code are UI-only and slow
text: The managed agent MCP routes (`orchestrate`, `data_explore`) answer the same questions headless; Show Code itself is still a UI element. Original text: NL-to-SQL questions show 'Generating queries...' and can take from many seconds to minutes; the generated SQL appears under Show Code in the UI after the query completes. There is no headless invocation route. Was believed 2026-07-09 to 2026-09-30; overturned by L-MCP-111.
evidence: Live UI query engaged with a 'Generating queries...' status; overturned by L-MCP-111 (2026-10-01)

title: CLAIRE GPT is nondeterministic: rehearse, and pin the good conversations
text: The same CLAIRE GPT prompt passed, asked 'which asset?', or drifted into a DQ-rule plan on different runs. Phrase questions with explicit anchors ('the business term X', the platform and the object type, and 'in the `<dataset>` dataset' for catalog and DQ-score questions only: in a 'Query the data' prompt the dataset name is searched as an asset and can switch the answer to a same-named view, L-MCP-122), start a new conversation for every prompt, run each prompt about 30 minutes before use and pin the good conversations as fallbacks, and do not rescan catalog sources shortly before.
evidence: Different answers across runs of one prompt; 70 recorded runs; a final 8-prompt set passed 7/8 the first time; a dataset-pinned 'Query the data' count passed 1 of 2 (2026-10-01)

title: An '@' in a CLAIRE GPT prompt opens the mention picker and the prompt is never sent
text: Do not type '@' (for example in an e-mail address) in CLAIRE GPT prompts in the UI: it opens the mention picker and nothing is sent.
evidence: Prompt not sent

title: Name the system and the bare table: dotted names and unlinked business names are not found
text: CLAIRE GPT did not resolve dotted names such as dataset.table; 'Show the upstream lineage of the `<system>` table `<table>`' (bare name plus system) returned 5 upstream assets across 5 hops, with the producing task directly upstream. Naming a catalog source inside the prompt also broke search, and business-language names that differ from technical object names (for example a SaaS custom object with a legacy prefix) are not found unless a glossary term links them.
evidence: A lineage answer after rephrasing; the dotted form and business-name lookups failed

title: Anchor prompts on 'the business term X' or the business name, or CLAIRE answers from product docs
text: Questions phrased as 'the business term X' or 'in `<business_name>` ...' were answered from the org's glossary (18 of 18 correct), while a generic question such as 'How is net revenue calculated?' was routed to Informatica product documentation. Define a company-context glossary domain and terms, including one that explains legacy technical names, so that answers stay on topic.
evidence: An 18-question test

title: What CLAIRE GPT answers reliably, and what fails
text: Several 'fails' fell on 2026-10-01: catalog-wide classification search (with the right wording), mappings by name, product how-to and view lineage now pass; the current list is L-MCP-091. Original text: Worked: glossary domains and terms; PII columns of a named table; upstream and downstream lineage and impact of a named table (including SaaS objects when cataloged); NL-to-SQL ending in '... Query the data.' on a warehouse table or view; executive summaries and simple charts. Failed: DQ scores or profiles when no rule occurrences are published in CDGC ('No Data Quality information'); rule recommend/generate after 'proceed' (nothing in 8-10 min; OVERTURNED 2026-09-30 by L-MCP-079: the button only fills the input, press Send); catalog-wide column or classification searches; dotted names; 'catalog source' in the prompt; classic mapping tasks by name; 'which tables implement `<term>`'; lineage of views or terms; column impact on a PG table; stakeholder or certification questions when none are assigned; product how-to questions. Tell a DQ story through a cataloged, queryable DQ results view. Was believed 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-30; overturned by L-MCP-091, L-MCP-092, L-MCP-093, L-MCP-094, L-MCP-107.
evidence: 70 recorded prompt runs with a pass/fail log; overturned by L-MCP-091, L-MCP-092, L-MCP-093, L-MCP-094, L-MCP-107 (2026-10-01)

title: CLAIRE GPT prompt shapes that passed repeatedly
text: With a new conversation each time (answers in 47-112 s): 'What business terms are in the `<domain>` glossary domain?'; 'What does the business term `<X>` mean and where does its data come from?'; 'Which columns in the Postgres table `<t>` contain personal data?'; 'Show the upstream lineage of the table `<t>`' (then click the LINEAGE card); 'Which `<SaaS>` objects are loaded from the `<warehouse>` table `<t>?`'; 'Which data quality checks fail in the `<warehouse>` view `<v>` in the `<dataset>` dataset? Query the data and explain the business risk of each failure.'; 'Who are the top 10 ... in the `<warehouse>` table `<t>` in the `<dataset>` dataset? Query the data.' (a chart plus Show Code). Pinning the dataset name improves stability. Order a set by stage: meaning, safety, trust, impact, quality, value, brief.
evidence: A pass/fail log per prompt over 70 runs

title: 'Query the data' runs through a Secure Agent's data gateway, which parses keys strictly
text: CLAIRE GPT's NL-to-SQL execution on a warehouse goes through a runtime environment of the org, so stopping that agent breaks the data prompts (lineage and glossary keep working): keep it running for a demo. The data gateway parsed the warehouse connection's private key more strictly than CDI: a stripped base64 key that CDI accepted gave 'Invalid PKCS#8 data', while the full PEM with literal backslash-n escapes worked on that pod. Key formats are pod- and engine-dependent, so test each consumer.
evidence: Warehouse queries failed until the key change (2026-09-25); an agent-stop step was cancelled to keep the path alive

title: CLAIRE GPT data exploration runs on BigQuery, not on PostgreSQL
text: CLAIRE GPT executed natural-language questions against BigQuery (row counts, group-bys, joins) and answered lineage questions, but PostgreSQL data queries are not supported ('data exploration is not supported for PostgreSQL sources'); PG tables are found and described only. Point data questions at warehouse tables.
evidence: Answers matched BigQuery; PG queries unsupported (2026-09-25/26)

title: CLAIRE GPT's index lags new and rescanned sources by hours
text: Assets created at 06:23 became answerable around 09:00, and assets created at 19:00 were still missing at 20:30. About 30 minutes after fresh scans (Lineage Discovery and auto-accept COMPLETED), glossary and PII questions passed while lineage and NL-to-SQL still failed, probably index lag. Plan around the lag, and gate any switch that depends on CLAIRE on a passing retest.
evidence: Observed answerability times (2026-09-24); a parity retest (2026-09-29)

title: CLAIRE goes blind on a source while its catalog scan runs
text: While a catalog scan on a source is RUNNING, CLAIRE GPT answers 'no relevant information' for that source's assets. Do not trigger rescans within about 40 minutes of a demo, and allow a long wait per answer (50-110 s; a fixed 60 s capture can end before a data query finishes).
evidence: Demo rules recorded after testing

title: Legacy duplicate catalog sources confuse CLAIRE: purge them
text: When the catalog still holds old sources with the same table names (a second copy of a table, stale mart copies), CLAIRE GPT picks the wrong asset for PII, lineage and impact questions. Purge the legacy sources, include-filter the live ones (with Metadata Change Option = Delete before a rescan), and retest.
evidence: Run 1 was confused; run 2, after the purge, passed the glossary and PII questions

title: Drive CLAIRE GPT with a scripted browser when no MCP route answers
text: From a host outside any enterprise proxy, a headless-browser harness logs in fresh (or refreshes its saved state before a batch), reads prompts from a JSON file, opens a new conversation per prompt, auto-clicks 'proceed', waits until the busy text including its trailing dots ('Analyzing concepts...') is gone, and saves the answer and a screenshot per prompt. Matching the busy text without the dots made one harness exit early.
evidence: 70 CLAIRE runs recorded (2026-09-28/29)

title: Make CLAIRE answer business questions: glossary context, linked terms, curated descriptions
text: Build a glossary domain whose description states the company, what it does and its goal; add a term for every business concept (and one explaining legacy technical names); link each term to its physical assets (tables, columns, SaaS objects); and write curated descriptions on catalog sources, databases and schemas, and also in the source system (warehouse dataset and view descriptions) so that rescans carry them. Script it idempotently with a term-id registry and an undo JSON before every change, then test with a fixed question set.
evidence: 18 of 18 CLAIRE test questions answered correctly afterwards

title: When CLAIRE GPT has no usable route, build deterministic no-credit fallbacks
text: Build deterministic fallbacks over the live catalog and warehouse: discovery through ranked hits from POST /data360/search/api/v1/search; NL-to-SQL through a curated intent matcher with pre-validated queries against the gold layer; documentation research through curated pointers to proven API mechanics. Prove them with a harness, and validate native CLAIRE GPT against them once it is enabled.
evidence: Harness PASS 3/3; answers matched live warehouse queries

title: A login that drives CDI, CAI, CDQ, CDGC and CLAIRE needs four roles
text: A single login delivering CDI, CAI, CDQ, CDGC governance and CLAIRE work needed the Admin, Designer, Governance Administrator and CLAIRE GPT User roles. Check them first when repeating a build in a new org.
evidence: A runbook prerequisite validated in a build

title: The managed MCP catalog is exactly five servers with eleven actions and one write
text: The April 2026 guide's five servers (11 actions; one write, checkout_data_order) were treated as the whole managed catalog, with '5 to 10' dismissed as unverified and '2 of 5 exposed' taken as the org limit. A September registry listed 19 servers (about 140 tools). Was believed 2026-07-25 to 2026-07-26; overturned by L-MCP-001.
evidence: Vendor guide pp.7-8; July probes

title: GET /public/core/v3/mcpServers is the org's MCP registry
text: A populated answer on one org (2 servers) and a 404 on another were read as 'no vendor MCP server is reachable'. The registry is on `hdm.<domain>/a2e-mcp-asset-mgmt-svc/api/v1/mcp-servers`, and the v3 404 was probably a wrong-path or wrong-host result. Was believed 2026-07-25; overturned by L-MCP-001.
evidence: 200 with 2 servers on one org; 404 on another

title: The MCP surface is DQ-only and cannot cross the integration walls
text: A verdict drawn after testing only the two MCP servers wired into one session. The full registry enumeration the same day showed connection, agent, promotion, glossary, user and job servers. Was believed 2026-09-23 (afternoon); overturned by L-MCP-001.
evidence: Two servers tested

title: MCP OAuth clients can only be created in the UI wizard
text: Only the Configuration > MCP Server Authorization wizard was documented, and a migration runbook draft repeated it. POST .../a2e-mcp-asset-mgmt-svc/api/v1/oauth2clients created a client with 201 on 2026-09-28; the secret is still shown only once. Was believed 2026-07-26 to 2026-09-28; overturned by L-MCP-018.
evidence: Vendor guide pp.17-18; draft runbook

title: The CLAIRE orchestrator has zero skills until the org owner loads them server-side
text: Only new_conversation and working were visible in a session's CLAIRE agent shim. The shim pointed at another org, and the org's managed datamanagementorchestrator exposed a live orchestrate tool. Was believed 2026-09-22 to 2026-09-23; overturned by L-MCP-033.
evidence: tools list of a local shim

title: The CLAIRE working action takes conversation_id
text: A published skill signature and an earlier catalog row passed conversation_id to working; the live tool schema (properties={}) shows that it takes no arguments. Was believed until 2026-07-26; overturned by L-MCP-037.
evidence: Skill signature

title: AI Agent Engineering is not entitled, so no native agentic process or MCP server can be built
text: Concluded from AI_AGENT, GENAI_AGENT and MCP_SERVER object counts of 0 and no agentic engine on the agents. The unvalidated type filter never proved absence, and a later registry listed 19 managed servers (disputed for the original org). Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-08; overturned by L-MCP-011.
evidence: Object counts of 0

title: CLAIRE GPT is not entitled, or has no plane
text: 404s on /data360/claire-gpt/*, /copilot/* and /ai/* (and a 32-path /data360/clairegpt/* sweep), plus no agentic engine among the agents' services, were read as 'not entitled'. The service lives on `claire-gpt.<domain>` and answered live queries. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-MCP-050.
evidence: 404 sweeps; engine lists

title: IDMC MCP servers are roadmap, not shipping
text: A pre-guide assumption. The April 2026 guide documents shipping managed servers. Was believed before 2026-07-25; overturned by L-MCP-009.
evidence: Pre-guide assumption

title: Nothing in MCP touches connections or administration, and glossary is UI-only on both REST and MCP
text: The July REST-versus-MCP table said connections, users, roles, agents and glossary had no MCP action. The September registry has connectionmanagement, usermanagement, secureagentmanagement and cdgccatalogenrichment, and glossary writes are headless on REST (data360/content). Was believed 2026-07-25; overturned by L-MCP-049.
evidence: July comparison table

title: MDM SaaS runs in the cloud pod on <pod>-mdm, not on a Secure Agent
text: There is no MDM engine on a Secure Agent: MDM SaaS (Business 360, Customer 360 and the other 360 apps) is hosted in the pod on `<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com`. Agent sizing and service selection do not affect it; an agent matters only for integration jobs that move data in or out.
evidence: no MDM service in the engine lists of two agents (2026-07-06)

title: Build the MDM host by adding -mdm to the pod label and stripping /saas
text: The MDM runtime is `https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/business-entity/public/api/v1/...` (also `/search/public/api/v1/...` and `/rdm-service/...`): take the pod base URL from the login, add `-mdm` to the pod label and drop the trailing `/saas`. The unprefixed `mdm.<domain>` has no DNS, and `<pod>-mdm-model`, `<pod>-b360` and `<pod>-cs` do not resolve either.
evidence: live on two pods (2026-07-26)

title: Authenticate MDM calls with the identity three-header set; the JWT lives 30 minutes from grant
text: Log in with `POST https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/api/v1/Login` (`sessionId`, `orgId`), mint a JWT with `GET https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/api/v1/jwt/Token?client_id=cdlg_app&nonce=<n>` and header `IDS-SESSION-ID: <sessionId>`, then send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, `IDS-SESSION-ID: <sessionId>` and `X-INFA-ORG-ID: <orgIdV3>` on every MDM call; Bearer alone returns 401 on writes. The JWT expires 30 minutes after it is minted, whatever the activity: re-mint it from the cached identity session (about 0.5 s, no password) at about 25 minutes or on a 401. The MDM session itself times out after 30 minutes idle.
evidence: record ingest with this set (2026-07-08); MDM search with a cdlg_app JWT (2026-09-28)

title: The MDM runtime plane is headless; the design plane is the Business 360 UI
text: Headless: record ingest, read by id, source-record (entity-xref) updates, record search and export, Reference 360 search, and the MCP fuzzy match. UI only: business-entity model authoring (fields, field groups, keys), publishing or deploying the model, registering source systems, match models, merge and survivorship rules (source ranking, trust), running match/merge and other jobs, and steward decisions. Plan the design clicks explicitly and script everything after them.
evidence: 18 design-plane route shapes 404 with no 405 (2026-07-26/27); runtime calls 201/200 (2026-07-08, 2026-09-28)

title: No public REST route publishes, deploys or authors a business entity: stop hunting
text: Six deploy shapes (`/business-entity/public/api/v1/{deploy,deployment,model/deploy,publish}`, `/mdm-config/api/v1/deploy`, `/data360/mdm/api/v1/deploy`) all return `404 CMN00005`, and twelve model-authoring host and path shapes (`.../model/businessEntity`, `/mdm-model/`, `/business-entity/{private,internal}/api/v1/businessEntities`, `/data360/businessentity/`, hosts `<pod>-mdm-model`, `<pod>-b360`, `<pod>-cs` and others) return 404 or NXDOMAIN, each matching its bogus twin, with no 405 anywhere. A uniform 404 without a 405 means the route does not exist. Holding the MDM Designer role and dozens of MDM privileges does not change that. Supersedes L-MDM-063.
evidence: sweep of 18 shapes with bogus twins (2026-07-26/27)

title: Address a business entity by its runtime id (for example c360.person), never by its design GUID
text: The record API addresses entities by their runtime metadata id, such as `c360.person`: `GET https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/c360.person/<recordId>`. Using the design or FRS GUID returns 404 "metadata ... cannot be found during load" even on a live runtime, which looks exactly like an undeployed model. An early-July "deploy wall" was this identifier mistake. Supersedes L-MDM-059.
evidence: 404 with the design GUID, 200 with the runtime id on the same live runtime; hundreds of active records already present (2026-07-06); 201 ingests (2026-07-08)

title: The one manual model step: runtime-effective on Save, or one Modeler Publish click
text: Every source agrees there is no REST deploy. They disagree on the UI step. The only direct observation of a deployed entity (2026-07-06) found no Publish on the business entity's menu (Properties and Automapping only), a model that was runtime-effective on Save, and a Published state only on match models. Later write-ups (2026-07-09 to 2026-07-27) describe one Business 360 Modeler Publish click that gates all 360 apps, but they come from an org with nothing modeled, where the button could not be seen. Plan one Modeler step (Save, plus Publish if your release shows it) and prove the result headless with the ingest gate (L-MDM-008).
evidence: UI inspection of a deployed entity (2026-07-06) versus sweep conclusions on an empty org (2026-07-26/27) [disputed]

title: Gate on the ingest POST, with a fake entity name as the control
text: `POST https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/<be>?sourceSystem=<src>` returns 404 "The requested metadata with GUID <be> cannot be found during load" while nothing is deployed under that name, and flips to 201 (or a validation 400) once it is. Send the same call with a fabricated name (`ZZFAKEENTITY`): it must stay 404, and if the fake name ever succeeds, discard the run. Keep the probe body invalid so no junk record is written. Corroborate an empty org with the unfiltered `GET /public/core/v3/objects?limit=5` (count 1, a single Default project). This makes the one UI step machine-checkable.
evidence: identical 404 for three real-looking names and the fake one on an empty org (2026-07-26/27); 201 on a deployed entity (2026-07-08)

title: A 403 on GET entity/<be>/<id> fires before the metadata lookup and proves nothing; data360 businessEntities is a fake 200
text: `GET .../business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/<be>/<id>` returns 403 identically for a nonsense entity name, because the access check runs before the metadata lookup, so a 403 proves only that the plane is real. On the `idmc-api` host, `/data360/mdm/v1/businessEntities` returned a byte-identical 200 for its bogus twin: prefix routing, not a handler. Never cite either as evidence. Supersedes L-MDM-062.
evidence: bogus twins on the entity name and on the path (2026-07-26/27)

title: The -mdm host is live even when one prefix 404s: a 403 with an errorId beside a bogus 404 is a role gap
text: On one pod, `/business-360/*` returned 404 and the host was declared unmounted. DNS resolved and `/business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/<be>/search` returned 403 "Authorization Client Error" with an errorId while a bogus sibling returned `404 CMN00005`: the route exists and the caller lacks a role. A host verdict needs more than one prefix. Supersedes L-MDM-064.
evidence: 403 errorId versus bogus 404 CMN00005 (2026-07-26)

title: Read MDM entitlement from privileges, roles and design objects; entitlement is not reachability
text: MDM entitlement shows as privileges (CRUD on `mdm.asset.be`, `.srcsystem`, `.hierarchy`, `.relationship`, `.jobdef`, `.appmodel`; `execute.mdm.flows`; `manage.mdm.jobs` and `manage.mdm.schedules`) in the identity Login's `effectivePrivileges`, roles such as MDM Designer and Customer 360 Data Steward, Manager and Analyst, and `MDM_*` or BUSINESS_ENTITY design objects in `GET /public/core/v3/objects`. The login `products[]` list is only a label. An org can hold 83 MDM privileges and still have no reachable deploy route: probe routes separately. Supersedes L-MDM-066.
evidence: privileges, roles and 97 MDM design objects read (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-27)

title: Enable MDM SaaS for an org in order: license, MDM administrator role, then set up the application
text: Per the Business 360 setup documentation: confirm the license, give the user the MDM administrator role, then in Customer 360 choose "Yes, Set up Application" to provision the application before modeling or loading anything.
evidence: vendor setup article cited in a demo install guide (2026-08-15) [doc]

title: Clone MDM design objects through the migration package (design layer only)
text: BUSINESS_ENTITY, MDM_SRC_SYSTEM, REFERENCE_ENTITY and RULE_SPECIFICATION objects travel in v3 migration packages: export a same-type template, retarget namespace, GUID, name and FRS id, recompute the checksums, upload with `POST /public/core/v3/import/package` (multipart), start it, and poll to SUCCESSFUL. It is free. The import lands design objects; whether they are runtime-effective without a Modeler step is part of the dispute in L-MDM-007, so verify with the ingest gate. An org with no same-type object has no template (export answers `400 MigrationSvc_041`), and importing an entity exported from another org into an empty MDM org is untested.
evidence: imports SUCCESSFUL for a 41-field and a 15-field entity, a source system, reference entities and a rule spec (2026-07-04/05)

title: The import route is open with multipart/form-data; MigrationSvc_025 was a JSON content-type trap
text: `POST /public/core/v3/import/package` with `Content-Type: application/json` returns `404 MigrationSvc_025 "Import request with identifier [package] doesnt exist"`, which reads like a closed route. With `multipart/form-data` (file field `package`) the same route accepts uploads. What an empty org lacks is a template, not the route; stale copies of the "closed backdoor" claim survive in older reference sections. Supersedes L-MDM-068.
evidence: four-encoding matrix (2026-07-26)

title: Calling MDM services from the console page context is blocked: use REST from outside or drive the UI
text: Direct calls to MDM job, process-template or license services from a page context redirect (302) to an internal host and are blocked by the page's CSP (`connect-src 'self'`) and missing X-INFA and CSRF headers. UI clicks were the reliable path for MDM job operations.
evidence: 302 plus a CSP block (2026-07-06)

title: Ingress, match/merge and other MDM job runs have no public route
text: `/data360/ingress/api/v1/jobs` returns 404 on GET and POST, and 11 job and flow shapes plus 5 x360 and config shapes (`/mdm/.../job`, `/business-entity/.../match`, `/cmx/.../match` and others) returned 404 although `execute.mdm.flows`, `manage.mdm.jobs` and `view.mdm.x360` were granted. Running match and merge, ingress and reindex jobs is a Business 360 Console action. An ingested record lands as a source record; the master record does not re-survive until a job runs.
evidence: 404 on every job and flow shape (2026-07-09 and 2026-07-26)

title: MDM process assets have no Run button: runs come from landing data, job schedules or the API/CLI
text: In Business 360 Explore, process assets (Ingress, MDMFlow) offer Properties, View, Edit, Publish, Unpublish, Export and Delete but no Run; system Ingress cannot be edited, moved or deleted; source systems have no ingest-now action. Job definitions (for example Job Recovery) expose Job Schedules and Add Job Schedule. Ingress, match/merge and reindex therefore run when data lands at the ingress location, on a job schedule, or through an API or CLI.
evidence: menus of 74 items inspected in a Customer 360 project (2026-07-06)

title: The Business 360 Console My Jobs page is the ground truth that native MDM ran
text: Successful `<BE> MatchMerge` and reference-data ingress jobs on My Jobs (`https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ui-config-app/main/jobs`) prove the entity is deployed and survivorship ran. REST 404s on record, steward and deploy routes reflected missing public routes, not an undeployed model, and headless signals (v3 objects, CDGC activity) do not show MDM runtime jobs at all. Supersedes L-MDM-060.
evidence: 26 job rows, 23 successful, including six MatchMerge runs (2026-07-06)

title: Ingest a source record with a bare field map and a string trustScore
text: `POST https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/<runtimeId>?sourceSystem=<sourceSystemId>` with the three identity headers and a bare JSON field map (not wrapped in `fields`, `attributes` or `record`) returns 201 `{"approvalRequired":false,"id":"MDM...","businessId":"MDM..."}`. For `c360.person`, `firstName` and `lastName` are required (`fullName` is computed), and `trustScore` must be a string such as `"85"`. The source system id must be a registered source (for example `c360.<system>.system`). Supersedes L-MDM-061.
evidence: 201 per record for 10 real records, state ACTIVE, validation passed, SEARCH_INDEXED (2026-07-08)

title: Ingest 400 signatures: a wrapped body, an integer trustScore, a field that is not in the model
text: A body wrapped in `fields`/`attributes`/`record` returns 400 "not allowed by the data model"; an integer `trustScore` returns 400 "Enter a valid [null]"; a field that is not in the model (for example a computed or invented field) returns 400. Fix the body; a 400 here also proves the entity is deployed.
evidence: 400s during the contract discovery, then 201 (2026-07-08)

title: Read a master record by id: 200 in July, disputed later
text: `GET https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/<runtimeId>/<id>` returned 200 with the record plus `_meta`, including `consolidation=MATCH_INDEXED` and `searchIndex=SEARCH_INDEXED`. A later review concluded that some early 200s were identity-service login HTML. Check the Content-Type and the body shape, not just the status. The consolidation and search-index tokens are not in the vendor docs, so pin their real values on a live read before gating on them.
evidence: 200 with a live master record (2026-07-06/08); disputed in a 2026-07-26 review [disputed]

title: Record ingest is not idempotent: a re-post created new master ids
text: Posting the same source record again created new master ids, so a retry loop can duplicate records. Track what was ingested (a client-side tally or checkpoint) and reconcile before re-posting. A later plan assumed a POST per (source, key) is an upsert; that assumption was never tested.
evidence: new master ids on re-post (2026-07-08); upsert assumption in a 2026-08-03 plan, untested

title: Send source-system updates to entity-xref, never to the master entity
text: Source-system updates belong on `/business-entity/public/api/v1/entity-xref/{...}` (GET, PUT and PATCH documented, not exercised); writing source data onto the master `entity` resource corrupts the master record. PATCH matters only in MDM, on entity and entity-xref.
evidence: vendor material and the skill's per-service rule (2026-07-25/26) [doc]

title: MDM request bodies carry search or fields, never both (indicative)
text: From an Informatica solution-architect deck, not product documentation: the MDM SaaS resources are `search`, `entity`, `entity-xref` and `searchmatch`, and a body carries `search` or `fields`, never both.
evidence: vendor deck (2026-07-25); not verified end to end [doc]

title: Search and export records with /search/public/api/v1/search; one query stops at 10,000
text: `POST https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/search/public/api/v1/search` with the three identity headers (JWT from `client_id=cdlg_app`) and `{"search":"*","entityType":"c360.person","recordOffset":0,"recordsToReturn":1000}` pages through master records. One query returns at most 10,000 records in total, so export a larger entity as a union of term and prefix-wildcard queries, dedupe by id, and check the union count against the entity count. Supersedes L-MDM-069.
evidence: 19,253 of 19,255 and 7,689 of 7,689 records exported for two entities (2026-09-28)

title: Reference 360 search is live on /rdm-service/external/v1/search
text: `POST https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/rdm-service/external/v1/search` with an empty body returns `400 RDM.0040044 "No input given to required..."` (the validator was reached, so the verb exists), GET returns 405 and a bogus twin 404. Reference 360 lookup is headless. `/rdm-service/api/v1/referenceDataSets` returns 404, which on its own is not evidence that Reference 360 is unavailable. Supersedes L-MDM-065.

title: Fuzzy master-record lookup: the Customer Identification MCP server
text: The managed Customer Identification MCP server offers `search_master_record` (fuzzy identity match that returns the business id of the best master record) and `get_master_record_details` (the consolidated master record). Use it when you need fuzzy matching, which the record API does not offer.
evidence: vendor MCP guide (April 2026); listed in the managed registry [doc]

title: The business-entity search route .../entity/<be>/search is 404/405, or a 403 role gap
text: `/business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/<be>/search` returned GET 404 and POST 405 on one pod and 403 "Authorization Client Error" on another. Do not build on it; use `/search/public/api/v1/search` (L-MDM-025) or the MCP fuzzy match.
evidence: live on two pods (2026-07-26)

title: Delete a record with ?sourceSystem=; deletes are soft
text: `DELETE .../business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/<runtimeId>/<id>?sourceSystem=<src>` needs the source-system qualifier. Per the Customer 360 guide, deleted master and source records are not removed from the data store: their state changes from active to deleted, they cannot be updated, search leaves them out unless you filter for deleted records, and deleted source records can be restored. Deleting a master record leaves its source records active; deleting a source record keeps the master while any contributing source stays active, and deleting all contributing sources deletes the master. A UI soft delete also removes a record from API search.
evidence: delete qualifier observed (2026-07-08); semantics per the Customer 360 guide p.79

title: Export every entity's records to JSON before deleting an MDM installation
text: Deleting MDM content (the 360 projects, business entities, reference entities) removes business records, not just design assets. First export the records of each entity with the search API as a union of queries (L-MDM-025), then v3-export the MDM design objects, then delete item by item and list anything the MDM service refuses instead of forcing it. Keep entities that live assets still use (for example an address-verifier entity).
evidence: four entities exported to JSON before a cleanup (2026-09-28); the outcome of the MDM deletion itself is not recorded

title: Records show in the UI only once search-indexed; a stuck Search Reindex job leaves search empty
text: Records appear in Customer 360 browse and search only once they are SEARCH_INDEXED. If search shows "No records found" although MatchMerge jobs succeeded, check the Search Reindex job (`c360.search.index`) on My Jobs: stuck in Running (a zombie), it never populates the index, its Stop and Restart can both be disabled, and there is no reindex-now button. A fresh reindex comes from a publish-time trigger, a job schedule or the API.
evidence: search 0 results with six successful MatchMerge runs; the reindex job Running for days with Stop/Restart disabled (2026-07-06)

title: Reconcile what the MDM runtime already holds before a bulk ingest
text: A runtime can already contain active master records from earlier match/merge runs or seeds. Before ingesting a new population, reconcile the runtime against your source of truth and check that the search-reindex job is not wedged; otherwise you create duplicate or conflicting masters, or records that never show in search.
evidence: hundreds of active runtime masters versus a 19-row source population (2026-07-05)

title: A bulk ingest outlasts the 30-minute JWT: refresh by grant time, back off, checkpoint
text: Record ingest is one POST per record: about 98,000 records were estimated at about 2.7 hours, while the JWT dies 30 minutes after it is minted. Before any bulk run: re-mint the JWT from the cached identity session at about 25 minutes or on a 401, send bounded batches with exponential backoff on 429 (an MDM ingest 429 threshold is not documented, so this is defence), keep a client-side submitted/ok/failed tally, and checkpoint so a failure resumes instead of restarting.
evidence: estimate plus the documented JWT lifetime (2026-08-03); plan, not executed at scale [plan]

title: Documented MDM SaaS caps and job queueing thresholds
text: CSV import: 100 MB and 100,000 rows. Search results and export: 10,000. Reports: 500 rows. Ingress and egress jobs queue once 25 run concurrently on a pod or 5 in an org. Step queueing: ingress load above 1,000 records, transform above 100,000, index for search above 10,000, generate match keys above 5,000; egress stage above 1,000. Match results of a match-and-export run expire 4 days after the Release The Job step. Rejected records are kept 7 days. There is no documented "1,000 addresses per call" limit for MDM (that figure belongs to address verification).
evidence: Customer 360 guide pp.65, 168, 247 and the match-and-export chapter; verified against the docs (2026-08-03) [doc]

title: Queued is normal for large MDM jobs, and a stopped job cannot be restarted
text: When a step lacks resources MDM moves the job from Running to Queued; with the thresholds in L-MDM-034 this is expected behaviour, not a failure. A stopped job cannot be restarted or resumed, and its data may be partially processed. Download rejected records within 7 days. A system Resolve Long-Running Operations job completes create, update and delete operations that timed out.
evidence: Customer 360 guide pp.246-247 [doc]

title: Create and run a Match and Merge job in the Business 360 Console
text: In the Business 360 Console (`https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ui-config-app`): New... > Jobs > Match and Merge > Create; set the display name, Process Type Match and Merge, the business entity, the match model (for example a published baseline deduplication model) and Version Latest; Save ("saved successfully"), then Run ("job started successfully"). The stage graph reads Lock, Match, Merge, Index for Search, Group Potential Matches, Release. Automation needed a headed browser (xvfb); headless runs stalled.
evidence: a job ran to Success with the full stage graph (2026-07-09)

title: A match-and-merge run took 16-25 minutes regardless of size
text: One run over 10 records took 25 min 16 s; runs took about 16-25 minutes whatever the row count (match-engine warm-up). Budget that time in demos and schedules, and do not read a slow small run as a failure.
evidence: job detail in the Business 360 Console (2026-07-09)

title: Survivorship lives in the model; the record vocabulary is Record State plus Match Outcome
text: Survivorship (trust, source ranking, criteria) is configured in the business-entity model by an administrator; an ingest-time `trustScore` does not define it, and it is unproven that survivorship honours it at all. Documented record axes: Record State (active, pending, inactive, deleted) and Match Outcome (Auto-merged, Auto-merged with Approval, User Merged, User Merged with Approval, Not Merged); CONSOLIDATED, UNMERGED and MATCH_INDEXED are not documented terms. Vendor terminology: "master record" (not golden), "Text" (not String), entity-xref = source and patch records. Outbound is batch (egress jobs, match and export, business events). The C360 docs give no per-record IPU rate.
evidence: Customer 360 guide terminology and dashboards, checked against a design deck (2026-08-03) [doc]

title: Rank every source system; define attribute-level best-version rules; treat match-model edits as change-controlled
text: If the Source Ranking survivorship rule lists only one source, precedence between sources is undefined. In the Modeler rank every contributing source system, then set attribute-level best-version-of-truth rules (most trusted source for email, most recent for name, non-null for external ids, earliest for first-seen dates, recompute for derived scores). Editing a published match model creates a new model version and a re-index, so schedule it like a change.
evidence: ranking authored and saved in the Modeler (2026-07-04)

title: Turn off out-of-the-box DaaS enrichment on a Supplier entity: it bills per external lookup
text: The stock Supplier business entity ships DUNS, SSN, tax and bank enrichment providers that bill per lookup. Deactivate the enrichment you have no source data for, verify by re-exporting the model and checking that fields such as `dunsNumber`, `identifier`, `tax` and `bankDetails` are gone, and keep DaaS providers off on optional match/merge runs.
evidence: suppression verified by re-export (2026-07-04/08)

title: The stock Person entity carries none of your domain fields until you extend it
text: The out-of-the-box Person business entity is SSN/DUNS-oriented. Extend the model with your own fields (in the Modeler, or by cloning an extended entity) before expecting domain attributes to land or survive.
evidence: stock Person entity with no domain fields and 0 domain records until extended (2026-07-08)

title: Check fuzzy thresholds and numeric survivorship claims with real numbers
text: Name similarity is weaker than it looks: Jaro-Winkler for nickname pairs such as Bob/Robert is about 0.69, far below a 0.92 threshold, so a rule needs another signal (exact normalized phone, exact surname token, a nickname map). For numeric survivorship over duplicates, SUM double-counts the duplicate's value; use MAX or a consolidated value.
evidence: computed JW 0.69; SUM gave 6,400 instead of 2,100 in a 10-row ledger (2026-08-15)

title: A surname plus street-number match rule is a household match: tighten it or label it
text: A fuzzy rule keyed on surname and street number merged people with different first names and different emails at full confidence. Either tighten it (add email domain or phone) or present it deliberately as a household match, and decide before showing match-and-merge results to anyone.
evidence: 45 merged pairs listed for review (2026-09-26)

title: Degenerate addresses collapse distinct records under fuzzy rules; match deterministically on the business key
text: A fuzzy address rule (normalized address plus zip and city) would have collided on tens of thousands of distinct record groups: the unit was almost always empty and one degenerate address was shared by 306 distinct records. SSA-NAME3 populations are person and organization identity models, with no population for things such as parcels. For non-party entities, match deterministically on a real business key and measure collisions before enabling any fuzzy rule.
evidence: collision measurement over a 2.5M-record sample (2026-08-03); design decision, not run in MDM [plan]

title: Verify the data premise before designing a survivorship demo
text: Before promising that MDM reconciles source A against source B, measure whether the sources actually diverge (sample fields across many records, count keys with more than one source version). Byte-identical mirrors give match/merge nothing to resolve. Treat heterogeneous opaque ids as exact-match keys only (never parse them), and keep a separate field map per source.
evidence: 0 divergence across 800 records x 22 fields in a two-store mirror (2026-08-03)

title: Model hygiene for a new business entity: types, keys, sentinels, a one-row canary
text: Map warehouse types deliberately (Float64 to Double, integers to Integer, Date32 to Date, DateTime64 to Date Time with milliseconds, money to Decimal, codes with leading zeros to Text). Do not attach a key-format validator to an id whose shape differs by source. Null out sentinel defaults (for example 'unknown', 'other') on extract. There is no field-schema list verb, so ingest one real record and read it back to prove that the UI-authored field names match the code's field map before any bulk load.
evidence: design guidance from an adversarially reviewed plan (2026-08-03); not executed end to end [plan]

title: 'Cannot load the data' on Add Job Schedule means the MDM schedule service is degraded
text: When the Business 360 Add Job Schedule form shows "Cannot load the data. Try again later ... contact Informatica Global Customer Support" and Save fails with "Enter a value", the schedule service backend is failing. It is not a selector or automation problem; open a support case.
evidence: same failure manually and under automation (2026-07-06)

title: Business 360 and Customer 360 app URLs, and how to automate them
text: On the `<pod>-mdm` host: Business 360 Console `/ui-config-app` (Modeler, Explore, My Jobs at `/ui-config-app/main/jobs`), Customer 360 `/ui-x360-app/app/c360/`, Multidomain MDM `/ui-x360-app/app/mde`, Product 360 `/p360`, Supplier 360 `/s360`, Reference 360 `/rdm-ui/`. Log in on the identity host and let SSO carry over. Deep links such as `/explore/<id>` render empty when cold: navigate Explore > All Projects > the project instead. Grid rows are `role=row`, the kebab menu appears only on hover, and the console JWT lasts about 30 minutes, so log in fresh per script. Customer 360 search: `div[data-testid='mdm-bui-search-dropdown']`, `span#selected-entity`, `input[aria-label='Search input']`.
evidence: all apps loaded and selectors drove a search (2026-07-06/07)

title: Capture the browser network trace during one Modeler publish to settle the hidden plane (open)
text: Every public route shape for model authoring and deploy 404s, so the Modeler must call something non-public or session-cookie-only. Capturing the network trace during one real Save/Publish is the cheapest way to settle the biggest untested gap in MDM; never paste captured cookies or Authorization headers anywhere.
evidence: recorded as the top open question (2026-07-26); not yet done [plan]

title: A warehouse SQL master-record stand-in per domain while native MDM is gated
text: Until native MDM is usable, a SQL realisation per domain keeps 360 use cases moving: stage, normalize, cross-reference (source system, source key, match tier, score, trust), attribute-level survivorship, a steward queue, a reversible merge-override table, a serving view and validation. Keep one canonical table (other names are views, so they cannot drift), keep consumers on the stand-in's id so the producer can switch to native MDM, and keep it as the conformance oracle afterwards.
evidence: stand-ins rebuilt and scheduled for three domains (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-08)

title: Cut over to native MDM only after a zero-drift reconcile, gated behind the runtime probe
text: Order: the one Modeler step, ingest, first match/merge, then a native-versus-stand-in reconcile (party count, cross-references, survivorship winners) that must show zero drift, then QA sign-off and approval, and only then re-point consumers (a configuration flip). Gate the reconcile harness behind the ingest-POST probe (L-MDM-008) so it reports DEFERRED and exits 0 until the entity is live.
evidence: harness gated and exiting cleanly before deploy (2026-07-05); cutover plan (2026-07-07/08)

title: Do not call a SQL dedup layer a golden record or MDM in an Informatica conversation
text: In Informatica terms "golden record" and "single source of truth" mean MDM. A warehouse pipeline that cleanses, standardises, DQ-scores and rule-deduplicates without MDM is better described as a trusted curated layer, and a CRM's unified profile is its own concept. Change the visible wording; identifiers can stay.
evidence: 0 visible golden/MDM strings after a relabel of demo pages and dashboards (2026-09-27)

title: Prepare an activation-readiness package per MDM domain before the first native run
text: Before activating each 360 domain, prepare an activation plan, runbook, entity spec, ingest script, reconcile/drift harness and done-checklist, plus a master pack (runbook, RACI, go/no-go, risk register). Define a machine-checkable activation proof (the ingest route flipping from 404 to 201) and treat the first native ingest and match/merge as a metered first run that needs approval.
evidence: a 44-file readiness package built for four domains (2026-07-05)

title: Interim collectors should emit an explicit 'unavailable' signal, not a green zero
text: While a native MDM runtime is not live, a collector should self-detect the 404 and emit an explicit unavailable metric (for example `mdm.run.available=0` with a reason) rather than a zero that renders green, and switch to native telemetry automatically once real jobs appear.
evidence: collector emitting an honest unavailable signal (2026-07-04)

title: Product 360 Cloud Edition is a different product from MDM SaaS and has no REST API
text: Informatica MDM - Product 360 Cloud Edition is an AWS-hosted PIM, not MDM SaaS or Business 360. Its automation is empty marker files (`do_deploy.txt`, `do_deploy_web.txt`, `stop_server.txt`, `restart_server.txt`) dropped into an S3 customization folder that a cron scans; workflows deploy through the ActiveVOS console; DEV to QA to PROD promotion is a support ticket with a window of at least 4 hours. Before answering a P360 question from MDM SaaS evidence, grep the org's privileges for `p360`, `s360`, `catalog.item` or `supplier360`. Supersedes L-MDM-067.
evidence: P360 Cloud Edition Configuration and Customization Guide v10.0; zero P360-family privileges on the probed org (2026-07-26/27)

title: MDM SaaS is licensed by records; its bundled services apply only where MDM is the source or target
text: Per the Cloud Product Description Schedule v39.1 (effective 2026-06-05), MDM SaaS is a separate license metered by unconsolidated records, not IPUs. It bundles Data Integration (the Business 360 connector and transformations), Data Synchronization, ingestion of Business 360 events, DQ assets (cleanse, verify, parse, deduplicate, profile, exception management), Application Integration (Process Designer and Server, OData), API Gateway, named users, sandboxes and hierarchy management, but only where MDM is the sole source or target of the data. Address verification consumption needs a Premium Address Cleansing pack or IPUs; integration or quality between non-MDM systems, standalone Mass Ingestion, standalone CAI or API Center, and all of CDGC draw on the IPU pool.
evidence: product description schedule citation (2026-07-29) [doc]

title: MDM meters outside the IPU pool; record-processing cost is unknown until measured
text: MDM (and Operational Insights) are metered outside the IPU pool. The Customer 360 docs give no per-record IPU rate, and a near-empty org's metering export showed only an API Center baseline line, which is not an MDM rate. Take a metering snapshot before and after an ingest and a match/merge run to get a real unit cost, and do not extrapolate before then.
evidence: CPDS v39.1 pp.7, 28 (2026-09-03); metering export review (2026-08-03) [doc]

title: Entitled on a trial org says nothing about a production license
text: A trial or embedded org can show nearly the whole suite entitled (MDM, the 360 apps and more) in roles, privileges and feature flags. That is not evidence of what a production commercial license includes; check the order or the license team for that.
evidence: trial org with 59 roles, 897 privileges and 88 feature flags (2026-07-04)

title: A record-API 404 'metadata ... cannot be found during load' means the business entity is not deployed
text: With `MDM_MATCH_MODEL` count 0 and the record API answering 404, the runtime was thought never to have activated, and a UI deploy was treated as the single gate. The entity had been addressed by its design GUID; by its runtime id it answered 200, and hundreds of active records already existed. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-06; overturned by L-MDM-006.
evidence: 404 with the design GUID (2026-07-04)

title: MDM is undeployed because about 30 config, deploy, record and steward REST endpoints return 404
text: The 404s reflected missing public routes. The Business 360 Console My Jobs page showed successful MatchMerge and ingress jobs, which prove deployment. Was believed to 2026-07-06; overturned by L-MDM-018.

title: Ingest Person records with fullName, sourceRecordCount and an integer trustScore
text: The early field map sent `fullName` and `sourceRecordCount` and treated `trustScore` as a number. `fullName` is computed (send `firstName` and `lastName`), `sourceRecordCount` is not in the model (400), and `trustScore` must be a string. Was believed 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-08; overturned by L-MDM-019.
evidence: dry-run field map (2026-07-05)
