A skill folder name must match the `name:` in its SKILL.md frontmatter or the skill silently fails to load. For vendor research, direct fetches of primary documentation usually work while search pages hit CAPTCHAs, some vendor doc sites hard-block fetches, and a fetch tool's summarizer can invent specifics: trust only verbatim quotes and re-validate every citation a subagent proposes. Before another probing campaign, obtain the missing vendor guides (the Administrator REST API reference is the keystone; also profiling, Business 360, Marketplace, catalog and ingestion API guides).
evidence: 0 clipped cells after the fix; the skill loaded after the frontmatter fix; a fabricated API version was caught

title: Zero PUT is proven anywhere in IDMC; never design on PUT
text: The July census counted PUT at 0 proven / 14 documented / 12 rejected / 140 untested across 166 endpoints and concluded that every update is `POST /{id}` on the v2 plane or DELETE plus re-POST. A PUT on runtime-environment selections was proven on 2026-09-28; the update idiom still holds for most resources. Was believed 2026-07-25 to 2026-09-27; overturned by L-METHOD-032.
evidence: Verb census 2026-07-25

title: A documented path that returns 404 means the capability is absent or unlicensed
text: Service-level 404s were read as absence without retrying on unlisted hosts. A free DNS sweep of the host family found the ingestion service live on the `-ing` host, which turned a whole-product "UI-only" verdict into a wrong-host error. Was believed to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-METHOD-029.
evidence: Service-level 404s never re-tried on other hosts

title: IDMC lets you read almost everything, run almost everything and design almost nothing
text: The July core insight: design-time authoring, publish and deploy had no REST verb except cloning. September evidence moved most of it: migration clones authored ingestion and CAI objects (09-22), CAI publish and ingestion create/deploy/start went over REST (09-25 to 09-28), glossary writes, deletes and a PUT on service selections worked (09-28), and multi-transformation mappings were imported as IMF JSON (09-29). Still standing in these sources: MDM model deploy, CDQ rule logic, classification accept, CAI API activate. Was believed 2026-07-13 to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-METHOD-093.
evidence: July corpus and a July meeting with Informatica's headless team; disputed by September evidence

title: The session cache can assume a 30-minute idle timeout
text: Early helpers treated the IDMC session as expiring after 30 minutes of inactivity. The v2 session dies about 30 minutes after it is granted, whatever the activity, so a cache must refresh by age (at most 25 minutes). Was believed 2026-06 to 2026-07; overturned by L-METHOD-003.
evidence: July helper design

title: Claim protocol v1: a wip label plus a self-expiring claim comment
text: A claim moved the issue to In Progress, added a `wip:<agent>` label and posted an `[[AGENTCLAIM agent=<a> exp=<isoZ>]]` comment with a 45-minute TTL, released by a sign-out command and a reaper cron. It coexisted with two other schemes, which caused double claims and a reaper that could not see foreign leases. Was believed 2026-07-04; overturned by L-METHOD-064.
evidence: The fleet drained a board to 241 of 391 without double claims before the schemes multiplied

title: Clone-authored design objects do not persist in a shared org
text: A read-only v3 scan found none of the objects authored by migration clones the day before and concluded they had been removed. The scan used the wrong type name (`DBMI` instead of `DBMI_TASK`, which returns 0 rather than an error) and missed objects sitting in another user's project. Was believed 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-25; overturned by L-METHOD-038.
evidence: One org-wide scan by type name

title: An org whose login lists only Integration Cloud has no catalog or CAI entitlement
text: Plans in one program marked catalog and MDM work "entitlement-blocked" because the login `products[]` showed only Integration Cloud. Runtime-environment selections showed CAI, ingestion and catalog enabled, and catalog sources, scans and a glossary were then created headless. Was believed 2026-09-21 to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-METHOD-033.
evidence: Login products[] list

title: July open questions that must not be asserted to a customer
text: In July these were open: MDM read-by-id (200 versus 404), CLAIRE GPT and AI Agent Engineering entitlement, the taskflow publish route and the API developer-portal gap. By September the managed MCP registry was present, CLAIRE GPT was used through the UI and MDM read-by-id answered with the runtime id; the taskflow-publish route and the portal question remain open. Was believed 2026-07-25; overturned by L-METHOD-011, L-METHOD-035.
evidence: Conflicting evidence recorded in July

title: QA suites: deterministic, hermetic and never weakened
text: Tests create their own data and delete it at teardown, with the cleanup lane proving residue=0 on every surface the suite writes (app database, identity provider, warehouse after a full resync, object store, mail catcher). Accept "passes every time" only after three consecutive clean full runs with root causes of nondeterminism removed first. Fix the application, never widen an assertion to pass; separate harness bugs from product-behaviour deltas and route the latter to a product decision; a run-everything button is aggregation of existing runners, not new tests; gate test fixtures out of transforms; promote critical watched behaviour into assertions; put a fail-closed guard in front of any test that can hit production (unknown environment = production, live payment keys refused, dry run by default); prove backup and restore before any destructive pass. For an IDMC-backed application, create test identities in a run-specific namespace (for example `qa.<run>.<n>@example.com`) and drive the real public endpoints on every channel. Before cleaning up, run a read-only trace for the namespace that prints, per source row, the event time, the CDC landing lag (APPENDS), the IDMC landing task and time, the golden-table appearance, the CRM record id and the BI publish time, so every hop is proven per record (one story: 18 of 18 rows reached CDC at a median 33.5 s and the landing tables, 11 of 11 the curated tables). Then purge net-zero on every surface with a script that refuses any pattern outside the namespace and dry-runs by default: application tables in foreign-key order, the identity provider, the mail catcher, the CRM (contacts and children by external id, then empty the recycle bin), while source deletes flow through CDC (L-DBMI-026). Budget IDMC jobs per story and read the job budget before and after (L-IPU-058).
evidence: Three consecutive clean runs with residue=0 verified; story suites over three channels with per-record traces and net-zero purges (2026-09-29 to 2026-10-01)

title: Reorganizing files while other sessions run
text: Several sessions reorganizing the same tree race, lose moves and write contradictory maps and undo logs: check for other active sessions and recent archive folders first, prefer additive work, and keep fixes surgical. Many files are outputs of generators with hard-coded paths (move the generator's target, not just the file), and apparent duplicates may be builder inputs. When the tree is not fully tracked by git, a reversible undo log (one line per move) is the only undo path.
evidence: Five same-day reorg archives and a file moved mid-operation by a parallel session

title: Workbooks generated by code
text: openpyxl stores any text starting with `=` as a formula: a label becomes `#NAME?`, and a prose note can make Excel refuse to open the file (`0x800A03EC`, even with repair) while openpyxl still loads it; never start text with `=` or force text format. openpyxl writes formulas without cached values: open the file through COM with a fresh instance (`DispatchEx`), run `CalculateFull()`, save, and scan for error values before sharing.
evidence: An unopenable workbook fixed by rewording one cell; blank formula cells filled after COM recalc

title: Customer decks: reuse native slides and edit only the words
text: Hand-built shapes read as machine-generated. Render the best-matching branded deck to images, import its native slides through PowerPoint COM copy and paste (keeps masters, fonts, native tables and logos), change only the text runs with python-pptx, reshape native tables rather than drawing new ones, and drop the wrong customer logo.
evidence: A rejected deck redone from native slides

title: BI and dashboard verification traps
text: A PDF export's text layer can list bar-chart values in reverse order and hide clipped text: rasterize the page and read the image. "One dashboard per area with drill-down" means collapsible rows in one dashboard, not a folder of linked dashboards. Retire an old dashboard stack additively (panel-by-panel parity port, relabel, redirect, keep the old one until the owner approves). Stop alert spam at the root (dead collectors, SLAs aligned with real cadence, empty-by-design sources classified as no-activity, every alert channel found). Publish a freshness contract per catalog aspect so no one treats a catalog as a live data source.
evidence: A false 'broken histogram' disproved by reading the image; alert storms quieted at the root

title: Code-edit traps
text: Inserting a helper between a decorator and its `def` binds the decorator to the helper and silently unregisters the original route; anchor edits on the decorator plus def as one unit. A gate that decides a legacy script is live by substring-matching a marker string also flags a retired file that only mentions the marker in a comment: match the activation, not the string.
evidence: A route restored and 142 tests passing; a false 'live shadow' flag cleared

title: Rewrite synthetic history consistently
text: When a synthetic-data generator's rule was wrong and history must be corrected, regenerate the affected rows with the generator's current rule seeded by the row id (deterministic), update every linked record (payments, ledger pairs) in the same transaction, keep status, timestamps and keys unchanged, take a dump and an undo SQL first, and verify the reconciliations (payments equal ledger, debits equal credits) afterwards.
evidence: 0 payment/order mismatches and balanced ledgers after re-pricing 514 rows

title: The v3 objects API is a read-only inventory; the migration import is the write path
text: `GET /public/core/v3/objects` (paged with `limit` and `skip`, optionally `q=type=='<TYPE>'`) lists design objects; `POST /public/core/v3/objects` returns 405 'Method not supported' and a per-object PATCH returns 404. Create and change design objects through the v3 import (or a service's own create API where one exists, such as DBMI task/create), and use the objects list for inventory and read-back.
evidence: 405 on POST and 404 on PATCH across orgs (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-25)

title: The v3 type filter is not validated: a wrong type name returns 0, not an error
text: `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='<X>'` returns the same clean `{"count":0,"objects":[]}` for a fabricated type as for an empty real one; an audit that asked for `DBMI` instead of `DBMI_TASK` missed 23 objects. Use exact type names (for example MTT, MAPPING, DTEMPLATE, DBMI_TASK, MI_TASK, PROCESS, TASKFLOW, WORKFLOW, RULE_SPECIFICATION, PROFILE, TOOL_CONNECTION, MCP_SERVER), or list unfiltered and group client-side. Never read count 0 as proof that a capability is absent. Supersedes L-MIG-064.
evidence: fabricated types returned identical envelopes (2026-07-25); 23 objects found under the right type (2026-09-24/25)

title: v3 export: start, poll, download
text: `POST https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas/public/core/v3/export` with header `INFA-SESSION-ID` and body `{"name":"<name>","objects":[{"id":"<frsGuid>","includeDependencies":true}]}` returns 200 with the export job `id`. Poll `GET /public/core/v3/export/<id>` (add `?expand=objects` for per-object state) until `status.state` is SUCCESSFUL ('Export completed successfully'), then download `GET /public/core/v3/export/<id>/package` with `Accept: application/zip`. An export is read-only for the source; a 194-object scope with dependencies gave 223 objects (a 616 KB zip) in about 20 s. Supersedes L-MIG-070.
evidence: export SUCCESSFUL with 0 missing references across 223 objects (2026-09-28)

title: Export body shape errors: V3API_007 and an empty `objects[]`
text: `objects[]` takes objects like `{"id":"..."}`; bare id strings, or an added `type` key, give 400 `V3API_007 Bad Request`. An empty `objects[]` gives 400, and `GET /public/core/v3/export` is 405.
evidence: live 2026-07-26; bare string ids confirmed 2026-09-28

title: MigrationSvc_041 'No asset selected' is a content verdict, not a shape error
text: 400 `MigrationSvc_041 'No asset selected for export operation'` means the body parsed and the named object contributes nothing exportable, for example an org whose only object is an empty default project. Pick another object; do not sweep body shapes against an endpoint that already accepted the request.
evidence: live on an empty org (2026-07-26)

title: 403 MigrationSvc_038 is a role gap; for Add-On Bundle templates it is org- and user-dependent
text: 403 `MigrationSvc_038 'User does not have required permissions'` on export means the user lacks the migration (export/import) role, while an empty-body POST returning 400 proves the route is writable. Granting the migration and object-admin roles in Administrator takes about a minute and is free. Exporting Add-On Bundle templates (for example `dsst__copy_data_new_tgt`, `dlt__copy_data`) can return the same 403 for a non-admin while user-owned objects export fine, and the result differed by org and date; do not depend on exporting bundle content (import with REUSE instead).
evidence: 403 before and 200 after the grant (2026-07-05/06); bundle 403 seen and not reproduced in different orgs (2026-09-22 to 2026-09-29)

title: MigrationSvc_034 'Object resolution failed': the wrong kind of id, or a CDGC governance object
text: Export takes the IDMC object id from `/public/core/v3/objects`; passing a CAI process GUID read from inside the process XML gives 400 `MigrationSvc_034`. CDGC governance objects (classifications, stakeholders, assignments) are not carried by v3 migration and give the same error.
evidence: MigrationSvc_034 on both (2026-07-04 and 2026-09-28)

title: v3 import upload: multipart/form-data with one part named `package`
text: `POST /public/core/v3/import/package` with `Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=<b>` and one part `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="package"; filename="pkg.zip"` (part type `application/zip`) returns 200 `{"jobId":"<id>","checksumValid":true}` in state NOT_STARTED: staged, not committed. `checksumValid:false` means the checksum file does not match the zip.
evidence: uploads accepted with checksumValid true (2026-07-06 to 2026-09-29)

title: The upload route answers by Content-Type: json 404 MigrationSvc_025, zip 415, multipart 400 MigrationSvc_030
text: On `POST /public/core/v3/import/package`: `application/json` gives 404 `MigrationSvc_025 'Import request with identifier [package] doesnt exist'` (the service reads `package` as an import id: a live handler, not a dead route); `application/zip` and `application/octet-stream` give 415; `multipart/form-data` with an empty or invalid zip gives 400 `MigrationSvc_030 'Invalid import package'` (the validator was reached); multipart with a valid package gives 200. `POST /public/core/v3/import` is 404 'No static resource', and `/import/upload` is `MigrationSvc_025 [upload]`. Vary the Content-Type before calling any upload route absent. Supersedes L-MIG-063.
evidence: four encodings on one org (2026-07-26)

title: Start the import on `/import/<jobId>` (not `/import/package/<jobId>`), then poll and read the log
text: `POST /public/core/v3/import/<jobId>` with `{"name":"<name>","importSpecification":{"defaultConflictResolution":"REUSE","includeObjects":[]}}` (or `OVERWRITE`) starts the staged import; `POST /import/package/<jobId>` is 404 'No static resource'. Poll `GET /public/core/v3/import/<jobId>` until `status.state` leaves IN_PROGRESS, QUEUED or NOT_STARTED (then SUCCESSFUL, FAILED or PARTIAL). The success envelope has `objects:null` unless you add `?expand=objects`, which returns per-object `sourceObject`, `targetObject` and `status` ('Create object' or 'Reuse existing object'); `targetObject.id` came back null, so read target ids from the target's objects list. `GET /public/core/v3/import/<jobId>/log` (Accept `*/*`) returns the log; a 214-object import ran about 3.5 minutes.
evidence: import SUCCESSFUL with 180 created and 34 reused (2026-09-28)

title: Import into a non-empty org with REUSE, then check the reused pairs
text: With `defaultConflictResolution: REUSE`, an object whose name and type already exist in the target is kept ('Reuse existing object'), nothing unrelated is overwritten, and bundle content comes from the target's own copy. The reused copy may be older than the source, so compare every reused pair whose source changed recently, or re-import that object with OVERWRITE. Test-import a small set first (a template plus one task).
evidence: 34 reused pairs, 9 verified by runtime evidence (2026-09-28)

title: An import is all-or-nothing, and `includeObjects` does not exclude objects from validation
text: If one object fails validation, the whole import fails (`MigrationSvc_031 'Import failed. Correct the errors in the Select Assets section and try again.'`) and every other object reports 'Object skipped because of previous failures'. Listing only some objects in `includeObjects` does not stop the others from being validated. Remove the failing objects from the package itself and import them separately.
evidence: 5 failures rolled back 180 objects; the edited package imported (2026-09-28)

title: `importSpecification.objectSpecification` returned V3API_007 in every shape
text: Mapping a package object onto a chosen existing target object (`objectSpecification: [{sourceObjectId, existingTargetObjectId | existingObjectId}]`) was rejected with V3API_007 in every shape tried. Use name-based REUSE, or edit the package so it references the target object by name.
evidence: V3API_007 each time (2026-09-28)

title: MigrationSvc_056: objects are missing required dependent objects
text: 'One or more objects are missing required dependent objects' lists the objects it skipped. Export with `includeDependencies:true` and make sure every dependency (runtime environments, connections, bundle templates, bundle rule specs) is in the package or already in the target under the same name.
evidence: first import attempt of a migration (2026-09-28)

title: The hosted runtime name is reserved: remap objects bound to it inside the package
text: A runtime environment named 'Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent' cannot be created by import (`REPO_38210`). If the target is not entitled to the hosted runtime, remap every object bound to it to a self-hosted runtime environment inside the package (inner files, `exportMetadata.v2.json` entries and objectRefs, checksum lines) before importing.
evidence: 15 objects remapped; import SUCCESSFUL (2026-09-28)

title: Imports drop tags: re-tag with TagObjects and read back
text: Imported objects arrive without their tags. `POST /public/core/v3/TagObjects` with `[{"id":"<frsGuid>","tags":["<tag>"]}]`, at most 50 items per call, answers 204 or a per-item status; folders and projects cannot be tagged ('of type: [Folder]'). Re-tag after every import, or tag-based audits and later exports miss the imported objects.
evidence: 189 objects re-tagged and read back (2026-09-28)

title: What a v3 package does not carry
text: Connection passwords (masked), schedules and their bindings, Secure Agents and runtime-environment service selections, CDGC content (catalog sources, glossary, links, classifications), object tags, DBMI deploy and start, CAI publish, profile rule occurrences, and every external caller's configuration (hard-coded ids and URLs). Plan each as its own step with a check: an import alone leaves nothing runnable.
evidence: nothing ran in the target after the import until those steps were done (2026-09-28)

title: Export packages can hold plaintext secrets: treat the zip as a secret
text: Connection passwords are masked, but a CAI app connection authored with `encrypted="false"` carries its OAuth client id and secret in clear, so every package containing it does too. Keep packages in a private 0600 location (not a desktop, share or repository), never print their contents in logs, and rotate the exposed secret after the migration.
evidence: found by package inspection (2026-09-28)

title: Edit a package: the inner file, its objectRefs, and upper-case SHA-256 lines for changed files only
text: (1) Change the inner file (rewrite the nested zip where there is one). (2) In `exportMetadata.v2.json` adjust or remove the object's entry and remap every `objectRefs` list that points at a changed or removed guid; each objectRef must point at an object present in the package. (3) In `exportPackage.chksum` replace only the lines of the files you changed with `<path>=<SHA-256 hex, upper case>`, including the line for `exportMetadata.v2.json` itself, and keep every other line byte-identical (the opaque object-hash lines stay valid). A missed hash gives `MigrationSvc_073 'package has been modified'`; a dangling objectRef gives `MigrationSvc_031` with empty details.
evidence: checksumValid true and SUCCESSFUL imports after each edit (2026-09-22 to 2026-09-29)

title: Swapping a mapping's connection: edit the GUID in place and do not add the new connection to objectRefs
text: IDMC GUIDs are 22 characters, so a connection GUID can be swapped in place inside a mapping entry (for example `bin/@3.bin`) without shifting offsets; recompute the path-keyed checksum lines of the changed entries and leave the GUID-keyed lines alone. Adding the new connection's GUID to `objectRefs` when that connection is not in the package breaks the import with `MigrationSvc_031`; the swapped GUID resolves in the target at import time.
evidence: the clone imported with checksumValid true and ran 52/52 rows into a different warehouse type (2026-08-19)

title: Anatomy of a v3 export package
text: Object files sit under `Explore/<project>/<folder>/<name>.<TYPE>.<ext>`: `.DBMI_TASK.dat` and `.TOOL_CONNECTION.dat` are plain JSON; CAI assets are `.PROCESS.xml`, `.AI_CONNECTION.xml` and `.AI_SERVICE_CONNECTOR.xml`; a mapping is a nested `<name>.DTEMPLATE.zip` holding `mappingTemplate.json`, `fileRecord.json`, `bin/@<n>.bin` and `metadata.meta`. Dependencies sit under `SYS/` (`<conn>.Connection.zip`, `<re>.AgentGroup.zip`), next to `<folder>.Folder.json` and `<project>.Project.json`. `exportMetadata.v2.json` lists `exportedObjects[]` (`objectGuid`, `objectName`, `objectType`, `path`, `metadata.objectRefs`, `additionalInfo`, and `repoInfo.repoHandle` = the v2 id), `exportPackage.chksum` holds the hashes, and a CSV lists the objects.
evidence: packages inspected and generated (2026-07-06 to 2026-09-29)

title: Packages built from scratch import when the metadata, folder entries and checksums are right
text: A self-built package imports SUCCESSFUL if it has the object files under `Explore/<project>/<folder>/`, the real `<folder>.Folder.json` and `<project>.Project.json` (copied from any genuine export in that folder), an `exportMetadata.v2.json` listing the folder, the project and each object with objectRefs to its dependencies (connections as `/SYS` entries with `repoInfo.repoHandle`), and correct upper-case SHA-256 lines. 400 `MigrationSvc_030` is what an empty or malformed multipart gets. Proven for CAI connectors, app connections and processes, advanced taskflows (import only) and multi-transformation mappings. Supersedes L-MIG-066.
evidence: import states SUCCESSFUL, checksumValid true (2026-09-25 to 2026-09-29)

title: Migration-clone authors design objects headless for most object types
text: Export a same-type object, change its name, GUID and references in the package, re-hash, import and start. Proven: RULE_SPECIFICATION (count 4 to 11 to 12), BUSINESS_ENTITY (41 and 15 fields), MDM_SRC_SYSTEM, reference entities and Data Marketplace products (2026-07); CAI PROCESS with its AI_CONNECTION and AI_SERVICE_CONNECTOR (2026-07 and 2026-09); MAPPING/DTEMPLATE (2026-08-19 and 2026-09); DBMI_TASK (2026-09-22). It costs no IPU, and needs the migration role plus an existing same-type object or a from-scratch package. Supersedes L-MIG-061, L-MIG-062, L-MIG-071.
evidence: imports SUCCESSFUL with the new objects visible in the org (2026-07-05 to 2026-09-28)

title: An import creates design objects only: deploy, publish and bind separately
text: The commit creates design objects (state SUCCESSFUL, `objects:null`): DBMI tasks are not deployed, CAI assets are not published, no schedule is bound, connections have no passwords, and objects may point at runtime environments with no agent. Follow each import with the service's own step: DBMI `task/deploy`, CAI `asset/v1/publish`, a v2 schedule bind. MDM model deploy is still a UI step in these sources (disputed). Check that objects already in the org survive each commit. Supersedes L-MIG-067.
evidence: each follow-up step was needed before anything ran (2026-09-22 to 2026-09-28)

title: A clone inherits the template's logic and target properties
text: A cloned rule spec inherits the template's expression body, and a cloned task built from a template for another target type carries that type's target property map. Fix the logic or the properties before the first real run, or clone from a template of the same target type.
evidence: noted before the first run (2026-07-09 and 2026-09-22)

title: Cloning needs a same-type object: an empty org has nothing to export
text: On an empty org the export fails with `MigrationSvc_041` because there is no template. Check with an unfiltered `GET /public/core/v3/objects?limit=5`: `count:1` with only a default project is decisive, while a type-filtered count 0 proves nothing. For a type with no object in the org, author one seed (UI), or build the package from scratch where its format is known (mappings, CAI assets, taskflows).
evidence: empty org (2026-07-26); from-scratch packages proven (2026-09-25 to 2026-09-29)

title: Rebinding a cloned mapping to a new connection type needs that connection's package entry
text: To rebind an exported mapping to a different connection type, the package needs that connection's `SYS/<conn>.Connection.zip`, which a pure clone only has if some mapping already uses it; if none does, author one seed mapping with that source or target and clone from it. Generated packages carry their own `/SYS` connection entries, which probably removes this limit for synthesized mappings (untested for a new connector type).
evidence: export inspection: no mapping used the needed connection type (2026-07-06)

title: MigrationSvc_031 on a mapping import: rule out package defects, then treat it as transient
text: A mapping package can upload (200 `checksumValid:true`) and still fail on start with 500 `MigrationSvc_031 ... type [DTEMPLATE] ... An error occurred while loading the mapping`. In July a known-good, already-live package failed identically, which pointed at a transient service fault (retry later or open a support case); later clones and synthesized mappings imported fine. The same code also comes from package defects (a dangling objectRef, another failing object, a TOOL_CONNECTION), so check those first.
evidence: 85-124 July failures with 0 recoveries, then clean DTEMPLATE imports (2026-08-19, 2026-09-29)

title: A mapping's `bin` entry is editable IMF JSON, not an opaque blob
text: In the exports inspected in September, the DTEMPLATE entry `bin/@<n>.bin` held IMF JSON text, and the connection references sit in `mappingTemplate.json` `references[]`, so cloning and repointing a mapping is mechanically possible; schema-bound mappings still need consistent field arrays. An MI or DBMI task's `.dat` is plain JSON too. Supersedes L-MIG-065.
evidence: package inspection (2026-09-22); connection swap ran (2026-08-19); mappings synthesized and imported (2026-09-29)

title: Retarget a mapping task by re-importing its mapping, not by a v2 POST
text: POSTing a mapping task back to `/saas/api/v2/mttask/<taskId>` with changed target parameters returns 200 but changes nothing, because the task re-derives its targets from the mapping. Retarget by editing the mapping's package and re-importing it with OVERWRITE under the same GUID, then read the task back.
evidence: POST 200 with the old target on read-back; the OVERWRITE re-import changed it (2026-09-29)

title: Promote between environments in three gates: plan, validate without running, gated execute
text: (1) Plan, read-only: enumerate the assets, show the intended deltas (usually only the warehouse connection), run a pre-flight parity check and write a plan file. (2) Validate without running: import into the target, test the connections, assert parity, run nothing. (3) Gated execute: run the promoted tasks, re-check parity, log the promotion, and exit non-zero on drift; keep rollback scoped to the target assets. Inside one org, org-scoped objects (catalog configuration, glossary, DQ rules, MDM model, roles) are shared by construction and only runtime-bound objects drift.
evidence: plan mode exit 0 with the one expected delta (2026-07-04)

title: One org with two runtime environments before production; split production into its own org at a trigger
text: Two runtime environments in one org share one control plane, login and catalog, which is fine before production. Move production to its own org when real customer or financial data arrives at volume, a compliance review needs it, or billing must be separated; the split follows the org-to-org runbook (new org, agent, connections, promotion by cross-org export and import, then remove the production runtime from the shared org). Keep an environment manifest and a parity script as the source of truth.
evidence: isolation audit 9/9 checks and a green parity script (2026-07-06)

title: A tag-scoped export misses untagged objects: cross-check folders and references
text: Objects created in a UI or by another tool may never have been tagged (for example an MCP_SERVER and a TOOL_CONNECTION with no dependency links). Cross-check the tag scope against the folder paths and the references graph, and export the stragglers as a second package imported with the main one.
evidence: a read-only cross-check found 2 untagged objects in scope (2026-09-28)

title: Dependency closure through the v3 references API
text: `GET /public/core/v3/objects/<frsGuid>/references?refType=uses&limit=50&skip=<n>` (and `refType=usedBy`) returns `references[]` with `id`, `path` and `documentType`. Walk it for every scoped object (a small thread pool is fine) and report what lies outside the scope: runtime environments, connections, bundle templates and bundle rule specs are dependencies, not scope creep.
evidence: 223 objects referencing 0 missing objects; 25 legitimate outside dependencies (2026-09-28)

title: Inventory an org: page the objects list and snapshot the v2 details
text: Page `GET /public/core/v3/objects?limit=200&skip=<n>` until `skip` reaches `count`, filter client-side (tag, path prefix, a `[<tag>]` description marker), and snapshot the v2 lists (`/api/v2/connection`, `runtimeEnvironment`, `agent`, `schedule`, `mttask`, `workflow`, `mapping`) plus every mapping-task and workflow detail, because the lists hide `scheduleId` and `frsGuid`. Save the raw JSON for diffs and id maps.
evidence: full inventories of two orgs (2026-09-28)

title: Build the source-to-target id map right after the import
text: For every migrated object record type, path, source v3 id, target v3 id (read from the target's objects list in the destination folder), source v2 id (the package's `repoInfo.repoHandle`) and target v2 id (found by name only among the objects this import created, for example by create time and folder, because the same names can exist elsewhere). Add the dependencies matched by name (connections, runtime environments, folders). Every caller flip, checklist and cleanup reads this one file.
evidence: a flip tool remapped 138 name/id pairs with 0 mismatches against the map (2026-09-28)

title: After a migration, address objects by id: the target may hold same-named objects
text: A target org that already holds content can contain objects with the same names in other folders (15 task names collided in one migration). Import into a dedicated project, never overwrite unrelated objects, check which legacy agents are still alive before installing a new one, and make every tool and caller use ids from the id map, never names.
evidence: name collisions found after the import (2026-09-28)

title: Imported tasks bind to the target's own copy of a bundle template
text: Tasks built on an Add-On Bundle template reuse the target's installed copy, which can be a different build. One task failed once with 'Cannot propagate link rule of type TmplPatternRuleImpl between Expression and IUpdateStrategyNode5' and passed on a plain rerun. Validate each migrated task once and rerun before debugging.
evidence: one transient failure, OK on rerun (2026-09-28)

title: A TOOL_CONNECTION (MCP tool connection) does not import: recreate it in the designer
text: The migration service rejected an MCP tool connection with `MigrationSvc_031` 'Internal error' in three jobs, even after the package was fixed with the live URL and a bearer token (the export had carried `token:null`). Recreate it in the Application Integration designer (MCP connection form) and attach it to its MCP server; the MCP_SERVER object itself imported.
evidence: three failed import jobs (2026-09-28)

title: CAI public URLs embed the pod and org id, so every caller changes at cutover
text: Anonymous CAI endpoints look like `https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/public/rt/<orgIdV3>/<process>`. Make the base URL an environment variable in every caller (a code default pointing at the old org is a trap), switch it in a separate step with one verified call, and keep the old value as the rollback. The target org needs its `CAI_Anonymous_<orgIdV3>` user.
evidence: a real call through the new base URL answered in 343 ms (2026-09-28)

title: Scan every host for consumers of the source org before repointing
text: Walk the app and tooling trees, cron tables, systemd units and env files, and classify each hit: hosts (login domain, pod, `-cai`, `-ing`, `-dqprofile`, `idmc-api`, `cdgc-api`, MCP hosts), org ids of both shapes, v2 ids (they start with the source org's v2 id), v3 22-character ids, credential file references, helper imports, id files and CAI URLs. The result is the switch list, including consumers nobody remembered; flip runtime consumers and list design-time builders separately.
evidence: the scan's plan dry runs caught 3 unmapped schedule ids before GO (2026-09-28)

title: Repoint callers with a flip tool: remap by id, block unmapped ids, back up, write in place
text: Offer `status | plan | apply --group <g> --execute | rollback --backup <ts> --execute`. Remap v2 ids by the source org prefix and v3 ids from the id map, never by name; swap host literals most specific first; refuse any file that would keep an unmapped source id; render a whole group first (all-or-nothing), back each file up with an UNDO log and a manifest, and write in place (same inode, because bind-mounted files keep the old inode otherwise). Comment out crons whose target side is not ready, rebuild and recreate services at an idle moment, verify (org id, agent, services), and read secrets from 0600 files at apply time without printing them.
evidence: verify passed per group; smoke 7/7 (2026-09-28)

title: Make the source org read-only in the migration library
text: In the shared migration client, raise on any non-GET call to the source org unless an explicit override is set (export POSTs are allowed), log in once per org per session with no retry loop, take the base URL from `baseApiUrl`, and never print secrets. A migration then cannot write to the source by accident.
evidence: the source stayed unchanged through inventory and export (2026-09-28)

title: Run an org-to-org migration with one lead, lanes, and one IDMC writer per org
text: One lead owns the plan and is the only session that logs in to either org and the only importer; lanes take host work (agent, drivers, slot preparation) without IDMC logins, caller repoint preparation (read-only until GO), read-only QA and checklists, and target cleanup. Lanes claim work with leases, post heartbeats and DONE with evidence, and the lead announces every import and risky step. Failed logins from several sessions once locked a target account; after the reset, one designated session made one attempt with confirmed credentials.
evidence: cutover completed with rollback kept and no second lockout (2026-09-28)

title: The org-to-org milestones, M0 to M13
text: M0 access and identity; M1 read-only inventory, closure and export; M2 target agent, runtime environment and services; M3 connections and secrets; M4 import with REUSE, package fixes, re-tag and id map; M5 CAI publish; M6 DBMI CDC tasks deployed but not started; M7 DQ rebind; M8 CDGC and glossary; M9 caller repoint prepared; M10 validation run per lane plus parity; M11 gated cutover; M12 soak and rotations; M13 cleanup of the target's legacy content. Each milestone has a lease, evidence and an undo. Supersedes L-MIG-069.
evidence: executed in about 10.5 hours (2026-09-28 15:15Z to 2026-09-29 01:50Z)

title: Validate every lane in the target before the cutover, with exact counts
text: Run each lane once in the target, announced, with the matching source schedule paused for that window. Compare per table the run's applied rows, the warehouse COUNT(*) and the source count as of the task's read time (so live inserts do not create false deltas); compare marts with the baseline and explain every delta; run the smoke checks and end-to-end stories and classify each failure as migration regression or unrelated change. Imported tasks keep their original targets, so a validation run may write production tables unless retargeted first.
evidence: landing 14/14 exact; marts 25/30 identical plus 5 explained; stories 8/9 (the miss was an app change); a 62-task taskflow ran 21.6 min vs 24.5 min in the source (2026-09-28)

title: Cutover sequence: snapshot, unbind the source, flip callers, switch CDC, bind the target, verify
text: On the owner's GO: (1) snapshot every source workflow binding and body, once (the rollback baseline); (2) unbind the source schedules (`POST /api/v2/workflow/<id>` with `scheduleId:null`) and read back; (3) flip the callers in groups; (4) stop the source CDC job and start the target job; (5) bind the target schedules, created unbound beforehand; (6) watch the first scheduled target runs; (7) scan every task detail in both orgs for task-level schedules.
evidence: cutover done in 21 minutes with each step read back (2026-09-28)

title: Task-level schedules survive a workflow-only unbind
text: A mapping task can carry its own `scheduleId`, and `GET /api/v2/mttask` (the list) does not return it. At one cutover a task-level binding was missed and the task ran once more in the old org. Scan every task's detail GET for `scheduleId` before and after the cutover, and move those bindings too.
evidence: the missed binding ran once in the old org and was fixed about 40 minutes after the cutover finished (2026-09-28/29)

title: Write the rollback before the cutover, one command per step
text: Rebind the source schedules from the snapshot and unbind the target; stop the new CDC job and resume the old one on the same slot; restore the callers from the flip backup (and rebuild); turn off any new execution flag. Keep the source org's objects, stopped jobs and agent in place through the soak. Rolling back into the source only works while its account exists and is under its monthly job cap, and CDC rollback ends once the old job is undeployed or its slot dropped.
evidence: rollback commands staged in the cutover report (2026-09-28); CDC rollback deliberately closed after a split (2026-09-29)

title: After the cutover, rotate every exposed credential at every touchpoint
text: List each exposed credential (a password pasted in chat, secrets carried by packages) and every place that stores or uses it: helper creds files, service env files, catalog-source scanner credentials, and MCP OAuth clients that store the user's password (recreate those). Change it at the source, update each touchpoint, clear the lockout-guard block, verify with exactly one login, then restart the consumers.
evidence: touchpoint list and rotation script prepared (2026-09-28/29)

title: After a cutover the source org stays as it is; delete only what the owner names
text: Leave the source org's objects, unbound schedules and stopped jobs in place unless the owner names something for deletion; a 'ready to delete' checklist is reference only.
evidence: owner instruction (2026-09-28/29)

title: Pre-migration gates worth running
text: Check host capacity (free RAM after the existing agent, swap, about 25 GB free for a second agent's roughly 20 GB of engines, a listener baseline with `ss -ltnp`, free replication slots, `wal_level`); the target's job limit and entitlements; each plane against a fake-path twin; and the import route (an empty multipart should give 400 MigrationSvc_030). Drive the cutover with a stateful script that stops at each manual step, saves its state, and resumes only with an explicit confirm token after a machine check.
evidence: draft runbook gates (2026-09-28); not all were run because the executed migration went headless

title: Cut a legacy pipeline over to IDMC with a cheap rollback
text: Snapshot the affected warehouse tables into a backup dataset with an expiry (for example 30 days) and export the view DDL; point the scheduler at the IDMC runner; stop the legacy service with a no-restart policy rather than removing it. Rollback = remove the scheduler entry and start the legacy service again. Keep tables that consumers MERGE into as real tables, and verify each downstream consumer after the switch.
evidence: first scheduled run 46/46 SUCCESS with consumers healthy (2026-09-23)

title: Move and copy assets with FRS MoveEntities and CopyEntities; ids are preserved
text: The public v3 API has no move verb. `POST https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/frs/api/v1/MoveEntities` (header `IDS-SESSION-ID: <v2 icSessionId>`) with `{"xferSpec":{"targetLocationId":"<folderId>","sourceSpecArr":[{"sourceEntityId":"<frsGuid>","mergeTags":""}]}}` (batches of 25) returns `value[].statusArr[]` with `resultValue` FRS_200 per item. GUIDs and v2 task ids are preserved, so schedules, taskflows and callers keep working, even during a run. `CopyEntities` takes the same `xferSpec`; profiles cannot be moved (FRS_108).
evidence: 95 assets moved with ids unchanged while a run finished 46/46 (2026-09-24)

title: Before declaring objects gone, search by id, by exact type name and in other users' projects
text: Objects that a scan reported missing were still there: the scan used type `DBMI` (0 results, no error) instead of `DBMI_TASK`, and some clones sat in the project of the user who owned the clone source. Confirm by id with the exact type name and include other projects before concluding that objects were deleted or never created. Supersedes L-MIG-068.
evidence: the objects were found and moved with ids preserved (2026-09-24)

title: A 62-task linear taskflow took about 21 minutes; the same tasks as a DAG at concurrency 4 about 5.5 minutes
text: Per-task overhead is about 20 s regardless of data size, so the lever for a long linear chain is concurrency, and the floor is the longest dependent chain. Record the new baseline in the target during validation. Newer evidence: L-CDI-300.
evidence: timing comparison from a dependency-DAG stage plan (2026-09-29)

title: Crosswalk catalog assets from a retired source to the live one by column-set similarity
text: Score each old table against the live tables by column-set Jaccard similarity, auto-map only above a threshold, list ambiguous candidates by name instead of guessing, and publish the residual that has no counterpart with the reason. This gives an honest floor instead of forced matches.
evidence: attached tables grew from 519 to 592 (2026-07-13)

title: Replace a governance or catalog consumer by coexistence, consumer inventory and sustained parity
text: Keep the old system running, inventory every consumer and whether it reads or writes, add new consumers additively, and repoint each existing reader only after sustained parity (for example two consecutive weeks). Every edit has a backup and fallback stays trivial; decommission only after the full checklist is green.
evidence: checklist method (2026-07-13)

title: Check which IDMC jobs write a dataset before renaming or retiring it
text: Before moving, renaming or deleting a warehouse dataset during a migration, read its IDMC run or audit tables (last write time) and the task and taskflow configurations that target it; naming conventions only hint at the writer.
evidence: dataset inventory before a tier migration (2026-09-07)

title: Retargeting a cloned mapping to another warehouse dialect by translating its SQL is disputed
text: A July record reports 22 mapping clones retargeted to another warehouse by exporting, translating the customQuery SQL (backticks to [schema].[table], IFNULL to ISNULL, SAFE_DIVIDE to *1.0/NULLIF) and re-importing; other July records say the mapping-task retarget silently reverted and that dialect retarget by package edit was impossible. The proven levers are a connection-GUID swap inside the package (L-MIG-020) and an OVERWRITE re-import of the mapping (L-MIG-030).
evidence: conflicting July records (2026-07-04 to 2026-07-09)

title: Design-object authoring is UI-only because POST /public/core/v3/objects returns 405
text: With the v3 objects POST at 405 and guessed create paths at 404, mappings, rule specs, processes, business entities and ingestion tasks were believed to need a UI author. The migration import writes objects by clone or from a built package. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-08, and again 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-21; overturned by L-MIG-023.
evidence: 405 on v3 objects read as no headless authoring

title: There is no v3 export/import API on this org; promotion is author-time UI
text: A promotion script reported the v3 export and import routes as 404 and planned per-asset UI export plus warehouse re-pointing. The same routes worked for other sessions on the same org; the 404 was a path, host or role problem. Was believed 2026-07-04 to 2026-07-08; overturned by L-MIG-023.

title: The migration clone backdoor is closed: import/package returns 404 MigrationSvc_025
text: A probe that sent `application/json` to `/public/core/v3/import/package` concluded the clone route was closed. The route needs `multipart/form-data`; what an empty org lacks is a same-type template, not the route. Was believed 2026-07-26 (one pass); overturned by L-MIG-009.
evidence: 404 MigrationSvc_025 under application/json (2026-07-26)

title: An empty type-filtered census proves the type is unsupported
text: A type-filtered count of 0 from the v3 objects list was used as capability evidence. The filter is not validated: fabricated types return the same empty envelope. Was believed July 2026 to 2026-07-25; overturned by L-MIG-002.
evidence: technique used across the July corpus

title: A mapping's connection and SQL are compiled into a binary blob, so a package edit cannot retarget a mapping
text: In July the DTEMPLATE `bin/@3.bin` entry was read as a compiled binary, direct edits failed with MigrationSvc_031, and clone-retarget of mappings was recorded as impossible ('fails for DTEMPLATE'). Later exports held IMF JSON, a 22-character GUID swap worked, and mappings were synthesized from scratch. Was believed 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-09; overturned by L-MIG-029.
evidence: import failures after binary edits (2026-07-05 to 2026-07-09)

title: The import rejects hand-built packages with MigrationSvc_030; upload only genuine exports
text: A hand-built package was rejected with MigrationSvc_030 in June, and a September draft runbook repeated the rule. Self-built packages import when the metadata, the real folder and project entries and the checksums are right; 030 is what an empty or malformed multipart gets. Was believed 2026-06-28 to 2026-09-28; overturned by L-MIG-022.
evidence: MigrationSvc_030 on a hand-built package (2026-06-28)

title: Anything a migration import creates needs a UI click to deploy or publish
text: The July verdict table said import creates an object but deploying or publishing it is always a UI click. CAI publish (`asset/v1/publish`) and DBMI deploy (`task/deploy` on `<pod>-ing`) are headless follow-ups; MDM model deploy is still UI in these sources. Was believed 2026-07-26 to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-MIG-024.
evidence: 58-headless-verdicts table (2026-07-26)

title: Objects authored headless in a shared org disappear within a day
text: A read-only scan found none of 13 clone-authored objects (9 DBMI tasks, 4 CAI processes) and concluded that authoring in a shared org is not durable. The scan used the wrong type name, and some objects sat in another user's project. Was believed 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-24 03:00Z; overturned by L-MIG-055.
evidence: v3 type scans returned none of the 13 (2026-09-23/24)

title: No cross-org export/import is available; promotion only re-points within one org
text: An early promotion design treated the v3 export and import as a same-org tool (re-point assets between runtime environments) and stated that no cross-org path existed. A full org-to-org migration later ran on the same API. Was believed 2026-07-04; overturned by L-MIG-045.
evidence: early design note (2026-07-04)

title: Export returns the zip synchronously; the /export/jobs and /import/jobs endpoints are the async form
text: One early note said `POST /saas/public/core/v3/export` returned the zip directly and that the job endpoints `/export/jobs` and `/import/jobs` 404 or 400 on some orgs. Export is a job: the POST returns an id, `GET /export/<id>` gives the state and `GET /export/<id>/package` the zip; the `/jobs` paths are not routes. Was believed 2026-07-04; overturned by L-MIG-003.
evidence: early probe notes (2026-07-04)

title: The clone list stops at MDM objects and rule specs; with MI_TASK at 0 there is nothing to clone for ingestion
text: The July skill listed clone proofs only for BUSINESS_ENTITY, MDM_SRC_SYSTEM, reference entities and RULE_SPECIFICATION, and recorded Mass Ingestion as having nothing to clone. DBMI_TASK and CAI PROCESS clones followed in September. Was believed 2026-07-26 to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-MIG-023.
evidence: skill Law 6 and content 18/58 (2026-07-26)

title: Automate the UI only after REST, MCP, cloning and XHR capture are exhausted
text: Order of attempts for an operation that looks UI-only: (1) the REST route on the right host with the right plane header, plus the probe toolkit (bogus twin, empty POST, Content-Type); (2) a managed MCP tool; (3) a clone through a v3 export/import package; (4) capture the UI's own XHR for that click and replay it headless; only then (5) drive the UI with Playwright, or hand one precise click to a human. Many September "UI-only" steps fell at steps 1-4 (service and connector selection, MCP OAuth clients, CAI publish, ingestion deploy, glossary writes, catalog-source create, profile runs, mapping authoring as IMF JSON). Still UI in these sources on 2026-09-29: MDM model publish and deploy, match-merge job creation, CLAIRE classification accept, steward assignment, CAI API activate, CDQ rule logic and console scorecards, CDQ dictionary "Convert to API", catalog-source definition delete (REST only purges), MCP tool-connection import, publishing API-created advanced taskflows, and discovering unknown property names (for example a pushdown setting).
evidence: Capability maps of the September log and the per-operation verdict reference

title: Capture the UI's own API calls to replace a UI step with REST
text: Log in once with a headless browser, open the page, record every XHR and fetch to `*.informaticacloud.com` (method, status, URL, request body with any password field redacted in the capture hook itself, the head of the response), filter the noise (telemetry, translations, icons, i18n, notification polls) and click the control. The captured request is the headless route: replay it with the helper's session. This found the MCP OAuth-client route and the runtime-environment selections route. Never paste captured cookies or Authorization headers into chat; keep only method, URL, body shape and status. The capture also records the identity-service login request, whose body carries the username and password in clear: redact login and password bodies at capture time (not afterwards), keep capture logs out of shared folders and transcripts, and rotate the password if an unredacted log was shared (L-METHOD-087).
evidence: The MCP OAuth-client and service-selection routes proven headless on 2026-09-28 came from this approach; an unredacted login capture found in a harness log (2026-09-29)

title: Log in to the IDMC console with Playwright
text: Open `https://<domain>.informaticacloud.com/identity-service/home`, wait for `input#username` (or `input[name=username]`), fill username and password from environment variables, and submit with `button:has-text("Log In"):not(:has-text("Single"))` (which skips the SSO button) or Enter. Some login pages are two-step (username, Log In, then password, Log In), so wait for the password field before filling it. After login the browser lands on `https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/cloudshell/showProducts`, and SSO carries to every service host. Scripted login works only for a user without MFA.
evidence: Logins scripted from a Windows workstation and from server containers between July and September

title: Stop at the first rejected login, and never auto-login from a probe on a shared account
text: After submitting, if the page is still on the identity service and its text matches `locked|not valid|invalid`, exit with "LOGIN REJECTED - not retrying": UI logins count toward the same lockout as REST logins. A probe that only measures rendering reuses a warm storage state read-only, never logs in by itself, aborts if it is bounced to the login page, and does not write the state back, so it cannot clobber a session that other runs depend on.
evidence: UI harnesses ran through a migration without causing a lockout

title: Reuse a saved storage state inside the session window; refresh it before each batch
text: Save `storage_state` after one login and reuse it (every login counts toward the lockout), but the console session lives about 30 minutes (JWT iat to exp about 1800 s): a stale state makes deep links redirect and grids render empty. Refresh the state with one explicit login command before each batch, and log in fresh when a run will outlast the window.
evidence: Empty grids with a reused stale state; batches ran cleanly after a login refresh

title: Storage-state files and browser profiles are credentials
text: A Playwright storage state holds the console's cookies, including session JWTs (one held 46 cookies), and a persistent browser profile cache can hold live session cookies too. Treat both as secrets: keep them out of repositories, shared folders and the script's own directory, give them 0600, sequester or delete stale ones (Playwright regenerates a profile), and never paste their contents.
evidence: State files and a profile cache were flagged and sequestered in a KB inventory

title: IDMC single-page-app quirks that break naive automation
text: Deep links such as `/explore/<id>` render empty on a cold load: navigate (Explore, All Projects, click) to hydrate. Heavy authenticated pages may never fire `load`: use `wait_until="commit"` or `"domcontentloaded"` plus `wait_for_url` and a specific element wait. A service-switcher modal intercepts clicks until closed (`button[aria-label=Close]` or Escape). Apps are embedded in frames: search every frame (`page.frames`) for controls and pick the right one by URL (the CAI shell frame's URL contains `bpmui-cai-app`). Grid rows are `role=row`, with a kebab menu that appears only on hover; react-select options match `[class*='-option']` (a `role=option` belongs to a background grid, and Escape closes the modal). Nested SPAs (the CAI designer under `/aiUI/`, Data Marketplace) rendered blank headless with a saved state: use a fresh login and a headed browser under `xvfb-run`.
evidence: Each quirk reproduced and worked around by the July UI drivers

title: Driving the mapping designer: CodeMirror, long queries, stuck spinners, target re-derive
text: Set expression or query text by calling the CodeMirror instance (`cm.setValue(<text>)` then `cm.save()`), then click the dialog's dynamically enabled OK; never press Escape before the commit (it discards the edit); call `scrollIntoView` on fields below the fold. Typing hundreds of lines with `press_sequentially` exceeds its 60 s default: use `delay=1, timeout=300000` and poll for OK to enable. A very large custom query (about 6 KB or more) can hang the field-derive spinner on a new mapping (the URL never becomes a GUID and Save is a no-op): list `DTEMPLATE` objects over v3 REST, open the auto-persisted `MappingN` by GUID and continue; capture the GUID from the URL right after the first save. After adding upstream ports, rename a create-at-runtime target (set the value with the native input setter and answer Continue) to force the designer to re-derive the target fields.
evidence: Mappings stayed Valid; a target went from 16 to 21 mapped fields; runs produced engine-changed rows

title: UI authoring is slow and must be serial
text: Authoring one CDI mapping plus its task through the designer with a Playwright subagent took about 30-75 minutes, rising with query size; parallel authoring sessions collided on shared storage-state files and on the same scratch target. Author serially, one object per browser session, and prefer a headless import path whenever one exists.
evidence: Per-object durations across 16 authored objects

title: UI receipts: the verbatim confirmation plus a REST read-back
text: For a UI-only operation a screenshot proves a click, not a commit. Record the console's confirmation text verbatim (it also identifies which dialog ran), the UI path, the REST call it substitutes for, and a REST read that verifies the change; for agent services the receipt was "Changes successful. The selected components are enabled for the runtime environment, and all unselected components are disabled for the runtime environment.", verified with `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>`. Receipts are captured by a user or by automation, never invented; capture failure strings too, because failure toasts and silent no-ops look alike in a screenshot. A confirmation is not completion: engines sat in DEPLOYING for 20-45 minutes or more while packages downloaded, so re-read before concluding that the action failed.
evidence: First receipt captured, with the engine count growing from 1 to 23 on read-back

title: Behind a transparent enterprise proxy, IDMC SPAs render blank under automation
text: From a laptop behind a transparent TLS proxy with CGNAT addressing, login and the launchpad rendered but every heavy IDMC micro-frontend (Data Profiling, Administrator) painted nothing, because its bootstrap requests failed (a worker script 404, a CORS block on the `hdm` host, a DNS failure on another service host, a 503 from a UI service). Headless, headful, `--disable-web-security` and a real Edge channel on a warm session all failed: a fresh automation profile does not get the proxy's enterprise network treatment, whatever the browser engine. Chromium flags that disable Private/Local Network Access checks (for proxies that resolve vendor hosts to 100.64/10 addresses) had helped earlier but were not sufficient. Run UI automation from a host outside the proxy (a cloud VM), or hand the click to the user's own browser. Disputed 2026-10-06 by L-UI-031: with the Local Network Access checks also disabled, the catalog, MCC and the mapping designer worked headless from such a proxy.
evidence: A DOM body of 2 nodes and 0 text across 5 configurations; about 130-160 MB of egress spent proving it

title: Detect a blank or logged-out page mechanically
text: Measure what the SPA painted instead of trusting a screenshot: in each frame count DOM elements, visible text length, buttons and inputs (`document.body.getElementsByTagName('*').length`, `innerText.length`); a body of 2 nodes and 0 text is blank. Byte-identical screenshot sizes across different pages mean you are photographing the login page (for example with a tool that ignores HTTP Basic credentials in the browser).
evidence: Blank DOM measured on 5 configurations; identical screenshots before a login fix

title: Run Playwright on a server in the official container
text: Use `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:<ver>-jammy` with `pip install playwright==<same ver>` inside it and `-e PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright`, run it with `--network host`, and mount an output folder for screenshots, page text and XHR logs; the Node image (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:<ver>-jammy`) runs JS suites on hosts without Node. Launch Chromium with `--no-sandbox` in the container. Map vhost names with `--add-host` so the browser can resolve them, and build a throwaway image from a temporary copy to preview changes safely.
evidence: Screenshot rigs and UI walks ran from server containers; a browser suite ran on a VM without Node for the first time

title: Screenshots and page text as evidence, one per step
text: For each capability that must be shown in the IDMC UI, write acceptance criteria, walk it headless from a server, and save a full-page screenshot plus the page text per step (`page.screenshot(full_page=True)`, `page.inner_text("body")`), with the login state kept in a file refreshed by a login command. Pass free-text inputs (for example chat prompts) through a JSON file, because shell wrappers split arguments on spaces. Save objects that the UI flags as "unsaved changes" before a demo.
evidence: Six capabilities verified by walks with per-step screenshots

title: Drive CLAIRE GPT with a browser harness
text: A harness on a server logs in, submits prompts from a JSON file, waits while the page shows busy text and auto-clicks "proceed". Match the busy text including its trailing dots (for example "Analyzing concepts...") or the harness exits early; allow 50-110 s per answer; start a new conversation per prompt; avoid `@` in prompts (it opens the mention picker and the prompt is never sent); refresh the saved login before a batch. Answers are nondeterministic, so pin the good conversations before a demo.
evidence: About 70 recorded runs

title: An IDMC UI click path for a capability walk
text: Agent: Administrator > Runtime Environments > <RE> > agent detail (services Up and Running). CDI: Data Integration > Explore > <project> > <folder>, open a mapping task, Run, then Monitor > Running Jobs; Operational Insights > Data Integration for 24-hour volumes. CAI: Explore > process opens the Process Designer; Operational Insights > Application Integration for completed and faulted counts. Profiling: open the profile (results, Rules tab). Catalog: Metadata Command Center > Explore > Catalog Sources; Data Governance and Catalog search (use Keyword search if AI search returns 0), asset tabs Contains, Lineage, Data Profiling, Relationships, Data Quality. Glossary: column > description, glossary and classification; term > Relationships; domain > terms.
evidence: An 8-10 minute walk validated with screenshots

title: Create Data Profiling profiles through the UI when you must
text: Reuse a saved login state, create one profile per browser session (it avoids cascading failures), select all columns with the header checkbox and verify through the page text, and expect the Location picker to be flaky (profiles may land in Default). Since 2026-09-28 profiles can be created and run over REST on the `<pod>-dqprofile` host, so prefer that path.
evidence: Six profiles created

title: Other IDMC surfaces: Marketplace delivery templates, MDM apps, Customer 360 search
text: Data Marketplace delivery templates (every REST verb 405 in July): the app at `https://cdmp-app.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/` stalls headless, so run headed; in Setup > Delivery the dropdowns are react-select and field rows carry `data-testid='field_deliveryType|deliveryFormatIds|deliveryMethodIds'` with text inputs `data-testid='TEXT'`. MDM app URLs: Business 360 Console `https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ui-config-app`, Customer 360 `/ui-x360-app/app/c360/`, Multidomain `/ui-x360-app/app/mde`, Reference 360 `/rdm-ui/`; the Data Integration designer is `https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/diUI/products/integrationDesign/main`. Customer 360 search: entity dropdown `div[data-testid='mdm-bui-search-dropdown']` then `button[data-testid='dropdown-button']`, current entity `span#selected-entity`, query box `input[aria-label='Search input']`.
evidence: A template created and an order fulfilled; the selectors drove a search to its results page

title: SaaS setup steps with no API: a frontdoor session plus Playwright, verified by API
text: For CRM setup steps that have no REST API (for example activating a data stream or renaming an identity-resolution ruleset in Salesforce), open an authenticated session with `sf org open --url-only` (a frontdoor URL), drive the page with Playwright, then verify through SOQL or the Metadata API.
evidence: Stream status ACTIVE and ruleset PUBLISHED on read-back

title: Verify dashboards in a real browser, and log in through the form
text: Passing HTTP Basic credentials to Playwright does not log in to some BI tools (the screenshots then capture the login page): fill the login form. API-only dashboard checks can pass while the panel throws in the browser (for example a target missing `url_options`), and re-issuing a simplified query can return 0 rows while the panel is fine: verify against the exact feed a panel reads and with a real-browser render. Drive end-to-end stories through every channel's real UI (web, mobile web, self-service terminals, staff consoles) before trusting downstream IDMC counts: an API-driven check passed while one channel had no screen for a step at all, so records that should have fed the pipeline were never created from it. Keep slow verification reads (warehouse or database queries of 20-80 s) out of timed UI flows: screens with idle resets (45 s, 3 min) time out the next click, so verify at the end of the story.
evidence: Byte-identical screenshots before the fix; browser errors that a 200 API check had missed; an API check green while a UI gap existed, and 176 of 176 per-channel UI stories passed after the fix (2026-10-01/02)

title: Playwright can author real IDMC design objects
text: The belief that the first mapping of a new source/target pair must be hand-authored fell when a Playwright session authored a PostgreSQL-to-warehouse mapping in the designer and its session log showed rows written (2026-07-07); by 2026-08-19 sixteen mappings with their tasks had been authored through the designer by automation, and profiles were created through the UI on 2026-09-03. Once such a seed exists, variants can be cloned headlessly; by 2026-09-29 mappings could also be built as IMF JSON and imported with no UI at all.
evidence: Session-log rows written; 16 of 16 objects authored and run

title: Playwright is a screenshot tool for IDMC, not an automation path
text: A July review counted 102 Playwright-on-IDMC scripts, found none documenting a successful mutating action, and rated every browser-dependent capability as a human click. Designer authoring by automation (08-19) and UI-created profiles (09-03) contradicted it; the lasting part is that UI automation is slow, fragile and a last resort. Was believed 2026-07-10; overturned by L-UI-021.
evidence: 102 scripts reviewed in July

title: The first mapping of a new source/target pair can only be authored by hand
text: Clone authoring could not change a mapping's connector types, so the first mapping for each new source/target pair was believed to need a human in the designer. A Playwright session authored one on 2026-07-07, and IMF JSON import removed the UI step entirely by 2026-09-29. Was believed to 2026-07-06; overturned by L-UI-021.
evidence: Clone limits recorded in July

title: Log in fresh in each script
text: Because the console session is short, early runbooks logged in at the start of every script. Login volume counts toward the account lockout, so the later rule is to reuse one saved state within the session window and refresh it with a single login before each batch. Was believed 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-08; overturned by L-UI-005.
evidence: July runbooks

title: Enabling agent services and connectors needs the Administrator UI (a UI bot)
text: A UI bot was built to enable Data Integration and connectors on an agent because no REST verb was known and the REST attempts gave router artifacts. A managed MCP tool did it on 2026-09-23 and a REST PUT on the runtime-environment selections did it on 2026-09-28, found by capturing the UI's own call. Was believed 2026-07 to 2026-09-22; overturned by L-UI-001, L-UI-002.
evidence: July and August bootstrap notes; the UI bot's stated goal

title: CAI publish has to be driven through the designer UI
text: In early July a Playwright driver published CAI processes through the designer (close the service-switcher modal, find the shell frame, click the exact Publish button, check publication status over REST first, run headed under xvfb). REST publish on the `<pod>-cai` host (`/active-bpel/asset/v1/publish`) replaced it from 2026-07-25 and was reconfirmed in September. Was believed 2026-07-08 to 2026-07-24; overturned by L-UI-001.
evidence: July UI publish driver

title: Chromium flags that disable Private Network Access are enough to automate the console behind the proxy
text: A UI bot on a proxied laptop launched Chromium with Private/Local Network Access checks disabled (the proxy resolved vendor hosts to CGNAT addresses) and produced screenshots from mid-August to mid-September. On 2026-09-20 the heavy SPAs rendered blank under every automation configuration, flags included; UI automation moved to a cloud VM. Was believed 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-13; overturned by L-UI-011.
evidence: UI bot screenshots from 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-13

title: A Process Server that restart-loops on a missing ae.keystore lost its database port to another Postgres
text:
Every Process Server version ships `localhost:5432/activevos` hardcoded in `bin/*.sh` and `conf/Catalina/*/process-engine.xml`. If another Postgres already owns 5432 on the host, the deploy script's Liquibase update reaches the wrong server (FATAL password authentication failed for the Process Server DB user), prints 'Process Server update failed', and exits before `configureCerts.sh` copies `ae.keystore`, `crypto.properties` and `tomcat-users.xml` into `/apps/process-engine/conf`. Tomcat then fails its HTTPS connector ('Error creating SSLContext ... conf/ae.keystore (No such file or directory)'), port 7443 never opens, the status check against `https://localhost:7443/process-engine/status` is refused, and the service restarts every ~2 min. Fix as the agent user: change 5432 to a free port in those files and add `port =

` plus `listen_addresses = 'localhost'` to every `data/*/user.conf`. Then run `.lcm/stop-wrapper.sh` followed immediately by `.lcm/deploy-wrapper.sh` from the version directory; its pre-check refuses while the running Tomcat still holds shutdown port 7005. Expect 'Deployment completed successfully', the conf files present, and the service RUNNING. A package re-extract restores 5432, and a running `deploy.sh` keeps reading its old inode, so a 10-minute root cron must re-patch the files and re-run stop plus deploy when the newest deploy result in `logs/scripts.log` is a failure.
evidence: Deploy completed and service RUNNING after the port move (2026-09-30); the same race broke another agent's Process Server on a same-version redeploy (2026-09-29)

title: Only one Process Server per host: the web ports are static
text: Two agents on one host can each move their Process Server's embedded Postgres to its own port (L-AGENT-089), but 7005 (shutdown), 7080 and 7443 are static. Whichever Process Server starts first owns them, and the other stays in ERROR. Pick the agent whose org runs the CAI processes, and leave the other one's Process Server down or deselected. This refines L-AGENT-016: a second agent can run the Process Server when the first one's is off. The Cloud Integration Hub processor binds a static API port too (`server.api.port=19443`): a second agent with CIH selected restart-loops (11 restarts seen, log 'The Tomcat connector configured to listen on port 19443 failed to start'). As the agent user set a free port (for example 19447) in `<agent_home>/apps/CIHProcessor/<version>/conf/application.properties`, restart the service, and re-apply it from the same root cron guard that re-applies the Process Server ports, because an upgrade re-extracts the package with the default.
evidence: Target Process Server holding 7005/7080 while the other agent's stayed in ERROR (2026-09-30); a CIH restart loop on port 19443 cleared by moving the port, with no restart for the rest of the soak (11 samples) (2026-09-30)

title: Data Access Management Agent/Proxy hang at 'Initializing TMS and CMS configuration services' when the org has no DAM configuration
text: When the Data Access Management services are selected in an org with no Cloud Data Access Management setup or entitlement behind them, each JVM starts cleanly (Tomcat up on a loopback port, 'Application status set to running'). Its last log line is always 'Initializing TMS and CMS configuration services'. About 3.5 min later the launcher exits with code 133 and the agent restarts it, indefinitely. The license read shows no Data Access Management entry. Vendor-hosted agents in such an org loop the same way, so ports, memory and host patches do not fix it. Either set up Data Access Management in the org (UI), or accept 'Not All Services Running' (see the deselect lesson in this file). Monitors should exclude these two services instead of alerting.
evidence: Loop on two customer-managed agents and one vendor-hosted agent; license read without a DAM entry (2026-09-30)

title: Parse the keyword from consoleAgentManager getStatus, not its last line
text: `./consoleAgentManager.sh getStatus` prints the status keyword on the first line (`READY`, or `NOT_ALL_SERVICES_ARE_RUNNING_OR_STOPPED`), then a 'Detail:' block with counts (Running, Restart, Deploying ...) and a trailing blank line. A monitor that takes `tail -1` reads an empty string and raises a false alert. Take the first line that matches `^[A-Z_]+$`, and read the `Restart` count when you need to tolerate a known-looping service.
evidence: False alert every 15 min fixed by parsing the keyword (2026-09-30)

title: A 17-service agent needs about 11-12 GB and hits a 12 GB cgroup high mark
text: With 17 services selected (CDI, CDC, catalog metadata, Process Server, B2B, CIH, file, streaming, DAM ...), one agent's systemd unit held about 11.2 GB, and `memory.events high` climbed steadily under a 12 GB `MemoryHigh`, which throttles job JVMs. Raise the unit's MemoryHigh/MemoryMax (for example to 14 GB/16 GB) only when the host still has at least 9 GB available, and re-check swap afterwards.
evidence: memory.current 11,324 MB and rising high events at MemoryHigh 12 GB (2026-09-30)

title: CLAIRE GPT creates, tests and publishes a DQ rule: the plan buttons only fill the input, so press Send
text: A prompt such as 'Create a data quality rule that checks that the `<column>` column in the `<warehouse>` table `<table>` is a valid `<format>`' finds the asset, drafts a rule specification (name, dimension, field, logic) and shows a 7-step plan. Clicking 'Yes, proceed with the plan' only puts that text in the message box: press Send (or Enter), or nothing happens. That is why automated runs saw 'nothing after proceed'. After Send it generates the dictionaries and script plus test data, tests the rule (for example '100.0% Rules Generated'), and asks 'Publish Rules / Don't Publish Rules'. Publish (again plus Send) creates a CDQ rule specification in the CLAIRE project and folder in about 4 minutes end to end, visible in `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='RULE_SPECIFICATION'`. A rule that already exists runs all 7 steps and ends with '0 new DQ rules ... duplicate', so demo with a rule that is not yet published. Publishing does not run the rule; that still takes a DQ task or mapping. This overturns the 'rule recommend/generate after proceed' failure listed in L-MCP-058.
evidence: Duplicate case, generate-and-test without publish, and full publish with the new asset read back over REST (2026-09-30)

title: v2 schedule update: interval is the unit, frequency is the number
text: On `POST /api/v2/schedule/<id>`, `interval` takes the unit ('Minutely', 'Hourly', 'Daily', 'Weekly', 'Monthly') and `frequency` the repeat count (for example `Hourly` + 6 = every 6 hours). Swapping them returns 403 `UI_10622` 'Interval is not valid', and a string frequency returns 400. Send the full object you read (drop create/update stamps), then read it back. Tasks keep their bindings.
evidence: 403 UI_10622 when swapped, then 200 with read-back for three schedules (2026-09-30)

title: A dataset of views looks unscanned if you count only Table assets
text: BigQuery (and other warehouse) views are cataloged as `com.infa.odin.models.relational.View`, not `...relational.Table`. A search filtered to the Table class returned 0 assets for a dataset that held only views, which read as 'the dataset was never scanned'. Include both classes (`should` on Table and View) before concluding an asset is missing from the catalog.
evidence: Search on the Table class: 0 assets for a 44-view dataset; Table+View: all 44 views present

title: Lineage Discovery on an IICS catalog source generates and auto-accepts connection assignments in the scan
text: A run of `POST /data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id>` with `capabilityNames: ['Metadata Extraction', 'Lineage Discovery']` on an IICS (Data Integration) source reports task steps Candidate Selection, Recommendations Generation and Auto Accept Recommendations, each COMPLETED. Connection assignment for the referenced endpoints is then done server-side, with no MCC 'Configure > Lineage' click. Poll `observable/v1/jobs/<jobId>?expandChildren=TASK-HIERARCHY` to see the steps. Recommendations that do not auto-accept still need the MCC page.
evidence: Job task hierarchy with the three steps COMPLETED (2026-09-30)

title: Renaming a catalog source is headless, but name-based filters on other sources must be renamed with it
