text: GET the source, change `name`, PUT it back as multipart (`dataSource` part) to `ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>`: 200, the id is unchanged and the read-back shows the new name. An IICS source's Lineage Discovery filter of type 'Catalog Source Name' stores the other sources by NAME, so update that filter in the same change or lineage stitching silently loses them. Also update local name-to-id maps and scripts that key by name.
evidence: 3 renames PUT 200 with read-back; the lineage filter values rewritten and read back (2026-09-30)

title: A Salesforce catalog source on the native Salesforce connection type does scan
text: The same Salesforce catalog source, bound to the same native `Salesforce` connection by its v2 id, scanned (Metadata Extraction: test connection COMPLETED, extraction PARTIAL_COMPLETED, ingestion COMPLETED) and cataloged every standard and custom object (`*__c`) with their fields. The earlier 'no permissions to access connections which are selected' refusal was therefore not a connection-type wall; its cause was not isolated (candidates: the metadata services were not selected on the runtime environment, or a connection permission since granted). Retry the scan with the metadata services selected before building a new connection.
evidence: Scan job ingested ~650 objects incl. custom objects (2026-09-30); refusal of 2026-09-29 on the same source

title: The AI Agent Engineering 'New...' dialog shows exactly which agent asset types the org is entitled to
text: Open AI Agent Engineering and click 'New...'. An org entitled to agents lists agent, tool and MCP tool asset types; an org that lists only 'Composite MCP Server' cannot create a tool connection (TOOL_CONNECTION) or an agent, and importing a TOOL_CONNECTION from another org fails with 'Internal error'. Corroborate on the agent: no `AIAgentRuntime` engine, and 'AI Agent Engineering' absent from the runtime-environment selection list. In that org the `a2e-flow-mgmt-svc` answered an empty 503 on every path, a bogus twin included, so its REST probes prove nothing. The managed MCP registry and OAuth clients (`a2e-mcp-asset-mgmt-svc`) still work there. It is not a UI step and not a simple licence toggle: the vendor is sunsetting the AI Agent Engineering builder (vendor KB, May 2026), and external MCP tool connections remain only in private-preview orgs. Plan around it: point external agents at a self-hosted MCP gateway that fronts the managed servers.
evidence: Playwright read of the dialog; engine and selection diff against an entitled org; 503 on real and bogus paths (2026-09-30)

title: Prove an entitlement gap between two orgs with an engine diff and a selection-list diff
text: For each org read `GET /api/v2/agent/details/<agentId>` and list `agentEngines[].agentEngineStatus.appname` + status, then `GET <pod>/runtime/api/v2/runtimeEnvironment/<reId>/selections/ui` (header IDS-SESSION-ID) and list `services` + `additionalServices` with `enabled`. An engine that one org runs and the other lacks, whose service is not even offered in the other org's selection list, cannot be enabled by any admin in that org: it is a licence ask. Example engines seen missing this way: `IDMC_Data_Gateway_Service` (CLAIRE GPT 'Query the data', L-AGENT-051), `AIAgentRuntime`, `Domain_Management_App`, `DVProcessor`, `PC2CDI_Modernization_App`. The org's licence records (customLicenses / assignedEditions) carry only opaque ids and cannot answer the question.
evidence: Two-org engine and selection diff (2026-09-30)

title: Never clear, prune or move the agent's downloads folder: installed services run from it
text: `<agent_home>/downloads/package-<name>.<n>/` looks like a pile of old installer packages, but it is not a re-fetchable cache: services under `apps/` load jars and run scripts from inside those package folders (agent logs show 'Actual JAR location: .../downloads/package-<x>.<n>/package/lib/...', and scripts such as `status.sh` resolve there), and an older version number can be the one a running service's current appspec pins. Deleting 'all but the newest version per package' put 14 of 20 services into ERROR ('./status.sh: not found', 'No such file or directory'); clearing the folder entirely, or moving 'unreferenced' packages into a hold folder, does the same. Recovery: restart the agent service; agentcore re-checks every appspec, logs 'package is not available', re-downloads the pinned packages and redeploys them (about 10 min to all RUNNING), after which disk usage is back where it was, so nothing is gained. Size the agent volume for package growth up front (about 20 GB after many enablements, L-AGENT-041, L-AGENT-052) and free disk elsewhere (agent and session logs, the systemd journal, Docker build cache, other volumes). This overturns L-AGENT-055.
evidence: Keep-newest prune: 14 of 20 services went to ERROR; one agent restart recovered them in about 10 min; net space saved 0 because every pruned version was still referenced (2026-09-30)

title: A stale AIAgentRuntime gunicorn.pid can kill agentcore after a host reboot
text: After a reboot, the AI Agent Runtime status script read a gunicorn.pid left from the previous boot, decided its Python process was gone, and its stop script killed that PID's process group. Once the PID number had been reused, that took agentcore down about 40 s after every start. With no agent processes alive (a pre-start hook), every app `.pid` file is stale: move them aside before starting the agent (for example in the systemd ExecStartPre reaper).
evidence: Agent died twice about 40 s after start; clean start once the stale pid file was moved (2026-09-30)

title: A pre-start port guard must count only its own agent user's processes
text: A reaper that refuses to start the agent while ports 7005/14479 are held or any `*.mv.db` is open blocked every start once a second agent on the same host legitimately held 7005 (its Process Server) and its own metadata H2 files. Scope the checks to the agent's OS user and install directory (processes owned by that user, files under its home).
evidence: Every start refused until the checks were scoped to the owning user (2026-09-30)

title: Catalog Data Quality scores need a runtime environment in typeCapabilities; without it Rule Profiling fails in 0 s
text: A catalog source has two config layers. `capabilities[]` holds the run switches (for Data Quality: `Run Rule Occurrence Frequency`, `Data Quality Automation`, `Data Quality Automation Scope`, `Data Quality Run Scope`, `Data Quality Remediation`, `Create Data Quality Failure Ticket`, `Cache Result`; the PUT validator names the mandatory ones). `typeCapabilities[]` holds the filters plus a Scope group (`Data Profiling Scope`, `Data Quality Scope`) that carries `Sampling Type`, `Runtime Environment` and `Text Qualifier`. The type-configuration endpoint `.../type/<type>/capability/<cap>/configuration` describes the typeCapabilities layer, not the capabilities layer. With no Runtime Environment in those Scope groups, a Data Quality run shows Rule Generation COMPLETED and Rule Profiling FAILED within a second, with no error text anywhere in the job API. Add both Scope groups with the runtime environment id (multipart PUT, read back), rerun `capabilityNames: ['Data Quality']`: Rule Profiling, Batch Profiling and Score Propagation then complete (about 15 min for a warehouse source) and the scores become visible to CLAIRE.
evidence: Two runs FAILED in 0-1 s; after adding the Scope groups the run COMPLETED with Score Propagation (2026-09-30)

title: Update a rule specification's description headless: FRS PATCH of description works
text: `PATCH https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/frs/v1/Documents('<frsId>')` with header `IDS-SESSION-ID: <v2 session>` and body `{"description": "<text>"}` returns 204, and a GET of the same Document reads the new description back. Unlike `customAttributes` (L-CLEAN-019), the description really changes. Catalog rule instances copy their read-only TechnicalDescription from the rule specification (TechnicalRuleReference = frsId), so fix the text at the rule specification, then re-run the catalog source's data quality capability so the instances pick it up.
evidence: Six rule specifications updated with 204 and exact read-back (2026-09-30)

title: Catalog DQ rule occurrences are RuleInstance assets: find them by class, delete them with the content API
text: A rule occurrence accepted from a CLAIRE recommendation (or created in the asset's Data Quality tab) is an asset of class `com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.RuleInstance` with external id `DQO-<n>`, name `DQREC_<column>_<dimension>_<rule>` and a `core.location` under the column it scores. Search on `core.classType` lists them (term queries on the name do not). `DELETE /data360/content/v1/assets/<identity>?scheme=internal` returns 201 'Asset ... deleted' and the asset leaves search within seconds; re-run the source's Data Quality capability to re-aggregate the DQResult scores. The DQ score read (`dataQuality` segment) returns only the per-dimension DQResult objects, not the instances.
evidence: 6 RuleInstances deleted, verified absent from search (2026-09-30)

title: A RuleInstance's TechnicalDescription is copied from the rule specification and is read-only in the catalog
text: CLAIRE shows a rule's text from the RuleInstance attribute `com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.TechnicalDescription`. Content PATCH rejects it on every segment (selfAttributes: 'not supported for business assets'; summary accepts only core.name and core.description; customAttributes: invalid). The value comes from the CDQ rule specification whose frsId is in `TechnicalRuleReference`: fix the description there (L-DQ-094). A catalog Data Quality re-run does NOT refresh existing instances (the text is copied once, when the instance is created, proven by two re-runs), so delete and re-create the affected instances (for example, re-accept the recommendation) to show the new text. Specs cloned from another org carry that org's wording into every answer.
evidence: 3 PATCH segments refused with 400 (2026-09-30)

title: Change a copy-data task's SQL logic headless: edit parameters[0].customQuery
text: Mapping tasks built on a copy-data template keep their logic as a custom SQL query in the task itself. `GET /api/v2/mttask/<taskId>`, change only `parameters[0].customQuery`, drop `createTime`/`updateTime`/`createdBy`/`updatedBy`, then `POST /api/v2/mttask/<taskId>` with the full object. It returns 200, and the next run uses the new SQL. Read the query back, keep the GET body as the backup (undo = POST it back), and dry-run the new expression against the warehouse first to count exactly which rows change.
evidence: Two live rule changes, each read back and proven by the next lane run (2026-09-30)

title: Change every live writer of a table, re-import and read back, and refresh the generator's schema before a swap
text: After consolidation, the same table can be written by an old per-table task in one lane and a new multi-target mapping in another. A rule changed in only one of them silently comes back the next time the other runs: a fixed dedupe key was overwritten by the older logic 3 hours later, when the full lane ran. Before changing a transformation rule, list every task or mapping whose targets include the table (the plan's target lists, the lanes and task-level schedules), change them all, then run each lane once and check the output. A spec patch is not a fix: re-import the mapping (OVERWRITE, same GUID), export it again and compare (for example the md5 of the exported IMF) with what you meant to ship. Change the rule in every target of a multi-target mapping too: a cleanse rule changed in only one of two targets made two downstream passes flip a value back and forth. A swap import of a proven mapping into the live project can create a second mapping of the same name beside the scratch copy (another folder and id): create the live mapping task on the live mapping's id, never repoint or reuse the scratch task. Refresh the generator's column list from INFORMATION_SCHEMA immediately before every build and swap, and diff source against target columns, not only rows: a cached schema that predated one column produced a mapping that wrote NULL into it, and parity had passed because the column was absent on both sides (L-CDI-141). If a controller re-creates warehouse views from its own plan after every run, a direct CREATE OR REPLACE is reverted at the next run: change the plan's DDL.
evidence: The old key reappeared after a full-lane run; fixed by patching the second writer (2026-09-30); a NULL key column caught 18 min after a swap and rolled back, a same-name second mapping after a swap import, and a view fix that survived only after the plan DDL changed (2026-09-30 to 2026-10-03)

title: Per-target row counts of a multi-target mapping are in transformationEntries
text: The activity-log entry of a mapping task with several targets reports one `successTargetRows` total, the sum over all targets. Per-table counts are in its sub-entry's `transformationEntries`: entries with `txType` TARGET carry `txName` (the table), `txInstanceName` (the transformation) and `successRows`. An insert target and an update target of the same table appear as `<table>` and `<table>_1`, so merge them by table. Two targets with the same table name in different datasets differ only by instance name, so map those by a naming hint such as Land/Raw/Stg. Log one lineage row per table, not one per task.
evidence: Five- and eleven-target mappings logged per table after the change (2026-09-30)

title: Key-sync deletes in a consolidated mapping can erase history the old tasks kept
text: A generated 'full key sync' pattern (source keys outer-joined to target keys, missing keys deleted) is right for mirrors, but wrong for append-history targets such as posted invoices. A mapping that posts one file at a time would have deleted every row from earlier files. For history targets use insert + update only. Prove it on a scratch copy seeded with the live rows: the count must stay the same and the diff must be 0.
evidence: Caught before go-live: 180 earlier invoices would have been deleted; insert+update kept all 360 (2026-09-30)

title: Generated mappings must carry the BigQuery writer poll interval (default 10 s)
text: The BigQuery V2 writer polls its load job every 10 s by default, adding up to ~9 s per BigQuery target. A mapping that writes 10 BigQuery tables pays it 10 times. Set `jobPollInterval`/`pollInterval` = 1 and the advanced attribute 'Job Poll Interval In Seconds' = 1 on every BigQuery target, and put them in the generator's template so new mappings inherit them. Measured on the same mapping and rows: 127 s → 56 s. A consolidation that forgot them made its lane slower than the tasks it replaced.
evidence: Same scratch mapping 127 s vs 56 s; an earlier task-level change 114 s → 40-69 s (2026-09-29/30)

title: Bulk soft-delete of MDM SaaS records: sourceSystem=c360.default.system
text: `DELETE https://<pod>-mdm.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/business-entity/public/api/v1/entity/<businessEntity>/<id>?sourceSystem=c360.default.system` with headers `IDS-SESSION-ID` and `X-INFA-ORG-ID: <orgIdV3>` returns 200 `{approvalRequired:false}`, and a GET of the record then returns 404. Without the parameter the answer is 400 'Missing required parameter sourceSystem'. For bulk: search the first page (`POST /search/public/api/v1/search`, 500 records), filter by `_meta.creationDate`, delete with about 6 parallel calls, pause for the index, and repeat. About 500 records/min; about 27k records took about 50 min. Deletes are soft (L-MDM-029).
evidence: 26,943 records deleted; search hits 0 afterwards (2026-09-30)

title: A real-time CRM contact is not created when the onboarding decision process returns REVIEW, and the batch sync then holds the record too
text: When a sign-up's onboarding decision process decides REVIEW (for example because the record fails a data-quality rule such as a phone with the wrong number of digits), the real-time process that creates the CRM contact does not run. The batch reverse-ETL that later upserts golden records to the CRM sends only rows whose DQ flag is valid, so the person exists in the warehouse golden table and nowhere in the CRM. This is the DQ gate working, not a sync gap: do not force the write; label such rows 'held by DQ gate' in reconciliation reports, and let a corrected profile flow through the next customers lane.
evidence: 1 sign-up with an 8-digit phone: warehouse golden 1, CRM 0; onboarding decision REVIEW

title: Salesforce org storage full surfaces as HTTP 500 from the real-time process; reverse-ETL windows refill it; deletes free nothing until the Recycle Bin is emptied
text: Every insert fails with STORAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED once a small (5 MB data) Salesforce org is full; a CAI process that upserts the contact returns 500 to its caller, while batch upserts of existing rows keep succeeding (updates need no new storage). Deleted records keep counting until the Recycle Bin is emptied, which REST cannot do (SOAP `emptyRecycleBin` only). The API user can empty (and undelete) ONLY records it deleted itself: records an admin deleted return 'insufficient access rights' on both, so only the admin (or Modify All on the objects) can purge them. A client-credentials OAuth flow runs as the connected app's Run-As user, so it grants nothing extra. Probe headroom with one insert, delete and empty before any test burst, and keep test identities out of the CRM at the source. An org that keeps refilling usually has reverse-ETL tasks that re-upsert every child record of a rolling window (60 days here) on each lane run: they re-create whatever you delete within minutes, so purging and emptying the bin bought only hours (the org filled three times in four days). Fix it at the source: narrow the window in each task's customQuery (60 to 7 days through the v2 mttask GET-edit-POST, L-CDI-196, read back), delete the older rows once with a backup and run `emptyRecycleBin` on exactly those ids, then schedule a daily retention job (delete rows older than the window plus 1 day, empty those ids, run the insert/delete/empty headroom probe, alert on failure). Traps: `queryAll` keeps listing IsDeleted rows after `emptyRecycleBin`, and an INVALID_ID_FIELD on them means they are already purged and free nothing, so IsDeleted counts are not reclaimable space; storage accounting lags about a minute after a purge, so trust a one-row insert probe over counts (the sync user may not be able to read the org's storage figure at all); after a purge child records can lose their parent lookup, so select bin rows to empty with `IsDeleted = true AND SystemModstamp > <purge time>`. Metrics that need more history than the CRM keeps read 0 there: compute them in the warehouse. A lane controller that fails a whole lane on a Salesforce WARNING marks lanes FAILED although the warehouse targets landed: classify CRM-only warnings separately (L-CDI-205). A minimum-access API profile does not see `DataStorageMB` in `/limits`, so the one-row probe is its only headroom reading.
evidence: insert probe 201 + delete 204 + emptyRecycleBin true; 51 admin-deleted records refused; client-credentials identity = integration user; the org filled three times in four days, traced to three window upserts; after the change 784 older rows deleted and emptied (784/784), about 1,930 of about 2,560 records in use, the probe passed twice and the failing lanes returned to SUCCESS; emptyRecycleBin answered INVALID_ID_FIELD on 70 rows queryAll still listed (2026-09-29 to 2026-10-01); /limits listed no DataStorageMB for the minimum-access API profile (2026-09-29)

title: Attribute spend to the golden customer through the match key, never by the raw email on the transaction
text: Lifetime-value or top-customer lists built by joining payments to customers on the transaction's email undercount everyone whose payments sit under a merged duplicate's email, and drop payments whose source row carries no email at all (reservation payments often reference only the booking). Credit each payment to the customer on its booking, order or subscription first, then map every sign-up email to its golden customer via the same person key the golden table uses, and aggregate by golden id. Two lists computed both ways looked like a 'unique customers vs accounts' definitional difference; it was an attribution bug (one customer: 1,111 vs 1,369).
evidence: top 10 identical to the golden-keyed LTV view after the fix; rows without email 221 to 61

title: New or consolidated mappings reach catalog lineage only after a rescan of the CDI catalog source; cross-system stitching needs endpoint connection assignment
text: After replacing many copy tasks with a few multi-transformation mappings, the catalog (and CLAIRE's lineage answers) keeps describing the old tasks until the Informatica CDI catalog source is rescanned (Metadata Extraction + Lineage Discovery). Even then the source-database to mapping to warehouse graph is not stitched until the endpoint connections are assigned to the catalog's database resources; mapping-level assets exist while the end-to-end graph does not. Plan the rescan and assignment before telling a lineage story. Newer evidence: L-CDGC-237.
evidence: rescan job completed: 11 consolidated + 2 showcase mappings listed; stitched graph pending connection assignment

title: A pipeline speed switch under a job cap: economy by default, a timed fast mode, one source of truth, mirrored knobs, synthetic load decoupled
text: An org capped at a fixed number of jobs per month cannot run its pipeline, or a synthetic-load generator (simulated activity that feeds it), at full cadence all month: one two-hour fast window was about 280 jobs. Put one mode switch on the orchestrator that starts IDMC jobs (`GET/POST /mode?mode=<id>&hours=<n>`), persisted to a state file, with the hard job-cap breaker winning in every mode; a small mode service mirrors it every 30 s into a file and an internal endpoint that every non-IDMC knob reads (feeds, BI refresh loops), so every switch path moves every knob, and an unknown or unreadable mode is economy. Example values: economy as the default (event-lane gap 60 s, full rebuild once a day, periodic feed every 6 h); fast (gap 0, full rebuild hourly, feed every 15 min), timed 1-8 h with fixed durations only and reverting by itself (3 h worked); CDC and CAI paths are the same in every mode. In fast mode also start lanes for sources that have no change trigger, and retry a critical-path task once on failure (L-CDI-205). Make waits interruptible (re-read the mode every 30 s) so a switch acts within 30-40 s, and let the UI ignore read-backs for about 12 s after a switch (a stale cached read swallowed a second click). Keep any synthetic-load generator off the switch, on its own economy cadence (one action every few hours, with one explicit manual trigger and never on page open): when it followed fast mode it created SaaS records faster than a small target's storage allowed, and simulated records are indistinguishable from real use in BI. A 'request' endpoint that only queues still honours the minimum gap; a force endpoint starts the run directly, keeping only the budget, drain and run-lock guards, and does not reset the gap timer. Label the modes plainly, state the trade-off, and quote the real number: even at gap 0 each change waits for the lane that carries it (85-148 s), so a record reaches the golden table in about 1.5-2 min and a dashboard only after its own refresh; sub-minute freshness everywhere needs CDC or CAI. Treat fast as an optional, explicit action, never a preparation step, and never lengthen the economy gap silently to save jobs when a live moment depends on it.
evidence: Economy interval 2-4 h, the manual trigger primed an action in 0 s and the new record landed about 40 s later (2026-09-30); the switch in production on two consoles for a week: the generator acted about 40 s after a switch, fast reverted by itself, the double-click race was reproduced and fixed, lanes ran 85-148 s in fast mode, and the generator was decoupled after the storage problem (2026-09-30 to 2026-10-01)

title: Tableau: a sheet added to a dashboard by XML needs a window AND a dashboard viewpoint, or publish fails 400011
text: Adding a worksheet to a dashboard by editing the TWB needs three things: the worksheet, a `<window class='worksheet' name=...>` entry, and a `<viewpoint name=...>` inside the dashboard window's viewpoints. Without the viewpoint, REST publish fails in about 4 minutes with 400011 'Dashboard references sheet X which has no visual representation in the workbook'. Worksheet shading defaults to white, so a sheet placed on a coloured band needs `<style-rule element='table'><format attr='background-color' .../>`. On a fixed-size dashboard in one layout-basic container, zone x/y/w/h are in 1/100000 of the dashboard size: split a caption zone by narrowing it and placing the new zone in the freed width; growing the page means raising the size and rescaling every zone's y and h.
evidence: first publish 400011; same file + viewpoints published OK; 5 split zones rendered

title: Tableau: one serial connection check per embedded BigQuery datasource makes big live workbooks slow to open; serve an extract copy
text: Opening any view of a live workbook with dozens of embedded BigQuery datasources runs one `SELECT 1 AS CheckBillableProject` per connection, in series, before the first data query: 34 connections cost about 105 s of a 132 s open, while the data queries took 15 s. Faster SQL or caching cannot fix it. A pruned copy published as an extract opens in about 8 s and keeps working when the OAuth credential expires (views never touch the warehouse); refresh it on new data within the site's backgrounder budget.
evidence: live 132 s vs extract copy 8 s; 37 of 37 datasources extracts

title: Tableau: text that is too wide renders as ####; concurrent publishes 503; a slow publish POST often never returns
text: A KPI tile whose title is wider than its zone renders the whole label as '####' (keep tile titles within the neighbour's length, about 31 characters for a 190 px tile). Two publishes at once on one site can fail with HTTP 503 'upstream connect error' (serialize publishes, including extract rebuilds). A 1.5 MB workbook POST takes 15-20 minutes and often never returns client-side: guard on the workbook's updatedAt before publishing and poll it afterwards. A browser save rewrites the whole TWB in a newer format (relations duplicated, CDATA-wrapped SQL), so compare normalized SQL/zones/text, not bytes.
evidence: #### fixed by a 31-char title; one 503 retried OK; 8 guarded publishes

title: A Google Workspace Cloud session-control policy expires BigQuery OAuth credentials in BI tools every N hours
text: When every BI connection to BigQuery uses one person's Google OAuth credential, a Workspace 'Google Cloud session control' reauthentication policy (for example 16 h) cuts every live dashboard at the same moment, and the same policy lapses the person's gcloud CLI login. Fixes: an admin unticks Require reauthentication, or marks the BI app (and the Cloud SDK) Trusted and exempts trusted apps; otherwise serve extracts so pages survive the cut: a service-account BigQuery credential cannot be attached headless in Tableau Cloud (L-ENV-080), but a host-built extract push needs no BI-side warehouse credential at all (L-ENV-081).
evidence: all BigQuery views failed with 'refresh token expired' ~16 h after each re-add

title: Patch generated queries with a marked wrapper, not by editing strings other patch steps anchor on
text: When a chain of idempotent patch scripts edits the same generated artefact, a later step that rewrites an earlier step's REPLACEMENT text makes the earlier step abort on the next run ('anchor found 0 times'), so a keeper that re-applies the chain raises an alert. Prefer a wrapper that leaves the inner text intact: `/* marker */ select o.* replace (<new expr> as col) from (/*i*/ <original> /*i*/) o`, re-built from the inner text on every run. When a later text edit is unavoidable, teach the earlier step to accept the new text as 'already applied'. A step that must CHANGE text it wrote before needs in-place old-to-new edits; 'exists, so SKIP' never updates. Always prove: the chain on the live artefact gives 0 aborts and output identical to input.
evidence: 2 earlier steps aborted after a text edit; fixed by acceptance markers; wrappers never broke an anchor

title: A remote-exec helper that retries on missing output re-runs non-idempotent commands; background jobs must be detached
text: A helper that runs a command over a tunnel and retries up to three times when it sees no result marker re-ran a whole command that had started a publish build, so the build ran twice. For anything that is not idempotent: call with a single attempt, start long jobs with `setsid nohup ... < /dev/null &` so they never hold the helper's pipe, and read their log in a separate call.
evidence: a duplicate build started 11 s after the first; killed before its publish step

title: `pkill -f <pattern>` in a remote command kills its own shell; a local file named like a stdlib module shadows it
text: A command line that contains the pattern it passes to `pkill -f` (or to a grep feeding kill) matches itself, so the shell dies and the rest of the command never runs, with no output. Kill by PID or with a pattern the command line cannot contain (for example `[w]orker_`). Separately, a helper script saved as `xml.py` in a folder shadows the standard `xml` package for every script run from that folder (ModuleNotFoundError: 'xml' is not a package). A VM reboot clears /tmp, so staged work files there vanish.
evidence: silent empty output twice; 'xml' shadowing reproduced; /tmp empty after a resize reboot

title: Two consumers of one lock with different freshness thresholds: back-date the lock to release only the looser one
text: When a publish lock is honoured by a keeper (blocks if the lock is under 60 min old) and by an extract rebuilder (blocks under 30 min), setting the lock's mtime to 31 minutes ago lets the rebuilder run while the keeper stays blocked. Useful to let a downstream copy follow while the upstream is still being republished. Remove the lock when done.
evidence: rebuilder ran at +10 min with a back-dated lock; keeper logged 'fresh lock' until removal

title: Validate a big dashboard change with a pruned throwaway workbook before the slow main publish
text: Prune the dashboard being changed into its own small workbook, publish it under a '(delete me)' name (about 4 minutes), render it headless, then publish the main workbook (15-20 minutes) and delete the throwaway. A publish error or a layout problem shows up in minutes instead of after a full cycle. To audit every tab of a slow workbook, open it once and switch tabs with the Embedding API (`workbook.activateSheetAsync`): one cold start instead of one per tab.
evidence: 400011 caught by the throwaway; 19 tabs audited in one session

title: An executive-grade addition per dashboard section: one live number that ties to the tile beside it
text: What lands with executives is one number per section, stated as money, time or risk, computed live from the same SQL as the tile next to it (embed the tile's own query at patch time so the numbers cannot drift): revenue run-rate, share of calls served without error, hours of manual clean-up the automatic fixes saved, what the AI catalogued by itself, upside of converting a list, seconds from sign-up to CRM contact, total value in play across the decisions, and concentration of spend. Avoid period trends when the history is short or the data-generation cadence changed; say what each assumption is (for example 3 minutes per manual fix).
evidence: 8 additions verified against their tiles

title: Count a governed pipeline's value as fixes applied, not rules passed
text: The number that explains data quality to a business audience is how many problems were fixed automatically (names/phones/emails standardized + duplicates merged + addresses corrected), with a stated minutes-per-fix assumption, rather than a pass rate. Derive it from the same before/after audit the cleansing view shows, so it ties to the examples on the page.
evidence: 422 fixes, ~21 h at 3 min each

title: Live dashboards read the real-time layer, so a fix made only in the batch layer does not reach them
text: When a dashboard reads real-time views over the change stream and a batch mapping builds the governed tables, a correction applied in only one layer (for example a dedupe key) leaves the dashboard unchanged. Find which layer each tile reads before calling a data fix done, and verify the tile's own query, not the table you changed.
evidence: batch table had the new customer record; the dashboard's real-time view did not until its key changed

title: A surname + street-number match key merges different people at one address; add the first initial and keep every copy of the rule identical
text: A deterministic person key of lower(surname)|house-number collapses two people of one household (same surname, same street number) into one golden record, so a new sign-up 'disappears' from every dashboard. Use surname|first-initial|house-number, and surname|first-initial|email when the address has no number. The key usually exists in more than one place (the batch mapping that builds the golden table AND any real-time view that dedupes the change stream); change all of them together and tie out counts before and after (raw sign-ups, curated, customers without tests), or the batch and real-time layers disagree by exactly the wrongly merged people.
evidence: before: household of 2 merged, customers 715; after: 2 separate keys, customers 716; batch and real-time layers equal again

title: The Data Gateway behind CLAIRE 'Query the data' is a licence package, not a service you select
text: CLAIRE GPT's data queries run through the Data Gateway service on a Secure Agent of the org (L-AGENT-051). It is licensed as its own Platform package (`IDMCDataGatewayService`, category Packages, a separate line from `CLAIRE GPT`) and deploys to the agent only on an org that holds that package. Even on an org where it runs it is not listed under Administrator → Runtime Environments → services, so there is nothing to tick, and copying another org's enabled-services list onto a second org cannot bring it. Ask the vendor to add the package to the org, then check for `<agent_home>/apps/IDMC_Data_Gateway_Service/` and its running process, and re-run one 'Query the data' prompt in that org. Once the vendor added the package, the agent received the service's AppSpec for the first time and started deploying it 3 ms later with no selection step; a minor-version AppSpec redeployed it about 20 minutes later. The first 'Query the data' prompt then ran through it: the gateway's own log shows `Executing GBQ Query TargetSQL` and a `Data Gateway ResultSet`, and the answer matched a direct warehouse query.
evidence: a licence export lists it as its own Platform package; an org running it shows no such entry in its service list; the second org's agent had no gateway app while the first org's agent ran it (2026-09-30); package added, service deployed and a CLAIRE query executed through it (2026-09-30)

title: 'Received new AppSpec' is inventory, not enablement: a deploy starts only when a service is selected
text: At registration the agent logs `AGENT_10014 AgentCore received new AppSpec [<service>, <version>]` for every service the org is entitled to, including ones never selected. Only a selection change produces `LCM_10001 Deploying app <service>-<version>`, `SERVICE_10000 ... state has changed to [DEPLOYING]` and a new folder under `<agent_home>/apps/`. To find when and what was switched on, read those lines and the `apps/` folder timestamps, not the AppSpec lines. Selecting another org's whole service list on a small shared host deployed about nine extra services within minutes (a Process Server failing its status script beside another agent's ports, load 18 on 4 vCPU): see L-AGENT-041.
evidence: AppSpec lines for every entitled service at registration vs LCM_10001 / DEPLOYING lines and new apps/ folders at the moment a selection changed (2026-09-28 and 2026-09-30)

title: PROFILE_SVC_00005 'Cannot find PROFILE with ID … for orgId …' means a stale profile id in your runner
text: After profiles are deleted (an org clean-up or a retired data source), a scheduled runner that still holds their ids gets `404 PROFILE_SVC_00005` on every execute, which reads like a platform fault. Remove the ids from the runner's profile list (comment them out with a dated tag rather than deleting the definitions) and check the next run: the remaining profiles complete normally.
evidence: 4 x 404 PROFILE_SVC_00005 on one daily run after profiles were deleted; the remaining 4 profiles COMPLETED (2026-09-29)

title: External MCP tool connections are retired with the AI Agent Engineering builder: newer orgs cannot create them
text: A vendor support notice (May 2026) sunsets the standalone AI Agent Engineering builder in favour of 'headless' data management: the vendor-hosted MCP servers (data integration, data quality, MDM, catalog) stay generally available, and the CLAIRE agents are being turned into skills callable over MCP, A2A or an agent SDK (preview announced). External MCP servers as agent tools (`TOOL_CONNECTION` / `MCPConnectionAsset`) survive only in orgs that were in the private preview. On a newer org, AI Agent Engineering → MCP Servers → New offers only 'Composite MCP Server' (CAI processes exposed as tools); the CAI connection types have no MCP entry; `a2e-mcp-asset-mgmt-svc` answers `/tool-connections`, `/connections`, `/mcp-connections` and `/tools` with the same 404 as a bogus twin; and importing the asset fails (L-CAI-027), so 'recreate it in the designer' works only on a preview org. It is not an entitlement to request. Invert the design: your own agent (any MCP client) calls the vendor-hosted MCP servers plus your own MCP server, for example through one aggregating gateway (L-MCP-082).
evidence: vendor support notice (May 2026) plus confirmation from a vendor contact (2026-09-29); UI and REST sweep on a newer org: only 'Composite MCP Server' offered, bogus-twin 404s, import failure (2026-09-29)

title: One MCP endpoint for outside agents: aggregate your database tools and the vendor-hosted MCP servers in a FastMCP gateway
text: Mount one FastMCP proxy per upstream: your MCP Toolbox server unprefixed, and each vendor-hosted server (`https://mcp.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/mcp-servers/public/<server>`) under a short prefix, authenticated with a client-credentials token from the org's MCP OAuth client (L-MCP-018), refreshed before expiry and on a 401. Give the vendor servers a plain `Client`: they reject the sampling capability that `ProxyClient` advertises. Guard write and admin tools per server with a middleware that hides and refuses them by name (connection create/update/delete, agent service start/stop, job stop/terminate). Put TLS and authentication in front of it, cache each upstream's tool inventory (L-MCP-083) and set client timeouts (L-MCP-084); any MCP client then sees one combined tool list (86-89 tools here).
evidence: initialize + tools/list from outside the host, SQL and vendor tool calls answered, guarded tools refused (2026-09-30)

title: FastMCP 2.14 mounted proxies list every upstream on every tools/call: cache each proxy's tool inventory
text: In FastMCP 2.14, `tools/call` runs `get_tool(key)`, which calls `get_tools()` across all mounted servers, and each proxy's tool manager opens a fresh upstream session to list its tools. Middleware `on_list_tools` never sees this path, so a middleware cache speeds up `tools/list` but not calls. With 13 upstreams every call cost about 26 s, even for a local SQL tool. Wrap each proxy's `_tool_manager.get_tools` in a TTL cache (300 s, failures not cached): tools/list then takes 0.6 s after one fill per restart, a local tool call 0.3 s and a vendor tool call about 3 s.
evidence: measured on a side-by-side test container: ~26 s per call before, 0.3 s (local tool) and ~3 s (vendor tool) after; tools/list 0.6 s after one fill (2026-09-30)

title: An upstream HTTP 500 hangs a proxied MCP call forever: set the client timeout
text: When an upstream MCP server answers a request with HTTP 500 (MCP Toolbox does this for a failing SQL tool, with a JSON-RPC error body), the streamable-HTTP client raises inside a background task nobody awaits (`Task exception was never retrieved … HTTPStatusError`), and the proxied call never completes. Give every proxy client a `timeout` (for example 60 s for a SQL toolbox, 300 s for long vendor skills) so the agent gets an error it can act on.
evidence: hang reproduced with a failing SQL tool; 'Task exception was never retrieved … HTTPStatusError' in the gateway log; with a timeout the error reaches the caller (2026-09-30)

title: MCP Toolbox tool descriptions steer the agent's SQL: name the real warehouse project
text: An agent writes fully qualified table names from the tool description. If a description names a project that is not the one in the Toolbox source (for example after an app rename: warehouse project ids cannot be renamed), every query fails with 403 'Access Denied … or perhaps it does not exist', although the service account is fine. Keep the source's `project:` and the text of every description identical, and after any rename test one real SQL call per source: a green dataset listing does not prove the SQL tool works. Extends L-MCP-016.
evidence: 403 'Access Denied … or perhaps it does not exist' on the name in the description, 200 with the source's project id; dataset listing worked throughout (2026-09-30)

title: A secret found in git may already be dead: compare by length and hash before rotating, then remove it with a path-limited commit
text: Before rotating a committed key, compare it with the live value without printing either: the length and a short md5 of each, and a history search for the live value (`git log --all -S"$LIVE" --oneline | wc -l`). If they differ and the verifier accepts only the live value, the committed one is dead: remove the literal (and whatever injects it), ignore the backup copies that still hold it, and record that the live key never entered git. In a shared working tree full of other sessions' changes, commit only your paths (`git commit --only -- <paths>`), and do not push a branch that carries other sessions' unpushed commits without a secret scan of `origin/main..HEAD`.
evidence: committed value 52 characters vs live key 64; the verifier accepts only the live key; 0 history hits for the live key, 4 for the dead one (2026-09-30)

title: Browser checks read CSS-transformed text: compare case-insensitively
text: Playwright's `inner_text` returns the text as rendered, so a heading or label styled `text-transform: uppercase` comes back upper-cased and an exact-case check fails on a correct page. Normalise case and whitespace before comparing, and look at the screenshot before calling a UI check a defect.
evidence: two false FAILs on correct pages, confirmed by their screenshots (2026-09-30)

title: Delete Mailpit messages through its HTTP API and verify the count
text: A `wget --method=DELETE` to Mailpit's search endpoint from inside another container returned without an error but deleted nothing. `DELETE /api/v1/messages` with the JSON body `{"IDs": [...]}`, taking the IDs from `GET /api/v1/search?query=to:<address>`, works. Re-run the search afterwards and expect 0.
evidence: 44, 10 and 2 test messages survived the in-container call; the API delete left 0 (2026-09-30)

title: The operational app often keeps its own copy of the match key: change it with the pipeline, or it keeps denying and flagging the people you split
text: Besides the batch mapping and the real-time view, the application that captures sign-ups often computes the same person key itself and stores it on the customer and subscription rows, where it drives business rules (a one-active-subscription-per-person guard, a staff duplicate worklist) rather than the golden table. A pipeline-only fix leaves those rules on the old key: the split people still collide at registration time (a false 'deny' event per registration) and still appear as a duplicate pair to staff, while every dashboard looks right. Search the application code and the stored key column for the key's definition, mirror the new rule exactly (same token rules, same fallback), update every parser of the key format (a two-part length check silently disables the guard once the key has three parts), then backfill the stored keys from a backup copy.
evidence: after the batch and real-time fix the app still stored the old key for both people of the split pair; the new customer's registration wrote a one-per-person 'deny' event; 1 such pair and 6 denies in 7 days

title: CLAIRE GPT rule recommendation: name the columns, or repository rules land on the wrong columns
text: 'Recommend data quality rules for the `<db>` table `<table>`.' lets CLAIRE pick the critical data elements itself, and it then pairs rules from the org's rule repository with them loosely: in one run 7 of 12 recommendations were nonsense (a ZIP-format rule on an id column, a phone-format rule on a confirmation code, email and tier rules on a boolean flag). Naming the columns makes them the critical data elements: '…for the `<c1>`, `<c2>`, … columns of the `<db>` table `<table>`.' put every rule on its matching column in two runs. Open the 'Recommended Data Quality Rules' card (rule, description, dimension, associated data element) before typing 'Accept all the recommended rules': accepted pairs become active rule instances at once, and a misbound one scores 0 and drags the asset's score down (delete it, L-CDGC-144, then re-accept with named columns).
evidence: Three no-accept dry runs with the recommendation card read, then one steered accept (9 of 9 pairings correct in two runs)

title: 'Show the tables that have no data quality scores' is flaky; 'Which <type> tables have no data quality scores?' is not
text: The generic wording passed 3 of 5 runs; the misses answered 'No tables without data quality scores were found' or 'I didn't find any relevant information'. 'Which `<source-type>` tables have no data quality scores?' passed 5 of 5 and lists the first 25 unscored tables of that source with the resource they come from. 'Show tables that have missing quality scores' and 'Which operational tables have no data quality rules or scores …' both missed. On a miss, open a new conversation and paste the prompt again.
evidence: 13 runs in fresh conversations

title: 'What should we fix first?' mixes real scores with invented issues; ask for the score and its rules instead
text: The anchor 'Use only the scores in the catalog' removed the invented tail on 2026-10-01. Original text: With no data quality scores on the asset, the answer invents plausible issues (nulls in an id, bad formats in a column that does not exist, out-of-range ages). With real scores its first part ranks the failing rules correctly, but the closing summary still adds generic issues (duplicates, referential integrity) that no rule measured. 'What is the data quality score of the `<warehouse>` table `<table>`, and which rules are applied to it?' returns the overall and per-dimension scores, the lowest rules with their data elements and a fix order, and it matched the warehouse recomputation. Was believed 2026-09-30; overturned by L-MCP-095.
evidence: Runs before and after the asset had scores, compared with the same checks recomputed in the warehouse (2026-09-30); overturned by L-MCP-095 (2026-10-01)

title: What CLAIRE GPT does, and doesn't, in an org without the data gateway service, and why it authors rather than acts
text: Works: generate, test and publish rules from an attached policy file (one rule per line, a reference dictionary when a rule needs one, duplicates skipped, about 7 minutes); one sentence to a published rule (L-MCP-079); recommend and accept rules (named columns); clean an attached messy file (a plan, every problem with examples and generated code; 'Proceed without testing' executes it and flags what it could not fix, while its self-test and reusable mapplet need the agent's Python runtime); a trust assessment of a table from metadata, data quality scores and lineage; the unscored-tables list; explaining a mapping in business terms; an executive brief of a table; one prompt that chains find, recommend and accept. Fails: 'Query the data' ('source unsupported', L-MCP-060, L-AGENT-097); profiling or cleansing a catalog table (it needs a data preview through the gateway); creating glossary terms ('not equipped'); mapping generation ('PostgreSQL … not supported for mapping generation', L-MCP-052); finding PII columns by classification (search miss). Even with the gateway the chat authors but does not act: on an org outside the private previews it cannot write source or target data, run non-SELECT SQL, save or run a pipeline, call a CAI process or call any MCP tool (the Data Integration agent 'can't perform create, move, store, or delete operations on existing data', and drafts are saved only from the designer canvas). What it persists: rule specifications (plus any dictionaries they need) and catalog rule occurrences when recommended rules are accepted; publishing a rule does not run it (L-MCP-079). Routes that do change data, ranked: (1) CLAIRE authors the rule and your own automation detects the new RULE_SPECIFICATION (diff by id and updateTime) and executes it in a mapping or the warehouse; (2) your own agent drives the vendor-hosted MCP servers (job management runs tasks and taskflows, catalog enrichment edits glossary and classifications, the DQ agent generates and persists rules); (3) a composite MCP server that exposes CAI processes as tools to your own agents (L-MCP-119; CLAIRE GPT is not a client of it); (4) CAI agent recipes with your own LLM key. Dead ends: non-SELECT SQL through 'Query the data', CLAIRE GPT calling your MCP tools, and requesting MCP tool connections for a newer org (a product decision, not an entitlement, L-MCP-081).
evidence: About 40 live runs in one org whose agent has no data gateway service; rule generation and publishing proven end to end on a standard org (about 4 min); 131 CLAIRE GPT and agent doc pages with no MCP or tool-call capability; route (1) designed, its execute half not built

title: After a catalog-source rename, CLAIRE keeps the old resource name until that source is rescanned
text: A rename (L-CDGC-141) changes the source's name at once, but CLAIRE answers kept naming the old resource ('sourced from the "`<old name>`" resource') for that source until it was rescanned with Metadata Extraction; a source rescanned earlier the same day already showed its new name. Rescan every renamed source before users see CLAIRE, and record the source's classifications before the rescan so you can prove they survived (they did with Metadata Extraction only; re-apply them if column identities change).
evidence: CLAIRE answers before and after a Metadata Extraction rescan of the renamed source

title: Auto-accepted connection assignments did not make job-level lineage appear in CLAIRE: verify before you promise it
text: After an IICS Lineage Discovery whose recommendations were all auto-accepted (L-CDGC-140) and rescans of the warehouse, CRM and database sources, CLAIRE still answered '0 upstream assets' for curated warehouse tables and a CRM object, and its downstream answers showed only view-on-table edges: no mapping tasks and no CRM objects. The tasks read through custom SQL queries (copy-data template tasks), which the scanner may not resolve into table-level lineage. Treat L-CDGC-146's rescan and assignment as necessary but not sufficient: check with a CLAIRE upstream and downstream prompt before a lineage story, and keep a static lineage feed for dashboards meanwhile.
evidence: Upstream and downstream prompts on four assets, 3 to 6 h after the discovery run and fresh rescans (unresolved)

title: Leftover connector temp views get cataloged and show up in CLAIRE's lineage answers
text: A `Temp_View<epoch-ms>` left behind by an aborted query-source run (L-CDI-160), six days old, was cataloged by a rescan and appeared as one of three downstream dependents of a curated table in CLAIRE's impact answer. Back up its DDL, drop it in the warehouse and rescan the source with Metadata Change Option = Delete (L-CDGC-028); it left CLAIRE's answer after the rescan. List `Temp_View%` objects before any rescan that users will query.
evidence: The view listed as a downstream dependent, then gone after the drop and a rescan

title: The CLAIRE-to-score loop: recommend and accept, run the catalog DQ capability, then ask for the score
text: Accepted recommendations (with named columns) are rule instances at once but carry no score. Run the source's `capabilityNames: ['Data Quality']` job, which needs the runtime environment in typeCapabilities (L-CDGC-143): Rule Profiling, Batch Profiling and Score Propagation give per-instance, per-dimension and overall scores, and CLAIRE then answers score, trust and low-score questions from them. Recompute each rule in the warehouse before a demo: a format rule at 0% can be a real finding, for example curated phone numbers stored as digits without the leading '+' fail an E.164 check on every row. To change the text an instance shows, recreate the instance (L-CDGC-145).
evidence: 9 instances accepted, scored in about 25 min; CLAIRE's score answer matched a warehouse recomputation

title: Switch a governance-facts feed to another org only after a per-kind dry-run diff
text: Before pointing a feed that copies catalog facts (glossary terms, classifications, rule specifications, lineage edges) into a dashboard from the source org to the target org, run its collector against both orgs without loading and diff each kind item by item. Switch only when the target meets the baseline, back up every edited script, force one refresh and compare the loaded counts. In the recorded case the only difference was three retired duplicate terms that existed only in the old org, so the switch improved the dashboard.
evidence: Dry runs against both orgs, a diff per kind, one forced reload with counts compared

title: Catalog changes by other sessions change CLAIRE's answers: re-test the demo prompts after each one
text: Rescans, renames, source deletions, a first data quality run and rule-instance deletions all changed demo answers in one morning: a reliable prompt started missing, a trust verdict changed once scores existed, an old resource name leaked into an answer, and a leftover view appeared in an impact answer. Keep one owner for the demo scene, have the catalog owner announce each change before running it, re-run the full prompt set afterwards (at least twice for flaky prompts), and stop catalog jobs once the answers are verified.
evidence: Five catalog changes in one morning, each followed by a prompt re-test

title: A settle rule for a CLAIRE GPT browser harness that neither exits early nor waits out the timeout
text: Record the page text length before sending and read only what comes after it, or an earlier reply's completion marker ends the wait at once. Treat the reply as busy while its last ~60 non-space characters contain the spinner text, which is letter-spaced in the page text ('L o a d i n g . . .'), so strip whitespace before matching. Never use a bare '...' as a busy marker (a refinement of L-UI-015): the input placeholder 'Ask CLAIRE...' always contains it, so every step waits out the full timeout. Treat the reply as done on markers ('let me know', 'would you like', 'shall I proceed', 'Cards (<n>)') or on text that stays unchanged and spinner-free for 150 s. After clicking an allowed button or chip, press Enter (L-MCP-079), and send a scripted follow-up only when you mean it: a harness that sends the next follow-up whenever no allowed button is visible posts it as a new prompt. The status line 'Checking available connections…' ends in U+2026 (a single ellipsis character), not three dots: add U+2026 to the busy patterns, because without it the harness treated the status as a finished answer and cut a data prompt before its table arrived (re-check earlier 'no table' failures for this cause).
evidence: About 60 multi-step runs; a data prompt cut at 76 s with no table passed in 116 s with the table after adding U+2026 (8/8 set)

title: Pin, unpin, rename and delete CLAIRE GPT conversations headless
text: Hover the list item that holds `span[data-testid=chat-nav-link]`; the row then shows `button[data-testid=chat-pin-button]` ('Pin Conversation'), `chat-edit-button` (rename: fill the inline input and press Enter) and `chat-delete-button`, and on the Pinned tab `chat-unpin-button` ('Unpin Conversation'). A rename can silently not stick, so list the Pinned tab's titles afterwards and fix any stray row. On a shared account, touch only conversations you created, matched by exact title or conversation id. Reopened conversations collapse their cards behind 'Cards (<n>)' and drop query results, so a pinned fallback shows the answer text but not its data preview.
evidence: 9 pins with renames, one swap, the Pinned tab's titles read back

title: Guard an expiring BI credential with a canary, a backoff and a timed reminder
text: Check one light view every few minutes. On failure, first rebind a single small workbook as a canary: if the credential is refused, send a DOWN alert only; if it is accepted but the canary view still fails, back off for 30 minutes; rebind everything only when the canary view passes. Schedule a reminder shortly before the known expiry (the re-add time plus the policy interval, minus about 90 minutes) with a one-tap action that triggers the rebind right after the person re-adds the login, and cool down failed rebinds (2 h) and button presses (30 min). This pairs with L-ENV-064.
evidence: A 3-minute cron guard with 12 stubbed branch tests, live across a reboot

title: API gateways in Local Mode make the vendor console show every API as inactive; demo from the gateway's own metrics
text: When the API gateways run in Local Mode (configuration from files, not from the vendor control plane), the vendor's API manager lists every API instance as inactive and every gateway as disconnected, and an expired trial subscription adds a warning banner, although the gateways serve traffic and enforce their local policies normally. Rate limiting was proven in Local Mode with 429s (L-ENV-090); client-id enforcement (401 without credentials, 200 with an approved client application) was proven only on Connected Mode and cloud-hosted gateways, and one Local Mode build was reported to fall back to rate limiting, so prove it on a Local Mode gateway with a no-credential call that must return 401 before relying on it. Before a demo, read the entitlements and the subscription expiry with a read-only API call, and show the policy effects from the gateway's own logs or metrics (calls, blocked calls, latency per API) instead of the vendor console.
evidence: A read-only account, API Manager and gateway listing through the vendor platform API; client-id enforcement 401 -> 200 proven on Connected Mode and cloud-hosted gateways only (2026-08-17 to 2026-08-20)

title: Inventory traps in v3 objects: linear taskflows are WORKFLOW, and references page at 50
text: `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='TASKFLOW'` returns only advanced taskflows. Linear taskflows are type `WORKFLOW` and need their own query: one org showed 1 vs 8. `GET /public/core/v3/objects/<id>/references?refType=uses` rejects `limit=200` with 400 `V3API_ObjectReferenceError_02` 'Invalid limit parameter'. Use `limit=50` and page with `skip`. Leaving out `refType` is also a 400. A pre-delete used-by check that misses either returns a clean result that is wrong.
evidence: Two orgs of evidence; 1 vs 8 taskflows and the limit=200 400 reproduced (2026-09-30)

title: v3 routes answer 401 to a v2 session header, and wrappers can hide it as 'no objects'
text: `/public/core/v3/...` routes need `INFA-SESSION-ID: <v3 session>`. Sending the v2 `icSessionId` returns 401 'API request does not contain a valid INFA-SESSION-ID'. A helper that returns an empty list for any non-dict body turns that 401 into '0 objects'. Check the status code before trusting an empty result, and cross-check one object you know exists.
evidence: 401 reproduced; an empty inventory traced to a swallowed 401 (2026-09-30)

title: Tasks run inside a taskflow appear only as activity-log sub-entries
text: In `/api/v2/activity/activityLog`, a mapping task started by a taskflow is not a top-level row. It appears only under the taskflow entry, in `entries[]` (and recursively `subTaskEntries`) with `type: MTT` and its `objectName`. A 'last run per task' built from top-level rows marks every taskflow member as never-run, and that is dangerous input for a delete list. Walk the sub-entries (and query `?taskId=` per task when in doubt). As with any count, check the unit, for example task vs task×target, against one known object.
evidence: Taskflow members reported never-run until the sub-entries were walked (2026-09-30)

title: When the data gateway licence lands, the service deploys to every agent by itself and 'Query the data' starts working
text: A new licence entry appeared on the org, and within about 10 minutes every Secure Agent of the org listed a new engine `IDMC_Data_Gateway_Service` RUNNING. Nobody selected a service (it is a licence package, L-AGENT-097), and one restart cycle followed within 20 minutes. CLAIRE GPT 'Query the data' then answered on warehouse tables and views: a top-N list, failing checks with their business risk, counts per category as a chart, and data distributions. The numbers were identical to the warehouse. When a name exists as both a table and a view, CLAIRE asks which one, so answer 'The Table' (or 'The View'). A prompt that said 'view <name>' missed twice because the search surfaced other assets. Watch the org's licence list on a schedule and diff it, rather than waiting on the agents.
evidence: A licence change seen by a 10-minute watcher; the engine RUNNING on two agents; four NL-to-SQL prompts passed with warehouse-identical numbers

title: What CLAIRE GPT answers reliably, and what fails (2026-10-01 update)
text: Works: glossary terms and the terms linked to a table; per-table personal-data columns; catalog-wide classification search with the right wording (L-MCP-092); explaining a mapping in business terms and listing projects, folders and mappings (L-MCP-093); MDM business entities with their match and survivorship rules, and Data Marketplace collections (L-MCP-113); product how-to, including help about an asset found earlier in the conversation (L-MCP-094); executive briefs and trust verdicts of a table; comparing two tables or a table and a view (exact column diff); suggesting glossary terms for columns without creating them; ownership and certification, answered honestly as 'not provided'; view-level lineage (L-MCP-107); 'Query the data' on one warehouse asset, with numbers identical to the warehouse to the cent (group-bys, CASE buckets, window functions, text-to-number casts, 3-sigma outliers, projections); DQ score, low-score diagnosis and a grounded fix order (L-MCP-095); rules from a sentence or a policy file (L-MCP-099). Fails or is unreliable: discovery by business question without a table name (L-MCP-103); cross-table joins (L-MCP-100); job-level and SaaS lineage (L-MCP-107); governance counts and 'terms with no linked assets'; data dictionary generation (L-MCP-106); 'show me the SQL' (L-MCP-102); mapping generation into a new target (L-MCP-108); PostgreSQL data queries (by design, L-MCP-114). Pass rates per lane were about 54-64% single-shot, so rehearse every prompt (L-MCP-054).
evidence: About 190 recorded runs in fresh conversations across three test lanes (catalog, analytics, DQ), every data answer checked against the warehouse

title: Catalog-wide classification search works: ask 'Which columns in the catalog are classified as <classification>?'
text: 'Which columns in the catalog are classified as <classification>?' (for example Email, or a phone-number classification) returned 25+ matching columns across several sources; 'Which tables in the catalog contain email addresses?' still fails. The wording must name the classification as the catalog shows it. Per table, 'Which columns in the <system> table <table> contain personal data?' swung between pass and 'no columns classified as personal data' (2 of 4); 'List the columns of the <system> table <table> and say which of them contain personal data.' passed. When several tables share a prefix, CLAIRE asks which one: answer 'Use the table <table>.' 'Which datasets contain sensitive data elements in the <system> system?' still missed. This overturns the catalog-wide classification failure in L-MCP-058 and the search miss in L-MCP-089.
evidence: Classification wording passed 3 of 4 runs (two classifications); the 'which tables contain' wording failed every time; per-table wording 50/50 vs 1 of 1

title: Mappings are catalog assets once Data Integration metadata is scanned: explain them by name, and name the folder when variants exist
text: With the org's Data Integration metadata in the catalog, 'Explain in business terms what the mapping <mapping> does, step by step.' returns the mapping's stages in business language, 'List all projects and folders in Data Integration.' and 'Which mappings are in the <folder> folder?' list the inventory (25 per answer), and 'Show all mappings and mapping tasks in Data Integration.' lists mappings but no mapping tasks. When variants share a stem (v2, v2b, v2c), CLAIRE asks which one or answers from product docs: add 'in the <folder> folder'. A mapping that is not scanned is 'not found'. Mapping and job lineage still answer 'This asset has no lineage' (L-MCP-107), and 'which mapping tasks write to <object>' still fails. This overturns 'mapping tasks by name are not catalog assets' in L-MCP-058 for mappings; classic mapping tasks are still not found.
evidence: 'Explain the mapping' passed 7 of 9 runs, 2 of 2 with the folder named; folder and project listings 4 of 4

title: Product how-to questions now pass, including help about the asset in hand
text: Generic product questions (setting up a DQ scorecard, how the catalog detects personal data and how to create a custom classification, mapping vs mapping task) were answered with correct steps and citations. A two-turn shape is the strongest: 'Find the <system> table <table>.' then 'How do I add data quality rules to this table?' (or '... protect or mask the sensitive columns of this table?') gives help tied to that asset. Keep glossary questions anchored on 'the business term X' (L-MCP-057): unanchored business phrasing is still routed to product docs. This overturns 'product how-to questions fail' in L-MCP-058.
evidence: 5 of 5 product-help runs, including 2 asset-contextual follow-ups

title: 'What should we fix first?' is grounded when you add 'Use only the scores in the catalog'
text: Ask 'Which rule has the lowest score on the <warehouse> table <table>, and what should we fix first? Use only the scores in the catalog.' The answer ranks the failing rules with their data elements and a fix order, with no invented tail. 'What could be the reason for the low data quality score of the <warehouse> table <table>?' gives the same root causes by rule and field, run after run. Without the anchor the closing summary still adds generic issues that no rule measured. This overturns L-MCP-088.
evidence: Fix-first with the anchor: no invented issues; score, low-score and fix-first prompts 5 of 5 in the UI and 3 of 3 over MCP, numbers matching a warehouse recomputation

title: Never send free text while 'Publish Rules / Don't Publish Rules' is showing: CLAIRE takes it as consent and publishes
text: After a rule is generated and tested, CLAIRE shows 'Publish Rules' and 'Don't Publish Rules'. A scripted follow-up typed at that moment ('Create it as a reusable rule specification that is not tied to any data source.') was taken as consent, and the rule specification was published to the CLAIRE project and folder. Treat any reply at that prompt as possibly binding: click 'Don't Publish Rules' (plus Send) or stop the conversation, and only then type. Audit with `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='RULE_SPECIFICATION'` by update time after any automated run (harness guard: L-UI-030).
evidence: A rule specification was published with nobody clicking Publish; read back over v3 objects

title: The 'Generate Dictionaries' plan step saves dictionaries to CDQ before any Publish
text: When a generated rule needs a reference list (for example state names to codes), the plan step 'Generate Dictionaries' creates the dictionary in the CLAIRE project and folder while the rules are being generated, before the Publish prompt. Stopping at 'Don't Publish Rules' leaves the dictionary behind. Rule generation is therefore not side-effect-free: list DICTIONARY objects by update time afterwards and delete strays, or reuse them.
evidence: A DICTIONARY object appeared in the CLAIRE folder during generation, with the rule itself left unpublished

title: Rule recommendation only matches rules already in the repository: use generation for new controls
text: 'Recommend data quality rules for the C1, C2 ... columns of the <system> table <table>' pairs the named columns with existing repository rules only; columns with no matching rule come back as 'No matching data quality rules were found'. For a new control (a positive amount, a percent range, a value list, no future dates), use rule generation from one sentence or a policy file (L-MCP-099), then bind it. Recommendation is the right tool once the repository holds the rule family. Still name the columns (L-MCP-086).
evidence: Recommendation on two operational tables: 0 rules for one, only the 2 email rules for the other

title: Rules from a policy file: start the prompt 'This file is a data quality policy with one rule per line.'
text: Attach a plain-text policy (one rule per line) and send 'This file is a data quality policy with one rule per line. Generate data quality rules from this file.' The bare 'Generate data quality rules from this file.' was misrouted once in three runs: it profiled the file as data and found 'no candidate rules'. Each rule is generated and tested in about 5 minutes for the set, and rules that already exist are deduplicated on every run. For one-sentence rules, name the system, table and column ('... the COLUMN column in the SYSTEM table TABLE ...'): a sentence with no table asked for a data source 2 of 3 times, while a named column went straight to the plan (about 3-4 minutes, tested 100%). Stop at the Publish prompt unless you mean to publish (L-MCP-096).
evidence: Policy file: 2 of 3 with the plain wording, 1 of 1 with the policy sentence; 6 one-sentence rules tested at 100%

title: 'Query the data' keeps one asset in scope: cross-table joins fail
text: A question that needs two assets ends with one asset in the 'scope context': '<asset2> ... not available in the provided scope context. Only <asset1> is present', or CLAIRE asks which one is the main dataset and then drifts to another source. Naming the join columns or answering 'use both' did not help. Pre-join the data in a cataloged view and ask about that view. In a chain, a follow-up that hops to a second asset re-runs discovery and often misses.
evidence: 0 of 4 join prompts, with the columns named and with 'use both views' follow-ups

title: The written insights describe only the first ~5 rows; trust the chart or table, and name the filter columns
text: For long results (a daily trend, week-over-week per group, per-customer daily counts) the 'Analysis & Insights' text is written from the first ~5 rows while the chart or table holds the full result: one narrative covered only the first five days of a month, another claimed a constant value its own chart contradicted, and a projection computed in the table was never stated. Show the card, not the narrative. CLAIRE also does exactly what the SQL says: a pseudo-category value (a placeholder 'subscription' value in a store column) won 'most revenue', and blank keys topped 'most orders'. Name the filter and definition columns in the prompt (a test flag, the activity date, the kind column) and exclude placeholder values explicitly.
evidence: Multi-row answers compared with their own charts and with warehouse results

title: 'Show me the SQL' and 'generate SQL' are refused: use Show Code
text: Asking for the SQL in chat ('show me the SQL', 'Generate SQL ...') returns 'I cannot show or generate code, scripts, or SQL directly due to platform constraints'. Ask the question with 'Query the data.' instead, then open the Show Code expander under the result: it holds the full warehouse SQL that ran. Ask for the chart type (bar, pie, line) in the same prompt; the card toggles table, bar, pie and line and offers download and copy.
evidence: Two refusals in chat; Show Code present under every data answer

title: Discovery without a table name is weak, and named-table search flakes about 1 in 6: re-ask in a new conversation
text: Questions such as 'Where can I find customer loyalty data?' or 'Which tables contain tier data?' mostly answer 'no relevant information', even when glossary terms link the tables; 'Which customers are at risk of churning?' lists relevant assets and asks which one to use. Name the asset and its type ('the BigQuery view V'). Even then, about one named search in six returns a generic list of 25 assets and 'X is not found in the limited set of 25 results', and the same prompt passes on the next run; misses grew while several testers ran in parallel. Re-ask the same prompt in a New Conversation, and in a chain re-name the asset in the follow-up so CLAIRE re-discovers it. A name shared by a table and a view triggers 'table or view?': answer 'The Table' or 'The View'.
evidence: Business-language discovery 1 of 7; about 10 table-search misses in about 60 discovery calls

title: Chained conversations work when every turn names its asset; refinements and 'Clear conversation memory' work
text: A conversation can carry a workstream: query, then 'Now show only <segment>.', then 'Show that as a bar chart.', then 'Write a short status update for <role> covering the numbers, the root sources and the top 3 fixes.' Chains that re-named the asset in every turn passed every run; a first-turn discovery miss poisons the following turns, so check turn one. Follow-ups take 20-75 s each, and a 4-turn chain about 3.5-4 minutes. 'Clear conversation memory' (prompt or icon) works: it replies that memory is cleared, keeps the visible history, and answers the next independent question correctly. The older rule of one prompt per conversation (L-MCP-054) still applies to independent questions.
evidence: 18 chained conversations: 11 full passes, 45 of 59 turns; chains that named the asset every turn passed 3 of 3

title: A numbered multi-intent prompt works for catalog tasks, not for analytics
text: '1. Find the <system> table <table>. 2. List its personal data columns. 3. Show its downstream lineage. 4. List the business terms linked to it.' returned each task as its own card in all three runs, the most stable catalog shape tested. A numbered analytics prompt (top 10, counts per group, a bar chart) failed at discovery before any step ran. For analytics, chain single questions instead (L-MCP-104).
evidence: Numbered catalog prompt 3 of 3 (about 75 s); numbered analytics prompt 0 of 1

title: Where CLAIRE GPT hallucinates: data dictionaries, coverage lists, governance counts, cleansing examples
text: 'Write a data dictionary for <table>' either hung or produced a generic schema with none of the real columns. 'Which business terms in the <domain> domain have no linked assets?' named linked terms and gave a different count on each run. Governance roll-ups ('datasets missing business descriptions', 'datasets missing DQ scores', 'critical data elements of a system') answered 'no relevant information' or contradicted prompts that work. A marketplace-availability claim for a table was unverified. A SaaS object whose name matches an MDM entity (a contact) was answered from the MDM entity. A file-cleansing run invented whitespace examples and a casing standard that were not in the file. Never demo these, and review any generated cleansing logic against the data.
evidence: Answers compared with the catalog and the source files

title: View-level lineage answers; job-level and SaaS lineage need the integration lineage setup
text: Downstream lineage of a warehouse table or view returns the dependent views with a LINEAGE card, and upstream lineage through views can span several hops ('Expand 5 Hops'). 'Show the lineage of the mapping <mapping>', upstream lineage into a table loaded by jobs, lineage of SaaS objects and lineage of source-database tables all answered 'This asset has no lineage' or '0 upstream assets'. Those need a Data Integration (IICS) catalog source scanned with Lineage Discovery and its connection assignments accepted (L-CDGC-148), and lineage from custom-query loads can stay empty even then. Impact answers are therefore view-level only until the job layer produces lineage. Newer evidence: L-MCP-128.
evidence: View-to-view lineage 2 of 2 and a 25-asset, 4-hop upstream lineage of a DQ view; job-level, SaaS and source-database lineage 0 of 9

title: 'Create a mapping to load these' gives an in-chat proposal only; mapplets are conversation artifacts
text: After an exploration answer, 'Create a mapping to load these <rows>.' produced an in-chat MAPPING ARTIFACT (a generated name, the source with the filter carried over, a placeholder target) with no save button, and nothing appeared in the org. A one-shot 'Create a mapping from <table> to a new <warehouse> table' failed with 'Unable to identify all assets required for the mapping generation' because the target does not exist. Cleansing runs 'package' their logic as a reusable mapplet that lives only in the conversation (0 MAPPLET objects in the org). Artifact reuse in the same conversation works ('Show me the mapplet you generated and explain each step.'). Headless mapping authoring still goes through packages (L-MCP-052).
evidence: v3 object query by update time: 0 mappings, tasks or mapplets created after the runs

title: Generated-code self-tests need Python on the Secure Agent: answer 'Proceed without testing'
text: File cleansing and anonymization runs generate Python code and then try to test it on the org's agent; without Python (Pandas and PyArrow) enabled for the data gateway the test fails ('error in the secure agent', 'cannot validate ... secure agent'). Click 'Proceed without testing' plus Send: the plan completes and flags what it could not fix. A duplicate-customer run gave a strong diagnosis and survivorship code but never rendered the final golden-record table ('Results will be shown as available').
evidence: Every cleansing run's self-test failed with a secure-agent error; 'Proceed without testing' completed them

title: CLAIRE GPT answer times, and the hangs to re-ask
