title: Data Profiling REST on a Salesforce object: the create body, the run, and where the results are read
text: A profile on a Salesforce object was created and run headless with no template: source.dataSourceType and source.properties.dataSourceType = SALESFORCE (the enum is UNSET, ORACLE, DB2, SQL_SERVER, DELIMITED, FIXED_WIDTH, TOOLKIT_CCI, SALESFORCE, MAPPLET; 'Salesforce' fails with PROFILE_SVC_00048 'JSON input is not valid'), no sourcePath, source.fields from GET <pod>/saas/api/v2/connection/source/<v2 connection id>/field/<object>?validateFields=false (dataType = the field's native type such as id, string, picklist, email, phone, datetime, double, boolean; pcType as returned), profileableFields only for the columns PUT <profiling base>/Configuration/columns/profilingFacts marks isSupported (long text areas are not), advancedOptions from GET /Configuration/getAdvancedOptionsForConnection/<v2 connection id> (one option, Enable Bulk Query = NO), samplingOptions ALL_ROWS. POST /profile/<id>/execute ran it to COMPLETED ('No errors encountered.') with the steps 'Generating data profiling mappings', one s_profiling_<profileKey>_<run>_1 session, 'Fetching the source row count' and 'Loading data from staging area to metric store'. Results: metric store OData Profiles('<profile id>')/Columns (filter runKey), and per column Profiles('<profile id>')/Columns('<columnId>')/Patterns | ValueFrequencies | DataTypes (the top-level Columns('<columnId>')/... form answers METRIC_STORE_00038, and the pattern list holds every run: filter on runKey). Patterns below the threshold are grouped as 'Others', so a rare bad value is counted but not named there: use a rule for that. The same body shape on a BigQuery V2 table still failed at mapping generation (L-DQ-107), which points at the BigQuery path, not at the REST body.
evidence: 1 warm-up + 3 runs on a 777-row, 89-field object: 87 columns profiled, 43-49 s from REST submit to job end, about 8 counted Salesforce API calls per run (series /limits estimate); null and pattern counts matched an independent SQL check (2026-10-04)

title: Snowflake key-pair connection headless: instanceName is the metadata type, and the key file lives on the agent host
text: Create body: type TOOLKIT_CCI, instanceName 'Snowflake Cloud Data Warehouse V2' (the type field of GET /api/v2/connector/metadata). The Administrator label 'Snowflake Data Cloud' returns 403 'There is no connector with type= Snowflake Data Cloud'. connParams: authentication = KeyPair (the newest adapter's valid list is Standard, AuthorizationCode, KeyPair, ClientCredentials, Programmatic Access Token), user, account (the org-account identifier ORGNAME-ACCOUNTNAME, no .snowflakecomputing.com), warehouse (mandatory), role, privateKeyFile = an absolute path ON THE SECURE AGENT HOST, privateKeyFilePwd only for an encrypted key, additionalparam = db=<DB>&schema=<SCHEMA> for defaults. IDMC stores only the path, so copy the unencrypted PKCS#8 .p8 to the agent host first, owned by the agent's OS user with mode 400 in a 700 folder; a host-local key never passes through IDMC. Pair it with a Snowflake TYPE=SERVICE user holding RSA_PUBLIC_KEY (no password). GET /api/v2/connection/test/<id> then answers 200 'The test for this connection was successful.', and the read-back shows authentication KeyPair and the stored path.
evidence: One create (200) + two tests (200 success) on a Linux Secure Agent, adapter metadata version 52000872, Snowflake trial account on AWS (2026-10-06)

title: Snowflake Data Cloud objects in a generated mapping: path DB/SCHEMA/TABLE, type system TOOLKIT, native types varchar, number, date, timestampntz
text: A designer-built mapping's Snowflake Data Cloud target uses dataAdapter.typeSystem TOOLKIT and an object whose path, name and label are <DATABASE>/<SCHEMA>/<TABLE> (objectName = the table), objectType 'table', and objectAttributes tableType = TABLE. Field native types are lower case: varchar, number, date, boolean, timestampntz (also timestamp). 'timestamp_ntz' is refused at session start ('Invalid Datatype: timestamp_ntz for field ...', then 'The DTM process terminated unexpectedly'). A generator's generic CCI path (no path rewrite) with these values imports valid and runs. The Snowflake writer bulk-loads through an internal stage: each target issues PUT + COPY, about 0.5 s of warehouse time per target for small loads, and all targets of one run share one warehouse resume. Custom-query lookups on the same connection work; use fully qualified <DB>.<SCHEMA>.<TABLE> names in the query.
evidence: One headless build of a multi-flow mapping (flat-file sources, Snowflake lookups and targets) on a Linux Secure Agent, adapter version 10.4 (build 872), five runs (2026-10-06)

title: Snowflake writer: Post SQL runs only from the runtime attribute 'postsql', not from the transformation's Post SQL property
text: A Post SQL written in the target transformation's advanced property 'Post SQL' was silently skipped by the Snowflake Data Cloud writer (the run succeeded, the UPDATE never ran). Putting the same SQL in the writer runtime attribute postsql (oprRuntimeAttributes; runtime display name 'Post SQL') made it run after the load. The writer's attribute list comes from GET /api/v2/connection/target/<connId>/metadata?objectName=<table>: UpdateMode, database, schema, warehouse, role, presql, postsql, batchrowsize, numberofstagingfiles, truncatetarget, additionalparam, tablename, rejectedfilepath, updateOverride. Use it for an SCD2 close-out (UPDATE ... FROM (a window over the table)); it runs even when the target loaded 0 rows.
evidence: One headless build of a multi-flow mapping (flat-file sources, Snowflake lookups and targets) on a Linux Secure Agent, adapter version 10.4 (build 872), five runs (2026-10-06)

title: A lookup on a Snowflake NUMBER column must be a decimal port: a bigint port fails with 'BigDecimal cannot be cast to java.lang.Long'
text: Snowflake NUMBER values (also NUMBER(9,0) and aggregates such as MAX(version)) reach the DTM as java.math.BigDecimal. A lookup return port typed bigint (javaType java.lang.Long) fails the run at the first matching row: 'Error Occured for Transformation - ISourceNode.. while writing the data to DTM Buffer - java.math.BigDecimal cannot be cast to java.lang.Long'. It passed while the lookup table was empty, so the failure shows up only on a later run. Declare the port decimal(19,0) and convert with TO_BIGINT in the expression. Writing a bigint field into a NUMBER target column works.
evidence: One headless build of a multi-flow mapping (flat-file sources, Snowflake lookups and targets) on a Linux Secure Agent, adapter version 10.4 (build 872), five runs (2026-10-06)

title: v2 field browse of a Snowflake connection fails on duplicate catalog entries; declare the fields in the mapping instead
text: GET /api/v2/connection/source/<connId> and /target/<connId> return [] for a Snowflake Data Cloud connection, and /field/<table> answers 403 APP_13400 'Failed to validate the data object because the entry [<DATABASE>] already exists in the collection [null]' (with db and schema defaults in additionalparam), or the same for [SNOWFLAKE] without them. A '%2F'-encoded path returns a Tomcat 400. The v2 browse routes do not handle the connector's hierarchical names. A generated mapping does not need them: declare the fields (names and native types) in the spec; the writer's runtime attributes still come from /target/<connId>/metadata?objectName=<table>.
evidence: Probes on one Snowflake Data Cloud connection (2026-10-06)

title: Mapping-task pre- and post-processing commands are set headless with v2 preProcessingCmd / postProcessingCmd; flat-file sources are validated before the pre-command runs
text: GET /api/v2/mttask/<id> omits the fields when they are empty. POST the task object back (drop createTime, updateTime, lastRunTime, createdBy, updatedBy) with preProcessingCmd and postProcessingCmd set to shell commands, then read back to confirm. The commands run on the Secure Agent host as the agent's OS user: pre before the mapping, post after a successful run (a failed run skips post). Two traps: (1) the task validates every flat-file source object BEFORE the pre-processing command runs; a missing file fails the run at once with 'Object <file> is not valid: ... File [<dir>/<file>] does not exist', so a pre-command that generates the source files needs them (headers are enough) to exist already; (2) re-importing the mapping in OVERWRITE mode keeps the task and its commands. This gives a headless script step around a mapping without an advanced taskflow Command Task (whose publish is UI-only).
evidence: One headless build of a multi-flow mapping (flat-file sources, Snowflake lookups and targets) on a Linux Secure Agent, adapter version 10.4 (build 872), five runs (2026-10-06)

title: Document-intake pattern in one mapping: per-flow check expressions, router OK / EXC / ALL, one exception union, per-document aggregates joined to a registry
text: For many small document feeds, one mapping keeps the cost to one job and one warehouse session per run. Per flow: source -> expression (typing with IS_NUMBER / IS_DATE guards plus unconnected cached lookups on master data) -> expression of checks (rule = first failing check, nested IIF; detail = every failing check's text concatenated) -> router with OK (no rule), EXC (rule) and ALLROWS groups, all gated by a 'document already processed' lookup -> OK to the typed target, EXC to a Union feeding one exceptions table, ALLROWS to an Aggregator by document id (rows, loaded, review, rejected, one example reason). The per-flow aggregates go through a second Union into a Joiner (master outer) with the registry source, and an expression derives each document's status (PROCESSED / PARTIAL / NEEDS_REVIEW / REJECTED / DUPLICATE). In-batch duplicates: Sorter on the business key plus VARIABLE ports comparing with the previous row; history duplicates: a lookup on the loaded table. Grouped 'packet' rules (all required documents present): Aggregator by folder, then join the packet status back to a second read of the same file (no self-join). One unconnected lookup can be called from several pipelines of the same mapping.
evidence: One headless build of a multi-flow mapping (flat-file sources, Snowflake lookups and targets) on a Linux Secure Agent, adapter version 10.4 (build 872), five runs (2026-10-06)

title: Event-driven pickup from SharePoint Online for a mapping task: a Graph change-feed poll triggers the job, the task's own pre-processing step downloads only new files
text: For 'drop a document in SharePoint and IDMC processes it' without a schedule: a small service on the Secure Agent host polls Microsoft Graph delta on the document library (GET /drives/<id>/root/delta, one call every few seconds; start with token=latest). When a file changes it waits until uploads go quiet for a few seconds (so a multi-file drop becomes one run) and starts the mapping task with POST /api/v2/job. The download itself happens inside the task: its preProcessingCmd pulls every file whose item id + cTag is not yet in a local ledger into the folder the flat-file connection reads, so the Run button behaves the same as an upload. No upload means no job and no warehouse wake-up. Guard it: one run at a time (check activityMonitor), runs per hour/day, the same file version at most twice, back-off after a failed run, a pause file.
evidence: One live build on a Linux Secure Agent: upload seen in 4 s, job started 18 s later, run 101 s; six demo uploads verified end to end (30 of 30 checks); offline tests of the watcher logic (17 cases).

title: A mapping-task post-processing command that starts background work must detach it from the command's stdout/stderr, or the post-session step waits for it
text: The agent runs postProcessingCmd through a shell and reads its output until EOF. A child process that inherits stdout keeps the step (and the task) open until the child ends. Start follow-up work (a BI refresh, a quality snapshot) in a new session with stdin from /dev/null and stdout/stderr to a log file (e.g. Python subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True, stdin=DEVNULL, stdout=logfile, stderr=STDOUT)); the step then returns at once. Remember the post command runs only after a successful session.
evidence: Live mapping task on a Linux Secure Agent: post step returned in ~1 s while the detached hooks ran 2-40 s afterwards and logged to their own file.

title: Snowflake views written as SELECT * (or X.*) break with 'declared N column(s), but view query produces M column(s)' when an underlying table or view gains columns
text: Snowflake records the column count of a SELECT * view when it is created. After ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN (or recreating an upstream view with more columns) the view fails to compile, and every view built on it fails too. Recreate the * views right after the change (same text) and check every dependent view with one SELECT; better, give views that other teams build on an explicit column list. In a multi-column ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, the IF NOT EXISTS covers only the first column: use one statement per column to stay re-runnable.
evidence: One live schema change on a Snowflake trial account: 7 dependent views failed until recreated; re-runnable DDL tested on scratch objects.

title: The Snowflake SQL API returns large results in partitions; a client that reads only the first response truncates silently
text: POST /api/v2/statements returns partition 0 only, with resultSetMetaData.partitionInfo listing the rest; fetch them with GET /api/v2/statements/<handle>?partition=<n>. A helper that reads data from the first response saw ~2,300 of ~3,300 query-history rows, which made a cost meter under-report spend for hours. Either page through the partitions or push the aggregation into SQL so the answer is one row.
evidence: One cost-meter script against a Snowflake trial account; fixed by aggregating in SQL (one result row).

title: Microsoft Graph facts for a SharePoint document-library pickup: delta has no paths, downloadUrl comes with listings, version labels and older versions are readable
text: Graph delta responses on a SharePoint drive omit parentReference.path: use delta only as the trigger and a /children listing for paths. /children (without $select) returns @microsoft.graph.downloadUrl, a short-lived pre-authenticated link. The SharePoint version label ('2.0') comes from ?$expand=listItem($expand=fields($select=_UIVersionString)); /items/<id>/versions/<versionId>/content downloads an earlier version, which lets a demo reset restore its baseline documents after people re-upload new versions with read-only access. A delegated refresh token for read-only scopes works headless once an admin has consented the app.
evidence: One live SharePoint Online tenant: 27-document library listed, downloaded, version-labelled and restored repeatedly.

title: Sort a shared org into one tag per workload plus a top-level Archive project, without deleting anything
text: Give every Explore object exactly one owner tag (one per workload plus `archive`) and move what belongs to no workload into a new top-level `Archive` project, one folder per theme, with FRS `MoveEntities`. Ids, v2 task ids, schedules and run history survive the move. Make Archive a top-level project, never a folder inside a workload project, so the IICS catalog-source include filter on that project does not scan it. Refute each archive verdict before moving: FRS inbound refs, linear-taskflow membership, task-level schedules, recent runs (taskflow sub-entries included), and a grep of the orchestrator's code AND its JSON plan files for the v2 ids and names. Tag in place what cannot move: profiles (FRS_108), installed MDM app content, CAI assets stuck in the runtime. Bundle content cannot be tagged either. Keep the folders that generators write to, re-run a tag sweep after builds, and write a per-object undo log (id, from container, to container).
evidence: 260 moves FRS_200 with every v2 task id read back unchanged; the orchestrator's id-based flows kept working; 725 objects tagged; nothing deleted

title: Some cleaned-up objects regenerate: the sample mock connections and the DQ capability schedules
text: Three 'Sample ... Connection' MockConnector connections on the hosted runtime reappeared about 25 minutes after a delete, when a database-ingestion CDC task was created. The `DQ_Capability_Schedule_{Daily,Weekly,Monthly}_<epoch>` schedules ('Auto generated schedule for existing Rule Templates') are created by catalog data-quality automation, and they came back after a delete once DQ scoring was enabled on a catalog source. Classify both as platform-generated: keep them, or switch the feature off first. Don't put them on a delete list.
evidence: connections recreated within 25 min of the delete; schedules recreated when DQ automation was enabled two days later

title: TagObjects: bundle content refuses tags, MDM app and CAI content accept them; hyphenated tags work; delete an empty tag through FRS
text: `POST /public/core/v3/TagObjects` answers 207. Each Add-On Bundle item (bundle mappings, mapplets, cleanses) comes back `FAILED ... skipped has no READ permission`, even for an org administrator. Objects inside installed MDM app projects, CAI assets (stuck published ones included), the system API policy and DQ preview mappings return SUCCESS. Tag names with a hyphen work, and `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=tag=='<tag>'` reads them back. `UntagObjects` takes the same body. A tag with no documents left still exists in FRS `Tags`: `DELETE https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/frs/api/v1/Tags('<tagId>')` with `IDS-SESSION-ID` returns 204, and the read-back is 404 `FRS_037` (no artifact).
evidence: 207 per-item results on a 20-object type probe; tag-query read-back; DELETE 204 then 404 FRS_037

title: Move a published process to another project without losing its endpoint: unpublish, move, republish from the new path
text: 1. Unpublish in dependency order: process, then app connection, then service connector. Call `POST https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/asset/v1/unpublish` with `Explore/<path>.<TYPE>.xml` asset paths and poll `/unpublish/<id>/Status`. 2. Move the assets with FRS `MoveEntities`. 3. Publish them from their NEW Explore paths in reverse order (connector, connection, process) with `/active-bpel/asset/v1/publish` and poll `/publish/<id>/Status`. Every job ended SUCCESS and the process kept its runtime endpoint. Never move a published CAI asset without unpublishing it first: a runtime catalog row that points at the old path is how assets get stuck, with publish and unpublish both faulting. A process can use an app connection that lives in another project: leave that connection published.
evidence: 3 unpublish and 3 publish jobs SUCCESS; v3 publicationStatus 'published' at the new path

title: An IICS catalog source harvests a mapping only through an in-scope mapping task
text: Take an IICS catalog source whose Metadata Extraction filter includes a project. Mappings stored in that project were still missing from its metadata and lineage, because their mapping tasks lived in `Default`, outside the filter: the scanner reaches a mapping through an in-scope task. Moving the tasks into the scanned project with FRS `MoveEntities` (ids preserved) and running one rescan brings them in. With Metadata Change Option = Delete, the same rescan also drops whatever was moved out of scope, which changes catalog and CLAIRE answers. Rescan deliberately, and not right before a demo.
evidence: the source's scanned metadata held none of the mappings whose tasks sat in Default, and all of the mappings whose tasks were in scope

title: data360 search stops at 10,000 hits and ignores aggregations: take a class census on ccgf-searchv2
text: `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/search/api/v1/search` returns at most 10,000 hits (`total.relation: gte`) and an empty `aggregations` object for a terms aggregation. A paged 'list everything' therefore truncates silently: one census missed 25 glossary terms. The index also returns relationship documents (`elementType: RELATIONSHIP`, no `core.classType`), so filter on `elementType` = `OBJECT`. For counts by class, run the aggregation on `https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-searchv2/api/v1/search`; it returned the full census (84 classes).
evidence: a 10,000-row cap and empty aggregations on data360; ccgf-searchv2 aggregation returned 84 classes

title: Column-level CDI lineage headless: connectionAssignment with operationType=MERGE stitches IICS references (SPLIT undoes; ASSIGN is not a value)
text: Catalog the physical systems (Metadata Extraction, plus profiling and classification as needed) and an IICS source over the project's Data Integration assets with Lineage Discovery (L-CDGC-029). Then stitch each connection reference of the IICS source to its physical catalog source: `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/assignment/connectionAssignment?operationType=MERGE` with the identity headers and `{"sourceRootAsset": {"externalId": "<iicsSourceId>_<CONN>://<CONN>~core.DataSource", "origin": "<iicsSourceId>", "location": "<iicsSourceId>://<iicsSourceId>/<iicsSourceId>_<CONN>/<CONN>"}, "targetRootAsset": [{"externalId": "<sourceId>://<DATABASE>~com.infa.odin.models.relational.Database", "origin": "<sourceId>", "isCaseSensitive": false, "location": "<sourceId>://<sourceId>/<DATABASE>"}], "initialAssignment": true, "modifyAssignment": false}` returns a job id; the same body with `operationType=SPLIT` undoes it. `ASSIGN`, `UNASSIGN`, `ACCEPT` and `CREATE` fail the enum conversion: the accepted values are the catalog UI's `Merge` and `Split`. The job also completes for a reference that does not exist, so prove the stitch by reading a target table's lineage (hops through the mapping task); it showed without another scan. In a new org the Lineage Discovery auto-accept (L-CDGC-140) had left these references unresolved.
evidence: ASSIGN, UNASSIGN, ACCEPT and CREATE rejected by enum conversion; MERGE job completed and a target table's lineage showed the mapping task with its sources and lookups; a bogus-twin reference also 'completed'

title: Stitch a mapping's flat-file reference to a File System catalog source
text: A mapping that reads or writes files through a flat-file connection shows up in the IICS source as a reference named after the file directory, slashes replaced by underscores (`<iicsSourceId>_<dir_with_underscores>://<dir_with_underscores>~core.DataSource`). Catalog that directory with a File System catalog source on the same Secure Agent, then MERGE-assign the reference (L-CDGC-159) to the File System root: target `{"externalId": "<fsSourceId>://FileServer~com.infa.odin.models.file.FileSystem", "origin": "<fsSourceId>", "isCaseSensitive": true, "location": "<fsSourceId>://<fsSourceId>/File Server"}`. Each file then appears upstream of the mapping task in lineage.
evidence: job completed; the staged files showed upstream of the mapping task in a table's lineage

title: Create a catalog Data Quality rule occurrence headless: contentv2 publish of a RuleInstance plus its column relationship, then sync
text: `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/publish` with the identity headers plus `X-INFA-PRODUCT-ID: CDGC` (without it: 500 'Required request header X-INFA-PRODUCT-ID') and two items: an OBJECT INSERT of type `com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.RuleInstance` with a provisional `identity` (`identityType` PROVISIONAL) whose attributes (each prefixed `com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.`) are `RuleType` (the dimension, e.g. Validity), `TechnicalDescription`, `MeasuringMethod` InformaticaCloudDataQuality, `Criticality`, `Target`, `Threshold`, `Frequency` null, `ruleInputPortName`, `ruleOutputPortName` and `TechnicalRuleReference` (the rule specification's frsId), plus `core.name`, `core.description` and `core.origin` (the catalog source id); and a RELATIONSHIP INSERT of type `com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.asscParentDataElementRuleInstance` from the column's external id (`sourceIdentityType` EXTERNAL) to the provisional id (`targetIdentityType` PROVISIONAL). It returns 207 with a 201 per item, the new `DQO-<n>` id and its internal id. Then `POST .../ccgf-ruleautomation/api/v1/dataQuality/sync` with `["<internal id>"]` answers PASSED. This is the request the asset form (New > Business Rules > Data Quality Rule Occurrence > Create) sends; take the port names and the description from L-DQ-109. Scores appear after the source's Data Quality capability runs.
evidence: the UI request captured once and replayed for nine column bindings: 207 with 201 per item, sync PASSED, all ten found by a class search

title: SharePoint Online catalog source: connection URL = the tenant root, Subsite URL = the full site URL
text: The catalog's SharePoint Online scanner asks Azure AD for a token whose resource is the connection URL. With the site URL there (`https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/sites/<site>`) the scan fails with AADSTS500011 (resource principal not found); with the tenant root as URL and a relative subsite (`sites/<site>`) it fails with 'no protocol: sites/<site>/_api/web'. Set URL = `https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com` and Subsite_URL = the full site URL. A catalog source create that omits any Scanner Configuration option answers 500: send all of them (Partition Detection false). The scan then catalogs the site, its libraries, folders and documents.
evidence: two failed scans with those two errors, then a completed Metadata Extraction of a site with 6 folders and 27 documents

title: A catalog source update must repeat the id inside the JSON part
text: `PUT https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>` (multipart, like the create) answers 400 'dataSource id in request path and body do not match' when the JSON omits `id`. GET the definition, change it, set `id` to the path id, PUT it back and read it back.
evidence: 400 without the id, 200 with it; the read-back showed the new connection binding

title: Describe a scanned (technical) asset with a PATCH of core.description alone
text: `PATCH https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/content/v1/assets/<identity>?scheme=internal` with `[{"operation": "add", "segment": "summary", "attributes": {"core.description": "<text>"}}]` sets the description of a table, view or column. A patch that also carries `core.name` answers 400 'Asset name update not supported for technical assets' (business assets accept both, L-CDGC-053). Bursts of these patches hit 429: back off and retry.
evidence: 400 with core.name, success with core.description alone on tables and views; 429 under a burst, then success after a back-off

title: data360 search takes term, bool, wildcard and exists queries; match and match_phrase answer 400
text: On `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/search/api/v1/search` an Elasticsearch `term`, `bool`, `wildcard` or `exists` query works, while `match` and `match_phrase` return 400. To find a glossary term by name, query its class (`core.classType` = `com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.BusinessTerm`) and compare `core.name` client-side. Term names are not unique across domains: an idempotent create must match the name AND the parent domain (the domain's identity inside the term's `core.location`), or it reuses another domain's term.
evidence: 400 for match and match_phrase; a name-only lookup returned another domain's term of the same name

title: Read a rule specification's ports and description headless: extensionPoint RuleSpecificationTx.getDescription
text: `POST https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/saas/api/v2/extensionPoint` with header `icSessionId` and `{"alias": "RuleSpecificationTx", "method": "getDescription", "payload": "{\"ruleId\": \"<frsId>\"}"}` returns a JSON string whose `ruleModel` (itself a JSON string) holds `name`, `description`, `fields` (the inputs, with name and type), `outputFields` (usually one, `Output`) and `testData`. The catalog's rule occurrence form calls it to map the input port and to fill the read-only TechnicalDescription (L-CDGC-145); use it to build an occurrence headless (L-CDGC-161).
evidence: 200 for an imported and a reused rule specification; fields and outputFields matched the rule specifications' ports

title: Create an intelligent structure model headless from a sample file: six calls, about 4 s
text: All on `https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com`. (1) `GET /saas/api/v2/intelligentstructure/getAtlanticWidget` (header `icSessionId`). (2) `POST /structurediscovery-service/atlweb/api/v3.0/validateWidget`, empty body, with cookie `USER_SESSION=<session>` and header `IDS-SESSION-ID: <session>`: `{"valid": true}` plus the service cookies (`JSESSIONID`, `XSRF-TOKEN`, ...). (3) `POST /structurediscovery-service/upload?<resumable params>`: multipart, the same params as form fields and the sample as part `file`, headers `X-CSRF-TOKEN: <XSRF-TOKEN cookie>`, `X-CSRF-PARAM: _csrf`, `X-Ajax-call: true` (all later POSTs too); it returns `inputText` and the learner used. (4) `POST .../RunDataPreview` with form `runData` (fileName, text = inputText, key, learnerUse, treeType horizontal) returns `aModelString`, the CLAIRE-discovered model, in under a second. (5) `POST .../getStructure` with form `formData` (name, description, learnerUse, fileName, aModelString) returns the model JSON. (6) `POST /saas/api/v2/intelligentstructure/create?containerId=<v3 folder id>` (header `icSessionId`) with `{"orgId": "<v3 org id>", "@type": "structureDefinition", "name", "modelName", "description", "amodel": <the step-5 JSON as a string>}` returns the structureDefinition and its v2 id. The model reads back on v2 and v3 and opens in the designer like a UI-made one. Newer evidence: L-CDI-297.
evidence: two models created from a spreadsheet and a PDF; read back on v2 and v3; per-call responses kept

title: Structure Discovery service: the session as cookie AND header, then X-CSRF-TOKEN on every POST, or a 404
text: The ISD service accepts the platform session only as both cookie `USER_SESSION` and header `IDS-SESSION-ID`: the cookie alone returns 200 `{"valid": false}` (a refusal dressed as success) and no session returns a 302 to the login page. After validateWidget, every POST must carry `X-CSRF-TOKEN` equal to the `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie the service set; without it, or with `X-XSRF-TOKEN` instead, Tomcat answers 404, not 403, which reads like a wrong path. GETs need no CSRF header. The unauthenticated 302 points at a plain http:// URL; a client that follows it through a corporate proxy reports a 504 after about 45 s, so probe without following redirects.
evidence: controlled test: no CSRF header 404, X-XSRF-TOKEN 404, X-CSRF-TOKEN 200; cookie-only validateWidget 200 valid:false

title: What CLAIRE structure discovery makes of a PDF and a spreadsheet: review the names before building the mapping
text: A PDF goes through the `PdfToModel` learner: the document becomes key/value records (header, details and footer groups) with dates typed as dates, and a free-text block that spans two lines is left out (it reaches the Unidentified port). The Excel learner splits code-like values such as `ABC-123` into `_token` and `_number` fields and can name a table-row group with a semantic guess unrelated to the content. Field names keep their spaces in the model; Structure Parser ports are cleaned to letters, digits and underscores, and every output field is a string(255) (the real types stay in the model). Fix names before the mapping is built, because the mapping copies them (the service exposes `singleNodeModification`, `mergeNodes` and `splitNode`; not exercised). Was believed 2026-10-06; overturned by L-CDI-229.
evidence: a tax-form PDF and a price-list spreadsheet discovered; the extracted fields compared with the source documents

title: A Structure Parser stores the model's v2 id and a copy of the model: model edits arrive only after Synchronize
text: In a mapping, a Structure Parser transformation keeps `isdModelId` = the intelligent structure model's v2 id (the export's `repoInfo.repoHandle`, not the v3 id) and `modelString` = a copy of the model, with `parserMode` isdMode, `inputType` FILE, `outputType` Relational and an empty `connectionId` for the CLAIRE engine. Its input group takes `FilePath` (string 4096) and `Data` (binary); it has one output group per model group plus `Unidentified`. Because the model is copied, a later edit of the model reaches the mapping only after Synchronize. The designer reads the detail from `GET /da/web.saas.service/saasinfo/structureDiscoveryDetail?id=<v2 id>`, which needs a designer session. Was believed 2026-10-06; overturned by L-CDI-230.
evidence: read from the designer code and an export package of a model; detail JSON captured for three models

title: Headless Chromium with the Private and Local Network Access checks off drove the catalog, MCC and the mapping designer behind a proxy again
text: From a laptop behind the kind of transparent proxy L-UI-011 describes, Playwright's bundled Chromium, headless, launched with `--no-sandbox --disable-features=BlockInsecurePrivateNetworkRequests,PrivateNetworkAccessSendPreflights,PrivateNetworkAccessRespectPreflightResults,LocalNetworkAccessChecks,LocalNetworkAccessChecksWarn`, a saved storage state and at most one scripted login rendered and finished work in Metadata Command Center (catalog source pages, lineage configuration), Data Governance and Catalog (asset pages, the lineage tab, new-asset forms with multi-step pickers) and the Data Integration mapping designer. Without the flags the console looped on authentication and stayed blank. Data Profiling and Administrator were not retested, so L-UI-011 is disputed: try this flag set before moving UI work to a cloud host.
evidence: screenshots and captured write requests from all three consoles in one day; a blank auth loop without the flags

title: Driving catalog pickers with Playwright: exact button names, Finish on the last step, check the radio input itself
text: In the catalog's multi-step pickers (for example a rule occurrence's Primary Data Element: catalog source > data set > data element) the stepper tabs are buttons too, so `get_by_role('button', name='Select')` matches the tab 'Select System or Catalog Source' and sends the wizard back to step 1: pass `exact=True`. The last step's button is 'Finish'; a parameter-mapping step ends with 'OK'. Search inside a picker by clicking its box and typing, then click the row by exact text. Radio buttons such as 'Pick an existing rule' draw the input over the label, so a label click times out ('input intercepts pointer events'): call `check(force=True)` on `input[type=radio][value=...]`. Use the form once to capture its write request, then replay that over REST (L-CDGC-161).
evidence: a substring match reset the wizard twice; exact names, Finish and the forced radio check completed the form and created the asset

title: The intelligent structure model editor spins forever in headless Chromium: wait for openStructureData instead
text: In headless Chromium the model editor keeps showing a spinner, for models made in the UI and over REST alike. A 200 response from the service's `openStructureData` request is the real 'loaded' signal: wait on that response, not on the spinner.
evidence: spinner on every model tried; openStructureData 200 each time

title: A message to a running background agent starts a second copy of it
text: Sending a message to a subagent or workflow agent that is still running does not reach the running copy: the harness resumes the agent from its transcript in a new process, so two copies then work the same task, the same UI session and the same objects in parallel. Do not message running agents. Read the output file for progress, wait for the completion notice, then resume the agent with the message. If it already happened, stop one copy at once and give the other sole ownership.
evidence: two copies of one agent writing the same scratch files after one message; stopping the parent workflow stopped the original

title: A catalog Data Quality run scores each rule occurrence on the RuleInstance itself: value, totalCount, exception
text: `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id>` with `capabilityNames: ['Data Quality']` on a relational source that has rule occurrences runs a Rule Profiling Task and a Batch Profiling Task on the Secure Agent (about 15 min for ten occurrences on five small tables). Afterwards each RuleInstance carries `com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.value` (the score in percent), `totalCount` (rows checked), `exception` (rows that failed) and `scannedTime` (epoch ms) in its selfAttributes: `GET https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/search/v1/assets/<internal id>?scheme=internal&segments=selfAttributes`. Occurrences created over REST (L-CDGC-161) score like ones made in the UI. Scoring curated tables whose loads already reject bad rows gives 100 everywhere; score the raw layer too to show what the rules caught.
evidence: one 884 s run; ten occurrences read back with value 100.0, totalCount 1 to 72, exception 0

title: CDI SharePoint Online connector: a Graph-scoped refresh token gives 0 objects while Test Connection passes
text: The CDI Sharepoint Online connector calls SharePoint's own REST API (`https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/sites/<site>/_api/...`), not Microsoft Graph, and renews its delegated token without asking for a scope, so it receives a token for whatever resource the stored refresh token was minted for. With a refresh token minted for Graph every metadata call answers 401: the object picker shows 0 objects and a refresh gives `infa.cloud.OBJECT_SEARCH_FAILED`, yet Test Connection passes. Mint the refresh token for `https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/.default offline_access` (redeeming an existing refresh token of the same app registration with that scope works headless, no sign-in) and store it in the connection.
evidence: 401 on every _api call and 0 objects with the Graph token; the SharePoint-scoped token listed all objects of the site

title: Test Connection proves only that a delegated token renews: prove access with an object browse
text: For OAuth connectors that renew a delegated token, a successful Test Connection says the refresh worked, not that the token can read metadata. Prove access by browsing objects: the designer's object picker, or `GET https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/da/w3.model/object/cloud/saas:<v2ConnId>@com.informatica.metadata.saas.Connection/search/?connKind=READ&searchRequest={"pageNumber":1,"maxRecordsCount":200,"context":{"txType":"SOURCE_TYPE","engineType":"CLOUD_NATIVE"}}` with a designer session (`totalRecords`, `records[].attributes`).
evidence: a passing Test Connection beside an empty picker; the browse returned the objects after the token fix

title: What the CDI SharePoint Online connector reads: one object per list or library, root rows, and a recursive download of every file
text: Objects are one per SharePoint list or document library, hidden system lists included; there is no site, version, permission or list-catalog object. Reading a document library returns one row per folder or file at the library root with 12 properties (TimeCreated, TimeLastModified, UniqueId, ServerRelativeUrl, Name, ProgID, WelcomePage, IsWOPIEnabled, Exists, ExistsWithException, ExistsAllowThrowForPolicyFailures, ItemCount, which is empty for files); size, ETag, version label, author, editor and content type are not exposed. The same read downloads every file of the library, recursively, to the connection's Attachment_File_Path, which must already exist and be writable by the agent user; Preserve Directory Structure = YES keeps the library tree. Preview Data shows only the root rows and ignores the advanced properties. As a source: single object or parameter, filter yes, sort no; as a target: Insert, Update, Upsert, Delete, Data Driven; lookups (cached and uncached) use the read settings.
evidence: a run that landed the library's root rows and downloaded all 27 documents (sizes matching the library); field list and capabilities read from the designer

title: One row per file from a SharePoint library: Indirect File Path with absolute, URL-encoded wildcard patterns
text: Set the source's advanced property Indirect File Path to an agent-side text file with one pattern per line, each a full server-relative path with spaces written `%20` (`/sites/<site>/Shared%20Documents/<folder>/*/*.*`; `*` and `?` work). Each matching file becomes one row and is downloaded. Relative or unencoded patterns produce broken URLs (404 or 403 in the session log). A `*` directly under the library also walks SharePoint's internal Forms folder and aborts the read with 'String index out of range: -1', so list the business folders by name. Use the flow run order when two flows of one mapping both download, so the downloads do not overlap.
evidence: three runs returned 0 rows while the pattern format was wrong; the final pattern file returned one row per file (27)

title: Unbounded Snowflake VARCHAR targets make the CDI writer run out of Java memory: give every target column a length
text: A Snowflake target table whose columns are plain `VARCHAR` (16,777,216 characters) made the CDI Snowflake writer fail with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded`: it sized its buffer from the declared lengths (a block of about 436 MB for 21 such columns). Create target tables with `VARCHAR(n)`, or set the native precision in Target Fields > Edit Metadata; there, type the value and press Enter, because a pasted value does not commit.
evidence: the first run failed with that error; the same mapping with explicit lengths of 20 to 1,200 ran in 93 s

title: Connector lookups have no operation context of their own; saving a mapping redeploys its tasks
text: Designer calls that take a connection operation context accept READ and WRITE only: a lookup uses the READ settings, so there is no separate lookup configuration to look for. Saving a mapping in the designer ends with `POST /saas/app/da/dTemplatesXHR.do?actionMethod=autodeploy` (`daId` = the v2 mapping id), which redeploys every task on it, so a mapping save changes what the next task run executes without touching the task.
evidence: designer request log of a lookup's metadata calls and of a mapping save followed by the autodeploy call

title: Stitch a mapping's SharePoint connection to the SharePoint catalog source: MERGE its reference onto the Site
text: An IICS catalog source can name a connection reference after the connection's v2 id instead of its name (`<iicsSourceId>_<connId>://<connId>~core.DataSource`), so list references by `core.reference` and class `core.DataSource`, not by connection name. MERGE-assign it (L-CDGC-159) to the SharePoint catalog source's Site: target `{"externalId": "<spSourceId>://<site title>~com.infa.odin.models.file.sharepoint.Site", "origin": "<spSourceId>", "isCaseSensitive": false, "location": "<spSourceId>://<spSourceId>/<site title>"}`. Lineage then reads SharePoint document library > mapping task > warehouse table, with the library resolved to the catalog's own asset.
evidence: job COMPLETED; the table's lineage walk showed the library (SharePoint source) feeding the mapping task that writes it

title: A Snowflake extraction ends PARTIAL_COMPLETED when the role cannot read tags, although every table and view was extracted
text: The agent-side scanner log (`<agent_home>/apps/Metadata_Foundation_Agent/data/workspaces/<source>-.../logs/*_Sync.log`) showed 'Unable to resolve TAGS objects from SNOWFLAKE for filter ...' and 'Total objects processed count N is the same as objects count with errors. Status will be altered to Partially completed', while its 'Overwriting table definition' lines showed every table and view (with view SQL) extracted and the new tables appeared in search. The job tree carries no message for it: read the scanner log before treating a partial as a failure.
evidence: a PARTIAL_COMPLETED job with those log lines; the new tables and views were in search right after it

title: In the mapping designer, copy a selection of transformations to clone a whole flow
text: Selecting a flow's transformations and copying them duplicates the flow with its links, edited field precisions and field mappings; rename the copies, repoint the source settings, and order the flows in Flow Run Order. It is the quickest way to build a second, similar flow in the same mapping.
evidence: a second flow built by copy, then repointed; both flows ran in one task

title: Paging data360 search with from/size and no sort drops assets silently: sort on core.identity
text: `POST https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/search/api/v1/search` paged with `from`/`size` and no `sort` returns overlapping pages: two consecutive full reads of one catalog source returned 882 and 970 of its tables, views and columns, so lookups by name failed at random (a link script reported existing assets as missing). Add `"sort": [{"core.identity": {"order": "asc"}}]` and filter on `core.origin` + `elementType` OBJECT instead of a wildcard on `core.externalId` (which also matches relationship documents): the read became complete and repeatable (1,311 fetched, 1,311 unique). A sort on `core.externalId` returned no hits at all.
evidence: 882 vs 970 assets on unsorted reads; 1,311/1,311 unique with the sort, twice in a row; 0 hits with an externalId sort

title: A catalog rule occurrence that binds a decimal-input rule to a text column is skipped without an error: bind a typed view column
text: A RuleInstance whose rule specification takes a decimal input, bound to a text (VARCHAR) column of a raw landing table, was accepted by publish and sync (L-CDGC-161) but never scored: the source's Data Quality run ended PARTIAL_COMPLETED with no message in the job tree, no profiling job for that table on the agent and no value on the RuleInstance. A view over the same table with `TRY_TO_NUMBER(<col>, 18, 4)` as a numeric column (non-numbers become NULL and fail a 'filled in' rule), cataloged by a Metadata Extraction and bound instead (view columns are `...~com.infa.odin.models.relational.ViewColumn`), scored on the next run although the view was never profiled. Bind rules to columns of the rule's input type.
evidence: text-column occurrence: no score after a PARTIAL_COMPLETED run; typed-view occurrence: 98.63 % (73 rows, 1 failed) after a COMPLETED run

title: What CLAIRE structure discovery makes of a PDF and a spreadsheet, and the types a Structure Parser emits
text: A PDF goes through the `PdfToModel` learner: the document becomes key/value records (header, details and footer groups) with dates typed as dates, and a free-text block that spans two lines is left out. The Excel learner splits code-like values into a token and a number (`ABC-001` becomes `ABC` + `1`: the separator and leading zeros are lost, so such a code cannot be rebuilt), and a banner line above a table becomes a field NAME with an empty value. Structure Parser output ports take the model's types (bigint, decimal(10,2), string(n)), not string(255) everywhere; they load into VARCHAR target columns without complaint, with numbers re-rendered (40 becomes 40.0). Field names are cleaned to letters, digits and underscores (`Customer account no.` becomes `Customer_account_no_`). Fix names before building the mapping: the mapping copies them.
evidence: three models (a spreadsheet price list, a pricing addendum, a tax-form PDF) parsed in one mapping run; ports and values compared with the source files

title: A Structure Parser stores '@<v3 id>' of its model plus a copy of the model; the designer resolves the model by its v2 id
text: In an exported mapping the Structure Parser carries `isdModelId: "@<v3 id of the model>"`, `isdLastModify`, `modelString` (a copy of the model, so a later model edit reaches the mapping only after Synchronize) and a `passthrough` flag per output group. The designer looks the model up by its v2 id: `GET /frs/api/v1/Documents?$filter=documentType eq 'SAAS_STRUCTURE_DISCOVERY' and repoInfo/repoHandle eq '<v2 id>'`, `GET /da/web.saas.service/saasinfo/structureDiscoveryDetail?id=<v2 id>` (needs a designer session), and fills the Output Fields tab from `POST /structurediscovery-service/groupsWithXpath` (form body `aModelString=<model string>`). Input group `Input_Group` takes `FilePath` (string 4096) or `Data` (binary); there is one output group per model group plus `Unidentified`. Newer evidence: L-CDI-298.
evidence: the export of a three-flow parsing mapping (isdModelId = '@' + the models' v3 ids) and the designer request log

title: Parse every document of a folder with a Structure Parser and keep the source file on each parsed row
text: Source = a warehouse view that lists the documents (one row per file with its path), filtered per flow on folder and extension in the source's Advanced filter; an Expression turns the server path into the local path of the connector's download folder (`REPLACESTR(1, PATH, '<server prefix>', '<local folder>')`) and feeds the parser's `FilePath`. In the parser's Output Fields tab, tick Passthrough on each output group: every incoming field except the one mapped to FilePath/Data then comes out on that group, so file name and path land on every parsed row. Land the `Unidentified` group too, so content no model can place never drops out silently. Give each document type its own flow and use Flow Run Order.
evidence: one run parsed 8 documents of 3 types into 32 rows, each with its file name and path; 0 rows unidentified

title: Changing the model on a Structure Parser clears its field mapping and every link
text: Swapping the intelligent structure model of an existing Structure Parser (for example on a copied flow) removes its field mapping, its links and the Passthrough ticks; re-link, re-map FilePath and re-tick Passthrough afterwards. Linking from a parser with several output groups opens a 'Select Output Group' dialog; dropping a new transformation onto an existing link keeps the group.
evidence: a copied flow lost its mapping and links when its model changed; re-linked and re-ticked, it ran

title: Snowflake source fields import at 16,777,216 characters: trim them, and know that the Advanced filter is passed verbatim
text: A Snowflake table or view with unbounded VARCHAR columns imports into a mapping source with precision 16,777,216 per field, the same memory risk as on targets (L-CDI-227): delete the fields the flow does not use and lower the precision of the rest in Edit Metadata. The source's Advanced filter is sent to Snowflake verbatim as the WHERE clause, and the reader selects only the fields used downstream. Preview Data ignores both the filter and the field edits, so verify with a run.
evidence: session log of the reader's SELECT (fields used + the filter as WHERE); preview showing unfiltered rows

title: Small mapping-designer traps: date fields rename themselves, descriptions lose symbols, pasted copies get a 1
text: In the New Field dialog, choosing a date/time type resets the name to 'NewField': rename it afterwards (double-click the field and type). The mapping description strips `<`, `>` and apostrophes, so write those in words. Pasted copies of transformations get '1' appended to each name. Arrange All puts each flow on its own row.
evidence: each seen while building a three-flow mapping in a headless browser

title: A PostgreSQL table with an array column is not profiled at all, while every profiling session reports success
text: A PostgreSQL catalog source's Data Profiling ended PARTIAL_COMPLETED after 34 minutes with no message in the job tree, and every `s_cp_*_session.log` on the agent (82 of 82) ended 'Session run completed successfully'. The catalog showed exactly the tables that have an array column (`text[]`) with `core.lastProfiledState` 'Not Profiled' and `core.profiled` false: no profiling session was ever created for them. Tables with jsonb columns were profiled. So the connector's habit of skipping array columns drops the whole table. Find such tables with a catalog search on the source for `core.profiled` false and compare their column types; profile a copy in which arrays are cast to text (a landing table or a view added to the scope).
evidence: 86 tables and views scanned, 82 profiled; the 4 not profiled were the only tables with text[] columns; 37 jsonb columns elsewhere did not block profiling

title: The profiling exclude filter is a Profiling Filter Config group with Filter Pivot 'Exclude Metadata'
text: In a catalog source's `typeCapabilities` > Data Profiling, an exclude is a `Profiling Filter Config` group with `Filter Pivot` ["Exclude Metadata"], `Filter Type` ["Tables"] and `Filter Value` ["<schema>.<table>"], placed next to the include groups (`Include Metadata`, `<schema>.*`). The string was read from a source whose exclude had been set in the UI and then sent in a multipart create: it persisted on read-back and the excluded tables got no profiling session. Use it for tables the reading role may not select, which would otherwise end the run PARTIAL_COMPLETED.
evidence: exclude groups for 4, 4 and 14 tables in three new sources persisted on read-back; no profiling session for any excluded table

title: A mapping with many pipelines opens a reader and a writer connection per pipeline even in a strict load order, and they linger
text: A landing mapping with 49 source-to-target pipelines, each in its own target load order group (the session log shows group N, concurrent set 1, one after another), still opened a new reader and a new writer JDBC connection for every pipeline, and the connections closed lazily. With pipelines of about 0.3 s, a database role with CONNECTION LIMIT 10 failed at the 24th pipeline with `[SDK_APP_COM_20000] too many connections for role`, after 3,643 rows had landed (the task ends failed; the earlier tables stay loaded). Sampling `pg_stat_activity` every second during later runs showed peaks of 14 reader and 11 writer connections for 49 to 70 pipelines. Give the roles such a mapping uses a limit of about 40 (after checking the server's max_connections headroom), or split the mapping.
evidence: failure at pipeline 24 with a limit of 10; with a limit of 40, runs of 49, 61 and 70 pipelines succeeded (8,208 / 11,732 / 8,993 rows) with peaks of 14 reader / 11 writer connections

title: Generate a sampled landing layer from the database catalog and validate it with zero IDMC jobs
text: Build each table's field list from `information_schema.columns` filtered by `has_column_privilege(<read role>, <table>, <column>, 'SELECT')`, so column-level grants are respected. Give every table a source with an SQL query: simple types keep their type (integer, bigint, numeric(p,s), timestamptz, date; timestamp converted with `AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'`), everything else becomes `::text` with a precision from the measured maximum length, and bytea and free-text bodies are left out. Write the aliases bare (`"col"::text AS col`): PostgreSQL accepts any keyword as a column label after AS, and quoted aliases defeat simple SQL-to-field checks. Sample inside the query with `ORDER BY <time column> DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT $$<cap>`, using one in-out parameter (retention NEVER) per class of table, so scaling up later means changing one value. Before any run, EXPLAIN every query as the read role and run the target DDL inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK: neither costs a job.
evidence: 180 queries EXPLAINed clean and the DDL rollback test was clean; then 3 of 3 mapping runs succeeded on the first full attempt with row counts equal to the planned samples

title: PostgreSQL n_live_tup can be stale by orders of magnitude: count rows before planning a landing or a profile
text: In a PostgreSQL database that was restored or bulk-loaded without a later ANALYZE, `pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup` read 2 for a table holding about 1,130 rows. A plan built on those statistics would have treated 34 of 75 non-empty tables as empty. When row counts decide what to land, profile or skip, use `count(*)` (cheap on small tables), and check `last_analyze` / `last_autoanalyze`: stale statistics also mislead the query planner, so fix them at the source.
evidence: 41 non-empty tables by n_live_tup against 75 by count(*) in one database

title: On PostgreSQL 15+ the PostgreSQL connector's primary/foreign-key metadata query fails, so imports carry no keys
text: The connector's key-metadata statement (the JDBC getImportedKeys/getExportedKeys SQL that starts `SELECT distinct null as pkcat,n.nspname as pkschema,...`) contains `CASE f.confdeltype WHEN 'c' THEN 0WHEN 'n' ...`: a numeric literal followed directly by a keyword. PostgreSQL 15 and later reject that with `ERROR: trailing junk after numeric literal at or near "0WHEN"`. The error is only in the database log (one per table read, e.g. 360 during a landing run of 180 tables); the mapping runs succeed, but imported objects and catalog assets come back without primary and foreign keys, so relationship discovery and key-based checks get nothing. Grep the server log for `0WHEN` to confirm. Workarounds: declare keys yourself in the rules and joins, or read keys from `pg_constraint` with a query of your own; check a newer connector build before relying on catalog keys.
evidence: 360 x 'trailing junk after numeric literal at or near "0WHEN"' on PostgreSQL 16.15 during three landing runs through the native connector; the runs themselves succeeded

title: DROP OWNED BY inside one database also revokes the role's CONNECT on every database: never use it to trim one database's grants
text: To remove an integration role's grants from a single database, `DROP OWNED BY <role>` was run while connected to that database. Besides the objects and grants in that database, PostgreSQL also revokes the role's privileges on SHARED objects, which include CONNECT on every database of the cluster. The integration's next run failed within seconds with `permission denied for database <another db>` on its first connection test, although no grant in that other database had been touched. Remove one database's grants with `REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA <s> FROM <role>` (plus USAGE on the schemas and CONNECT on that one database) instead, and after any role cleanup re-run a connection test for every database the role still needs. Repair: `GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE <db> TO <role>` for each database; table-level grants in the other databases survive.
evidence: one DROP OWNED in one database removed CONNECT from 9 databases; a mapping task failed on its first connection test; CONNECT re-granted on 9 databases and the 15 positive/negative access checks passed again

title: A content-API PATCH that links a term to an asset also starts a 'Content Publish Task' job
text: `PATCH https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/content/v1/assets/<assetIdentity>?scheme=internal` with `[{"operation":"add","segment":"glossary","items":[{"core.identity":"<termIdentity>"}]}]` (L-CDGC-056) is followed by one CDGC system job 'Content Publish Task' (job category SYSTEM_JOB), exactly like a domain or term create (L-CDGC-153). A link script that sends one PATCH per link therefore costs one catalog job per link, so a plan that counts glossary PATCHes as free under-counts by the number of links. Budget one job per PATCH, or batch the links in one publish call (L-CDGC-174). The v2 activity-log job windows did not move after 28 of these jobs, so a guard that reads only the activity log misses them (L-IPU-055). Whether a rule-occurrence publish (L-CDGC-161) starts one is untested: the job list cannot answer it afterwards (L-CDGC-175), so read the list within minutes of the first publish.
evidence: One glossary-link PATCH followed by 1 Content Publish Task within 40 s; activity-log windows unchanged after 28 such jobs

title: Batch term-to-asset links in one ccgf-contentv2 publish: one Content Publish Task per call, not per link
text: `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/publish` with the identity headers plus `X-INFA-PRODUCT-ID: CDGC` and `{"items":[{"operation":"INSERT","elementType":"RELATIONSHIP","type":"com.infa.ccgf.models.governance.IClassTechnicalGlossaryBase","fromIdentity":"<asset externalId>","toIdentity":"BT-<n>","sourceIdentityType":"EXTERNAL","targetIdentityType":"EXTERNAL","attributes":{"core.curationStatus":"ACCEPTED","core.channels":["MANUAL"],"core.inferred":false}}, ...]}` answers 207 with a 201 per item and starts ONE Content Publish Task for the whole call. The relationship matches what the content PATCH writes (source = the harvested asset, target = the term, `core.associationKind` semanticKind) and the term shows ACCEPTED on the asset's `glossary` segment. Without `core.channels` and `core.inferred` the link is still accepted and shown, but its relationship document has empty channels and no inferred flag, unlike UI or PATCH links. The asset external id is the harvested form `<catalogSourceId>://<db>/<schema>/<table>[/<column>]~com.infa.odin.models.relational.<Table|Column>` (L-CDGC-057). Skip pairs that are already linked, then read back each asset (`/data360/search/v1/assets/<identity>?scheme=internal&segments=glossary`) or search `elementType` RELATIONSHIP with this `type` and `core.targetIdentity` in your term ids.
evidence: 2 links in one publish: 207, 2 x 201, 1 Content Publish Task; then 96 links in one publish: 207, 96 x 201, 1 Content Publish Task; 99 of 99 links read back on 90 assets

title: Content Publish Task jobs show PARTIAL_COMPLETED before COMPLETED and are purged from the job list within minutes
text: Right after a glossary write, its Content Publish Task (one child, 'Commit Task') can read PARTIAL_COMPLETED; about two minutes later the Commit Task runs again and the job turns COMPLETED. One job's Commit Task stayed RUNNING for more than 20 minutes while its term was already Published and searchable. Completed Content Publish Tasks then drop out of `GET .../data360/observable/api/v1/jobs` (the list reports `partialResult` true and its total shrinks), and the single-job route `observable/v1/jobs/<jobId>` answers 500 for them, within about 20 minutes. Judge a glossary write by reading the assets back (`core.assetLifecycle` Published), not by the job status; keep these jobs out of failure alerts; and count them for a job budget at write time (one per create, PATCH or publish call), because a later read of the job list under-counts.
evidence: 25 publish jobs from one load of 25 creates: 15 COMPLETED, 9 PARTIAL_COMPLETED and 1 RUNNING on the first read, 23 COMPLETED and 1 RUNNING two minutes later; 20 minutes later only the running one was still listed and by-id reads of the others returned 500; all 24 terms and the domain Published

title: A PostgreSQL table with an enum (user-defined type) column is not profiled either; profile a copy with the enum cast to text
text: Same symptom as array columns (L-CDGC-171): in a PostgreSQL catalog source of 128 tables, every non-empty table that has a column of a user-defined enum type (for example a status or kind column) ended `core.lastProfiledState` 'Not Profiled' while the scan reported PARTIAL_COMPLETED and no failed session. Seven of seven such tables were skipped, including the core booking and payment tables, while tables with jsonb columns profiled. Find them by joining the source's `core.profiled` false assets with `information_schema.columns.data_type = 'USER-DEFINED'`; profile a landed copy (enum landed as text) or a view that casts the enum with `::text`.
evidence: 7 of 7 non-empty tables with enum columns not profiled in one PostgreSQL source; no table with an enum column was profiled; jsonb tables profiled

title: PostgreSQL catalog source: Filter Type 'Tables' catalogs no views, and 'All' also pulls every stored procedure; give each include value one filter group per type (Tables, Views)
text: In a PostgreSQL catalog source, a Metadata Extraction include filter (`Filter Pivot` Include Metadata, `Filter Value` <schema>.*) with `Filter Type` 'Tables' catalogs base tables only: every view in the included schemas is silently missing, with no warning in the scan. Switching the filter type to 'All' brings the views in, but it also extracts every stored procedure and function, with its body, into the catalog. To get tables and views and nothing else, add two filter groups per include value, one with `Filter Type` 'Tables' and one with 'Views'. A later metadata-only scan with that filter removes the procedures an 'All' scan added (`Metadata Change Option` Delete). Before you trust a PostgreSQL source's lineage or glossary links to a view, count its View assets: zero is this gotcha, not an empty schema.
evidence: 8 PostgreSQL sources with 'Tables' filters held 0 View assets although their schemas contain views; one source scanned with 'All' cataloged 119 stored procedures; after one metadata-only rescan with Tables + Views groups: 67 tables and views, 0 procedures

title: CDGC lineage parsing of PostgreSQL views fails on ordered-set aggregates and on table names without a schema; the scan ends PARTIAL_COMPLETED while columns and profiles are complete
text: A PostgreSQL source whose views include `percentile_cont(...) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...)` or a table referenced without its schema (resolved by search_path at run time) ends PARTIAL_COMPLETED: the lineage step cannot parse those view definitions, so they get no view-to-table lineage. Columns, keys, profiles and classification of the same views are complete. Read which assets failed before treating such a scan as broken, and schema-qualify every table name in view SQL you control. A rescan does not change the outcome while the view text stays the same.
evidence: 2 of 67 tables and views in one PostgreSQL source failed lineage parsing (one ordered-set aggregate, one unqualified table name); the source stayed PARTIAL_COMPLETED after a metadata-only rescan; all other assets complete

title: Reach a PostgreSQL that sits only on an internal Docker network from a Secure Agent on another VM: a socat proxy narrowed by range=, a pinned proxy address and a DOCKER-USER drop
text: When the database container is attached only to an `internal` Docker network, the Secure Agent on another VM cannot reach it. Do not re-network or restart the database. Run a small proxy container (socat, read-only, all capabilities dropped, non-root) attached to that internal network and to its own bridge, and publish it only on the host's private address. As built first, it was open to every VM in the subnet and every container on the host. Three measures close it: (1) `TCP4-LISTEN:<port>,fork,reuseaddr,range=<agent ip>/32`, which works because Docker's DNAT keeps the client's source address; (2) a fixed address for the proxy on the internal network, chosen outside the low range the network's IPAM hands out, so pg_hba can admit exactly that address and only the integration role; and (3) an iptables DOCKER-USER rule that drops the published port unless the source is the agent. The database's pg_hba sees the proxy's internal address, never the agent's, so an hba line keyed on the internal subnet admits anything that comes through the proxy. The DOCKER-USER rule does not survive a host reboot; re-apply it from the same script. Also turn IP masquerade off on the proxy's own bridge, so the proxy cannot reach out.
evidence: before: proxy reachable from other VMs in the /24 and from local containers; after range= + pinned address + DOCKER-USER drop: only the agent host gets a PostgreSQL answer, other roles from the proxy address are rejected by pg_hba, and all 10 IDMC connection tests pass

title: Kafka and AMQP (JMS) listener connections author headless in an import package: the Camel javaConnector values and the consumer and producer elements
text: An AI_CONNECTION for Kafka or for AMQP is authored from scratch like any other package asset (L-CAI-020) and published over REST to a Secure Agent's Process Server. Kafka: `<agent><agent name></agent>`; attributes `kafkaHost`, `kafkaPort`, `additionalBrokers`, `otherAttributesCommon`, `Use SSL` and `Use SASL`; `<consumers><consumer name="<eventSource>" typeName="KafkaConsumer" enabled="true|false">` with `loadBalance`, `topic`, `groupId`, `contentFormat` (TEXT, XML or JSON), `simplifyContent` and `otherAttributesProducerConsumer`; `<producers><producer name="<eventTarget>" typeName="KafkaProducer">` with `topic`, `groupId`, `contentFormat` and `otherAttributesProducerConsumer`; then `<javaConnector xmlns="http://schemas.informatica.com/appmodules/screenflow/2014/04/avosConnectors.xsd" plugin="Camel" type="KAFKA" uuid="c5d3f9bc-95ba-48e6-99df-5bca133b44b3" name="KAFKA" agentOnly="true"/>`. AMQP 1.0 (a JMS broker such as ActiveMQ Artemis): `type="AMQP"` and `uuid="59b13626-0180-4d48-a749-38f8f33f7b18"`, attributes `User Name`, `Password`, `Virtual Host`, `Host`, `Port`, `Use SSL` and `Query Parameters`, and a consumer `typeName="AMQP Source"` with `Destination Type` (queue), `Destination`, `Payload Format` (Xml, Json, Text or Binary), `Objectlist Field Name`, `Dead Letter Queue Name`, `Custom Message ID`, `Enable Load Balancing` and `Other Attributes`. `plugin="Camel"` is what the agent's connector search renders for the provider type 'Event-Connectors'. Other Attributes take Camel endpoint option names joined with `&` (consumers: `autoOffsetReset`, `consumersCount`, `maxPollRecords`, `maxPollIntervalMs`, `autoCommitIntervalMs`; producers: `requestRequiredAcks`, `enableIdempotence`, `retries`, `maxInFlightRequest`, `maxRequestSize`). The AMQP connector uses the agent's bundled Qpid JMS client: SASL PLAIN against the broker worked with no extra jars and no agent restart. Kafka was proven over PLAINTEXT; Kafka SSL and SASL are untested. Supersedes L-CAI-117.
evidence: Kafka probe connection published, consumers subscribed and records dispatched (2026-10-08); AMQP probe connected with SASL PLAIN and dispatched 2 TextMessages (2026-10-08); 2 Kafka and 1 AMQP production connections published and consuming for hours (2026-10-08)

title: Kafka and JMS event sources, listener processes and fault handling can only be authored in the Process Designer
text: Recorded with the CAI authoring wall (L-CAI-025) and in the capability map: event sources (Kafka, JMS), listener processes and fault and retry design were taken to be designer-only because nobody had authored them any other way. Kafka and AMQP connections, event-bound processes and catch handlers were authored in import packages and published over REST. Was believed 2026-09-22 to 2026-10-07; overturned by L-CAI-116.
evidence: never authored outside the designer before; the authoring probes of 2026-07-25 and 2026-09-22 did not cover event sources

title: Event-bound (listener) process XML, and what a Kafka event carries
text: Bind a process to an event source in its deployment: `<deployment><targetLocation><agent name></targetLocation><event eventSource="<conn>:<eventSource>"/></deployment>`, and declare the input `<parameter name="event" type="reference">` with the options `referenceTo` = `<conn>:KafkaMessage` (or `<conn>:AMQPMessage`), `required`, `isCopy` and `guid` = the connection's GUID. A Kafka event carries `body` (a string for contentFormat TEXT), `headers` as repeated `<headers><name>..</name><value>..</value></headers>` elements without a namespace (read one with `string(($input.event/headers[name = '<header>']/value)[1])`), `topic` and `partitionId`; `messageKey` stays EMPTY on consume, so send the business key and the message id as headers.
evidence: 2 records consumed and their headers read with that XPath (2026-10-08); listener processes in production for hours (2026-10-08)

title: Start a new listener safely: publish its connection with the consumer enabled='false', publish the processes, then republish the connection with enabled='true'
text: Author the consumer with `enabled="false"`: publishing the connection then starts only its producer routes, so no consumer runs before its process exists. Publish the listener processes, then re-import the connection with `enabled="true"` (OVERWRITE) and republish it: the agent's catalina log shows 'Starting route ... <conn>:<eventSource>' and 'Subscribed to topic(s)', and the consumer group turns STABLE with members. A new consumer group with `autoOffsetReset=earliest` then processes everything still retained in the topic, which is how a subscriber added later catches up on history. Republishing a connection restarts all of its event sources, so give a subscriber that you start and stop on its own a connection of its own.
evidence: consumers enabled='false' at the first publish (only producer routes started), processes published, connection republished enabled='true', consumer groups STABLE (2026-10-08); a subscriber added later on a new group replayed 31 retained records (2026-10-08)

title: The CAI Kafka listener runs one process at a time per consumer: the next record of a partition waits until the started process ends
text: On a one-partition topic, a listener process with a 20 s Wait step started its records 20.5 s apart, and the offsets were committed after each. A Wait or a retry backoff inside a Kafka-started process therefore holds its partition: an unrelated record on the same partition waited about 7 s behind another record's target-outage retries. Per-key order is kept, but each consumer runs one process at a time. Keep Kafka-started processes short; make holds and approvals hand-offs (park the message in a store, end the process, republish it when it is ready) instead of long waits; bound the retry backoff; and raise `consumersCount` up to the partition count for parallelism (L-CAI-126).
evidence: 3 records with a 20 s Wait: process starts 20.5 s apart (2026-10-08); a record held about 7 s behind retries on its partition (2026-10-08)

title: Stopping a CAI Kafka listener resumes from the last offset auto-commit, not from the last processed record
text: A stop of a Kafka event source (a restadmin stop or a connection republish) does not commit the last processed offset: the listener resumes from the last auto-commit. With Camel's default `autoCommitIntervalMs` of 5,000, a stop and start in the middle of a 20 msg/s stream reprocessed 63 of 600 records; with `autoCommitIntervalMs=1000` in the event source's Other Attributes, 10 of 600. Nothing was lost in either run. Make every target idempotent (message id plus revision) and set a short commit interval to shrink the replay window.
evidence: two mid-stream stop/start runs of 600 records at 20 msg/s: 600 of 600 delivered each, 63 and 10 records processed twice (2026-10-08)

title: Stop and start a listener event source with restadmin eventconnection: it needs IDS-SESSION-ID
text: `POST https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/local/restadmin/eventconnection/stop?agentName=<agent>` with `{"eventRoute":["project:/rt.connection/<conn>/$public/<conn>:<eventSource>"]}`, and `.../eventconnection/start?agentName=<agent>` with `{"routeInfo":[{"eventRoute":"project:/rt.connection/<conn>/$public/<conn>:<eventSource>"}]}`, answer 200 with `eventRouteStatus` IN_ACTIVE or ACTIVE in about 1 s when the header is `IDS-SESSION-ID`. With `INFA-SESSION-ID` every body shape answered HTTP 500 'NullPointerException: Cannot read the array length because "<local4>" is null'. A stopped Kafka event source leaves its consumer group EMPTY (no members) while lag grows; start resumes from the committed offset (L-CAI-121). This is how a windowed subscriber runs: stop at the end of its window, start at the beginning. Refines the documented route in L-CAI-046.
evidence: stop, 3 records waited (lag 3), start, all 3 processed within 1 s of the start, no duplicates; INFA-SESSION-ID answered 500 on the same calls (2026-10-08)

title: The CAI AMQP connector drops JMS properties whose names are not Java identifiers, unless the connection's Query Parameters carry jms.validatePropertyNames=false
text: Qpid JMS, under the CAI AMQP connector, leaves out of the event headers every application property whose name is not a valid Java identifier (a hyphen or a dot, as in `msg-id` or `msg.id`); identifier names such as `msg_id` arrive. Set the connection's `Query Parameters` attribute to `jms.validatePropertyNames=false` (it is appended to the Qpid connection URI) and the hyphenated names arrive unchanged. Without it, read the ids from the message body or ask the publisher for identifier-style names. Newer evidence: L-CAI-160.
evidence: hyphenated properties missing and identifier names present on the first probe (2026-10-08); with the parameter the publisher's hyphenated properties arrived and were copied to Kafka headers (2026-10-08)

title: Produce to Kafka from a process with the native CAI producer: record key, value and headers
text: Call the producer as a Service step with `serviceName="<conn>:<eventTarget>"` and the input `event` = a temp field typed as the reference `<conn>:KafkaMessage`. Set `messageKey` (the record key), `body` (the value) and `headers` in an Assignment, the headers as a sequence of `<headers><name>..</name><value>{..}</value></headers>` elements; assigning the sub-fields one by one and assigning a whole KafkaMessage element both worked. The topic comes from the producer definition on the connection.
evidence: 2 records read back from the topic with their key and every header (2026-10-08)

title: An idempotent CAI Kafka producer needs retries set explicitly, and a route that fails to start still publishes SUCCESS
text: Camel's Kafka option `retries` defaults to 0, so a producer with `enableIdempotence=true` alone fails at route start with 'Must set retries to non-zero when using the idempotent producer' while the connection publish reports SUCCESS. Only the agent's catalina log shows it, and callers then get 'No consumers available on endpoint: direct://<conn>_<eventTarget>'. Use `requestRequiredAcks=all&enableIdempotence=true&retries=10&maxInFlightRequest=5` and check the ProducerConfig dump in catalina (`acks = -1`, `enable.idempotence = true`, `retries = 10`). After every connection publish, grep catalina for 'Failed to start route' and send one live message.
evidence: a producer route failed to start after a SUCCESS publish (2026-10-08); the idempotent producer with retries ran live and its ProducerConfig was confirmed in the agent log (2026-10-08)

title: Measured drain rate of a CAI Kafka listener on one Secure Agent: about 30 msg/s with 3 consumers, about 47 with 6
text: A listener process making one REST call per message drained about 30 msg/s (peak 36) with `consumersCount=3` and about 47 msg/s (peak 61) with `consumersCount=6` on a 6-partition topic, on one Secure Agent on an 8-vCPU host. 40 msg/s for 30 s kept up (peak lag 32, end-to-end p50 106 ms, p95 331 ms). Bursts of 3,000 messages at 200 msg/s queued in Kafka and cleared in 101 s with 3 consumers and 66 s with 6, with 0 lost and 0 duplicates. Bursts above the drain rate wait in the topic; scale with partitions, consumers and agents in an agent group, and size production in a proof of concept.
evidence: 1,200 messages at 40 msg/s and two 3,000-message bursts at 200 msg/s, 0 lost, 0 duplicates (2026-10-08)

title: A 4 MB XML message goes through a CAI Kafka listener, and through an AMQP-to-Kafka bridge, in about 5 s
