text: A 19,500-line purchase-order message (4,115,335 bytes) was consumed 1.9 s after it was published, parsed with `util:parseXML` in 3.7 s, mapped to JSON and posted to two REST targets: delivered 5.3 s after its approval; a 2,000-line message (423 KB) took 1.3 s. Through an AMQP-to-Kafka bridge process it first needed the bridge producer's `maxRequestSize` raised from the 1 MB default to 5,242,880 (the broker's and topic's `message.max.bytes`); then it bridged in 1.9 s and was delivered in 4.9 s. Keep the broker, topic and producer limits at or above the largest message; 4.1 MB stayed under the 5 MB payload limit documented in L-CAI-051.
evidence: 2,000-line and 19,500-line messages delivered over Kafka and over AMQP (2026-10-08)

title: A REST service-connector action's requestTimeout is in seconds
text: The action attribute `requestTimeout` is the designer's 'Request Timeout in seconds': `requestTimeout="10000"` means 10,000 s, so effectively no timeout (a 12 s answer was simply waited for). With `requestTimeout="10"` a 15 s answer timed out after 10 s and the step returned HTTP 500 (with failOnError false, L-CAI-129), which a retry loop treats like any 5xx; the idempotent target answered the retry as a duplicate because the first call had been applied.
evidence: a 12 s answer accepted with 10000; a 10 s timeout, a retry and a duplicate answer with 10 (2026-10-08)

title: REST service-connector errors: failOnError false returns the status as data, true raises a fault HTTP_<n>
text: With `failOnError="false"` on an action, the HTTP status lands in an output field marked `responseStatusCode="true"` and the JSON properties of the error body are still mapped, with no fault; a transport or URL error comes back as status 500. With `failOnError="true"` the step faults with the code `HTTP_<n>` and the response body as the reason, which an eventContainer (catch) around the Service step catches. Use false when the process decides by status (retry on 5xx, park or reject on 4xx).
evidence: a 422 returned as data, a 422 raised as HTTP_422 and caught, a dead URL returned as 500 (2026-10-08)

title: A process with no access configuration publishes as a private subprocess on a Secure Agent
text: `<deployment><rest></rest></deployment>` with no anonymous access and no allowed users, groups or roles publishes, gets no service URL, and is still callable as a subprocess from REST-started and event-started processes. Direct calls on the agent answer 403 on `/process-engine/public/rt/<name>` and 401 on `/process-engine/rt/<name>`. A subprocess with allowed roles is also callable as a subprocess. Use it for handlers that must not be an API. This proves L-CAI-034 on a Secure Agent.
evidence: a parent called two children (no access, allowed roles) in 693 ms, direct calls 403 and 401 (2026-10-08); 4 production handlers subprocess-only for hours (2026-10-08)

title: util:getProcessId() gives the CAI instance id for tracing
text: `util:getProcessId()` in an Assignment or a formula returns the running process instance id; a subprocess returns its own id. Write it into every tracking or audit event a process emits, so ledger rows join to the instances in the Application Integration Console.
evidence: a parent and two children returned their own ids (2026-10-08); 8,982 of 8,982 tracking events in 44 minutes carried it (2026-10-08)

title: Set a connection secret encrypted without the UI: author it encrypted with an empty value, then PUT asset/v1/update on the -cai host
text: Author the secret attribute in the AI_CONNECTION XML as `encrypted="true"` with an empty value and import it. Then `PUT https://<pod>-cai.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/active-bpel/asset/v1/update?assetType=AppConnection` (header `INFA-SESSION-ID`, JSON) with `{"connections":[{"guid":{"$t":"<objectId>"},"attributes":[{"key":{"$t":"Password"},"value":{"$t":"<secret>"}}]}]}` returns `{"status":{"$t":"SUCCESS"}}`. Republish the connection, then its dependent processes (L-CAI-133). The export then carries `encrypted="true"` with an empty value and the runtime authenticated; a wrong value set the same way was refused by the broker. If the attribute was authored `encrypted="false"`, the same call stores, and exports, the value in plaintext. This proves L-CAI-015 for app connections and settles the open point of L-CAI-060 and L-CAI-061.
evidence: plaintext in the export before; after the route no plaintext and the connection authenticated; a wrong value refused 'Client failed to authenticate using SASL: PLAIN' (2026-10-08)

title: Republishing a connection or connector marks every dependent process out-of-date
text: After a connection or service connector is republished, every process that uses it reads 'out-of-date' in `GET .../active-bpel/asset/v1/status`, although the runtime already uses the new connection; an OVERWRITE re-import also sets each imported asset out-of-date. To end in a clean 'published' state, import only the objects you changed (`includeObjects`), publish in dependency order with the processes last, and stop the listeners over restadmin during the process republish (L-CAI-122), then start them again.
evidence: 20 of 21 assets out-of-date after a full-package re-import; 21 of 21 published after a dependency-ordered republish (2026-10-08)

title: Wait step with a period taken from a field
text: `<duration source="formula"><expression language="XQuery">concat('PT', $temp.secs, 'S')</expression></duration>` works, and so does `<arg name="value">{$temp.secs}</arg>`; `<arg source="field">` and `<arg source="formula">` are taken literally and fail at run time with 'String "PTtemp.secsS" is not a valid xsd:duration'.
evidence: 4 variants run on a Secure Agent: 2 waited 2.0 s, 2 failed (2026-10-08)

title: A Decision whose branches all end must have no outgoing link
text: If every branch of a Decision ends in End or a Jump, the Decision must have no outgoing link; otherwise publish fails with 'Link definition error: /process/flow/links/link[...]'. The long 'ActiveVOS specific extension function used' list in itemStatusDetail is noise; the real error is at its end.
evidence: publish ERROR, then SUCCESS after the link was removed (2026-10-08)

title: A hand-built CAI package must carry the dependency closure of its processes
text: Processes whose connections or service connectors are not in the package fail the import with `MigrationSvc_031` 'Correct the errors in the Select Assets section' and empty details, even with their `objectRefs` entries removed: a CAI process references its connections inside its own XML (service names and reference GUIDs). Put every referenced connection and connector in the package, and limit the import with `includeObjects` to the objects you mean to change, or OVERWRITE the others with identical content. Narrows L-MIG-020 and the empty-details MigrationSvc_031 signature for CAI packages. Newer evidence: L-CAI-156.
evidence: import FAILED without the connections and SUCCESSFUL with them (2026-10-08); an import limited by includeObjects to 3 new assets, with 2 unchanged dependencies in the package, succeeded (2026-10-08)

title: Subprocess outputs need an explicit output mapping, and a callee fault is caught around the Subprocess step
text: A Subprocess step returns results only through `<output><operation source="field" to="temp.<x>"><calleeOutput></operation></output>`, with the callee's outputs declared in `outputDef`; there is no same-name automatic mapping. A fault in the callee (for example `util:parseXML` on malformed XML: 'Error evaluating function xmlStringToElement - SAXParseException ...') is caught by an eventContainer (catch) around the Subprocess step, so a thin listener can call a handler subprocess and send any fault to an error queue.
evidence: good and malformed payloads through a parse subprocess: outputs mapped only with the explicit mapping, the parse fault caught (2026-10-08)

title: Retries and replays lose hand-off headers: let the process ask the system of record for the decision
text: A parked message (waiting for an approval or for missing items) is republished with a hand-off header, for example approved=1, when it is released. An operator retry or a replay of the same message from an error queue arrives without that header, and a process that decides on the header parks it again. Have the process ask the approval or hold store for the message's current decision on every run: approved continues, rejected ends in a terminal state, pending parks.
evidence: an approved message was parked again on an error-queue retry; after the change its retry was delivered (2026-10-08)

title: Generated Normalizer transformations failed at the agent's DTM load; fan out with Expressions into a Union instead
text: A generated mapping with Normalizer transformations (5 occurring fields, and also with a single occurring 512-character field) imported as valid but failed when the agent loaded it: the session log showed only '<Error> : [transformation< NRM_x > ]' and the run ended 'The DTM process terminated unexpectedly'. Replacing each Normalizer with one Expression per output row, fanned out from the same pipeline into a Union, ran successfully. This narrows the Normalizer entry of L-CDI-204: give every new transformation shape one small test run before relying on it.
evidence: runs 1 and 2 FAILED at DTM load; runs 3 and 4 SUCCESS after the Union rewrite (2026-10-08)

title: A Database Ingestion deploy to BigQuery reads region-level INFORMATION_SCHEMA: a dataset-scoped service account gets 403
text: Deploying a DBMI task with a Google BigQuery target runs `SELECT ... FROM region-<location>.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA`, which needs project-level dataset metadata (`bigquery.datasets.get`). A service account that holds only dataset-level writer roles (plus job user) on its target datasets fails the deploy with 403. Grant project-level metadata read (for example `roles/bigquery.metadataViewer`), or run the DBMI connection as an identity that has it. The CDGC BigQuery scanner needs the same grant (L-CDGC-182).
evidence: deploy 403 on the region-level SCHEMATA query with a dataset-scoped writer; deploy and run succeeded with a project-level identity (2026-10-08)

title: CDC into BigQuery bills at least 30 MiB per changed table per apply cycle
text: Each apply of a changed table is one SCRIPT job (CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE <t>_TEMP from the <t>_EXT external staging table, then MERGE into <t>) billed 30 MiB (3 tables at the 10 MiB per-table minimum) however few rows changed, plus one MERGE into INFORMATICA_CDC_RECOVERY (20 MiB) per cycle; the CREATE and DROP EXTERNAL TABLE jobs are free. Two tasks (12 tables on a 5 s cycle, 3 high-churn tables on a 15-minute cycle) under test traffic ran 612 SCRIPT jobs (18,360 MiB) and 160 recovery MERGEs (3,200 MiB) in 2 h 40 min. Keep high-churn monitoring tables on a separate task with a long cycle, make the cycle no shorter than the freshness you need, and count bytes billed with jobs.list on the connection's identity before you leave a short cycle running (L-DBMI-019 splits hot and cold tables for latency; this is the cost side).
evidence: BigQuery jobs.list of the connection's identity over 2 h 40 min, statements and bytes billed per job (2026-10-08)

title: Stop and resume a CDC job without a re-baseline: resume continues from the stored restart point
text: `job/stop` then `job/resume` (L-DBMI-003) on a running PostgreSQL-to-BigQuery CDC job continued from its stored restart token: no unload and no re-baseline, and every row written during the pause landed with no gaps and no duplicates. The first apply after the resume came at the task's next cycle (about 15 minutes on that task), so plan the catch-up time by the cycle, not by the resume call.
evidence: a 4-minute stop: 3,074 rows written meanwhile all landed after the resume, target row count equal to distinct ids (2026-10-08)

title: Data Profiling of BigQuery V2 fails with 'Cannot parse null string' when the connection's hidden retry attributes are empty
text: A BigQuery V2 connection created over REST can carry `maxRetryAttempts`, `initialRetryDelay`, `retryDelayMultiplier`, `maxRetryDelay` and `totalTimeout` as empty strings (hidden while Enable Retry is false; the connector defaults are 6, 1, 2.0, 32 and 50). CDI mappings run fine on such a connection, but every Data Profiling run fails in 'Generating data profiling mappings' with 'Profile job failed with error Cannot parse null string.' and no DTM starts. Fill the five attributes with the defaults (POST the full connection body, with the key, again; Enable Retry stays false) and the same profile completes. With the same service account, a profile failed on the connection with empty attributes and completed on a copy with the defaults, and a body with only the four mandatory BigQuery options also completed, so the option set was not the cause. This resolves the generation-step failure in L-DQ-107 and L-DQ-108; catalog-source profiling of BigQuery still fails (L-CDGC-184).
evidence: 1 run FAILED on the connection with empty attributes; 9 BigQuery tables (up to 43,210 rows, about 50 s each) profiled to COMPLETED on connections with the defaults (2026-10-08)

title: A rule specification's advanced script can compute a UPC-A check digit with TO_INTEGER, SUBSTR and MOD
text: A cloned single-input rule specification whose advanced script checks 12 digits with REG_MATCH and then the GS1 mod-10 sum (three times the digits in odd positions plus the digits in even positions, the check digit included, `MOD(..., 10) = 0`, each digit read with `TO_INTEGER(SUBSTR(<input>, <n>, 1))`) imported, validated as a mapplet at DTM load and scored rows in a mapping with exact parity to an SQL check of the same rule.
evidence: 343 of 343 record-by-rule results equal to an SQL check, 1 bad check digit caught (2026-10-08)

title: Write curated lineage edges headless: ccgf-contentv2 publish RELATIONSHIP items with core.DataSetDataFlow for tables and core.DirectionalDataFlow for columns
text: When a scanner leaves a hop out (for example Database Ingestion CDC tasks, whose task instances come out empty), publish the edges yourself: `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/publish` (header `X-INFA-PRODUCT-ID: CDGC` plus the identity headers) with RELATIONSHIP items `{operation INSERT, type <association>, fromIdentity and toIdentity = the assets' external ids, sourceIdentityType and targetIdentityType EXTERNAL, attributes {core.curationStatus ACCEPTED, core.channels [MANUAL], core.inferred false}}`. Table to table works with `core.DataSetDataFlow`, column to column with `core.DirectionalDataFlow` (207 per call, every item accepted). `core.DataFlow` is refused ('Invalid or Null association Type') and a task instance cannot be an endpoint (INVALID_RELATIONSHIP_CLASS_TYPE), so the edge goes straight from the source table to the target table. The asset's lineage segment (L-CDGC-181) and the Lineage tab then show the hop across catalog sources, joined to the scanner's CDI lineage. Undo: the same items with operation DELETE. Supersedes L-CDGC-180.
evidence: 204 edges (15 table, 189 column) published in 4 calls, each 207 with every item accepted; the lineage segment and the Lineage tab showed the new hop (2026-10-08)

title: Lineage edges cannot be written over REST: a ccgf-contentv2 lineage publish answers 207 with items: [] and changes nothing
text: Recorded with the ccgf-contentv2 write plane (L-CDGC-065) and in the capability map as 'write lineage edges: rejected'. The data-flow edge published in that test came back with no items; RELATIONSHIP items with core.DataSetDataFlow or core.DirectionalDataFlow are written and show in lineage. Was believed 2026-08-20 to 2026-10-07; overturned by L-CDGC-179.
evidence: one data-flow edge publish answered 207 with items: [] (2026-08-20)

title: Read lineage over REST hop by hop: the asset read's lineage segment lists inbound and outbound data-flow hops
text: `GET https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/search/v1/assets/<identity>?scheme=internal&segments=all` returns, besides the neighborhood segment (L-CDGC-156), a `lineage` list of `{direction inbound|outbound, hops[{distance, items[{from, to, fromType, toType, fromLocation, toLocation, attributes.core.associationKind = core.DataFlow}]}]}`. It gave every direct data-flow hop of BigQuery tables written and read by CDI mapping tasks (table to MappingTaskInstance and back, plus view-SQL edges) and, after curated edges were published (L-CDGC-179), the database-to-warehouse hop across catalog sources. Walk it asset by asset for a chain; only distance-1 hops were seen. The `/data360/lineage/*` graph routes are still not found. Supersedes L-CDGC-085.
evidence: lineage segments of 13 warehouse tables read over REST, matching the Lineage tab (2026-10-08); cross-source hops read after curated edges were published (2026-10-08)

title: The BigQuery catalog scanner needs project-level dataset metadata, even inside one project
text: Metadata Extraction lists datasets with `region-<location>.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA` (and SCHEMATA_OPTIONS). A connection whose service account holds dataset-level roles plus job user in the same project still failed: 'Unable to resolve EXTERNAL_TABLES/VIEWS/... objects from BIG_QUERY ... Exception during execution of query: select s.schema_name ...' and 'Scan finished with abnormal exit status. Reason: No input was processed'. The same source on an identity with project-level metadata read (for example `roles/bigquery.metadataViewer`) COMPLETED; include filters still limit the scan to the wanted datasets. This refines L-CDGC-154, which needs job user in the dataset's project: both grants matter.
evidence: scan FAILED on a dataset-scoped identity and COMPLETED on a project-level identity 22 minutes later (2026-10-08)

title: An IICS catalog source's Database Ingestion filter needs Filter Conditions 'Database'
text: An IICS catalog source whose Metadata Filter Config has Filter Type CDIR with Filter Conditions 'All Types' ends Catalog Source Extraction PARTIAL_COMPLETED with 'Failed to extract CDIR inputs: Could not parse filter expression: Include:All Types:<project>'. Filter Conditions 'Database' extracts the project's Database Ingestion and Replication tasks (class DatabaseIngestionAndReplicationTask). CDGC derived no lineage edges for those CDC tasks (their task instances came out empty), so add the source-to-target hop as curated lineage (L-CDGC-179).
evidence: scan PARTIAL_COMPLETED with 'All Types'; COMPLETED with 'Database', 2 CDC task assets cataloged, 0 lineage hops (2026-10-08)

title: Catalog-source Data Profiling of BigQuery fails with no message, even on a connection that Data Profiling profiles fine
text: The Data Profiling capability of a Google BigQuery catalog source ended FAILED (Data Profiling Task and Task Progress Tracker, no message in the job tree, no profiling session on the agent) with Sampling Type All Rows and with Limit N Rows, before and after the connection's retry attributes were filled (L-DQ-110), while Data Profiling profiles on the same connection and tables completed and a PostgreSQL catalog source on the same agent profiled 179 of 189 columns. The BigQuery scanner stores STRING columns without a length and parameterized NUMERIC columns as the type string 'NUMERIC(18, 4)' without length or scale; a catalog-driven mapping generation may parse those nulls (unproven). Profile BigQuery with Data Profiling profiles over REST, keep catalog profiling for databases that complete, and send the job ids in a vendor case.
evidence: 3 catalog profiling jobs FAILED (2026-10-08); 9 Data Profiling profiles of the same tables COMPLETED (2026-10-08)

title: Catalog Data Quality on BigQuery skips every table that carries a decimal-input rule occurrence; score decimal rules through text-input twins
text: On a BigQuery catalog source, occurrences of string-input rule specifications on STRING columns scored, but a decimal-input occurrence bound to a NUMERIC column, a NUMERIC(18,4) column or a view column got no score, and the string occurrences of the same table were skipped with it; the run ended PARTIAL_COMPLETED without a message (0 of 7 occurrences on typed NUMERIC tables scored). Workaround: clone a string template into a 'text input' twin of each decimal rule (IS_NUMBER(LTRIM(RTRIM(x))) then TO_DECIMAL in the advanced script), write the figures as STRING columns in a snapshot table that holds no other occurrence, and bind the twins there; keep the original decimal rules in the CDI mapping that scores them. With the twins, 15 of 15 occurrences scored. This narrows L-CDGC-170: a typed view column scored on another warehouse, not on BigQuery.
evidence: 6 of 15 and 8 of 15 occurrences scored in two runs before (2026-10-08); 15 of 15 after the twins (2026-10-08)

title: Grafana's BigQuery plugin 3.x needs Grafana 11.6 or later: pin grafana-bigquery-datasource 2.2.1 on older Grafana
text: On Grafana OSS 11.3.1 an unpinned install pulled grafana-bigquery-datasource 3.4.3, whose frontend needs Grafana 11.6 or later: the plugin frontend failed to load in the browser ('react/jsx-runtime' 404) and every BigQuery panel showed an error, while server-side queries through POST /api/ds/query still worked. Pin the version in the install variable (`GF_INSTALL_PLUGINS="grafana-bigquery-datasource 2.2.1"`), recreate only the Grafana container, and check the version at `/api/plugins/grafana-bigquery-datasource/settings`.
evidence: panels broken with 3.4.3 and rendering with 2.2.1 after the pin (2026-10-08); 79 panel queries, 0 errors (2026-10-08)

title: An anonymous Grafana Viewer can send any SQL through /api/ds/query: allow only the dashboards' own queries
text: With anonymous Viewer access, `POST /api/ds/query` runs whatever query the caller sends, with no credentials, against every datasource the dashboards use: PII columns, raw payloads, sleep queries and large warehouse scans billed to the project. A bytes-billed cap per query and a read-only database role with a statement timeout limit the damage, not the exposure. A small guard in front of Grafana closed it: a reverse-proxy route that sends every non-GET request to a service allowing only the exact panel queries of the provisioned dashboards, plus 403 on the datasource proxy, the alert-rule evaluation endpoint and the admin login. Serve the dashboards from views without PII columns as well.
evidence: arbitrary SQL answered on the public URL without credentials (2026-10-08); 17 of 17 public guard tests passed (2026-10-08)

title: Rename a repository object in place: PATCH the FRS Documents entity, not BaseEntities
text: `PATCH https://<pod>.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/frs/api/v1/Documents('<frsId>')` with header `IDS-SESSION-ID` and body `{"name": "<new name>"}` answers 204 and renames the object in place: the id is unchanged, and `GET /public/core/v3/objects` (path), `GET /api/v2/mapping/<id>` and `GET /api/v2/mttask/<id>` show the new name at once. Proven on mappings (DTEMPLATE), mapping tasks (MTT) and CLAIRE structure models (SAAS_STRUCTURE_DISCOVERY); names with spaces, a dot and a hyphen were accepted. A task keeps its mapping and a Structure Parser keeps its model, because both bind by id; a task run after the rename loaded the same rows as before. The same PATCH on `BaseEntities('<id>')` gives `400 FRS_068` 'Operation not allowed for the entity set BaseEntities': the opposite of a delete, where `BaseEntities` works and `Documents` gives 403 (L-CLEAN-005). FRS has no Rename action in its `$metadata`. Probe on a scratch object first and keep `{id, old name}` as the undo. Exporting, renaming and re-importing a package instead creates a second object, because the import matches by path.
evidence: Scratch mapping renamed and renamed back (204/204, v2 by-name read 200); 2 mappings, 2 tasks and 1 structure model renamed twice with read-back; task run after the rename 12 read / 9 loaded, the same as before; BaseEntities PATCH 400 FRS_068

title: Renaming a connection in place: re-supply its secrets, URL-quote name lookups, and rename every builder keyed by name
text: `POST /api/v2/connection/<connId>` with the full GET body (audit fields removed) and a new `name` renames in place; the id, and every task and catalog source bound to it, are unchanged. Connections with no stored secret (a key-pair connection whose key is a file on the agent, a flat-file connection) need nothing else. OAuth connections (for example SharePoint Online: `Client_Secret`, `Refresh_Token`) come back masked and must be re-supplied (L-CONN-007). Redeem the stored refresh token against the identity provider first, without printing it: a dead token would leave the connection broken until someone signs in interactively. Names with spaces and dots are accepted; `GET /api/v2/connection/name/<name>` then needs the name URL-quoted. Update every idempotent builder and generator profile that looks the connection up by name in the same change: a mapping-package profile lists the connection by name and v2 id, and a builder keyed by name would create a duplicate on its next run. Test each connection afterwards.
evidence: 5 connections renamed twice (2 key/file based, 3 OAuth with secrets re-supplied after a live token check); all 5 connection tests success; by-name lookup 200 with the quoted name

title: Catalog-source names may contain spaces, dots and hyphens; rewrite the lineage filters that name them in the same pass
text: A catalog-source rename by multipart PUT (L-CDGC-141) accepted display-style names such as '<Demo> 3.0 - Snowflake', not only snake_case: 200, id unchanged, read-back shows the name. Rename the sources a data-integration source's Lineage Discovery filter lists ('Catalog Source Name') first, then rewrite that filter's values in the same PUT as the data-integration source's own rename, so stitching never points at a name that no longer exists. Also check that source's Metadata Extraction filter: it names projects by their name, so a project renamed in Explore silently drops out of the next scan.
evidence: 4 catalog sources renamed with spaces and a dot (PUT 200 x4, read-back); the lineage filter rewritten and read back

title: Import OIE_007 'Internal application provider error' on a pruned mapping: its template still references models the package no longer lists
text: A mapping cloned from a multi-lane export and pruned to one lane imported as `OIE_007 ... Failed to import object [...] of type [DTEMPLATE] ... Internal application provider error`, with nothing more in the job log and a 500 on the job's `?expand=objects`. The IMF itself was consistent (every `##ID` resolved). The cause was `mappingTemplate.json` inside the DTEMPLATE zip: its `references[]` still listed the structure models (`refType: structureDefinition`) of the removed lanes, while the package's `exportMetadata.v2.json` listed only the kept model and the connection in the mapping's `objectRefs`. Making the two agree (drop the removed references, or keep both lists complete) imported SUCCESSFUL on the next try. When pruning, rebuild `references[]` from the transformations you keep, and list each referenced model and connection in `exportedObjects` by id with its CURRENT path and name. Newer evidence: L-MIG-100.
evidence: Same package FAILED with the stale references and SUCCESSFUL after removing them; the clone then validated and ran

title: Snowflake writer: a full reload needs the runtime attribute 'presql'; the truncate flag and the transformation's Pre SQL are ignored
text: A Snowflake Data Cloud target with `writeOptions.truncate = true` (the task's target parameter then reads `truncateTarget: true`) and a TRUNCATE in the transformation's advanced property 'Pre SQL' still appended on every run (14 rows, then 28, then 42). Putting `TRUNCATE TABLE <db>.<schema>.<table>` in the data adapter's runtime attributes made each run a clean reload: `oprRuntimeAttributes.attributes` = `[{"name": "presql", "value": ...}]` and `runtimeAttributes.attributes` = `[{"name": "Pre SQL", ...}]` (the same pair as postsql in L-CONN-094). In a mapping cloned from an older export the two containers can be empty and the class `com.informatica.metadata.template.ext.da.cloud.common.RuntimeAttribute` can be missing from `metadata.$$classInfo`: add the class under a new index and give each attribute a fresh `$$ID`. Count rows per run id after the second run, because an appending target looks right after the first one.
evidence: 4 runs of one cloned mapping: appended with the truncate flag and with transformation Pre SQL; 14 rows / 1 run id with presql

title: A package cloned from an export still carries the source objects' GUIDs: give the mapping and task fresh ones
text: A v3 export lists each object with its live GUID (exportMetadata objectGuid, mappingTemplate assetFrsGuid, the task's mapping reference). A clone built from it under a new name and path imported as a new object in the cases seen, but the GUIDs still point at the source objects, so a clone of a still-existing object risks landing on it. Replace the mapping and task GUIDs with fresh 22-character ids everywhere they occur (outer files and the files inside the DTEMPLATE/MTT zips), then check that none of the old ones is left. When the template package listed its Project or Folder twice and both entries now carry the same id, the upload fails before anything is imported: 500 MigrationSvc_002 'Duplicate key <id> (attempted merging values ObjectInfo...)'. Keep one exportedObjects entry per (objectType, objectGuid).
evidence: 3 parse mappings + 1 pickup cloned into a new project: the template GUIDs were live objects; after the swap 0 left, the source objects' update times unchanged; one upload refused with Duplicate key until the entries were deduplicated

title: The v3 project create refuses a dot in the name; create it without, then rename through FRS
text: `POST /public/core/v3/projects` with a name like '<Demo> 4.0' answers 400 V3API_ContainerError_004 'Project name attribute contains illegal characters: #?`|{}"^&[]/\\..'. Create '<Demo> 4_0', then `PATCH .../frs/api/v1/Projects('<id>')` with `{"name": "<Demo> 4.0"}` (204): the project shows the dotted name in Explore, folders are created under it with `POST /public/core/v3/projects/<id>/folders`, and package imports address it by that path. Renaming existing projects and folders the same way also accepts dots (L-MIG-075).
evidence: v3 create 400 with the dot, 201 without; FRS rename 204; 5 folders created and 9 packages imported under it

title: Finding your tasks: the v2 mttask list has no frsGuid and its 'valid' is always false; a v3 type query stops at 200
text: `GET /api/v2/mttask` lists every task but without `frsGuid`, and its `valid` field read false for every task, also ones that run (the per-task `GET /api/v2/mttask/<id>` says valid true). `GET /public/core/v3/objects?q=type=='MTT'&limit=200` returned only the first 200 of an org's 260 tasks, so new tasks were missing from it. Match tasks by a name convention (for example a project prefix) or query by location (`q=location=='<Project>/<Folder>'`), and read validity per task. A new v2 linear taskflow (`POST /api/v2/workflow`) is created in Default and its v2 read has no frsGuid either: find it with `q=location=='Default'` by name and move it with FRS MoveEntities.
evidence: list valid=false for 260 tasks incl. running ones; per-task GET valid=true; v3 type query 200 of 260; taskflow found in Default by name and moved (FRS_200)

title: Drive Gold from the master entity, not from the documents, so a missing document shows as 'waiting' instead of nothing
text: A Gold mapping whose source is the checked document lines produces no row for an entity whose documents have not arrived, so the page loses it. Make the source the master list (for example every CRM opportunity) LEFT JOINed to the Silver lines in the source query; in the Aggregator a COUNT of a line key is then 0 for an entity without documents, and the decision Expression can say WAITING FOR <document> (or WRITE <reply> when only the first document came). Together with a starting point (a config row the reset sets to now, and a file-list view that only keeps files modified since then, joined into every Silver read), the same mappings give a clean demo start, a staged arrival one document at a time, and the full picture, with no special code paths.
evidence: 6 entities: reset -> 6 waiting; first document -> 1 'write the reply'; second -> 1 'fix'; all -> 6/6 expected decisions

title: A reset step inside IDMC: a 3-transformation mapping whose Snowflake target runs CALL <procedure>() as its presql
text: Source `SELECT 1` -> Expression (run id, SESSSTARTTIME) -> target: a small log table, with the writer runtime attribute `presql` (and display 'Pre SQL') = `CALL <db>.<schema>.<RESET_PROC>()` (KB L-CONN-106: the Snowflake writer only runs SQL from that attribute). The procedure (Snowflake Scripting) sets the starting point and truncates Silver and Gold; the mapping then logs one row per reset. Put it first in a 'reset' taskflow followed by the Silver and Gold steps, so the page is rebuilt in its starting state and the BI refresh (post step of the last task) runs too. SQL runners that split files on ';' cut a procedure body: run the CREATE PROCEDURE as one statement.
evidence: reset taskflow 6/6 SUCCESS: starting point set, 0 documents in play, Gold rebuilt as all-waiting, BI refreshed

title: Clone a catalog source: GET a working one, drop the read-only fields, change name and scope, multipart POST
text: GET `.../ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>`, remove id, createdBy, lastModifiedBy, createdTime, lastModifiedTime, seedVersion, clonedCatalogSourceId, modelVersion, isDeleted; set name, description, custom=false, endOfLife=false; rewrite the 'Filter Value' options per capability (Metadata Extraction scope, Data Profiling scope, Lineage Discovery 'Catalog Source Name' list), then POST it as multipart part `dataSource` -> 201 with the new id. For a data-integration (IICS) source re-supply the IDMC login (IICS URL / User / Password options) in the same body: the GET carries the password encrypted. Start the scan with `POST /data360/executable/v1/catalogsource/<id>` {capabilityNames: [...]} and poll `/data360/observable/v1/jobs/<jobId>?expandChildren=TASK-HIERARCHY`. Scan the database source before the data-integration source so lineage can stitch onto it.
evidence: 2 sources cloned (database with profiling scope, IICS with lineage filter): POST 201 x2, read-back scopes as set, scans ran

title: A Data Access Service Connector would not publish in one org: an empty 'Publish Error' from the designer and from asset/v1/publish
text: In one org every publish of a Data Access Service Connector ended in item state ERROR 'Publish Error' with no message: the designer's call `.../activevos-central/<org>/app/florence-design/services/JSON/cpfPublish` answered HTTP 500 `{"publishErrorResponse":{"errorTitle":"Publish Error","errorMessage":{}}}` and the REST job `asset/v1/publish` gave the same item state. It failed for a connector with no action, with a SELECT, with a stored-procedure call and with test values set; neither Secure Agent's process engine logged a request, so the cloud rejected it before any agent was involved, and a REST service connector published minutes later in the same org. Check that a Data Access Service Connector publishes in the target org before designing on it; the routes around it are the database's own REST layer (L-CAI-146) or a JDBC app connection on an agent whose runtime has that connector, and the cpfPublish 500 is the signature for a vendor case.
evidence: 4 headless variants and 1 designer publish, all ERROR; a REST service connector published SUCCESS in the same org; no agent access-log line in the window (2026-10-08)

title: Data Access Service Connector XML: a `businessConnector agentOnly="true"`, the JDBC pool attributes and `<dasActions>`
text: A designer export shows `<businessConnector agentOnly="true" ...>` with the connection attributes driver, jdbcUrl, username, password (masked), schema, includeTables, excludeTables, checkSqlInjection and the pool settings (initialSize, maxActive, minIdle, maxIdle, maxWait, defaultTransactionIsolation, minEvictableIdleTimeMillis, numTestsPerEvictionRun, testOnBorrow, testOnReturn, testWhileIdle, validationQuery). Actions sit in `<dasActions>`, not `<actions>`: `<action name><input><parameter name type="string"/></input><binding><sqlStatement statementId columnCase="lowercase" [maxRows] [maxWaitSeconds]><statement>SQL</statement>[<procedure><parameter id mode="out" name sqlType="string|int|clob|..."/></procedure>]</sqlStatement></binding><output><field name property="<column>"/> | <field xmlElement=""/> (the whole result set) | <field><xquery>...</xquery></field></output></action>`. Inputs are substituted into the SQL text as `'{$name}'` (string substitution, hence the SQL-injection check), every `?` is an OUT parameter of the procedure, INOUT is not supported, and all statements of an action commit once at the end; the runtime schema is data-access.xsd in the engine's data-access jar. The format imports; it could not be run where the publish failed (L-CAI-139).
evidence: a designer export of a probe connector and the engine's data-access.xsd; 4 hand-built variants imported (2026-10-08)

title: A JDBC driver for the process engine without a restart: unzip the jar into apps/process-engine/ext
text: The process engine's Tomcat `shared.loader` (in `conf/catalina.properties` of the process-engine version folder) lists `"${catalina.base}/../ext/"` as a directory and `"${catalina.base}/../ext/*.jar"` as a glob. Tomcat expands the glob once at start, so a jar copied in later is ignored until the engine restarts, while a directory entry is searched when a class is first requested. Unzipping the driver jar (without its MANIFEST.MF) into `<agent_home>/apps/process-engine/ext` therefore puts its classes on the engine's class path without a restart. Use a driver built for the engine's JVM: the process engine runs on the agent's Java 8, so ojdbc8 (the agent's Data Gateway service package ships one), not ojdbc11 or ojdbc17. Narrows L-CAI-065. Not yet exercised by a JDBC call: the connector that would use it could not be published (L-CAI-139).
evidence: shared.loader read on an agent; 2,702 driver files unzipped into ext on a running agent, no restart (2026-10-08) [not exercised]

title: The restadmin scheduler stored a schedule for an agent-run process but never ran it; the agent's own scheduler answered 401 or 403
text: `POST .../active-bpel/restadmin/scheduler/schedules` for a process published to a Secure Agent answered 204, but the stored item stayed `enabled: false` with `planId: -1` and never ran, also after a `PUT` with `enabled: true`. On the agent, `GET http://<agentHost>:7080/process-engine/restadmin/scheduler/schedules` answered 401 to `INFA-SESSION-ID` and 403 to `IDS-SESSION-ID` (authenticated, a role missing; compare L-CAI-048). The documented scheduler route (L-CAI-045) therefore did not cover a process published to an agent. For agent-run timer processes grant the user the scheduler role on the agent, or start them from the agent host: a system timer that posts to the agent's anonymous endpoint every minute, with a lock per process that plays the scheduler's 'skip if running'.
evidence: one 1-minute schedule created, read back enabled false and planId -1 with no run in 3 min, then deleted; agent scheduler probes 401 and 403 (2026-10-09)

title: A process published to a Secure Agent answers on the agent host, and ?swagger there returns its Swagger 2.0 document
text: A process deployed to an agent with anonymous access answered on `http://<agentHost>:7080/process-engine/public/rt/<ProcessApiName>` (https on 7443), and `GET` on the same URL with `?swagger` returned a Swagger 2.0 document with the process description and its input fields. This proves the agent twin of L-CAI-047 and the `?swagger` form of L-CAI-032 for agent processes. The engine port 7080 is plain HTTP: keep 7080 and 7443 closed to outside networks and expose only the processes callers need, through a reverse proxy with authentication.
evidence: two agent-published processes answered 200 and 400, swagger 200 (2026-10-09)

title: A contract-checking REST API in CAI: a Milestone step with an HTTP status returns 400 or 503 with the output fields
text: Validate the inputs in an Assignment (for example a `string-join` of the problems found), then a Decision. Problems: set the outputs (status, reasons), then a Milestone step `<milestone><title>...</title><httpStatus>400</httpStatus></milestone>`, which sends the reply with every output field, then End. Valid: do the work and end in a Milestone with 200, or with 503 in the fault branch when the downstream system refused the message. The caller gets the reasons in the body of the 400 and retries only a 503. Measured: a broken contract answered 400 with its field list in 4 ms of process time.
evidence: one process: 400 with the reasons in 4 ms, 200 after the downstream accepted; the 503 branch authored, not drilled (2026-10-09)

title: Separate query parameters in a REST action URL with `&`: a single-escaped `&` publishes, then fails at run time
text: The `url` of a `restSimpleBinding` is evaluated as an XQuery template, so after XML parsing it must contain `&` between query parameters: write `&amp;` in the connector XML. With `&` in the file (a plain `&` after parsing) the connector imports and publishes, but every call fails before it is sent, with only 'An error occurred when executing the expression' in the agent's catalina log; a catch with a default output around the Service step hides it completely (here a dependency check silently answered 'not blocked'). The trap starts with the second query parameter. L-CAI-023 found the same double escaping in a form-encoded body.
evidence: a 4-parameter GET never reached its server until the URL was double-escaped; afterwards it answered and the process used the result (2026-10-09)

title: Call database PL/SQL APIs from CAI through the database's REST layer (Oracle REST Data Services)
text: When no JDBC route publishes (L-CAI-139), run Oracle REST Data Services next to the database, listening only on localhost of the agent host, and give each PL/SQL API a handler in one REST module: a POST handler whose PL/SQL block reads the request with `JSON_OBJECT_T.parse(:body_text)`, calls the procedure and prints the OUT values as JSON. A CAI REST service connector then has one action per handler and runs on the agent next to the database. ORDS needs its own JVM: in a systemd unit quote the whole `Environment="_JAVA_OPTIONS=-Xms128m -Xmx512m"`, because unquoted the second option is dropped, the heap is sized from the host's memory and a memory cap kills the service. Measured: an idle queue-polling process made 25 calls in 50 s; a record sent by a CAI subscriber through a handler was in the database 1.2-1.7 s after it was published to Kafka.
evidence: a module of 8 handlers called by 6 processes; 25 idle polls in 50 s; 4 of 4 records applied 1.2-1.7 s after the publish (2026-10-09)

title: eventconnection stop works per event source: the other consumers of the same Kafka connection keep running
text: A Kafka connection with three consumers (three event sources, three consumer groups) had one event source stopped with restadmin `eventconnection/stop` (route `<conn>:<eventSource>`, IN_ACTIVE in 6.8 s): its group went EMPTY and its messages waited in Kafka, while the connection's other two event sources kept consuming with lag 0. The start (ACTIVE in 2.1 s) drained the waiting messages in 3.3 s with nothing lost. One connection can therefore hold several independently controlled listeners, for example one per warehouse, like an adapter manager that stops one adapter. Extends L-CAI-122.
evidence: one of three event sources stopped while the other two ran; 3 messages waited and drained in 3.3 s after the start, none lost (2026-10-09)

title: A bulk delete at the source reaches a BigQuery CDC target within about 2 minutes, as hard deletes
text: Standard apply turns source row deletes into deletes in the BigQuery target: the target tables carry no soft-delete or change columns, so after a purge the target holds the current state of the source (L-DBMI-026), while the change history stays reachable through APPENDS() and time travel (L-DBMI-051). Measured: one 3-second DELETE of about 607,000 rows in 15 PostgreSQL tables (the largest 229,102 and 183,778 rows), replicated by two CDC tasks (12 tables on a 5-second cycle, 3 on a 15-minute cycle), left 14 target tables empty 75 s later and the last one (183,778 rows) empty 114 s later; the 15-minute task's cycle happened to fall in that window (its next apply came 15 minutes later), so allow up to one full cycle on a slow task. Reset a demo or a test the same way: purge at the source, wait for the slowest task's cycle, check the target row counts, then rebuild any layer that is truncated and reloaded from the target.
evidence: a source purge of about 607,000 rows in 15 tables: target counts read at +75 s and +114 s, 0 delete-marker columns on the 15 target tables (2026-10-08)

title: CAI API calls per message in a listener + handler design: S x (1 + h) + d + b + r; count the runs on the CAI Monitor, not from an event ledger
text: One execution of a process or subprocess is one CAI API call; the connector calls inside it (REST, JDBC, a Kafka produce) add none (L-CAI-096). When each subscriber is a Kafka listener process that calls one handler subprocess, a message makes S x (1 + h) + d + b + r calls: S = the subscribers (consumer groups) that receive it, h = 1 when the handler is a separate subprocess (0 when its logic sits in the listener), d = the runs of a delivery subprocess (one per call to a target when every target call goes through it), b = 1 when a JMS-to-Kafka bridge process carries it (a cutover from JMS), r = the re-runs it needed (a retry or a reprocess). Count the runs on the CAI Monitor's run list (every process and subprocess run on the agent): a count from an event ledger in which each run writes its instance id misses every run that writes no event (delivery subprocesses, routers, pass-through listeners) and read 2 to 5 calls a message where the Monitor showed 7 to 10. Keeping the target calls and the routing inside the listener, with retries as Wait steps there, gives 1 call per subscriber, but the listener handles one record at a time per consumer (L-CAI-120), so long waits belong in a hand-off, not in the listener. Newer evidence: L-CAI-161.
evidence: CAI Monitor run list for one business day (2026-10-09): 2,008 runs = 1,960 for 240 message revisions + 48 timer runs; the delivery subprocess ran 708 times, one per target call; the event-ledger count of the same day missed 1,016 runs that write no event

title: The CDI SharePoint Online connector can WRITE files: a document-library INSERT row = folder (ServerRelativeUrl) + file name (Name); the bytes come from Attachment_File_Path on the agent
text: Read from the connector's own runtime adapter (SharePointInsert / CreateFolder / AttachFileToFolder): for a document library target, each INSERT row needs ServerRelativeUrl = the folder's server-relative URL (created with /_api/web/folders when missing) and Name (Title is accepted as a fallback) = the file name; the connector opens <connection Attachment_File_Path>/<Name> on the Secure Agent and posts it to GetFolderByServerRelativeUrl('<folder>')/Files/add(url='<Name>'). There is no overwrite parameter, so a name that already exists fails: version names upstream (<title> (v2).pdf) or move the old folder aside before a re-run. For a plain list the same INSERT creates an item (Title) and, with Attachments=true, attaches the file to it. Declare only the fields you map (ServerRelativeUrl, Name) on the target. The bytes must be on the agent before the session starts: stage them in the mapping task's pre-processing command (one command, exit 1 on failure so the task fails visibly), and give the write connection its own Attachment_File_Path (the read side downloads into the same attribute). Newer evidence: L-CONN-140.
evidence: adapter 10.4.x read from its runtime jar (method-level string/call dump); a mapping CRM files -> Expression -> library target imports and validates; the write itself waits on the write-scope grant (L-CONN-111)

title: A delegated SharePoint token carries the CONSENTED scopes, not the ones the app registration lists; SharePoint REST then shows read-only effective permissions and every write is 403
text: An Entra app can list Files.ReadWrite.All / Sites.ReadWrite.All in its API permissions while only the read scopes were ever consented: the refresh-token grant returns scp = Files.Read.All Sites.Read.All for both the Graph and the SharePoint audience, and asking for a write scope on refresh fails AADSTS65001 (no consent). With that token, /_api/web/EffectiveBasePermissions shows View/Open only (no AddListItems) even for a user who can write in the browser, Graph POST .../children and SharePoint REST /_api/web/folders both answer 403 accessDenied, and an app-only (client credentials) token has no roles and gets 401. So 'the connector can't write' is a consent question: decode the token's scp (and roles) before blaming the connector, then ask the tenant admin for 'Grant admin consent' on the scopes the app already lists (tenants that block user consent need the admin).
evidence: 2 refresh tokens x 3 audiences decoded; 65001 on the write scope; EffectiveBasePermissions Low=136515681 (View, Open, AddAndCustomizePages only); Graph + REST folder create 403; app-only 401

title: A Salesforce SOURCE in a mapping built without the designer: typeSystem Salesforce, objectAttributes owner/resource, Salesforce native types, the SOQL filter in readOptions.filterCondition
text: Copy the shape of an exported Salesforce source: data adapter typeSystem 'Salesforce', objectType SINGLE; DataObject objectType TABLE with objectAttributes owner='' and resource='' (not tableType); each field with its Salesforce nativeType (id, string, reference, picklist, currency precision 18 scale 2, date, datetime) and javaType java.lang.String / BigDecimal / Timestamp; the WHERE condition (SOQL) goes in readOptions.filterCondition, for example IsLatest = true or AccountNumber LIKE 'X%'. Base64 fields such as ContentVersion.VersionData arrive as a String (Maximum Base64 Body Size, default 7 MB). Several objects in one mapping are separate flows; a Joiner of two Salesforce sources collides on Id/Name, so land them separately and join in the warehouse. Avoid boolean fields when the generator has no proven boolean type: derive them (IIF on StageName).
evidence: 2 generated mappings (2 and 1 Salesforce sources) import valid on the first try; shape diffed against exported Salesforce sources

title: 'Internal error. The DTM process terminated unexpectedly' with an empty session log = the connection's login failed before the session; the reason is only in the agent's tomcat log
text: When a task fails with that message and its session log is ~70 bytes, the DTM never started the session: the agent failed to connect while reading the connection metadata and the DTM exited (exitCode 254). The cause is in <agent>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/logs/tomcat/tomcat_<version>.log around the start time, for example 'SalesforceConnection_10122 Login failed ... Fault code [LOGIN_MUST_USE_SECURITY_TOKEN]'. Fix the login (L-CONN-110), not the mapping; the connection test from the same agent shows the same error. Newer evidence: L-CONN-137.
evidence: 2 tasks, same symptom, tomcat log shows the login fault then 'exitCode: 254'

title: A Salesforce password login depends on the agent's egress IP: the same credentials work from an agent inside the org's trusted ranges and fail LOGIN_MUST_USE_SECURITY_TOKEN from another
text: A connection that tests fine on one runtime environment can fail on another with LOGIN_MUST_USE_SECURITY_TOKEN: the first agent's public IP is in the org's Network Access (or profile login IP) ranges, the second is not, and the security token kept with the credentials may be stale (it resets whenever the password changes, so resetting it breaks every other connection of that user). Options: add the second agent's egress IP to Network Access (an admin click), or supply a current token; a Connected App with client credentials is not an option for the CDI connector. Find the egress IP with a curl to an IP echo service from the agent host. Newer evidence: L-CONN-141.
evidence: one user, two agents: test OK on one, LOGIN_MUST_USE_SECURITY_TOKEN on the other

title: Nightly batch with a source that can be down: append its Bronze with a run id, read the latest run, and let its taskflow steps continue on error
text: A truncate pre-SQL empties the Bronze table before the source is read, so a failed read leaves nothing and every decision downstream goes blank. Append instead (no presql), stamp each row with the run id, and read QUALIFY IDMC_RUN_ID = MAX(IDMC_RUN_ID) OVER () (per table, before any join); set stopOnError = false on those steps only. A failed read then writes nothing, the batch processes what is already archived, and Monitor shows the failed step honestly. Keep truncate-and-reload for Silver and Gold, which are rebuilt from Bronze every run.
evidence: taskflow 10 steps: the 2 source steps failed (login), 8 SUCCESS, decisions unchanged (6/6)

title: Archive every version, read only the newest: '<title> (vN).<ext>' in the archive, ROW_NUMBER per document in the file-list view
text: When a document is attached again upstream as a new version, archive it next to the first one as '<title> (v2).<ext>' (the library connector never overwrites, L-CONN-107) and make the file list the readers use keep one row per document: QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY <folder>, REGEXP_REPLACE(<name>, ' [(]v[0-9]+[)]', '') ORDER BY <version number> DESC NULLS LAST, <modified> DESC) = 1. Every reader that filters its Bronze on that list then sees exactly the newest version, and taking the version out of play restores the previous one.
evidence: what-if: v2 in play -> the decision flips to the corrected copy; v2 out of play -> back (real runs)

title: v3 folder create also refuses a dot (400); FRS MoveEntities to a missing target answers HTTP 200 with XFER_500 per entity
text: POST /public/core/v3/projects/<id>/folders with a name containing '.' returns 400 (like projects, L-MIG-075): create it with '_' and rename it through FRS PATCH Folders('<id>') {name}. And FRS /frs/v1/MoveEntities with a null or wrong targetLocationId still answers HTTP 200: the failure is in value[].resultValue = 'XFER_500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR'. Check resultValue for every entity and stop before any follow-up (tagging) when one failed.
evidence: folder create 400 with a dot, 201 without; 11 moves 200/XFER_500, then 11 moves OK after the fix

title: A cloned file-pickup mapping keeps the clone source's pattern file: it lists the other project's folders and never its own
text: A SharePoint (or any file) pickup copied from another project keeps the source's runtime attribute 'Indirect File Path' (a pattern file on the agent) in both runtimeAttributes and oprRuntimeAttributes. It runs green but lists only the folders of the project it was cloned from. Give each pickup its own pattern file (one line per folder depth, URL-encoded) and patch both attributes in place (export -> edit the IMF -> import OVERWRITE; the task keeps the same mapping GUID). Never edit the shared file: the original project still reads it.
evidence: cloned pickup listed 6 files of the original project; patched to its own file (2 patterns)

title: An integration user with object access can still miss fields: Salesforce answers 'No such column' (INVALID_FIELD) for a field its field-level security hides
text: A permission set can grant Read/Create on an object (Account) while the field permissions leave standard fields such as AccountNumber, Industry or Description unticked. The API then behaves as if they do not exist: SOQL fails with INVALID_FIELD 'No such column ... on entity', describe omits them, and a mapping that reads or filters on them fails at run time. Before designing on a field, describe the object AS THE CONNECTION'S USER and keep to the fields it returns; when a business key is hidden, use one the user can see (for example a naming rule on a visible field) or ask the admin to tick the field permissions in the same permission set. A wholly invisible object answers INVALID_TYPE ('sObject type ... is not supported') and a 404 on describe.
evidence: Account readable, AccountNumber/Industry/Description invisible (INVALID_FIELD); Opportunity invisible (INVALID_TYPE, describe 404)

title: Re-importing a mapping under the same GUID renames the task's parameters but keeps the task's description
text: When a mapping is re-imported with OVERWRITE under its existing GUID and its transformations have new names, the mapping task re-derives its `parameters[]` from the new names (`$<NEW_NAME>$`) and keeps their connections, objects and operations. Its pre- and post-processing commands are kept too. The task's `description` and `shortDescription` are not updated: Explore keeps showing the old text. To change them, GET `/api/v2/mttask/<id>`, drop orgId/createTime/updateTime/createdBy/updatedBy, set `description`, POST the body back to the same id, then read it back.
evidence: read-back of the task before and after an OVERWRITE redeploy and a v2 POST (2026-10-12)

title: The Databricks Delta Lake catalog source type is end-of-life: a create is refused
text: `datasourceTypes` lists `Databricks Delta Lake` with `endOfLife: true` (bound to Databricks Delta connections); a create answers 500 'Informatica dropped support for DataSourceType Databricks Delta Lake'. The only other Databricks type, `Databricks Notebooks`, catalogs notebooks, not Unity Catalog tables or views. So there is no Databricks physical source to MERGE a Databricks connection reference onto: lineage shows the Databricks tables an IDMC task writes as referenced nodes, and view-on-table lineage inside Databricks is not derived. Page `datasourceTypes` with offset (100 per page; totalElements 105 seen) before concluding a type is absent.
evidence: multipart create on the catalog-source-management API and a full paged datasourceTypes read (2026-10-12)

title: A task whose target is the Tableau V3 connector gets no lineage from an IICS source
text: The IICS scanner log shows 'Unknown writer type: TableauV3_extracts Writer' and then 'Analysing lineage for Graph ... Inputs: 1, Outputs: 0': the target is dropped and the task's asset has zero lineage hops, upstream as well as downstream (its source dataset is not created either). Tasks writing to relational targets in the same project got full column-level lineage in the same scan. Read the agent's Metadata_Foundation_Agent workspace log `<source>_Sync.log` for 'Unknown writer type' when one task of a project shows no lineage.
evidence: scanner Sync log on the agent and the asset lineage segment of each task (2026-10-12)

title: Stitch a Salesforce connection reference onto the Salesforce source's Organization root
text: For an IICS source whose tasks read Salesforce, MERGE the reference `<iicsSourceId>_<CONNECTION NAME>://<CONNECTION NAME>~core.DataSource` (the name is upper-cased) onto `{"externalId": "<sfSourceId>://<OrgName>~com.infa.odin.models.Salesforce.Organization", "origin": "<sfSourceId>", "isCaseSensitive": false, "location": "<sfSourceId>://<sfSourceId>/<OrgName>"}` (OrgName = the Salesforce org's company name, as the scan cataloged it). The job took about 6 minutes; afterwards each Salesforce field read showed an inbound hop from `<OrgName>/<Object>/<Field>` into the task and an outbound hop to the target column, without a rescan.
evidence: connectionAssignment MERGE job COMPLETED, then asset lineage segments read hop by hop (2026-10-12)

title: Copy-data template tasks with an object source (no custom query) give column-level lineage
text: Tasks on the copy-data template that name a source object and a target object, with no `customQuery`, produced column-level lineage through an IICS source with Lineage Discovery: source field > task Calculation > target column, one per field. The 'two-box canvas, logic invisible' limit of L-CDI-115 / L-CDGC-091 applies to tasks that carry SQL in `customQuery`, not to object-to-object copies.
evidence: IICS source scan of six copy-data tasks, asset lineage segment reads (2026-10-12)

title: A catalog source scans on its own runtime environment, not on the bound connection's: use that to scan a SaaS source whose agent cannot sign in
text: A Salesforce catalog source binds a connection by `ConnectionId` but runs on the runtime environment set in `globalConfigOptions` > Execution > Runtime Settings. A connection whose own agent failed every test with LOGIN_MUST_USE_SECURITY_TOKEN (that agent's IP is not trusted by the Salesforce org) scanned with Test Connection COMPLETED when the catalog source ran on another agent whose IP is trusted. The mapping tasks keep running where they are. Objects the integration user cannot see are not cataloged: after the reference MERGE they stay grey references until the permission set grants them and the source is rescanned.
evidence: Salesforce catalog source on a connection whose agent fails login: scan PARTIAL_COMPLETED, test connection COMPLETED, 2 of 3 filtered objects cataloged (the third lacks object permission) (2026-10-12)

title: A view-SQL lineage chain breaks at any object outside the warehouse source's include filter
text: When a narrow include filter (for example a table prefix) leaves out a shared table and the views that read it, the downstream view's lineage shows the missing view as a dead end, and a mapping task that writes the shared table is not linked to anything downstream. Add the shared table and every view between it and your objects to the Metadata Filter Config `Filter Value` (a PUT of the source), rescan Metadata Extraction, then rescan the IICS source. The chain table > view > view > mapping task then reads through.
evidence: after adding 1 table + 2 views to the include filter and rescanning, the walk ran from the writing task through both views to the reading tasks (2026-10-12)

title: A Tableau catalog source needs a 'Tableau V3' connection on an agent that can reach the Tableau server
text: `datasourceTypes` lists type Tableau with one option, `ConnectionId` (iicsConnectionTypes 'Tableau V3'), versions 2019.x through 2023.x, username/password or token authentication, and filters by Path pattern. Its scanner runs on the Secure Agent, so a Tableau Server that only allows the corporate network cannot be scanned from cloud-hosted agents (requests time out). Until an agent inside that network exists, read the catalog lineage over REST and show it in the BI tool itself.
evidence: datasourceTypes + type capability configuration read; curl from two cloud agents to the server timed out while a corporate laptop got 200 (2026-10-12)

title: Object permissions over REST: read, add and remove access-control entries on projects, assets, connections and runtime environments
text: `GET /saas/public/core/v3/objects/<frsId>/permissions` returns the object's access-control list; `[]` means no restriction (anyone whose roles allow the type). `POST` to the same path with `{"principal":{"type":"USER"|"GROUP","name":"<user name or group name>"},"permissions":{"read":true,"update":true,"delete":true,"execute":true,"changePermission":true}}` returns 201 and a list holding the new entry with its `id`; the same principal given by `id` instead of `name` gets a bare 400 V3API_007. `DELETE .../permissions/<entryId>` returns 204. Connections and runtime environments take their v2 `federatedId`; a catalog-source UUID is refused with 400 V3API_AccessControlError_001. The first entry restricts the object to the listed principals, so add the owner first, and list the CAI anonymous user too or CAI processes cannot run the restricted tasks (vendor Asset Management guide). An empty body names the missing parts (`principal`, then `permission`). Writes took about one second each.
evidence: 201 + read-back + 204 on a probe connection; 972 entries written on 81 objects (projects, assets, connections, runtime environments) and read back (2026-10-13)

title: Role, group and membership writes: the 'must not be empty' message names the Java field, not the JSON property
text: `POST /public/core/v3/roles` answers "Field 'privilegeIds' must not be empty", yet a body with `privilegeIds` gets a bare 400 V3API_007; the JSON property is `privileges`, a list of privilege ids (read them with `GET /roles?q=roleId==%22<id>%22&expand=privileges`; 'Default'-status privileges are accepted) -> 201. In the same way `POST /userGroups` names 'roleIds' but takes `roles` (role ids), and `PUT /userGroups/<id>/addUsers` names 'userNames' but takes `users` (user names) -> 204. `PUT /users/<id>/removeRoles` and `/addRoles` take `roles` as role NAMES (a bad value is reported as 'name is invalid'), `/removeGroups` and `/addGroups` take `groups` as group names. A user must keep one direct role: removing the last one answers 400 V3API_IDSError_044 "The group must have at least one role" (it means the user), so add the new role before removing the old ones. When a correctly named body gets a bare V3API_007, drop the Ids/Names suffix. In `q=` filters, URL-encode the double quotes and spaces (`roleName==%22Data%20Viewer%22`).
evidence: role create 400 with privilegeIds, 201 with privileges; group create and addUsers 400 with the validator's names, 201/204 with roles/users; removeGroups by name 204; removeRoles of all six direct roles 400 IDSError_044, then addRoles + removeRoles by name 204 (2026-10-13)

title: Limit one user to one project: a view-and-run role, a group, and object permissions on everything else for everyone else
text: Role privileges cap what a user can do; object permissions cap which objects the user sees. (1) Build a custom role from the view and execute privileges of the system roles Data Integration Task Executor and Monitor (DI, DQ, Profile and Monitor services plus Admin view.project, view.folder, view.connection, view.agent, view.agent.group; no schedule, CAI, catalog, MDM, Marketplace or CLAIRE privileges) and a group that holds it. (2) On every other project, connection and runtime environment, add entries with all five permissions for every other group, every other named user and the CAI anonymous user, which keeps everyone else's access as it was. (3) Remove the user's other groups and direct roles and add the new group. Leave the target project, its connections and its runtime environments without entries (the role already limits the user to view and run there). Installed-app projects (MDM) and system content can stay open when the role cannot list their asset types; restrict only the viewable assets inside them. Snapshot users, groups and every list first, and log each entry id for the undo.
evidence: applied on an org with 27 projects, 58 connections and 4 runtime environments: 81 objects x 12 principals, read back; undo = DELETE of the logged entry ids plus the role and group writes (2026-10-13)

title: A Snowflake BINARY column cannot feed a CDI source ('Unknown native type'): keep the bytes as base64 text
text: A mapping whose Snowflake source (a view) exposed a BINARY column failed with 'Unknown native type' for that field. The same bytes kept as base64 text in a VARCHAR(16777216) column read fine and decode in an Expression with DEC_BASE64 (L-CDI-244). Check large values inside the warehouse, for example `SHA2(BASE64_DECODE_BINARY(<col>))` against the file's SHA-256, not through the SQL API: the API splits a large result into partitions (`resultSetMetaData.partitionInfo`, more pages with `?partition=<n>`), and a client that reads only the first response sees part of it.
evidence: the BINARY source failed; base64 text read and decoded; both documents' hashes matched inside the warehouse (2026-10-13)

title: Parse a document whose bytes sit in a column, with no file on the agent: DEC_BASE64 to a binary port, then a Structure Parser in BUFFER mode
text: When the document arrives as base64 text in a column (for example a CRM file body landed in a warehouse VARCHAR), parse it without writing a file. Add an Expression output port `DEC_BASE64(<base64 column>)` with platform type binary and a precision at least the largest document (8,388,608 worked). Set the Structure Parser's `inputType` to `BUFFER`, give its Input_Group field `Data` (binary) and the data adapter's input field `Data` the same precision, and map the binary port onto `Data` in the parser's field mapping. Keep the base64 text out of the parser's input group (an exclude rule on the link): every incoming field is passed through to each parsed row, so a 1.3 MB text column would be repeated on every output row.
evidence: two PDFs (15 pages and 1 page) parsed from warehouse rows in one run each: 29 line rows and 1 form row (2026-10-13)

title: A Salesforce datetime source field validates at precision 24, scale 0; a semi-join SOQL filter runs but hides the source from lineage
text: In a generated mapping, a Salesforce source field with nativeType `datetime` (platform date/time, precision 24, scale 0) passed source-definition validation and loaded into a warehouse timestamp column. Precisions 29/0, 19/0 and 29/9 had stopped the session with "Field <name>'s precision is invalid" (L-CDI-217). The source's SOQL filter (`readOptions.filterCondition`) may use a semi-join on another object at run time, for example `<lookupField> IN (SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name IN ('<a>','<b>'))` (Salesforce refuses a semi-join on the same object as the outer query), but the catalog cannot parse it and drops the source from lineage (L-CDGC-196): prefer a literal list.
evidence: the first run stopped with the precision error (agent session log); precision 24 ran and loaded every row; the semi-join filter returned only the matching parents' rows (2026-10-13)

title: REG_EXTRACT returns NULL unless the pattern matches the whole value
text: In the CDI expression language REG_EXTRACT matches its pattern against the whole input, like a full match: a pattern for a leading code, `'^([0-9A-Z]+(-[0-9A-Z]+)+)'`, returned NULL on values that continue after the code, and the same pattern ending in `.*` returned the code as group 1. Test an expression on real values before a run, and backfill rows already loaded with NULL.
evidence: rows landed with NULL; with `.*` appended the next run extracted the code (2026-10-13)

title: After a profiled table is recreated with other columns, recreate its profile, on a view: a new profile on the table returned no rule metrics
text: When the columns of a profiled table changed (drop and recreate), its profile with rule occurrences failed with 'Invalid operation field name'. A new profile on the same table ran but returned no rule metrics, while a new profile on a view over the table returned them (cause not isolated). Delete the old profile with `DELETE /profiling-service/api/v1/profile/<id>`, recreate it, and profile a view when the table's DDL may change again.
evidence: 2 profiles deleted and recreated; the view-based profile returned rule-occurrence metrics on its first run (2026-10-13)

title: No per-catalog-source permission route was found: a user who must not see other sources gets no catalog role
text: To show one user only some catalog sources: `GET /ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>` carries no access-control fields, six guessed sub-resources (`permissions`, `acl`, `acls`, `accessControl`, `accessControlList`, `access`) answer 404 'No static resource' exactly like a bogus id, and the platform object-permissions API refuses a catalog-source UUID (400 V3API_AccessControlError_001). Until a route is found, give such a user no catalog role and show the lineage and glossary they need through a BI view fed from the catalog's REST reads.
evidence: probes on one catalog source and a bogus twin (2026-10-13)

title: A Snowflake resource monitor that suspends at its quota stops every IDMC, catalog and BI job on the warehouse
text: When a resource monitor with a suspend trigger reaches its credit quota, every client of the warehouse fails at once: the SQL API answers 422 with code 090073 "Warehouse '<wh>' cannot be resumed because resource monitor '<monitor>' has exceeded its quota", and IDMC tasks, catalog profiling and BI extract refreshes on that warehouse fail the same way until an account admin raises the quota or the monitor's period resets. A role without MONITOR on the monitor sees no rows in SHOW RESOURCE MONITORS. A catalog scan with data profiling runs its queries on the connection's warehouse and counts against the quota: size the quota for profiling, or profile only the tables that matter. Newer evidence: L-ENV-135, L-ENV-136.
evidence: 090073 on every statement after a week of builds and a catalog scan with profiling (2026-10-13)

title: A semi-join in a Salesforce source's SOQL filter drops that source from catalog lineage
text: The IICS catalog source parses each Salesforce source's SOQL filter (`readOptions.filterCondition`, shown in the task metadata as the 'SOQL Filter Condition' attribute). A semi-join such as `<field> IN (SELECT Id FROM Account WHERE Name IN ('<a>','<b>'))` fails with `ERROR ... SalesforceSOQLFailedProcessingHandler ... ParseException: Parse error (InputMismatch) on token: '<field>'` in the scanner log, and the source object is silently left out: the target columns it feeds have no upstream, the task's inbound lineage lists only the other sources, and the catalog job still ends COMPLETED. The run itself works. For lineage, filter on literal values instead (for example `<field> IN ('<id1>','<id2>')`), then run the task once (L-CDGC-197).
evidence: scanner debug log of two syncs (ParseException on the semi-join filter); the agency source of the same mapping (plain filter) linked, the documents source (semi-join) did not; column lineage of its target columns empty (2026-10-13)

title: The IICS catalog source reads each mapping task's run metadata: a mapping change reaches lineage only after the task runs again
text: The scanner's task reader (`LdmTaskReader`) downloads, per mapping task, the metadata IDMC writes when the task runs (a PowerMart-style XML, cached on the agent under `<agent_home>/apps/Metadata_Foundation_Agent/data/workspaces/<source>-*/jobs/<job>/cache/iics/<task>.xml`). A task that never ran is skipped ("cannot be downloaded because there is no corresponding metadata ... might not have metadata because it has never been run"), and after a mapping is changed and redeployed the catalog keeps showing the old definition (old filters, old sources) until the task has run once with the new mapping. Saving a change in a cataloged project starts an automatic job of type 'Catalog Source Sync' named '<source>_IICS_sync' within seconds; it re-applies the connection assignments (Merge Operation), and a manual scan of that source meanwhile is refused with 406 'Job is in progress'. Diagnose lineage gaps from `<workspace>/logs/*.log` (search 'Converting source', 'ERROR', 'cannot be processed').
evidence: a redeployed mapping's task XML in the sync cache still carried the old SOQL filter; the never-run task warning; the sync job started 14 s after the redeploy and listed Merge Operation and Connection Assignment tasks (2026-10-13)

title: Lineage passes a Structure Parser only as an unknown transformation
text: For a mapping task with a Structure Parser (CLAIRE intelligent structure model), the IICS scanner logs `Unknown custom transformation type: StructureDiscovery` and keeps the task's object-level lineage (the parser's input table -> the task -> the target table). Do not promise column-level lineage through the parser in a demo; show the object level, and the model in the mapping.
evidence: warning logged for both parsing tasks in two scans; object-level edges into and out of both tasks present (2026-10-13)

title: ContentVersion.FirstPublishLocationId is set on version 1 only: filtering on it misses every new version of a file
text: Salesforce fills `FirstPublishLocationId` (the record a file was first attached to) only on a file's first ContentVersion; every later version, uploaded with `ContentDocumentId`, has it null. A source filter such as `FirstPublishLocationId IN ('<parentId>')` (or a semi-join on the parent object) therefore never reads a new version, and a pipeline that should react to an updated document silently keeps the old one. Filter on `ContentDocumentId IN ('<docId>',...)` instead (the same on every version), or find the documents first through `ContentDocumentLink` (`LinkedEntityId = '<parentId>'`), and carry the parent attributes from version 1 downstream (for example `MAX(<parent column>) OVER (PARTITION BY <document id>)` in a warehouse view).
evidence: SOQL read-back of four versions: version 1 had the parent id, versions 2 had null; the pipeline read no new version until the filter moved to ContentDocumentId, then decided on version 2 (2026-10-13)

title: A ContentVersion new-version insert through the CDI Salesforce connector was rejected although the same fields work over REST
text: A generated mapping inserting ContentVersion (ContentDocumentId, Title, PathOnClient, ReasonForChange, and VersionData as base64 text in a string port of native type base64; standard SOAP API, normal mode, API 64.0) failed every row with `WRT_8164 ... REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING ... [Title]` and `INVALID_ARGUMENT_TYPE ... The argument is null or invalid`, although the session log's row data shows Title and VersionData filled. The same five fields sent with REST `POST /services/data/v<nn>/sobjects/ContentVersion` returned 201. Reading VersionData through the connector works (L-CONN-108). Not tried: a binary-typed port for VersionData, Bulk API mode. Workaround that works: write the file version over REST (a CAI REST connector, or a task's pre-processing command) and keep the mapping for logging.
evidence: two rows rejected in three runs with Title present in the row data; REST insert of the same fields 201 (2026-10-13)

title: Scan a Tableau Server that only the corporate network reaches: a temporary reverse SSH tunnel to the scanning agent
text: When the Secure Agent that runs catalog scans cannot reach the Tableau Server (L-CDGC-194) but a workstation can, open `ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:<port>:<tableau-host>:<port> <agent-host>` from the workstation and add `127.0.0.1 <tableau-host>` to the agent host's /etc/hosts, so the server keeps its real name in the catalog. Enable the Tableau V3 connector on the agent's runtime environment, create a Tableau V3 connection (tableauProduct 'Tableau Server', authMethod 'Username & Password', connectionURL = the plain server URL `http://<host>:<port>` with no /api suffix: with /api/<version> the test answers 404003 Resource Not Found; site empty for the default site), and scan. Keep the tunnel up only for the scan, then remove the hosts line and kill the ssh process; on Windows a stopped background shell can leave ssh.exe running, so check the agent host for the listener afterwards. Enabling a connector can roll the Data Integration Server: a scan started in that window fails at Test Connection, so wait until every agent engine reports RUNNING.
