Clear it with the network owner first: the tunnel lets an outside host reach an internal server.
evidence: Tableau Server 2021.4 scanned from a cloud VM agent through a laptop tunnel; connection test 200, a wrong password gave 401001 Signin Error; scan PARTIAL_COMPLETED with workbooks, dashboards, worksheets and data sources cataloged (2026-10-16)

title: Tableau catalog source path filters are site/project/workbook patterns
text: The Tableau type's Metadata Filter Config takes Filter Type 'Path', Filter Conditions 'Pattern' and Filter Value patterns that the scanner splits on '/' into site, project and workbook (it logs them as `tableau.inputFilters.N=Include:<site>:<project>:<workbook>`). A bare workbook pattern such as `*Sales*` is matched against SITE names, and the scan fails at Test Connection with 'No sites matches given site patterns'. Use `*/<Project>/<Workbook pattern>`. Narrow filters matter on a shared server: other teams' workbooks would otherwise be cataloged.
evidence: first scan failed 'No sites matches given site patterns'; with */<project>/<workbook> patterns 5 workbooks and 14 dashboards were cataloged (2026-10-16)

title: A Tableau calculated field with a blank caption drops its whole data source from catalog lineage
text: If a Tableau data source holds a calculated field whose caption is blank (for example a single space, a common trick for empty table cells), the Tableau scanner logs 'Can not convert graph <datasource> ... Trying to build asset from Calculation but it's name is blank' and leaves that data source's upstream out: no edge from the warehouse table or view to the data source, although the workbook, worksheets and dashboards are cataloged and the scan ends PARTIAL_COMPLETED. Give the field a real caption, or a no-break space (U+00A0), which renders the same but is not blank to the scanner; republish and rescan. Then MERGE the Tableau source's warehouse connection reference onto the warehouse catalog source (connection assignment, L-CDGC-159) so the edge lands on the scanned view.
evidence: before: 0 downstream edges from the warehouse view; after the caption fix, republish, rescan and MERGE: view -> Tableau data source -> worksheets -> dashboard (2026-10-16)

title: DELETE on a catalog source purges its metadata but keeps the definition; update it with a multipart PUT that carries its id
text: `DELETE .../ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>` answers 200 with a datasourceDeleteJobResponse whose only task is 'Metadata Bulk Purge'; the job COMPLETES and the catalog source definition is still listed afterwards (same id, isDeleted false). To change its filters, send `PUT .../datasources/<id>` as multipart part `dataSource` with the full definition INCLUDING `id`: 200 'datasource <name> updated successfully', and a read-back shows the new Filter Values.
evidence: source still listed 8 min after the purge job COMPLETED; PUT with id updated the filters (2026-10-16)

title: A generated Rule Specification transformation must copy the rule's field scale, or the Mapping Designer shows Invalid
text: When a mapping embeds a rule specification (TmplRuleSpecification inputFields/outputFields), each field's precision AND scale must equal the rule specification's own field (documentBlob inputFields, for example decimal 18,4). With scale 0 against a decimal 18,4 input, the server still reports the mapping valid=true and every run succeeds, but the Mapping Designer badge shows Invalid when the mapping is opened. Read the rule's inputFields from a v3 export and write the same precision and scale; a re-import with OVERWRITE under the same GUID keeps the task and taskflow.
evidence: rule input decimal(18,4) embedded as (18,0): designer Invalid, v2 valid=true, runs OK; fixed by writing scale 4 and re-importing in place

title: A PostgreSQL catalog filter of type 'Tables' leaves views out, so mappings reading views show grey referenced nodes
text: With Metadata Filter Config Filter Type 'Tables' and a value such as `<schema>.*`, a PostgreSQL scan catalogs only tables: a schema that holds only views gets no assets at all, and every mapping that reads those views shows them as grey 'referenced' DataSets in lineage, even after the connection reference is MERGEd onto the database. Use Filter Type 'All' for schemas that hold views, rescan the database source, then rescan the IICS source.
evidence: a schema of views had 0 cataloged objects with 'Tables'; after 'All' + rescans its 4 objects resolved in lineage (2026-10-17)

title: A newly provisioned catalog tenant can have no built-in Data Element Classifications
text: In a catalog tenant provisioned the same day (by the first interactive open), an ES term query on `core.classType` = `core.DataElementClassification` and a knowledgeQuery search for 'Email' returned no classification assets, although a PostgreSQL scan with Data Classification completed (including its Auto Classification step). So the manual PATCH of segment dataClassification (L-CDGC-060) has no classification identity to add. Check that the library exists before planning classification work in a new org; opening the Classifications area in the UI once is the likely trigger (not yet verified).
evidence: 0 DataElementClassification assets in the new tenant; 6 reviewed classifications could not be re-applied (2026-10-17)

title: An IICS catalog scan can fail at Test Connection on a transient IDMC 500: retry before changing the source
text: An IICS source's scan failed at Test Connection with 'Unexpected response received, code: 500 ... CMN_001 ... I/O error on GET request for "https://<pod>/cloudshell/api/v1/Products": Read timed out' in the agent's `<source>_Sync.log`. The same definition scanned COMPLETED on the next try minutes later. Read the Sync log first: a 500 from cloudshell is the service, not the IICS URL, user or password.
evidence: failed in 124 s, COMPLETED on the retry 15 min later with no change (2026-10-17)

title: After the agent is killed mid-cycle, a CDC job can fail on resume with 'recovery table has more than one entry of type CYCLE_ENTRY': dedupe the identical rows, then resume
text: When the Secure Agent host's OOM killer took down a Database Ingestion CDC job (PostgreSQL to BigQuery), the job went awaiting_auto_restart, then failed, and job/resume failed again after about 13 s with DBMIP_20004 'Recovery manager failed to initialize ... Internal logic error - recovery table has more than one entry of type CYCLE_ENTRY'. The target's INFORMATICA_CDC_RECOVERY table held byte-identical duplicate rows for that task (one CYCLE_ENTRY and some TABLE_ENTRY rows written twice), so the restart position itself was intact. Fix: copy the table to a backup, then in one transaction replace that TASK_ID's rows with SELECT DISTINCT of them (touch no other task), then POST job/resume: the job stayed running. If the duplicate rows differ (not identical), stop and read them: choosing a restart point is a data decision.
evidence: BigQuery target, 10 rows -> 7 distinct for the task; resume running and error-free afterwards (2026-10-19)

title: An OOM kill of one agent JVM stops the whole infaagent systemd unit as 'failed': it does not restart itself
text: On a Linux Secure Agent run as a systemd service, the kernel OOM killer took one java process; systemd then stopped every agent service (orderly shutdown in agentcore.log, which reads like a manual stop) and left infaagent.service in 'failed' (result oom-kill). IDMC shows the agent active=false and every engine STOPPED. Check `journalctl -u infaagent` for 'oom-kill' before suspecting a person or the IDMC login. Recover with `systemctl reset-failed infaagent && systemctl start infaagent` (about 9 minutes until every engine is RUNNING), then resume any failed CDC jobs. Adding engines (for example the CAI process engine, about 1.8 GB resident) raises memory use; size the host or set Restart=on-failure.
evidence: journalctl 'Failed with result oom-kill'; restart brought 10/10 engines RUNNING (2026-10-19)

title: The 'Databricks Notebooks' catalog source type is the full native Databricks (Unity Catalog) scanner
text: `Databricks Delta Lake` stays end-of-life (a create is refused, L-CDGC-188), but `Databricks Notebooks` is the current unified Databricks source despite its name (the vendor docs call it 'Databricks'). Its Metadata Extraction configuration offers Filter Type Path / Table / AI Model / Workflow Job / Pipeline / Volume / Dashboard Path and a 'Databricks parameters' group with `databricks.lineageFromUnity` (Disabled / Enabled for filtered assets / Enabled for all assets) and `databricks.extractTagAssets`. Bound by `ConnectionId` to a native Databricks Delta connection, it cataloged a Unity Catalog schema's database, schema, tables, views and columns (the same objects a JDBC V2 source of that schema holds) and derived view-on-table and view-on-view lineage from the view SQL with no curated edges. A metric view is cataloged as a Table and gets no edge to its source table (the metric-view YAML is not parsed; metric views are announced for the October 2026 scanner release). Unity Catalog lineage needs the scan user to read `system.access.table_lineage` and `column_lineage`: without USE SCHEMA on `system.access` the scanner logs 'System tables are not present, will proceed with API fetch', and `/api/2.0/lineage-tracking/table-lineage` then answered 403 'does not have permission to query table' even for the table owner. Every object is flagged and the job ends PARTIAL_COMPLETED although the metadata is complete. A metastore or account admin grants USE SCHEMA on `system.access` and SELECT on the two lineage tables. Create body: typeOptions 'Databricks Notebooks Connection OptionGroup'; Metadata Extraction typeCapability groups 'Metadata Filter Config' (Table, Pattern, '<catalog>.<schema>.*'), 'Databricks parameters', 'Scanner Configuration Options' and 'Partitioned File Configuration' (201 on the first POST). Prefer it to a JDBC V2 source for Databricks: no driver shim, and view lineage is derived.
evidence: full paged datasourceTypes read (105) and capability configuration reads; multipart create 201; scan PARTIAL_COMPLETED with Lineage Discovery COMPLETED; catalog search and asset lineage reads; scanner Sync and debug logs on the agent; a direct lineage-tracking API call answering 403 (2026-10-19); a second native source that replaced a JDBC V2 source derived view-on-view lineage from the SQL and again cataloged the metric view as a Table (2026-10-19); vendor docs, Metadata Command Center 'Databricks Sources' (Sept 2026)

title: FRS rename refuses parentheses in the NEW name (FRS_082), even when the old name has them; a rename also updates linear taskflows
text: `PATCH .../frs/api/v1/Documents('<id>')` with a name containing '(' or ')' answers 400 FRS_082 "Name '<n>' is not valid because it contains the following characters: '()'" and changes nothing (the description in the same body is not applied either), although objects created by import can carry parentheses. Drop them from the new name and resend. A rename of a mapping task through FRS also shows at once in every v2 linear taskflow that runs it (`GET /api/v2/workflow/<id>` tasks[].name), because the taskflow binds by taskId; the taskflow, the tasks' mapping, runtime and pre/post commands were unchanged and a run after the rename succeeded with the same row counts. Activity-log entries keep the name the object had at run time, so scripts that match runs by name must accept both names.
evidence: 71 objects renamed or re-described in one org (mappings, mapping tasks, linear taskflows, rule specifications, CLAIRE models, folders, project): all 204 + read-back; one 400 FRS_082 for a name with '(5 digits)'; two taskflow runs green after the rename

title: Rename a data profile through the profiling service, not FRS: GET the full profile, change name and description, PUT it back
text: A data profile keeps its own name and description in the profiling service (`GET https://<pod>-dqprofile.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/profiling-service/api/v1/profile/<id>`), which is what profile-list scripts read. `PUT .../profile/<id>` with the complete GET body and only `name` and `description` changed answers 200 and updates both the profiling service and the FRS document (Explore) at once; profileableFields and source.rules stay as they were because the full body is sent (an omitted field would be ignored, not removed). Scripts that look profiles up by exact name need the new name or an alias.
evidence: 3 profiles renamed: service name, FRS name and description read back equal; field and rule counts unchanged (13/4 and the others)

title: Move a Linux Secure Agent to a bigger host by copying its install directory: same agent id, same runtime environment, no re-registration
text: To move an agent to a new VM (for example a host that cannot be resized because the bigger size has a smaller disk), create the new host with the same OS release, the same agent user and UID/GID, the same install path and the same hostname. rsync the whole agent home live first (-aHAX --numeric-ids), then stop any CDC jobs with job/stop, stop the old agent service, rsync the delta (seconds), and start the service on the new host. It came back as the same agent id in the same runtime environment, with every engine RUNNING in about a minute; third-party drivers under ext/, host-side fixes and the embedded process-engine database came along, and nothing in IDMC changed. Then repoint anything that reached the old host by IP (SSH tunnels, file pushes, source-side IP allow lists such as a Salesforce trusted range) and resume the CDC jobs. Rollback = stop the new service and start the old host. Keep the old host powered off, never both agents running.
evidence: 17 GB agent moved; delta copy 24 s; agent active with 10/10 engines; CDC resumed with zero slot lag; a Postgres-reading mapping task succeeded on the new host (2026-10-19)

title: A Tableau dashboard window without <viewpoints> makes the scanner skip the whole workbook, and a Delete-mode rescan purges it
text: The Tableau scanner logs 'Could not process workbook <name> in project <project> because of Cannot invoke ...XmlViewpoints.getViewpoint() because the return value of ...XmlWindow.getViewpoints() is null' when a `<window class='dashboard'>` in the TWB has no `<viewpoints>` child (typical of generated workbooks whose text-only dashboards hold no worksheet). The workbook, its embedded data sources and its connection references are left out, the job still ends COMPLETED, and with Metadata Change Option = Delete everything previously cataloged for that workbook is purged, including the connection assignments (MERGE) on its warehouse references. Fix: write `<viewpoints />` in every dashboard window (Tableau renders it the same), republish, rescan, then re-run the reference MERGE (L-CDGC-159). After a Tableau rescan, count the workbooks the source holds and grep the Sync log for 'Could not process workbook'.
evidence: scan COMPLETED with the workbook gone (workbooks 5 -> 4); after adding <viewpoints /> to 3 dashboard windows and republishing, the next scan cataloged the workbook and its 4 dashboards (2026-10-19)

title: Curated lineage takes a task only as the target: dataset -> task with core.DataSetDataProcess; task -> dataset is refused
text: On the ccgf-contentv2 publish (L-CDGC-179), `type: core.DataSetDataProcess` (the association the IICS scanner writes for table <-> task hops) accepts a dataset as source and a MappingTaskInstance as target (201). The opposite direction is refused with INVALID_RELATIONSHIP_CLASS_TYPE for a task instance, a mapping task or a mapping as source, toward a relational table, a Tableau data source or a referenced dataset, under core.DataSetDataProcess, core.DataSetDataFlow and core.DataProcessDataFlow; internal identities change nothing. Only the scanner writes task -> dataset. So when a scanner drops a task's writer (L-CDGC-189), publish dataset -> task (the read) and draw the write as dataset -> dataset with core.DataSetDataFlow; an upstream walk then skips the task. Also: a multi-item 207 does not return items in request order and the items carry no from/to, so publish one item per call when you record results; RELATIONSHIP_ALREADY_EXISTS (403) means the edge is there. Refines L-CDGC-179 ('a task instance cannot be an endpoint').
evidence: probes on one org: dataset -> task 201; task/mapping task/mapping -> 4 target classes x 3 associations all 400 INVALID_RELATIONSHIP_CLASS_TYPE; 15 other association names INVALID_REQUEST_PARAM (2026-10-19)

title: A Tableau published data source that holds a Hyper extract is cataloged as a referenced <name>.hyper/Extract dataset
text: When a workbook connects to a published data source whose content is a Hyper extract (for example one a Tableau V3 task publishes), the Tableau scanner downloads it, logs 'Published data source file is not available; lineage may be simplified', and does not create a Tableau DataSource asset named after it. The workbook's embedded data source gets an inbound hop from a reference `core.DataSet` named `Extract`, located under a reference `core.DataSource` `extract_<a>_<b>_{<GUID>}_<name>.hyper` (> `<name>.hyper` > `Extract`, with its columns as `core.DataElement`). Point curated edges at that `Extract` dataset. Its external id carries the extract GUID, so after the data source is republished and rescanned, resolve it again (the one with an outbound hop to a workbook data source) before writing edges.
evidence: Tableau scan of a workbook reading a published extract data source; asset and lineage reads (2026-10-19)

title: An unlock does not stick while a scheduled client still holds the old password: find it from the failed-login cadence in the security log
text: After a password reset, an IDMC user re-locked (IDS_086) minutes after an admin unlock. GET /public/core/v3/securityLog?limit=100..1000 (limit below 100 is a 400) showed USER_LOGIN_FAILED by 'System built-in user' twice every 5 minutes at hh:m0:02 and hh:m5:02, then ACCOUNT_LOCKED: the fingerprint of a */5 cron that logs in twice per run. Comparing SHA-256 prefixes of the stored passwords (never the values) located every copy of the stale one: a monitor's env file, a container env_file (needs a container recreate, not just a file edit), and a CAI app connection secret (asset/v1/update, then republish the connection). Pause the scheduled client first, then unlock, then update every copy, then re-enable; confirm with zero USER_LOGIN_FAILED afterwards. Prefer a dedicated integration user so a person's password reset cannot lock the automation.
evidence: failed-login cadence matched a */5 cron; after updating 3 copies and re-enabling: 0 failures, all runs green (2026-10-19)

title: Run connectionAssignment MERGE and SPLIT jobs one at a time: overlapping jobs on one reference both report FAILED
text: Each `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/assignment/connectionAssignment?operationType=MERGE` (or `SPLIT`) job took about 5 minutes. When a SPLIT on a connection reference was started while a MERGE on the same reference was still running, both jobs ended FAILED ('Merge/Split Operation FAILED', with no error text in the job's `outputProperties`), although the MERGE's Bulk Ingestion step had completed and its lineage edges appeared. So a FAILED assignment job does not tell you what was written: read the lineage back. Start one assignment job, poll `GET https://idmc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/data360/observable/v1/jobs/<jobId>?expandChildren=TASK-HIERARCHY` until it is COMPLETED, then start the next; re-run that way, all three jobs COMPLETED. Budget about 5 minutes per job when you move references from one catalog source to another.
evidence: a SPLIT started on a reference while its MERGE was running: both jobs FAILED with no error text in outputProperties, yet the MERGE's Bulk Ingestion step COMPLETED and its edges were read back; the same three jobs re-run one at a time all COMPLETED, about 5 minutes each (2026-10-19)

title: A SPLIT removes the connection assignment, not the lineage edges the old source already holds: a replaced source keeps a duplicate copy
text: When one catalog source replaces another for the same system (for example a JDBC source replaced by the native scanner, L-CDGC-206), you MERGE the IICS and Tableau connection references onto the new source and SPLIT them from the old one. The completed SPLIT does not remove the edges already written: the old source's tables kept their task and Tableau hops (`origin` = the old source) after both SPLIT jobs COMPLETED, so lineage and search show two copies of the same flow. Expect the duplicate to stay until the old source's metadata is purged (`DELETE .../ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>`, a Metadata Bulk Purge, L-CDGC-202); that the purge removes these edges is untested. Prove the swap by reading lineage from the new source's assets, and move whatever else points at the old assets (curated edges, L-CDGC-179; glossary term links) before the purge. Refines 'SPLIT undoes' in L-CDGC-159: it undoes the assignment, not the edges.
evidence: SPLIT jobs of an IICS and a Tableau connection reference from the old source COMPLETED; asset lineage reads of the old source's tables still showed the task and Tableau hops with origin = the old source (2026-10-19)

title: A catalog source PUT still needs id in the body, and its read-back reorders the capabilities: diff by capabilityName
text: `PUT https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources/<id>` (multipart part `dataSource`) again answered 400 'dataSource id in request path and body do not match' when the JSON omitted `id` (L-CDGC-163), so a script that strips read-only fields before the PUT must keep `id`. The GET after a successful PUT returns the `capabilities` and `typeCapabilities` arrays in a different order from the body sent, so a read-back diff by array index reports capabilities as changed that are not. Key both arrays by `capabilityName` before comparing. The Script Library's `idmc_cdgc.py source-update` keeps `id` and sorts both arrays by `capabilityName` before its diffs since 2026-10-19.
evidence: multipart PUT without id 400 'dataSource id in request path and body do not match', with id 200; the GET after the PUT listed capabilities and typeCapabilities in a different order from the body sent (2026-10-19)

title: What the Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent ran, and what still needed a Secure Agent
text: In a new org with no Secure Agent, the reserved runtime 'Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent' (v2 id `025000000000002`, the same short id with no org prefix; its federatedId is per org) ran CDI mapping tasks on Salesforce, Snowflake (Programmatic Access Token), Databricks and BigQuery connections, embedded Rule Specification transformations, and linear taskflows. Five things failed there and ran on a small Linux Secure Agent instead: Structure Parser (CLAIRE document parsing), Data Profiling, CDQ deduplicate/decision transformations, Tableau V3 targets, and SharePoint Online file transfers that stage bytes in Attachment_File_Path (each has its own lesson with the exact error). Bind only those tasks to the Secure Agent (the task's runtimeEnvironmentId) and keep everything else on the hosted runtime, so the Secure Agent can stay small.
evidence: Three demo projects cut over to a new org: every hosted task ran green, the five exceptions failed with the errors quoted in the related lessons and ran on the Secure Agent (2026-10-16)

title: A Structure Parser (CLAIRE document parsing) does not run on the Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent
text: A mapping task with a Structure Parser transformation that uses a CLAIRE intelligent structure model fails on the hosted runtime with "Cannot get object class for ... structurediscovery/runtime/StructureDiscoveryPlugin": the hosted Data Integration Server has no structure-discovery plugin. The same task, rebound to a Linux Secure Agent (whose DIS carries the pmstructurediscovery jars), parsed the documents. Rebind only the parser tasks (v2 mttask runtimeEnvironmentId) and leave the rest of the pipeline on the hosted runtime; give that agent's DTM enough heap for large documents (L-AGENT-056).
evidence: Both parser tasks failed on the hosted runtime and succeeded on a Secure Agent (29 lines and 1 form parsed), 2026-10-16

title: Data Profiling does not run on the Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent: EP_13236 libpmdpaggregate.so
text: Data Profiling profiles bound to the hosted runtime fail in under a minute with "EP_13236 Could not open the following dll: [.//libpmdpaggregate.so]. The reason is : [... cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory]" (read from the job log service, L-DQ-106): the hosted runtime has no profiling engine. Enable the 'Data Quality' service on a Secure Agent's runtime environment (selections PUT; it rolls DIS, L-AGENT-042) and rebind the profiles to it (next lesson); the same three profiles then COMPLETED in about 65 s each.
evidence: 3 imported profiles FAILED on the hosted runtime, COMPLETED on a Secure Agent with the Data Quality service (2026-10-16)

title: Move a Data Profiling profile to another runtime: runtimeOptions.runtimeEnvironmentId = the runtime's federatedId
text: To rebind a profile (for example after a cross-org import), GET the full profile, set `runtimeOptions.runtimeEnvironmentId` to the runtime environment's federatedId (the 22-character GUID from GET /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment, not its v2 id) and PUT the whole body back. A v2 id there answers FRS_070, and a top-level `runtimeEnvironmentId` field is accepted but ignored (the profile keeps running on the old runtime). Read the profile back and run it to confirm.
evidence: 3 profiles rebound and COMPLETED; the v2-id attempt returned FRS_070 and the top-level field changed nothing (2026-10-16)

title: CDQ deduplicate/decision transformations do not run on the Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent: libIDQDecisionZTransform.so
text: Mapping tasks that embed CDQ Deduplicate or decision-type DQ assets failed on the hosted runtime with "EP_13236 Could not open the following dll: [libIDQDecisionZTransform.so]. ... cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory" (the DTM terminated, 0 rows). Plain Rule Specification transformations did run there. Bind the dedupe/decision tasks to a Secure Agent that has the Data Quality service; they then ran with the same row counts as before the move. Newer evidence: L-CDI-279.
evidence: Cutover runs failed with the quoted error; the same tasks succeeded on a Secure Agent from the next run on (2026-10-16)

title: The Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent has no Tableau V3 adapter, even when its selections list the connector as enabled
text: A Tableau V3 connection bound to the hosted runtime fails its test with 403 APP_105060 naming the `tableauv3` adapter, although the hosted runtime's connector selections show Tableau V3 enabled; the adapter is simply not deployed there (L-CONN-018). Publishing to Tableau from IDMC therefore needs a Secure Agent with the Tableau V3 connector that can reach the Tableau server. Alternative with no agent: have IDMC write the governed result to a warehouse table and let Tableau read it live.
evidence: Connection test on the hosted runtime: APP_105060 tableauv3; the same connection type on a Secure Agent published data sources (2026-10-16, 2026-10-19)

title: A Tableau V2 connection test passes with a wrong password and a bogus host; a Tableau V3 test is a real sign-in
text: The IDMC Tableau V2 connection answered 'The test for this connection was successful.' with a wrong password and with a host that does not exist, so its test proves nothing. Tableau V3 (URL `http(s)://<tableau-server>:<port>`, no /api suffix, Tableau Server type) signs in for real: with the server reachable GET /api/v2/connection/test/<id> returned 200, and with it unreachable 403 APP_105060 "Connect to <host>:<port> [...] failed: Connection refused" (or a hang over 120 s on a fresh agent JVM). Prove a BI connection with a negative test (bad password) before trusting a green test.
evidence: V2: green with wrong password and bogus host; V3: 200 through a reachable path, APP_105060 'Connection refused' without it (2026-10-16, 2026-10-19)

title: Snowflake on a runtime that cannot hold a key file (the Hosted Agent): authenticate with a Programmatic Access Token
text: Key-pair auth stores only a path to a key file on the agent host (L-CONN-092), which the Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent cannot offer. Use the Snowflake Data Cloud connection's `authentication` = `Programmatic Access Token` with connParam `programmaticAccessToken` = the PAT (drop `privateKeyFile`/`privateKeyFilePwd`; user, account, warehouse, role and additionalparam as for key-pair) and bind the connection to the hosted runtime. On the Snowflake side an ACCOUNTADMIN attached an authentication policy that allows PATs with `PAT_POLICY = (NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION = ENFORCED_NOT_REQUIRED)` (otherwise a PAT needs a network policy on the user, and the hosted egress IPs would have to be listed) and granted MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS so the token could be minted. PATs expire (60 days here): record the expiry and rotate the connection secret before it.
evidence: Connection test 200 on the hosted runtime; mapping tasks read and wrote Snowflake there; key-pair connections of the same account kept working on Secure Agents (2026-10-16)

title: Databricks connection headless: TOOLKIT_CCI 'Databricks Delta' with a SQL-warehouse JDBC URL, PAT and a Unity Catalog volume for staging
text: POST /api/v2/connection with type `TOOLKIT_CCI`, instanceName `Databricks Delta` (shown as 'Databricks'; connectorGuid com.informatica.adapter.databricksdelta) and connParams: `sqlEndpointUrl` = `jdbc:databricks://<workspace-host>:443/default;transportMode=http;ssl=1;AuthMech=3;httpPath=/sql/1.0/warehouses/<id>;`, `AuthenticationMode` = `PAT`, the token (next lesson: in both token fields), `unityCatalog` = <catalog>, `Database` = the default schema, `jdbcDriverClassName` = `com.databricks.client.jdbc.Driver`, `clusterEnvironment` = `Volume` and `volumePath` = `/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<volume>` (the staging volume the writer uses). It tested 200 on a Secure Agent and on the Hosted Agent, and mapping tasks read tables, views and metric views (custom query) and wrote tables through it, against a serverless SQL warehouse.
evidence: Connections created and tested 200 in two orgs; read and write runs succeeded (2026-10-10, 2026-10-16)

title: Databricks connection: put the personal access token in both dbToken and PersonalAccessToken, or the test says the token expired
text: On a newly created Databricks connection (hosted runtime, current adapter), setting only `PersonalAccessToken` made the test fail with HTTP 401 'access token has expired' although the token was fresh. Setting the same PAT in both `dbToken` and `PersonalAccessToken` made the test pass and the tasks run. When rotating the token, update both fields in one full-body POST (the read masks them, L-CONN-105).
evidence: 401 'access token has expired' with one field, 200 with both, same token (2026-10-16)

title: Databricks target full reload: set writeDisposition Truncate in the writer attributes; the truncate flag, Pre SQL and create-at-runtime all append
text: A Databricks target with the mapping's truncate flag, a TRUNCATE in Pre SQL or other operation attributes still appended on every run, and a target created at run time also appends on reruns (L-CDI-166). Put `writeDisposition` = `Truncate` in the target adapter's operation and runtime attributes (generated IMF: `oprRuntimeAttributes` and `runtimeAttributes`, the same pair as the Snowflake presql fix, L-CONN-106); reruns then replaced the table. Count rows after the second run, because an appending target looks right after the first. Refines L-CDI-166.
evidence: Reruns of two tasks kept 5 and 3 rows with writeDisposition Truncate; earlier runs had appended (2026-10-10, 2026-10-16)

title: The Databricks connector sends a source custom query verbatim: a Unity Catalog metric view can be read with MEASURE() directly
text: A mapping source on the Databricks connector with a custom query such as `SELECT <dim>, CAST(MEASURE(`<measure>`) AS DOUBLE) AS <col> FROM <catalog>.<schema>.<metric_view> GROUP BY ALL` (also a UNION ALL of a total and a per-dimension query) ran unchanged: the session log line `DATABRICKSDELTA_10000 [INFO] SQL QUERY:` shows exactly the text sent, and no wrapper view, table or staging object was created in Databricks. Declare the measure as a DOUBLE/FLOAT port (cast DECIMAL measures, see the Hyper limit when the target is Tableau). Reading the metric view as a plain object (SELECT *) does not evaluate measures, so use the custom query.
evidence: Test task read 3 rows (total + 2 channels) from the metric view and published them; values matched the warehouse's own answer (2026-10-21)

title: A Data Transfer (copy-data template) task caches the source column metadata: recreate it after a source type change
text: Mapping tasks built on the Add-On Bundle copy-data template (`dsst__copy_data_new_tgt`) kept the source columns and types they were created with. After a source column changed type, the task kept writing the old type until the task was deleted and created again. Recreate (or re-fetch the fields of) such a task whenever a source changes shape, and drop a create-at-runtime target table that carries the old schema (L-CDI-166).
evidence: Type change in the source only took effect after the task was recreated (2026-10-10)

title: Tableau V3 target in a generated mapping: Overwrite, a .hyper file name, project and data source in both attribute sets, Tableau native types
text: Writer attributes, in both the operation and the runtime attribute sets: `targetOperation` = `Overwrite`, `project` = <Tableau project>, `dataSource` = <published data source name>, `extractFileName` = `<name>.hyper`, with `createTarget` true. Field nativeTypes are Tableau's (`text`, `double`, ...). The failures on the way: nativeType `string` -> "The native type system does not support the data type [string] in the native metadata field"; a file name without the extension -> "[FATAL] The name specified for the Extract file must have a .hyper extension."; `Replace` -> "Exception occurred while converting [targetOperation$] value [Replace] to [Parameter]". With an empty workbook name the writer publishes a data source; the session log (`TABLEAUV3_10000`) echoes Target Operation, File name, Project and Data source, then 'Publishing the Extract ... is successful.' Newer evidence: L-CDI-302, L-CDI-303.
evidence: Each quoted failure was a real run; the corrected task published the data source and a Hyper read-back matched (2026-10-19, 2026-10-21)

title: Tableau V3 on a Linux Secure Agent: make hyperd executable, and delete the previous .hyper in the DIS working directory before each run
text: After the Tableau V3 package is downloaded, its bundled `hyperd` (`<agent_home>/downloads/package-TableauV3*/package/tableauv3/thirdparty/informatica.tableauv3/hyper/hyperd`) arrived with mode 644, so the writer cannot start Hyper. The writer builds the extract in the DIS working directory (`<agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/<ver>/ICS/main/bin/rdtm`) and refuses to overwrite a leftover file of the same name. A mapping-task pre-processing command handles both on every run: `chmod 755 <...>/hyperd; rm -f <agent_home>/apps/Data_Integration_Server/*/ICS/main/bin/rdtm/<name>.hyper` (the globs survive package and DIS version rolls). Staging goes to /tmp.
evidence: Runs failed until the pre-command was set; with it every run published (2026-10-10, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-21 session logs)

title: Tableau Hyper rejects NUMERIC with precision above 18: cast wide decimals to DOUBLE before a Tableau V3 target
text: A Tableau V3 target fed a NUMERIC/decimal column with precision above 18 fails, because Hyper's numeric type holds at most 18 digits. Cast the column to DOUBLE in the source query or an Expression (and declare the target field `double`), or reduce the precision to 18 or less; warehouse aggregates and measures can come back as wide decimals.
evidence: A publish of a wide NUMERIC column failed; it succeeded after the DOUBLE cast (2026-10-10)

title: The Tableau V3 writer prints the Tableau REST session token in the mapping session log
text: At INFO level the Tableau V3 writer logs 'Tableau Rest Runner: User logged in.' followed by 'Session token: <token>' and the site id in clear text. Anyone who can download the session log (GET /api/v2/activity/activityLog/<id>/sessionLog, L-CDI-211) can reuse that session until it expires. Treat Tableau V3 session logs as secret-bearing: restrict who can read them, do not attach them to tickets unredacted, and prefer a dedicated Tableau user with publish rights only on the target project.
evidence: Session log of a successful publish run shows the token line (2026-10-21)

title: The agent JVM caches host-name resolution: removing an /etc/hosts override does not take effect for running connections
text: A Secure Agent reached a server through a temporary /etc/hosts line pointing at a local tunnel. After the line and the tunnel were removed, the connection test failed at once with "Connect to <host>:<port> [<host>/127.0.0.1] failed: Connection refused": the running JVM still resolved the name to the old address. A JVM started after the change hung for over 120 s instead (the real address was unreachable). Restart the agent services after changing name resolution, and read the address in the error text before debugging the server.
evidence: Same connection, two failure modes with and without the cached mapping (2026-10-19)

title: Reach a database that only listens on localhost from a Secure Agent on another host: a reverse SSH tunnel started by the database host
text: When the source database is bound to 127.0.0.1 on its own VM and the Secure Agent runs elsewhere, the database host keeps a reverse SSH tunnel (`ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:<port>:127.0.0.1:<dbport> <tunnel-user>@<agent-host>` under a systemd unit with restart) to the agent host. The tunnel user there has no shell and a key restricted with `permitlisten="127.0.0.1:<port>"`; the agent host's firewall allows SSH only from the database host. The IDMC connection uses host 127.0.0.1 and port <port>, so no database port or cloud firewall rule opens. Batch reads and a PostgreSQL CDC job ran through it; if the agent moves, repoint the tunnel and the allow-list. Refines L-CDGC-199.
evidence: 28 mapping tasks and two CDC jobs ran through the tunnel; survived an agent host move (2026-10-16, 2026-10-19)

title: Re-point an exported package to another org: connections, runtime environments (AgentGroup objects), org ids, pre-commands, checksums
text: Edit every file of the v3 export, nested DTEMPLATE zips included: replace each old connection's federatedId and v2 id with the target org's tested connection (and its name in SYS entries); map each old runtime's federatedId and v2 id to a target runtime per object (hosted or Secure Agent); replace the old org's v2 and v3 ids (profiles and CAI assets carry them); blank preProcessingCmd/postProcessingCmd values that call hosts the target cannot reach. Drop the old `SYS/<re>.AgentGroup.zip` and its exportedObjects entry and add, for EVERY target runtime that objects now reference, a `SYS/<re name>.AgentGroup.zip` (`runtimeEnvironment.json` = [{name, federatedId}] plus the original `metadata.meta`) and an exportedObjects entry (objectType AgentGroup, path /SYS, repoInfo.repoHandle = the runtime's v2 id). De-duplicate objectRefs (two old runtimes mapped onto one produce duplicates), rewrite `exportPackage.chksum` (spaces in paths escaped as '\ ', uppercase SHA-256) and string-scan the result for any old id. Import with REUSE. Refines L-CONN-024.
evidence: One project imported on the first attempt (36 created, 4 reused); a second (28 tasks, 2 CDC tasks, CAI assets) imported after the bundle-template fix; every task then ran in the target org (2026-10-16)

title: Tasks built on Add-On Bundle templates do not migrate: the export lists the template and its project but carries no file, and the import fails MigrationSvc_031
text: An export of tasks over `dsst__copy_data_new_tgt` (or another Add-On Bundle template) lists the template object and the 'Add-On Bundles' system project in exportMetadata.v2.json, but the package has no file for them, so the import fails with MigrationSvc_031; a target org may not have the bundle at all. Remove the system project entry and the template references, and rebuild those tasks as ordinary user mappings (a spec-to-IMF generator did 10 of them) before importing, or recreate them on the target org's own copy of the template. Check an export for objects that have no file before the first import attempt. Refines L-CDI-004.
evidence: Import failed MigrationSvc_031 until the 10 template-based tasks were rebuilt as user mappings; then the import succeeded (2026-10-16)

title: License-installed MDM bundle content cannot be deleted headless, even by an admin: FRS answers 403 FRS_127
text: In an org provisioned with MDM bundles, the bundle projects' content (for example the unused C360/P360/S360 objects) unpublished fine, but `DELETE` of the entities through FRS BaseEntities answered 403 FRS_127 "permission [delete] not available" for an org admin. The content is system-locked like the Add-On Bundles (L-CLEAN-016). Republish what was unpublished (state restored and verified) and leave bundle content in place; hide it from demo users with roles instead. Refines L-CLEAN-016.
evidence: Unpublish OK, delete 403 FRS_127, republish restored all 7 objects (2026-10-16)

title: Clone a connection into another org over v2: drop agentId, agentGroupId and orgId from connParams, set the target runtime, re-supply secrets
text: GET /api/v2/connection/<id> in the source org; build a body with `@type` connection, name, description, `runtimeEnvironmentId` = the target runtime's v2 id, and `type`, `instanceName`, `serviceUrl`, `username`, `timeout` copied; copy `connParams` minus `agentId`, `agentGroupId` and `orgId` (they name the source org's agent and runtime), then put back every secret (reads come masked: tokens, client secrets, refresh tokens, passwords). POST /api/v2/connection, then GET /api/v2/connection/test/<newId>. Run the clone once per connection and look the name up first, so a rerun updates instead of duplicating.
evidence: Four connections (Salesforce, SharePoint Online, Snowflake, Databricks) cloned and tested 200 in a new org (2026-10-16)

title: Renaming a v2 connection with a name-only body: 403 'There is no connector with type= TOOLKIT' (APP_10501)
text: `POST /api/v2/connection/<id>` with only the new name (or a partial body) answers 403 APP_10501 "There is no connector with type= TOOLKIT": the update is a full replacement, not a patch. Send the full GET body with the new name and every masked secret re-supplied (L-CONN-105); the id and all bindings stay the same. Refines L-CONN-105.
evidence: 403 APP_10501 on the name-only POST; four renames with the full body succeeded and tested 200 (2026-10-16)

title: Connection names refuse parentheses: APP_10500; letters, digits, spaces and _ . + - , are accepted
text: Creating a CDI connection named like '<system> (catalog)' failed with APP_10500; the allowed characters are letters, digits, spaces and `_ . + - ,`. Use a suffix such as '<system> - catalog'. Other object types have their own lists (FRS renames refuse '()' with FRS_082, L-MIG-080; v3 projects refuse '/' and others, L-MIG-078), so normalise names to letters, digits, spaces and hyphens across connections, projects and assets.
evidence: APP_10500 on create; the hyphenated name created and tested 200 (2026-10-16)

title: SharePoint Online connection: Attachment_File_Path is mandatory even to test, and a hosted runtime cannot move files with it
text: A SharePoint Online connection cannot be saved without `Attachment_File_Path`; on the Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent `/tmp` was accepted and the test passed. But the connector stages file bytes in that folder on the agent (reads download every file there, writes read the bytes from it, L-CONN-102, L-CONN-107), and nothing can place or collect files on the hosted runtime, so a document-library file write failed there. Run SharePoint file transfers on a Secure Agent with its own attachment folder, or move the file over Microsoft Graph from a CAI process (next lesson). The CDI connection URL is the site URL; the catalog connection uses the tenant root plus Subsite_URL (L-CDGC-162).
evidence: Test 200 on the hosted runtime with /tmp; the file-write task failed there and ran on a Secure Agent / CAI (2026-10-16, 2026-10-17)

title: A SharePoint Online read that fails with 'Operation failed: Documents is not found..' has a Graph-scoped refresh token
text: A mapping reading the document library 'Documents' failed with "Operation failed: Documents is not found..", and the object list of the same connection was empty. The stored refresh token had last been redeemed with Microsoft Graph scopes, so the connector got a Graph-audience token for SharePoint REST (L-CONN-100). Redeem the refresh token once with scope `https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/Sites.ReadWrite.All offline_access` (or `.default`), store the new refresh token in the connection (full-body update), and rerun. If another client (for example a process that calls Graph with the same app) redeems the same refresh token, give each audience its own refresh token. Refines L-CONN-100.
evidence: Two failed runs with the quoted error; after the SharePoint-scoped refresh the task read 7 rows (2026-10-16)

title: Upload a file to SharePoint with no agent: a CAI process calls Microsoft Graph JSON batching with the base64 content as the body
text: On the CAI Cloud Server (no Secure Agent, no disk), a service connector action gets a delegated Graph token with the refresh-token grant, then POSTs `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/$batch` with one request: method PUT to the drive item's `:/content` path (`/drives/<driveId>/root:/<folder>/<file>:/content`), a Content-Type header for the file, and `body` = the file's base64 text: Graph decodes base64 bodies inside a JSON batch, so the binary never passes through the process as bytes. The base64 can come straight from a warehouse column or a Salesforce ContentVersion. The uploaded PDF was byte-identical (SHA-256) to the source; a loop over 'next untransferred row' plus a log row made it incremental.
evidence: Probe and 14 later transfers byte-identical by SHA-256 (2026-10-16)

title: A JSON REST response comes into a CAI process as XML, without its key order
text: A service connector action calling a JSON API returns `entireResponse` as XML (`<data><_1>...</_1></data>` for arrays), not JSON, so read it with XQuery/XPath. The JSON-to-XML conversion does not keep the key order, so a positional read picks the wrong element: for an IDMC activity-log response, strip the nested `<entries>...</entries>` block before reading the top-level runId, state and endTime, or select them by name.
evidence: Activity-log polling in a process read a child entry's state until the nested block was stripped (2026-10-16)

title: A CAI Jump must sit in a top-level Decision and point at a sibling step; a deeply nested jump fails publish with 'Plan .pdd is invalid'
text: A polling loop authored as a Jump inside nested containers failed to publish with 'Plan .pdd is invalid'. Moving the Jump into a Decision at the top level of the flow, targeting a step at the same level (for example the Wait before the poll), published and looped. Assignment targets are written `temp.<field>` / `output.<field>` (no $), while expressions read `$temp.<field>` and `$input.<field>`.
evidence: Publish error with the nested jump; the flattened loop published and polled up to 60 times (2026-10-16)

title: A from-scratch CAI import gets new runtime asset ids: look the id up by path before asset/v1/update
text: Importing hand-built CAI assets into an org where they do not exist yet creates them under ids the org mints, not under the package GUIDs, so an `asset/v1/update` (secrets, access, Run On) aimed at the package GUID misses. After the import, read the asset id by its path (asset status / FRS by name and folder) and use that; to change only a process later, re-import just the process XML (includeObjects limited to it, L-CAI-136) so the connection's secrets are not overwritten.
evidence: asset/v1/update needed the id looked up by path after the first import; process-only re-imports kept the connection secrets (2026-10-16)

title: Orchestrate CDI taskflows from a CAI process with no agent: IDMC login, v2 job, then poll the activity log, behind a Milestone
text: A process on the Cloud Server can run Data Integration work through the IDMC REST API in a service connector: an IDMC login (user and password held as connection secrets), `POST /api/v2/job` {taskId, taskType WORKFLOW or MTT}, then poll `GET /api/v2/activity/activityLog?taskId=<id>&runId=<runId>` every 15-20 s with a Wait + Jump loop. A synchronous REST invoke of the process times out at about 90 s, so reply first with a Milestone ('STARTED run N' in about 2 s) and let the process continue. Use a dedicated integration user: a password change of that user makes the process fault in about 1 s and can lock the account (L-AUTH-092).
evidence: Run button: 6/6 taskflow steps + 2 follow-up tasks green in 186-282 s, milestone reply in 2 s (2026-10-16)

title: Poll a linear taskflow run with taskId AND runId: child entries carry their own runIds
text: The activity log lists finished runs only, and a linear taskflow's row holds its tasks in `entries[]` (L-CDI-061), each with its own `runId`. Matching 'runId == my run' anywhere in the response therefore matched a child task's entry and reported the taskflow finished early. Query `GET /api/v2/activity/activityLog?taskId=<workflowId>&runId=<runId>`: it returns an empty array until that taskflow run ends, then exactly one row, whose top-level state and endTimeUtc are the taskflow's. Refines L-CDI-059.
evidence: Premature 'finished' with the loose match; the runId-filtered poll ended exactly when the run did (2026-10-16)

title: Starting a linear taskflow that is already running answers REPO_17315
text: `POST /api/v2/job` for a taskflow (taskType WORKFLOW) while an instance of it is still running is refused with REPO_17315 (another instance of the taskflow is running). Callers that can be pressed twice (a button, a scheduler retry) should treat REPO_17315 as 'already running' and attach to the running instance (latest activity-monitor entry) instead of retrying. Newer evidence: L-CDI-304.
evidence: REPO_17315 on a second start while the first run was active (2026-10-16)

title: Activity-log and v2 local times are UTC-4 on a US west pod too: the offset is not the pod's zone, so always read the *Utc fields
text: On a us-west pod (usw1) the activity-log `startTime`/`endTime` still read 4 hours behind `startTimeUtc`/`endTimeUtc` with a 'Z' suffix, the same offset as on an east pod, so the offset is not pod-local time (and not Pacific time either, as an earlier note assumed). Never derive the offset from the pod: use `startTimeUtc`/`endTimeUtc` for completion and durations, and re-check schedules' startTime against startTimeUTC after any daylight-saving change. Refines L-AUTH-014.
evidence: Activity-log rows read 2026-10-18/19 on a usw1 org: endTime - endTimeUtc = -4 h on every row

title: A profile PUT ignores omitted fields and rules: mark them isDeleted=true to remove them
text: To drop rule bindings and columns from a Data Profiling profile, sending a PUT body without them changes nothing: the omitted `profileableFields`, rules and their field mappings stay. Send them with `isDeleted: true` (the rule entry and its mappings) and read the profile back; readers of profile results must then skip entries flagged isDeleted. Keep the GET body as the undo.
evidence: 14 rule checks reduced to 7 only after isDeleted was set; the plain PUT had left all 14 (2026-10-16)

title: A new org's catalog tenant is provisioned by the first interactive open of Data Governance and Catalog; until then cdgc-api answers 0-byte 200s
text: In a new org with CDGC licensed, `cdgc-api.<domain>` and `idmc-api.<domain>` answered 0-byte 200 for real and bogus paths alike (gateway prefix routing, L-AUTH-006), and a headless browser open of the catalog hung on 'Loading...'. Right after a user opened Data Governance and Catalog once in a normal browser, `GET ccgf-catalog-source-management/api/v1/datasources` returned real JSON (totalElements 0) and a bogus path a 404 problem+json. Make that one interactive open part of org setup before any catalog automation; a new tenant may also lack the built-in classifications (L-CDGC-204). Refines L-CDGC-204.
evidence: 0-byte 200s before, real JSON and 404s minutes after the first browser open (2026-10-16)

title: Curated lineage edges to SharePoint folder or file assets are refused (CONTENT_FAILED): get the hop from a scanned mapping instead
text: A contentv2 publish of a curated data-flow edge from a warehouse table to a cataloged SharePoint Folder or PDF File asset returned CONTENT_FAILED in every variant tried (DataSetDataFlow and DirectionalDataFlow, EXTERNAL and INTERNAL ids), while a table-to-table edge with the same call returned 201. To show a SharePoint hop that a non-scanned process makes (for example a CAI transfer), add a small CDI mapping that reads the SharePoint library into a table, scan the IICS source, and MERGE the mapping's SharePoint connection reference onto the Site (L-CDGC-167): the scanner then draws SharePoint -> mapping -> table.
evidence: Every SharePoint-endpoint edge CONTENT_FAILED; the confirm-mapping route drew the hop after rescans (2026-10-16, 2026-10-17)

title: Catalog rule occurrences: Target and Threshold must be numbers, and RuleType must be a platform dimension (no 'Conformity')
text: In the contentv2 RuleInstance publish (L-CDGC-161), `Target` and `Threshold` sent as strings were refused; JSON numbers published. `RuleType` must be one of the dimensions the profiling service lists at /ruleOccurrence/ruleType: Accuracy, Validity, Completeness, Consistency, Uniqueness, Timeliness. 'Conformity' (a common DQ term) gives CONTENT_FAILED; map format checks to Validity. Keep the rule specification's own dimension consistent, or dashboards will show two names for one check. Refines L-CDGC-161.
evidence: CONTENT_FAILED with 'Conformity'; the occurrences of two sources published with numeric Target/Threshold and Validity (2026-10-17)

title: The catalog Data Quality scope needs Maximum Precision of String Fields as well; the Data Profiling scope also needs a Profiling Run Scope
text: A catalog-source PUT that enables Data Quality was refused until the `Data Quality Scope` group in typeCapabilities carried Sampling Type, Runtime Environment, Maximum Precision of String Fields and Text Qualifier (L-CDGC-143 lists three of them); the Data Profiling scope additionally needs Profiling Run Scope. Copy the full groups from a source of the same type that already scores, change only the runtime id, and read the source back by capabilityName (L-CDGC-212). Refines L-CDGC-143.
evidence: PUT validator refusals until all fields were present; DQ capability then COMPLETED on two sources (2026-10-17)

title: A catalog source cloned from another org keeps the old org's runtime inside its Data Profiling scope: catalog profiling then fails silently
text: A source cloned across orgs had its connection and its Runtime Settings runtime remapped (L-CDGC-015), but the `Data Profiling Scope` group in typeCapabilities still named the source org's runtime environment. Its catalog Data Profiling capability then failed with no message and no DTM session, alone or in a combined scan, while classic Data Profiling of the same tables worked. Remap the runtime in every Scope group too, and string-scan the whole body (capabilities and typeCapabilities) for old-org ids before the PUT. Refines L-CDGC-015.
evidence: Silent failures until the scope runtime was corrected; the next Data Quality/Profiling run COMPLETED 14/14 (2026-10-17)

title: Databricks over JDBC V2: a Java 8 driver (2.6.x), catalog and schema in the URL, five connParams, and a test that stays red
text: The JDBC V2 connector runs on Java 8, so it needs databricks-jdbc 2.6.x in `<agent_home>/ext/connectors/thirdparty/informatica.jdbc_v2/common` (3.x fails with a 'class version 55' error there; the catalog's metadata services take 3.x in their own driver folders). URL `jdbc:databricks://<host>:443/default;transportMode=http;ssl=1;AuthMech=3;httpPath=<path>;IgnoreTransactions=1;ConnCatalog=<catalog>;ConnSchema=<schema>`, user `token`, password = PAT. connParams `subtype` Others, `quoteChar` backtick, `schemaname`, `autocommit` true, `supportmixedcaseidentifier` false; a missing one surfaces as an NPE shown as 'null'. The connection Test stays red because the driver rejects setTransactionIsolation(READ_COMMITTED) and setAutoCommit(false), yet catalog scans through it complete; a thin wrapper driver that turns those two calls into no-ops makes the Test green and lets catalog Data Quality run. For cataloging, prefer the native Databricks source (L-CDGC-206).
evidence: Scanner test COMPLETED with the red connection test; with the wrapper the test went green and catalog DQ scored 100% (2026-10-17)

title: A JDBC catalog source over Databricks Unity Catalog: filter <schema>.*, and ConnCatalog in the URL, or it finds nothing
text: On a JDBC catalog source bound to a Databricks JDBC V2 connection, a three-part filter `<catalog>.<schema>.*` matched nothing, and without `ConnCatalog=<catalog>` in the URL the scanner treated the Unity Catalog catalog as a schema. With ConnCatalog (and ConnSchema) in the URL and the filter `<schema>.*`, the scan cataloged database <catalog> / schema <schema> with its tables, views and columns. Under load, uploads to the metadata staging service can time out once: retry the scan before changing it.
evidence: Empty scans with the 3-part filter; complete scan (2 tables, 3 views, columns) with the 2-part filter (2026-10-17)

title: A Salesforce catalog scan by an API-only integration user ends PARTIAL_COMPLETED: the Tooling API refuses CustomObject, CustomField, ApexTrigger
text: Every Salesforce scan through a connection whose user has an API-only minimum-access profile ended PARTIAL_COMPLETED with all objects flagged, because the Tooling API answered INVALID_TYPE "sObject type 'CustomObject' / 'CustomField' / 'ApexTrigger' is not supported" for that user. Objects and fields were still ingested and lineage worked. Either give the scan user metadata-read permissions so the Tooling API objects are visible (not verified), or accept PARTIAL as benign after checking that ingestion COMPLETED. Refines L-CDGC-142.
evidence: Same PARTIAL on every Salesforce scan from two agent hosts; Test Connection and ingestion COMPLETED (2026-10-16 to 2026-10-19)

title: Catalog DQ scores roll up column -> table -> schema, not along lineage: a BI dashboard's Data Quality tab stays empty
text: After rule occurrences scored on warehouse columns, the tables and schemas showed the scores, but the Tableau dashboard and data source assets downstream in the lineage had an empty Data Quality tab. Scores propagate up the containment hierarchy, not along data flow. To show quality next to a report, put the score in the report's own data (a scorecard table) or point users to the upstream table's tab.
evidence: Two demos: column and table scores visible, dashboard DQ tab empty (2026-10-17)

title: A CDC job left 'failed, Not retriable' by a source database outage resumes from its restart point with job/resume
text: When the PostgreSQL source crashed (a full disk put it in a PANIC loop), the PowerExchange reader hit a fatal error and two Database Ingestion CDC jobs went to failed with 'Not retriable'. After the database was healthy again, `POST /dbmi/public/api/v2/job/resume` {"jobId": <id>} restarted each job from its stored position; about 1 GB of slot lag drained in minutes with no re-baseline. A watchdog that decides 'transient or not' from task logs must read them on the host of the agent that runs the job (`<agent_home>/apps/Database_Ingestion/logs/tasks`, L-DBMI-030): after moving the runtime, a watchdog still reading the old host saw empty failure text and never resumed. Refines L-DBMI-056.
evidence: Both jobs resumed after about 26 h down; slot lag drained; watchdog path found stale (2026-10-26)

title: A Secure Agent auto-upgrade wrote a 1.1 GB package that filled a shared disk and crashed the database next to it
text: A Secure Agent that only ran a leftover job in an old org still received an automatic upgrade, which wrote a ~1.1 GB `infa_rpm.tar` under its install directory on a data disk that also held a PostgreSQL data directory. The disk filled, PostgreSQL went into a PANIC loop on 'No space left on device', and a CDC job on another agent that read that database failed. Keep an agent's home on its own filesystem or with several GB free, alert on disk usage there, and unregister agents you no longer need: they keep upgrading.
evidence: Disk full traced to the upgrade package; database and CDC recovered after space was freed (2026-10-25, 2026-10-26)

title: Why one OOM kill stops every agent engine: a systemd unit with Restart=no and the default OOMPolicy=stop
text: On the agent host whose whole unit went 'failed' after one JVM was OOM-killed (L-AGENT-101), `systemctl show infaagent` read `Restart=no` and `OOMPolicy=stop` (the systemd default): systemd stops the entire unit when any process in it is OOM-killed and then does not restart it. When you write the unit, add a drop-in with `OOMPolicy=continue` (so the agent core can respawn the killed JVM without taking down the other engines and CDC) plus `Restart=on-failure` and `RestartSec=30` as a backstop, then `systemctl daemon-reload` (no restart needed). The drop-in itself has not been exercised by a real OOM yet. Refines L-AGENT-101.
evidence: Unit settings read back on the host after the 2026-10-19 OOM incident; independent review of the fix (2026-10-19)

title: Size a Linux Secure Agent that runs DI, Data Quality, CDC, the CAI process engine and catalog scans at 16 GB, not 8 GB
text: One Linux agent carrying Data Integration (including Structure Parser jobs with a 3 GB DTM heap), the Data Quality service, Database Ingestion CDC, the CAI process engine (about 1.8 GB resident) and the metadata/catalog services used 6.5 of 7.9 GB and was OOM-killed on an 8 GB host; on a 16 GB host the same workload used about 10 GB with 0 OOM. With 2 vCPU, catalog scans saturate the CPU: run scans one at a time and outside timed demos (L-CDGC-045). Moving the agent to the bigger host was an install-directory copy (L-AGENT-102). Refines L-AGENT-053. Newer evidence: L-AGENT-123.
evidence: OOM on the 8 GB host; 10/10 engines RUNNING with ~7 GB free on the 16 GB host (2026-10-19)

title: Each IDMC user carries its own lockout threshold (maxLoginAttempts): read it before pointing automation at a user
text: `GET /public/core/v3/users` returns `maxLoginAttempts` per user, as a string, and it differs inside one org: a newly created admin user had '3' while another admin had '10' and the CAI anonymous user '3'. With 3, one stale stored password in a */5 job locks the user within minutes (IDS_086, L-AUTH-092). Check the value of any user that unattended jobs will use, raise it where policy allows, and keep people's interactive users out of automation.
evidence: Users read-back in a new org (2026-10-19)

title: Salesforce field precisions in a generated mapping: date is 10, datetime is 24; take them from the IDMC field metadata
text: When a mapping is generated without the designer, a Salesforce `date` field must be declared with precision 10 (scale 0) and a `datetime` field with precision 24 (L-CDI-245); the generic date/time default of 29 that other connectors use was not accepted for Salesforce date fields. Read each field's precision and scale from the connection's own field metadata (the values the designer would import) instead of a type-wide default, and keep the Salesforce nativeType (date, datetime, currency, picklist). Refines L-CDI-245.
evidence: Rebuilt Salesforce-sourced tasks validated and ran after switching date fields to precision 10 (2026-10-16)

title: PostgreSQL fields in a generated mapping take the connector's type names: bigint, not the int8 alias
text: Generated PostgreSQL source, lookup and target fields need the native type names the IDMC PostgreSQL connector reports: `bigint` for a 64-bit integer column, not PostgreSQL's catalog alias `int8` (likewise the connector's own spellings such as `character_varying` and `timestamp_with_time_zone`). `int8` was not accepted for those fields; `bigint` ran. Copy native types from a designer-built mapping or the connector's field metadata, never from information_schema/pg_catalog short names.
evidence: Rebuilt PostgreSQL-reading tasks ran after int8 -> bigint (2026-10-16)

title: A mapplet package's documentType is exactly 'DMAPPLET': 'MAPPLET' is rejected, and the import assigns a new id
text: A synthesized mapplet is a `<name>.DMAPPLET.zip` holding `mappletTemplate.json`, with `documentType` "DMAPPLET" (case-sensitive); "MAPPLET" is rejected by IDMC. A REUSE import assigns the mapplet a new id, so look it up by name in its folder after the import and use that id in the calling mapping's mapplet transformation and in its package `assets` entry (type DMAPPLET, path /Explore/<project>/<folder>); an OVERWRITE re-import keeps the FRS GUID.
evidence: Generator deploys proven live (mapplet imported, resolved by name, called by a mapping that ran) (2026-10-04)

title: A SharePoint Online connection is created with type TOOLKIT, not TOOLKIT_CCI: TOOLKIT_CCI fails in the cloud with 'argument "content" is null'
text: The general rule creates connections with type TOOLKIT_CCI and the connector name in instanceName (L-CONN-001), but a v2 `POST /api/v2/connection` for the 'Sharepoint Online' connector with type TOOLKIT_CCI failed in the cloud with `argument "content" is null` and never reached the agent. The same body with type `TOOLKIT` created the connection, and its test reached SharePoint: the test passed with a valid delegated refresh token and failed with a deliberately wrong one, so the test is real. The connection fields are Client_Id, Client_Secret, Refresh_Token, Redirect_URL, URL (the site URL), Subsite_URL and Attachment_File_Path (L-CONN-125); the refresh token must be minted for SharePoint, not Microsoft Graph (L-CONN-100).
evidence: TOOLKIT_CCI create failed with the null-content error; TOOLKIT create succeeded, test passed, and a negative test with a bogus token failed (2026-10-06)

title: Cancel a running or stuck catalog job: POST ccgf-orchestration-management-api-server jobs/<jobId>/operations/cancel
text: The Cancel Job button on Metadata Command Center > Monitor > <job> sends `POST https://cdgc-api.<domain>.informaticacloud.com/ccgf-orchestration-management-api-server/api/v1/jobs/<jobId>/operations/cancel` (200). The job shows CANCEL REQUESTED at once and CANCELLED about two minutes later, which releases the source lock, so the next scan run is accepted instead of 406 'Job is in progress'. Get the job id from `GET .../data360/observable/api/v1/jobs?limit=N` (L-CDGC-037): the stuck one is the source's sync job still RUNNING. A catalog job can sit in a RUNNING task (for example Test Connection) long after its client gave up; cancel it before re-running. The call was captured from the console; a direct script replay with the identity headers is not yet recorded. Newer evidence: L-CDGC-225.
evidence: a Tableau source sync stuck 74 min in Test Connection: Cancel Job -> captured POST .../jobs/<id>/operations/cancel 200 -> CANCELLED in ~2 min; the next connection test passed (2026-10-26)

title: An unconnected lookup called with a NULL argument can return the value of a NULL-key row
text: `:LKP.<lookup>(<key>)` with `<key>` NULL returned the value stored on a row whose key column is NULL, so every record without a key got that one value. Guard the call (`IIF(ISNULL(<key>), NULL, :LKP.<lookup>(<key>))`), add `WHERE <key> IS NOT NULL` to the lookup query, and give records that have no natural key a stable stand-in key (for example `'NOID-' || MD5(<email>)`) so they can still be looked up on the next run.
evidence: 44 records with no source key all received one previous value from a cached query lookup (Use First Value) whose key column held NULLs; the next run gave 44 golden records the same identifier (2026-10-28)

title: A previous-row comparison after a Sorter did not mark repeats on the runtime: decide ties set-wise with a ranking lookup
text: Do not rely on comparing a row with the previous row to break ties between groups. Compute the winner per contested value in the warehouse instead: a query lookup `SELECT K, W FROM (SELECT K, GROUP_KEY AS W, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY K ORDER BY <size> DESC, GROUP_KEY) AS RN, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY K) AS C FROM (...)) WHERE RN = 1 AND C > 1`, then `IIF(NOT ISNULL(:LKP.<winner>(K)) AND :LKP.<winner>(K) <> GROUP_KEY, <new value>, K)`. Only contested keys are cached, so the lookup stays small. A running counter variable is still fine for numbering.
evidence: Sorter on the claimed value, then an Expression with v_taken = (value = v_last) followed by v_last = value: 43 groups claiming one value all kept it, while a running counter (v_seq = v_seq + v_new) in the same Expression incremented correctly; a query lookup ranking with ROW_NUMBER fixed it (2026-10-29)

title: In a multi-flow mapping (flowOrder), an earlier flow saw a table empty that a later flow of the same mapping rewrites
text: Targets of a mapping are emptied when the mapping starts, not when their flow runs, so a source or lookup in an EARLIER flow that reads a table a LATER flow truncates finds it empty. Flows may read what earlier flows wrote (that worked: a hierarchy flow read the golden table the flow before it wrote). When consolidating dependent steps, read 'last run' state from a table the mapping only appends to (a merge log: latest event per source key), or keep the steps in separate mappings. Check by fingerprinting every output table before and after the consolidated run; BigQuery time travel (copy `<table>@<epoch-ms>` over the table) restores a bad run.
evidence: A consolidated match + merge mapping whose match flow looked up the previous identifiers in the cross-reference table that the merge flow writes with truncate gave all 167,440 records new identifiers; with the previous identifiers read from the append-only merge log instead, 167,430 of 167,440 kept theirs and the rest were logged rule changes (2026-10-29)

title: A large aggregation that runs on the Hosted Agent can fail on a small Secure Agent: keep the step that needs the Secure Agent in its own mapping
text: A mapping runs on one runtime. When one flow needs the Secure Agent (cleanse or deduplicate need its Data Quality engine) and another does heavy aggregation, putting them in one mapping moves the aggregation onto the Secure Agent's memory. Keep the Data Quality-engine step in its own small mapping and leave memory-heavy flows on the Hosted Agent.
evidence: Merging an aggregation over about 720,000 groups with a deduplicate step forced the mapping onto a small Secure Agent; it failed with TE_7041 'Aggregate Error: Failed to allocate'; split back, the aggregation ran on the Hosted Agent (2026-10-29)

title: BigQuery SQL in a lookup query: a CTE named like the returned column returns the whole row
text: BigQuery names are case-insensitive, so a CTE `r` and a column `R` collide and `R` resolves to the whole row of `r`. Give CTEs names that are never column names (`res`, `cand`), and run every lookup query once in BigQuery before deploying the mapping.
evidence: A lookup query ending in `SELECT KEY, R FROM r` (CTE r, column R) returned a STRUCT per row instead of the text (2026-10-29)

title: IICS lineage to BigQuery: MERGE the connection reference onto the BigQuery source's Database root (the project)
text: Find the IICS source's reference `<iicsSourceId>_<CONN>://<CONN>~core.DataSource` (class core.DataSource, core.reference true), then `POST .../ccgf-contentv2/api/v1/assignment/connectionAssignment?operationType=MERGE` with targetRootAsset `{"externalId": "<bqSourceId>://<gcpProject>~com.infa.odin.models.relational.Database", "origin": "<bqSourceId>", "isCaseSensitive": false, "location": "<bqSourceId>://<bqSourceId>/<gcpProject>"}`: the BigQuery project is the Database root. The job took about 4 minutes; prove it with a lineage walk.
evidence: Lineage Discovery COMPLETED with no ConnectionAssignmentRecommendation and the connection reference unresolved; after one MERGE the upstream walk from a gold table went from 0 to 52 edges, file -> raw -> mapping tasks -> silver -> gold, without a rescan (2026-10-28)

title: A hyphenated systemd slice name nests the agent under another slice and inherits its memory cap
text: systemd reads a hyphen in a slice name as hierarchy: `<name>-<suffix>.slice` is a child of `<name>.slice`. A Secure Agent put in such a slice inherited the parent's MemoryMax=4G and CPUQuota=100%, while the child's own caps applied to a cgroup that was never created. Pressed against 4 GB, the agent's page cache was evicted again and again; its JVMs re-read their files from disk until the database host's persistent disk ran out of IOPS (load above 100, IO pressure 98%, CPU idle). Name agent slices without a hyphen (or deliberately nest them) and verify the caps on the real cgroup: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/<slice>/memory.max io.max cpu.max`. An idle agent needs about 3-4 GB; give it headroom above that. Newer evidence: L-AGENT-119.
evidence: Agent on a shared database VM: load 125 with the agent's JVMs as the only significant disk readers; after moving it to a top-level slice with MemoryHigh 10G, io.max present and refaults flat, a full 100M-row DQ run kept load under 12

title: Reinstalling an agent on the same host into the same runtime environment reuses the existing agent id
text: `consoleAgentManager.sh configureTokenWithRuntime <user> <token> <runtimeEnvironment>` from a fresh install directory on the same host registered as the existing (stopped) agent id in that runtime environment: the registration matched the host name. Connections bound to the runtime environment needed no edit and tested green on the new install. Move the old install directory aside afterwards so nothing can start two installs with one id. A separate `DELETE /api/v2/agent/<id>` is refused with 403 REPO_38225 while the agent is the only member of a runtime environment that connections or tasks use, and `POST /api/v2/agent/<id>` (rename) returns 405. Newer evidence: L-AGENT-120.
evidence: Fresh install, same host name, same runtime environment: agent id unchanged, all engines RUNNING in about 5 minutes, two JDBC V2 connections tested green without edits

title: Run CDQ rule specifications on ClickHouse through a JDBC V2 mapping, and prove them against SQL
text: Profiling ClickHouse stays blocked (L-CONN-089), but a mapping works: a custom-query source on a JDBC V2 ClickHouse connection (strings cast with `toFixedString(substring(x,1,N),N)`, unsigned ints with `toInt64`, dates as ISO strings; L-CDI-172), rule specification transformations chained with an Expression that renames each `Output`, an Aggregator per group and a JDBC V2 target on a second connection whose URL names the results database (L-CDI-040). The padding is stripped before the rules see the value: an independent SQL computation of the same checks on the same 1M-row sample matched in 866 of 867 group x check cells. Use a deterministic hash filter for the sample so both sides read the same rows.
evidence: 1,009,410-row sample in 90 s on a 2-CPU capped agent; full 100M-row run on the same mapping; the one mismatch was a rule definition (next lesson)

title: A CLAIRE-generated US state-code rule rejects DC
text: A rule specification CLAIRE generated for 'valid two-letter US state abbreviation' returned Invalid for every District of Columbia row (state 'DC'), while a SQL check with the 50 states plus DC passed them. Read a generated rule's allowed list before using it on national data, or extend it to DC (and territories if they occur).
evidence: 2,121 DC rows failed the rule, 0 failed the SQL check; every other state matched

title: REST profile create on a JDBC V2 ClickHouse source: NSTRING is refused and 'string' passes but the create hangs
text: Cloning a PostgreSQL profile body onto a JDBC V2 ClickHouse connection with hand-built fields (the untested idea in L-CONN-089): `pcType` NSTRING fails at once with 400 PROFILE_MDL_00006 ('PowerCenter data type NSTRING ... is not supported'); with `string` the validator accepts the body but `POST /profiling-service/api/v1/profile` never answers within 300 s, no profile is created, and nothing reaches the agent's logs. Direct profiling of ClickHouse remains blocked; profile a PostgreSQL copy or use the mapping route (L-DQ-117). Newer evidence: L-DQ-128.
evidence: Five create attempts (NSTRING, string, STRING, varchar, VARCHAR) against a running agent whose JDBC V2 connections tested green [disputed 2026-11-03 by L-DQ-128: profiling a JDBC V2 ClickHouse source ran to completion headless by cloning a working profile body]

title: JDBC V2 writer: rows per INSERT = min(writer batch size, rows per DTM block); wide ports and the 200-row default make a ClickHouse write storm
text: A JDBC V2 target sends one INSERT per writer batch, and a batch never spans DTM buffer blocks. With the writer batch size left at 0 the writer uses 200 rows; with a large batch size the block caps it: rows per block = `Default buffer block size` / declared row width (string precision x 2 bytes). A mapping that carried a 128K-character JSON port wrote 60-82 rows per INSERT (about 52 inserts per second, about 150 rows per second per task, a new ClickHouse part per insert). Fix: keep ports narrow (no raw payload through the DTM unless needed), set the task session properties `DTM buffer size` (1-2 GB) and `Default buffer block size` (32-64 MB) on the v2 task (`sessionProperties`), and set the target's `writeOptions.batchSize` (10,000-20,000). Rows per INSERT went 200 -> 2,108 (wide golden rows) and about 10,000 (narrow cross-reference rows). Raise the DTM Java heap at the same time (next lesson).
evidence: query_log written_rows per INSERT measured before/after on the same target: 60-82, 200, 2,108, ~9,957 (2026-11-01)

title: JDBC V2 with big DTM blocks or batches needs a bigger DTM Java heap; the reader OOM leaves the session hung
text: With `JVMOption1` blank in `pmrdtm.cfg` the DTM's embedded JVM keeps a small default heap. After raising the block size to 64 MB, the JDBC V2 reader thread died with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded` 20 s into the run and the session then hung with 0 rows and no failure (stop it over the API); a writer with a 10,000-row batch failed `Java heap space` inside `IInputBuffer.getTimestamp`. `JVMOption1=-Xmx4096m` in the running DIS version's `pmrdtm.cfg` fixed both for the next DTM without a restart; set it cloud-side as well (L-AGENT-056, L-AGENT-088) or a version roll drops it.
