Set both values in JAVA_ARGS (for example `-Xms128M -Xmx384M`), recreate the container and wait for the broker's started log line before creating queues.
evidence: container 'Restarting (1)' 25 s after start; logs showed -Xms512M -Xmx384M; fixed to -Xms128M -Xmx384M, broker started, 3 ANYCAST queues created (2026-10-08)

title: Grant a service account access to one BigQuery dataset through the dataset access list: `bq add-iam-policy-binding` on a dataset failed
text: For a least-privilege IDMC writer and a read-only BI reader, `bq add-iam-policy-binding --member=serviceAccount:<sa> --role=roles/bigquery.dataEditor <project>:<dataset>` failed for every dataset with the installed CLI. The access-list route works: `bq show --format=prettyjson <project>:<dataset> > ds.json`, append `{"role":"WRITER","userByEmail":"<sa>"}` (or READER) to `access` only if it is missing, then `bq update --source=ds.json <project>:<dataset>` and read the list back. The writer also needs project-level roles/bigquery.jobUser and roles/storage.objectAdmin on the staging bucket (L-CONN-034). Refines L-CONN-034.
evidence: 6 of 6 dataset bindings FAILED with add-iam-policy-binding; 3 of 3 datasets 'successfully updated' through the access list, WRITER/READER entries read back (2026-10-08)

title: A GCP project id is permanent and shows inside IDMC: pick a neutral warehouse project before building a customer-facing demo, because moving later needs a billing admin
text: The warehouse project id appears in the IDMC BigQuery connection, in CDGC asset paths and lineage, and in service-account e-mails, and GCP project ids cannot be renamed. Relabeling dashboards does not reach those places. Moving to a new neutral project means recreating datasets, connections and CDC targets and rescanning the catalog (about 1-2 h), and creating the project is not enough: an org admin could create it, but linking billing needs a billing-account admin, so the new project stayed empty and the move was dropped. Decide the project id, and get billing linked, before the first connection is made.
evidence: new project created but the billing link was refused without billing-account admin rights; move abandoned, demo stayed in the original project with relabeled BI only (2026-10-08)

title: Park demo pipelines that spend warehouse credits without deleting anything: point their shared IDMC connection at a warehouse that does not exist
text: To guarantee that old pipelines, their schedules, external watchers and catalog scans cannot spend credits, after unbinding schedules and stopping triggers, change the warehouse attribute of the IDMC connection they share to a name that does not exist (re-supply the secret on the update, L-CONN-007) and log the old value as the undo. Any job or catalog scan on that connection then fails at connect time before a warehouse resumes. Combine with a resource monitor (L-ENV-096) and check afterwards with SHOW WAREHOUSES that every warehouse is SUSPENDED. Keep the live demo on its own connection so it is unaffected. Refines L-ENV-096.
evidence: Four older demos parked this way, each change with an undo line; all three warehouses read SUSPENDED afterwards and only manual runs spent credits (2026-10-13)

title: A Snowflake resource monitor guards only its warehouses: a system warehouse granted to PUBLIC lets the IDMC service user spend outside the guard
text: The quota guard was attached to the demo warehouse only. Snowflake trial accounts also have system warehouses such as `SYSTEM$STREAMLIT_NOTEBOOK_WH`, granted to PUBLIC, so the IDMC service user could use it (PUBLIC is always among a user's roles, and default secondary roles widen this) and spend credits the monitor never sees. List what the service user can use (`SHOW WAREHOUSES` as that user), then close the gap as ACCOUNTADMIN: `REVOKE USAGE ON WAREHOUSE <wh> FROM ROLE PUBLIC` (may be refused for a system warehouse) or `ALTER USER <service user> SET DEFAULT_SECONDARY_ROLES = ()`, or attach the monitor at account level. Refines L-ENV-096.
evidence: SHOW WAREHOUSES as the service user listed 3 warehouses, one outside the monitor (2026-10-13)

title: As of October 2026 there is no public mapping-creation MCP or mapping-design API: package export/import is still the only headless way to author CDI mappings
text: A public-web search on 2026-10-02 found no GA or preview record of a vendor MCP server or REST API that authors CDI mappings. The docs list 20 shared MCP servers and none creates mappings; the Troubleshooting MCP reads mapping details but cannot write them; CLAIRE mapping generation exists only in the designer Copilot and the CLAIRE GPT Data Integration agent ('Open in Data Integration'). The only dated roadmap line is 'Agentic Integration - Q4 2026' (vendor press release, May 2026), plus a 'Data Integration Agent' described with no availability or MCP mention (Sept 2026 blog). When a vendor contact says a mapping MCP 'will be preferred', keep building with synthesized packages and `POST /public/core/v3/import` (or the asset-promotion MCP) and re-check the MCP registry each release. Refines L-MCP-003.
evidence: Research subagent with web search and fetch, 2026-10-02: 20 shared servers in the docs; the headless What's New page (updated 2026-09-23) adds no mapping server

title: When you present IDMC MCP coverage, mark each server as called-live or registry-only, and quote the tool count as a range
text: A capability slide built from the MCP registry listed all managed servers as if usable. The KB evidence showed real calls for only some of them (connection management, Secure Agent management, the data-quality agent, address verification, the orchestrator and data-exploration agents); the rest were only enumerated (job, log, audit, asset promotion, catalog search, discovery and enrichment, provisioning, MDM search, user and IPU management, and a preview troubleshooting server). Per-server tool counts summed to about 120 while the enumeration summary said about 140, so say 'about 120-140 tools'. There is still no MCP verb for authoring mappings, deploying CDC or publishing CAI: those stay REST. The MCP layer itself is not metered, but the services behind each call bill as usual (L-MCP-008, L-MCP-026). Refines L-MCP-119.
evidence: 20 servers in the registry; 7 with recorded live calls; 13 listed only; tool sum about 120 vs summary 140 (2026-11-13)

title: Stage a risky CAI cutover so the one unproven publish runs first, with a parallel test path and an undo for every step
text: When a cutover depends on an asset type that has failed to publish before in the org (here a Data Access Service Connector, L-CAI-139), stage everything offline, then make the runbook's first IDMC step a publish test of only that asset; if it fails, stop with nothing live changed and pick a fallback (the database's REST layer, a JDBC app connection, or a vendor case). Put stand-ins in their own folder, expose the new path on parallel URLs before switching the live ones, keep the old implementation running until the last step, and write each step's check and undo. Messages wait in Kafka during the switch, so a short pause loses nothing.
evidence: package of 67 assets staged; runbook 60-75 min with a 10-15 min pause on the live path and a 10-15 min undo; first IDMC step = connector publish test (2026-10-12)

title: A chat 'yes' does not clear an auto-mode block on a production deploy: stage everything, then run the cutover with the user approving each step in ask mode
text: In auto mode the permission classifier refused a subagent's publish-and-switch of live CAI processes as a production deploy, and the user's approval typed in chat did not change that verdict. Do not retry the action in pieces or through another agent (L-METHOD-121). Keep the agent on staging, then have the user switch the session to the normal ask-each-time mode and run the scripted cutover step by step with their approval. That is narrower than adding a permanent allow rule. Refines L-METHOD-121.
evidence: one 'production deploy' denial on a cutover; staging continued; cutover parked for step-by-step approval (2026-10-12)

title: A subagent that reads for minutes before writing can die with nothing: brief restarts to write skeleton outputs early and cap the reading
text: Three parallel build subagents died after about 3 minutes of reading source and left no files. The restarts succeeded with four brief additions: create the output skeletons (README, build notes, config example) within the first ~15 tool calls and fill them in afterwards; read for at most ~40 tool calls before writing; write a per-lane keys file (name, meaning, where to get it, no values) for the coordinator to merge; and finish with compile, `--help` and secret-gate checks. Partial progress then survives a crash, and the coordinator resumes from files instead of from scratch. Refines L-METHOD-127.
evidence: 2026-10-14: 3 lanes died with zero output; the restarts finished in 25-40 minutes each with gates CLEAN; final bundle 572 files, 132 Python files compiled, 60 scripts answered --help

title: A guard that greps a package zip's raw bytes for a marker never fires: entries are deflate-compressed, so scan each decompressed entry
text: An import step meant to refuse IDMC packages built offline (with placeholder ids) searched the zip file's bytes for the placeholder marker and always passed, because zip entries are compressed. Open the package with `zipfile`, read every entry (the IMF JSON and the manifest files) and search the decompressed text, refusing the import if any entry contains the marker. Test the guard with a deliberately offline-built package, the way a secret scanner is tested with a planted fake value.
evidence: 2026-10-14: bug found by a reviewing subagent; after the fix an offline-built package was refused and the 13-step offline self-check still passed

title: Before calling agent status stale or a connection test a false pass, check whether the same agent identity now runs on another host
text: After an agent's install directory was copied to a bigger host (L-AGENT-102) and the old host stopped and disabled, one session saw the old host down, IDMC still reporting every engine RUNNING and v2 connection tests answering 200, and concluded that the status was stale and that tests pass with the agent stopped. Both were wrong: the same agent id was running on the new host, so the status and tests were real. Another session was then told to restart the agent on the OLD host, which would have put two hosts on one agent identity. Before acting on 'agent down' or 'status stale', read the agent's reported host/IP from the v2 agent details, compare it with the host you are inspecting, and ask whether a migration is in progress; never start a second copy of an agent identity. Refines L-AGENT-068.
evidence: Old host stopped 06:25-06:28Z; new host active 06:29Z with 10/10 engines; tests at 06:37Z 200 were the new host; the restart on the old host was cancelled (2026-10-19)

title: An object id in a designer URL resolves only in the org that owns it: find the owning org before concluding the mapping is unsaved or missing
text: A user pasted a Mapping Designer link (`.../diUI/products/integrationDesign/main/mapping/<id>/edit`). Looked up with the first login that matched the pod host, the id was not found, and the first answer guessed it was an unsaved draft and described the wrong org's connections. Several orgs (and sub-orgs) share one pod host, so the host does not identify the org. Search every stored org profile for the id (v3 objects or FRS lookup per login), or the local notes and export inventories that record ids, before answering; then answer from the owning org's real mapping and connections. Refines L-AUTH-011.
evidence: Id not found under two logins on the same pod; found in a third org's inventory; the corrected answer read that org's mapping and its connections (2026-10-19)

title: Test a packaged IDMC skill in isolated headless Claude sessions: one temporary config folder per edition, parallel offline scenarios, live-login scenarios one at a time
text: To prove a skill works for a stranger, run each scenario with `claude -p` under a temporary config directory (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) whose `skills/` holds only the edition under test, from a working folder with no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md in any parent, and with auth from environment variables so the temp config needs no secrets. Confirm the session lists only that skill. Run offline scenarios in parallel; run every scenario that logs in to IDMC serially and last, with the lockout guard on (L-METHOD-004). Grade each transcript: refuses to push another technology, gives real API calls instead of 'impossible', GET-only on live reads, never writes a password inside the skill folder. Also check the shipped zip: entry point at the top, empty login file, no private folder. Refines L-METHOD-094.
evidence: 16 scenarios: 13 in parallel, 3 live serially; all passed; 7 small fixes found (null orgName in the login check, no rule for a missing guide, a password saved inside the skill folder, competing old skills still installed) (2026-11-12)

title: Fact-check every product-comparison claim against current vendor docs before it ships: a first draft from model knowledge had 8 of 31 claims wrong
text: A technical comparison of IDMC with a cloud ETL service, written first from model knowledge, had 8 of 31 claims wrong after a doc check (connector counts, which CDC sources are log-based, an activity limit, external vault support, masking features), and it missed that the competitor's catalog and data-quality product was being retired. Add a Fact Check tab that lists each claim with its status (confirmed, corrected, unverified), its source, and whether it comes from vendor docs or your own lab runs. Read the live deployment rather than inferring what is configured. Refines L-METHOD-145.
evidence: 31 claims: 19 confirmed, 8 corrected, 1 added, 2 unverified, 1 lab-only (2026-11-13)

title: IDMC native source control with a self-hosted GitLab: choose Platform = On-Premise, and Git traffic goes through a runtime environment's GitRepoConnectApp
text: IDMC source control supports GitHub and GitLab (cloud or self-hosted), Bitbucket (self-hosted, or cloud for Data Integration assets only) and Azure DevOps (cloud only). For a GitLab on your own domain set Administrator > Settings > Source Control > Platform = On-Premise and pick a runtime environment: the agent's GitRepoConnectApp service keeps a clone of only the configured branch under `<agent_home>/apps/GitRepoConnectApp/data/git_repository/`, so the Git host never has to be reachable from the vendor cloud, but every agent in that runtime environment must reach it over HTTPS. OAuth works only for cloud repos. As you type the repository URL the UI calls `GET /vcs/api/v1/remoteRepo/lookupConnectionType?uri=<repo_url>`; for a self-hosted host it returns `{"type":"ONPREM_GIT"}`, which tells you Cloud mode is the wrong choice. Before the org is configured, related calls answer 'The connection to the source control repository for this organization cannot be found', and an intermediate URL value can return 400 `VCS_029` 'The source control repository URL is not valid'.
evidence: Vendor Administrator source-control pages (updated Aug 2026) read 2026-10-02; live XHR capture: lookupConnectionType -> ONPREM_GIT for a self-hosted GitLab URL, an earlier 400 VCS_029 on the same field (2026-10-03)

title: Once an asset is source-controlled, an OVERWRITE package import of it needs a checkout first: make headless importers check out, import, then check in
text: After source control is enabled nothing is versioned until objects are checked in, and checking in one object makes its folder or project source-controlled. From then on, source-controlled objects must be checked out to change them, and the import docs say an asset must be checked out to be overwritten, so a generator that rebuilds mappings with `POST /public/core/v3/import` and OVERWRITE will start failing. Make the importer read the package's exported objects, `POST /public/core/v3/lookup` their ids to find the controlled ones, `POST /public/core/v3/checkout` those, import, then `POST /public/core/v3/checkin`; call `/undoCheckout` when the import fails, and keep a switch that skips all of it on orgs without source control. Mapping edits deploy to their mapping tasks even when the tasks are not checked out, and undo checkout reverts to the last pulled version with no history.
evidence: Vendor asset-import and checkout pages (Jul 2026); a checkout-aware importer compiled and its lookup tested offline against a real package (2026-10-02). The org was not yet switched on, so the live error code for an import without checkout is unverified

title: IDMC source-control REST is v3 and asynchronous: POST checkin, checkout or pull, then poll sourceControlAction
text: Endpoints under `/public/core/v3/`: POST `checkout`, `undoCheckout`, `checkin` (`objects[{id, includeContainerAssets}]` plus a required `summary` of at most 255 characters), `pull` (`commitHash`, `objects[{id|path,type}]`, and `objectSpecification` to remap connections and runtime environments) and `pullByCommitHash`; GET `commit`, `commitHistory?q=path=='<project>/<folder>/<asset>' and type=='DTEMPLATE'`, `compare` and `repositoryConnection?projectIds=`. Each POST returns `{"Id":...,"status":{"state":"NOT_STARTED"}}`; poll `GET /public/core/v3/sourceControlAction/<id>?expand=objects` until SUCCESSFUL, FAILED or WARNING. Check-in types include DTEMPLATE, MTT, DSS, DMAPPLET, MAPPLET, WORKFLOW, TASKFLOW, MI_TASK, UDF, PCS, FWCONFIG and the CAI types PROCESS, AI_CONNECTION, AI_SERVICE_CONNECTOR, GUIDE, PROCESS_OBJECT, HUMAN_TASK. Connections, runtime environments, schedules and Database Ingestion assets cannot be source-controlled, so they must already exist in a target org before a pull. The vendor's asset-management CLI has no Git commands. URL-encode the `q=` filter (quotes and spaces) when building these queries in code.
evidence: Vendor platform v3 REST reference, source-control pages (Jul 2026), read 2026-10-02; the CLI binary's strings show only login/logout/lookup/objects/export/import

title: Decide the source-control scope before you switch it on: there is no unlink endpoint, and the way back is manual
text: Before source control can be disabled on a read/write org every asset must be unlinked, and projects and folders unlink only after every object in them is unlinked. The repository URL cannot be changed while any asset is source-controlled, and the org cannot move from read/write to read-only while anything is checked out. UNLINK exists only as an action type in status responses, not as an endpoint, so backing out of source control on a large org is click work in the UI. Pilot on a scratch org or a single project (Enable Project Level Source Control), use one development org per repository with read-only test and production orgs, and check in a planned scope rather than everything.
evidence: Vendor disabling and unlinking pages (Aug 2026) read 2026-10-02; no unlink route in the v3 reference

title: IDMC source-control limits and pull traps: 800 objects per check-in, a branch that already exists, an empty repo, case-insensitive names
text: Use an empty repository with no `Explore` folder and a branch that already exists (a blank branch name means master or main); on save IDMC writes a small readme into the repository. Limits: 50 MB and at most 800 objects per check-in, at most 1,000 objects per container, and cloud-hosted GitLab check-ins of more than 100 objects fail after about 30 minutes, so batch them. A pull deletes objects that are not in the selected version, does not bring dependent objects, fails when a project holds names differing only by case (`sales` and `SALES`), and in a read-only org can silently overwrite local edits. The docs also warn that GitLab can show incorrect commit history in pull and compare. Count the scope first with v3 objects queries.
evidence: Vendor best-practice and limits pages read 2026-10-02; scope counted live: 195 objects across three projects, none source-controlled yet

title: Mapping-task package import OIE_007 'Internal application provider error': mtTask.json holds the runtime environment as an '@<FRS id>' reference; do not overwrite it with a v2 id
text: When cloning a mapping-task (MTT) from an export, the task's `mtTask.json` carries `runtimeEnvironmentId` as an FRS reference of the form `@<22-character id>`, not the v2 `01...25...` runtime id. Replacing it with the v2 id made the mapping import fine but the task fail with `OIE_007 ... Failed to import object [...] of type [MTT] ... Internal application provider error` (no further detail). Removing the override (keeping the exported `@` reference, which resolves by the runtime's FRS id in the target org) imported SUCCESSFUL. To change the runtime, set the FRS-id form, or update the task over v2 after import and read it back. Refines L-MIG-076.
evidence: Package FAILED with the v2 id in runtimeEnvironmentId, SUCCESSFUL after deleting that one line; both parse tasks then validated and ran (2026-10-13)

title: Enabling org source control and entering Git credentials are UI-only: automate the two screens with Playwright, and expect a 'Configure' button
text: No REST endpoint configures source control for an org or stores a user's Git credentials. The org screen is Administrator > Settings > Source Control > Edit (Enable Source Control, Enable Project Level Source Control, Allow Push to Git Repository, Platform, Repository Type, Global Git Repository URL, Global Git Branch Name, OAuth, Runtime Environment); the per-user screen is user menu > Settings > Source Control Access (Git user name plus a personal access token with full repository control, e.g. GitLab scope `api`). Traps seen live: the Edit control is an icon button (`aria-label="Edit"`), not a text button; after Save a modal 'Git Repository Configuration Credentials' asks for User Name and Personal Access Token and its primary button is 'Configure', not OK or Save; a Playwright `fill` on a still-disabled field retries silently every 500 ms until its 30 s timeout ('element is not enabled'), so wait for the field to be enabled or for the dialog. Build a read-only walk first (open, dump the fields, Cancel), then a save run that logs every non-GET and every >=400 XHR. Users see no source-control columns or actions until they enter their own credentials.
evidence: Read-only form dumps, then save attempts 2026-10-02/03: one fill timed out after 64 retries on a disabled field; dialog text 'Enter the Git credentials ... User Name Personal Access Token Configure Cancel'

title: Starting a mapping task on demand while its scheduled pipeline run is active fails at once with 'The Mapping task failed to run. Another instance of the task is currently running.' and fails the whole lane
text: To beat a latency target, extra runs of a golden-record mapping task were started with `POST /api/v2/job` (taskType MTT) whenever a new record landed. When the pipeline's own run was already in progress, the extra run ended in about 1 s with state 3, 0 rows and that message in the activity log, and the controller marked that lane's cycle (7 tasks) FAILED. A mapping task runs one instance at a time, and re-starting it cannot shorten a chain whose floor is the task's own runtime (about 2 min 10 s here). Before an on-demand start, read the latest activity-log entries or the activity monitor for that taskId and skip if one is running, or coalesce triggers into the next scheduled run (L-CDI-128). Refines L-CDI-253.
evidence: activityLog: runs of 1-2 s with state 3 and 0 rows between successful ~2-min runs (11,171 rows); controller alert and 'run ... FAILED (7 tasks)' two minutes later

title: Pushdown would not rescue a mapping-based master on ClickHouse: SQL ELT is proven only within one warehouse family, and Cleanse, Verifier, Deduplicate and cloud address verification never push down
text: Asked whether enabling pushdown would have closed the gap with native SQL: full SQL ELT is documented and proven only when source and target share an ecosystem (BigQuery to BigQuery, L-CDI-043/L-CDI-202), and nothing shows pushdown generating ClickHouse SQL through the JDBC V2 connector. Even where it works, only set work (joins, survivorship aggregations, match keys, routing) pushes down; the DQ engine steps run in the agent's engine and address verification is a cloud service call either way. Plan ClickHouse mastering as agent mode: incremental volume, tuned JDBC writes (L-CDI-262) and a Post SQL fold. For certainty, test pushdown once on a copy of one task and look for generated SQL in the session log. Refines L-CDI-043.
evidence: Not probed live (would need a task change); KB evidence only; measured agent-mode gap 10-100x on full rebuilds

title: Address verification of a single free-text address box returns low-confidence matches because users type only the street: use required street, city, state and ZIP fields and full street forms
text: A sign-up form with one address field expected 'street, city, ST 12345' but users typed only the house number and street, so the verification service could only return a low-confidence match and the UI showed nothing. With four required fields (street, city, state, ZIP), even messy input (extra spaces, lower case, 2-letter state) came back VERIFIED with ZIP+4 about 28 s after the record landed. Abbreviated forms such as '20 W 34th St, New York 10001' were still rated LOW_CONFIDENCE_MATCH while full forms ('West 34th Street') verified, and an invented address finished as low confidence in 27-33 s. Collect structured fields and treat low confidence as a reviewable result, not a pending state. Refines L-DQ-016.
evidence: Messy 4-field input -> standardized upper-case street, city, state and ZIP+4; 29 people over four 2-minute runs, none stuck; 1 abbreviated address low confidence in 46 s

title: An IDMC name-cleansing capitalization step lowercased the letter after an apostrophe: 'siobhán O'NEILL' became 'Siobhán O'neill'
text: In a sign-up -> CDC -> cleanse/match golden-record pipeline, the name standardization handled accents correctly but treated the apostrophe as part of the word, so O'NEILL came out O'neill. The same class of defect is documented for CAI and plain INITCAP (L-CAI-086, L-CDI-104): treat straight and curly apostrophes and hyphens as word delimiters in the capitalization logic, and include O'/Mc/Mac and hyphenated names in the test set before loading real customers. Refines L-CDI-104.
evidence: 1 of 10 scripted user stories; the other stories, including accented names, passed

title: Pause address verification while entity ids are still being merged and re-keyed; after the migration run it once on the final master for 'no result or changed address' only
text: Verifying during an identity migration wastes paid calls: results land on ids that are about to be merged or re-keyed, and the sweep mostly re-pays for addresses that already failed. With 99.9% of the new master's addresses already verified, pausing cost nothing except that new or changed entities are held from serving until the reset (safe). Pause properly: stop every external starter (cron, timer, a session-launched driver), disable the IDMC schedules that drive the verification tasks, let in-flight runs finish, and read the schedules back at the next boundary (L-METHOD-135). Reset = keep all paid results, verify once in big batches only entities with no result or a changed address fingerprint, count 'premise found, unit unconfirmed' as verified, route no-house-number or placeholder addresses to review, then verify only new or changed addresses in each incremental cycle. Refines L-METHOD-135.
evidence: Master address methods: certified 87.8M, verifier 2.1M, suggestion 1.7M, not verified 55k of 91.7M; ~98M paid results kept; 3 IDMC schedules + 2 external starters identified

title: Close the profile -> recommend -> clean -> score -> gate loop on the table you actually serve: 17 profiles and 60 rules had scored only the old table and samples, and gated nothing
text: IDMC profiling had run 17 profiles over 1,290 columns (one at 101M rows on ClickHouse), 60 rule specifications and 218 checks, and CLAIRE insights found real defects (a status with no score, an empty-input hash, ZIP+4 in a 5-digit column, half the rows provisional). Yet the score column stayed empty on 100% of rows, no rule could stop a publish, and the new golden table was never profiled. Run the loop on the served table per scope with rules bound: profile, keep only recommended rules that test something (L-DQ-122), clean in a mapping on changed records only, write the score back per row and per scope, and let a failing hard rule block that scope's publish. Count profile runs where they run, not in the activity log (L-IPU-055). Refines L-DQ-136.
evidence: 17 profiles / 1,290 columns / 60 rule specs / 218 checks; gold 90.3% vs staging 97.3%; 73 CLAIRE insights on one table; score column NULL on 100% of rows a week later

title: Preflight for a live IDMC-backed demo: check the causes that actually stopped cleanse, match and verify, not just whether the agent is up
text: Causes that made name, email and address steps hang in one live pipeline, each with its check: pipelines switched off to save the job budget (turn on; watchdog every 15 min); the hosted runtime down, so batch SaaS-sync tasks failed while CAI real-time calls kept working (rebind, or show values from earlier stages); the agent host's disk full, which broke address verification twice; the warehouse's daily query quota used up by BI refreshes, which failed every DQ task (L-CONN-133: cap refreshes, grep for 'quota exceeded'); the monthly job count (count this month's activity-log jobs against soft/hard limits, L-IPU-041); recent failure counts of the golden and DQ tasks; CDC lag; SaaS storage and daily API limits (do a test insert, since the storage gauge recalculates late). Include one real end-to-end test record in the check. Refines L-CONN-133.
evidence: Disk full on two dates broke verification; quota exhaustion failed every DQ job on one day; job budget 1,588 used vs soft 8,500 / hard 9,500; SaaS API 9,455 of 15,000 left; 16 containers checked

title: A BigQuery service key without bigquery.jobs.list/listAll cannot read INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT or JOBS_BY_USER, so it cannot measure the quota it is spending
text: When checking how much of a project's daily query quota IDMC tasks and dashboard refreshes used, both `region-us.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT` and `JOBS_BY_USER` returned 403 accessDenied for the pipeline's key (needs bigquery.jobs.listAll at project level, or bigquery.jobs.list). Either grant a read-only monitoring identity those permissions, or estimate from your own logs (bytes per build x builds) and cap the callers (for example 24 refresh builds an hour at about 3.8 GB each against a shared 2 TiB/day quota). Refines L-CONN-133.
evidence: ERR 403 Access Denied ... 'bigquery.jobs.listAll' / 'bigquery.jobs.list' permission(s) at the project level

title: A ReplacingMergeTree golden table read without FINAL returns superseded versions: readers counted ~104M rows for 91.7M real entities
text: Golden tables on ClickHouse's replacing engine keep old row versions until a background merge, so count(), duplicate checks, DQ profiles and downstream readers that omit FINAL (or an argMax by version) see stale and duplicate rows. Measured: 204.58M rows vs 203.87M distinct ids in one table (710,905 unmerged versions) and about 104M rows read vs 91.7M with FINAL in another. Run every acceptance gate with FINAL and cap memory/threads in SETTINGS (needs readonly=2 on read-only sessions, L-ENV-112); list the table's readers in query_log and fix any that skip FINAL, including IDMC source queries. Refines L-MDM-079.
evidence: 204,582,711 rows / 203,871,806 distinct ids; golden table 91,749,560 rows with FINAL vs ~104M without

title: An external runner starting an address-verification mapping every few minutes at ~4,800 addresses per run burned ~728 jobs a day, on track for ~22,000 a month against a ~10,000 org cap
text: A script outside IDMC re-imported the verification mapping with new key bounds and started it every few minutes; no IDMC schedule showed that cadence, so the burn was visible only by counting activity-log entries per task per day. Each run handled only about 4,800 addresses, so 9.8M results cost about 2,030 jobs in four days, plus four certified-mode shard tasks. It also paid twice: about 391k addresses had already verified in an earlier run, and most of the rest were retries of rows that had failed or come back unresolved and could not improve (no house number, placeholder street). At the monthly cap every Data Integration job in the org stops (L-IPU-041). Fix: few large runs, select inputs by anti-join on stored results (L-CDI-283), classify and route unfixable failures to review instead of re-calling (L-DQ-129), and count jobs per task per day in a daily check. Refines L-CDI-283.
evidence: One day: 728 jobs (572 verifier runs + 156 shard runs); runs/day 57, 1,060, 504, 406 over four days; 9,800,544 results for 9,800,519 entities over 2,030 run ids; 390,963 previously verified; prior statuses secondary_unverified 4.59M, failed 2.52M, unresolved 1.87M

title: A repeat sign-up with the same name and address is correctly merged into the existing golden customer, but downstream CRM writes then land on the survivor while the new CRM contact stays orphaned
text: Match-and-merge folded re-registered people into their existing golden record, and their purchase then attached to the survivor's CRM record; the new sign-up's own CRM contact had no plan, so an agent querying CRM listed paying customers as open trials. A later write also overwrote the sign-up source tag with a sales channel, dropping contacts out of the agent's filter. Downstream systems must resolve identity through the golden id / cross-reference, not through their own per-sign-up record: merge or link the duplicate CRM contact when the master merges, and never reuse a tag or lineage field for a second meaning.
evidence: 2 paid customers listed as open trials; 2 contacts lost their tag and were re-tagged; the duplicate-merge story itself passed as designed

title: Mapping-based mastering on ClickHouse ran 10-100x slower than in-warehouse SQL on full rebuilds; it is viable only when each cycle processes the changed ~1%
text: Measured from ClickHouse system.query_log on the same server: IDMC mappings writing over JDBC V2 reached about 1,100-18,000 rows/s (all tasks together), while set-based SQL inside ClickHouse wrote 124,000-660,000 rows/s, because without pushdown every row leaves the database, crosses the agent's engine and comes back. A full national rebuild through mappings would take about 8-25 h per pass against about 4 h/day for the SQL. Only 0.93% of golden rows changed per build, and that slice (about 850k rows) takes roughly 1-13 minutes in IDMC. Design a mapping-based master as incremental from day one (input fingerprint; re-run match and survivorship only for touched entities); do not compare IDMC with SQL on full rebuilds. Refines L-AGENT-118.
evidence: IDMC: standardization 383M rows in 5.8 h (1,372 rows/INSERT), merge routing 29.7M in 7.4 h (200 rows/INSERT); SQL: 2.0B rows in 50.5 min and 1.09B in 147 min of query time; 850,912 of 91,749,560 rows changed per build; ~1.8B rows rewritten/day

title: Post-mortem of a home-grown MDM built with IDMC mappings: it worked on one state and was abandoned at national scale for design reasons, not because mappings cannot master
text: A property master built with IDMC transformations (Cleanse/Verifier, Rule Specifications, match on sorted input, sorted-Aggregator survivorship, Router to a review queue) was proven on single states, then replaced by plain SQL when scaled to about 92M entities. The costly mistakes, in order: (1) full rebuilds instead of incremental; (2) jumping from a 235k-row pilot to national without a sizing step; (3) four competing golden builds in 12 days instead of one owner evolving one pipeline; (4) logic as SQL text, first in mapping source queries, then outside IDMC; (5) one copy per state (123 mappings/tasks) instead of one parameterized mapping, with one state re-run about 11 times; (6) tuned JDBC write settings not carried into new mappings; (7) matching on blank standardized keys; (8) gates measured but never allowed to stop a publish; (9) IDMC merge decisions computed and never consumed; (10) rules prototyped in Python/SQL and never ported back; (11) orchestration by AI coding sessions (reaped after 120 min idle) instead of a scheduled IDMC taskflow; (12) no budget for jobs and paid calls. Use the list as a pre-scale checklist. Refines L-MDM-081.
evidence: Single-state results: 2.52M source records -> 2.52M masters with 0 diffs on single-source masters (golden step 13-38 min); identity matching 235,734 rows -> 169,916 entities, 0 wrong merges in 939 checked pairs; national IDMC standardization 383M rows in 5.8 h; the national master then built by 6,649 plain-SQL statements

title: IDMC merge decisions and DQ results that no downstream step reads: 29.7M routing decisions, a 3.56M-pair review queue and 140M+ rule-result rows changed nothing in the golden table
text: The IDMC pipeline wrote merge-or-review routing decisions with keep-apart rules, a steward review queue and per-rule DQ results, but the golden build re-derived duplicates with its own SQL rules, so two rule sets existed and the IDMC outputs were dead ends (only ad-hoc SELECTs read them). Before claiming IDMC masters a table, prove each IDMC output has a consumer: in query_log, look for INSERT ... SELECT statements whose `tables` include the decision table and whose target is a golden-stage table. Either make the IDMC decisions the input of the merge (then a short Post SQL fold, L-CDI-273) or retire the IDMC step; compare IDMC and SQL decisions on one scope first. Refines L-METHOD-043.
evidence: Routing 29.7M rows, review queue 3.56M rows, DQ rule rows 140M+; IDMC standardized facts WERE consumed (via one SQL facts table), routing and queue were not

title: Standardized match-key columns left blank on held (provisional) rows made half a golden table unmatchable: millions were exact duplicates of confirmed entities by raw address
text: The matcher keyed on standardized address columns, but those columns were empty on every provisional row, so 49% of the golden table stayed provisional and could never merge. Matching the same rows on the raw normalized address found 12.85M provisional-address rows equal to a confirmed entity's state + address and 2.5M provisional-parcel rows equal to a confirmed parcel id (about 17-19M likely unmerged duplicates). Add a gate that fails the run when any row entering matching has a blank match key, and profile match-key completeness per scope (state, source) before every match run. Refines L-DQ-145.
evidence: Golden table 204.6M rows / 302 GB; provisional 100.6M (49.2%): address 44.75M, parcel 43.39M, source-id-only 12.45M; standardized address blank on 100% of provisional rows

title: Condo units without a unit number collapse onto one served address: gate on no duplicate (address, ZIP, unit) among served rows and recover units before matching
text: In a property master, about 916k served rows shared a standardized address with a blank unit number across different parcels, and 85k more shared both the address and the parcel (condo units that lost their unit). Address-only match keys either merge distinct units or leave visible duplicates; a rule that unit-less units must not be served had been written but was not enforced. Gate: group served rows by state, ZIP, house number, street, suffix and unit and fail on any group > 1. Recover units by cleansing the source unit field, verifying it, and placing units under their building by parcel (L-MDM-076). Check first whether the sources carry units at all. Refines L-MDM-076.
evidence: Blank unit + different parcels 408,251 groups / 916,284 rows; blank unit + same parcel 41,828 / 85,521; unit set + different parcel 10,173 / 21,717; old table 442,526 groups / 1.61M served rows; one address repeated 53 times

title: Insert a sizing step between pilot and fan-out: measure rows/s, jobs per run and sort memory on one scope, then extrapolate before scaling a mastering pipeline
text: A master went from a 235k-row single-state pilot straight to about 92M entities; throughput, the monthly job count and the warehouse sort-memory cap (L-CDI-272) were all discovered at go-live under deadline, and the team switched to plain SQL. Before fanning out: run one mid-size scope, record rows/s per stage from the warehouse log, jobs per scope (N tasks in a taskflow = N+1 jobs), and peak memory of the sorted reads; compute national time, monthly jobs and memory headroom; fan out in scope groups only if all three fit, otherwise redesign first (incremental, sharding, fewer bigger runs).
evidence: Pilot 235,734 rows; national ~92M entities; full IDMC pass estimated 8-25 h; job cap ~10,000/month; one state re-run ~11 times (197M rows written for 17.9M entities)

title: A live UI over batch IDMC steps must never wait unbounded: show each value from the earliest stage that has it, start verification on landing, and time out to an amber 'flagged for review' state that updates in place
text: A demo page traced sign-up -> CDC -> cleanse/match -> address verification -> DQ check and spun on 'checking...' whenever a batch job was slow, failed during a runtime outage or skipped the record. What worked: (1) show cleaned name/phone/email as soon as the golden record has them (about 25 s after CDC) instead of waiting for a later DQ job that ran once per 3-6 minute cycle, and add the check mark when it finishes; (2) trigger verification when the record lands instead of on the next scheduled cycle (result 8 s after CDC instead of up to 20 s more); (3) after 75 s with no result, finish the step in amber ('not verified yet, flagged') and update in place if the result arrives; dashboards use 2 minutes. Verify with an N-person burst test whose pass rule is 'every step finished, not running, within 2 minutes'. Refines L-CDI-206.
evidence: Page steps (CDC + cleaned values + address) finished in 33-49 s; dashboard rows ready 29-53 s; CDC 11-43 s (avg ~21 s); DQ check mark ~3 min; 21/21 checks passed after the change

title: Tell 'plain SQL', 'SQL inside IDMC' and 'real IDMC transformations' apart from ClickHouse system.query_log: user, client_name, interface and initial_address of every write
text: Query `system.query_log WHERE type='QueryFinish' AND query_kind NOT IN ('Select','Show','Describe')`, filter on the statement text `INSERT INTO <database>.<table>` (not on `has(tables, ...)`, which also lists tables an INSERT ... SELECT only reads, L-ENV-116), and group by user, client_name, client_hostname, initial_address and interface. IDMC JDBC V2 writes arrive as the IDMC database user over HTTP (interface 2) from the agent host's address with an empty client_name; scripts run through `docker exec ... clickhouse-client` arrive as the default user, client_name 'ClickHouse client', native TCP (interface 1) from 127.0.0.1. 'SQL inside IDMC' (logic in a mapping's source query, Pre/Post SQL or an SQL task) shows the IDMC user while the rule logic is SQL text: confirm by exporting the mapping and measuring source-query length. Answer per table and per pipeline stage, because one master can mix all three. Refines L-METHOD-043.
evidence: 6,649 create/insert/delete statements on 5 golden tables: 100% default user, ClickHouse client, interface 1, 127.0.0.1; IDMC user: 1.76M inserts from the agent address over interface 2, none into a golden table; an earlier stage: 1.43B rows written by IDMC but with 16 MB of SQL in source queries

title: Do not let AI coding sessions orchestrate a multi-day IDMC build: sessions reaped after 120 idle minutes stalled it repeatedly; move the chain into a scheduled linear taskflow with a failing gate mapping
text: A national mastering go-live was driven by several Claude sessions, babysitter scripts, cron and per-scope switch scripts over SSH; sessions were reaped after 120 minutes without a check-in, work stopped part-way, decisions (holds, rollbacks, GO lists) lived only in a server log, and an alert script ran every 5 minutes with an empty destination so nothing reached anyone. An IDMC linear taskflow on a native schedule runs with no session alive, a gate mapping that fails the run replaces the UI-only Decision step (L-CDI-069/L-CDI-073), and the monitor gives per-step rows and restarts. Before handing off, read back that alerts reach a real channel and record every pending decision on the tracker.
evidence: Sessions reaped after 120 min; 3 scopes switched then rolled back with no recorded reason; alert job every 5 min with an empty destination; 6 downstream cron clocks not waiting for the build

title: CDQ Deduplicate can consolidate duplicates into one preferred record (row or field rules), but it is not MDM: no source trust, cross-reference, history, unmerge or steward inbox
text: The Deduplicate asset does fuzzy identity matching (scores plus a ClusterId) and has an optional Consolidation tab. Row-based consolidation picks one survivor (Most Data, Most Filled, Modal Exact); field-based picks each field separately (Highest row ID, Average, Longest, Max, Min, Most frequent, Most frequent non-blank, Shortest). So basic rule-based survivorship exists in CDQ. What it does not give you: source-trust ranking, a persistent golden record with a cross-reference to source ids, merge history, unmerge, or a steward merge/unmerge screen; Exception Management only routes borderline scores to a target. Describe it as 'dedupe + consolidate (batch)' and 'preferred record', not 'match and merge' or 'golden record', and position MDM when trust, xref, unmerge or stewardship is needed.
evidence: CDQ April 2026 Data Quality Assets guide ch. 6 (Deduplicate / Consolidation); corrected by an MDM SME review

title: CDI-PC is PowerCenter in the customer's own domain, registered to IDMC; IDMC hosts domain management and PC2CDI, and DEI/IDQ modernization reached production only with the optional October 2026 update
text: CDI-PC (Cloud Data Integration for PowerCenter) keeps the PowerCenter engine and desktop clients in the customer's on-prem domain; IDMC hosts the Domain Management service (status, alerts, automatic domain updates, licence sync, metering) plus the PC2CDI assess/convert tooling. A Secure Agent only links the domain to IDMC, and the domain goes offline after about 2 hours without IDMC. In the October 2026 release DEI and IDQ modernization (Developer and Analyst tools) moved from preview to production, but only for orgs that take the optional October update (otherwise April 2027); the April update is mandatory within 90 days. The CDI-PC PAM 2026.10 still lists DQ/DEI as unsupported, so check both documents. None of the Product Description Schedule versions 37.0.1 to 39.2 name CDI-PC in the IPU-eligible matrix: CDI-PC meter rates appear only on the org's Metering rate card. Operational Insights alerts cannot be set up for CDI-PC.
evidence: CDI-PC Oct 2026 doc set, PowerCenter 10.5.11, PAM 2026.10, CPDS 37.0.1-39.2, Measurement Guide 39.1, Informatica KB 000246690

title: Rate an IDMC capability in three tiers: built in, built with IDMC assets and proven, or buildable but not yet built; headless-built mappings count as IDMC, not DIY
text: When comparing what IDMC can do (for example against MDM or a graph database), a capability Claude built as an IDMC mapping or taskflow over the REST APIs is IDMC-native, not custom code: the assets live, run and are monitored in IDMC. Use three tiers: built in (out of the box), built with IDMC assets and proven (deployed asset plus successful runs, checked in the live org before you claim it), and buildable in IDMC but not yet built. Reserve 'DIY' for code that runs outside IDMC (Python, Cypher, shell). Read back the live org before rating, because 'proven' needs a deployed asset and runs.
evidence: Customer 360 behaviour (fuzzy dedupe, survivorship, incremental golden sync, reverse ETL) built headless and validated live; reviewers had labelled it DIY
